scenario: 电商购物车服务：每用户一个购物车，读写频繁，要求毫秒级读取，可容忍极短暂不一致，结构简单 (user_id → 商品列表)。
q: 最适合做购物车主存储的是？
options: PostgreSQL（关系型）
Redis（内存 KV）
Neo4j（图数据库）
Elasticsearch（搜索引擎）
why: 购物车是高频读写、按 key 存取、结构简单、可容忍短暂不一致的典型场景，内存 KV 的毫秒延迟正好匹配。
why_en: A shopping cart has simple key-based access, high read-write throughput, and tolerates brief inconsistency, so an in-memory key-value store like Redis fits best.
whenOtherWins: 若购物车必须和库存/订单强一致（下单即扣减、不能超卖），关系型数据库反而更合适——决定因素是一致性要求。

scenario: 支付系统存用户账户余额，并发扣款绝不能丢更新，需要审计与事务。
q: 最安全的主存储是？
options: PostgreSQL
Cassandra
Redis
Amazon S3
why: 余额是钱，需要 ACID 事务和行级锁来防止并发丢更新，关系型数据库天然提供。
why_en: Account balances are money, so they need ACID transactions and row-level locking to prevent lost updates, which a relational database provides.
whenOtherWins: 若只是不可变的追加式流水日志，也可以用其它存储，但作为可变的余额真相源，关系型最稳。

scenario: 社交产品的信息流写入存储：写放大巨大（一次发帖扇出到百万粉丝），要求水平写扩展，稍有延迟/最终一致可接受。
q: 最合适的存储是？
options: 单实例 PostgreSQL
Cassandra（宽列）
SQLite
Neo4j
why: 写扇出巨大、需要无主的水平写扩展、且能容忍最终一致，正是宽列库 Cassandra 的强项。
why_en: A feed write store needs masterless horizontal write scaling and tolerates eventual consistency, which is exactly what a wide-column store like Cassandra offers.
whenOtherWins: 若需要强一致或复杂 join/事务，关系型或分布式 SQL 更合适——Cassandra 的代价是没有 join、要按查询设计表。

q: 以下哪些是关系型 (SQL) 数据库？（多选）
options: PostgreSQL
MySQL
CockroachDB
Cassandra
why: PostgreSQL、MySQL 是经典关系型；CockroachDB 是分布式 SQL（NewSQL），仍是关系型。Cassandra 是宽列 NoSQL。
why_en: PostgreSQL and MySQL are classic relational databases, and CockroachDB is distributed SQL, while Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL store.

q: 补全 ACID：
text: ACID = {{Atomicity}} 原子性、{{Consistency}} 一致性、{{Isolation}} 隔离性、{{Durability}} 持久性。
why: ACID 是关系型事务的四个保证，是「为什么强一致数据放关系型」的根本原因。
why_en: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability—the four guarantees behind relational transactions.

q: 相比单主关系型数据库，Cassandra 在写密集负载下的主要优势是？
options: 更强的 ACID 事务
无主架构下的水平写扩展
更丰富的 SQL join
更低的存储成本
why: Cassandra 无主、每个节点都能接受写，写吞吐随节点数近似线性扩展；这是它牺牲 join 和强一致换来的。
why_en: Cassandra is masterless so every node accepts writes, giving near-linear horizontal write scaling—traded off against joins and strong consistency.

q: 你给用户资料更新选了最终一致 (eventual consistency)，最主要的代价是？
options: 写入会丢失
写完立刻读可能读到旧值
数据会损坏
写延迟变高
why: 最终一致下副本需要时间收敛，写完马上读可能命中还没更新的副本（读到旧值）。缓解：read-your-writes 或读主。
why_en: Under eventual consistency, replicas take time to converge, so a read right after a write may return stale data—mitigated with read-your-writes routing.

scenario: 商品目录需要全文搜索：相关性排序、拼写容错、按多字段过滤。
q: 最合适的组件是？
options: PostgreSQL 的 LIKE 查询
Elasticsearch
Redis
Cassandra
why: 全文相关性排序 + 模糊/拼写容错需要倒排索引和打分，Elasticsearch 正是为此而生。
why_en: Full-text relevance ranking with typo tolerance needs an inverted index and scoring, which is what Elasticsearch is built for.
whenOtherWins: 若只是少量数据的前缀/简单匹配，PostgreSQL 的 GIN/trigram 索引就够了，不必背上 ES 的运维成本。

scenario: 需要存储并分发大量图片和视频原文件（每个几 MB 到几 GB）。
q: 文件本体应该放在哪？
options: PostgreSQL 的 BYTEA 字段
对象存储 (Amazon S3)
Redis
MySQL BLOB 字段
why: 大文件走对象存储（便宜、可扩展、能配 CDN），数据库只存元数据和文件 URL。把大 blob 塞进数据库会拖垮它。
why_en: Large media belongs in object storage like S3 with a CDN, while the database only keeps metadata and the file URL.

q: 经验数量级：单个 Redis 实例大致能处理多少 ops/秒？
why: 面试常用锚点：单 Redis 实例约 10 万 ops/秒量级（简单命令可更高，接近百万）。用来快速估算要不要分片。
why_en: A common interview anchor is that a single Redis instance handles on the order of a hundred thousand operations per second.

q: 经验数量级：SSD 一次随机读的大致延迟是？
options: ~10 毫秒
why: 内存 ~100ns、SSD 随机读 ~100µs、机械盘寻道 ~10ms。这条延迟阶梯是「该不该加缓存」的判断依据。
why_en: Memory access is about 100 nanoseconds, an SSD random read about 100 microseconds, and a disk seek about 10 milliseconds.

q: 强一致 vs 最终一致，本质上是在权衡哪两者？
options: 成本 vs 性能
一致性 vs 可用性/延迟
持久性 vs 隔离性
读 vs 写
why: CAP/PACELC：网络分区时要在一致性和可用性间取舍；即使没分区，强一致通常也以更高延迟为代价。
why_en: By CAP and PACELC, strong versus eventual consistency trades consistency against availability and latency.

scenario: 实时游戏排行榜：数百万玩家，分数频繁更新，要随时取 Top 100 和某人排名。
q: 最合适的结构是？
options: SQL 表 + ORDER BY
Redis Sorted Set (ZSET)
Cassandra
Elasticsearch
why: Redis 有序集合按分数排序，更新和取排名都是 O(log n)，取 Top-N 是原生操作，天生就是排行榜。
why_en: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by score with O(log n) updates and native top-N range queries, making it ideal for leaderboards.

scenario: 服务器监控指标：每秒海量写入、按时间范围查询、需要降采样和过期。
q: 最合适的存储类型是？
options: 普通 PostgreSQL 单表
时序数据库 (TimescaleDB / InfluxDB)
Redis
Neo4j
why: 时序库针对「时间为主轴」优化：高写入、时间分区、降采样和保留策略开箱即用。
why_en: Time-series databases are optimized for time as the primary axis, with high write rates, time partitioning, downsampling, and retention built in.
whenOtherWins: 数据量不大时，PostgreSQL 加 BRIN 索引或 TimescaleDB 扩展也能顶，不必立刻上专用系统。

scenario: 社交网络要频繁做「朋友的朋友」「最短关系路径」这类多跳关系查询。
q: 最合适的存储是？
options: 关系型 + 递归 join
Neo4j（图数据库）
Cassandra
Redis
why: 多跳遍历在关系型里是层层昂贵的 join，图数据库把关系当一等公民，遍历是原生高效操作。
why_en: Multi-hop relationship traversal is expensive with recursive joins, so a graph database like Neo4j, which treats relationships as first-class, is a better fit.
whenOtherWins: 若只是一两跳、数据量也不大，关系型的 join 完全够用，别为此引入图库。

q: 补全缓存的代价与缓解：
text: 在数据库前加了缓存，就必须处理 {{stale}} 旧数据，常用 {{TTL}} 过期或写时 {{invalidation}} 失效来控制。
why: 缓存必然引入一致性代价（可能读到旧值），标准缓解是 TTL 到期和写路径上的失效/更新。
why_en: Adding a cache introduces staleness, which is typically bounded with TTL expiry or write-time invalidation.

scenario: 要求缓存和数据库在每次写入后尽量保持一致，可以接受写入稍慢一点。
q: 应选哪种缓存写策略？
options: Cache-aside（旁路）
Write-through（写穿透）
Write-back（写回）
不用缓存
why: Write-through 在写数据库的同时写缓存，一致性最好，代价是写路径多一步、稍慢。
why_en: Write-through updates the cache and database together, giving the best consistency at the cost of slightly slower writes.
whenOtherWins: 若更在意写吞吐、能容忍少量丢失，write-back 更快；若读多写少，cache-aside 最简单常用。
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as 应用
    participant Cache as 缓存
    participant DB as 数据库
    App->>Cache: 写入 x
    Cache->>DB: 同步写入 x
    DB-->>Cache: OK
    Cache-->>App: OK
    Note over Cache,DB: 两边始终一致，代价是写路径多一步

q: Cache-aside（旁路缓存）什么时候把数据写进缓存？
options: 每次写数据库时
读缓存未命中时
从不
定时刷新时
why: Cache-aside 是懒加载：读时未命中才回源数据库并回填缓存；写时通常只更新/失效数据库那一份。
why_en: Cache-aside lazily loads data into the cache on a read miss, rather than on every write.

scenario: 支付接口要做边缘临时防重：高并发下快速判断「这个请求 ID 近期见过没有」，记录 24 小时后可过期；最终扣款幂等仍由持久表/唯一约束兜底。
q: 最顺手的做法是？
options: 关系型唯一索引
Redis SETNX + TTL
Amazon S3
Kafka topic
why: 高并发、临时、可过期的边缘防重，Redis 的 SETNX+TTL 一步搞定且极快。但支付最终幂等不能只靠易失缓存，核心扣款路径仍要用数据库唯一约束或 durable idempotency table。
why_en: For a fast expiring edge dedupe check, Redis SETNX with a TTL is useful, but final payment idempotency still needs a durable idempotency table or database uniqueness.
whenOtherWins: 若去重必须持久且强一致（比如扣款、对账、退款），关系型唯一约束或幂等表更可靠——决定因素是「能不能容忍过期/丢失」。

q: DynamoDB 的数据模型最准确的描述是？
options: 带 join 的关系型表
按分区键+排序键访问的键值/文档
图
全文索引
why: DynamoDB 是托管 KV/文档库，靠 partition key + sort key 访问，单位数毫秒延迟；没有跨表 join。
why_en: DynamoDB is a managed key-value and document store accessed by partition and sort keys, with single-digit millisecond latency and no joins.

q: 在分片(sharded)数据库里，一个「名人/爆款」热 key 会导致？
options: 数据丢失
热分区（负载倾斜）
一致性变强
存储变少
why: 所有请求打到同一个分区键会造成热分区，单个分片过载而其它空闲。缓解：给 key 加随机后缀打散、或对热点单独处理。
why_en: A hot key sends all traffic to one partition, creating a hot partition and skewed load—mitigated by adding a random suffix or handling hot keys separately.

scenario: 系统既要 SQL 和强一致事务，又要能水平扩展写入（单机写已经到顶）。
q: 最合适的选择是？
options: 加大单台 PostgreSQL
CockroachDB / Google Spanner
Cassandra
MongoDB
why: 既要关系型/强一致、又要水平写扩展，正是分布式 SQL (NewSQL) 的定位。
why_en: Wanting both relational strong consistency and horizontal write scaling points to distributed SQL such as CockroachDB or Spanner.
whenOtherWins: 如果单机 PostgreSQL 加只读副本还没到瓶颈，就别急着引入分布式 SQL 的复杂度。

q: 补全 SQL vs NoSQL 的取向：
text: SQL 数据库偏向 {{强一致}} 和丰富查询；典型 NoSQL 偏向 {{水平扩展}} 和灵活 schema。
why: 这是选型的第一层直觉：要事务和复杂查询偏 SQL，要海量规模和弹性结构偏 NoSQL——再用具体需求收敛。
why_en: SQL databases favor strong consistency and rich queries, while typical NoSQL favors horizontal scalability and flexible schemas.

q: 把「为什么加缓存」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 加 Redis（内存、O(1) 读）
热点数据被反复读、对延迟敏感
代价：可能读到旧数据
用 TTL + 写穿透来控制旧数据
why: 一条合格的决策 = 需求(热点重复读) → 选型(Redis) → 代价(旧数据) → 缓解(TTL/写穿透)。面试考的就是你能把这条链说清楚。
why_en: A solid decision runs requirement, choice, cost, then mitigation: hot repeated reads lead to Redis, which risks stale data, bounded by TTL and write-through.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["需求：热点反复读
延迟敏感"] --> C["选型：Redis 缓存"] C --> K["代价：可能读到旧数据"] K --> M["缓解：TTL + 写穿透"]

q: 把「为什么给信息流选 Cassandra」排成正确顺序：
steps: 选 Cassandra（无主宽列）
需求：写密集、超大规模、可最终一致
代价：没有 join，只能按分区键查
缓解：反范式，按查询设计表
why: 需求(写密集/大规模/最终一致) → 选型(Cassandra) → 代价(无 join) → 缓解(反范式建表)。决策链的形状和上一题一样。
why_en: Requirement of write-heavy massive scale with eventual consistency leads to Cassandra, whose lack of joins is mitigated by denormalizing tables per query.

scenario: 要在数十亿行历史数据上做分析报表：大范围聚合、按列扫描，不是逐行事务。
q: 最合适的存储是？
options: OLTP 的 PostgreSQL 主库
列式/数仓 (ClickHouse / BigQuery)
Redis
Neo4j
why: 大规模聚合扫描适合列式存储 + MPP（数仓），只读需要的列、并行扫描；行存的 OLTP 库做这个会很慢。
why_en: Large-scale aggregation scans suit columnar warehouses like ClickHouse or BigQuery, which read only needed columns in parallel, unlike a row-store OLTP database.
whenOtherWins: 数据量中等时，PostgreSQL 加物化视图或列存扩展也够，不必单独搭数仓。

scenario: 一个 OLTP 系统读多写少。读请求可以走缓存或读副本，但所有订单/评论写入仍必须提交到同一个关系型 primary。
q: 流量继续增长时，最先要警惕哪类上限？
options: 单 primary 的写吞吐上限
只读查询的副本扩展上限
SQL 语法本身的表达上限
客户端到数据库的网络带宽上限
options_en: The write-throughput ceiling of one primary.
The read-scaling ceiling of read replicas.
The expressiveness limit of SQL itself.
The network-bandwidth ceiling between clients and the database.
why: 面试锚点：单机关系库读约 50k+ QPS，简单写约 10k-20k TPS，实际取决于硬件和事务。读能靠缓存/副本分摊；写必须过 primary、WAL 刷盘、索引和锁，所以更早卡住。
why_en: Use 50k+ reads/s and 10-20k simple writes/s as rough anchors; writes bottleneck first because one primary must log, index, and commit them.
whenOtherWins: 如果写入很少、查询很复杂，读侧 CPU/IO 或缓存命中率可能先成为瓶颈。
tradeoff: 单主强一致写入 vs 水平写扩展
optionMeanings: 所有写入仍进入同一个 primary。
读流量被缓存或只读副本分摊。
把瓶颈误解为 SQL 能不能表达。
把瓶颈放到客户端到数据库的网络。
optionScenarioImpacts: 继续涨写入时，primary 的 CPU、WAL、索引和锁会顶住。
它描述读侧压力，不解释为什么写入排队。
SQL 表达力不决定单主能写多少。
网络可能卡，但本题没有说请求体巨大或链路饱和。
optionDirectness: 最直接；题干强调所有写都压在单主库。
不够直接；读副本不能分摊写提交。
不直接；语法不是吞吐瓶颈。
不直接；客户端网络不是当前约束。
optionMeanings_en: All writes still enter one primary database.
Read traffic is spread across cache or read replicas.
This mistakes the bottleneck for SQL expressiveness.
This puts the bottleneck on client-to-database networking.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: As writes grow, the primary's CPU, WAL, indexes, and locks become hot.
It describes read pressure, not why write commits queue up.
SQL expressiveness does not decide single-primary write capacity.
Network can matter, but the prompt does not say payloads or links are saturated.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: every write still goes through one primary.
Less direct: replicas help reads, not write commits.
Not direct: syntax is not the throughput bottleneck.
Not direct: client network is not the stated constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线事务处理：大量短事务读写用户状态的业务数据库负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OLTP means many short transactions that read and update live business state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库：负责接收写入并把变更复制给副本的数据库节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary is the database node that accepts writes and replicates changes to replicas.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预写日志：提交前先把变更记录刷到持久存储，用于崩溃恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records changes durably before data pages are treated as committed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，常用来估算读请求吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS means queries per second, often used for read throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒事务数，常用来估算写入或事务提交吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS means transactions per second, often used for write or commit throughput.

q: 经验数量级：关系型数据库按主键点查（有索引）大致多快返回？
options: ~1 微秒
个位数毫秒
why: 命中索引的主键点查通常个位数毫秒返回。用它估算「要不要加缓存」——缓存能把它压到亚毫秒。
why_en: An indexed primary-key lookup in a relational database typically returns in single-digit milliseconds.

q: 「宽列 (wide-column)」存储（如 Cassandra）最准确的理解是？
options: 像关系型一样固定表结构 + 跨表 join
按 row key 定位，每行可有大量、可不同的列，按 (分区键, 聚簇键) 组织
把整张表当一个 JSON 文档来存
纯内存 key→单值 的缓存
why: 宽列 = 每行由 row key 定位、行内可有成千上万且各行不必相同的列；数据按分区键分片、分区内按聚簇键排序。它不是「列很多的关系表」，而是「每行一个可扩展的有序列集合」。
why_en: A wide-column store addresses rows by a row key, where each row can hold many and possibly different columns, partitioned by a partition key and sorted by a clustering key.

q: 相比关系型的行存，Cassandra 宽列模型的关键取舍是？
options: 支持任意 join，但不能水平扩展
放弃 join / 多表事务，换来无主水平写扩展；要按查询预先建反范式表
强制固定 schema，写入更慢
只能存数字类型
why: 宽列库不做 join、也不擅长即席查询；你得提前知道查询模式、为每种查询建一张反范式表。换来的是无主、可线性扩展的写入和分区容错。
why_en: A wide-column store gives up joins and ad-hoc queries in exchange for masterless horizontally scalable writes, so you denormalize and design one table per query pattern.
whenOtherWins: 如果你需要 join、多表事务或即席分析，关系型或分布式 SQL 更合适——宽列是为「已知查询 + 海量写入」优化的。

scenario: 支付接口去重：同一 request_id 只处理一次，记录保留 24 小时后自动过期，且「判断是否存在 + 写入」必须原子完成。
q: 哪条 Redis 命令最适合做这个幂等标记？
options: SET req:{id} 1 EX 86400
SET req:{id} 1 NX EX 86400
SETEX req:{id} 86400 1
INCR req:{id}
why: NX = 仅当 key 不存在时才写入，用返回值就知道「是不是第一次」；EX 86400 顺带设 24h 过期。判断 + 写入一步原子完成，正是幂等标记要的。
why_en: Use SET with NX and EX so the write happens only when the key is absent and expires in 24 hours, giving an atomic idempotency guard.
codeSample:
# 原子：仅当不存在时写入 + 24h 过期
SET req:abc123 1 NX EX 86400
#  返回 OK  -> 首次请求，继续处理
#  返回 nil -> 重复请求，直接跳过

scenario: 游戏排行榜存在 Redis Sorted Set：member = 玩家，score = 分数。
q: 取「分数最高的前 10 名」（含分数）的命令是？
options: ZRANGE lb 0 9 WITHSCORES
ZREVRANGE lb 0 9 WITHSCORES
LRANGE lb 0 9
SORT lb LIMIT 0 10
why: ZSET 默认按分数升序；要「高分在前」用 ZREVRANGE 取倒序，0 9 表示前 10 名，WITHSCORES 连分数一起返回。
why_en: A sorted set is ascending by default, so use ZREVRANGE with WITHSCORES to read the top ten highest scores.
codeSample:
ZADD      lb 1500 alice       # 加/更新某玩家分数
ZREVRANGE lb 0 9 WITHSCORES   # 前 10 名，高 -> 低
ZREVRANK  lb alice            # 某玩家排名（0 起）

scenario: 用 Cassandra 存每个用户的信息流：按 user_id 查询，同一用户内按时间倒序取最近的帖子。
q: 哪个建表最匹配这个查询模式？
options: PRIMARY KEY (user_id, post_id)
PRIMARY KEY ((user_id), created_at) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (created_at DESC)
PRIMARY KEY (post_id)
PRIMARY KEY ((created_at), user_id)
why: 按查询建表：user_id 做分区键（按用户定位），created_at 做聚簇键并设 DESC，就能高效地「按用户取最近的帖子」。用时间做分区键会造成热分区。
why_en: Partition by user_id and cluster by created_at descending so reads fetch a user's most recent posts efficiently; partitioning by time would create hot partitions.

scenario: 商品搜索：用户输入可能有拼写错误，要按相关性返回标题匹配的商品。
q: 哪个 Elasticsearch 查询最合适？
options: { "term": { "title": "ipone" } }
{ "match": { "title": { "query": "ipone", "fuzziness": "AUTO" } } }
{ "wildcard": { "title": "*ipone*" } }
{ "ids": { "values": ["ipone"] } }
why: match 会过分析器并按相关性打分，加 fuzziness:AUTO 容忍拼写错误；term 是精确不分析，用 term 查「ipone」匹配不到「iphone」；wildcard 慢且不打分。
why_en: Use a match query with fuzziness AUTO so it analyzes the text, ranks by relevance, and tolerates typos, unlike an exact term query.

scenario: 面试官让你解释你如何驱动 AI agent 完成工程任务，而不是只问你用过哪些工具。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants you to explain how you drive an AI agent through engineering work, not just list which tools you've used.
q: 面试官问「你怎么用 AI/agent 工作」，最能拿分的回答核心是什么？
q_en: The interviewer asks how you work with AI/agents — what's the strongest core answer?
options: 把用过的 AI 工具按项目顺序逐一报一遍，讲清版本和特性
强调自己几乎全程手写代码，尽量少让 AI 插手关键逻辑
把 agent 当成要工程化驾驭的系统：讲清怎么喂上下文、定成功标准、防失败
强调 AI 很快会取代程序员，讨论这份工作还有没有必要存在
options_en: List every AI tool you've used, project by project, with versions and features.
Emphasize that you hand-write almost all the code and rarely let AI touch core logic.
Treat the agent as a system to engineer: how you feed context, define success, and guard against failure.
Emphasize that AI will soon replace programmers and question whether the job still matters.
why: 这题考工程化理解，不是工具清单：高分答案讲清怎么喂上下文、怎么定义成功(evals)、怎么防失败(failure modes)。
why_en: The strongest answer treats the agent as an engineered system: how you feed context, define success with evals, and prevent failure modes.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题明确是工具经验盘点，可以简短列工具，但仍要回到你如何控制质量和风险。
tradeoff: 工具清单的广度 vs 工程化驾驭的深度

scenario: 你要在白板上画出一个自主 agent 从接到任务到完成的完整运行链路。
scenario_en: You're sketching on a whiteboard how an autonomous agent runs end-to-end, from receiving a task to finishing it.
q: 一个自主 agent 的基本工作循环是什么？
q_en: What is the basic working loop of an autonomous agent?
options: 读取上下文、规划下一步、调用工具行动、观察结果，再对照成功标准判断是否收尾
把最终代码方案一次性生成，不做任何验证或修正就交付
只生成代码草稿，从来不真正执行，也不做任何验证
不断随机尝试各种可能操作，直到偶然凑巧碰对答案
options_en: Read context, plan the next step, act via a tool, observe the result, then check it against success criteria before looping again.
Generate the final code solution in one shot and ship it with no verification or correction.
Only draft code but never actually execute it or verify anything.
Keep randomly trying possible actions until one happens to work by luck.
why: agent = 在循环里运行的 LLM。工程发力点都在这个循环的每一步：上下文、工具、验证、终止条件。
why_en: An agent is an LLM in a loop: read context, plan, act via tools, observe, then verify against success criteria before looping again.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  P[读取上下文] --> PL[规划下一步]
  PL --> A[调用工具 行动]
  A --> O[观察结果]
  O --> V{达到成功标准?}
  V -->|否| PL
  V -->|是| D[完成]

scenario: 你要决定把一个任务做成固定 workflow，还是让模型自主规划、调用工具并迭代。
scenario_en: You must decide whether to build a task as a fixed workflow or let the model plan, call tools, and iterate on its own.
q: 该先用固定 workflow，还是该上能自主决策的 agent？
q_en: Should you use a fixed workflow, or an agent that decides autonomously?
options: 只要能用 agent 就用，它永远比固定 workflow 更好用
agent 不需要任何工具，也能独立完成整个工程任务
两者本质上没有区别，选哪个都不影响结果
复杂、高价值、模型能胜任、出错可恢复时才上 agent，否则用固定 workflow
options_en: Use an agent whenever you can — it's always better than a fixed workflow.
An agent can finish the whole engineering task without any tools at all.
The two are basically the same, so it doesn't matter which one you pick.
Only go agentic when the task is complex, high-value, the model can handle it, and errors are recoverable — otherwise use a fixed workflow.
why: 先用最简单的方案；workflow 是预定义路径，agent 让模型自决步骤。判断看四问：复杂度、价值、可行性、错误代价，任一为否就别上 agent。
why_en: Go agentic only when the task is complex, valuable, the model can handle it, and errors are recoverable — otherwise keep the predefined workflow.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务路径稳定、错误代价高，或规则就能覆盖，固定 workflow 更可控、更便宜。
tradeoff: agent 自主决策的灵活性 vs 固定 workflow 的可控与低成本

q: 该给 agent 补上什么，才能同时防死循环和防收尾过早？
q_en: What should you add to the agent to prevent both infinite loops and early stopping?
options: 定义明确可量化的完成标准，给循环清晰终止条件

why: 明确的完成标准把无限循环变成告警而不是天价账单；像给探员写任务书一样定义可量化的成功条件。
why_en: Explicit completion criteria turn a runaway loop into an alert instead of a runaway bill, by giving the agent a quantifiable definition of done.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务本来就简单、几步就能完事，加终止条件的工程成本可能不值得。
tradeoff: 可量化终止条件的确定性 vs 模型/工具/提示词调整的间接性

Misattributes the problem to having too many tools.
Misattributes the problem to not having enough prompt text.
optionScenarioImpacts: 同时防住死循环烧钱和收尾过早两种情况
换模型不会给循环加终止条件，问题依旧
没工具 agent 更难完成任务，无法解决终止问题
堆词不会给循环一个可量化的停止信号
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It guards against both a runaway loop and stopping too early.
Swapping models doesn't add a stop condition — the problem remains.
Without tools the agent struggles even more and the stop problem is unsolved.
Piling on words gives the loop no quantifiable stop signal.
optionDirectness: 循环没有清晰终止条件时最贴切
只有真正因为模型能力不足才答错时才适用
只有工具本身在制造无限循环时才沾边
只有提示词本身缺失必要信息时才有点用
optionDirectness_en: Fits best when the loop has no clear stop condition.
Fits only when the model's capability is genuinely the bottleneck.
Relevant only if the tools themselves are what's causing the infinite loop.
Only helps if the prompt is genuinely missing necessary information.

scenario: agent 的输出经常格式不对或编造字段，下游系统直接崩。
scenario_en: The agent's output is often malformed or has invented fields, and it crashes the downstream system.
q: 性价比最高的一道防线是什么？
q_en: What's the highest-ROI defense to add here?
options: 安排人工逐条检查所有输出
一旦报错就整体重启 agent 重来
忽略这个问题，反正大多数输出是对的
用 schema 校验输出格式，在进入下游前挡掉不合规内容
options_en: Have a human manually review every single output.
Restart the whole agent from scratch every time it errors.
Ignore the problem since most outputs are correct anyway.
Validate output against a schema and block noncompliant results before they hit downstream systems.
why: schema 校验是最高 ROI 的韧性手段之一：结构化输出符合机器可校验的格式，低成本挡掉大量幻觉/畸形输出。
why_en: Schema validation is one of the highest-ROI resilience patterns — machine-checkable structured output cheaply catches malformed or hallucinated results.
whenOtherWins: 如果输出格式本来就自由（如长文创作），schema 校验意义不大，更适合靠人工或 LLM judge 把关。
tradeoff: 机器可校验的低成本防线 vs 人工逐条检查的高成本保障

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述数据应有字段和类型的规范，用来机器校验输出是否合规。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema defines the expected fields and types of data, letting a machine check whether output is valid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型按预定义格式(如 JSON schema)产出结果，而不是自由文本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Structured output means the model produces results in a predefined format, such as JSON matching a schema, instead of free text.

optionMeanings: 靠人力逐条兜底校验
出错就整体重启，没有针对性校验
放任不管，赌大多数输出没问题
用机器可校验的格式规则挡在下游前面
optionMeanings_en: Relies on a human to check every item as a backstop.
Restarts everything on any error, with no targeted validation.
Does nothing and bets that most outputs are fine.
Uses a machine-checkable format rule as a gate before downstream systems.
optionScenarioImpacts: 能挡住错误，但人力成本随输出量线性增长
浪费已完成的工作，也不保证下次不再出错
少数错误一旦流入下游系统仍会崩溃
低成本挡住大量幻觉和畸形输出，规模化可行
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It catches errors, but labor cost grows linearly with output volume.
It wastes completed work and doesn't guarantee the next run avoids the error.
Even a few bad outputs reaching downstream systems still cause a crash.
It cheaply blocks most hallucinated or malformed output and scales well.
optionDirectness: 只有输出量很小、可以负担人工时才现实
只有重启成本极低、且错误随机不复现时才勉强适用
只有下游对错误完全容忍时才可能适用，通常不成立
输出量大、需要自动化把关时最贴切
optionDirectness_en: Realistic only when output volume is small enough for a human to keep up.
Barely works only when restarts are nearly free and errors are random, not systematic.
Only viable if downstream is fully tolerant of errors, which is rarely true.
Fits best when output volume is high and gating needs to be automated.

scenario: agent 感知不到你的代码库现状、运行环境和你的真实意图。
scenario_en: The agent can't perceive the current state of your codebase, its runtime environment, or your real intent.
q: 为了让它对齐，你要承担的核心工程任务是什么？
q_en: What's the core engineering task this creates, so the agent stays aligned?
options: 什么都不用管，相信模型自己能补全所有背景信息
做上下文工程：策划系统提示、精简工具、按需检索，给出精确规格和意图
把整个代码库一次性全部塞进上下文窗口喂给它
换成价格更贵、参数量更大的基础模型
options_en: Do nothing and trust the model to fill in all the missing background itself.
Do context engineering: curate the system prompt, trim tools, retrieve just-in-time, and give a precise spec and intent.
Dump the entire codebase into the context window all at once.
Switch to a more expensive base model with more parameters.
why: 上下文是有限资源，越长模型越容易走神(context rot)。要主动 curate：合适高度的提示、按需检索、必要时压缩。
why_en: Context is a finite resource — the longer it gets, the more the model drifts (context rot) — so you curate it deliberately instead of dumping everything in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上下文越长，模型准确率和专注度反而下降的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context rot is the phenomenon where a longer context window makes the model less accurate and less focused, not more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为 agent 主动策划提示、工具、检索和记忆，而不是被动塞入所有信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context engineering is deliberately curating an agent's prompt, tools, retrieval, and memory instead of passively dumping in everything.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在需要时才取相关信息，而不是提前把所有数据都放进上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Just-in-time retrieval fetches only the information needed at the moment, instead of loading everything into context upfront.

optionMeanings: 假设模型能凭空补全缺失的项目背景
主动为 agent 策划提示、工具、检索和压缩
把全部代码库不加筛选地塞进上下文
把问题误归因为模型参数不够大
optionMeanings_en: Assumes the model can conjure up missing project background on its own.
Proactively curates the agent's prompt, tools, retrieval, and compaction.
Stuffs the entire codebase into context without any curation.
Misattributes the problem to the model not being large enough.
optionScenarioImpacts: 模型会猜测代码库状态，输出经常文不对题
让 agent 拿到刚好够用、准确的背景信息
触发 context rot，模型反而更容易走神出错
换模型不会补上它本来就拿不到的项目背景
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The model guesses at the codebase state and output often misses the mark.
The agent gets background information that is accurate and just enough.
It triggers context rot, making the model more likely to drift and err.
Swapping models doesn't supply the project background it never had access to.
optionDirectness: 只有任务极简单、不依赖具体环境时才勉强成立
感知不到环境和意图这个约束下最贴切
只有代码库极小、完全装得下时才可能不出问题
只有原模型确实能力不足时才是正确方向
optionDirectness_en: Barely holds only for extremely simple tasks that don't depend on the environment.
Fits best given the constraint that the agent can't perceive environment or intent on its own.
Only safe when the codebase is tiny enough to fit entirely.
Only the right move when the original model's capability is genuinely the bottleneck.

scenario: 你在给一个处理退款的 agent 写评估脚本，要决定主要给什么打分。
scenario_en: You're writing an eval script for a refund-processing agent and deciding what to grade primarily.
q: 评估 agent 时，应该主要给什么打分？
q_en: When evaluating an agent, what should you primarily grade?
options: 严格规定并检查它走的每一步操作路径
它一共调用了多少次工具、耗费多少 token
它最终达成的结果状态，路径(trajectory)只用来调试
它的回复措辞是否得体、风格是否讨喜
options_en: Strictly define and check every step of the path it takes.
How many tool calls it made and how many tokens it burned.
The final outcome it achieves — use the trajectory only to debug why.
Whether its wording is polite and its tone is likeable.
why: outcome(如「退款真落库了吗」)是客观达成证据；trajectory 只用来调试为什么。原则是主要给结果打分，别过度规定路径。
why_en: Grade the outcome, the final state such as whether the refund landed, and use the trajectory only to debug why it happened.
whenOtherWins: 如果需要审计安全合规或调试反复失败的用例，trajectory 检查同样必不可少。
tradeoff: 结果导向的评分客观性 vs 路径规定的可解释性/可调试性

rows: 判断任务是否真的完成
调试为什么失败或低效

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务执行后达成的最终状态，是否客观完成目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Outcome is the final state after execution — whether the goal was objectively achieved.

termDefinitions.meaning: agent 为完成任务走过的具体步骤、工具调用和推理过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Trajectory is the specific sequence of steps, tool calls, and reasoning an agent takes to complete a task.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型处理文本的最小计量单位，调用成本通常按 token 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the basic unit of text a model processes, and usage cost is typically billed per token.

optionMeanings: 把路径本身当成评分标准
把资源消耗量当成评分标准
把最终达成状态当成评分标准，路径只做调试
把语言风格当成评分标准
optionMeanings_en: Treats the path itself as the scoring criterion.
Treats resource consumption as the scoring criterion.
Treats the final achieved state as the score, using the path only for debugging.
Treats language style as the scoring criterion.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会惩罚 agent 找到的、你没预料到的有效解法
调用次数和 token 量说明不了任务是否真的完成
既不束缚 agent 找新解法，又能在失败时回查原因
退款有没有真正落库，跟措辞讨不讨喜无关
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It penalizes valid solutions the agent finds that you didn't anticipate.
Call count and token usage don't tell you whether the task was actually completed.
It doesn't constrain the agent's creativity yet still lets you trace failures.
Whether the refund actually landed has nothing to do with how likeable the wording is.
optionDirectness: 只有路径本身有强合规要求(如审计)时才该这样评
只有优化成本本身是目标时才该主要看这个
评估「任务是否真的完成」这个目标时最贴切
只有面向用户的语气确实是评估目标时才适用
optionDirectness_en: Should be graded this way only when the path itself has strict compliance requirements.
Worth grading mainly on this only when cost optimization itself is the goal.
Fits best when the goal is judging whether the task was truly completed.
Applies only when user-facing tone is itself the thing being evaluated.

scenario: 你要给一个多步骤 agent 建评估集，需要选合适的打分方式组合。
scenario_en: You're building an eval set for a multi-step agent and need to pick the right mix of graders.
q: code / LLM-judge / human 三种评分器该怎么组合使用？
q_en: How should you combine code-based, LLM-judge, and human graders?
options: code 查客观结果，LLM judge 打主观维度，定期人工校准
只用人工评分最稳妥、别的都不需要
只用 LLM 打分，不需要代码检查或人工介入
评分标准不重要，随便打个分数就行
options_en: Code checks objective outcomes, LLM-judge grades subjective dimensions, humans calibrate periodically.
Only use human review — nothing else is needed.
Only use an LLM to score — no code checks or human review needed.
The grading rubric doesn't matter much — any rough score works.
why: 有效评估通常组合：确定性 code 检查客观结果 + LLM rubric 打主观维度 + 定期人工校准，评估集从真实失败里攒。
why_en: Effective evals combine deterministic code checks for objective outcomes, an LLM rubric for subjective dimensions, and periodic human calibration.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务极简单、结果二元可判，单用 code 检查就够，不必上 LLM judge。
tradeoff: 自动化评分的速度与规模 vs 人工评分的准确与信任度

termDefinitions.meaning: 用另一个大模型按 rubric 给 agent 输出打分的评估方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM-as-judge uses another large language model to score an agent's output against a rubric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述评分维度和标准的打分细则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rubric is the set of criteria and standards used to score an output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一批用来系统检验 agent 表现的任务样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An eval set is a batch of task samples used to systematically check an agent's performance.

optionMeanings: 三种评分器按各自强项组合使用
只信任人工评分
只信任 LLM judge 单一评分器
认为评分标准不重要
optionMeanings_en: Combines all three graders, each used for its own strength.
Trusts only human grading and nothing else.
Trusts only a single LLM-judge grader.
Assumes the grading rubric doesn't really matter.
optionScenarioImpacts: 客观结果、主观维度、人工校准三层都覆盖到
人工成本高、难规模化，覆盖不了大量任务
LLM judge 本身非确定性，缺了客观核对和人工校准
评分不一致，无法真实反映 agent 是否变好
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It covers objective outcomes, subjective dimensions, and human calibration all at once.
Human review is expensive and doesn't scale to cover a large task volume.
LLM-judge is itself non-deterministic and lacks objective checks and human calibration.
Inconsistent scoring can't reliably show whether the agent is actually improving.
optionDirectness: 多步骤、既有客观又有主观维度时最贴切
只有任务量极小、结果高风险时单靠人工才现实
只有任务纯主观、允许一定噪声时才可能够用
几乎不成立，任何评估都需要明确标准
optionDirectness_en: Fits best for multi-step tasks that have both objective and subjective dimensions.
Realistic only when task volume is tiny and the stakes are very high.
May be enough only for purely subjective tasks that tolerate some noise.
Almost never valid — any evaluation needs a clear standard.

scenario: 你在给一个『帮用户填退款表单』的 agent 定评估指标，要求每次交互都必须成功，不能偶尔失败。
scenario_en: You're defining an eval metric for an agent that fills out refund forms, and every single interaction must succeed — occasional failure is not acceptable.
q: 面向用户、要求「每次都稳」的场景，该看哪个指标？
q_en: For a user-facing case that must succeed every single time, which metric should you use?
options: pass@k：k 次里至少 1 次成功
只看单次调用的成功率
只看平均响应延迟
pass^k：k 次必须全部成功
options_en: pass@k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
Just look at the single-call success rate.
Just look at average response latency.
pass^k: all k tries must succeed.
why: pass@k=1-(1-p)^k(至少1次成功)，pass^k=p^k(全部成功)。次次要稳就看 pass^k：p=99%时10步全稳概率仅约90%，逼你把单次成功率顶到99.9%+。
why_en: pass@k means at least one success in k tries; pass^k means all k succeed. User-facing reliability needs pass^k, since 99% per step compounds to ~90% over 10 steps.

termDefinitions.meaning: k 次尝试里至少成功一次的概率/指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pass@k measures the probability that at least one of k attempts succeeds.

termDefinitions.meaning: k 次尝试全部成功的概率/指标，等于单次成功率的 k 次方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pass^k measures the probability that all k attempts succeed, equal to the single-run success rate raised to the k-th power.

scenario: AI 编码面试刚开始，你被放进一个已有多文件项目，类、模型和业务逻辑都已经存在。
scenario_en: At the start of an AI coding interview, you are dropped into an existing multi-file project with classes, models, and business logic already in place.
q: 面对陌生代码库，最先应该做什么？
q_en: What should you do first when facing an unfamiliar codebase?
options: 马上让 AI 根据题目生成完整实现
先重构目录结构，让代码更符合你的习惯
先快速建立代码库地图，再决定怎么提示 AI
只读 README，不打开源码
why: 已有项目里最容易踩的坑是改到现有模式之外；先扫入口、模型和状态流建地图，提示才会贴合代码库。代价是多花几分钟阅读，但能省下返工。
why_en: Orient yourself first so your prompts fit the entry points, models, and state flow that already exist, instead of drifting from established patterns.
whenOtherWins: 如果是完全空白的开放式题目，可以更快进入建模和实现，但仍要先读清需求边界。
tradeoff: 先建心智地图 vs 直接提示 AI 生成
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Task[New repo] --> Read[Read structure]
  Read --> Map[Mental map]
  Map --> Plan[Plan change]
  Plan --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
options_en: Ask the AI to generate a full implementation right away.
Refactor the directory structure to match your own habits first.
Quickly build a mental map of the codebase, then decide how to prompt the AI.
Only read the README and never open the source files.
optionMeanings: 跳过阅读，把需求直接丢给 AI 生成代码
还没搞懂用途就先按个人习惯重排目录
先扫入口、模型、接口和状态，建立心智地图
只看文档摘要，完全不打开源码文件
optionScenarioImpacts: 提示词会踩中未知的既有模式，生成代码容易和代码库冲突
破坏现有约定，还可能引入无关的改动风险
提示会贴合真实入口和状态，减少后续返工
README 通常滞后于代码，看不到真实类和调用关系
optionDirectness: 空白原型且没有既有接口时，快速生成可当探索稿
目录确实混乱且需求允许重构时，重排应放在理解之后
已有代码有模式和状态流时，先建地图再写提示
README 可当入口线索，但不能覆盖真实调用路径
optionMeanings_en: Skip reading and hand the requirement straight to the AI.
Reorganize folders to your own taste before you understand them.
Scan entry points, models, interfaces, and state to build a mental map.
Only skim the README summary and never open the source files.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Prompts will hit unknown existing patterns and clash with the codebase.
It breaks existing conventions and adds unrelated change risk.
Prompts stay grounded in real entry points and state, cutting rework.
READMEs usually lag the code, so real classes and calls stay hidden.
optionDirectness_en: Fast generation can work as an exploration draft only in a blank prototype.
If the tree is truly messy, refactor only after you understand it.
When existing patterns and state flow matter, map first and prompt second.
A README is a useful entry clue, but it cannot replace tracing real calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 项目根目录下介绍用途和用法的说明文件，内容常滞后于实际代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A README is the top-level file that explains a project's purpose, and it often lags behind the actual code.

q: 跳过代码库阅读、直接提示 AI，最容易给面试官什么信号？
q_en: If you skip codebase reading and prompt the AI right away, what signal are you most likely sending the interviewer?
options: 你会在不了解系统时就开始改代码
你很会节省时间
你已经掌握了所有业务约束
你不需要验证 AI 输出
why: 面试官会把这种行为映射到真实团队协作：没弄懂系统就动手，后续决策也更容易偏离现有设计。代价是这类信号会直接拉低候选人评价。
why_en: Skipping orientation signals you might change unfamiliar production code before understanding it, which lowers how interviewers rate you.
options_en: You might start changing a system before you understand it.
You're good at saving time.
You already grasp all the business constraints.
You don't need to verify AI output.
optionMeanings: 把跳过阅读映射成未来会不了解系统就动手改代码
把跳过阅读的行为包装成效率优势
假设几分钟内就已经吸收了全部业务约束
假设跳过阅读后也不用检查 AI 生成的内容
optionScenarioImpacts: 这正是面试官在真实团队场景里最担心的行为模式
面试官不会把跳步骤读成效率，反而读成风险信号
几分钟内不可能吃透所有约束，这个假设不成立
跳过阅读和跳过验证是两件不同的事，此项文不对题
optionDirectness: 未读代码就动手改时，这个团队协作风险最明显
已掌握边界后省略低价值步骤，才会被读成效率
只有长期维护者才可能已知全部约束，新面试场景不适用
验证 AI 输出是后续环节，不能解释跳过取向的信号
optionMeanings_en: Map skipping reading to changing a system before understanding it.
Frame skipping reading as an efficiency win.
Assume all business constraints are already absorbed in minutes.
Assume AI output no longer needs verification either.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This is exactly the team-risk behavior interviewers watch for.
Interviewers read this as risk, not efficiency.
No one absorbs every constraint in minutes; the assumption fails.
Skipping reading and skipping verification are separate issues.
optionDirectness_en: This team-risk signal is strongest when you change code before reading it.
Skipping steps reads as efficiency only after the boundaries are clear.
Only a long-time maintainer could already know every constraint.
AI verification is a later step; it does not explain skipping orientation.

q: 把快速建立代码库心智地图的顺序排好：
q_en: Put the quick codebase orientation steps in order:
steps: 追踪数据如何流过关键类和方法
找到执行入口或请求入口
确认公共接口、状态归属和测试
先看目录结构，判断项目的大致组织方式
why: 先看整体组织，再找入口并顺着数据流深入，最后确认接口、状态和测试，能用最少时间抓住代码库骨架。
why_en: A strong orientation moves from structure to entry point to data flow, then checks interfaces, state ownership, and tests.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Tree[Project tree] --> Entry[Entry points]
  Entry --> Core[Core logic]
  Core --> Data[Data models]
  Data --> Tests[Tests]

q: 阅读陌生项目时，为什么入口点通常是第一批要找的代码？
q_en: When reading an unfamiliar project, why are entry points usually among the first code to find?
options: 入口点里一定包含全部业务逻辑
入口点通常是全库最短、读起来最快的文件
入口点能够替代阅读测试用例
入口点标出执行起点和请求/命令进入系统的方式
why: 入口点能让你沿真实调用路径追踪对象创建和方法调用，而不是孤立读文件；代价是复杂系统里入口可能不止一个。
why_en: The entry point shows where execution begins so you can trace real calls instead of reading files in isolation.
options_en: The entry point always contains all the business logic.
The entry point is usually the shortest file in the repo, so it's the fastest read.
The entry point can replace reading the test suite.
The entry point marks where execution starts and how requests or commands enter the system.
optionMeanings: 假设入口文件本身装下了全部业务逻辑
把入口点的价值错误归因为文件短小
假设入口点能替代对预期行为的验证
把入口点定义为执行起点和外部请求进入系统的位置
optionScenarioImpacts: 真实系统里业务逻辑通常分散在多个类里，这个假设会让你漏读
文件长短和是否值得优先读没有必然关系
跳过测试会让你错过一份现成的行为说明书
顺着入口能看到对象怎么被创建、方法怎么被调用
optionDirectness: 入口文件适合当起点，不适合当全量业务说明
短文件可先读，但长度不是判断入口价值的主因
测试适合确认行为，不能替代入口处的调用路径
需要顺调用链建图时，入口点是最合适的起点
optionMeanings_en: Assume the entry file itself contains all business logic.
Misattribute the entry point's value to being a short file.
Assume the entry point can substitute for checking expected behavior.
Define the entry point as where execution starts and requests enter the system.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Real systems spread logic across many classes, so this assumption misses code.
File length has no real link to whether it's worth reading first.
Skipping tests means missing a ready-made behavior spec.
Following it shows what gets instantiated and which methods get called.
optionDirectness_en: An entry file is a starting point, not a complete business spec.
A short file may be easy to read, but length is not the reason.
Tests confirm behavior, but they do not replace the entry call path.
When you need a call-chain map, the entry point is the best start.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序或服务开始执行的位置，比如 main 函数或 HTTP 请求处理器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The entry point is where a program or service begins executing, such as a main function or an HTTP request handler.

q: 哪些位置通常是陌生代码库里的高价值“代码指针”？（多选）
q_en: Which places are usually high-value code pointers in an unfamiliar codebase? (Select all that apply.)
options: 请求处理器、main 函数或 CLI 入口
承载核心业务逻辑的复杂函数
核心数据模型和类层级
随机挑一个样式文件从头读到尾
why: 入口、核心函数和数据模型能解释系统怎么启动、做什么、数据长什么样；随机文件通常解锁不了全局理解。
why_en: Entry points, core functions, and data models reveal how the system starts, what it does, and how data is shaped, far more than a random file.
options_en: Request handlers, the main function, or the CLI entry point.
The complex function that carries the core business logic.
Core data models and the class hierarchy.
Pick a random stylesheet file and read it start to end.
optionMeanings: 入口处理器/main/CLI 是外部请求或命令进入系统的位置
复杂核心函数是其他代码都在围绕的那个中心
数据模型和类层级定义对象关系和不变量
随便挑一个样式文件，和系统行为基本无关
optionScenarioImpacts: 顺着它能看到请求怎么被处理、调用了哪些组件
读懂它比读十几个简单辅助文件更快建立系统直觉
理解对象关系后，很多后续 bug 能提前避免
样式文件通常不影响业务逻辑，读了也解锁不了全局
optionDirectness: 要找请求从哪里进来时，入口是第一层线索
业务结果由少数复杂函数决定时，先读它收益高
修改依赖对象关系时，模型和类层级必须先看
只有 UI 样式任务才优先读样式文件；取向阶段不是
optionMeanings_en: Request handlers/main/CLI are where external calls enter the system.
The complex core function is the center everything else revolves around.
Data models and the class hierarchy define object relationships and invariants.
A random stylesheet file, mostly unrelated to system behavior.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Following it shows how requests get handled and which components get called.
Reading it builds system intuition faster than a dozen small helper files.
Understanding relationships here prevents many later bugs.
Stylesheets rarely affect business logic, so it won't unlock the big picture.
optionDirectness_en: Use this first when you need to find where requests enter.
Use this early when a few complex functions drive the business result.
Read this first when the change depends on object relationships.
Stylesheets come first only for UI styling tasks, not orientation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过终端命令与程序交互的入口方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CLI is a command-line interface where you interact with a program via terminal commands.

q: 补全入口点阅读目标：
q_en: Complete the goal of reading an entry point:
text: 找到入口点后，要顺着它看清哪些{{类被实例化}}、哪些{{方法被调用}}，以及组件之间如何{{交接工作}}。
why: 入口点的价值不只是“文件在哪”，而是让你沿真实执行路径理解系统组织。
why_en: An entry point matters because it reveals instantiation, method calls, and handoffs along the real execution path.

q: 相比读十几个简单辅助文件，优先读“硬核心”函数的主要收益是？
q_en: Compared with reading a dozen simple helper files, what is the main benefit of reading the hard core function first?
options: 它一定没有 bug
它通常能说明系统真正的输入、输出和业务工作流
它能让你避免阅读数据模型
它通常由 AI 自动生成
why: 核心函数往往是其他代码围绕的中心；理解它的调用方式、输入和输出，能比读一堆辅助文件更快建立系统直觉。
why_en: The core function often reveals the real inputs, outputs, and workflow that the rest of the code supports.
tradeoff: 读核心函数快速建直觉 vs 读大量辅助文件覆盖细节
options_en: It is guaranteed to be bug-free.
It usually reveals the system's real inputs, outputs, and business workflow.
It lets you skip reading the data models.
It is usually AI-generated.
optionMeanings: 把优先阅读的理由归因到代码质量保证
把核心函数的价值归因到它浓缩了系统的真实行为
把优先阅读核心函数当成跳过数据模型的理由
把优先阅读的理由归因到代码的生成方式
optionScenarioImpacts: 核心函数一样可能有 bug，这不是优先读它的理由
读懂输入输出和工作流后，后续提示 AI 会更精准
数据模型仍然要读，核心函数不能替代它
生成方式和是否值得优先读没有因果关系
optionDirectness: 任何复杂代码都可能有 bug，核心函数不提供正确性保证
要快速掌握主工作流时，核心函数最值得先读
数据模型决定输入形状，读核心函数后仍要回到模型
代码来源只在判断生成质量时有用，不解释阅读顺序
optionMeanings_en: Attribute the reason to a guarantee of code quality.
Attribute the core function's value to concentrating real system behavior.
Treat reading the core function as a substitute for the data models.
Attribute the reason to how the code was generated.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The core function can still have bugs; that's not why you read it first.
Understanding I/O and workflow makes later AI prompts more precise.
You still need the data models; the core function can't replace them.
How code was generated has no bearing on whether it's worth reading first.
optionDirectness_en: Complex code can still have bugs; the core function gives no guarantee.
Read it first when you need the main workflow quickly.
Data models still define input shape, even after you read the core path.
Code origin helps judge generated quality, not reading order.

scenario: 你在游戏项目中看到 `Game` 持有 `Board`，`Board` 里有 `Cell`，每个 `Cell` 记录状态和邻居。
scenario_en: In a game project, `Game` owns a `Board`; the `Board` contains `Cell`s, and each `Cell` tracks state and neighbors.
q: 接下来最有价值的理解重点是什么？
q_en: What is the most valuable thing to understand next?
options: 画清核心对象之间的关系和数据如何流动
先忽略模型，直接让 AI 写搜索算法
把所有类合并成一个文件
只看 UI 渲染代码
why: 数据模型定义了后续逻辑的边界，很多 bug 都来自误解对象关系或数据形状；代价是花几分钟画关系图，换来更少的返工。
why_en: Core object relationships define the boundaries for later logic, and many bugs come from misunderstanding the data shape.
whenOtherWins: 如果项目确实是单函数算法题且没有持久模型，模型映射可以很轻，但仍要确认输入输出结构。
tradeoff: 先画清对象关系 vs 直接跳到算法实现
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Models[Data models] --> State[State shape]
  State --> Invariants[Invariants]
  Invariants --> SafeChange[Safer change]
options_en: Map out how the core objects relate and how data flows between them.
Ignore the model and have the AI write the search algorithm right away.
Merge all the classes into a single file.
Only look at the UI rendering code.
optionMeanings: 梳理 Game/Board/Cell 之间的持有和数据流关系
跳过对象关系，直接把搜索逻辑交给 AI
把清晰的类边界压缩成一个大文件
只关注展示层，忽略状态和数据结构
optionScenarioImpacts: 理解清楚后，后续提示 AI 时能准确描述数据结构
AI 不清楚 Cell 的状态和邻居结构，容易写错搜索逻辑
合并类会丢掉原本的职责边界，让改动更难追踪
UI 代码看不到 Board/Cell 的状态和邻居关系
optionDirectness: 对象关系会影响算法提示时，先画关系图最稳
只有数据结构已经明确时，才适合直接进入算法提示
只有无职责边界的小脚本，合并文件才可能不伤结构
UI 调整任务才优先读渲染层；本题核心在状态模型
optionMeanings_en: Map out how Game, Board, and Cell hold each other and how data flows.
Skip object relationships and hand the search logic straight to the AI.
Compress clear class boundaries into one large file.
Focus only on the presentation layer and ignore state and data structure.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Once it's clear, later prompts can describe the data structure precisely.
The AI doesn't know Cell's state and neighbor shape, so search logic goes wrong.
Merging classes erases the original responsibility boundaries, making changes harder to track.
UI code never reveals Board or Cell's state and neighbor relationships.
optionDirectness_en: Map relationships first when they affect the algorithm prompt.
Jump to the algorithm only after the data structure is clear.
Merging files is safe only for tiny scripts with no real boundaries.
Read rendering first for UI changes; this task is about state models.

q: 补全数据模型的常见风险链：
q_en: Complete the common risk chain around data models:
text: 如果误解数据模型，后续 bug 往往来自错误判断数据的{{形状}}、{{归属}}和{{流向}}。
why: 实现逻辑时你会不断依赖这些假设，一开始错了，AI 生成的代码也会跟着错。
why_en: Wrong assumptions about data shape, ownership, and flow propagate into the code the AI generates.

scenario: 你想在几秒内看完整个项目有哪些文件，用文件名和目录先判断 MVC、分层或按功能模块组织。
scenario_en: You want to see all project files in seconds and use names and folders to infer MVC, layering, or feature-based organization.

git commit -am orient
find . -type f

why_en: Listing files first quickly exposes the project's organization so you can choose which entry points and models to inspect next.
whenOtherWins: 如果环境有更快更清晰的工具，比如 `rg --files` 或 IDE 文件树，也可以用它达到同样目的。
tradeoff: 先看文件全貌 vs 直接打开某个文件深入
codeSample:
find . -type f
# 观察目录和文件名：models/controllers/views、layers、features、tests 等

Make a git commit with the message "orient".

Delete the node_modules dependency folder.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It shows test results, not the directory structure or file layout.
Committing before making any change has nothing to do with mapping structure.

optionDirectness_en: Tests build a behavior baseline; they do not replace a file-layout scan.
Commits come after an explainable change, not during orientation.
Use recursive listing when you need the whole file layout quickly.
Delete dependencies only to fix install pollution, never to orient.

termDefinitions.meaning: Unix 命令，用来按条件递归列出文件系统里的文件和目录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: find is a Unix command that recursively lists files and directories matching given criteria.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把代码分成模型、视图、控制器三层的经典架构模式。

Structure is most useful when deciding which layer should take new code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把代码分成模型、视图、控制器三层的经典架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVC is a classic architecture that splits code into Model, View, and Controller layers.

q_en: What is the best reaction to this suggestion?
options: 接受建议，因为 AI 生成速度快
按现有 repository 模式重定向 AI
删除 repository 层，减少文件数量

q: 为什么要特别扫描关键类的 public 和 private 边界？
q_en: Why should you scan the public and private boundary of key classes?
options: 这样可以绕过封装直接改内部数组
private 字段通常比 public 方法更可靠
能知道 AI 该调用哪些公开方法，别碰内部实现
public/private 对面试没有意义
why: 公共接口是类对外承诺的使用方式，把 AI 指向这些接口能减少破坏封装和碰内部状态的风险；代价是要先花时间把接口读全。
why_en: Public interfaces show how classes are meant to be used, keeping the AI from reaching into internals it shouldn't touch.
tradeoff: 遵守公开接口边界 vs 图方便直接碰内部字段
options_en: So you can bypass encapsulation and edit the internal array directly.
Private fields are usually more reliable than public methods.
So you know which public methods the AI should call instead of touching internals.
Public/private boundaries don't matter for the interview.
optionMeanings: 把扫描边界的目的说反，当成绕过封装的手段
把可靠性错误归因到字段是否私有
把扫描边界的目的定义为找到该用的公开方法
否认 public/private 边界在面试里有价值
optionScenarioImpacts: 绕过封装会让改动脱离类原本的约束，容易引入 bug
可靠性取决于实现质量，和是否私有没有必然关系
AI 会被限定在安全的公开方法上，不去碰内部状态
面试官恰恰会通过这一点判断你是否尊重封装
optionDirectness: 绕过封装只适合临时调试观察，不适合提交代码
private 字段适合保护内部状态，不代表更可靠
需要让 AI 调用类时，先找 public 方法边界
小脚本可能没有封装边界；类设计题里必须尊重它
optionMeanings_en: Reverses the purpose, treating the scan as a way to bypass encapsulation.
Wrongly attributes reliability to whether a field is private.
Defines the purpose as finding the public methods that should be used.
Denies that the public/private boundary has any interview value.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Bypassing encapsulation pulls changes outside the class's own constraints, inviting bugs.
Reliability depends on implementation quality, not on whether a field is private.
It keeps the AI confined to safe public methods instead of touching internal state.
This is exactly the kind of signal interviewers use to judge your respect for encapsulation.
optionDirectness_en: Bypass internals only for temporary debugging, not committed code.
Private fields protect internal state; they are not automatically more reliable.
Before asking AI to call a class, find the public method boundary.
Tiny scripts may lack boundaries, but class design questions require them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把对象内部状态隐藏起来，只通过公开方法暴露该暴露的行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation hides an object's internal state and exposes only the behavior meant to be public.

scenario: `Deck` 类已有 `getCards()`，内部 `cards` 数组不是公开接口；AI 生成代码直接访问 `deck.cards`。
scenario_en: The `Deck` class already has `getCards()`, and its internal `cards` array is not a public interface; the AI generated code reads `deck.cards` directly.
q: 该怎么纠正这段 AI 生成的代码？
q_en: How should you correct this AI-generated code?
options: 保留直接访问，因为更短
把 `cards` 改成全局变量
删除 `getCards()`
改用 `getCards()`，并说明接口边界
why: 使用公开方法能尊重封装，也让代码贴合项目原本的对象边界；代价是要多说一句提示词，明确该走哪个接口。
why_en: Use the public method because it preserves encapsulation and matches the class's intended boundary.
whenOtherWins: 如果公开接口确实缺失能力，可以先设计一个小的接口扩展，而不是随手穿透内部字段。
tradeoff: 尊重封装走 getCards() vs 图省事直接读内部数组
options_en: Keep the direct access because it's shorter.
Turn `cards` into a global variable.
Delete `getCards()` entirely.
Switch to `getCards()` and state the interface boundary in the prompt.
optionMeanings: 为了少打几个字符而接受破坏封装
把私有数组升级成全局可见的状态
移除原本安全的公开访问入口
把访问方式纠正回类已经暴露的公开方法
optionScenarioImpacts: 以后 Deck 内部一改结构，这处代码就会跟着炸
全局变量会让状态被任何地方随意修改，风险更大
删除接口后调用方彻底失去安全访问 cards 的方式
封装边界保持不变，未来改内部实现不影响调用方
optionDirectness: 临时代码里短访问也许能跑，但长期会绑死内部结构
全局状态只适合少数配置常量，不能替代对象字段
删除访问器只在接口确实错误时考虑，本题相反
已有访问器覆盖需求时，应改回公开方法
optionMeanings_en: Accept broken encapsulation to save a few keystrokes.
Promote the private array into globally visible state.
Remove the safe public access point entirely.
Correct the access back to the method the class already exposes.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The moment Deck's internals change, this code breaks.
A global variable lets state be mutated from anywhere, raising the risk.
Callers lose any safe way to access cards at all.
The encapsulation boundary stays intact, so future internal changes don't ripple out.
optionDirectness_en: Short direct access may run temporarily, but it ties callers to internals.
Global state fits a few constants, not a class's owned field.
Delete an accessor only when the interface itself is wrong.
When an accessor covers the need, switch back to the public method.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把对象内部状态隐藏起来，只通过公开方法暴露该暴露的行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation hides an object's internal state and exposes only the behavior meant to be public.

q: 补全状态管理阅读目标：
q_en: Complete the goal of reading state management:
text: 读状态管理时，要确认状态存在哪里、如何{{变化}}，以及系统是否有{{单一事实源}}。
why: 状态归属决定副作用在哪里发生，也决定你排查 bug 时应该从哪里开始。
why_en: State ownership tells you where side effects happen and where bugs are likely to hide.

q: 如果同一份状态散落在多个对象里，最需要警惕什么？
q_en: If the same state is scattered across multiple objects, what should you watch for most?
options: 不同副本可能悄悄不同步，让 bug 难定位
代码一定运行得更快
测试数量会自动减少变少
AI 一定能自动修复同步

why_en: Distributed state requires clear synchronization rules, or the AI may update one copy and silently miss another.
options_en: Copies can quietly drift, making bugs hard to trace.
The code is guaranteed to run faster.
The number of tests automatically shrinks.
The AI is guaranteed to auto-fix the sync.
optionMeanings: 把状态分散的风险定义为副本不同步
把状态分散和运行性能划等号
把状态分散和测试数量挂钩
假设 AI 能自动发现并修复同步问题
optionScenarioImpacts: 改了一处、漏了另一处，bug 会出现在意想不到的地方
分散状态本身不影响运行速度，这个归因不成立
状态分散和测试数量没有必然的因果关系
AI 看不到隐藏的同步规则，不会自动补全
optionDirectness: 多副本状态最常见的问题就是更新漏同步
性能优化要看读写路径和数据结构，状态分散本身不保证
测试数量由风险和行为面决定，不会因状态分散自动减少
AI 只有看到明确同步规则时，才可能帮你维护一致性
optionMeanings_en: Define the risk of distributed state as copies drifting out of sync.
Equate distributed state with better runtime performance.
Link distributed state to a shrinking test count.
Assume the AI will automatically find and fix sync issues.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Update one copy, miss another, and bugs surface in unexpected places.
Distributed state doesn't itself affect speed, so this attribution fails.
Distributed state has no causal link to test count.
The AI can't see the hidden sync rules, so it won't fill the gap on its own.
optionDirectness_en: The common multi-copy failure is missing one update path.
Performance depends on read/write paths and data structures, not spread alone.
Test count follows risk and behavior surface, not state placement by itself.
AI can preserve consistency only when the sync rule is explicit.

q: 为什么已有测试是很好的代码库说明文档？
q_en: Why are existing tests good documentation for a codebase?
options: 测试只对 CI 有用，面试里不用看
测试通常展示系统被期望如何使用和返回什么结果
测试一定覆盖所有边界条件
测试能替代对实现的理解
why: 测试把期望行为具体化，还给你一个验证理解和修改是否破坏现有行为的入口；代价是有些测试可能过时或覆盖不全。
why_en: Existing tests document expected behavior and give you a concrete way to verify your understanding.

flowchart LR

  Tests --> Boundaries[Edge cases]

假设测试天然就有完整的边界覆盖
把读测试当成理解实现的替代品

很多项目测试覆盖并不完整，这个假设会误导判断
测试展示行为，但不展示为什么这样实现

覆盖率高的项目才可多信边界用例，不能默认全覆盖
测试能说明行为，具体实现仍要回源码确认

Define tests as a spec for expected behavior and return values.
Assume tests naturally have complete edge-case coverage.
Treat reading tests as a substitute for understanding the implementation.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Skipping tests in an interview means missing a ready-made behavior spec.
Reading tests quickly shows expected input/output without guessing.
Many projects have incomplete coverage, so this assumption misleads.
Tests show behavior but not why it's implemented that way.
optionDirectness_en: Looking at tests only through CI misses example usage.
Tests are fast evidence when you need expected behavior.
Trust edge coverage only when the project actually has high coverage.
Tests explain behavior; implementation details still require source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次提交代码后自动运行构建和测试的流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CI, continuous integration, automatically builds and tests code on every commit.

q: 刚进项目时运行已有测试，如果测试已经失败，最合理的解读是？

可能就是题目要你修的已知问题
说明测试完全没有价值

why_en: Pre-existing failing tests are context you should account for; they might be the very bug you are expected to fix.

It means tests have no value at all.

把失败测试当成噪音，直接删掉了事

把个别失败测试推广成测试整体没有价值

scenario: 环境允许断点调试，你还不确定真实运行时对象长什么样。

更快看到真实数据形状和执行路径

why_en: A debugger quickly shows real runtime data shapes and execution paths, validating what you inferred from reading.

options_en: It writes all the code for you automatically.

It shows real data shapes and execution paths faster than reading cold.
optionMeanings: 把 debugger 的作用夸大成自动写代码

Narrating to the interviewer and debugging are separate activities.
At the breakpoint you see real values directly, more accurate than guessing.

Type errors should be exposed by debugging or compilation, not hidden.
Communication shares reasoning; the debugger observes runtime state.
When object shape is unclear, a breakpoint gives evidence faster than reading.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让程序暂停、单步执行并查看变量和调用栈的开发工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A debugger is a tool that pauses code, steps through execution, and inspects variables and the call stack.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调试器里设置的暂停点，程序运行到这里会停下，方便查看当时的变量和调用栈。
