scenario: 拼写纠错要从字典中找和输入词最接近的词，距离按插入、删除、替换字符数计算。
scenario_en: A spell checker must find the closest dictionary word to the input word, where distance is counted by insertions, deletions, and replacements.
q: 解决“最接近的词”这个核心子问题，应该用哪种算法？
q_en: Which algorithm should solve the core closest-word subproblem?
options: LRU Cache
Edit distance 的二维 DP
拓扑排序
只按字符串长度排序
options_en: An LRU cache
The 2D edit-distance DP
Topological sort
Sorting purely by string length
why: 两个字符串、三种编辑操作、求最小操作数，是 edit distance 的标准形状。外层可以遍历候选词，核心距离用 DP 算。
why_en: Spell-check closeness by single-character edits is the classic edit-distance DP.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是固定模式查找，KMP、trie 或正则可能更合适；edit distance 用于允许模糊编辑的相似度。
tradeoff: 允许模糊编辑求最小代价（edit distance DP）vs 只做精确/固定模式匹配（trie、KMP）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Empty[empty prefix] --> Row[base row]
  Empty --> Col[base col]
  Row --> Cell[dp i j]
  Col --> Cell
  Cell --> Answer[dp m n]
optionMeanings: 缓存淘汰策略，和字符串相似度计算无关。
两个字符串前缀的二维表，衡量把一个变成另一个的最少编辑次数。
给有依赖关系的节点排出线性顺序的图算法。
只比较单词长度，不看具体字符差异。
optionScenarioImpacts: 解决的是内存管理问题，不能衡量两个词有多接近。
能精确算出输入词和每个候选词之间的最少编辑次数，直接支撑“最接近”的判断。
拼写纠错里候选词之间没有依赖关系，用不上拓扑排序。
长度接近的词不一定编辑距离小，例如替换和插入代价不同。
optionDirectness: 不直接；LRU 是缓存策略，不衡量字符串相似度。
最直接；正是插入/删除/替换求最小操作数的标准场景。
不直接；本题没有节点依赖关系需要排序。
不直接；长度排序会漏掉字符本身的差异。
optionMeanings_en: A cache-eviction policy unrelated to string similarity.
A 2D table over two string prefixes that measures the minimum edits to turn one into the other.
A graph algorithm that orders dependent nodes linearly.
Comparing only word length, not the actual character differences.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This solves a memory-management problem and cannot measure how close two words are.
It computes the exact minimum edit count between the input and each candidate, directly supporting the closeness ranking.
Spell-check candidates have no dependency relationship, so topological sort has nothing to order.
Similar-length words are not necessarily close in edits, since insert and replace have different effects.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; an LRU cache does not measure string similarity.
Most direct; this is exactly the standard insert/delete/replace minimum-edit setup.
Not direct; there is no node dependency here to order.
Not direct; length-based sorting misses the actual character differences.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to turn one string into another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种线性时间的精确子串匹配算法，不处理模糊编辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KMP is a linear-time exact substring matching algorithm that does not handle fuzzy edits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀树：按公共前缀组织字符串的树形结构，适合精确前缀查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a tree that organizes strings by shared prefixes, suited to exact prefix lookups.

q: 填空：Edit distance 的状态定义。
q_en: Fill in the state definition for edit distance.
text: `dp[i][j]` 表示把第一个字符串的{{前 i 个字符}}变成第二个字符串的{{前 j 个字符}}所需的最少编辑次数。
why: 这个状态定义直接解释了为什么需要二维表：两个前缀长度各占一个维度。后续 base case 和递推都从它推出。
why_en: Edit-distance state is the minimum edits between prefixes of lengths i and j.

q: Edit distance 的边界行列应该如何理解？
q_en: How should you understand the border row and column in edit distance?
options: `dp[0][j] = j`，空串变成长度 j 的前缀需要 j 次插入
`dp[i][0] = i`，长度 i 的前缀变成空串需要 i 次删除
`dp[0][j]` 全部为 0，因为空串不需要操作
`dp[i][0]` 全部为 1，因为只删一次
options_en: dp[0][j] = j: turning an empty string into a length-j prefix takes j insertions.
dp[i][0] = i: turning a length-i prefix into an empty string takes i deletions.
dp[0][j] is always 0 because an empty string needs no operations.
dp[i][0] is always 1 because it only takes one delete.
why: 边界值可以直接从状态语义看出来，不需要递推。它们也是最常见的 off-by-one bug 来源。
why_en: The edit-distance borders count insertions from empty and deletions to empty.
optionMeanings: 正确的边界：空串到长度 j 前缀的编辑数等于插入次数 j。
正确的边界：长度 i 前缀到空串的编辑数等于删除次数 i。
误把“空串不需要操作”套用到了另一个前缀非空的方向。
误把删除次数当成固定值 1，忽略了前缀长度 i。
optionScenarioImpacts: 这是顶部一整行的正确初始化，不需要经过递推计算。
这是最左一整列的正确初始化，不需要经过递推计算。
只有 `dp[0][0] = 0` 成立；`dp[0][j]`（j>0）应该等于 j，不是 0。
只有 i=1 时才恰好是 1；i=3 时应该是 3 次删除，不是 1。
optionDirectness: 正确；直接从状态定义推出，不用递推验证。
同样正确；只是把方向从空前缀行换成了空前缀列。
不正确；混淆了 `dp[0][0]` 和 `dp[0][j]`（j>0）两种情况。
不正确；把变量 i 错误地固定成了常数 1。
optionMeanings_en: Correct border: the edits from empty to a length-j prefix equal the insert count j.
Correct border: the edits from a length-i prefix to empty equal the delete count i.
Wrongly applies the empty-to-empty case to the direction where the prefix is non-empty.
Wrongly treats the delete count as a fixed 1, ignoring the prefix length i.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This correctly initializes the entire top row without needing the recurrence.
This correctly initializes the entire left column without needing the recurrence.
Only dp[0][0] = 0 holds; dp[0][j] for j>0 should equal j, not 0.
This only happens to be 1 when i=1; for i=3 it should be 3 deletions, not 1.
optionDirectness_en: Correct; it follows directly from the state definition, no recurrence needed.
Also correct; it is the same idea applied to the empty-prefix column instead of the row.
Incorrect; it confuses dp[0][0] with dp[0][j] for j greater than 0.
Incorrect; it wrongly fixes the variable i to the constant 1.

q: Edit distance 内部格子的递推核心是什么？
q_en: What is the core recurrence for an inner edit-distance cell?
options: 不管字符是否相等，永远取上方格子
相等复制左上角；不等则替换/删除/插入取最小加一
不管字符是否相等，永远取左方格子加 2
字符相等时也必须额外加 1 的代价
options_en: Always take the cell above, regardless of whether the characters match.
On a match, copy the diagonal; otherwise take one plus the minimum of replace, delete, or insert.
Always take the cell to the left plus 2, regardless of match.
Even a matching character must add an extra cost of 1.
why: 左上、上方、左方分别对应替换、删除、插入。字符已经相等时不需要额外编辑，直接继承左上角。
why_en: Edit distance copies the diagonal on a match and otherwise takes one plus the cheapest replace, delete, or insert predecessor.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Up[delete] --> Min[min plus 1]
  Left[insert] --> Min
  Diag[replace] --> Min
  Same[same char] --> Copy[copy diag]
optionMeanings: 只考虑删除操作，忽略替换和插入两条路径。
正确的递推：按字符是否相等分两支，取三种操作中最便宜的一种。
既忽略了替换/插入路径，也凭空多加了固定代价 2。
把“字符相等不需要编辑”误当成“字符相等也要付一次代价”。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会漏掉替换和插入更便宜的情况，算出的编辑距离偏大或直接错误。
三条路径（替换、删除、插入）都被考虑，取最小值保证结果最优。
凭空加 2 没有任何操作语义支撑，纯属编造的规则。
如果对每个匹配字符都多算一次编辑，最终距离会比真实值大。
optionDirectness: 不直接；只覆盖了删除这一种操作。
最直接；覆盖了匹配与不匹配两种情况和全部三种操作。
不直接；这个规则没有对应任何真实的编辑操作。
不直接；违反了“匹配字符不产生编辑”的基本定义。
optionMeanings_en: Considers only the delete path, ignoring replace and insert.
The correct recurrence: branch on whether characters match and take the cheapest of the three operations.
Ignores replace and insert while also adding an unexplained constant of 2.
Wrongly treats a matching character as still costing one edit.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This misses cases where replace or insert is cheaper, producing an inflated or wrong edit distance.
All three paths — replace, delete, insert — are considered, and taking the minimum guarantees optimality.
Adding 2 has no operational meaning behind it; it is simply invented.
Charging an edit for every matching character makes the final distance larger than the true value.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; it only covers the delete operation.
Most direct; it covers both the match and mismatch cases across all three operations.
Not direct; this rule corresponds to no real edit operation.
Not direct; it violates the basic definition that a matching character costs nothing.

scenario: AI 已经按“字符相等复制左上角、不等取三者最小值加一”的递推写出了下面这段 edit distance 内层代码，你在检查匹配分支。
scenario_en: The AI has written the edit-distance inner loop using copy diagonal on a match and one plus the minimum of three choices on a mismatch; you are checking the match branch.
q: 这段 edit distance 的分支中，`dp[i - 1][j - 1]` 在字符相等时代表什么？
q_en: In this edit-distance branch, what does dp[i - 1][j - 1] mean when the characters match?
options: 当前字符必须替换的成本
哈希冲突次数
去掉当前两个相同字符后，两个前缀的最优编辑数
整张表的最大值
options_en: The cost of replacing the current character.
The number of hash collisions.
The optimal edit count for the two prefixes with the current matching characters removed.
The maximum value across the entire table.
why: 当前字符相等时不用编辑它们，问题退化为对齐前面的两个前缀。这个分支是检查递推正确性的重点。
why_en: On a character match, the cost is exactly the diagonal subproblem for the previous prefixes.
optionMeanings: 误以为匹配分支仍然在计算一次替换操作的成本。
把 DP 表格错认成哈希表，套用不相关的概念。
正确解释：对角线格子就是去掉这对相同字符后，剩余前缀的最优编辑数。
误以为这个格子存的是全表统计量，而不是某一对前缀的答案。
optionScenarioImpacts: 字符相等时代码没有加 1，说明这里根本没有付出替换成本。
DP 数组是按索引寻址的表格，不存在哈希冲突这个概念。
这正是为什么匹配分支直接复制对角线格子而不额外加一的原因。
整张表并不是在维护一个全局最大值，每个格子只对应它自己的一对前缀。
optionDirectness: 不直接；代码里没有 +1，说明没有产生替换成本。
不直接；哈希表和这段 DP 递推无关。
最直接；直接对应代码里 `dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1]` 这一行的语义。
不直接；每个格子对应特定前缀对，不是全表最大值。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly assumes the match branch still charges a replace cost.
Mistakes the DP table for a hash table and applies an unrelated concept.
Correct: the diagonal cell is the optimal edit count for the remaining prefixes once the matching pair is removed.
Wrongly assumes this cell stores a whole-table statistic instead of one prefix pair's answer.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The code adds no 1 on a match, showing no replace cost is charged here.
A DP array is indexed by position; there is no hash collision concept involved.
This is exactly why the match branch copies the diagonal cell without adding anything.
The table is not tracking a running maximum; each cell belongs to its own prefix pair.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; there is no +1 in the code, so no replace cost is charged.
Not direct; hash tables are unrelated to this DP recurrence.
Most direct; it matches exactly what dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] means.
Not direct; each cell belongs to a specific prefix pair, not a table-wide maximum.

q: 把 edit distance 的推导顺序排好。
q_en: Put the edit-distance derivation steps in order.
steps: 说出 base cases：空串到前缀是插入，前缀到空串是删除。
定义状态：两个字符串前缀之间的最少编辑数。
用一个小例子如 KATE 到 SAT 手算答案 2。
描述递推：相等取左上，不等取插入/删除/替换的最小值加 1。
提示 AI 写 bottom-up 代码，再用测试和表格验证。
why: 先用具体例子确认语义，再抽象成状态、边界和递推。这样 AI 输出有明确的验证依据。
why_en: A strong edit-distance derivation moves from a tiny example to state, base cases, recurrence, and AI-assisted implementation.
tradeoff: 先手推例子再抽象（多两分钟但有验证基准）vs 直接抽象定义（省时间但没有可核对的具体答案）

termDefinitions.meaning: 自底向上：从最小子问题开始按依赖顺序填表，不使用递归调用栈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bottom-up fills the table from the smallest subproblem in dependency order, without a recursive call stack.

scenario: AI 生成了 DP 代码，你不想逐行盯所有索引，但需要快速验证递推和边界。
scenario_en: The AI generated DP code, and you need to quickly verify the recurrence and borders without staring at every index.
q: 文章推荐的高杠杆调试提示是什么？
q_en: What high-leverage debugging prompt does the article recommend?
options: 只盯着函数最后一行的变量名反复对照
让 AI 打印小输入的完整 dp 表，然后对照手推的几个格子
不看任何中间输出，直接删掉所有测试用例
不做任何验证，直接把 DP 全部换成贪心重写
options_en: Only stare repeatedly at the variable names on the function's last line.
Ask the AI to print the full dp table for a small input, then check it against a few hand-traced cells.
Skip every intermediate output and delete all the test cases outright.
Skip verification entirely and rewrite the whole thing as greedy instead.
why: 打印表格能把隐藏在循环里的错误变成可观察状态。先对照左上 2x2，就能定位 base case 或递推问题。
why_en: Printing a small DP table makes base-case and recurrence bugs visible without reading every loop expression.
whenOtherWins: 如果代码很短且你已经很熟悉，也可以直接读循环；但表格验证在面试压力下更稳。
tradeoff: 打印表格核对（多一步但错误可定位）vs 直接读循环代码（省步骤但压力下容易漏看）
optionMeanings: 只看返回值所在的那一行，忽略中间过程。
把循环内部的隐藏状态变成可以对照的具体数字。
彻底放弃用具体输入检验代码是否正确。
误以为验证手段是换算法，而不是核实当前算法的实现。
optionScenarioImpacts: 只看最后一行看不出 base case 或中间格子是否算错。
对照左上 2x2，base case 错就在首行/首列露出来，递推错就在第一个内部格子露出来。
没有测试就没有可重复验证的依据，bug 只能靠肉眼通读代码猜。
换算法不解决当前 DP 实现是否正确的问题，而且贪心不一定适用。
optionDirectness: 不直接；只看变量名看不出中间计算是否正确。
最直接；这是文章点名的高杠杆调试手段。
不直接；删测试只会让验证更难，不会帮你定位问题。
不直接；这是换了问题而不是验证当前代码。
optionMeanings_en: Only looks at the line holding the return value, ignoring intermediate steps.
Turns the loop's hidden state into concrete numbers you can check.
Gives up entirely on verifying the code against a concrete input.
Wrongly assumes verification means switching algorithms rather than checking the current implementation.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Looking only at the last line reveals nothing about whether base cases or intermediate cells are wrong.
Checking the top-left 2x2 shows a base-case bug in the first row/column and a recurrence bug in the first inner cell.
Without tests there is no repeatable evidence, and bugs can only be guessed by reading code.
Switching algorithms does not verify whether the current DP implementation is correct, and greedy may not even apply.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; variable names alone reveal nothing about intermediate correctness.
Most direct; this is the high-leverage debugging move the article names.
Not direct; deleting tests only makes verification harder, not easier to locate the bug.
Not direct; this changes the problem rather than verifying the current code.

q: 验证 edit distance 时，哪些测试很有价值？
q_en: Which tests are valuable for verifying edit distance?
options: 两个相同字符串应返回 0
空串到 `abc` 应返回 3
`kate` 到 `sat` 应返回 2
只测试一个很长随机字符串且不知道答案
options_en: Two identical strings should return 0.
Empty string to 'abc' should return 3.
'kate' to 'sat' should return 2.
Testing only one long random string with an unknown expected answer.
why: 这些小测试分别覆盖相等、边界行列和非平凡递推。未知答案的大随机输入不适合作为第一轮正确性验证。
why_en: Good DP tests include equal inputs, empty-prefix cases, and a small hand-computed nontrivial case.
optionMeanings: 覆盖“字符完全相同，编辑距离应为 0”的基础情况。
覆盖空串这一整行/整列边界的插入次数。
覆盖一个非平凡的手算例子，同时检验递推的替换/删除/插入分支。
用一个连答案都不知道的大输入去测正确性。
optionScenarioImpacts: 如果这个都算错，说明匹配分支或 base case 有明显 bug。
如果这个算错，说明边界初始化（`dp[0][j] = j`）有问题。
如果这个算错，能直接定位到递推的三选一最小值逻辑。
算出一个数字后你没有基准可以判断对不对，无法定位任何具体 bug。
optionDirectness: 直接；是最基础也最容易先验证的用例。
直接；专门验证边界初始化是否正确。
直接；专门验证内部递推是否正确。
不直接；没有已知答案，测试失败或通过都无法归因。
optionMeanings_en: Covers the basic case: identical characters should give edit distance 0.
Covers the entire empty-prefix row/column boundary and its insert count.
Covers a nontrivial hand-computed example that also checks the replace/delete/insert branches.
Tests correctness with a large input whose expected answer is unknown.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Getting this wrong points straight at a bug in the match branch or a base case.
Getting this wrong points straight at broken border initialization such as dp[0][j] = j.
Getting this wrong points straight at the recurrence's three-way minimum logic.
Without a known answer, you have no baseline to attribute a pass or fail to any specific bug.
optionDirectness_en: Direct; it is the simplest and easiest case to verify first.
Direct; it specifically checks that border initialization is correct.
Direct; it specifically checks that the inner recurrence is correct.
Not direct; with no known answer, a pass or failure cannot be attributed to anything.

scenario: 一个 DP 测试失败了，你正准备把报错信息发给 AI。
scenario_en: A DP test failed, and you are about to send the error output to the AI.
q: 为什么不该只把报错扔给 AI 说“修一下”？
q_en: Why should you not just throw an error at the AI and say fix it?
options: 所有隐藏测试都会自动覆盖这个具体边界
DP 代码天生正确，永远不需要调试
先形成具体假设，再带着假设去提示 AI
AI 完全无法读取或理解测试失败信息
options_en: Every hidden test will automatically cover this specific edge.
DP code is inherently correct and never needs debugging.
Form a hypothesis first, such as an off-by-one base case, then prompt the AI with it.
The AI is entirely unable to read or understand test-failure output.
why: 带假设的提示证明你仍在控制调试方向，也能防止 AI 盲目重写整个方案。面试官会看到你的定位能力。
why_en: When a DP test fails, prompt with a concrete hypothesis so the AI fixes the suspected structure rather than thrashing.
optionMeanings: 把测试覆盖率和调试策略混为一谈。
误以为调试这个动作本身对 DP 不适用。
正确做法：先自己定位可能出错的结构，再带着具体假设提示 AI。
误以为 AI 完全看不懂测试失败的输出。
optionScenarioImpacts: 测试覆盖率是提前写测试时决定的，和这次“怎么提示 AI 修 bug”无关。
DP 代码和其他代码一样会有 bug，需要照常调试，只是要带着假设去做。
带假设提示能让 AI 直接检查你怀疑的那部分，而不是重写整个方案碰运气。
AI 完全可以读懂报错和期望/实际值的差异，只是它不知道该往哪个方向改。
optionDirectness: 不直接；这里的问题是调试策略，不是测试覆盖率。
不直接；DP 一样需要调试，只是调试方式有讲究。
最直接；这正是文章点名的“先假设再提示”策略。
不直接；AI 能读报错，缺的是方向而不是能力。
optionMeanings_en: Conflates test coverage with debugging strategy.
Wrongly assumes debugging itself does not apply to DP.
The correct move: locate the likely broken structure yourself, then prompt the AI with that specific hypothesis.
Wrongly assumes the AI cannot understand test-failure output at all.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Test coverage was decided when the tests were written earlier and is unrelated to how you prompt a fix now.
DP code has bugs like any other code and still needs debugging, just guided by a hypothesis.
A hypothesis-driven prompt lets the AI check exactly the part you suspect instead of rewriting the whole solution on a guess.
The AI can perfectly well read the error and the expected-vs-actual values; what it lacks is direction, not ability.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; the issue here is debugging strategy, not test coverage.
Not direct; DP still needs debugging, just done thoughtfully.
Most direct; this is exactly the hypothesis-first prompting strategy the article names.
Not direct; the AI can read the error — what is missing is direction, not capability.

q: DP bug 最常住在哪些结构位置？
q_en: Where do DP bugs most often live structurally?
options: base cases
递推表达式
遍历顺序
返回的格子或状态
options_en: The base cases
The recurrence expression
The traversal order
The returned cell or state
why: DP 代码表面相似，错误通常是结构性的一个格子、一条边或一个循环方向。审查时按这四处逐项过。
why_en: DP bugs concentrate in base cases, recurrence, traversal order, and return state.

q: AI 给出一个“几乎正确”的 DP 递推（能跑、通过部分测试却是错的），为什么特别危险？
q_en: Why is an almost-correct DP recurrence especially dangerous?
options: 这种代码一定会编译失败
这种问题只会影响代码风格
类型检查总能自动发现这种错误
AI 可能套用了相邻问题的错误递推模板
options_en: Code like this is guaranteed to fail to compile.
A problem like this only affects code style.
Type checking will always catch this kind of error automatically.
The AI may have borrowed the wrong recurrence template from a neighboring problem.
why: 相邻 DP 题的表格形状很像，但递推语义不同。代码能跑、简单测试也可能过，隐藏测试才会暴露。
why_en: Almost-right recurrences are dangerous because neighboring DP problems can share table shapes but need different transitions.
optionMeanings: 误以为逻辑错误一定表现为语法错误。
误以为递推写错只是美观问题，不影响正确性。
误以为类型系统能检查出算法语义上的错误。
指出错误的真实来源：借用了相邻问题的递推模板。
optionScenarioImpacts: “几乎正确”的代码通常语法完全合法，能正常编译运行。
递推选错会直接导致输出的数值错误，不是风格问题。
类型检查只管变量类型对不对，不管数值语义对不对。
edit distance 和 LCS（最长公共子序列）表格形状几乎一样，但一个是最小代价、一个是最大长度，混淆后代码依然能跑。
optionDirectness: 不直接；语法层面完全没问题，这不是编译错误。
不直接；这是正确性问题，不是风格问题。
不直接；类型检查不覆盖算法语义。
最直接；这正是文章点名的“几乎正确的递推”成因。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly assumes a logic error must show up as a syntax error.
Wrongly assumes a wrong recurrence is only a style issue, not a correctness issue.
Wrongly assumes the type system can catch algorithmic semantic errors.
Names the real cause: borrowing the recurrence template from a neighboring problem.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Almost-right code is usually syntactically valid and compiles and runs fine.
Picking the wrong recurrence directly produces wrong output values, not a style problem.
Type checking only validates variable types, not numeric semantics.
Edit distance and LCS (longest common subsequence) share almost the same table shape, but one minimizes cost and the other maximizes length, so mixing them still runs.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; there is no syntax problem here, so it is not a compile error.
Not direct; this is a correctness issue, not a style issue.
Not direct; type checking does not cover algorithmic semantics.
Most direct; this is exactly what the article calls an almost-right recurrence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最长公共子序列：两个序列中都出现且顺序一致的最长子序列长度，用最大化递推求解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LCS is the length of the longest subsequence appearing in the same order in both sequences, solved with a maximizing recurrence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数，用最小化递推求解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements to turn one string into another, solved with a minimizing recurrence.

q: AI 在 DP 里多加了一个你解释不了的维度（例如 `dp[i][j][k]`），应该怎么处理？
q_en: What should you do if the AI adds a DP dimension you cannot explain, such as dp[i][j][k]?
options: 把整个二维状态表硬换成一个字符串
让 AI 证明这个维度的语义和必要性；解释不了就要求简化状态
直接删掉所有已经验证过的 base case
无条件全盘接受，维度越多说明考虑越周全
options_en: Forcibly turn the entire 2D state table into a string.
Ask the AI to justify the dimension's meaning and necessity; simplify the state if it cannot.
Delete all the base cases that were already verified.
Accept it unconditionally — more dimensions must mean more thorough thinking.
why: 额外维度常是模型在不确定状态时的保守堆叠。你无法解释的维度，就是无法验证的不变量。
why_en: An unexplained DP dimension is a state-design smell that should be justified or removed.
optionMeanings: 提出一个和维度问题无关的改动。
正确做法：要求 AI 解释新增维度代表什么，说不清就砍掉。
提出一个会破坏整个递推根基的错误动作。
把“维度多”误当成“更保险”，不做任何审查。
optionScenarioImpacts: 把表结构换成字符串不会回答“这个维度到底在追踪什么”这个问题。
能确认这个维度是真实需要（比如额外约束）还是模型的保守堆叠。
base case 是递推的根基，删掉后整个表都失去起点。
维度越多状态空间越大，调试和验证难度也越高，并不天然更安全。
optionDirectness: 不直接；换数据结构不解决维度语义不清的问题。
最直接；这是文章给出的具体处理办法。
不直接；这是无关且有破坏性的动作。
不直接；维度多不等于正确，也不等于更保险。
optionMeanings_en: Proposes a change unrelated to the dimension problem.
The correct move: make the AI explain what the new dimension tracks, and simplify if it cannot.
Proposes a destructive action that breaks the recurrence's foundation.
Wrongly treats more dimensions as inherently safer, with no review at all.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Swapping the table for a string does not answer what the dimension is actually tracking.
This confirms whether the dimension is genuinely needed, such as for an extra constraint, or just defensive padding.
Base cases anchor the recurrence; deleting them removes the table's starting point entirely.
More dimensions mean a larger state space and harder debugging, not inherently more safety.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; changing the data structure does not resolve an unclear dimension.
Most direct; this is the concrete remedy the article recommends.
Not direct; this is an unrelated and destructive action.
Not direct; more dimensions do not equal correctness or safety.

scenario: 你的状态是“前 i 个元素”，循环需要写到 `i = n`。
scenario_en: Your state means the first i elements, and the loop needs to write through i = n.
q: 这个 DP 数组的大小通常应该是什么？
q_en: What size should this DP array usually be?
options: 固定 1
与输入无关
options_en: A fixed size of 1
n minus 1
n plus 1
Independent of the input
why: 前缀状态通常包含空前缀 `0` 到完整前缀 `n`，所以需要 n+1 个格子。分配 n 个元素再写 dp[n] 会越界。
why_en: Prefix-based states usually need n plus one cells to include the empty prefix and the full prefix.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态定义是“从索引 i 开始”而不是“前 i 个”，大小可能是 n；关键是让数组大小和状态语义一致。
tradeoff: 数组大小 n+1（覆盖空前缀到满前缀）vs 数组大小 n（仅当状态语义是“从 i 开始”时才对）
optionMeanings: 完全忽略输入规模，把数组大小写死成常量。
少分配了一格，会让最后一次写入越界。
正确大小：覆盖从空前缀 0 到完整前缀 n 的全部状态。
误以为数组大小和状态定义无关。
optionScenarioImpacts: 常量大小 1 放不下 `i` 从 0 到 n 的所有状态。
循环写到 `dp[n]` 时数组只有 n 格（索引 0..n-1），会越界。
`dp[0]` 到 `dp[n]` 共 n+1 格，正好对上“前 i 个”这个状态。
数组大小必须和状态定义的取值范围一致，不能凭空决定。
optionDirectness: 不直接；常量大小无法覆盖变化的输入规模。
不直接；这是典型的少一格 off-by-one。
最直接；直接从“前 i 个元素”这个状态语义推出来。
不直接；数组大小恰恰应该由状态定义决定。
optionMeanings_en: Ignores the input size entirely and hardcodes a constant array size.
Allocates one cell too few, so the final write goes out of bounds.
The correct size: covers every state from the empty prefix 0 to the full prefix n.
Wrongly assumes array size is unrelated to the state definition.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A constant size of 1 cannot hold all states for i from 0 to n.
Writing dp[n] goes out of bounds since the array only has n cells, indices 0 through n-1.
dp[0] through dp[n] is n+1 cells, matching the first-i-elements state exactly.
Array size must match the range the state definition allows, not be picked arbitrarily.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; a constant size cannot cover a variable input size.
Not direct; this is a classic off-by-one under-allocation.
Most direct; it follows directly from the first-i-elements state semantics.
Not direct; array size should be exactly determined by the state definition.

q: AI 为了修一个空输入测试，在函数开头硬编码 `if len(s) == 0: return 0`，这是什么味道？
q_en: What smell does this hardcoded empty-input fix suggest?
options: 这足以说明递推逻辑一定完全正确无误
这说明后续测试都可以完全省略不写
这是业界公认的所有 DP 面试标准写法
可能是在掩盖 base case 错误，而不是修正表格初始化
options_en: This is enough to prove the recurrence logic is completely correct.
This means every later test can be skipped entirely.
This is the industry-standard way to write every DP interview solution.
It may be papering over a base-case bug instead of fixing the table's initialization.
why: DP 的边界应和状态表语义一致。硬编码通过一个测试，可能让其他边界继续错。
why_en: A hardcoded edge fix can mask a broken DP base case instead of correcting the state table.
optionMeanings: 误以为通过一个补丁测试就能证明整个递推没问题。
误以为一个测试通过后就不用再测其他边界。
误把这种补丁当成通用的 DP 写法。
指出真实风险：这只是掩盖了 base case 初始化本身的 bug。
optionScenarioImpacts: 递推逻辑完全没被这行代码验证过，只是绕开了一个具体输入。
其他边界（单字符、相等字符串等）可能仍然存在同样的 base case 问题。
标准 DP 写法是让 `dp[0]` 或首行首列在表初始化时就正确，而不是在函数入口特判。
如果 base case 初始化本身是对的，根本不需要在函数开头单独硬编码这个分支。
optionDirectness: 不直接；一个特判测试不能证明整个递推正确。
不直接；其他边界仍然需要测试覆盖。
不直接；这不是标准写法，而是一个警示信号。
最直接；这正是文章点名的“硬编码掩盖 base case”的坏味道。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly assumes a single patched test proves the whole recurrence is correct.
Wrongly assumes passing one test means no other edges need testing.
Wrongly treats this patch as the standard way to write DP.
Names the real risk: it papers over a bug in the base-case initialization itself.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The recurrence logic is never exercised by this line; it just routes around one specific input.
Other edges, like single-character or equal strings, may still carry the same base-case bug.
The standard approach initializes dp[0] or the first row/column correctly in the table itself, not with a special-cased entry guard.
If the base-case initialization were correct, there would be no need for this special-cased branch at all.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; one patched test cannot prove the whole recurrence correct.
Not direct; other edges still need test coverage.
Not direct; this is not the standard approach — it is a warning sign.
Most direct; this is exactly the hardcoded-masking-a-base-case smell the article names.

q: 文章说的 “DP spiral” 指什么？
q_en: What does the article mean by a DP spiral?
options: DP 表格在纸上必须严格画成螺旋形状
AI 一次次换状态、加维度、重写方案，看似进展但没有定位根因
所有 DP 问题都必须用递归方式来实现
写的测试数量越少，代码就天然越稳定

Every DP problem must be implemented recursively.

why_en: A DP spiral is uncontrolled rewriting of state and dimensions instead of fixing the specific bug.

误以为测试数量少反而更能保证代码稳定。

测试少只会让你更晚发现 bug，不会让代码本身更稳定。
optionDirectness: 不直接；这是对术语的字面误解。
最直接；这正是文章定义的“DP spiral”现象。
不直接；tabulation 是常见的非递归实现方式。
不直接；测试数量和代码稳定性是两回事。
optionMeanings_en: Reads the term literally as a visual table shape.
The correct explanation: the AI keeps rewriting state and structure without ever pinning down the specific bug.
Wrongly assumes DP must be implemented recursively.
Wrongly assumes fewer tests make the code more stable.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This term has nothing to do with how the table is drawn; it is a metaphor for debugging going out of control.
If the third generation looks very different from the second, the AI is thrashing rather than converging on the root cause.

Fewer tests only delay when you discover a bug; they do not make the code itself more stable.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; this is a literal misreading of the term.
Most direct; this is exactly the DP spiral phenomenon the article defines.
Not direct; tabulation is a common non-recursive implementation style.
Not direct; test count and code stability are unrelated.

scenario: 题目要求列出所有和为 k 的子集，而不是只问有多少种或最优值。
scenario_en: The problem asks you to list all subsets that sum to k, not just count them or find one optimal value.
q: 更自然的起点是什么？
q_en: What is the more natural starting point?
options: Dijkstra
LRU Cache
只返回一个 DP 数字
回溯枚举所有合法子集
options_en: Dijkstra's algorithm
An LRU cache
Return a single DP number
Backtracking to enumerate every valid subset
why: “列出所有”通常要求保留每个具体解，回溯更直接。DP 可用于计数或可行性，也可和回溯结合，但不是默认替代。
why_en: Enumerating every valid subset is naturally backtracking, while DP is better for counts or optimal values.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目只问可行性或方案数，且重复状态明显，DP 会更高效。
tradeoff: 枚举所有具体解（回溯）vs 只求一个最优值或方案数（DP）
optionMeanings: 求带权图最短路径的算法，和枚举子集无关。
缓存淘汰策略，和枚举子集无关。
只压缩输出一个数字，丢失了每个具体子集的内容。
系统枚举并回退的搜索方式，天然能保留每一个具体解。
optionScenarioImpacts: 本题没有图和边权，Dijkstra 无从下手。
本题不涉及内存淘汰问题，LRU 无从下手。
题目要的是“列出所有子集”，只给一个数字答不了这个要求。
每条搜索路径对应一个具体子集，找到和为 k 的路径就直接输出。
optionDirectness: 不直接；本题不是最短路径问题。
不直接；LRU 和求子集无关。

optionMeanings_en: An algorithm for shortest paths in a weighted graph, unrelated to subset enumeration.
A cache-eviction policy, unrelated to subset enumeration.
Compresses the output to a single number, losing the content of each specific subset.
A systematic search-and-backtrack approach that naturally preserves every specific solution.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: There is no graph or edge weights here, so Dijkstra has nothing to run on.
There is no memory-eviction concern here, so LRU has nothing to do.
The task asks to list every subset; a single number cannot satisfy that requirement.
Each search path corresponds to one specific subset, so a path summing to k is output directly.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; this is not a shortest-path problem.
Not direct; LRU is unrelated to enumerating subsets.
Not direct; DP is good at a single optimal value or a count, not at preserving every specific solution.
Most direct; listing all solutions is the standard backtracking scenario.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统地尝试、递归深入、遇到不满足条件就撤销选择的搜索方式，能枚举所有合法解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking systematically tries choices, recurses deeper, and undoes a choice when it fails, enumerating every valid solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 求带权图中单源最短路径的经典算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest paths from a single source in a weighted graph.

scenario: 输入规模 n ≤ 20，暴力枚举 2ⁿ 个子集能在时间内跑完，且 DP 状态设计复杂。
scenario_en: The input size is n <= 20, brute-force enumeration of 2^n subsets fits the time limit, and the DP state is complicated.
q: 合理的工程选择是什么？
q_en: What is the reasonable engineering choice?
options: 先用暴力或回溯，因为更简单也更容易验证
只写正则
放弃写测试
无条件上复杂 DP
options_en: Start with brute force or backtracking because it is simpler and easier to verify.
Just write a regex.
Skip writing tests.
Reach for the complex DP unconditionally.
why: DP 以状态设计复杂度换取性能。输入足够小且暴力可验证时，不必为了模式而上模式。
why_en: For tiny inputs, brute force can be the better engineering choice because it is simpler and easier to verify.
whenOtherWins: 如果输入上限变大或隐藏测试会压性能，再转向 DP 或剪枝优化。
tradeoff: n≤20 时暴力枚举（简单、易验证、O(2ⁿ)可接受）vs 复杂 DP（状态设计成本高，收益在小输入下不明显）
optionMeanings: 正确判断：n 很小时，2ⁿ 枚举的时间可接受，且实现和验证都更简单。
把无关的字符串匹配工具当成了这里的解法。
误以为工程上可以跳过测试这一步。
误以为任何优化问题都必须上 DP，不考虑输入规模。
optionScenarioImpacts: n≤20 时 2ⁿ 最多约一百万级别，现代机器和面试时限都能接受。
正则解决的是模式匹配，不解决“枚举所有子集”这类组合问题。
没有测试就无法确认暴力实现或未来的 DP 实现是否正确。
为小输入设计复杂状态是不必要的工程投入，还增加了出错概率。
optionDirectness: 最直接；小规模输入下暴力比 DP 更划算。
不直接；正则和枚举子集完全是两回事。
不直接；测试任何时候都不该被跳过。
不直接；没有考虑到输入规模已经小到暴力可行。
optionMeanings_en: The correct call: with n this small, 2 to the n enumeration is affordable, and it is simpler to implement and verify.
Applies an unrelated string-matching tool to this problem.
Wrongly assumes tests can be skipped as an engineering shortcut.
Wrongly assumes any optimization problem must use DP regardless of input size.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: With n at most 20, 2 to the n is around a million, which modern machines and interview time limits can handle.
Regex solves pattern matching, not combinatorial problems like enumerating all subsets.
Without tests there is no way to confirm either the brute-force or a future DP implementation is correct.
Designing a complex state for a tiny input is unnecessary engineering effort that adds room for error.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct; brute force is the better deal at this small input size.
Not direct; regex and subset enumeration are unrelated problems.
Not direct; tests should never be skipped.
Not direct; it ignores that the input is already small enough for brute force.

scenario: 状态之间天然形成一个图，题目问最短步数或可达性，状态转移很清晰。
scenario_en: The states naturally form a graph, the problem asks for shortest steps or reachability, and the transitions are clear.
q: 除了 DP，还应考虑什么？
q_en: What should you consider besides DP?
options: 手写 LRU
按字母排序
只用双向链表
BFS / Dijkstra 等图搜索
options_en: Hand-writing an LRU cache
Sorting alphabetically
Using only a doubly linked list
Graph search such as BFS or Dijkstra
why: 一些问题可建成状态图，最短路径或可达性用图搜索更容易向 AI 说明和验证。不要把所有状态转移题都强行 DP 化。
why_en: When states form a natural graph and the question is reachability or shortest path, graph search may be cleaner than DP.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态有明确拓扑顺序并且要聚合最优值，DP 表或 DAG 上 DP 可能更直接。
tradeoff: 状态天然是图、求最短路/可达性（图搜索更直接）vs 状态需要聚合最优值且有拓扑序（DP 更直接）
optionMeanings: 缓存淘汰策略，和最短路径/可达性无关。
只是一种数据整理方式，不解决状态转移问题。
一种数据结构，本身不能解决图上的搜索问题。
用无权层级或带权边搜索状态图，求最短步数或可达性的标准方案。
optionScenarioImpacts: 这个场景问的是最短步数/可达性，不是内存淘汰。
排序不会告诉你从起点到终点最少要几步。
双向链表本身不携带节点间的转移关系。
BFS 求无权图最短步数，Dijkstra 求带权图最短路径，两者都直接对应本题结构。
optionDirectness: 不直接；LRU 是缓存策略，不是搜索算法。
不直接；排序不能解决图上可达性问题。
不直接；链表是容器，不是搜索算法。
最直接；状态天然成图，图搜索比强行套 DP 更清晰。
optionMeanings_en: A cache-eviction policy, unrelated to shortest path or reachability.
Just a way to organize data; it does not address state transitions.
A data structure by itself, not a way to search a graph.
The standard approach for searching a state graph with unweighted or weighted edges to find shortest steps or reachability.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This scenario asks about shortest steps or reachability, not memory eviction.
Sorting tells you nothing about the minimum number of steps from start to end.
A doubly linked list by itself carries no transition relationships between nodes.
BFS finds shortest steps in an unweighted graph and Dijkstra finds shortest paths in a weighted one, both matching this structure directly.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; an LRU cache is not a search algorithm.
Not direct; sorting cannot solve graph reachability.
Not direct; a linked list is a container, not a search algorithm.
Most direct; the states naturally form a graph, so graph search is cleaner than forcing DP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按层扩展，是无权图求最短步数的标准算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS expands layer by layer and is the standard algorithm for shortest steps in an unweighted graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 求带权图中单源最短路径的经典算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest paths from a single source in a weighted graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有向无环图：节点间有方向且没有环，天然给出可用于 DP 的拓扑顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DAG is a directed graph with no cycles, which naturally provides a topological order usable for DP.

q: DP 题中，哪些行为是强信号？
q_en: Which behaviors are strong signals in a DP interview problem?
options: 用 DP 术语说出状态、递推、base cases
手推或打印表格验证 AI 的递推
能解释为什么是二维而不是一维
测试失败后沉默地让 AI 一直重写
options_en: Naming the state, recurrence, and base cases out loud in DP vocabulary.
Hand-tracing or printing the table to verify the AI's recurrence.
Being able to explain why the table is 2D instead of 1D.
Silently letting the AI keep rewriting after a test fails.
why: 面试官知道 AI 能写 DP 代码，真正要看你是否能指向正确状态并验证输出。失控重写是负信号。
why_en: Strong DP signals are naming the state and recurrence, verifying the table, and defending dimensionality.
optionMeanings: 在写代码前，用一句英文/中文清楚描述状态、递推来源和边界。
拿一个具体小例子核对 AI 生成的表格数值。
能说清楚为什么状态需要两个维度而不是压缩成一维。
测试失败时既不形成假设，也不主动介入，只是反复让 AI 重来。
optionScenarioImpacts: 这是面试官判断“你是否真的设计了这个方案”的第一信号。
能把隐藏在循环里的 bug 变成可观察、可核对的数字。
能证明你理解状态语义，而不是照抄了一个看起来对的模板。
这会让面试官怀疑你没有真正主导调试，只是在旁观 AI 试错。
optionDirectness: 强信号；直接体现你对状态设计的掌控。
强信号；是文章反复强调的验证手段。
强信号；说明你能为设计决策辩护。
负信号；文章明确说这是要避免的行为。
optionMeanings_en: Before writing code, clearly stating the state, recurrence origin, and boundaries in one sentence.
Checking the AI-generated table's numbers against a small concrete example.
Being able to explain why the state needs two dimensions instead of being compressed to one.
When a test fails, forming no hypothesis and not intervening, just letting the AI keep retrying.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This is the first signal an interviewer uses to judge whether you actually designed the solution.
It turns bugs hidden inside loops into observable, checkable numbers.
It proves you understand the state's semantics rather than having copied a template that merely looks right.
It makes the interviewer suspect you never actually directed the debugging and were just watching the AI guess.
optionDirectness_en: A strong signal; it directly shows control over the state design.
A strong signal; it is the verification move the article repeatedly emphasizes.
A strong signal; it shows you can defend the design decision.
A negative signal; the article explicitly calls this out as behavior to avoid.

q: 把 AI 编码面试中的 DP 工作流按顺序排列。
q_en: Put the DP workflow for an AI coding interview in order.
steps: 让 AI 生成 bottom-up 或 memoized 实现。
识别产品包装下的 DP 模式。
用测试、手推格子或打印表格验证输出。
用一句话定义状态，并说出 base cases。
先写几个小测试，尤其是边界输入。
why: 先识别和定义状态，再用测试约束实现，最后验证。这个流程把最容易错的边界放在 AI 写代码之前。
why_en: The DP interview loop is recognize, define state and bases, write tests, generate code, and verify the table.
tradeoff: 先定状态和测试再生成代码（多几分钟但可验证）vs 直接生成代码再补救（省时间但容易在错的方案上调试）

scenario: 你要在提示 AI 之前先手推一个具体例子，既验证自己理解了编辑语义，又能把它变成后续的自动化测试用例。
scenario_en: Before prompting the AI, you want to hand-work a concrete example that checks your edit semantics and later becomes an automated test.
q: 填空：文章中的 edit distance 手算例子。
q_en: Fill in the article's hand-worked edit-distance example.
text: `KATE` 变成 `SAT` 至少需要 {{2}} 次编辑：先把 K 替换成 S，再删除末尾的 E。
why: 手推公式：替换 1 次 + 删除 1 次 = 2 次编辑，这个数字直接变成测试用例 `edit_distance('kate','sat') == 2`，是后续验证 AI 代码表格是否正确的基准。
why_en: KATE to SAT has edit distance two, making it a useful hand-checkable DP test.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to turn one string into another.

scenario: AI 写了一个前缀 DP，你需要快速检查 loop 边界和 return cell 是否匹配状态。
scenario_en: The AI wrote a prefix DP, and you need to quickly check whether the loop bounds and return cell match the state.
q: 下面哪项最符合 `dp[i][j]` 表示两个前缀完整消耗后的返回？
q_en: Which return cell best matches dp[i][j] after both prefixes are fully consumed?
codeSample:
m, n = len(s), len(t)
dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(m + 1)]
# fill table...
return ???
options: dp[n][m] 一定正确
dp[m][n]
options_en: dp[n][m] is always correct.
dp[m][n]
why: 如果状态包含空前缀到完整前缀，完整字符串对应 `m` 和 `n`。返回 `m-1,n-1` 是典型 off-by-one。
why_en: For prefix lengths including zero, the full strings live at dp[m][n].
whenOtherWins: 如果状态定义用真实字符索引而不是前缀长度，返回位置可能不同；必须回到状态语义判断。
tradeoff: return cell 由状态语义决定（dp[m][n] 对应两个前缀长度）vs 想当然套用行列互换或减一的写法
optionMeanings: 把行列维度对调，误认为顺序无所谓。
正确答案：m 做行、n 做列，完整前缀是 `dp[m][n]`。
把两个空前缀误当成最终答案。
把“前 i 个字符”误当成第 i 个字符索引，多减 1。
optionScenarioImpacts: 数组是 m+1 行、n+1 列，`dp[n][m]` 大概率越界。
对应两个字符串都消耗完的那个格子。
是还没比较的起点，不是最终答案。
完整字符串在 i=m，减一读到少一字符的子问题。
optionDirectness: 不直接；行列顺序对调了。
最直接；匹配数组声明的行列顺序。
不直接；这是起点，不是终点。
不直接；典型少一格 off-by-one。
optionMeanings_en: Swaps rows and columns, wrongly assuming order does not matter.
Correct: s's length m is rows, t's length n is columns, so full prefixes land at dp[m][n].
Mistakes the two-empty-prefix starting cell for the final answer.
Misreads first-i-characters as the index of the i-th character, subtracting one too many.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The array has m+1 rows and n+1 columns; dp[n][m] likely goes out of bounds or reads the wrong cell.
This matches the declared row/column order, landing where both strings are fully consumed.
dp[0][0] is the starting point before any comparison, not the final answer.
The full string sits at index i=m; subtracting one reads a subproblem missing a character.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; it does not match the declared m-rows, n-columns order.
Most direct; it matches the range(m + 1) rows and (n + 1) columns declaration.
Not direct; this is the starting cell, not the ending one.
Not direct; this is a classic off-by-one under-count.

scenario: 两个字符串长度分别为 m 和 n，你在检查 AI 声明的前缀 DP 数组大小是否正确。
scenario_en: The two strings have lengths m and n, and you are checking whether the AI declared the prefix DP table with the right size.
q: 为什么前缀 DP 表格通常要开成 `(m + 1) x (n + 1)`，而不是 `m x n`？
q_en: Why is a prefix DP table usually (m + 1) by (n + 1), not m by n?
options: 因为 n 和 m 总是相等
因为答案需要两个副本
因为 Python 数组必须多一行
要包含空前缀行和空前缀列
options_en: Because n and m are always equal.
Because the answer needs two copies.
Because Python arrays must always have one extra row.
To include the row and column for the empty prefix.
why: 空前缀（长度 0）是合法的起始子问题，公式是行数=m+1、列数=n+1，覆盖 0..m 和 0..n 两个前缀长度区间。少这一行列会导致 base case 无处安放、后续所有格子索引错位。
why_en: Prefix DP tables add one row and column to represent empty prefixes.

q: 文章建议练习哪些 DP 形状来训练识别？
q_en: Which DP shapes does the article recommend practicing for recognition?
options: House Robber 这种一维 DP
Unique Paths 这种二维表
Word Break 这种不那么显然的状态
Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling 这种排序 + 二分 + DP
options_en: House Robber, a one-dimensional DP
Unique Paths, a two-dimensional table
Word Break, whose state is less obvious
Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling, which combines sorting, binary search, and DP
why: 练习目标不是打字速度，而是识别包装、定义状态、写测试和验证输出。不同形状能覆盖不同状态设计。
why_en: Practicing varied DP shapes trains recognition and state definition rather than implementation speed.

q: memoization 和 bottom-up tabulation 的共同点是什么？
q_en: What do memoization and bottom-up tabulation have in common?
options: 都必须使用二维数组
都不需要 base case
都不能处理字符串
都保证每个不同子问题只计算一次
options_en: Both must use a 2D array.
Neither needs base cases.
Neither can handle strings.
Both guarantee each distinct subproblem is computed only once.
why: memo 是递归时缓存；tabulation 是从小到大填表。形式不同，但目的都是复用子问题答案。
why_en: Memoization and tabulation both avoid recomputing the same subproblem.
tradeoff: memoization：递归 + 缓存，写起来更接近暴力递归，但有调用栈开销 vs tabulation：显式循环填表，无栈开销，但要自己想清楚遍历顺序
optionMeanings: 误以为两种技巧都限定了数组维度。
误以为两种技巧都不需要边界条件。
误以为两种技巧的适用范围排除字符串问题。
正确的共同点：两者都通过复用已算过的子问题答案，避免重复计算。
optionScenarioImpacts: 一维、二维甚至三维状态都能用两者，维度由状态本身决定。
两者都仍需 base case：memo 是递归终止条件，tabulation 是填表起点。
edit distance、LCS 等字符串 DP 正是两者的常见应用场景。
memo 靠递归+缓存，tabulation 靠按序填表，殊途同归到每个状态只算一次。
optionDirectness: 不直接；数组维度由状态设计决定，不是这两种技巧的限制。
不直接；两者都仍然依赖 base case 才能终止或起步。
不直接；字符串 DP 是这两种技巧最常见的应用之一。
最直接；这正是两者共享的核心目的。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly assumes both techniques restrict the array to a fixed dimensionality.
Wrongly assumes neither technique needs boundary conditions.
Wrongly assumes both techniques exclude string problems.
The correct shared trait: both avoid recomputation by reusing already-solved subproblem answers.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: 1D, 2D, even 3D states can use either technique; dimensionality comes from the state itself.
Both still need base cases: recursion stop conditions for memo, starting values for tabulation.
String DP problems like edit distance and LCS are common uses of both techniques.
Memo uses recursion plus a cache, tabulation fills in order; different paths, same one-compute-per-state result.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; array dimensionality comes from the state design, not a limit of these techniques.
Not direct; both still rely on base cases to terminate or start.
Not direct; string DP is one of the most common uses of both techniques.
Most direct; this is exactly the shared purpose of both techniques.

termDefinitions.meaning: 递归时把已经算过的子问题结果存起来，下次遇到直接返回缓存值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memoization stores the result of a subproblem the first time it is computed and returns the cached value on repeat calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自底向上填表：从最小的子问题开始，按依赖顺序逐个算到目标状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tabulation fills a table bottom-up, computing each state in dependency order from the smallest subproblem to the target.

scenario: DP 表的每一行只依赖上一行，你已经有正确的二维版本并通过测试。
scenario_en: Each DP table row only depends on the previous row, and you already have a correct 2D version that passes tests.
q: 什么时候才应该让 AI 做滚动数组优化？
q_en: When should you ask the AI to optimize with a rolling array?
options: 测试失败时用滚动数组掩盖问题
一开始就优化，哪怕状态还没定义清楚
永远不要优化
确认正确性后，且空间约束或输入规模需要时
options_en: Use a rolling array to paper over a failing test.
Optimize from the very start, even before the state is clearly defined.
Never optimize at all.
Only after correctness is confirmed, and only when memory constraints or input size justify it.
why: 先有可读可验证版本，再优化空间。滚动数组会增加索引复杂度，不应该用来替代正确性验证。
why_en: Space optimization should come after the clear DP version is correct and memory pressure justifies it.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试明确要求 O(1) 或 O(n) 空间，可以较早讨论滚动数组，但仍要先说清依赖关系。
tradeoff: 先正确后优化（二维表更易调试，滚动数组延后）vs 一开始就滚动数组（省内存但索引更难验证，容易掩盖 bug）
optionMeanings: 把优化手段用错了地方：拿来掩盖一个还没定位的 bug。
在状态本身还没验证清楚时就急着做空间优化。
完全拒绝任何空间优化，哪怕面试明确要求。
正确顺序：先在二维表上验证递推和 base case 全对，再按需要压缩空间。
optionScenarioImpacts: 滚动数组会让索引变得更难读，掩盖问题只会让根因更难定位。
状态定义如果本身有误，优化后的代码只是更难调试的错误代码。
有些面试明确限制空间复杂度，完全不优化会答不到点上。
先用二维表核对手推例子和测试，通过后再优化，风险和收益都更可控。
optionDirectness: 不直接；这是滥用优化手段掩盖未解决的 bug。
不直接；顺序反了，正确性应该先于空间优化。
不直接；完全不考虑面试要求空间复杂度的情况。
最直接；这是文章给出的正确顺序：先验证，再按需优化。
optionMeanings_en: Misapplies an optimization technique to hide a bug that has not been located yet.
Rushes into space optimization before the state itself has been verified.
Refuses any space optimization at all, even when the interviewer explicitly asks for it.
The correct order: first verify the recurrence and base cases on the 2D table, then compress space if needed.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A rolling array makes indices harder to read, and hiding a problem only makes the root cause harder to find.
If the state definition itself is wrong, the optimized code is just harder-to-debug wrong code.

把代码里的注释全部删掉

Skip testing and submit this solution directly.
Delete all the comments from the code.
Give me a small input where this greedy strategy could fail.

让 AI 忽略容量检查以简化代码

Claim outright that the solution is guaranteed optimal.

q: 审查 AI 生成的贪心解时，应按哪些维度检查？

是否跑过 adversarial（对抗性）测试用例
NP-hard 问题是否被错误地声称为精确最优
options_en: What exactly the greedy choice is.
Whether the greedy-choice property holds, or a counterexample exists.
Whether adversarial test cases were run.
Whether an NP-hard problem is wrongly claimed to be exactly optimal.

q: 下面哪组测试输入最能暴露这个策略不总是最优？
q_en: Which test input best exposes that this strategy is not always optimal?
codeSample:
while amount > 0:
    coin = max(c for c in coins if c <= amount)
    amount -= coin
    used.append(coin)
options: coins=[1,5,10,25], amount=30
coins=[1], amount=3
coins=[1,3,4], amount=6
coins=[1,2], amount=4

coins = [1], amount = 3
coins = [1, 3, 4], amount = 6
coins = [1, 2], amount = 4

q: 把贪心题的 AI 面试工作流按顺序排列。
q_en: Put the AI interview workflow for greedy problems in order.
steps: 提示 AI 实现具体策略，并说明 exact 还是 heuristic。
识别优化目标和自然排序键。
寻找小反例或给出交换论证。
明确每一步的贪心选择。
用 adversarial tests 验证策略和边界。
why: 贪心不能先写代码再补理由：先说清选择、验证它，再让 AI 实现，最后用反例式测试守住正确性。
why_en: A solid greedy workflow names the ordering and choice, proves or refutes it, then implements and adversarially tests it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Name[Name greedy choice] --> Test[Try counterexample]
  Test --> Proof[Explain why safe]
  Proof --> Code[Ask AI to code]
  Code --> Adversarial[Run adversarial tests]

q: 下面哪些现实场景本质上是 bin packing 问题？
q_en: Which real-world scenarios are essentially bin-packing problems?
options: 把任务分配到内存容量固定的服务器上

课程排序关心的是顺序合法性，不是容量装箱。

经典的物流装箱场景，装箱算法的原型问题。

这其实是拓扑排序问题，不是装箱问题。

q: AI 注释说“FFD 返回最优装箱数”，你应该怎样处理？
q_en: If an AI comment says FFD returns the optimal bin count, how should you handle it?

scenario: 你要计算至少需要多少服务器处理一批有开始/结束时间的任务。

q: 本质上，这个“最少服务器数”问题要追踪的是什么量？

q: 一个真实日志分析器可能组合哪些层？
q_en: What layers might a real log analyzer combine?

diagram:
flowchart LR
  Raw[Raw log text] --> Records[Record boundaries]
  Records --> Regex[Extract fields]
  Regex --> Classify[Classify known signatures]
  Classify --> Aggregate[Aggregate results]
optionMeanings: 判断一条堆栈跟踪是否属于同一个逻辑日志条目，跨越多行。
从每行结构化文本里切出各个字段，供下游使用。
把已抽出的错误码和已知签名集合比对，做分类。
中位数统计和日志分析器的分层设计无关。

Slices each structured line into fields for downstream use.
Compares extracted error codes against a known signature set to classify them.
A running median has nothing to do with a log analyzer's layering.

diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Raw log line] --> B[Regex tokenize]

C --> D[Normalize fields]
D --> E[Aggregate results]

q: 最合适的第一版策略是什么？
q_en: What is the best first-version strategy?
options: 按行列完整扫描所有格子，射击后检查 `all_sunk()`
随机射击，直到某艘船返回 SUNK 就停手
只打 `(row + col) % 3 == 0` 的格子，命中后也不追击
从棋盘四个角同时向中心搜索
options_en: Scan every cell row by row, firing and checking `all_sunk()` after each shot
Fire at random cells and stop as soon as any single SUNK comes back
Only fire at cells where `(row + col) % 3 == 0`, and never chase after a hit
Search inward from all four corners of the board toward the center
tradeoff: 确定性覆盖保证 vs 射击预算效率
why: 完整扫描利用棋盘有限这一事实保证正确性，并且实现最少。它的问题不是会漏船，而是不会利用 HIT 信息。
why_en: A full scan is the simplest correctness baseline because a finite grid guarantees every ship cell is eventually probed.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是通过平均枪数测试，而不是只验证最终击沉，稀疏 hunt 加 target 模式会更合适。

q: 下面哪行控制流最应该保留？
q_en: Which control-flow line should you keep?
options: `continue`，继续扫完这一行
`return`，立刻结束求解
`break`，只跳出内层循环再扫下一行
`random.shuffle(shots)`，打乱历史记录

`return` — stop the solver immediately
`break` — only exit the inner column loop, then move to the next row
`random.shuffle(shots)` — shuffle the recorded shot history

self.board.check_shot(row, col)
self.shots.append((row, col))
if self.board.all_sunk():
    return

whenOtherWins: 如果 API 要求输出完整覆盖轨迹而不是最少枪数，扫完棋盘才可能有意义。

q: 完整扫描在 n x n 棋盘上的最坏射击次数是多少量级？

O(n log n)
O(3n)

O(n log n) — linearithmic in the board dimension
O(n^2) — quadratic in the board dimension

q: 完整扫描和 hunt+target 的关键区别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between full scan and hunt+target?
options: 完整扫描会重复打同一格，hunt+target 永远不会
完整扫描的下一枪不看上一枪反馈，hunt+target 会根据 HIT/SUNK 调整下一枪
完整扫描需要用 BFS，hunt+target 完全不需要队列
完整扫描只能对付 3 格船，hunt+target 只能对付 2 格船

Full scan ignores prior feedback for its next shot, hunt+target reshapes the next shot from HIT/SUNK
Full scan needs BFS, hunt+target needs no queue at all
Full scan only handles 3-cell ships, hunt+target only handles 2-cell ships

why_en: The optimized solver closes the loop by feeding shot feedback into the next-shot decision.

q: 填空：当最短船长是 3 时，打所有满足 {{(row + col) % 3 == 0}} 的格子可以保证每艘 3 格直船至少被碰到一次。

text: 当最短船长是 3 时，打所有满足 {{(row + col) % 3 == 0}} 的格子可以保证每艘 3 格直船至少被碰到一次。
why: 任意连续 3 个整数的模 3 余数会覆盖 0、1、2。横船和竖船的 row+col 都形成连续值，所以三格船必有一格落在 hunt 集合里。

q: 为什么 mod-3 hunt 对 3 格横船和竖船都成立？
q_en: Why does mod-3 hunt work for both horizontal and vertical 3-cell ships?
options: 横向相邻时 col 每次加 1，row+col 连续变化
纵向相邻时 row 每次加 1，row+col 连续变化
三个连续整数的模 3 余数一定各出现一次
所有船都必须从 `(0, 0)` 开始
options_en: For a horizontal ship, col increases by 1 each step, so row+col changes by 1 each time
For a vertical ship, row increases by 1 each step, so row+col changes by 1 each time
Any three consecutive integers hit every residue mod three exactly once
Every ship must start at `(0, 0)`
why: 证明只依赖轴对齐和长度至少 3。它不依赖船出现在哪一行、哪一列。
why_en: The guarantee follows from axis alignment and three consecutive sums, not from any particular ship location.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取模运算：整数除以 3 后的余数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo three is the remainder left after dividing an integer by three.

scenario: 舰队里最短船长为 3，你想在不知道位置的情况下减少搜索格子，同时不能漏掉任何船。

q_en: Which hunt set should you choose?

why: mod-3 格局大约覆盖三分之一棋盘，却对所有 3 格以上直船保留一次命中保证。其它集合没有通用覆盖证明。
why_en: The modulo-three hunt pattern cuts the search space while retaining a formal coverage guarantee for length-three ships.
whenOtherWins: 如果最短船长变成 2，就应该改用更密的 mod-2 奇偶模式或其它覆盖方案。

termDefinitions.meaning: hunt 阶段用的稀疏格局：只打行列坐标之和能被 3 整除的格子，即 (row + col) % 3 == 0。

q: 位置空间和点数直方图空间在这个题里的关键差异是什么？

hist only tracks how many empty slots remain on the grid.

scenario_en: You are enumerating `(v1, v2, v3)` in value space and want to avoid counting the same value combination in multiple orders.
q: 为什么循环和检查要维持 `v1 <= v2 <= v3`？
q_en: Why should the loops and checks maintain `v1 <= v2 <= v3`?
options: 为了让目标和的数值变大
为了把同一组点数只枚举一次，并统一处理重复值的库存要求
为了保证选出的三张牌来自同一花色
为了直接跳过所有包含重复点数的组合
why: 排序约束去掉排列重复，比如 7,9,23 不会再以 9,7,23 出现。重复值仍允许，只是要检查库存数量。
why_en: Maintaining sorted value triples removes permutation duplicates while still allowing repeated values when counts permit.
whenOtherWins: 如果后续逻辑需要区分牌的顺序或位置角色，就不能把这些排列合并。
options_en: To make the target sum value larger.
To enumerate each value combination only once and uniformly handle repeated-value inventory checks.
To guarantee the three cards come from the same suit.
To skip every combination that contains a repeated value.
tradeoff: 排序约束去重 vs 允许值顺序自由但产生重复枚举

q: 值三元组枚举中，哪些重复值库存检查是必要的？

v1 == v2（前两个点数相同）时，该点数至少要有 2 张

why_en: Repeated-value triples are valid only when the histogram has enough physical cards of that value.
options_en: When v1 == v2 == v3, that value needs at least three physical cards.
When v1 == v2 (the first two match), that value needs at least two cards.
When v2 == v3 (the last two match), that value needs at least two cards.
Every legal triple must have three mutually different values.

scenario: 你要给几百个值三元组候选做一层 lookahead，热点循环里不想为每个候选复制数组。
scenario_en: You are scoring hundreds of value-triple candidates with one-step lookahead and do not want to copy arrays inside the hot loop.
q: lookahead 热循环里应该用什么实现技巧？
q_en: What implementation trick should the lookahead hot loop use?
options: 每次都深拷贝整个网格对象
把所有候选先写入磁盘，排序后再处理
原地把三个值的计数减一，评分后再加回来
直接禁用所有包含重复点数的候选
codeSample:
hist[v1] -= 1; hist[v2] -= 1; hist[v3] -= 1
score = self._count_value_triples(hist)
hist[v1] += 1; hist[v2] += 1; hist[v3] += 1
why: 减一再恢复避免了热循环中的大量分配。只要恢复严格成对执行，外层状态保持正确。
why_en: In-place decrement-and-restore keeps lookahead allocation-free in the hot loop.
whenOtherWins: 如果代码可读性比速度更重要且候选很少，复制直方图会更不容易写错。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Hist[hist before] --> Minus[minus candidate]
  Minus --> Score[score rest]
  Score --> Restore[add counts back]
  Restore --> Next[next candidate]
options_en: Deep-copy the entire grid object for every candidate.
Write every candidate to disk and sort them before processing.
Decrement the three value counts in place, score, then add them back.
Simply disable any candidate that contains a repeated value.
tradeoff: 原地减一/加回换取零分配 vs 深拷贝换取更简单但更慢的实现

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接修改已有数据结构而不复制新副本，省内存分配，但要小心把状态恢复原样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-place mutation edits the existing data structure directly instead of copying it, saving allocation cost but requiring careful state restoration.

把选中的点数值本身原封不动地直接传给 play_move 函数

options: 前者的判断天生更准确，后者给出的结果几乎总是错的

options_en: The former's judgment is inherently more accurate, and the latter's result is almost always wrong.

q: 共同好友计数的典型实现为什么是 O(min(|A|, |B|))？

Assume the mutual friend count is capped at one, so no traversal is needed.
Iterate the smaller friend set and probe the larger one as a hash set for constant expected lookups.

why: hash set membership 期望常数时间。遍历较小集合能把交集成本压到较小度数。
why_en: Set intersection is cheap when you iterate the smaller set and probe the larger hash set.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: O of the minimum of the two set sizes means the cost scales with whichever friend set is smaller.

q: scan-all 每次查询的复杂度该如何近似？

options: O(d²)：这其实是二跳版本的量级，不是 scan-all 的
O(1)：因为最终只返回 5 个名字，跟用户规模无关
O(2^V)：把每种好友组合都枚举一遍
O(V·d)：外层扫 V 个用户，每个候选做一次度数级交集
options_en: O of d squared — that is actually the two-hop version's magnitude, not scan-all's.
O of one, because only five names are ultimately returned, independent of network size.
O of two to the V, by enumerating every possible friend combination.
O of V times d — the outer loop scans V users and each candidate pays one degree-sized intersection.
why: 全量扫描的成本随全网用户数 V 增长。返回上限 5 不会消除前面的候选检查。
why_en: The scan-all approach scales with the whole network size, not just the returned five names.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图论里一个节点的度数，等于它的好友数量。

options: 这个提速只对 huge 数据集成立，换数据集就会反转
361.8ms 已经说明 scan-all 存在 bug，需要重写而不是优化
二跳遍历把候选空间从全网收窄到局部邻域，带来约 48 倍的实测提速

options_en: This speedup only holds for the huge dataset and would reverse on a different one.
The 361.8 millisecond result proves scan-all has a bug that needs a rewrite, not an optimization.
The two-hop walk narrows the candidate space from the whole network to a local neighborhood, giving roughly a 48x measured speedup.
Both algorithms have identical asymptotic complexity, differing only by a constant factor.
why: benchmark 量化了候选空间收窄带来的真实收益：48 倍不是常数因子差异，而是从 O(V·d) 降到局部邻域的结构性变化。
why_en: The benchmark quantifies a real structural win: the 48x gap comes from narrowing the candidate space, not from a constant-factor tweak.

q: Inventory Packer 的题目规则包括哪些？

item 不能拆分到多个 bin

options_en: Every item has both a weight and a size.

termDefinitions.meaning: weight cap：bin 允许承载的总重量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight cap is the maximum total weight a bin is allowed to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

scenario: Bin 0 已经放了 Monitor(8kg,6size) 和 Keyboard(2kg,3size)，两者 weight 加起来是 10，正好把这个 bin 的 weight cap 用满；size 只用了 9。
scenario_en: Bin 0 already holds Monitor (8 kg, size 6) and Keyboard (2 kg, size 3). Their total weight is 10, exactly filling the weight cap, while size used is only 9.
q: 为什么这时候 Mouse(1kg,1size) 不能放进同一个 bin？
q_en: Why can Mouse (1 kg, size 1) not go into the same bin now?
options: 它说明 size cap 在这个例子里可以忽略不计
它说明 Monitor 和 Keyboard 应该拆开分别装到两个 bin
它说明只要某一个维度（weight 或 size）满了，就算另一个维度还有空间，也不能再放入新 item
它说明之后所有物品都必须各自新开一个 bin
options_en: It shows the size cap can be ignored in this example.
It shows the Monitor and Keyboard should be split across two bins.
It shows that once either dimension, weight or size, is full, no new item can be placed even if the other dimension still has room.
It shows every later item must open its own separate bin from then on.
why: weight 和 size 都是硬约束，任一维度超限都非法。装箱判断必须同时检查两个维度。
why_en: A bin is feasible only when both weight and size limits remain satisfied.

termDefinitions.meaning: weight cap：bin 允许承载的总重量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight cap is the maximum total weight a bin is allowed to hold.

termDefinitions.meaning: size cap：bin 允许占用的总体积/尺寸上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A size cap is the maximum total size or volume a bin is allowed to hold.

q: 填空：找到绝对最少 bin 数的通用 bin packing 是 {{NP-hard}}，所以 Inventory Packer 采用快速 {{heuristic}}。
q_en: Fill in: Finding the absolute minimum bin count for general bin packing is {{NP-hard}}, so Inventory Packer uses a fast {{heuristic}}.
text: 找到绝对最少 bin 数的通用 bin packing 是 {{NP-hard}}，所以 Inventory Packer 采用快速 {{heuristic}}。
why: 题目要的是在测试输入上接近最优且足够快，而不是证明全局最优。贪心启发式是合理选择。
why_en: Because exact bin packing is NP-hard, the practical goal is a fast near-optimal heuristic.

q: First-Fit 的规则是什么？
q_en: What is the First-Fit rule?
options: 对每个 item 都尝试所有已开 bin 的组合，挑出全局最优的分配方案
按输入顺序处理每个 item，放进第一个能同时满足两个容量的已开 bin；都放不下才新开一个 bin
把 item 和 bin 都随机打乱，反复重排直到凑出一个合法分配
不管当前 bin 是否还有空间，每个 item 都直接新开一个独立 bin
options_en: Try every combination across all opened bins for each item and pick the globally optimal assignment.
Process items in input order and place each one in the first already-open bin that satisfies both capacity limits; open a new bin only if none fit.
Shuffle items and bins randomly and keep reshuffling until a legal assignment appears.
Open a brand-new bin for every item regardless of whether an existing bin still has room.
why: First-Fit 是纯贪心：第一个合法位置就提交，不回头。它实现简单且保证约束有效。
why_en: First-Fit greedily places each item into the first existing bin that can hold it.
tradeoff: 先合法即提交的贪心速度 vs 穷举比较求全局最优
whenOtherWins: 如果输入顺序对抗性强，先排序的 First-Fit Decreasing 通常更稳。

The item's size must not exceed the bin's remaining size capacity.
The item's name must sort alphabetically before the bin id.
Both capacity conditions must pass before the item can be placed.
why: 两个 cap 任一超限都不能放。正确性测试会抓住只检查一个维度的实现。
why_en: A fit check must require both remaining weight and remaining size to be sufficient.

q: 为什么 `break` 很关键？

break 触发后会自动新开一个 bin，把当前 item 重新放进这个新开的 bin 里
break 会让后面所有 bin 的两个容量检查都被跳过，从而让放置流程整体变快
item 已经放置成功；继续扫描后面的 bin 可能造成重复放置，或者把 assignment 记录覆盖成错误的 bin id

Triggering break automatically opens a new bin and re-places the current item into that new bin.
break skips both capacity checks on every remaining bin, making the whole placement loop faster.

why: First-Fit 的定义就是第一个能放就停。继续循环既浪费，也可能覆盖记录。
why_en: First-Fit commits to the first feasible bin, so the bin loop must stop after placement.

q: First-Fit 装 n 个物品、已开 b 个 bin 时总体复杂度如何描述？

options: O(log n)，因为每次放置都在做二分查找
O(n · b)，最坏情况 b = n 时退化为 O(n²)
O(2ⁿ)，因为要枚举所有子集
O(1)，因为每个 item 只放一次就结束
options_en: O(log n), because each placement does a binary search.
O(n times b), which degrades to O(n squared) in the worst case when b equals n.
O(2 to the n), because it enumerates every subset.
O(1), because each item is placed exactly once.
why: 每个 item 最多扫一遍已有 bin，n×b 是 O(n·b)；最坏每个物品都新开 bin 时 b=n，退化成 O(n²)。这说明千级 catalog 下 First-Fit 仍够快，不必换算法。
why_en: First-Fit scans existing bins for each item, so n items times b bins gives O(n·b), which only degrades to O(n squared) when every item opens its own bin.

O(b), because the sorting overhead can be ignored entirely.

q: 实现 Inventory Packer 时，哪些是常见的 bug 或风险？

options: 放入第一个可行 bin 后忘记 break
新开 bin 后忘记 add item
新开 bin 后忘记记录 item name 到 bin id
对已放入 item 再进行全局最优证明
options_en: Placing an item into the first feasible bin and forgetting to break out of the loop.
Opening a new bin but forgetting to add the item into it.
Opening a new bin but forgetting to record the item name against its bin id.
Trying to prove a global optimum for items that are already placed.
why: 这些都是会让合法 assignment 或记录出错的实现细节。全局最优证明不是本文启发式的目标。
why_en: The common bugs are placement-control and assignment-recording mistakes.

why: warehouse 内部状态和返回 map 都要一致。只把 item 加进 bin 而不记录 assignment 也会失败。
why_en: The returned assignment maps each item name to the id of the bin containing it.

scenario: 一个 item 太大，不能和当前 bin 的剩余 weight 或 size 同时兼容。
scenario_en: An item is too large to fit within the current bin's remaining weight or size at the same time.
q: 算法应该怎么处理这个 item？
q_en: How should the algorithm handle this item?
options: 临时提高这个 bin 的容量上限来放下它
不能拆分这个 item；继续尝试下一个 bin，如果都放不下就新开一个 bin
把 item 的 weight 放进一个 bin、size 放进另一个 bin
直接丢弃这个放不下的 item
options_en: Temporarily raise this bin's capacity cap to fit the item.
The item cannot be split; keep trying the next bin, and open a new bin if none of them fit.
Put the item's weight in one bin and its size in another bin.
Just drop the item that does not fit.
why: 题目明确 item 不可拆分。启发式只能改变放入哪个 bin，不能改变约束本身。
why_en: Items are indivisible, so the solver must find one feasible bin or open a new one.
tradeoff: 遵守不可拆分约束、只挑 bin vs 违规拆分约束换取放置成功率
whenOtherWins: 如果业务允许拆分装运，问题会变成不同的流量或线性规划模型。

why_en: FFD also improves the basic catalog from four bins to three.

q: Inventory Packer 这道装箱题体现了哪些 greedy/bin-packing 模式？
q_en: Which greedy and bin-packing patterns does Inventory Packer illustrate?
options: First-Fit：第一个可行位置即提交
First-Fit Decreasing：先按 footprint 降序再 First-Fit
Best-Fit Decreasing：可作为更强变体
minimax alpha-beta
options_en: First-Fit: commit to the first feasible position immediately.
First-Fit Decreasing: sort by descending footprint, then run First-Fit.
Best-Fit Decreasing: a stronger variant worth naming.
Minimax alpha-beta pruning.
why: 前三个都是装箱启发式家族。minimax 属于对抗搜索，不是本题主线。
why_en: The relevant pattern family is greedy bin-packing heuristics.

termDefinitions.meaning: FFD：先把 item 按 footprint 降序排序，再运行同一套 First-Fit 放置逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit Decreasing sorts items by descending footprint first and then runs the same First-Fit placement loop.

termDefinitions.meaning: BFD：先按 footprint 降序排序，再把 item 放进剩余空间最少但仍可行的 bin。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Best-Fit Decreasing sorts by descending footprint and places each item into the feasible bin with the least remaining room.

termDefinitions.meaning: First-Fit：贪心装箱策略，把每个 item 放进当前扫描到的第一个可行 bin，不比较其它选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First-Fit is a greedy bin-packing rule that places each item into the first bin that fits, without comparing other options.

termDefinitions.meaning: footprint：本文用 weight + size 估计一个 item 有多难放，值越大越难放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Footprint here is the weight-plus-size estimate of how hard an item is to place; a larger footprint means a harder fit.

termDefinitions.meaning: greedy（贪心算法）：每一步都选当前看起来最好的选项，不回头也不做全局比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step without backtracking or global comparison.

scenario: 你的贪心算法对输入顺序特别敏感，而且坏顺序会让早期选择堵住后续选择。
scenario_en: Your greedy algorithm is highly sensitive to input order, and a bad order lets early choices block later ones.
q: 从 Inventory Packer 这个案例最该迁移到其他题目的修复动作是什么？
q_en: What repair move from Inventory Packer is most useful to transfer to other problems?
options: 把之前所有的早期选择全部删除重来
不再对任何放置结果做合法性检查
把最终输出结果直接随机打乱
在贪心之前，先按“处理难度”对输入排序
options_en: Delete every earlier greedy choice and start over.
Stop validating the legality of any placement result.
Randomize the final output order.
Sort the input by how hard each item is to place before running the greedy pass.
why: sort-before-greedy 是很多贪心题的关键预处理。它不能保证全局最优，但常能消除对抗性输入顺序。
why_en: Sorting by difficulty before a greedy pass is a common way to reduce order sensitivity.
tradeoff: 排序预处理换顺序鲁棒性 vs 零预处理但对输入顺序敏感
whenOtherWins: 如果贪心选择不受输入顺序影响，排序可能只是额外开销。

q: 为什么不能直接把一维 FFD 的近似证明套到 Inventory Packer 这种两维装箱问题上？
q_en: Why can't you directly apply the one-dimensional FFD approximation proof to this two-dimensional Inventory Packer problem?
options: 本文同时有 weight 和 size 两个 cap，排序 key 又是启发式的 weight+size 之和
本文其实只有一个容量维度，跟经典的一维 bin packing 完全一样，没有第二个约束
本文允许把同一个 item 拆分成几份，分别装进不同的 bin 里去
经典一维 FFD 从一开始就没有被证明过任何近似比的上界
options_en: This problem has two caps, weight and size, and its sort key is the heuristic weight-plus-size sum.
This problem actually has only one capacity dimension, just like classic one-dimensional bin packing, with no second constraint.
This problem allows splitting a single item into pieces placed across different bins.
The classic one-dimensional FFD bound was never proven to have any approximation ratio upper bound at all.
why: 经典证明假设单一容量维度。两维装箱更复杂，sum key 只是实用启发式。
why_en: The classic FFD bound assumes one capacity dimension, while this problem has two.

scenario: 你要实现 bin 的可放入判断，避免只检查一个容量维度。
scenario_en: You need to implement the bin fit check without accidentally checking only one capacity dimension.
q: 下面哪种逻辑符合题意？
q_en: Which logic matches the problem requirements?
options: 只要 weight 足够就返回 true，不看 size
只要 size 足够就返回 true，不看 weight
剩余 weight 足够，并且剩余 size 也足够，才返回 true
永远返回 true，放完再回头修复超限的 bin
options_en: Return true whenever weight is enough, without checking size.
Return true whenever size is enough, without checking weight.
Return true only when both remaining weight and remaining size are enough.
Always return true and fix any overfull bins after the fact.
codeSample: return item.weight <= self.remaining_weight and item.size <= self.remaining_size
why: 两个 cap 是同时约束，不是二选一。can_fit 是所有贪心放置的正确性底座。
why_en: The fit predicate must enforce both dimensions before an item is placed.
tradeoff: 同时校验两个维度（正确） vs 只校验一个维度（更快但不合法）
whenOtherWins: 如果业务只有一个容量维度，检查逻辑可以退化为一维 bin packing。

q: 四个相同 item 测试中，为什么 FFD 不会比 First-Fit 更好？
q_en: Why does FFD not beat First-Fit on the four-identical-item test?
options: FFD 在完全相同的 item 上会被禁用，直接报错
所有 item 的 footprint 完全一样，排序没办法改变有意义的处理顺序
First-Fit 在这种情况下会自动做全局搜索
完全相同的 item 不受任何容量限制
options_en: FFD is disabled and errors out on fully identical items.
Every item has the exact same footprint, so sorting cannot change the order in any meaningful way.
First-Fit automatically performs a global search in this case.
Fully identical items are exempt from any capacity limit.
why: 排序只在不同物品的难放程度有差异时提供信息。同质输入里顺序没有可利用的结构。
why_en: Sorting helps only when items differ in how hard they are to place.

scenario: 面试官问如果 FFD 还不够好，你会怎么继续。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what you would try next if FFD still is not good enough.
q: 最好的回答组合是什么？
q_en: What is the best answer combination?
options: 直接告诉面试官，这个装箱方案已经没有任何办法可以再继续改进了，只能维持现状
建议删掉 weight 或 size 两个容量约束中的一个，用简化问题换取更少的 bin 数
建议把一部分 item 随机丢弃掉，用减少物品总数来减少最终的 bin 数
先提 Best-Fit Decreasing 作为小幅改进，再提 branch-and-bound/IP 作为小输入下的精确解
options_en: Just tell the interviewer there is no way to improve this packing further and it must stay as is.
Suggest dropping either the weight or the size constraint to simplify the problem into fewer bins.
Suggest randomly discarding some items so fewer total items means fewer bins.
Name Best-Fit Decreasing as a small average-case improvement, then branch-and-bound or IP as an exact option for small inputs.
why: 这展示你知道启发式和精确解的边界。BFD 是近似改进，搜索/IP 是精确但更慢的逃生口。
why_en: Naming BFD and exact search options shows the tradeoff between heuristic quality and optimality.
tradeoff: 近似小改进（BFD）先说 vs 精确但慢的搜索（branch-and-bound/IP）留作备选
whenOtherWins: 如果当前 FFD 已满足测试和业务 SLA，继续加复杂度未必值得。

q: Kitchen Orders 的问题建模里，哪些对象是核心？

options: order 由多个 dish 组成
每个 dish 有固定的 recipe step 顺序
每个 step 占用一个 station 和一个 chef
一个 chef 可以同时做多个 step

Each dish has a fixed order of recipe steps.
Each step occupies one station and one chef.
A chef can work on multiple steps at the same time.
why: 每个 dish 内部有前置关系约束，每个 step 还要同时占用一个 station 和一个 chef；chef 同一时间只能做一件事。
why_en: The scheduling problem combines per-dish step order with chef and station resource constraints.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一道 dish 内部固定顺序的 station step 链，后一步必须等前一步完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recipe is a dish's fixed chain of station steps, where each step must wait for the previous one to finish.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

scenario: Kitchen Orders 里，每道菜的 recipe 是一串固定顺序的 station 步骤，后一步要等前一步做完。
scenario_en: In Kitchen Orders, each dish has a recipe: a fixed sequence of station steps where each step waits for the previous one.
q: 下面哪些 recipe 步骤顺序符合 Burger、Salad、Pasta 的定义？
q_en: Which recipe step orders match the definitions of Burger, Salad, and Pasta?
options: Burger: PREP 30 -> GRILL 90
Salad: PREP 30 -> CHOP 60
Pasta: PREP 30 -> CHOP 60 -> GRILL 90
Burger: CHOP 60 -> PREP 30
options_en: Burger: PREP 30 then GRILL 90.
Salad: PREP 30 then CHOP 60.
Pasta: PREP 30 then CHOP 60 then GRILL 90.
Burger: CHOP 60 then PREP 30.
why: 这些固定顺序定义了每个 dish 内部的前置关系，调度器只能在不同 dish 之间交错，不能打乱同一 dish 内部顺序。
why_en: Recipes impose a fixed step sequence within each dish, and only the order across different dishes can be rearranged.

scenario: 你要判断后面搜索版能不能把 chef 选择直接固定成每个 station 的 specialist。
scenario_en: You need to decide whether the search version can pin chef choice to each station's specialist.
q: 填空：三个 specialist 的快速时间是 PREP {{15}}、CHOP {{30}}、GRILL {{45}} 秒。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: the specialist fast times are PREP {{15}}, CHOP {{30}}, and GRILL {{45}} seconds.
text: 三个 specialist 的快速时间是 PREP {{15}}、CHOP {{30}}、GRILL {{45}} 秒。
why: base time 乘以 specialist 的 0.5 factor 得到最快时间；non-specialist 是 1.5 factor，慢了三倍。这个三倍速度差正是后面把 chef 选择固定成 specialist 剪枝的依据。
why_en: Specialists run a station at half the base time while non-specialists take three times as long, and that gap is what later lets the search pin the chef choice to the specialist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 station 上速度是 0.5 factor 的 chef，比其余 1.5 factor 的 chef 快三倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialist is the one chef who runs a given station at half the base time, three times faster than a non-specialist there.

q: 一个 schedule 必须满足哪些约束？

options: 同一 dish 的 step 必须按 recipe 顺序运行
一个 chef 同一时间只能做一个 step
一个 station 同一时间只能被一个 chef 使用
不同 dish 不能交错执行
options_en: Steps within the same dish must run in recipe order.
A chef can work on only one step at a time.
A station can be used by only one chef at a time.
Different dishes are never allowed to interleave.
why: 不同 dish 其实可以交错，这正是优化空间；约束来自 dish precedence、chef 资源和 station 资源三者。
why_en: A valid schedule respects dish precedence plus one-at-a-time chef and station resources.

why: 105 秒是这单的真实最优解；后面两版 greedy 在同一 order 上都产出 135 秒，这 30 秒差距就是评估它们结构性缺陷的基准。
why_en: 105 seconds is the true optimum for this order, and it is the benchmark against which the greedy schedulers' 135-second results expose their structural flaw.

q: 第一版 greedy pass 的策略是什么？
q_en: What is the strategy of the first greedy pass?
options: 对所有 step 排列做穷举搜索并证明最优
按 dish 和 step 顺序推进，每步交给能最早完成的 chef
随机挑选 station，不管是否空闲
忽略同一 dish 内部的 step 先后顺序
options_en: Exhaustively search every step permutation and prove optimality.
Walk dishes and steps in order, assigning each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.
Pick a station at random regardless of whether it is free.
Ignore the recipe order of steps within the same dish.
why: 这版保证约束有效且实现简单，代价是过早固定了 dish 顺序。
why_en: The first greedy pass schedules dishes in input order and assigns each step to the earliest-finishing chef.
whenOtherWins: 如果只要求合法 schedule 或输入很小且目标宽松，这个基线足够好写。
tradeoff: 一次性锁定 dish 顺序、实现简单 vs 交给搜索去找更优顺序

A random chef, without comparing finish times.

options: PREP station 因为唯一的 specialist 请假而空闲
Pasta chop 排在 Salad 后面，grill 60 到 90 秒空闲
Alice 这个 chef 完全不会操作 grill 站
所有 chef 都被安排同时做多个 step
options_en: The PREP station sits idle because its only specialist is off shift.
Pasta's chop is queued behind Salad's, leaving the grill idle from 60 to 90 seconds.
Alice, one of the chefs, does not know how to run the grill station.
Every chef is scheduled to work on multiple steps at the same time.
why: Burger grill 60 秒结束后，Pasta 还没完成 chop，只能等到 90 秒；这个空档就是 30 秒差距的来源。
why_en: The greedy order delays Pasta's chop, leaving the grill idle before Pasta can use it.

q: 为什么说“问题不在换个更好的 chef”？
q_en: Why is the problem not simply picking a better chef?
options: 所有 chef 的速度参数完全一样，换谁都没区别
station 没有任何容量限制，可以并行处理
greedy 已用 specialists，浪费来自 step 顺序排空 grill
makespan 这个指标根本不受 step 顺序影响
options_en: Every chef's speed factor is exactly the same, so swapping chefs changes nothing.
Stations have no capacity limit at all and can run steps in parallel.
Greedy already uses the specialists; the waste comes from step order leaving the grill idle.
The makespan metric is not affected by step order at all.
why: Pasta 晚到 grill 不是因为 chef 慢，而是因为 Pasta 的上一步排晚了，需要优化的是 ordering。
why_en: The bottleneck is step ordering, not a failure to pick the station specialists.
tradeoff: 把浪费归因于 chef 选择 vs 把浪费归因于 step 顺序（ordering）

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 station 上速度是 0.5 factor 的 chef，比其余 1.5 factor 的 chef 快三倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialist is the one chef who runs a given station at half the base time, three times faster than a non-specialist there.

scenario_en: You want to stop walking dishes strictly in input order and allow ready steps from different dishes to interleave.
q: 第二版 dispatch 策略是什么？
q_en: What is the second dispatch strategy?
options: 继续按输入顺序做完第一个 dish 再做第二个 dish
随机选一个未完成的 step，完全不管前置关系
每轮从所有 dish 的 ready step 里选最早完成者提交
一次性把所有 step 都提前排给同一个 chef
options_en: Keep finishing dishes one at a time in strict input order.
Pick a random unfinished step while ignoring precedence entirely.
Each round, commit whichever ready step across all dishes finishes earliest.
Assign every step to the same single chef up front.
why: dispatch 延后了承诺时间，可以 interleave dishes，但仍是单向 greedy，不能撤销已选步骤。
why_en: Dispatch chooses the earliest-finishing ready step across dishes each round.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标只需要简单合法排程，dish-order greedy 更短；如果需要最优，dispatch 仍不够。
tradeoff: 延后承诺、按 ready step 交错 vs 提前锁定 dish 顺序

text: 任一时刻，每个未完成 dish 最多只有 {{一个}} ready step，也就是它的 {{下一道}} recipe step。
why: 同一 dish 内部步骤不能并行，后续 step 要等前一步完成，搜索候选只需要看每个 dish 的 next_step。
why_en: Each unfinished dish exposes only its next recipe step as a ready candidate.

scenario: dispatch 每轮有多个 ready step 候选，每个候选也要试所有 chefs。
scenario_en: In dispatch, each round has multiple ready-step candidates, and each candidate still tries all chefs.
q: `key = (end, start, index)` 的作用是什么？
q_en: What is `key = (end, start, index)` doing?
options: 计算这批 dish 的全局安全下界数值
判断这份 recipe 的内容是否出现重复
按完成时间、开始时间、dish index 做确定性 tie-break
强制只挑选速度最慢的那一个 chef
options_en: Compute a global safe lower bound across these dishes.
Check whether this recipe's content repeats.
Sort by finish time, start time, then dish index as a deterministic tie-break.
Force the selection of the single slowest available chef.
codeSample:
key = (end, start, index)
if best_key is None or key < best_key:
    best_key = key
    best_move = (index, dish, step_index, station, chef, start, end)
why: dispatch 仍然是局部最早完成规则，tie-break 只是让输出稳定，它没有全局 lookahead。
why_en: The dispatch key chooses the locally earliest-finishing ready step with deterministic tie-breaking.
whenOtherWins: 如果改成 branch-and-bound，候选排序只是搜索顺序，不能直接提交第一个。
tradeoff: 局部最早完成规则 vs 全局 lookahead/下界剪枝（dispatch 没有后者）

termDefinitions.meaning: 当多个候选的主要排序键相同时，用来确定唯一顺序的次要比较规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tie-break is a secondary comparison rule that produces one order when candidates are equal on the main sort key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

scenario: 你要评估 dispatch 在更大规模 order 上是否还跑得动。
scenario_en: You need to estimate whether dispatch still runs on larger orders.
q: dispatch 的复杂度如何描述？
q_en: How should dispatch complexity be described?
options: O(total steps!)，阶乘级增长
O(total steps * dishes * chefs)，三者相乘
O(stations only)，只由 station 数决定
O(1)，常数时间不随输入变化
options_en: O of total steps factorial, growing extremely fast.
O of total steps times dishes times chefs.
O of stations only, ignoring steps and chefs.
O of 1, constant time regardless of input.
why: 每放一个 step，都扫描所有 dish 的 ready step，并为每个候选试 chefs；仍然是多项式单向 pass。
why_en: Dispatch scans ready steps across dishes and tries chefs for each placed step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

q: dispatch 为什么仍然错过所有 targets？
q_en: Why does dispatch still miss all targets?
options: 它每次都会生成不满足约束的非法 schedule
它禁止任何两个不同 dish 互相交错执行
它完全忽视不同 chef 之间的速度差异
它每轮局部提交，无法撤销挡住后续关键资源的选择
options_en: It always produces an illegal schedule that breaks the constraints.
It forbids any two different dishes from interleaving at all.
It completely ignores the speed differences between chefs.
It commits locally each round and cannot undo a pick that later blocks a key resource.
why: dispatch 比按 dish 顺序聪明，但仍是单步 greedy，需要搜索 ordering 才能处理后悔成本。
why_en: Dispatch still commits greedily without lookahead or undo.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。

text: busy orders 上 dispatch 有改善，例如 six-dish 从 {{225}} 降到 {{210}}，nine-dish 从 {{285}} 降到 {{255}}。
why: dispatch 通过交错 dish 改善了忙碌 order，但仍没达到目标，说明只靠更聪明的单向规则还不够。
why_en: Dispatch improves busy schedules but still misses the optimal targets.

scenario: 两个 greedy 都生成合法但不够快的 schedule，真正难点是 step ordering。
scenario_en: Both greedy schedulers produce legal but too-slow schedules; the hard part is step ordering.
q: 第三版应该搜索什么？
q_en: What should the third version search over?
options: 搜索 ready step 顺序，配合 branch-and-bound 剪枝
搜索所有 chef 名字按字母排列的顺序组合
搜索所有 station 名字拼写方式的组合
只搜索第一个 dish 内部的 step 排列顺序
options_en: Search over ready-step orderings, pruned with branch-and-bound.
Search over alphabetical arrangements of chef names.
Search over combinations of station name spellings.
Search only the step ordering within the first dish.
why: 每个搜索节点选择一个 ready step，递归到剩余步骤；bound 负责砍掉不可能超过当前 best 的分支。
why_en: The optimal scheduler searches over ready-step orderings and prunes with branch-and-bound.
whenOtherWins: 如果 greedy 已满足 makespan target，完整搜索的复杂度可能不值得。
tradeoff: 对 step 排列做剪枝搜索 vs 继续用单向 greedy 规则
