termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

q: 填空：branch-and-bound 的 lower bound 必须是 {{乐观}} 估计，不能 {{高估}} 任何可完成 schedule 的最优 makespan。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: a branch-and-bound lower bound must be {{optimistic}} and must not {{overestimate}} the best possible makespan.
text: branch-and-bound 的 lower bound 必须是 {{乐观}} 估计，不能 {{高估}} 任何可完成 schedule 的最优 makespan。
why: 只有安全下界才能用于剪枝；如果下界可能高估，就可能剪掉真正更优的 schedule。
why_en: A pruning lower bound must be optimistic so it never discards a potentially optimal completion.

q: Kitchen Orders 的 lower bound 由哪些部分取最大值？
q_en: Which components are maxed together to form the Kitchen Orders lower bound?
options: 当前所有 chef/station 已忙到的最晚时间
每个 station 当前空闲时间 + 该 station 剩余最快工作量
每个 dish 当前 ready time + 该 dish 剩余最快 tail
随机选择的一个完整 schedule makespan
options_en: The latest time any chef or station is already busy until.
Each station's current free time plus its remaining fastest-chef workload.
Each dish's current ready time plus its remaining fastest-chef tail.
The makespan of a randomly chosen complete schedule.
why: 三个部分分别从资源占用、station 序列化和 dish precedence 给出乐观下界；取最大值仍是安全下界。
why_en: The bound combines resource occupancy, per-station remaining work, and per-dish remaining tails.

q: 把三 dish greedy 失败的因果链排成正确顺序。

steps: Pasta chop 被排在 Salad chop 后面，直到 90 秒才完成

q: 把流程排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the branch-and-bound scheduler flow in the correct order.
steps: 计算安全 lower bound，若不可能 beat 当前 best 就剪枝
枚举每个未完成 dish 的 next ready step，应用 symmetry cut
选择一个候选 step，更新 dish_ready、chef_free、station_free 后递归
完成所有 steps 时用 makespan 更新 best schedule
why: 搜索先用 bound 排除无望状态，再展开候选；完整 schedule 才能更新 incumbent。
why_en: The search prunes by bound, expands ready-step candidates, recurses on updated resources, and updates the incumbent at completion.

q: dish-order greedy 和 dispatch 的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between dish-order greedy and dispatch?
options: dispatch 会对已经提交的选择做完整回溯撤销
greedy 锁定 dish 顺序；dispatch 每轮选局部最早完成的 ready step
greedy 执行完就能证明自己达到全局最优解
dispatch 调度时完全不维护 station_free 状态
options_en: Dispatch fully backtracks and undoes choices it already committed.
Greedy locks in dish order up front; dispatch picks the locally earliest-finishing ready step each round.
Greedy can prove it reaches the global optimum once it finishes.
Dispatch never tracks station_free state at all.
why: dispatch 延迟了承诺并允许 interleaving，但仍没有搜索；两者都可能被局部选择卡住。
why_en: Dispatch interleaves dishes by choosing among ready steps, but it remains a greedy one-pass scheduler.
tradeoff: 一次性锁定 dish 顺序 vs 每轮重新挑 ready step（都不做搜索/回溯）

search 会无视 dish 内部固定的 recipe 顺序
dispatch 执行完就能保证达到全局最优解
search 完全不需要任何形式的 lower bound

Search ignores the fixed recipe order inside each dish.
Dispatch is guaranteed to reach the global optimum.
Search needs no lower bound of any kind.

q: 为什么这不适合作为 branch-and-bound 的 lower bound？
q_en: Why is this unsuitable as a branch-and-bound lower bound?
options: 高估会让搜索直接变成 O(1) 且仍然正确
lower bound 只要越大越好，不管准不准
高估只会影响打印的顺序，无关正确性
高估可能把真正最优的分支剪掉，破坏最优性保证

A lower bound just needs to be as large as possible, regardless of accuracy.
Overestimating only affects print order, not correctness.

q: Maximize Unique Characters 的合法解必须满足什么条件？
q_en: What condition must a valid Maximize Unique Characters solution satisfy?
options: 选出的所有单词按字典序连续
任意两个被选单词不能共享任何字符
只能选择长度相同的单词
必须覆盖完整字母表

q: 最自然的第一版搜索框架是什么？
q_en: What is the most natural first search framework?
options: 按字符做 BFS
对每个单词做 include/skip 回溯
把单词排序后贪心全选最长
动态规划枚举所有 26 位 mask 状态
why: 每个单词都是二叉决策，且做出选择后要递归、撤销、再试另一支，这是回溯的典型形状。
why_en: Each word creates an include-or-skip branch, so recursive backtracking matches the decision structure directly.
whenOtherWins: 如果输入已经满足区间贪心或有可证明的最优子结构，贪心或 DP 才更合适；这里冲突组合没有这种简单性质。
optionDiagrams:
flowchart TD
  Word[i] --> Skip[skip]
  Word[i] --> Include{disjoint}
  Include -->|yes| Next[i plus 1]
  Include -->|no| Prune[no include]

flowchart LR
  Masks[All masks] --> DP[full DP space]
optionExplanations: 错：字符间没有图的边关系，BFS 无法表达冲突约束。
对：每个单词恰好是二元决策，天然匹配回溯的分支结构。
错：贪心选最长词无法证明全局最优，冲突关系会被忽略。
错：状态数达 2^26，本题规模下枚举所有 mask 太浪费。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: characters have no graph edges for BFS to traverse.
Correct: each word is a binary decision, the exact shape backtracking handles.
Wrong: greedily taking the longest words cannot prove global optimality.
Wrong: enumerating all 2^26 mask states is wasteful at this problem's scale.
options_en: Run BFS over individual characters.
Backtrack over an include-or-skip decision for each word.
Sort words and greedily take the longest ones first.
Enumerate all 26-bit mask states with dynamic programming.
tradeoff: 回溯穷举搜索 vs 贪心/DP 需要的额外结构性质

q: 在朴素 include/skip 回溯中，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: In plain include/skip backtracking, which statements are correct?
options: skip 分支永远合法
include 分支必须先确认当前单词字符与 used 不相交
include 后必须在返回前撤销 current 和 used 的修改
到叶子节点时不需要更新 best
why: 跳过单词不会破坏合法性；选择单词必须无冲突，并且所有就地修改都要对称撤销，叶子或改进点都要维护 best。
why_en: Skip is always legal, include requires disjoint characters, and every mutation must be undone after the recursive call.
optionExplanations: 对：跳过不修改任何状态，不可能违反约束。
对：字符集合有交集时 include 非法，必须先判断。
对：current/used 是共享可变状态，退出前必须复原对称。
错：叶子或任何改进点都要检查并更新 best，否则丢最优解。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: skipping mutates nothing, so it can never break legality.
Correct: overlapping characters make the include illegal, so check first.
Correct: current and used are shared mutable state and must be restored.
Wrong: every leaf or improvement must update best or the optimum is lost.
options_en: The skip branch is always legal.
The include branch must first confirm the word's characters are disjoint from used.
After including, current and used must be restored before returning.
There is no need to update best at a leaf node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个集合没有任何共同元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two sets are disjoint when they share no common elements.

scenario: 回溯当前已经使用字符为 `used`，准备尝试把 `word` 加入当前选择。

q: 哪段 Python 判断最直接表达「word 与已用字符没有冲突」？
q_en: Which Python check best says that word has no conflict with used?
options: if set(word) <= used:
if used.isdisjoint(set(word)):
if len(word) > len(used):
if word not in used:
why: 合法 include 的条件是两个字符集合交集为空，`isdisjoint` 正好表达这个判断。
why_en: The include branch is legal exactly when the word's character set is disjoint from the used-character set.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态已经是整数 bitmask，就应该用按位与判断，而不是再构造 set。
codeSample:
word_chars = set(word)
if used.isdisjoint(word_chars):
    current.append(word)
    used.update(word_chars)
    recurse(i + 1)
    current.pop()
    used.difference_update(word_chars)
optionExplanations: 错：子集关系判断方向反了，且未处理相等的边界。
对：两个集合没有交集，用 isdisjoint 一次调用直接表达。
错：长度比较和字符冲突无关，无法判断是否合法。
错：`word not in used` 是判断整词是否为成员，语义完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the subset direction is backwards and misses the disjoint check.
Correct: isdisjoint directly expresses zero character overlap.
Wrong: comparing lengths says nothing about character conflicts.
Wrong: `word not in used` checks whole-word membership, not character overlap.
options_en: Check whether word's character set is a subset of used.
Check whether used and word's character set are disjoint.
Check whether the word is longer than the used set.
Check whether word as a whole is a key in used.
tradeoff: 集合 isdisjoint 判断 vs 后续 bitmask 按位与判断

termDefinitions.meaning: Python 集合方法，判断两个集合是否没有交集。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: isdisjoint is a Python set method that checks whether two sets share no elements.

q: 回溯 include 分支中忘记 `current.pop()` 或忘记从 `used` 移除刚加入字符，最直接的后果是什么？
q_en: What happens if the include branch forgets current.pop() or removing new chars from used?
options: 只会影响运行时间，不影响答案
兄弟分支会看到不属于自己的选择，导致错误剪枝或错误答案
递归深度会自动变浅
Python 会自动回滚局部变量
why: 回溯依赖「进入分支前后状态一致」；撤销不完整会污染兄弟分支，让后续合法选择被误判成冲突。
why_en: If mutations are not undone, sibling branches inherit stale state and the search can reject legal combinations or return a wrong result.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Parent[used is ab] --> Include[add cd]
  Include --> Return[return without undo]
  Return --> Sibling[sibling sees abcd]
  Sibling --> Wrong[legal word pruned]
optionExplanations: 错：脏状态会让别的分支误判冲突，答案本身会错，不只是变慢。
对：没撤销的字符残留在 used 里，后续分支会误判成冲突。
错：状态没清理和递归深度无关，深度由 i 决定。
错：`used`/`current` 是可变对象，Python 不会自动帮你撤销。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: stale state corrupts correctness, not just speed.
Correct: leftover characters in used make sibling branches see false conflicts.
Wrong: recursion depth is driven by index i, unrelated to cleanup.
Wrong: used and current are mutable objects; Python never auto-restores them.
options_en: It only affects running time, not correctness.
Sibling branches inherit stale state, causing wrong pruning or a wrong answer.
Recursion depth automatically becomes shallower.
Python automatically rolls back local variables.

q: 把朴素回溯的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the plain backtracking decision chain in the right order.
steps: 到达叶子或发现更大 used 时更新 best
对当前单词先尝试 skip 分支
若字符不冲突，加入当前单词并递归 include 分支
返回 include 分支后撤销加入的单词和字符
递归状态从第 i 个单词和当前 used 集合开始
why: 朴素搜索围绕同一状态展开两个分支，任何 include 的状态修改都要在回到父帧前恢复。
why_en: Plain backtracking branches from the current state, tries skip and legal include paths, restores mutations, and updates the best solution at terminal or improved states.

q: 朴素 include/skip 回溯的最坏时间复杂度最接近哪一个？
q_en: What is the closest worst-case time complexity for plain include/skip backtracking?
options: O(n log n)
O(m · 2^n)，m 是单词长度量级
why: n 个单词各有选或不选两种分支，最坏有 2^n 个组合；每帧还要做与单词长度相关的集合检查或更新。

optionExplanations: 错：这是排序级复杂度，回溯树的分支数不是 n log n。
对：n 个二元决策给出 2^n 组合，每帧还有 O(m) 的集合操作。
错：26 是字母表大小的常数，和单词数 n 的搜索树无关。
错：n^3 是多项式，掩盖了每个单词二元分支带来的指数增长。

Correct: n binary decisions give 2^n combinations, each frame doing O(m) set work.
Wrong: 26 is the constant alphabet size, unrelated to the search tree over n words.
Wrong: n cubed is polynomial and hides the exponential branching per word.
scenario: 词表里有 n 个单词，每个单词长度约 m；你要预估朴素 include/skip 回溯在最坏输入下的运行时间量级，判断这套方案能不能扛住较大的 n。
scenario_en: The word list has n words of length about m; you need the worst-case runtime scale for plain include/skip backtracking to judge whether it can handle a larger n.
options_en: O(n log n).
O(m times 2 to the n), where m is the word-length scale.
O(26 squared).
O(n cubed).

q: 为什么包含大量二三字母短词的数据集会让朴素回溯变慢？
q_en: Why do many two- or three-letter words make plain backtracking slow?
options: 短词冲突少，合法分支能扎得很深
短字符串同样能转换成 set
短词字符少，通常覆盖不了全部字母
短词长度不会让递归失败返回

why_en: Short words collide with few others, so conflict-based pruning leaves many deep legal branches alive.
optionExplanations: 对：冲突是唯一的自然剪枝，短词冲突少，深层分支大量存活。
错：任何长度的字符串都能用 set() 转换，和这无关。
错：短词字符少，远达不到覆盖完整字母表。
错：递归返回由函数结构决定，跟单词长短无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: conflict is the only natural pruning, and short words rarely conflict.
Wrong: any string converts to a set() regardless of length.
Wrong: short words have few characters and rarely cover the full alphabet.
Wrong: recursion always returns based on control flow, unrelated to word length.
options_en: Short words rarely conflict, so legal branches can go deep.
Short strings convert into a set just as well as long ones.
Short words have few characters and rarely cover the full alphabet.
Word length has no effect on whether recursion returns.

q: 应该引入哪类优化？

options: branch-and-bound，用乐观上界剪掉无望子树

why_en: The pruning is correct because it cuts only branches whose optimistic maximum cannot improve the best solution.
optionExplanations: 对：这正是它的定义，是剩余单词字符的完整并集。
对：减去已用字符后剩下的，就是最乐观情况下还能拿到的新字符。
对：只有连乐观上限都赢不了 best，才能保证剪掉不会漏解。
错：排序只重新安排访问顺序，不会移除任何候选单词。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: that's exactly its definition — the full union of remaining characters.
Correct: subtracting used gives the best-case count of new characters left.
Correct: only when even the optimistic ceiling can't beat best is pruning safe.
Wrong: sorting only reorders visits; it never removes any candidate word.
options_en: suffix_union contains every character the remaining words could possibly contribute.
Subtracting used from suffix_union gives an optimistic ceiling on new characters.
Pruning only fires when the ceiling cannot strictly beat best.
Sorting deletes all low-coverage words.

why: 本题最大化的是不同字符覆盖；单词贡献应看字符集合大小或 mask 的 bit_count，而不是字符串长度。
why_en: The score counts distinct covered characters, so repeated letters inside a word must not be counted multiple times.
optionExplanations: 对：`letter` 长度 6 但只有 4 个不同字符，len 会多算 2。
错：`len(word)` 和 disjoint 检查用的字符集合是两回事。
错：字母表大小由题目定义，不受单个单词写法影响。
错：高估贡献值会让 best 和上界都算错，直接影响正确性。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: `letter` has length 6 but only 4 distinct characters, over-counting by 2.
Wrong: len(word) is unrelated to the character set used in the disjoint check.
Wrong: alphabet size is defined by the problem, not by any single word's spelling.
Wrong: overcounting corrupts both best and the bound, breaking correctness.
options_en: Repeated characters get double-counted, overstating coverage.
It automatically makes the disjoint check faster.
It changes the alphabet size.
It has no effect at all.

错：DP 慢不代表回溯可以不剪枝，两者是完全独立的问题。

Correct: two independent levers — search fewer branches, then make each cheaper.
Wrong: sorting only speeds up how fast best grows; worst case stays exponential.
Wrong: DP being slow says nothing about whether backtracking still needs pruning.

Because sorting turns exponential complexity into linear complexity.

q: bitmask 版常见 bug 包括哪些？（多选）

对：不扣 used_mask 会让上界偏高，可能漏剪本该剪掉的子树。
错：多搜是纯粹浪费时间，不改变结果，不算破坏正确性的 bug。

Correct: a wrong base maps digits to incorrect or negative bit positions.
Correct: skipping the subtraction inflates the bound and can miss valid prunes.
Wrong: extra searching only wastes time; it doesn't corrupt the returned answer.

def _filter_against(possibilities, line):
    return [p for p in possibilities
            if all(line[i] == UNKNOWN or line[i] == p[i]

options: 检查已关闭 run 是否匹配 clue 前缀
发现 run 超过 clue 长度时返回 false
完整列时做最终 extract_runs 对比
把正在尾部增长的 run 当作已经关闭，要求它立刻等于 clue
options_en: Checking that closed runs match the clue prefix.
Returning false when a run exceeds the clue's length.
Doing a final extract_runs comparison once the column is complete.
Treating an open trailing run as closed and requiring it to equal the clue immediately.
why: 开放 run 还可能继续增长，只能检查它没有超过目标长度；过早要求相等会剪掉合法分支。
why_en: The common bug is treating an open trailing run as completed and requiring it to equal the clue too early.

An all-EMPTY grid.
An all-FILLED grid.
null / None.

why_en: If no grid satisfies all clues, every branch fails and the solver returns null.

termDefinitions.meaning: 格子状态之一：该格已确定为空白。

q: 补全从三版解法抽象出的路线：

text: 先写 {{raw backtracking}}；再把工作单位从 cell 提升到 {{row/line candidates}}；最后先做 {{propagation}}，只在推不动时搜索。

why_en: The progression is raw backtracking, larger structured choices, then propagation before search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先试一个决策、递归下去，失败就撤销换下一个选项的搜索方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking tries a choice, recurses, and undoes it on failure to try another option.

q: 文章建议遇到类似约束题时先问哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: What questions does the article suggest asking for similar constraint problems? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 输入是否有来自多个轴的约束
是否能便宜地枚举每条线的合法选项
固定一条线是否会明显约束另一条线
是否可以忽略所有局部矛盾
options_en: Does the input carry constraints from more than one axis?
Can you enumerate each line's valid options cheaply?
Does fixing one line meaningfully constrain another?
Can you just ignore every local contradiction?
why: 如果多轴约束、候选可枚举、交叉影响强，传播通常比直接搜索更值得优先写。
why_en: Propagation is attractive when constraints come from multiple axes, line options are enumerable, and fixing one line constrains another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 约束满足问题：给一组变量赋值，同时满足多条约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CSP, a constraint satisfaction problem, assigns values to variables so every constraint holds at once.

scenario: Nonogram Solver 的评测套件按 5×5、10×10、15×15、25×25 四档递增出题，每档都有独立的 5000ms 时间预算。
scenario_en: The Nonogram Solver benchmark uses increasing puzzle sizes, 5x5, 10x10, 15x15, and 25x25, each with its own 5000 ms time budget.
q: 题解为什么要专门设计这四档递增规模，而不是只测一个大棋盘？
q_en: Why does the solution use four increasing puzzle sizes instead of testing only one large board?
options: 只是想确认程序在更大网格上不会因内存不足而崩溃
要求所有解法在四档上都必须使用完全相同的时间复杂度
规模越大意味着 clue 携带的约束信息越少，只是让题目更难猜
让每一档依次暴露不同解法各自在哪个量级开始超时
options_en: It's only to confirm the program does not crash from running out of memory on larger grids.
It requires every solution to have the exact same time complexity across all four tiers.
A larger grid means the clues carry less constraining information, just making it a harder guess.
So each tier exposes exactly where a given solution starts blowing its time budget.
why: 四档规模像一把标尺，逐步逼出每种解法各自在哪个量级失速：cell-by-cell 在 10×10、row-by-row 在 15×15，只有传播能撑到 25×25。
why_en: The four size tiers act like a ruler that exposes exactly where each solution stalls, from cell-by-cell at 10x10 up to propagation clearing 25x25.

scenario: 面试官问你为什么不直接继续优化 row-by-row 的排序或剪枝。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why you would not just keep optimizing row-by-row ordering or pruning.
q: 最好的回答是什么？
q_en: What is the best answer?
options: 因为给行排序一定能把 NP-hard 问题变成 O(n)
因为 row-by-row 在所有 15×15 题目上都已经足够快
因为列 clue 其实是多余的，完全可以删除
列 clue 和行 clue 一样强，只当拒绝器浪费了一半信息，该让它主动传播
options_en: Because sorting rows can turn an NP-hard problem into O(n).
Because row-by-row is already fast enough on every 15 by 15 puzzle.
Because column clues are actually redundant and can be deleted.
Column clues carry just as much signal as row clues; using them only as a rejector wastes half the information — they should actively propagate.
why: row_bt 的问题不是单纯顺序不好，而是没有把列约束用来推导格子；传播把两轴信息都前置使用。
why_en: The key is that columns are not just validators; they should actively shrink possibilities and force cells.
whenOtherWins: 如果列约束非常弱或题目只要求小规模，row-by-row 加简单剪枝也可能足够。
tradeoff: 把列约束当主动推导源（传播，更快但要维护候选状态）vs 把列约束只当事后过滤器（row backtracking，简单但慢）
optionMeanings: 错误地认为排序能改变问题的复杂度类别。
与实测矛盾，row_bt 在 15×15 上明显超预算。
错误地认为列约束不携带有效信息。
点出 row_bt 的根本问题：列信息只用来拒绝，没用来推导。
optionScenarioImpacts: 排序不改变搜索空间大小，NP-hard 本质不会因排序消失。
benchmark 显示 row_bt 在 15×15 要 68000ms，远超预算。
删除列约束会让候选过滤少一半信息来源，传播效果大降。
传播提前用列约束推导，这是它比 row_bt 快几个数量级的原因。
optionDirectness: 不直接；排序只是换顺序，不改变复杂度类别。
不直接；与 benchmark 数据矛盾。
不直接；列约束是传播推导格子的关键信息来源。
最直接；指出 row_bt 的信息利用缺陷，也是传播更快的原因。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly assumes sorting changes the problem's complexity class.
Contradicts the benchmark — row_bt clearly blows the budget at 15x15.
Wrongly assumes column constraints carry no useful information.
Names row_bt's real flaw: column info is used only to reject, never to derive.

The benchmark shows row_bt takes about 68000ms at 15x15, far past the 5000ms budget.
Dropping column constraints removes half the information propagation needs to filter candidates.
Propagation uses column constraints for derivation up front, which is exactly why it beats row_bt by orders of magnitude.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; reordering only changes try order, not complexity class.
Not direct; it contradicts the benchmark data.
Not direct; column constraints are exactly what propagation needs to derive cells.
Most direct; it names row_bt's real information gap, which is also why propagation is faster.

q: 为什么文章说 Nonogram 仍然可能需要 fallback search？
q_en: Why does the article say a Nonogram solver may still need fallback search?
options: 传播永远不会填任何格
所有 Nonogram 都能纯传播解出
fallback search 是为了打乱输出
传播只能推出逻辑强制格，遇到局部歧义时必须尝试假设
options_en: Propagation never fills in any cell at all.
Every nonogram can be solved by pure propagation alone.
Fallback search exists just to shuffle the output.
Propagation only derives logically forced cells, so local ambiguity still requires a guess.
why: 传播是局部推理，不保证消除所有歧义；搜索负责处理需要假设才能推进的分支。
why_en: Propagation handles forced deductions, but ambiguous puzzles can still require guesses and backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传播卡住后，对某个 UNKNOWN 格做假设并重新传播的兜底搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fallback search guesses a value for an unknown cell and reruns propagation when deduction stalls.

q: Nonogram Solver 这篇题解最核心的经验是什么？
q_en: What is the core lesson from the Nonogram Solver breakdown?
options: 所有约束题都应该逐格暴力搜索
只要用递归就不需要候选列表
列 clue 可以最后一次性检查
约束题要先寻找可传播的结构，尽量让推理缩小搜索树
options_en: Every constraint problem should be brute-forced cell by cell.
Using recursion means you never need candidate lists.
Column clues can be checked just once at the very end.
For constraint problems, first look for propagable structure so deduction shrinks the search tree.
why: 本题从逐格暴力到行候选再到行列传播，核心就是把 clue 转成主动约束，少靠盲目搜索。
why_en: The main lesson is to turn constraints into propagation so deduction shrinks the search before backtracking is used.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复用已知格过滤各线候选、推出强制格，直到没有新变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propagation repeatedly filters line candidates against known cells and commits forced cells until nothing changes.

q: Route Planner 的主方法要最小化什么？
q_en: What does the main Route Planner method minimize?
options: 总站点数
总旅行时间，包括换乘线时的 5 分钟罚时
线路名称字典序
路径中不同线路数量，不看时间
why: 边有 travel_time，且切换 line 会额外加 5 分钟；目标是最小化累计时间。
why_en: The planner minimizes total travel time, including a five-minute penalty whenever the route switches lines.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Edge[Travel time] --> Total[Total route time]
  Transfer[Line change penalty] --> Total
  Total --> Min[Minimize total]
options_en: The total number of stations visited.
Total travel time, including a five-minute penalty per transfer.
Alphabetical order of the line names.
The number of distinct lines used, ignoring time.
optionDirectness: 错：只数站点数会丢掉边权和换乘罚时信息。
对：对应题目定义——总时间=边权之和+每次换乘 5 分钟。
错：字典序和路线是否最优毫无关系。
错：忽略具体时间，无法比较线路数相同但耗时不同的路线。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: counting stations alone throws away edge weights and the transfer penalty.
Correct: this matches the objective — edge weights summed plus five minutes per transfer.
Wrong: alphabetical order has nothing to do with route optimality.
Wrong: ignoring actual time can't distinguish two routes with the same line count but different durations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 切换线路时额外加的 5 分钟成本，只有到达线路和下一条边线路不同才触发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The transfer penalty is the extra five minutes added whenever the route switches lines.

q: 补全换乘罚时规则：
q_en: Complete the transfer-penalty rule:
text: 第一条边没有上一条线路，因此 {{不算换乘}}；后续边如果 `current_line != next_line`，就加 {{5 分钟}} 并把 transfer count 加一。
why: 换乘成本取决于到达当前站时所在线路，这也是后续 state key 必须包含 line 的根本原因。
why_en: A transfer penalty applies only after the first edge when the next edge's line differs from the line used to arrive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 切换线路时额外加的 5 分钟成本，只有到达线路和下一条边线路不同才触发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The transfer penalty is the extra five minutes added whenever the route switches lines.

termDefinitions.meaning: Dijkstra 用来判断某个状态是否已经找到最优解的键；相同 key 的到达会被合并成一个状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The state key is what Dijkstra uses to decide whether two arrivals count as the same state and can be merged.

q: 为什么按 hop count 的 BFS 不适合这个主路由问题？
q_en: Why is hop-count BFS a poor fit for the main routing problem?
options: 边权不同时，跳数少不等于总时间少
BFS 无法处理带环的图
BFS 出队时不会保存路径
BFS 会漏掉部分邻居站点
why: 测试图里 Blue 三跳共 7 分钟，比 Red 两跳 8 分钟更快；BFS 会优先返回两跳路径。
why_en: BFS minimizes number of edges, but this route planner must minimize weighted travel time.
options_en: Different edge weights mean fewer hops doesn't mean less time.
BFS cannot handle graphs that contain cycles.
BFS never keeps track of the path while dequeuing.
BFS can skip some neighboring stations.
optionDirectness: 对：三跳路线的边权总和仍能小于两跳路线，跳数不是判断标准。
错：BFS 能处理有环图，只是仍按跳数分层，不看权重。
错：BFS 完全可以在每个 queue entry 里带 path，只是排序标准不对。
错：BFS 的 visited 集合会覆盖所有邻居，不会漏站。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: a three-hop route can still sum to a lower total weight than a two-hop one, so hop count is not the right criterion.
Wrong: BFS handles cyclic graphs fine — the issue is it still ranks by hop count, not weight.
Wrong: BFS can carry the path in each queue entry; the real problem is its ordering criterion.
Wrong: BFS's visited set covers every neighbor, so it never skips a station.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按跳数一层层扩展的图搜索算法，不看边的权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS is Breadth-First Search, a graph search that expands nodes layer by layer in hop-count order, ignoring edge weight.

scenario: 站点图的每条边有非负旅行时间，还可能加非负换乘罚时，需要找最小总时间。
scenario_en: Each edge in the station graph has non-negative travel time, and transfers add a non-negative penalty; find the minimum total time.
q: 应该从哪类算法开始？
q_en: Which algorithm family should you start with?
options: Dijkstra
普通 BFS
拓扑排序
二分搜索
why: 非负加权最短路的标准工具是 Dijkstra；关键是定义正确的状态，而不只是换一个优先队列。
why_en: Dijkstra is the right family for non-negative weighted shortest paths, provided the state captures everything future costs depend on.
whenOtherWins: 如果每条边代价完全相同，BFS 更简单；如果有负权边，Dijkstra 不适用。
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Heap[min time heap] --> Pop[pop best state]
  Pop --> Relax[relax weighted edges]
  Relax --> Heap

flowchart LR
  Queue[FIFO queue] --> Hops[hop layers]
tradeoff: 非负权最短路正确性 vs 模板简单但假设更强（无权/无环）
options_en: Dijkstra's algorithm.
Plain breadth-first search.
Topological sort.
Binary search.
optionDirectness: 对：非负权最短路的标准解法，只要状态定义对就正确。
错：BFS 按跳数分层，忽略边权，会选错路线。
错：拓扑排序要求无环 DAG，交通线路图通常有环。
错：二分搜索用于有序数组查找，不是图上最短路问题。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: it's the standard tool for non-negative weighted shortest paths, as long as the state is defined correctly.
Wrong: BFS ranks by hop layer and ignores edge weight, so it can pick the wrong route.
Wrong: topological sort needs an acyclic graph, but transit line maps usually contain cycles.
Wrong: binary search is for searching sorted arrays, not shortest paths on a graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理非负权最短路径的经典算法，每次从堆里弹出当前累计代价最小的候选状态来扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm repeatedly expands the lowest cumulative-cost candidate to find shortest paths on non-negative weighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按跳数一层层扩展的图搜索算法，不看边的权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS is Breadth-First Search, a graph search that expands nodes layer by layer in hop-count order, ignoring edge weight.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只对无环有向图（DAG）成立的排序方法，按依赖顺序排列节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort is an ordering that only works on a directed acyclic graph, arranging nodes by dependency order.

q: BFS baseline 虽然返回错路线，但它仍记录了哪些运行信息？（多选）
q_en: Even though the BFS baseline returns the wrong route, what runtime information does it still track? (Select all that apply.)
options: 当前 path
当前 line
累计 total_time
transfer count
why: BFS baseline 的问题不是不会累计时间，而是 queue 的出队顺序仍按 hop count，不按累计时间。
why_en: The BFS baseline can track time and transfers, but it still expands by hop count instead of accumulated cost.
options_en: The current path so far.
The current line.
The accumulated total_time.
The transfer count.
optionDirectness: 对：queue 每个 entry 都带着 path 列表一起入队。
对：entry 记录 line，用来判断下一跳是否要付换乘罚时。
对：total_time 在每次入队时累加 travel_time 和罚时。
对：transfers 在每次判定换乘时加一，一起存进 entry。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: every queue entry carries its path list along with it.
Correct: the entry tracks the arrival line to know whether the next hop needs a transfer penalty.
Correct: total_time accumulates travel time and any penalty every time an entry is pushed.
Correct: transfers increments whenever a transfer is detected and is stored in the entry too.

q: 这组耗时数据最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design conclusion does this timing example support most strongly?
options: 该按累计时间选路线，而不是按跳数选路线
跳数最少的 Red 一定是最优路线
边数越少，总时间就一定越短
换乘更多条线路的路线一定更慢
why: Blue 三跳共 7 分钟，比两跳的 Red（8 分钟）和 Green（10 分钟）都快；必须按累计权重排序而不是跳数，这正是后面要换成 Dijkstra 的原因。
why_en: Blue wins at seven minutes despite having the most hops, so routes must be ranked by accumulated time, not hop count.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  C[Central] -->|Green 5| P[Park]
  P -->|Green 5| A[Airport]
  C -->|Red 4| H[Harbor]
  H -->|Red 4| A
  C -->|Blue 2| M[Mall]
  M -->|Blue 2| S[Stadium]
  S -->|Blue 3| A
scenario: 同一起点 Central 到 Airport 有三条候选线路：Green 经 Park 两跳共 4+6=10 分钟，Red 经 Harbor 两跳共 5+3=8 分钟，Blue 经 Mall、Stadium 三跳共 2+3+2=7 分钟。
scenario_en: From Central to Airport, Green takes two hops for 10 minutes, Red takes two hops for 8 minutes, and Blue takes three hops for 7 minutes.
options_en: Rank routes by accumulated time, not by hop count.
The fewest-hop Red route must be optimal.
Fewer edges always means less total time.
A route touching more lines is always slower.

termDefinitions.meaning: 路径经过的边数，不考虑每条边具体权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hop count is the number of edges on a path, regardless of each edge's weight.

scenario: 你已经决定用 Dijkstra，需要每次扩展当前累计时间最小的未完成路径。
scenario_en: You have chosen Dijkstra and need to expand the unfinished route with the lowest accumulated time each step.
q: 应该用什么 frontier 结构？
q_en: What frontier structure should you use?
options: FIFO 队列（按加入顺序出队）
按累计时间排序的 min-heap
栈（后进先出）
普通哈希 set
why: Dijkstra 的核心是始终弹出当前最便宜的候选状态；min-heap 正好支持这个操作。
why_en: Dijkstra needs a min-heap frontier so it always expands the lowest accumulated-time state next.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有边代价相同，FIFO queue 的 BFS 就已经按距离递增扩展。
tradeoff: 按代价排序的堆 vs 按加入顺序的队列
options_en: A FIFO queue that pops in insertion order.
A min-heap ordered by cumulative time.
A stack (last in, first out).
A plain hash set.
optionDirectness: 错：按加入顺序出队，不看代价，等价于 BFS。
对：每次弹出当前最小累计时间，正是 Dijkstra 需要的顺序。
错：后进先出会优先扩展最新加入的候选，和代价无关。
错：set 不保证任何弹出顺序，无法充当 frontier。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: it pops in insertion order regardless of cost, which just reduces to BFS.
Correct: it always pops the lowest accumulated time next, exactly what Dijkstra needs.
Wrong: a stack expands whatever was pushed most recently, unrelated to cost.
Wrong: a set has no defined pop order, so it can't serve as the frontier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出队列，BFS 按加入顺序处理站点，不看权重。

scenario: `line` 是到达当前站的线路，`conn.line` 是下一条边的线路，需要计算换乘。
scenario_en: `line` is the line used to arrive at the current station, and `conn.line` is the next edge's line.
q: 哪段逻辑正确处理第一跳和同线继续？
q_en: Which logic correctly handles the first hop and staying on the same line?
options: is_transfer = line is not None and line != conn.line
is_transfer = line != conn.line
is_transfer = True
is_transfer = conn.travel_time > 5
why: 第一跳没有 prior line，不应罚时；之后只有线路变化才算换乘。
why_en: A transfer occurs only when there is a previous line and the next edge uses a different line.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务把上车也算一次换乘，第一跳规则要改；本文规则明确第一跳不罚。
codeSample:
is_transfer = line is not None and line != conn.line
new_time = time + conn.travel_time + (5 if is_transfer else 0)
new_transfers = transfers + (1 if is_transfer else 0)
# line is None only on the first hop, so it never counts as a transfer
# is_transfer flips to True only when the next edge uses a different line
tradeoff: 首跳不罚时 vs 之后按线路是否变化判断
options_en: Only count it as a transfer when there was a previous line and it differs from the next edge.
Count it as a transfer whenever the current line differs from the next edge.
Always treat every edge as a transfer.
Treat it as a transfer whenever the edge's travel time exceeds five minutes.
optionDirectness: 对：line is None 时跳过判断，第一跳不罚时，之后按线路是否变化判断。
错：line 初始是 None，None != conn.line 恒为真，第一跳也会被误罚。
错：把每条边都当换乘，同线继续走也会被多罚 5 分钟。
错：换乘和边自身耗时无关，5 分钟只是罚时数值，不是判断条件。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: it skips the check while line is None, so the first hop is free, and later hops are judged by whether the line changed.
Wrong: line starts as None, and None != conn.line is always true, so even the first hop gets penalized.
Wrong: treating every edge as a transfer penalizes staying on the same line too.
Wrong: whether an edge is a transfer has nothing to do with its own travel time; five minutes is the penalty amount, not the trigger.

termDefinitions.meaning: 切换线路时额外加的 5 分钟成本，只有到达线路和下一条边线路不同才触发。

q: Dijkstra 的状态 key 应该是什么？
q_en: What should Dijkstra's state key be?
options: `station`
`(station, line)`
`line`
`(station, total_time)`
why: 同一站、不同到达线路会有不同的下一跳换乘成本，因此必须作为不同状态展开。
why_en: For the plain route, each state should include both station and arrival line because future transfer costs depend on both.
whenOtherWins: 如果完全没有换乘罚时或未来规则不看上一条 line，station-only key 就足够。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Station[Station A] --> S1[A on Red]
  Station --> S2[A on Blue]
  S1 --> R[Red neighbors no transfer]
  S2 --> B[Blue neighbors no transfer]
tradeoff: 状态区分到到达线路 vs 只区分到到达站点
options_en: Just the station.
The station paired with the arrival line.
Just the line.
The station paired with total_time.
optionDirectness: 错：丢失到达线路，未来换乘罚时算不出来。
对：换乘成本取决于到达线路，必须把 line 并入 key。
错：只保留 line 会丢失到达了哪个站，无法判断是否到达终点。
错：total_time 是会变化的代价而非上下文，用它做 key 等于不合并任何状态。

Correct: transfer cost depends on the arrival line, so line must be folded into the key.
Wrong: keeping only the line loses which station was reached, so you can't tell when you hit the destination.
Wrong: total_time is a changing cost, not context — using it in the key means states are never merged at all.

q: 哪段 key 更新最正确？
q_en: Which key update is most correct?
options: next_state = (conn.destination, conn.line)
next_state = conn.destination
next_state = (station, line)
next_state = (conn.line, time)
why: 走过这条边后，到达的是目标站，上一条线路变成该边的 line。
why_en: After traversing an edge, the next state is the destination station paired with that edge's line.
whenOtherWins: 在 transfer-capped 版本中，还要把 transfers_used 加进 key。
codeSample:
next_state = (conn.destination, conn.line)
if new_time < best.get(next_state, math.inf):
    best[next_state] = new_time
    parent[next_state] = state
    heapq.heappush(heap, (new_time, counter, conn.destination, conn.line))
# best/parent only update on strict improvement, so parent always matches the recorded best time

options_en: Pair the destination station with that edge's line.
Use just the destination station.
Keep the current station and line unchanged.
Pair the edge's line with the accumulated time.
optionDirectness: 对：走完这条边后，下个状态是目的站加上这条边的 line。
错：丢了到达线路，会重现 station-only key 的合并 bug。
错：这是没走边之前的状态，没有推进到新站点。
错：time 是代价不是上下文，且丢掉了目的站，无法定位状态。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: after traversing this edge, the next state is the destination station paired with that edge's line.
Wrong: dropping the arrival line reproduces the station-only merge bug.
Wrong: this is the state before crossing the edge, not the advanced one.
Wrong: time is a cost, not context, and this also loses the destination station entirely.

q: 在 `(station, line)` Dijkstra 中，哪些 map/结构是核心？（多选）
q_en: In `(station, line)` Dijkstra, which maps or structures are core? (Select all that apply.)
options: `best[(station, line)]` 存该状态最小时间
`parent[state]` 存成功 relax 时的前驱状态
`transfers[state]` 存该状态已用换乘数
`visited[station]` 单独决定是否丢弃所有同站状态
why: best 和 parent 都要以完整状态为 key；只按 station 丢弃会重现旧 bug。
why_en: The best, parent, and transfer-count maps must be keyed by the full state, not by station alone.
options_en: `best[(station, line)]` stores that state's minimum known time.
`parent[state]` stores the predecessor on a successful relax.
`transfers[state]` stores the transfer count used to reach that state.
`visited[station]` alone decides whether to discard all same-station states.
optionDirectness: 对：best 记录每个完整状态目前已知的最小时间，用于剪枝旧 heap entry。
对：parent 只在 relax 改善时更新，保证回溯路径和 best 时间一致。
对：transfers 和 best/parent 一样按完整 state 存，最后随 Route 返回。
错：只按 station 丢弃会把不同 line 的到达状态错误合并，重现旧 bug。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: best tracks the smallest known time per full state, used to prune stale heap entries.
Correct: parent updates only on improvement, so the reconstructed path matches the recorded best time.
Correct: transfers is keyed the same way as best/parent and is returned with the final Route.
Wrong: discarding by station alone wrongly merges arrivals on different lines, reviving the old bug.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录每个状态的前驱状态，只在终点弹出后一次性回溯出完整路径，而不是每次都复制整条 path。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A parent pointer records each state's predecessor so the route can be rebuilt once at the end instead of copying the path on every push.

q: 为什么 parent pointer 只应在 `new_time` 真正改善 `next_state` 时写入？
q_en: Why should the parent pointer be written only when `new_time` truly improves `next_state`?
options: 否则更差路径可能覆盖最优状态的前驱，重建路径与时间不一致
因为 parent 只能写一次，语言限制
因为 Dijkstra 不需要路径
因为 heap 无法存字符串
why: parent 必须描述 best 时间对应的路径；无条件覆盖会让返回路线和累计时间脱节。
why_en: Parent pointers must be updated only on improvement so the reconstructed route matches the recorded best time.
options_en: Otherwise a worse path could overwrite the optimal state's predecessor, so the rebuilt path stops matching the recorded time.
Because a parent pointer can only be written once due to language limits.
Because Dijkstra doesn't need to return a path.
Because a heap cannot store strings.
optionDirectness: 对：只在改善时更新，才能保证 parent 链条和 best 时间描述同一条路径。
错：parent 是普通字典，可以随时覆盖写入，不存在语言层面的一次性限制。
错：本题两个方法都要返回 Route 里的站点列表，需要路径。
错：parent 存的是 state 元组不是字符串，heap 也能存元组。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: updating only on improvement is what keeps the parent chain describing the same path as the recorded best time.
Wrong: parent is a plain dict that can be overwritten anytime; there is no such language-level restriction.
Wrong: both planner methods must return a station list in Route, so a path is required.
Wrong: parent stores state tuples, not strings, and heaps can hold tuples fine.

Write the parent pointer only on improvement, then walk it back once at the end.
Don't store any path information at all.
Encode the path inside the station name.

q: 哪段逻辑能构造站点列表？
q_en: Which logic reconstructs the station list?
options: 沿 parent 回溯到起点，取站点分量后反转
直接返回 parent 所有 key 组成的列表
只取当前 state 的线路分量作为结果
对 parent 的 key 排序后作为站点列表

whenOtherWins: 如果 heap entry 已经携带完整 path，可以直接返回它，但会增加每次扩展的复制成本。

    state = parent.get(state)
stations.reverse()

Just return a list of all the keys in parent.
Take only the line component of the current state.
Sort the keys of parent and use that as the station list.

错：字典序和实际路径顺序无关，排序不能还原路径。

Wrong: parent.keys() is every state ever seen, wrong order and wrong count.
Wrong: state[1] is the line, not the station, and this only grabs one state.
Wrong: alphabetical key order has nothing to do with the actual route order.

if new_used > max_transfers:

options_en: station → (station, line) → (station, line, transfers_used).

Every edge must be treated as bidirectional.
Dijkstra cannot handle directed edges.

scenario: 搜索系统需要语义召回：在线 query 千变万化，文档库很大但更新相对慢。
scenario_en: A search system needs semantic retrieval: live queries vary constantly, while the document corpus is large and changes slowly.

why_en: For semantic retrieval, stable documents should be embedded offline while only the query is embedded online.
whenOtherWins: 如果语料只有几百条、延迟不敏感，直接交叉编码全量候选可能更简单且质量更高。

diagram:
flowchart LR

Pre-enumerate every possible query in advance.
Embed documents offline into an index, and embed the query online.

固定 query 列表很小时可缓存；开放搜索无法穷举。
文档慢变、查询快变时，应离线文档、在线查询。

When documents change slowly and queries vary, embed documents offline and queries online.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Semantic retrieval finds relevant documents using vector similarity instead of keyword matching.

why_en: InfoNCE gives denser supervision than triplet loss by treating every other candidate in the batch as a negative.

scenario: 两塔模型训练检索用的 embedding，需要负样本教模型分辨相关与不相关候选。

q: 训练检索 embedding 时，hard negative 指什么？

options: 随机从全库采到的冷门候选
已经被用户点击过的正样本
模型觉得相关但实际标签为负的候选
完全没有任何特征的空样本
why: Hard negative 最能暴露模型边界错误，因为它看起来像好候选但标签为负。只用随机负样本提升有限。
why_en: A hard negative is a candidate the current model thinks is relevant but is actually labeled negative.
options_en: A random, rarely-seen candidate sampled from the whole pool.
A candidate already labeled positive by a user click.
A candidate the current model ranks as relevant but is actually negative.
A blank candidate with no features at all.
optionMeanings: 随机负样本通常太容易，模型学不到细节。
点击过的样本本身是正样本，不是负样本。

空样本没有信号，训练价值很低。

把正样本当负样本会直接污染标签。

空样本对梯度几乎没有贡献。

点击正样本用于拉近距离，不能当 hard negative。

空样本可测鲁棒性，但不是有效的检索负例。

Blank samples may test robustness, but they are not useful retrieval negatives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型当前认为相关、但真实标签是负的候选，最能暴露模型边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hard negative is a candidate the current model ranks as relevant that is actually labeled negative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门为召回排序训练、让相关查询-候选更靠近的向量表示。

why_en: Periodic hard-negative mining trains the model against the confusing candidates it currently retrieves.
whenOtherWins: 如果模型还没学到基本正负关系，先扩大正样本覆盖和修正标签质量更重要。

前者不需要任何图结构信息

先上线，暂不做任何检索评估
why: 普通英文文本、缺少海量点击日志时，先用预训练文本 embedding 能快速达到可用质量，再用少量数据微调。
why_en: Starting with a pretrained sentence encoder is the pragmatic path when text is ordinary and labeled domain data is limited.
whenOtherWins: 如果领域语言非常特殊且已有海量交互数据，深度微调专用模型可能更值。
tradeoff: 预训练起步 + 小数据微调 vs 从零训练
options_en: Train a billion-parameter encoder from random initialization.
Start from a pretrained sentence-transformer, then fine-tune on the small dataset.
Represent documents only with a one-hot document ID.
Ship first and skip retrieval evaluation entirely.
optionMeanings: 十亿参数从零训练需要海量数据和算力。
复用通用语义，只需少量点击/相关性数据对齐。
one-hot 每篇文档一个维度，没有语义共享。
跳过评估会让检索质量不可控。
optionScenarioImpacts: 团队没有海量点击日志，从零训练会严重过拟合。
能快速拿到可用质量，再逐步用领域数据打磨。
新文档不断加入时完全没有共享结构。
上线后无法知道召回效果是否达标。
optionDirectness: 海量点击和算力充足时，才考虑从随机初始化训练。
普通英文、小数据、要快上线时，预训练句向量最稳。
只要查 ID 时 one-hot 可用，文本语义检索不够。
评估可以先轻量，但不能完全跳过。
optionMeanings_en: Training a billion parameters from scratch needs massive data and compute.
Reusing general semantics needs only a small amount of click or relevance data to align.
One-hot gives each document its own dimension with no semantic sharing.
Skipping evaluation leaves retrieval quality uncontrolled.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Without massive click logs, training from scratch badly overfits.
It reaches usable quality fast, then improves with domain data over time.
New documents keep arriving with no shared structure at all.
You never learn whether retrieval quality is good enough after launch.
optionDirectness_en: Training from random init fits only when you have huge logs and compute.
For ordinary English, little data, and fast launch, a pretrained sentence encoder fits.
One-hot can identify documents, but it is weak for semantic text retrieval.
Evaluation can start lightweight, but it cannot be skipped entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门为句子/段落生成语义向量的预训练模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sentence-transformer is a pretrained model designed to produce semantic vectors for sentences or passages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个类别分配独立维度、其余为零的稀疏编码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One-hot encoding assigns each category its own dimension, with all other dimensions set to zero.

scenario: 你的团队已经训练出高质量的商品 embedding，讨论它能用在哪些地方。
scenario_en: Your team has trained high-quality product embeddings and is discussing where they can be used.
q: 以下哪些是 embedding 在系统中的常见用法？（多选）
q_en: Which uses of embeddings are common in systems? (multi-select)
options: 作为下游模型的紧凑特征
完全替代所有线上监控指标
按向量距离做聚类或去重
做 ANN 检索召回的索引 key
why: embedding 可作特征、聚类空间和检索 key 三种常见用途，但不能替代数据质量或线上监控。
why_en: Embeddings commonly serve as model features, a clustering space, and retrieval keys, but they never replace monitoring.
options_en: Use it as a compact feature for a downstream model.
Let it fully replace all online monitoring metrics.
Cluster or de-duplicate items by vector distance.
Use it as the index key for ANN retrieval.
optionMeanings: embedding 可以直接喂给排序/分类模型。
embedding 不度量系统健康度或业务指标。
距离近的向量可视为同类或近似重复。
候选向量入 ANN 索引，支持近邻检索。
optionScenarioImpacts: 省掉手工特征工程，还能迁移到新任务。
监控异常会因为误信这点而被忽略。
常用来做用户分群、话题聚类、去重。
这是推荐、搜索、RAG 的检索基础。
optionDirectness: 下游排序或分类要紧凑输入时，embedding 可直接当特征。
监控要看延迟、错误率和业务指标，embedding 不能替代。
要分群或去重时，向量距离就是可用空间。
要做语义召回时，embedding 可作为 ANN 索引 key。
optionMeanings_en: Embeddings can feed directly into ranking or classification models.
Embeddings do not measure system health or business metrics.
Vectors close in distance can be treated as similar or near-duplicate.
Candidate vectors go into an ANN index to support nearest-neighbor search.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It saves manual feature engineering and transfers to new tasks.
Monitoring failures get ignored if this claim is believed.
It is commonly used for user segmentation, topic clustering, and dedup.
This underlies retrieval in recommendation, search, and RAG.
optionDirectness_en: Use embeddings as features when a ranker or classifier needs compact input.
Monitoring still needs latency, error-rate, and business metrics.
Use vector distance when clustering or deduplicating similar entities.
Use embeddings as ANN keys when building semantic retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在向量索引里快速找到与查询最接近的候选集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN retrieval quickly finds the set of candidates closest to a query vector inside a vector index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把相似样本按距离分组，常用 k-means 等算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clustering groups similar samples by distance, often using an algorithm like k-means.

scenario: RAG 系统回答不相关，prompt 已经调过，但检索 top-k 经常漏掉同义概念。
scenario_en: A RAG system gives irrelevant answers; the prompt has been tuned, but top-k retrieval often misses synonym concepts.
q: 最优先排查的是？
q_en: What should you debug first?
options: LLM 输出使用的字体大小
数据库表名是否足够短
前端页面是否用了深色模式
文档与查询 embedding 能否表达同义关系
why: RAG 质量强依赖检索：embedding 不懂领域同义词，prompt 补不回缺失上下文。先修检索，再修生成。
why_en: RAG failures often start with embeddings that cannot retrieve semantically related documents, which prompt tuning cannot fix.
whenOtherWins: 如果检索命中文档正确但答案仍乱编，生成模型或上下文拼接才是主要问题。
tradeoff: 先修检索质量 vs 先调 prompt
options_en: The font size of the LLM's output.
Whether database table names are short enough.
Whether the frontend uses dark mode.
Whether document and query embeddings capture domain synonym relationships.
optionMeanings: 字体是前端展示问题，与检索质量无关。
表名长度不影响向量相似度计算。
深色模式是 UI 偏好，不影响检索。
embedding 不懂同义词，检索就会漏召回。
optionScenarioImpacts: 排查这个不会解决 top-k 漏召回。
改表名不会让相关文档被找回。
UI 调整和检索质量是两个维度。
找到问题根因才能针对性改进召回。
optionDirectness: 字体只影响展示，不会让相关文档进入 top-k。
表名可读性不改变 query 和文档的向量距离。
深色模式是 UI 设置，和 RAG 检索链路无关。
prompt 已调过且漏同义概念时，应先修 embedding 检索。
optionMeanings_en: Font size is a display concern unrelated to retrieval quality.
Table name length does not affect vector similarity.
Dark mode is a UI preference that doesn't affect retrieval.
The embedding doesn't know the synonym, so retrieval misses it.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Checking this won't fix the missed top-k retrieval.
Renaming a table won't surface the relevant document.
UI changes and retrieval quality are unrelated dimensions.
Finding the real root cause lets you improve retrieval directly.
optionDirectness_en: Font size affects display, not whether relevant documents enter top-k.
Table names do not change distances between query and document vectors.
Dark mode is a UI setting, not part of the RAG retrieval path.
If prompt tuning is done and synonyms are missed, debug embedding retrieval first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索增强生成：先检索相关文档，再让 LLM 基于它们回答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAG, retrieval-augmented generation, retrieves relevant documents first and then has the LLM answer using them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索返回的前 k 个最相关候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-k means the k most relevant candidates returned by a retrieval search.

scenario: 面试官告诉你：多数生产 embedding 维度落在 64-1024，128-512 最常见。
scenario_en: The interviewer states that most production embedding dimensions fall around 64-1024, with 128-512 most common.
q: 这个量级最支持哪个设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this order of magnitude support?
options: 维度是成本-质量旋钮，可按需调整
维度必须精确等于业务类别数量
维度越高，成本必然可以忽略不计
维度够大就不用再做效果评估
why: 64-1024 是常见区间，128-512 是甜点：维度是成本和质量的可调旋钮，不是越大越好的固定数字。
why_en: The 64-to-1024 range shows dimension is a tunable cost-quality knob, not a number you memorize or maximize blindly.
options_en: Dimension is a tunable cost-quality knob you adjust to fit the workload.
Dimension must exactly equal the number of business categories.
Higher dimension always makes cost negligible.
A large enough dimension means you can skip evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 向量的长度，决定表达力与训练/检索成本的权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding dimension is the length of the vector, trading off representational power against training and search cost.

scenario: 短视频首页召回 QPS 极高，候选库巨大，召回阶段延迟预算很紧。
scenario_en: A short-video home feed has very high retrieval QPS, a huge candidate pool, and a tight latency budget.
q: embedding 维度应该偏向哪种选择？
q_en: Which embedding dimension choice should you lean toward?
options: 1024+ 的大维度，不考虑成本
维度和用户数量保持一致
64-256 的小/中维度，先权衡吞吐和成本
每次请求都随机改变向量维度
why: 召回面对亿级向量和高 QPS，成本敏感；64-256 的小/中维度常能给出足够的粗召回质量。
why_en: High-QPS retrieval over huge candidate pools usually starts with a compact 64-to-256 dimensional embedding because serving cost dominates.
whenOtherWins: 如果是低 QPS、高价值的重排或离线分析，更大维度更可能赢。
tradeoff: 小维度换吞吐和成本 vs 大维度换表达力
options_en: A large 1024+ dimension, ignoring cost.
Keep the dimension equal to the number of users.
A small-to-medium 64-256 dimension, weighing throughput and cost first.
Randomly change the vector dimension on every request.
optionMeanings: 大维度表达力强，但训练/存储/检索都更贵。
维度和用户规模没有必然对应关系。
小/中维度能在高 QPS 下压低检索成本。
维度必须固定，否则索引无法比较向量。
optionScenarioImpacts: 亿级候选下检索延迟会显著上升。
用户增长会让维度失控式膨胀。
延迟预算紧张时仍能给出足够的粗召回质量。
不同维度的向量根本无法做近邻搜索。
optionDirectness: 大维度适合低 QPS 或重排，这里会放大服务成本。
用户数影响向量行数，不要求维度跟着增长。
高 QPS 粗召回先用小/中维度压低延迟和内存。
固定维度是 ANN 索引比较向量的基本前提。
optionMeanings_en: Large dimensions carry more expressive power but cost more to train, store, and search.
Dimension has no necessary relationship to the number of users.
Small-to-medium dimensions keep search cost down under high QPS.
Dimension must stay fixed, or the index cannot compare vectors.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Retrieval latency rises sharply over billion-scale candidates.
Dimension would balloon uncontrollably as users grow.
It still gives enough coarse-retrieval quality under a tight latency budget.
Vectors of different dimensions cannot be compared by nearest-neighbor search at all.
optionDirectness_en: Large dimensions fit low-QPS or reranking cases; here they raise serving cost.
User count affects the number of vector rows, not the dimension itself.
For high-QPS coarse retrieval, smaller dimensions reduce latency and memory.
Fixed dimension is required for an ANN index to compare vectors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量系统承受的请求速率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, queries per second, measures how many requests a system handles each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 向量的长度，决定表达力与训练/检索成本的权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding dimension is the length of the vector, trading off representational power against training and search cost.

scenario: 召回既要快速粗筛候选，又想在精排阶段保留高质量向量。
scenario_en: Retrieval needs fast coarse filtering, while reranking should still use a higher-quality vector.
q: Matryoshka embedding 的用途是什么？
q_en: What is Matryoshka embedding used for?
options: 把所有向量都压缩成 one-hot
同一向量的前缀维度本身也是有效 embedding
让 ANN 检索完全不需要建索引
自动帮所有新实体消除冷启动
why: Matryoshka 训练让前 64、128、256 维等前缀都能独立当向量用，小前缀粗召回、完整向量再重排。
why_en: Matryoshka embeddings let smaller prefixes of the same vector work on their own for fast coarse retrieval before full-vector reranking.
options_en: Compress every vector down into one-hot form.
A prefix of the same vector is also a valid, usable embedding.
Make ANN retrieval work without building any index.
Automatically eliminate cold start for every new entity.
optionMeanings: one-hot 是稀疏独立维度，和 Matryoshka 训练目标相反。
同一向量截取前段（如 64 维）依然是可用的表示。
ANN 仍需要索引结构来做近邻搜索。
冷启动仍要靠内容特征，不是维度技巧解决的。
optionScenarioImpacts: 误信会完全搞反 Matryoshka 的设计目标。
检索链路可以先用短向量筛选，后段再用长向量精排。
跳过索引会让检索退化成暴力扫描。
新用户/新物品依旧需要内容侧兜底。
optionDirectness: one-hot 和 Matryoshka 的前缀可用目标相反。
需要粗召回再重排时，可先用短前缀降低成本。
ANN 仍要建索引；Matryoshka 只改变可用维度前缀。
冷启动要靠内容或探索信号，不靠前缀训练解决。
optionMeanings_en: One-hot is sparse and isolated, the opposite of Matryoshka's goal.
Training makes prefixes like the first 64 or 128 dimensions usable as vectors on their own.
ANN still needs an index structure to do nearest-neighbor search.
Cold start still needs content features; it isn't solved by a dimension trick.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Believing this completely reverses Matryoshka's design goal.
A small prefix does coarse retrieval, then the full vector reranks.
Skipping the index degrades search into brute-force scanning.
New users or items still need a content-side fallback.
optionDirectness_en: One-hot conflicts with Matryoshka's prefix-usable vector goal.
Use short prefixes when coarse retrieval needs lower cost before reranking.
ANN still needs an index; Matryoshka changes usable vector prefixes.
Cold start needs content or exploration signals, not prefix training alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时让向量的前缀（如前 64/128 维）也单独有效的技巧。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Matryoshka embedding is trained so that its prefixes, like the first 64 or 128 dimensions, are also valid embeddings on their own.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻搜索，在向量索引里快速找出最接近的候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN, approximate nearest neighbor search, quickly finds the closest candidates inside a vector index.

scenario: 你训练完 embedding，面试官问怎么评估质量。
scenario_en: You have trained embeddings, and the interviewer asks how you would evaluate their quality.
q: intrinsic 和 extrinsic 评估的主要区别是？
q_en: What is the main difference between intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation?
options: 前者只能线上跑，后者只能离线跑
前者用于 SQL 查询，后者用于 Redis 缓存
前者不需要任何数据就能评估
前者看向量空间本身，后者看下游任务效果
why: Intrinsic 看向量空间本身（邻居、相似词）；extrinsic 看下游任务效果（recall@k、线上转化）。面试主指标应锚定 extrinsic。
why_en: Intrinsic evaluation inspects the embedding space itself, while extrinsic evaluation measures performance on the downstream task.
tradeoff: 向量空间自身结构 vs 下游任务真实效果
options_en: Intrinsic can only run online, extrinsic only offline.
Intrinsic is for SQL queries, extrinsic is for Redis caching.
Intrinsic needs no data at all to evaluate.
Intrinsic inspects the vector space itself; extrinsic measures downstream task performance.
optionMeanings: 两者的线上/离线归属和实际情况相反。
SQL/Redis 是存储技术，不是评估方法。
两类评估都需要数据，只是数据类型不同。
intrinsic 看几何结构，extrinsic 看任务指标。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会让人误判该在什么阶段用哪种评估。
混淆存储技术和评估方法两个概念。
会误以为可以不用数据就下结论。
extrinsic 结果应该是汇报给业务方的主线数字。
optionDirectness: 线上/离线是执行环境，不是 intrinsic/extrinsic 的定义。
SQL 和 Redis 是存储组件，不是 embedding 评估维度。
两类评估都要样本或任务数据，不能凭空判断。
选主指标时，应区分看空间本身还是看下游效果。
optionMeanings_en: This reverses the actual online/offline association.
SQL and Redis are storage technologies, not evaluation methods.
Both evaluation types need data, just different kinds.
Intrinsic looks at geometry; extrinsic looks at task metrics.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It leads to using the wrong evaluation at the wrong stage.
It confuses storage technology with an evaluation method.
It wrongly implies conclusions can be drawn without data.
Interviews should anchor the headline metric on extrinsic, with intrinsic as a sanity check.
optionDirectness_en: Online versus offline is an execution setting, not this definition.
SQL and Redis are storage components, not embedding evaluation types.
Both evaluation types need samples or task data.
For the main metric, separate space inspection from downstream performance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接检查向量空间本身的性质，比如近邻是否合理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Intrinsic evaluation directly inspects properties of the embedding space itself, such as whether nearest neighbors look sensible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用下游任务的真实效果衡量 embedding 好坏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Extrinsic evaluation measures embedding quality by performance on the actual downstream task.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序结果质量的指标，位置越靠前权重越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG is a ranking-quality metric that weights correctly ranked results more heavily near the top of the list.

scenario: 你训练了商品 embedding 用于召回，面试官问怎么评估。
scenario_en: You trained product embeddings for retrieval, and the interviewer asks how to evaluate them.
q: 最该作为主评估指标的是？
q_en: What should be the primary evaluation metric?
options: held-out 数据上的 Recall@K 或 NDCG
只看训练用的二维可视化投影好不好看
只汇报模型训练阶段的 loss 数值
只问同事的主观感觉并打分
why: 召回 embedding 的价值在能否找回相关候选，held-out 上的 recall@k / NDCG 最贴近这一点。
why_en: Retrieval embeddings should be evaluated mainly by recall or ranking metrics on held-out query-item pairs.
whenOtherWins: 早期训练调试时，邻居检查和向量分布 sanity check 更快，可作辅助。
tradeoff: 下游检索指标 vs 训练期代理指标
options_en: Recall@K or NDCG on held-out data.
Only whether the training-time 2D visualization plot looks nice.
Only report the model's training loss value.
Only ask a coworker for their subjective opinion and a score.
optionMeanings: 在没参与训练的数据上测真实检索效果。
二维投影是可视化技巧，不是评估指标。
训练 loss 只反映拟合过程，不等于检索质量。
主观感觉无法量化、不可复现。
optionScenarioImpacts: 能直接关联线上转化，指导上线决策。
好看的投影不代表召回效果好。
loss 低不代表 recall 高。
无法追踪迭代是否真的在改进。
optionDirectness: 做召回上线判断时，held-out 检索指标最贴近目标。
二维投影适合 sanity check，不能代表真实召回。
loss 适合看训练是否收敛，不等于业务检索效果。
主观评分可收反馈，但无法稳定比较迭代。
optionMeanings_en: It measures real retrieval performance on data never used in training.
A 2D projection is a visualization trick, not a metric.
Training loss only reflects fitting progress, not retrieval quality.
Subjective opinion cannot be quantified or reproduced.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It links directly to online conversion and informs ship decisions.
A nice-looking projection doesn't mean good retrieval.
Low loss does not imply high recall.
It cannot track whether iterations are truly improving.
optionDirectness_en: For retrieval launch decisions, held-out retrieval metrics match the goal.
A 2D projection is a sanity check, not proof of retrieval quality.
Loss shows optimization progress, not business retrieval performance.
Subjective ratings can collect feedback, but they cannot compare iterations reliably.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时完全没用过、专门留来测试的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Held-out data is data kept aside and never used during training, reserved for testing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索返回的前 K 个结果中，命中真正相关项的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@K measures the fraction of truly relevant items found within the top K retrieved results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序结果质量的指标，位置越靠前权重越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG is a ranking-quality metric that weights correctly ranked results more heavily near the top of the list.

scenario: 推荐系统的候选库很大，检索延迟预算很紧。
scenario_en: A recommender has a huge candidate pool and a tight retrieval latency budget.
q: 候选侧 embedding 生产环境通常怎么 serving？
q_en: How are candidate-side embeddings usually served in production?
options: 每次请求都现算全部候选库
只存进浏览器 localStorage
批量预计算后加载进 ANN 索引
只写进日志，从不参与查询
why: 候选库大且相对稳定，离线批量编码入 ANN 索引是低延迟检索的前提；在线只算请求侧向量。
why_en: Candidate embeddings are usually batch-computed offline and loaded into an ANN index so online serving only embeds the request.
options_en: Recompute the entire candidate pool on every request.
Store them only in the browser's localStorage.
Batch-precompute them and load them into an ANN index.
Only write them to logs and never query them.
optionMeanings: 在线现算全库对延迟和算力都不现实。
localStorage 是客户端存储，服务不到全体用户请求。
候选量级很大但变化不快，适合提前批量处理。

scenario: 新闻推荐要求几分钟内适应用户刚点击的突发事件，夜间批量刷新太慢。

whenOtherWins: 如果兴趣变化慢、延迟不敏感，批量刷新更简单可靠。
tradeoff: 近实时更新的工程复杂度 vs 批量刷新的简单稳定

Use no user behavior signal at all.

Update user embeddings in near real-time.

没有行为信号，推荐就无法个性化。

Minute-level freshness calls for near-real-time user embedding updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存放和近实时更新大规模 embedding 表的服务组件。

scenario: 推荐系统里，新用户和新物品还没有任何互动记录。
scenario_en: In a recommender, new users and items have no interaction records yet.

scenario: 新视频刚上传，0 次观看，但推荐系统仍要给它有限曝光。
scenario_en: A new video has just been uploaded with zero views, but the recommender still needs to give it limited exposure.
q: 最合理的初始表示是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable initial representation?
options: 等它自然积累大量观看后再处理
随机给它一个热门视频的向量

whenOtherWins: 如果平台明确只推荐成熟库存，等待行为数据更安全，但会牺牲新创作者成长。

flowchart LR

  Interactions[New interactions] --> Blend[Blend behavior]
  Initial --> Blend

scenario: 系统要在毫秒级从大规模候选库里检索最相关结果。
scenario_en: The system needs to retrieve the most relevant results from a large candidate pool within milliseconds.
q: 按正确顺序排列 embedding 检索 serving 流程。
q_en: Put the embedding retrieval serving flow in the right order.
why: 候选侧预计算是规模化关键；在线路径只做请求编码、近邻检索和下游处理，把重计算放到离线。
why_en: Retrieval scales by precomputing candidate vectors offline, embedding the request online, searching the ANN index, then handing results downstream.
whenOtherWins: 如果候选库很小、延迟不敏感，在线全量编码和精排会更简单。

离线编码候选并构建 ANN 索引
用 ANN 找 top-k 近邻
把候选交给 ranker 或生成器下游处理
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[Encode candidates] --> B[Build ANN]
  B --> C[Embed request]
  C --> D[Search top K]
  D --> E[Rank or generate]

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持快速近邻搜索的向量索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ANN index is a vector index structure built to support fast nearest-neighbor search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线把用户请求或查询实时编码成的向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A query embedding is the vector produced by encoding the user's request or query online, in real time.

scenario: 你在训练两塔召回模型，需要让 loss 把 query 和 candidate 向量对齐到同一空间。
scenario_en: You are training a two-tower retrieval model and need the loss to align query and candidate vectors in one space.
q: 按正确顺序排列两塔 contrastive 训练流程。
q_en: Put the two-tower contrastive training flow in the right order.
why: 训练先定义正负关系，再编码两侧、算相似度，最后用 loss 调整空间，负样本质量决定边界学得多细。
why_en: Two-tower contrastive training collects pairs, encodes both sides, scores similarity, and updates the towers to separate positives from negatives.
whenOtherWins: 如果候选数量很小且质量优先，交叉编码器可直接联合看 query 和 candidate。
tradeoff: 双塔预计算效率 vs 交叉编码质量
steps: 计算 batch 内所有 query-candidate 相似度
收集正样本对并采样负样本
更新两个塔让正样本更近、负样本更远
分别编码 query/user 和 candidate/item
diagram:
flowchart LR
  P[Positive pairs] --> E[Encode both sides]
  N[Negatives] --> E
  E --> S[Similarity matrix]
  S --> L[Contrastive loss]
  L --> U[Update towers]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用两个独立编码器分别编码查询和候选，输出到同一向量空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model uses two separate encoders, one for the query and one for the candidate, that output into the same vector space.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拉近正样本、推远负样本的训练目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A contrastive loss trains the model to pull positive pairs closer together and push negative pairs farther apart.

审核模型会自动变成无监督模型
所有向量维度都自带人工标签
训练目标可能和审核风险不一致
why: 推荐 embedding 表示的是原训练目标学到的结构，可能编码“会互动”而非“是否违规”，需验证下游收益和偏差。
why_en: Shared embeddings carry the structure of their original training objective, which may not align with a new downstream task.
options_en: Embeddings can never be used as an input feature.
The moderation model automatically becomes unsupervised.
Every dimension comes with a human-readable label.
The original training objective may not align with moderation risk.
optionMeanings: 跨团队复用 embedding 做特征是常见做法。
换用途不会改变模型本身的监督方式。
embedding 维度通常没有人工可读标签。
推荐目标学的是“会互动”，不等于“是否违规”。
optionScenarioImpacts: 这个说法直接否定了 embedding 迁移的价值。
监督方式取决于任务设计，不会自动改变。
维度含义通常隐式，需要额外分析才能解释。
直接套用可能漏检或误伤，需要验证下游收益。
optionDirectness: embedding 可迁移做特征，但必须验证任务是否对齐。
监督方式由审核模型训练决定，不由 embedding 来源决定。
维度通常不可解释，不能当人工标签直接用。
跨任务复用时，先检查原训练目标和新风险是否一致。
optionMeanings_en: Reusing embeddings across teams as features is common practice.
Changing the use case does not change the model's own supervision.
Embedding dimensions usually carry no human-readable label.
The recommendation objective learns 'will engage,' not 'is this a violation.'
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This claim directly denies the value of transferring embeddings.
Supervision style depends on task design, not on reuse.
Dimension meaning is usually implicit and needs extra analysis to interpret.
Direct reuse risks misses or false flags, so downstream gains must be validated.
optionDirectness_en: Embeddings can transfer as features, but task alignment must be checked.
The moderation model training setup decides supervision, not embedding origin.
Dimensions are usually implicit, so they cannot serve as human labels.
For cross-task reuse, compare the old training objective with the new risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断内容是否违规、需要处理的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content moderation is the system that judges whether content violates policy and needs action.

scenario: 平台需要找出内容库里高度相似的重复内容。
scenario_en: The platform needs to find highly similar duplicate content in a large content library.
q: 有了好 embedding 后，近重复检测通常怎么做？
q_en: With good embeddings, how do you usually detect near duplicates?
options: 按向量距离阈值找邻近样本
只比较原始字符串长度
随机抽样，全靠人工肉眼看
按主键做哈希取模分组
why: embedding 把语义或行为相似的实体放得近，近重复可以用距离阈值系统性发现；阈值要按误报/漏报权衡调。
why_en: Near-duplicate detection typically uses a distance threshold inside a good embedding space.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Item[Item embedding] --> ANN[Nearest neighbors]
  ANN --> Dist[Distance threshold]
  Dist --> Dup[Near duplicate set]
  Dup --> Review[Tune FP FN]
options_en: Find neighboring samples using a vector-distance threshold.
Compare only the raw string length.
Randomly sample and eyeball every pair manually.
Group items by hashing and modding the primary key.
optionMeanings: 距离近的向量代表语义或行为上相近的实体。
字符串长度和内容相似度基本无关。
人工肉眼查看在大规模数据下不可扩展。
哈希取模只是分桶，不反映内容相似度。
optionScenarioImpacts: 用 ANN 或阈值就能系统性地找出近重复。
长度相同的内容可能完全不相关。
覆盖率低，容易漏掉大部分重复对。
同一哈希桶里的内容不一定相似。
optionDirectness: 有可靠向量空间时，距离阈值能规模化筛近重复。
字符串长度只适合粗过滤，不代表语义重复。
人工抽查适合校准阈值，不能覆盖大库。
哈希取模适合分片，不表达内容相似。
optionMeanings_en: Vectors close in distance represent entities similar in meaning or behavior.
String length has almost nothing to do with content similarity.
Manual eyeballing does not scale to large datasets.
Hash-and-mod grouping only buckets items and ignores content similarity.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: ANN plus a threshold systematically surfaces near-duplicates.
Content of the same length can be completely unrelated.
Coverage is low, missing most true duplicate pairs.
Items in the same hash bucket are not necessarily similar.
optionDirectness_en: In a reliable vector space, a distance threshold scales near-duplicate search.
String length can be a crude filter, but not a semantic duplicate test.
Manual review can calibrate thresholds, but cannot cover a large library.
Hash modding is for sharding, not content similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容高度相似但不完全相同的一对样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A near-duplicate is a pair of samples that are highly similar but not exactly identical.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断两个向量是否“足够近”的截断值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distance threshold is the cutoff value used to decide whether two vectors are 'close enough' to count as similar.

scenario: 你已经有商品 embedding，面试官问它该进 ranker 还是只做召回。
scenario_en: You already have product embeddings, and the interviewer asks whether they belong in the ranker or only in retrieval.
q: 最合理的回答是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable answer?
options: embedding 只能用来做召回
embedding 只能当分类标签用
召回用相似度，ranker 也能把它当特征
embedding 只能用来做离线可视化
why: embedding 既能做 ANN 检索 key，也能作为 ranker 的紧凑语义特征，是否同时用取决于延迟和收益。
why_en: The same embedding can power retrieval by similarity and also serve as a compact feature for the ranker.
whenOtherWins: 如果 ranker 已有更强的原始多模态特征，直接喂 embedding 的边际收益可能较小。
tradeoff: 召回相似度用法 vs ranker 特征用法
options_en: Embeddings can only be used for retrieval.
Embeddings can only serve as a classification label.
Retrieval uses similarity, and the ranker can also use it as a feature.
Embeddings can only be used for offline visualization.
optionMeanings: 召回之外，embedding 还能给 ranker 当输入特征。
标签是离散类别，embedding 是连续向量，不是一回事。
同一份向量能同时支撑召回和精排两个阶段。
可视化只是分析手段，不是它的唯一用途。
optionScenarioImpacts: 这个说法会让你漏掉精排阶段的一个便宜信号。
把向量和标签混淆会误导模型设计。
两阶段可以共用同一份 embedding，节省成本。
低估了 embedding 在生产模型里的实际用途。
optionDirectness: 只做召回会漏掉 ranker 可用的紧凑语义特征。
分类标签是监督目标，embedding 是连续输入特征。
同一向量可先召回，再作为 ranker 的一个特征。
可视化适合调试，不是生产里的唯一用途。
optionMeanings_en: Beyond retrieval, an embedding can also be an input feature for the ranker.
A label is discrete while an embedding is continuous; they are not the same thing.
The same vector can support both the retrieval and ranking stages.
Visualization is just one analysis tool, not its only use.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This claim makes you miss a cheap signal available at ranking time.
Confusing a vector with a label misleads model design.
Both stages can share the same embedding, saving cost.
It underestimates how embeddings are actually used in production models.
optionDirectness_en: Retrieval-only use misses a compact semantic feature for the ranker.
A label is a supervision target; an embedding is a continuous input feature.
The same vector can retrieve candidates and then feed the ranker.
Visualization helps debugging, but it is not the only production use.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对召回候选做精细排序、给出最终展示顺序的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ranker is the model that finely sorts retrieved candidates to produce the final display order.

scenario: 面试官让你从头讲一个 ML 系统该怎么评估，你要给出一个可复用的框架顺序。
scenario_en: An interviewer asks you to explain how to evaluate an ML system from scratch, and you need a reusable discussion order.
q: ML 系统设计里组织 evaluation 讨论的推荐顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the recommended order for structuring an ML system evaluation discussion?
why: 先锚定业务目标，再逐层落到产品指标、ML 指标和评估方法，最后处理不平衡、标注成本等挑战。
why_en: A strong evaluation answer works top-down: business goal, product metric, ML metric, methodology, then known pitfalls.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Biz[Business goal] --> Product[Product metric]
  Product --> ML[ML metric]
  ML --> Method[Offline or online]
  Method --> Risks[Bias and drift]
options: 先调超参 → 再找业务目标 → 最后上线
只报 accuracy → 结束
业务目标 → 产品指标 → ML 指标 → 评估方法 → 挑战
先画数据库表 → 再谈模型
options_en: Tune hyperparameters first, then look for a business goal, then ship.
Just report accuracy and stop there.
Business goal, then product metric, ML metric, evaluation method, and challenges.
Start by drawing database tables, then discuss the model.
optionExplanations: 反了：先调参数会让指标脱离业务价值，价值判断应该在最前面。
单一 accuracy 没有区分产品指标和 ML 指标，也漏掉了方法论和挑战。
对；这个顺序保证每一层指标都能回溯到业务价值，不是拍脑袋定的。
评估框架是自上而下的目标分解，不是从数据库表结构开始的。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards — tuning first detaches metrics from business value, which should anchor the discussion.
A single accuracy number skips product metrics, ML metrics, and the challenges discussion.
Correct — each layer of metric traces back to business value instead of being picked arbitrarily.
The framework decomposes a goal top-down; it does not start from a database schema.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接衡量模型输出质量的技术指标，如 precision、NDCG。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ML metric is a technical measure of model output quality, such as precision or NDCG.

termDefinitions.meaning: 好看但不反映真实业务价值的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vanity metric looks impressive on a dashboard but does not track real business value.

scenario: 面试官问“怎么评估这个 ML 系统”，题目还很模糊。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how you would evaluate this ML system, but the prompt is still vague.
q: 你最应该先问或先确定什么？
q_en: What should you ask or pin down first?
why: 没有业务目标，ML 指标容易变成 vanity metric。先确定动作和价值，再选择产品指标与技术指标。
why_en: Evaluation should begin with the business outcome because technical metrics only matter if they track that outcome.
tradeoff: 业务目标优先 vs 技术指标优先
options: 系统要优化的业务结果是什么
模型有几层神经网络
数据库主键类型
前端展示颜色
options_en: What business outcome is this system meant to move?
How many neural network layers does the model have?
What is the primary key type in the database?
What color scheme does the front end use?
whenOtherWins: 如果业务目标已被明确约束，下一步才是选择产品/ML 指标和实验设计。
optionExplanations: 对；没先钉住业务结果，后面所有指标都可能是空转。
模型层数是架构细节，回答不了“评估什么”这个问题。
主键类型属于存储设计，和评估要解决的问题无关。
UI 配色不是技术判断，和 ML 系统评估无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — without a pinned business outcome, every downstream metric risks being arbitrary.
Layer count is an architecture detail; it does not answer what to evaluate.
Primary key type is a storage decision, unrelated to evaluation.
UI color scheme is not a technical judgment relevant to ML evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 好看但不反映真实业务价值的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vanity metric looks impressive but does not track real business value.

scenario: 内容审核模型判断一条帖子是否违规，你要向面试官解释 precision 和 recall 分别衡量什么。
scenario_en: A content moderation model decides whether a post violates policy, and you need to explain what precision and recall measure.
q: 分类系统里 precision 和 recall 的区别是？
q_en: In a classifier, what is the difference between precision and recall?
why: Precision 关心误杀少不少，recall 关心漏抓少不少。阈值移动会在两者之间做权衡。
why_en: Precision measures correctness among positive predictions, while recall measures how many true positives were found.
tradeoff: precision（误判成本）vs recall（漏判成本）
options: precision 只反映延迟高低
precision 看预测为正的准确率，recall 看正例的覆盖率
precision 用来做回归，recall 用来做排序
两者衡量完全相同的东西
options_en: Precision only reflects latency.
Precision measures accuracy among positive predictions, recall measures coverage of real positives.
Precision is used for regression, recall for ranking.
The two measure exactly the same thing.
optionExplanations: 错；precision 和延迟无关，它算的是预测为正里对了多少。
对；precision = 判为正里真对的比例，recall = 真实正例里被抓到的比例。
错；precision/recall 都是分类指标，不是回归或排序专用词。
错；分母不同——一个基于预测为正，一个基于真实为正，会给出不同数字。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — precision has nothing to do with latency; it measures correctness among positive predictions.
Correct — precision is accuracy among predicted positives; recall is coverage of actual positives.
Incorrect — both are classification metrics, not one for regression and one for ranking.
Incorrect — they use different denominators (predicted-positive vs actual-positive), so they diverge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测为正的样本里，真正为正的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the share of positive predictions that are actually correct.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有真实正例里，被模型正确找出的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the share of actual positives that the model correctly identifies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型打分转成是/否判断所用的分界值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A threshold is the score cutoff used to turn a model's score into a yes/no decision.

scenario: 有害内容自动删除必须避免误删，产品要求删除内容 95% 以上确实违规。
scenario_en: An automated harmful-content remover must avoid false removals, and product requires over 95 percent of removed items to truly violate policy.
q: 离线主阈值指标应更靠近哪个？
q_en: Which offline operating-point metric should be the primary threshold metric?
why: 自动动作的 guardrail 是高 precision，所以在 precision=95% 的操作点看 recall 更贴近决策。Accuracy 在低 prevalence 下会误导。
why_en: When automated action requires 95% precision, recall at that precision is the meaningful operating metric.
tradeoff: precision 门槛（误删风险）vs recall（覆盖率）
options: 总体 accuracy
训练 loss 最低值
ROC 曲线截图
Recall@Precision95
options_en: Overall accuracy.
The lowest training loss value.
A screenshot of the ROC curve.
Recall at 95 percent precision.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是早期模型比较且没有固定动作阈值，PR-AUC 更稳定。
optionExplanations: 错；类别很不平衡时 accuracy 会被大量负例主导，掩盖误删风险。
错；训练 loss 不是业务对齐的评估指标，也不反映线上误删率。
错；ROC 曲线本身不是一个可跟踪的单一数字，也不对齐 95% precision 门槛。
对；先卡住 95% precision 的误删门槛，再看这时能抓到多少，最贴近业务约束。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — with heavy imbalance, accuracy is dominated by negatives and hides the false-removal risk.
Incorrect — training loss is not aligned to the business guardrail or live removal errors.
Incorrect — a ROC curve is not a single trackable number, and it ignores the 95% precision requirement.
Correct — fix the 95% precision guardrail first, then track how much you catch at that point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 precision 固定为 95% 的阈值下，模型能达到的 recall。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall at precision 95 is the recall achieved at the threshold where precision equals 95 percent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测正确的样本占全部样本的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Accuracy is the share of all predictions that are correct.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在不同阈值下画出真阳性率对假阳性率的曲线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ROC curve plots the true positive rate against the false positive rate across thresholds.

scenario: 内容审核数据里正例只占 1%，你要向面试官解释为什么团队用 PR-AUC 而不是 ROC-AUC 报告模型质量。
scenario_en: In content moderation data, positives are only 1 percent, and you need to explain why the team reports PR-AUC instead of ROC-AUC.
q: 强类别不平衡时，为什么 PR-AUC 往往比 ROC-AUC 更有用？
q_en: Why is PR-AUC often more useful than ROC-AUC under heavy class imbalance?
why: 正例 <1% 时，模型对正例很差也能有好看的 ROC-AUC；PR 曲线直接暴露 precision/recall 权衡。
why_en: PR-AUC is more informative under heavy class imbalance because it focuses on positive-class retrieval quality.
tradeoff: PR-AUC（正类质量）vs ROC-AUC（整体区分能力）
options: PR-AUC 不需要人工标签数据
PR-AUC 高就能直接自动上线
PR-AUC 更关注正类，不被负例稀释
ROC-AUC 只适用于回归任务
options_en: PR-AUC does not need any human labels.
A high PR-AUC means you can auto-launch the model.
PR-AUC focuses on positive-class quality and is not diluted by negatives.
ROC-AUC only applies to regression tasks.
optionExplanations: 错；PR-AUC 和 ROC-AUC 一样都要靠标注好的正负例来算。
错；再高的 PR-AUC 也只是代理指标，上线还要看业务和安全信号。
对；PR-AUC 只看正类，不会被海量真负例稀释，对稀有正例更敏感。
错；ROC-AUC 是分类指标，衡量正负样本的区分能力，不用于回归。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — PR-AUC needs labeled positives and negatives just like ROC-AUC does.
Incorrect — a high PR-AUC is still a proxy metric; launch decisions need business and safety signals too.
Correct — PR-AUC focuses on the positive class and is not diluted by the huge number of true negatives.
Incorrect — ROC-AUC is a classification metric measuring class separability, not a regression metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: precision-recall 曲线下的面积，综合衡量不同阈值下的表现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PR-AUC is the area under the precision-recall curve across all thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下的面积，衡量模型整体区分正负样本的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ROC-AUC is the area under the ROC curve, measuring how well a model separates positive from negative classes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 正负样本数量差距很大，比如正例只占 1%。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Class imbalance means one class is far rarer than the other, such as positives being only 1 percent of the data.

q: 补全 F1 的含义。
q_en: Fill in what F1 means.
why: F1 方便但会隐藏业务上 precision 与 recall 的不对称成本。
why_en: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, but it can hide asymmetric business costs.
text: F1 是 precision 和 recall 的{{调和平均}}，适合需要单数概括两者权衡时使用。

termDefinitions.meaning: precision 和 recall 的调和平均数，用一个数概括两者的权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, summarizing their tradeoff in one number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种平均方式，对较小值更敏感，常用于比例型指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A harmonic mean is an average that is more sensitive to small values, often used for rate-like metrics.

scenario: 新审核模型尚未被信任，但你想知道它在线会标哪些内容。
scenario_en: A new moderation model is not trusted yet, but you want to see what it would flag on live traffic.
q: 最安全的上线评估方式是？
q_en: What is the safest online evaluation method?
why: Shadow mode 只记录预测、不影响用户，能观察分数分布和候选样本，建立信心后再进 A/B。
why_en: Shadow mode lets a classifier make predictions without taking user-visible actions while labels and safety are checked.
tradeoff: 观察风险（shadow mode）vs 反应速度（直接上线）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Traffic[Live traffic] --> Old[Old model acts]
  Traffic --> New[New model shadows]
  New --> Logs[Predictions only]
  Logs --> Labels[Sample labels]
  Labels --> Decision[Go or hold]
options: Shadow mode：预测但不动作，再抽样校验
直接全量替换旧模型并执行删除
只看训练集上的 accuracy
让用户自己猜模型的判断结果
options_en: Shadow mode: predict without acting, then sample and review.
Fully replace the old model and start removing content immediately.
Only look at training-set accuracy.
Let users guess what the model would decide.
whenOtherWins: 如果动作风险很低、可快速回滚，小流量 A/B 可能更快。
optionExplanations: 对；先看预测不动手，能在零用户风险下积累信心和标注样本。
错；新模型没被验证就全量替换，误删风险和信任成本都很高。
错；训练集 accuracy 不代表线上分布，也看不到误删/漏放情况。
错；这不是评估方法，只是把判断丢给用户，没有任何系统性验证。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — observing predictions without acting builds confidence and labeled samples with zero user risk.
Incorrect — replacing fully before validation risks over-removal and destroys trust if it is wrong.
Incorrect — training accuracy does not reflect live distribution or catch removal/miss errors.
Incorrect — this is not an evaluation method at all; it offloads judgment to users with no rigor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型只做预测记录，不对外采取真实动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shadow mode lets a model make predictions without taking any user-facing action.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把流量随机分组，各自看不同版本来比较效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test randomly splits traffic into groups that each see a different version to compare outcomes.

scenario: 内容审核正例只占很小比例，团队打算随机抽样发给标注员打标签。
scenario_en: Positive moderation cases are rare, and the team plans to send random samples to human labelers.
q: 在少数类很稀有的分类评估里，随机标注的主要问题是什么？
