termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.

q: 每加一种支付方式都要改 PaymentProcessor，最大的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest risk of editing PaymentProcessor every time a payment method is added?
options: 反复改核心逻辑，增加回归 bug 风险
新增的实现类数量变得太少
接口的数量会变得太多太杂
自动化测试变得完全不需要
options_en: Repeatedly editing core logic raises regression-bug risk.
You end up creating too few new implementation classes.
You end up with too many, too scattered interfaces.
Automated testing becomes completely unnecessary.
why: OCP 想避免的正是稳定代码被反复打开修改；把变化放进新的实现类能缩小回归范围。
why_en: OCP exists precisely to avoid reopening stable code again and again, and pushing change into new implementation classes shrinks the regression surface.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

scenario: CoffeeMachine 类同时管理库存、收款、冲泡配方和屏幕渲染，后续每个新需求都要改它。
scenario_en: CoffeeMachine manages inventory, payment, brew recipes, and screen rendering all at once, so every new requirement means editing it.
q: 你会如何解释重构方向？
q_en: How would you explain the refactoring direction here?
options: 把所有方法都统一改成 static 方法
按变化原因拆成四个协作类分开管理
只在原有方法里继续叠加 if 分支判断
只把类的名字换一个就足够
options_en: Turn every method into a static method.
Split into four collaborating classes by reason to change.
Keep stacking if-branches inside the original method.
Just rename the class and call it done.
why: SRP 不是为了类的数量多，而是让库存、支付、配方、显示的变化互不牵连。
why_en: SRP isn't about having more classes — it's about keeping inventory, payment, recipe, and display changes from tangling with each other.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目只要求最小冲泡流程、不涉及支付和显示，先留一个简单 orchestrator 也可以。
tradeoff: 单类快速起步 vs 拆分后每个变化互不影响
diagram:
flowchart LR
CM["CoffeeMachine orchestrator"] --> I["Inventory"]
CM --> P["Payment"]
CM --> R["Recipe/Brewer"]
CM --> D["Display"]
I --> IR["stock changes"]
P --> PR["payment changes"]
R --> RR["brew rules"]
D --> DR["UI text"]

q: 为什么「接口越多越好」不是正确理解 SOLID？
q_en: Why is "more interfaces is always better" a wrong reading of SOLID?
options: 接口这种语法只能用在 Java 语言里
接口在任何场景下都完全没有成本
接口也有认知成本，只有真实变化点才值得加
接口会自动帮你生成对应的实现代码
options_en: Interfaces only exist as a Java-only syntax feature.
Interfaces never carry any cost in any scenario.
Interfaces have cognitive cost too, so they're worth adding only at a real variation point.
Interfaces automatically generate their implementations for you.
why: 抽象能隔离变化，但也会增加间接层；面试里要展示你知道何时加、何时不加。
why_en: Abstraction isolates change but also adds a layer of indirection, so the interview signal is knowing when to add it and when not to.
tradeoff: 接口带来的扩展安全 vs 额外的间接层认知成本

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

q: 关于如何在面试里使用这些设计原则，哪些说法是合理的？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about using these design principles in an interview are reasonable? (multi-select)
options: 不需要不断点名原则
用原则指导决策并解释取舍
原则是思考工具，不是打勾清单
必须在每句话里都提一次 SOLID
options_en: You don't need to keep naming principles out loud.
Use principles to guide decisions and explain tradeoffs.
Principles are thinking tools, not a checklist to tick off.
You must mention SOLID in every single sentence.
why: 好的设计会自然体现原则；刻意报术语不如清楚说明为什么这样拆类或抽象。
why_en: Good design shows the principles naturally, so explaining why you split a class or added an abstraction beats reciting the term names.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

scenario: 面试官问：“为什么不现在就抽象出一个 Validator 服务？”
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: "Why not abstract out a Validator service right now?"
q: 哪个回答最成熟？
q_en: Which answer sounds the most mature?
options: 因为 DRY 原则从来都不重要
我会立刻抽象出所有校验逻辑
Validator 必须做成 Singleton 模式
现在只有 User 一处用，先放 User 里；多处重复再提取
options_en: Because the DRY principle never matters.
I would abstract all validation logic immediately.
Validator must be built as a Singleton.
Only User uses this today, so keep it there for now and extract once the rule repeats in multiple places.
why: 这个回答同时体现了 KISS、DRY 和 YAGNI 的平衡；没有拒绝抽象，只是把它推迟到有证据时再做。
why_en: This answer balances KISS, DRY, and YAGNI at once — it doesn't reject abstraction, it just defers it until there's real evidence for it.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求已经写明多个实体共享同一验证规则，提前抽出 Validator 就合理。
tradeoff: 现在保持简单 vs 提前抽象共享校验逻辑

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

q: 低层设计（LLD）面试主要考什么？
q_en: What do low-level design interviews mainly test?
options: 大规模分布式架构和容量估算
把一个自包含问题组织成清晰的类、接口和交互
只写 SQL 查询优化
只背诵设计模式名称
options_en: Large-scale distributed architecture and capacity estimation.
Organizing a self-contained problem into clean classes, interfaces, and interactions.
Just writing SQL query optimizations.
Just memorizing design pattern names.
why: LLD 的核心是代码结构：对象是什么、谁拥有状态、方法如何协作、后续需求能否自然加入。它不是在白板上画服务拓扑。
why_en: Low-level design interviews test whether you can turn a scoped problem into clean classes, interfaces, state, and interactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计：面试中考察类、接口、方法和对象交互的设计能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD, or Low-Level Design, is an interview format that tests how you design classes, interfaces, and object interactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于查询和操作关系型数据库的语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL, or Structured Query Language, is the language used to query and manipulate relational databases.

scenario: 题目是“设计停车场系统”，面试官要求你做低层设计而不是系统设计。
scenario_en: The prompt is "design a parking lot," and the interviewer wants low-level design rather than system design.
q: 你的第一层关注点应该是什么？
q_en: What should you focus on first?
options: 先规划跨美国、欧洲、亚洲三地的部署方案
ParkingLot、Spot、Vehicle 类与方法
先估算 Kafka 分区数和每秒吞吐量
先设计 CDN 边缘节点缓存策略
options_en: Start by planning a deployment across the US, Europe, and Asia.
Model classes and methods like ParkingLot, Spot, and Vehicle.
Start by estimating Kafka partition count and per-second throughput.
Start by designing a CDN edge-node caching strategy.
why: LLD 关注单个功能或服务内部的代码蓝图。先建模类、状态和操作，再讨论边界和扩展。
why_en: For LLD, start with the domain objects, state, methods, and relationships inside the feature rather than distributed infrastructure.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求系统设计停车场平台或网约车后端，才切到服务、存储、流量和扩展架构。
tradeoff: 对象建模的代码蓝图 vs 分布式基础设施的架构取舍
optionMeanings: 把停车场系统直接扩成多区域部署问题。
把停车场核心实体和方法当成设计起点。
把停车场读写简化成消息队列吞吐问题。
把停车场缓存简化成边缘节点分发问题。
optionScenarioImpacts: 跳过对象和状态设计，答案会偏离 LLD 主线。
能直接产出 ParkingLot/Spot/Vehicle 的类和状态机。
分区吞吐属于系统设计容量估算，不是本题要点。
边缘缓存策略和单场地停车逻辑无关。
optionDirectness: 只有跨区域停车平台才需要先谈部署。
当题目限定 LLD 时，类和方法是先交付物。
只有要设计事件流或异步管线时才先算 Kafka。
只有静态内容分发或读缓存题才先谈 CDN。
optionMeanings_en: Turns the parking lot into a multi-region deployment problem.
Uses the core parking-lot entities and methods as the starting point.
Reduces parking-lot reads and writes to a message-queue throughput problem.
Treats the parking lot as an edge-cache distribution problem.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It skips object and state design, so the answer drifts away from LLD.
It can produce ParkingLot, Spot, Vehicle, and their state transitions.
Partition throughput is a system-design capacity topic, not the core LLD task.
Edge caching does not decide the single-facility parking logic.
optionDirectness_en: Start here only if the prompt is a cross-region parking platform.
Use this when the prompt is scoped as LLD and asks for classes and methods.
Start with Kafka only for an event-streaming or async-pipeline design.
Start with a CDN only for static-content delivery or read caching.

termDefinitions.meaning: 停车场系统里代表整个场地、管理车位分配的核心类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ParkingLot is the core class that represents the whole facility and manages spot assignment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种分布式消息队列，常用于系统设计里的异步事件流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue commonly used for asynchronous event streaming in system design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN, or Content Delivery Network, caches static content on edge servers close to users.

scenario: 你在准备一道“设计电梯调度系统”的 LLD 题，脑子里冒出要不要把 Factory、Observer、Visitor 等模式全部用上、并按经典 UML 继承层级建模。
scenario_en: You are preparing an elevator scheduling LLD and wondering whether to force Factory, Observer, Visitor, and a classic UML inheritance tree into it.
q: 更贴近现代生产代码的取向是什么？
q_en: What approach is closer to modern production code?
options: 把每个模式目录里的模式都尝试套进设计
先背熟 GoF 模式定义，再决定要不要用
优先组合和简单状态，只在真正需要变化点时才引入模式
用最深的继承层级覆盖所有电梯类型
options_en: Try to force every pattern from the catalog into the design.
Memorize GoF pattern definitions first, then decide whether to use them.
Default to composition and simple state, and only reach for a pattern at a real variation point.
Use the deepest inheritance hierarchy to cover every elevator type.
why: 现代生产代码更看重组合、简单状态和务实取舍；模式只在真正遇到变化点时才引入，不是提前铺好目录。
why_en: Modern production code favors composition and simple state, reaching for a design pattern only at an actual variation point instead of pre-loading the whole catalog.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确追问某个模式名称（常见于部分印度/亚洲公司），可以在合适场景点名模式，但仍以解决变化点为主。
tradeoff: 组合+按需引入模式 vs 教材式套用继承层级和模式目录

termDefinitions.meaning: 工厂模式：把对象创建逻辑集中封装，调用方不用关心具体子类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern centralizes object creation so callers don't need to know the concrete subclass.

termDefinitions.meaning: 观察者模式：状态变化时自动通知一组订阅者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern notifies a set of subscribers automatically when state changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 访问者模式：把对一组对象的操作抽出来，不用修改这些对象本身的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Visitor pattern pulls an operation on a group of objects out of those objects' own classes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指经典《设计模式》一书作者合称，书中列出 23 种经典模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GoF, or Gang of Four, refers to the authors of the classic Design Patterns book and its 23 catalog patterns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，用图表表示类、关系和继承结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a diagram notation for classes, relationships, and inheritance.

q: LLD 和系统设计最根本的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between LLD and system design?
options: 两者都要求提交可编译完整项目
LLD 只画网络拓扑图，不谈状态
LLD 和系统设计都不需要解释取舍
LLD 管类和状态；系统设计管服务和流量
options_en: Both require a full compilable project submission.
LLD only draws network topology diagrams and ignores state.
Neither LLD nor system design requires explaining tradeoffs.
LLD is about classes and state; system design is about services and traffic.
why: 系统设计画的是大系统地图，LLD 写的是某个组件或功能内部的代码蓝图。二者问题、尺度和评价点都不同。
why_en: System design focuses on large-scale architecture, while LLD focuses on object models, APIs, state, and code-level behavior.
tradeoff: 组件内部代码蓝图 vs 分布式服务架构取舍

termDefinitions.meaning: 组件对外暴露的方法调用接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API, or Application Programming Interface, is the set of methods a component exposes to callers.

scenario: 同样是网约车题，面试官说这是低层设计面试。
scenario_en: The same rideshare prompt is explicitly framed as a low-level design interview.
q: 哪种产出更符合 LLD？
q_en: Which output better matches an LLD interview?
options: 画 matching service、pricing service、queue、datastore 的服务图
设计 Trip、TripState、PricingCalculator 以及状态转换方法
估算全球司机位置写入 QPS
讨论多区域强一致性
options_en: Draw a service diagram with a matching service, pricing service, queue, and datastore.
Design Trip, TripState, and PricingCalculator along with their state-transition methods.
Estimate global QPS for driver location writes.
Discuss multi-region strong consistency.
why: LLD 需要把某个功能的对象和行为讲清楚，例如 Trip 如何分配司机、开始、完成、取消。服务拓扑属于系统设计。
why_en: For rideshare LLD, model classes like Trip and PricingCalculator and their state transitions rather than distributed services.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确是“设计 Uber 后端架构”，服务图和扩展性讨论才是主线。
tradeoff: 对象/状态建模 vs 分布式服务拓扑与容量规划

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量系统吞吐量的常用指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, or Queries Per Second, measures how many requests a system handles each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 表示 Trip 生命周期状态的枚举，例如已请求、已分配司机、进行中、已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TripState is an enum representing the trip's lifecycle, such as requested, assigned, in progress, or completed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责根据行程数据计算车费的组件接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PricingCalculator is the component interface responsible for computing the fare from trip data.

scenario: 你在设计 Trip 类，Trip 只能在 DRIVER_ASSIGNED 后 start，只能在 IN_PROGRESS 后 complete。
scenario_en: You are designing a Trip class: it can start only after DRIVER_ASSIGNED and complete only after IN_PROGRESS.
q: 这段代码展示了哪种 LLD 能力？
q_en: What LLD skill does this code demonstrate?
options: 只展示系统容量估算
把所有规则推给 UI
把业务状态转换封装在拥有状态的对象里
把 Trip 做成全局单例
options_en: Only show system capacity estimation.
Push all the validation rules into the UI layer.
Encapsulate business state transitions inside the object that owns the state.
Make Trip a global singleton.
why: LLD 看重对象是否能维护自己的不变量。Trip 拥有 state，就应该在相关方法里拒绝非法转换。
why_en: The code shows LLD state ownership by keeping transition rules inside the Trip object that owns the state.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态流非常复杂且行为随状态大幅变化，可以进一步引入状态机结构。
tradeoff: 对象自我校验状态转换 vs 把校验规则丢给外部调用方/UI
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> REQUESTED
REQUESTED --> DRIVER_ASSIGNED : assign driver
DRIVER_ASSIGNED --> IN_PROGRESS : start_trip
IN_PROGRESS --> COMPLETED : complete_trip
REQUESTED --> CANCELED : cancel
DRIVER_ASSIGNED --> CANCELED : cancel

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象在任何时刻都必须保持成立的规则，例如状态只能按合法顺序转换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a rule that must always hold for an object, such as only allowing legal state transitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单例模式：整个程序里某个类只允许存在一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A singleton is a pattern that allows only one instance of a class to exist in the whole program.

q: 不同地区 LLD 面试格式的一个常见差异是？
q_en: What is one common regional difference in LLD interview format?
options: 所有地区都完全禁止使用伪代码
美国只问 UML，亚洲只问 CDN 架构
所有地区都要求提交可编译项目
美国偏真实语言代码，亚洲偏结构化伪代码
options_en: Every region completely forbids pseudocode.
US interviews only ask about UML, and Asian interviews only ask about CDN architecture.
Every region requires a fully compilable project submission.
US Big Tech leans toward real-language code, while some Asian interviews lean toward structured pseudocode.
why: 文章强调格式会变，但核心能力不变：类、关系、行为和解释。你应提前问清目标公司的期望。
why_en: Some interviews expect partial real-language code while others accept structured pseudocode, but the design skills are the same.
tradeoff: 真实语言部分代码 vs 结构化伪代码

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，用图表表示类、关系和继承结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a diagram notation for classes, relationships, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用接近自然语言的结构描述逻辑，不追求语法可编译。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pseudocode describes logic in near-natural-language structure without requiring compilable syntax.

scenario: 你在面试中发现面试官明确追问 Factory、Strategy 等模式名称。
scenario_en: During the interview, the interviewer explicitly asks about pattern names such as Factory and Strategy.
q: 更合适的应对是什么？
q_en: What is the better way to respond?
options: 完全拒绝讨论模式
在自然适用时点名模式，并解释它解决的变化点
强行在每个类上套模式
只背定义不讲设计
options_en: Flatly refuse to discuss any design patterns.
Name a pattern when it naturally applies, and explain the variation point it solves.
Force a pattern onto every single class.
Just recite pattern definitions without discussing the design.
why: 有些地区或公司更直接考模式。你不需要强塞，但要能识别合适场景并说明取舍。
why_en: When pattern vocabulary is expected, name the pattern only where it naturally solves a concrete variation point.
whenOtherWins: 在更偏美国大厂的面试里，模式名称通常不如设计理由重要，但自然点名也没问题。
tradeoff: 按需点名模式并解释变化点 vs 完全回避或强行套用模式

termDefinitions.meaning: 策略模式：把可互换的算法封装成独立类，运行时切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms as separate classes that can be swapped at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工厂模式：把对象创建逻辑集中封装，调用方不用关心具体子类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern centralizes object creation so callers don't need to know the concrete subclass.

scenario: 题目只给一句“设计咖啡机”，没有说明饮品类型、支付、补料、错误处理或 UI 范围。
scenario_en: The prompt only says "design a coffee machine" and does not specify drinks, payment, refills, errors, or UI scope.
q: 你应该先做什么？
q_en: What should you do first?
options: 直接写完整代码
问少量澄清问题并确认范围
默认所有功能都要做
只讨论缓存
options_en: Immediately start writing complete code.
Ask a few clarifying questions and confirm scope.
Assume every possible feature is in scope.
Only discuss caching.
why: LLD prompt 常常故意模糊。先把核心能力、规则、错误和边界问清楚，才能避免设计跑偏。
why_en: Start ambiguous LLD prompts by asking focused clarifying questions and confirming scope before designing classes.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官已经给出完整需求并催促设计，就快速复述确认后进入实体和类设计。
tradeoff: 先澄清范围 vs 直接开始编码

q: LLD 面试常见评估维度有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which dimensions are commonly assessed in LLD interviews? (Select all that apply.)
options: 问题分析
类设计
代码质量
可扩展性和沟通
options_en: Problem analysis
Class design
Code quality
Extensibility and communication
why: 不同公司 rubric 细节不同，但通常都在看你是否能理解问题、拆类、写出可维护结构，并清楚说明取舍。
why_en: LLD interviews commonly assess problem analysis, class design, code quality, extensibility, and communication.

q: 问题分析阶段强候选人的表现是什么？
q_en: What does a strong candidate do during problem analysis?
options: 把所有可能未来功能都实现
不听题直接写代码
只背 SOLID 定义
提取关键实体和职责，问少量澄清问题，先框定范围
options_en: Try to implement every possible future feature.
Start writing code without listening to the requirements.
Just recite the SOLID definitions.
Extract key entities and responsibilities, ask a few clarifying questions, and scope the problem first.
why: 面试官不希望你在没理解需求时开写。好的开局是把题目变成可设计的清晰范围。
why_en: Strong problem analysis extracts entities and responsibilities, asks clarifying questions, and scopes the problem before coding.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open-Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: 五个面向对象设计原则的首字母缩写：单一职责、开闭、里氏替换、接口隔离、依赖倒置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is an acronym for five object-oriented design principles: single responsibility, open-closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, and dependency inversion.

q: 类设计阶段面试官主要看什么？
q_en: What does the interviewer mainly look for during class design?
options: 是否估算了机房带宽
是否画了最复杂的 UML 符号
是否使用最多设计模式
类的职责、状态所有权、方法签名和依赖方向是否清楚
options_en: Whether you estimated data-center bandwidth.
Whether you drew the most elaborate UML notation.
Whether you used the largest number of design patterns.
Whether class responsibilities, state ownership, method signatures, and dependency direction are clear.
why: 好的类设计会让后续实现自然流动。职责和边界不清会让代码质量、扩展和解释都变难。
why_en: Class design is judged by clear responsibilities, state ownership, APIs, and dependency direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，用图表表示类、关系和继承结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a diagram notation for classes, relationships, and inheritance.

q: LLD 面试里的代码质量不只是语法，它还包括什么？
q_en: Beyond syntax, what does code quality mean in an LLD interview?
options: 写了注释就算合格
能跑就行，不用管代码结构
封装、状态管理和关注点分离
只用运行时间复杂度打分
options_en: Having a comment is good enough.
As long as it runs, the structure doesn't matter.
Encapsulation, state management, and separation of concerns.
Only grade it by runtime complexity.
why: 即使用伪代码，面试官也在看你的代码是否像真实团队愿意维护的结构。
why_en: Code quality in LLD includes encapsulation, state management, separation of concerns, naming, and disciplined structure even in pseudocode.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装：把对象内部状态隐藏起来，只通过方法暴露受控的操作接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation hides an object's internal state and exposes only controlled operations through its methods.

scenario: 你完成了核心设计，面试官追问“如果要支持新车辆类型/新支付方式怎么办？”
scenario_en: After your core design, the interviewer asks how it would support a new vehicle type or payment method.
q: 这个追问主要在考什么？
q_en: What is this follow-up mainly testing?
options: 你是否背出所有 GoF 模式
你能否估算全球流量
设计能否扩展而不重写主体结构
你能否写前端样式
options_en: Whether you can recite every GoF pattern.
Whether you can estimate global traffic.
Whether the design can absorb new functionality without rewriting the core structure.
Whether you can write frontend styling.
why: 跟进需求通常测试边界是否干净。好设计能通过新增类或小范围修改吸收变化。
why_en: Follow-up requirements test whether your design can evolve cleanly without rewriting the core structure.
whenOtherWins: 如果初始需求很小，不要提前实现所有未来扩展；只要能解释如何扩展即可。
tradeoff: 干净边界支撑扩展 vs 大范围重写主体结构

termDefinitions.meaning: 指经典《设计模式》一书作者合称，书中列出 23 种经典模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GoF, or Gang of Four, refers to the authors of the classic Design Patterns book and its 23 catalog patterns.

q: 为什么沟通本身是 LLD 评分项？
q_en: Why is communication itself part of LLD scoring?
options: 面试官要跟上推理路径并能一起调整设计
沟通可以完全替代设计能力
说得越多就越不用写代码
LLD 面试本质是销售话术面试
options_en: The interviewer needs to follow your reasoning and adjust the design together when probing.
Communication can fully substitute for design ability.
The more you talk, the less code you need to write.
An LLD interview is essentially a sales pitch.
why: LLD 是协作式设计。清楚讲出范围、取舍和修改点，比沉默写完一坨代码更能展示工程判断。
why_en: Communication matters because the interviewer needs to follow your reasoning and see how you adapt under probing.

q: 把一场 LLD 面试从题目到实现的自然顺序排好：
q_en: Put an LLD interview flow in the natural order from prompt to implementation:
steps: 定义核心类、状态和方法
澄清需求并确认范围
提取实体和关系
实现关键方法并走查场景
why: 先把问题框清楚，再建模对象，最后写关键逻辑。跳过前两步直接写代码通常会丢分。
why_en: A good LLD flow clarifies scope, extracts entities, defines classes, and then implements and verifies core methods.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["clarify scope"] --> B["extract entities"]
B --> C["define classes, state, APIs"]
C --> D["implement key method"]
D --> E["walk through scenario"]

q: 补全文章里的类比：
q_en: Complete the analogy for system design versus low-level design:
text: 系统设计像{{地图}}，低层设计像地图上一栋建筑的{{蓝图}}。
text_en: System design is like a {{map}}, while low-level design is like the {{blueprint}} for one building on that map.
why: 类比强调两者尺度不同：系统设计关注宏观组件，LLD 关注具体代码结构和对象协作。
why_en: The analogy is that system design is the map and low-level design is the blueprint for one building on that map.

scenario: 你不确定目标公司要求伪代码、真实语言、UML 还是模式名称。
scenario_en: You are not sure whether the target company expects pseudocode, real-language code, UML, or pattern names.
q: 最务实的做法是什么？
q_en: What is the most practical move?
options: 等面试结束后再去问清楚
默认所有公司要求完全相同
只准备一种固定表达方式
面试前先问清期望格式
options_en: Wait until after the interview to ask.
Assume every company expects exactly the same format.
Prepare only a single fixed way of presenting.
Ask the recruiter ahead of time what format is expected.
why: 文章明确说差异存在但不应主导准备。提前问清格式能减少不必要的不确定性。
why_en: Ask the recruiter or interviewer what format they expect so you can adapt without changing the core preparation.
whenOtherWins: 如果无法提前问到，就准备能在伪代码和常用语言之间切换的表达方式。
tradeoff: 面试前主动确认格式 vs 面试中默认单一固定表达

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调面试流程、可以提前说明面试期望格式的人。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recruiter coordinates the interview process and can tell you the expected format ahead of time.

q: 文章对现代 LLD 取向的描述包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which statements match the guide's modern LLD approach? (Select all that apply.)
options: 组合通常比深继承更实用
简单状态优先于过度层级
务实取舍优先于模式崇拜
所有问题都必须先设计抽象工厂
options_en: Composition is usually more practical than deep inheritance.
Simple state is preferred over excessive hierarchy.
Pragmatic tradeoffs come before pattern worship.
Every problem must start with an Abstract Factory design.
why: 现代生产代码更看重可读、可维护和适度抽象。强行套模式通常是负信号。
why_en: The guide favors composition, simple state, and pragmatic tradeoffs over deep inheritance and pattern worship.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象工厂模式：提供一族相关对象的创建接口，不暴露具体实现类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Abstract Factory pattern provides an interface for creating families of related objects without exposing concrete classes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 子类自动获得父类的属性和方法的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance is the mechanism where a subclass automatically gets the properties and methods of a parent class.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过持有其他对象的引用来复用行为，而不是继承它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composition reuses behavior by holding a reference to another object instead of inheriting from it.

q: 只看材料但不练习，文章认为最大的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest risk of reading the material without practicing?
options: 真正面试时无法把概念应用到具体题目
会忘记所有网络协议
一定无法写任何语法
会把 LLD 变成系统设计
options_en: You won't be able to apply the concepts to an actual problem under real interview conditions.
You will forget every network protocol.
You definitely won't be able to write any syntax at all.
LLD will turn into system design.
why: LLD 是应用型面试。知道原则不等于能在 35 分钟内澄清需求、拆类、写方法和应对追问。
why_en: The main risk of only reading is failing to apply the ideas under interview time pressure.

scenario: 题目是“设计 Tic Tac Toe”，你开始讨论全球多人在线同步和匹配服务。
scenario_en: The prompt is "design Tic Tac Toe," but you start discussing global multiplayer synchronization and matchmaking services.
q: 这暴露了什么问题？
q_en: What problem does this reveal?
options: 缺少数据库索引
类设计过于简单
范围失控，把 LLD 题扩成系统设计
状态机一定不能用
options_en: The design lacks a database index.
The class design is too simplistic.
Scope has run away, turning an LLD prompt into a system design problem.
A state machine can never be used here.
why: LLD prompt 常常只要求本地核心逻辑。把 UI、网络、AI 对手等都拉进来会浪费时间并模糊主线。
why_en: Expanding a local game prompt into global online infrastructure is scope creep from LLD into system design.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求网络多人游戏后端，那才讨论服务和同步架构。
tradeoff: 本地核心逻辑 vs 全球多人同步基础设施

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用有限状态和转换规则描述对象行为的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state machine models an object's behavior using a finite set of states and transition rules.

scenario: 面试官希望看到你如何让一个小系统工作并能扩展。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants to see how you make a small system work and leave it extensible.
q: 最能打动面试官的产出通常是什么？
q_en: What output usually impresses the interviewer most?
options: 少量清楚的类 + 方法伪代码 + 场景走查
大量空接口和没用上的模式
只画一张服务拓扑图不落地
只列出名词，不写具体行为
options_en: A small set of clear classes, method pseudocode, and a scenario walkthrough.
A pile of empty interfaces and unused patterns.
Just one service-topology diagram with no implementation.
Just a list of nouns with no behavior.
why: LLD 不是名词收集。你要展示状态放在哪里、方法如何改变状态、边界如何保持清楚。
why_en: A strong LLD output is a small set of clear classes, core method pseudocode, and a walkthrough that proves the behavior.
whenOtherWins: 如果是非常早期需求澄清阶段，先列实体和范围再进入代码。
tradeoff: 少量类+方法走查证明行为 vs 只堆名词或服务拓扑图
diagram:
flowchart LR
A["clear classes"] --> B["core method pseudocode"]
B --> C["scenario walkthrough"]
C --> D["confident follow-up discussion"]
A --> D

q: 补全 LLD 评分主线：
q_en: Complete the main scoring thread for LLD interviews:
text: 面试官想看你能否把小而明确的问题拆成{{可维护的代码结构}}，并通过清晰沟通解释{{职责、状态和扩展点}}。
text_en: The interviewer wants to see whether you can turn a small, clear problem into a {{maintainable code structure}} and explain {{responsibilities, state, and extension points}} clearly.
why: 这比背出术语更重要。术语只是帮助表达，最终评分落在设计质量和推理过程。
why_en: The core evaluation is whether you can create maintainable code structure and explain responsibilities, state, and extension points.

q: 系统设计白板和 LLD 白板内容通常有什么不同？
q_en: How do system design and LLD whiteboards usually differ?
options: 系统设计画服务和数据流；LLD 画类和状态转换
系统设计只写代码，LLD 只写容量公式
系统设计和 LLD 都禁止画任何图
LLD 白板必须画完整 UML 图
options_en: System design draws services and data flow; LLD draws classes and state transitions.
System design only writes code, and LLD only writes capacity formulas.
Both system design and LLD forbid drawing any diagram.
An LLD whiteboard must contain a complete UML diagram.
why: LLD 可以画简单关系，但主要是为了支持代码结构讨论。系统设计图则表达分布式组件和数据流。
why_en: System design whiteboards show services and data flow, while LLD whiteboards show classes, methods, relationships, and state transitions.
tradeoff: 服务与数据流示意图 vs 类/方法/状态转换示意图

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，用图表表示类、关系和继承结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a diagram notation for classes, relationships, and inheritance.

scenario: 面试官在你设计后提出一个小扩展，例如添加新支付方式或撤销操作。
scenario_en: After your design, the interviewer adds a small extension, such as a new payment method or undo operation.
q: 回答时最好强调什么？
q_en: What should you emphasize in your answer?
options: 直接拒绝这个新需求
马上把所有代码推倒重写
指出现有边界如何吸收变化，需要改哪些类
只回一句“用设计模式”
options_en: Flatly refuse the new requirement.
Immediately rewrite all the code from scratch.
Point out which existing boundary absorbs the change and which classes need to change.
Just answer with "use a design pattern."
why: 扩展追问是在看初始设计是否有干净边界。具体说改哪里、为什么不会波及全局，比喊模式名更有说服力。
why_en: For follow-ups, explain which existing boundary absorbs the change and what minimal classes or methods need to change.
whenOtherWins: 如果扩展彻底改变需求，先承认原设计假设变化，再提出新的结构。
tradeoff: 指出边界吸收变化 vs 推倒重写或拒绝需求

q: 哪些是 LLD 面试中的常见负信号？（多选）
q_en: Which are common negative signals in an LLD interview? (Select all that apply.)
options: 没澄清需求就直接写代码
为了炫技强行加很多模式
把问题范围扩到不相关系统设计
用简洁类和方法解释状态变化
options_en: Writing code immediately without clarifying requirements.
Forcing in lots of patterns just to show off.
Expanding the scope into unrelated system design.
Explaining state changes with clean classes and methods.
why: 负信号都指向同一个问题：没有按题目需要做取舍。简洁清楚的类和方法反而是正信号。
why_en: Common negative signals are skipping requirements, forcing patterns, and expanding beyond the requested LLD scope.

q: 把这份指南建议的学习路径排好：
q_en: Put the guide's suggested study path in order:
steps: 用常见题目拆解和练习把方法应用出来
先学习交付框架管理面试时间
复习设计原则、OOP 概念和常见模式
根据目标公司确认格式差异
why: 先掌握流程，再补充工具箱，最后通过题目练习形成肌肉记忆。公司差异是准备中的校准项。
why_en: The preparation path is delivery framework, design fundamentals, practiced problem breakdowns, and then company-specific format calibration.

q: LLD 面试和纯算法面试的关注点有什么不同？
q_en: How does an LLD interview differ from a pure algorithm interview?
options: LLD 看对象结构和状态；算法看计算步骤和复杂度
LLD 面试只看 Big-O 一个指标
算法面试只看你画没画类图
两者面试都不需要解释思路
options_en: LLD looks at object structure and state; algorithm interviews look at computational steps and complexity.
An LLD interview only looks at Big-O.
An algorithm interview only checks whether you drew a class diagram.
Neither interview requires explaining your reasoning.
why: LLD 当然也要写正确逻辑，但评分重点是代码组织和变化承受能力。算法题则主要围绕数据结构、复杂度和正确性证明。
why_en: LLD emphasizes object structure, state, and maintainable interactions, while algorithm interviews emphasize computational steps and complexity.
tradeoff: 对象结构与可维护交互 vs 计算步骤与复杂度证明

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来描述算法运行时间或空间随输入规模增长趋势的记号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Big-O notation describes how an algorithm's runtime or space grows as the input size increases.

q: OOP 概念页与设计原则页的关系是什么？
q_en: How do the OOP concepts page and the design principles page relate to each other?
options: 两者是互不相关的两套独立知识
OOP 概念只在系统设计面试里出现，LLD 不会考
设计原则决定取舍方向，OOP 概念是实现这些取舍的语言机制
设计原则的内容只适用于前端框架代码
options_en: The two pages are unrelated, independent topics.
OOP concepts only appear in system-design interviews, not LLD.
Design principles decide the direction of a tradeoff, and OOP concepts are the language mechanisms that implement it.
Design principles only apply to frontend framework code.
why: 设计原则回答“该怎么取舍”，封装、抽象、多态、继承回答“怎么把取舍写进类和接口里”。两者是同一决策链的上下游。
why_en: Design principles decide what tradeoff to make, and OOP concepts are the language mechanisms that turn that tradeoff into classes and interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象编程（OOP）：用类和对象组织代码、通过封装/抽象/多态/继承表达设计决策的编程范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming, a paradigm that organizes code into classes and objects using encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层次设计（LLD）：面试中要求把需求落到具体类、接口和方法的设计环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD stands for Low-Level Design, the interview stage that asks you to turn requirements into concrete classes, interfaces, and methods.

q: 补全四个核心 OOP 概念：
q_en: Fill in the four core OOP concepts:
text: LLD 面试中最重要的四个 OOP 概念是：{{封装}}、{{抽象}}、{{多态}}、{{继承}}。
why: 不需要死背术语，但要能在类设计里自然应用它们。
why_en: The four core OOP concepts are encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象编程（OOP）：用类和对象组织代码、通过封装/抽象/多态/继承表达设计决策的编程范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming, a paradigm that organizes code into classes and objects using encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

q: 封装的核心含义是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea of encapsulation?
options: 隐藏对象内部数据，通过方法控制访问和修改
把所有字段都设为 public，方便外部直接读写
让每个类都必须继承一个公共父类
只写静态函数，不定义任何实例方法
options_en: Hide an object's internal data and control access and changes through methods.
Make every field public so external code can read and write it directly.
Force every class to inherit from a common parent class.
Write only static functions and define no instance methods.
why: 封装让对象自己维护规则，例如余额不能为负、停车位不能被外部随意改。调用方通过行为而不是直接改字段来交互。
why_en: Encapsulation hides internal data and exposes controlled behavior so the object itself can enforce its own rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

scenario: ParkingLot 暴露 public spots: list[ParkingSpot]，任何调用方都能直接增删停车位。
scenario_en: ParkingLot exposes a public spots: list[ParkingSpot] field, so any caller can add or remove parking spots directly.
q: 主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem here?
options: 列表本身不能用来存对象，得换成字典
外部代码可以绕过 ParkingLot 的规则，直接增删内部车位列表
每个 ParkingSpot 都必须实现成 Singleton 才安全
问题在于 Python 语言本身不支持 private 约定
options_en: Lists simply cannot hold objects, so it must become a dict.
External code can bypass ParkingLot's rules and mutate the internal spot list directly.
Every ParkingSpot must be implemented as a Singleton to be safe.
The real problem is that Python has no private-field convention.
why: 公开可变集合会让调用方绕过 park_vehicle 等受控方法直接改内部状态，破坏不变量。应提供受控方法并返回副本或只读视图。
why_en: Exposing a mutable internal collection lets callers bypass ParkingLot's rules and mutate its internal state directly, breaking its invariants.
whenOtherWins: 只读 DTO 或测试夹具可以直接暴露简单字段，但核心领域对象应保护可变状态。
tradeoff: 私有集合 + 受控方法 vs 公开可变集合：前者安全但多一层方法调用，后者简单但任何人都能破坏不变量。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的停车场领域对象，管理车位集合与停车逻辑。

q: 抽象的核心含义是什么？

Expose all internal fields to every caller.
Rewrite every class to be a shared parent class.

Using inheritance automatically improves maintainability.

options: 允许任何调用方直接写 balance 字段
把字段设为私有或受保护
通过 deposit/withdraw 等方法修改状态
返回内部可变集合的副本或只读视图
options_en: Allow any caller to write the balance field directly.
Make fields private or protected.
Change state only through methods like deposit/withdraw.
Return a copy or read-only view of an internal mutable collection.
why: 封装的目标是让对象守住自己的规则。直接写 balance 会绕过校验和关联逻辑，破坏不变量。
why_en: Encapsulation uses private state, controlled methods, and safe views of collections rather than direct external mutation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

termDefinitions.meaning: balance：本例中账户对象持有的余额字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Balance is the account object's stored balance field in this example.

q: 哪些信号说明可能需要抽象？（多选）
q_en: Which signals suggest you might need an abstraction? (multi-select)
options: 同一能力存在多个不同的实现
这块逻辑只有一个字段、并且以后也不会变化
某块逻辑里藏着很多变化的规则
调用方本不应该知道外部 API 的实现细节
options_en: The same capability has multiple different implementations.
This logic has only one field and it will never change.
A piece of logic hides a lot of varying rules.
Callers shouldn't need to know the implementation details of an external API.
why: 抽象适合隐藏复杂性和变化点。没有变化也不复杂的地方，抽象往往只是额外成本。
why_en: Abstraction helps when there are multiple implementations, complex variation, or details callers should not know about.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: API：应用程序编程接口，供调用方使用的一组预定义方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: API stands for Application Programming Interface, a predefined set of methods a caller can use.

scenario: 你看到 checkout 里根据 payment_type 字符串 switch 到不同支付逻辑。
scenario_en: You see checkout switch on a payment_type string to branch into different payment logic.
q: 这通常提示你使用什么概念？
q_en: What concept does this usually signal you should use?
options: 继承一个巨大的 PaymentProcessor 基类
把每种支付方式的字段都公开出来
定义 PaymentMethod 接口，让多态处理每种支付方式
在 checkout 里继续往 switch 加更多分支
options_en: Inherit from one giant PaymentProcessor base class.
Expose every payment method's fields publicly.
Define a PaymentMethod interface and let polymorphism handle each payment type.
Keep adding more branches to the switch inside checkout.
why: 支付方式是行为变化点。接口让每种支付自己实现 process，checkout 只调用统一方法。
why_en: A payment-type switch is a cue to use polymorphism through a shared PaymentMethod interface.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有一种支付方式且没有扩展信号，先保持简单实现也可以。
tradeoff: PaymentMethod 多态 vs switch 分支：接口让新增支付方式不用改 checkout，但多定义一层接口；switch 写起来快，但每加一种支付都要回来改这段代码。

termDefinitions.meaning: PaymentMethod：本例中定义“处理支付”这一能力的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PaymentMethod is the interface in this example that defines the capability to process a payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中一个试图把所有支付方式塞进同一个继承体系的巨大基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PaymentProcessor here is a giant base class that tries to cram every payment method into one inheritance hierarchy.

q: 用继承表达行为差异时，常见后果是什么？
q_en: What commonly happens when you use inheritance to express behavior differences?
options: 所有的变化都会自动变得更容易处理
子类会大量覆写父类方法，父类的契约变得脆弱
用继承之后就再也不需要接口了
只要用了继承，所有方法就自动是正确的
options_en: Every future change automatically becomes easier to make.
Subclasses end up overriding many parent methods, and the parent's contract becomes fragile.
Once you use inheritance, you never need interfaces again.
Using inheritance automatically makes every method correct.
why: 当子类只是为了不同实现而覆写父类方法，说明共享父类可能不是合适的抽象。组合可变行为通常更稳。
why_en: Using inheritance to express behavior variation often leads to many overrides and a fragile base-class contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

why: 先识别行为随类型变化，再把变化移进类型本身，最后调用方依赖统一契约。
why_en: Refactor type checks by identifying type-varying behavior, defining a contract, implementing it per type, and calling the contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

q: 把从错误继承到组合动力系统的步骤排好：
q_en: Put the steps of refactoring from broken inheritance to composed drivetrains in the correct order:
steps: Car 组合一个 Drivetrain 并委托 start
发现 ElectricCar 不共享 gasoline engine 行为
定义 Drivetrain.start 抽象
实现 GasEngine 和 ElectricMotor
why: 先承认继承关系不稳定，再把可变行为抽出来组合。这样新增动力类型不会破坏 Car。
why_en: Move unstable behavior out of inheritance by defining a Drivetrain abstraction, implementing variants, and composing it into Car.

scenario: 接口只有 doWork(request)，所有实现都要解析 request 内部并猜调用方意图。
scenario_en: An interface has only doWork(request), so every implementation must parse the request internals and guess the caller's intent.
q: 这可能是什么问题？
q_en: What is the likely problem here?
options: 问题在于封装做得太强、外部什么都看不到
问题在于这里定义的继承层次太少、太浅了
问题在于这种写法下多态根本不可能发生
接口太泛，doWork(request) 没表达出真实业务操作
options_en: The problem is encapsulation is too strong and nothing is visible from outside.
The problem is the inheritance hierarchy defined here is too shallow.
The problem is polymorphism simply can't happen with this shape.
The interface is too generic — doWork(request) never expresses the real business operation.
why: 接口名和参数应该表达调用方需要的业务能力。过泛接口会把复杂性转移给实现和读者。
why_en: An interface like doWork(request) is often too vague because it fails to express the real operation callers need.
whenOtherWins: 通用框架回调可能需要泛接口，但业务 LLD 中应优先清晰契约。
tradeoff: 泛接口 doWork(request) vs 具体方法名：泛接口看起来更通用，但每个实现都要重新解析意图；具体方法名（如 process(amount)）多写几个方法，但契约一看就懂。

termDefinitions.meaning: doWork(request)：一个只有动词、没有业务语义的过泛接口方法名示例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: doWork(request) is an example of an overly generic method signature that carries no real business meaning.

scenario_en: Account.balance is public, so any code can set it directly to a negative number.
q: 封装式修复是什么？
q_en: What is the encapsulation-based fix here?
options: balance 私有化，靠 deposit/withdraw 校验并修改
让所有调用方都能自觉记得不要把余额设置成负数就行
把 balance 这个字段名字换成别的名字就能解决问题
用继承的方式把 balance 字段隐藏起来避免暴露
options_en: Make balance private and change it only through deposit/withdraw, which validate the amount.
Rely on every caller to remember never to set a negative balance.
Just rename the balance field to something else and that solves it.
Use inheritance to hide the balance field away from view.
why: Account 拥有余额规则，就应在自己的方法里防止非法状态。依赖调用方自律不是可靠设计。
why_en: Make balance private and update it only through methods so Account itself can enforce valid balance rules.
whenOtherWins: 只读数据传输对象可以简单暴露字段，但有业务不变量的对象不应这样做。
tradeoff: 私有 balance + 方法校验 vs 公开字段：前者多写 deposit/withdraw 两个方法，但杜绝非法状态；后者零封装成本，但任何调用方都能把余额写成负数。

q: 封装和抽象的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between encapsulation and abstraction?
options: 封装规定只能用在接口上，抽象规定只能用在字段上
封装保护对象内部状态；抽象隐藏实现细节、暴露能力契约
封装和抽象说到底其实都等价于继承
封装和抽象都要求把状态改成全局变量
options_en: Encapsulation only applies to interfaces, and abstraction only applies to fields.
Encapsulation protects an object's internal state; abstraction hides implementation details and exposes a capability contract.
Encapsulation and abstraction are really just the same thing as inheritance.
Both encapsulation and abstraction require turning state into global variables.
why: 封装更关注对象边界和状态不变量，抽象更关注调用方依赖什么能力而不是具体实现。二者常一起出现但不是同一件事。
why_en: Encapsulation protects internal state, while abstraction exposes a capability contract and hides implementation details.
tradeoff: 封装 vs 抽象：封装管的是“谁能碰我的状态”，抽象管的是“调用方需要知道多少实现细节”——一个是边界问题，一个是契约问题。

q: 最自然的 OOP 组合是什么？
q_en: What is the most natural OOP combination here?
options: 写一个巨大的 if/else 处理所有支付方式
让所有支付方式的类都去继承 OrderService
把支付方式直接放进一个 public 字符串字段里
定义 PaymentMethod 抽象，让每种支付方式多态实现
options_en: Write one giant if/else that handles every payment method.
Have every payment-method class inherit from OrderService.
Put the payment method directly into a public string field.
Define a PaymentMethod abstraction and let each payment method implement it polymorphically.
why: 抽象定义 process(amount) 契约，多态让每个支付方式自己处理细节。这样 checkout 不需要知道具体类型。
why_en: A PaymentMethod abstraction with polymorphic implementations lets checkout depend on one contract instead of concrete payment types.
whenOtherWins: 如果当前只有一种支付方式且没有扩展信号，简单具体实现可能更符合 KISS。
tradeoff: PaymentMethod 抽象+多态 vs 巨大 if/else：前者新增支付方式只需加一个实现类；后者短期少写一个接口，但每加一种支付都要回来改同一段分支代码。

q_en: Which signals suggest inheritance might be a reasonable choice? (multi-select)
options: 子类确实是父类的稳定特例
多个子类共享相同且稳定的实现
子类不会破坏父类承诺
子类主要通过抛异常来拒绝父类方法
options_en: The subclass is genuinely a stable special case of the parent.
Multiple subclasses share the same, stable implementation.
The subclass never breaks the parent's promised contract.
The subclass mainly rejects inherited methods by throwing exceptions.
why: 继承需要稳定 is-a 和共享实现。靠抛异常拒绝父类方法通常说明违反了 LSP。
why_en: Inheritance is reasonable when subtypes are stable specializations, share real implementation, and preserve the base contract.
tradeoff: 合理继承 vs LSP 违反信号：真正稳定的 is-a + 共享实现值得继承；子类靠抛异常拒绝父类方法，说明它其实不是父类的合法替代品。

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP：里氏替换原则，子类必须能替换父类使用而不破坏程序正确性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP is the Liskov Substitution Principle: a subclass must be usable wherever its parent class is expected, without breaking correctness.

why_en: When variation is mainly behavior, prefer interface-based composition and reserve inheritance for stable shared implementation.

q: 设计模式在 LLD 面试中最健康的定位是什么？
q_en: What is the healthiest way to think about design patterns in an LLD interview?
options: 只用于系统设计容量估算
可复用结构的名字，在问题自然需要时使用
替代需求分析的捷径
每道题都必须强行套用的模板
options_en: They are only used for system-design capacity estimates.
They are names for reusable structures, used only when the problem naturally calls for them.
They are a shortcut that replaces requirement analysis.
They are a template you must force into every problem.
why: 模式是好设计自然形成的结构和沟通词汇，不是设计的起点。强行套用通常是过度设计的信号。

q: 哪个模式可能有帮助？

options: Observer
Builder
Facade
Singleton
options_en: Observer
Builder
Facade
Singleton
why: Builder 让复杂对象一步步配置，并在 build 时校验必填字段，适合可选字段多、构造细节杂的对象。
why_en: Builder fits complex object construction with many optional fields and validation at build time.
whenOtherWins: Python 中很多时候用 dataclass 默认值、关键字参数或字典更简单，不需要专门的 Builder。
tradeoff: 分步构造+build 时校验 vs 单个长参数构造函数的简单性

    .url("https://api.example.com")
    .method("POST")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .build())
# build() 校验 url 是必填项，缺失就抛 ValueError

q: 这时更稳妥的默认回答方向是什么？
q_en: What is the safer default answer in this situation?
options: Python 不能共享对象，所以无所谓
所有共享对象都必须做成 Singleton
谨慎；通常通过构造函数传共享对象更清楚、更好测试
Singleton 能自动解决所有并发问题
options_en: Python cannot share objects, so it does not matter.
Every shared object must be turned into a Singleton.
Be cautious; passing the shared object through the constructor is usually clearer and easier to test.
Singleton automatically solves all concurrency problems.
why: Singleton 隐藏依赖并增加测试难度；除非确实需要全局唯一实例，否则显式构造函数注入更可维护。
why_en: Be cautious with Singleton because explicit constructor injection is usually clearer and easier to test than a hidden global instance.
whenOtherWins: 配置、日志或连接池确实要求进程内唯一实例时，可以讨论 Singleton 或模块级实例。

options_en: Global string concatenation.
Inherit from every service class that needs it.
Call `new` on a class-based Singleton every time it is used.
A module-level object, because a module is only loaded once.
why: Python 模块本身具有单例式加载语义；类式 Singleton 在 Python 里多数时候不符合语言习惯。

tradeoff: 模块级对象的零样板 vs 类式 Singleton 的显式 __new__ 控制

whenOtherWins: 如果使用依赖注入容器或注册表，映射可能在配置中完成而不是硬编码 factory。
tradeoff: 改一处 factory 映射 vs 改遍每个调用点的 new

q: Subject 最不应该做什么？
q_en: What is the one thing the Subject should avoid doing?
options: 支持 attach/detach
知道每个 observer 的具体业务细节并逐一硬编码
维护 observers 列表
调用 observer.update
options_en: Supporting attach/detach.
Knowing each observer's specific business logic and hard-coding calls to each one.
Maintaining a list of observers.
Calling observer.update.
why: Observer 的价值在于 subject 只知道统一接口，不知道订阅者如何处理事件；硬编码会重新耦合。
why_en: The subject should notify observers through a common interface rather than hard-coding each observer's business logic.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有一个固定后续步骤且必须同步成功，直接调用可能更清楚。
tradeoff: 统一接口通知、subject 不知情 vs 硬编码调用带来的紧耦合

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Observer lets multiple subscribers receive notifications through one common interface whenever a subject's state changes.

q: 创建型模式速记中，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: In this creational-pattern cheat sheet, which statements are correct? (select all)
options: Factory：调用方不该关心具体类创建
Observer：逐步构造复杂对象
Builder：对象有很多可选字段或构造细节
Singleton：确实需要全局唯一实例时才考虑
options_en: Factory: callers should not care which concrete class gets created.
Observer: assembling a complex object step by step.
Builder: the object has many optional fields or messy construction details.
Singleton: consider it only when you truly need one global instance.
why: Observer 是行为型事件通知模式，不是创建型构造模式，不属于这张速记。
why_en: Factory, Builder, and Singleton are creational patterns for object creation decisions, complex construction, and rare global uniqueness, unlike Observer.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Singleton guarantees a class has only one instance within the process and exposes a global access point to it.

q: 结构型模式速记中，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: In this structural-pattern cheat sheet, which statements are correct? (select all)
options: Decorator：运行时叠加可选行为
Strategy：替换算法行为
Facade：隐藏复杂子系统，提供简单入口
Factory：通知订阅者
options_en: Decorator: layers optional behavior on at runtime.
Strategy: swaps out algorithm behavior.
Facade: hides a complex subsystem behind a simple entry point.
Factory: notifies subscribers.
why: Strategy 是行为型模式，Factory 是创建型模式；Decorator 和 Facade 才是这里的结构型例子。
why_en: Decorator layers optional behavior and Facade provides a simple entry point over internal complexity, while Strategy and Factory belong to other categories.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构型模式：用包装对象在不修改原类的前提下叠加行为，可按运行时条件组合多层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Decorator wraps an object to add behavior at runtime without modifying the original class, and multiple decorators can be stacked.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms for the same operation as swappable objects chosen at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构型模式：用一个简单入口协调并隐藏一组复杂子系统的内部细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Facade offers one simple entry point that coordinates and hides the internal details of a more complex subsystem.

q: 行为型模式速记中，哪些说法正确？（多选）

options: Builder：事件通知多个订阅者
Strategy：替换 if/else 为可互换行为
Observer：多个组件响应单个事件
State Machine：行为随当前状态和转移规则变化
options_en: Builder: notifies multiple subscribers of an event.
Strategy: replaces if/else chains with interchangeable behavior.
Observer: multiple components react to a single event.
State Machine: behavior changes with the current state and transition rules.
why: Builder 是创建型模式，不属于行为型速记；Strategy、Observer、State Machine 都处理对象间的行为流。
why_en: Strategy, Observer, and State Machine are behavioral patterns for interchangeable behavior, event notification, and state-dependent behavior, unlike the creational Builder.

scenario_en: An order has states CREATED, PAID, SHIPPED, DELIVERED, CANCELLED, and whether an action is legal depends on the current state.
q: 你面试里应优先画什么辅助说明？
q_en: What visual aid should you prioritize drawing in the interview?
options: 状态图：状态是节点，动作是箭头
CDN 边缘节点的拓扑连接图
一张详细的数据库容量估算表格
订单类的继承树深度示意图
options_en: A state diagram: states as nodes, actions as arrows.
A topology diagram of CDN edge nodes.
A detailed database capacity estimation table.
An inheritance-depth diagram of the order class.
why: 状态图能让面试官快速验证转移是否完整，非法路径是否被拒绝。
why_en: A state diagram is the clearest way to show legal order transitions and invalid paths.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态很少且规则简单，文字列出 enum 和转换条件也足够。
tradeoff: 状态图的可视化验证 vs 文字列出 enum+条件的省时

q: 一个 LLD 方案同时强行加入三个以上模式，常见信号是什么？
q_en: If an LLD solution forces in three or more patterns at once, what is that usually a sign of?
options: 说明需求已经完全实现
一定比简单方案更可读
一定是更高级的设计
可能过度工程化，没有从问题本身出发
options_en: It means the requirements are fully implemented.
It is definitely more readable than a simple solution.
It is definitely a more advanced design.
It may be overengineering, not driven by the problem itself.
why: 多数面试设计不用模式或最多一两个；模式数量多通常意味着候选人在展示知识而不是解决问题。
why_en: Using many patterns at once is often a sign of overengineering rather than problem-driven design.

q_en: Which pattern is the most natural fit?

Facade only
Strategy
Singleton

Facade only

q_en: Which pattern avoids writing a subclass for every combination?
options: Decorator
Builder
Singleton

Singleton

把内部所有对象字段都设成 public
CheckoutService 作为 Facade 统一入口
调用方自己依次调用 cart/payment/inventory
options_en: Have the checkout method always return None.
Make every internal object field public.
Use CheckoutService as a single Facade entry point.
Let the caller call cart, payment, and inventory itself, one by one.

why: 先识别非法动作，再按投币、选择、出货、回到初始状态的路径讲清楚。

text: 先解决问题，再命名模式；如果一个模式没有减少真实{{复杂度}}、{{重复}}或{{耦合}}，就不要强行加入。
