ACID 事务模型里根本不存在一致性这个约束项
含义不同：CAP 的 C 指读到同一份最新数据，ACID 的 C 指事务不破坏约束
options_en: They mean exactly the same thing and can be used interchangeably in any context.
CAP's consistency is just another name for database transaction isolation level.
The ACID transaction model has no consistency guarantee at all.
They differ: CAP's C means nodes read the same latest value, while ACID's C means a transaction never violates database constraints.
why: 同名不同义：CAP 的 C 是「跨节点看到同一最新值」，ACID 的 C 是「事务前后满足完整性约束」。面试里别混为一谈。
why_en: CAP consistency is about all nodes seeing the same latest data, which differs from ACID consistency about preserving database invariants.
optionExplanations: 两者是不同的概念。
CAP C 和隔离级别是不同的。
ACID 当然有一致性。
正确，这是关键的区分点。
optionExplanations_en: They are different concepts with different meanings.
CAP C and isolation levels are different things.
ACID definitely includes consistency.
Correct, this is the critical distinction between them.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统在一致性、可用性、分区容错三者中最多同时满足两个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系数据库事务的四个经典保证：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID is the classic set of database transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

q: 一致性哈希要解决的核心问题是什么？
options: 让哈希函数的输出更难被反推或碰撞，提升系统的加密安全性
把敏感业务数据做端到端加密，防止被中间人窃取
把数据分布到一组服务器上，并在节点增减时把重新分布的数据量降到最小
优化单机数据库的索引结构，让单节点查询延迟更低
why: 一致性哈希是分布式系统的基础算法：解决「数据放哪台服务器」的问题，且在节点数量变化时只移动一小部分数据。
why_en: Consistent hashing distributes data across a cluster while minimizing how much data must move when servers are added or removed.
options_en: Make the hash function's output harder to reverse or collide, improving cryptographic security.
Encrypt sensitive business data end to end so it cannot be intercepted.
Spread data across a set of servers while minimizing how much data must move when nodes join or leave.
Optimize a single database's index structure for lower query latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任意长度输入映射成固定长度数值的函数，常用来快速定位数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash function maps input of any length to a fixed-size number, used to quickly locate data.

q_en: What core problem does consistent hashing solve?

q: 单库扛不住负载时，把数据分布到多个数据库实例的过程叫什么？
options: 复制（replication）
分片（sharding）
归档（archiving）
缓存（caching）
why: 分片是把数据水平拆分到多个实例；随之而来的第一个问题就是「哪条数据存到哪个实例」——这正是哈希分配策略要回答的。
why_en: Sharding means distributing data across multiple database instances, which raises the question of which data lives on which instance.
options_en: Replication
Sharding
Archiving
Caching
q_en: When one database cannot handle the load, what is the process of spreading data across multiple database instances called?

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一份数据保留多份拷贝，用来提高可用性或读吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication keeps multiple copies of the same data to improve availability or read throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据水平拆到多个实例上，让容量和吞吐能横向扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across instances so capacity and throughput can scale out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把常读数据放到更快的存储层，减少后端数据库压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Caching keeps frequently read data in a faster layer to reduce pressure on the backing database.

q: 补全最朴素的取模分片流程：
text: 取模分片：先对 event ID 做{{哈希}}得到一个数字，再对{{数据库数量}}取模（%），结果就是目标实例编号：database_id = hash(event_id) % N。
why: 取模哈希实现最简单、分布也均匀，但它把「节点数量」写死进了映射关系——这就是后面所有问题的根源。
why_en: Modulo sharding hashes the key and takes it modulo the number of databases, which bakes the cluster size into the mapping.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["key"] --> B["hash key"]
  B --> C["mod N"]
  C --> D["DB index"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 取余数运算，hash(key) % N 的结果是 0 到 N-1 之间的余数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo returns the remainder of division, so hash(key) % N yields a value between 0 and N minus 1.

q_en: Fill in the basic modulo-sharding flow:
text_en: Modulo sharding: first {{hash}} the event ID into a number, then take modulo by the {{database count}}; the result is the target instance: database_id = hash(event_id) % N.

q: 取模分片下从 3 台库扩到 4 台（% 3 改成 % 4），会发生什么？
options: 只有新库需要接收数据，其余三台库的现有路由保持原样不变
几乎每个 key 的目标库都变了——绝大部分数据要跨库搬迁，所有实例负载暴涨
什么都不用动，取模结果的变化会被数据库自动兼容处理
只有四分之一的新增数据会被分配到新库，旧数据原地不动
why: 模数一变，几乎所有 key 的哈希结果落点都变了：不只是新实例，而是全部实例之间的大规模数据搬迁，数据库活动全面飙升。
why_en: Changing the modulus remaps almost every key, forcing massive data movement across all instances, not just the new one.
options_en: Only the new instance needs to receive data; the other three keep their existing routing unchanged.
Almost every key's target database changes — most data must move across instances and load spikes everywhere.
Nothing needs to change; the database automatically adapts to the new modulo result.
Only about a quarter of the data moves, and it is all newly written data.
q_en: Under modulo sharding, what happens when you scale from 3 databases to 4?

q: 举例：事件 #1234 原来 hash(1234) % 3 = 1 存在 DB1；扩容后 hash(1234) % 4 = 0，说明什么？
options: 这条数据必须从 DB1 搬到 DB0——而且这不是个例，是普遍现象
数据会短暂同时存在两个库，直到后台同步任务清理旧副本
这条数据在搬迁过程中丢了，需要从备份手工恢复
只有本次新写入的数据受影响，历史数据的库位置不变
why: 同一个 key 在新模数下落到了不同实例，旧位置的数据必须搬走；取模分片下绝大多数 key 都是这样。
why_en: Under the new modulus the same key maps to a different database, so its data must move, and most keys share this fate.
options_en: This record must move from DB1 to DB0 — and this is not an isolated case, it's the norm.
The record briefly exists in both databases until a background job cleans up the old copy.
The record was lost during the move and must be restored from backup by hand.
Only newly written data is affected; existing records keep their old database location.
q_en: What does this modulo example tell us about event #1234 after scale-out?

q: 取模分片下一台数据库宕机（硬件故障/软件 bug），把它移出池子后会怎样？
options: 剩余节点自动均分它的数据，其他数据不动
系统自动恢复，无需搬数据
只丢失宕机节点的数据
% 3 变成 % 2，和扩容一样触发几乎全量的重新分布
why: 缩容和扩容是同一个病：模数从 3 变 2，几乎所有 key 重新映射——故障时最脆弱的时刻反而要做最大规模的搬迁。
why_en: Removing a failed node changes the modulus and triggers the same near-total redistribution as adding one.
options_en: The remaining nodes automatically split its data evenly among themselves; nothing else moves.
The system recovers automatically without moving any data.
Only the data on the failed node is lost.
The modulus changes from 3 to 2, triggering the same near-total redistribution as scaling up.
q_en: Under modulo sharding, what happens when a failed database is removed from the pool?

q: 大规模数据重新分布对线上系统的直接伤害是？
options: 数据库负载出现巨大尖峰，用户要么访问不到数据、要么响应变慢
只是磁盘占用短暂翻倍，几分钟后自动回落到正常水平
没有实际影响，因为搬迁流量会被自动限速到后台低峰期
数据永久丢失，必须从最近一次全量备份整体恢复
why: 搬迁本身要吃大量 IO 和带宽：数据库活动飙升，正常请求被挤压，表现为不可用或高延迟。
why_en: Mass redistribution spikes database load so users see slow responses or cannot access data at all.
options_en: Database load spikes hard, so users either cannot reach data or see slow responses.
Disk usage briefly doubles and settles back down within minutes.
There is no real impact because the move is automatically throttled to off-peak hours.
Data is permanently lost and must be restored wholesale from the last full backup.
q_en: What direct harm does large-scale data redistribution cause in production?

q: 一致性哈希的关键洞见是什么？
options: 换用密码学强度更高的哈希函数，减少碰撞概率
把所有数据复制到集群里的每一个节点，读写都本地完成
把数据和服务器节点都安排在同一个环形哈希空间（hash ring）上
用二叉搜索树按 key 范围组织节点，走树形路径查找
why: 核心思想：数据和数据库都映射到同一个圆环上；key 的归属由「环上顺时针遇到的第一个节点」决定，而不是由节点总数决定。
why_en: The key insight is to place both data and servers on a circular hash ring so ownership no longer depends on the total node count.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["hash key"] --> B["point on ring"]
  B --> C["walk clockwise"]
  C --> D["first node owns key"]
options_en: Switch to a cryptographically stronger hash function to reduce collisions.
Replicate all data to every node in the cluster so reads and writes stay local.
Place both data and server nodes on the same circular hash space, the hash ring.
Organize nodes in a binary search tree keyed by range and walk the tree to look up a key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把哈希值空间首尾相接成一个环，数据和节点都映射到环上的位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash ring wraps the hash-value space into a circle onto which both data and nodes are mapped.

q_en: What is the key insight behind consistent hashing?

q: 补全一致性哈希的查找流程：
text: 先把 key 做哈希、定位到环上的一个点，然后沿{{顺时针}}方向走，遇到的第一个{{节点}}就是这个 key 的归属；节点增减时只有{{相邻区间}}的 key 需要移动。
why: 「环 + 顺时针找下一个节点」就是一致性哈希的全部核心；正因为归属只看相邻关系，节点变化的影响才是局部的。
why_en: Hash the key onto the ring and walk clockwise to the first node, so membership changes only affect the adjacent range of keys.
q_en: Fill in the lookup flow for consistent hashing:
text_en: Hash the key to a point on the ring, walk {{clockwise}}, and the first {{node}} you meet owns the key; when nodes change, only the {{adjacent range}} moves.

q: 实际系统中，哈希环的取值空间通常是？
why: 0-100 只是教学简化；生产环境常用 0 到 2^32-1（约 43 亿个刻度）的哈希空间，刻度足够密，几百个虚拟节点也很少互相重合，分布仍然均匀。
why_en: Production hash rings typically span zero to two-to-the-32nd-minus-one so even hundreds of virtual nodes rarely collide and stay evenly spread.
options_en: Zero to one hundred
Zero to two to the thirty-second power minus one
Zero to one thousand
Zero to two to the eighth power minus one

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希函数所有可能输出值组成的取值范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The hash space is the full range of possible output values a hash function can produce.

scenario: 你在实现一致性哈希的环结构，要决定哈希函数输出值的取值范围，这个范围决定了环上能装下多少个不重合的刻度。
q_en: In real systems, what value range is usually used for the hash ring?
scenario_en: You are implementing a consistent-hashing ring and must choose the hash-function output range, which controls how many distinct ring positions are available.

q: 环大小 100，4 台数据库在位置 0、25、50、75。某 key 哈希到位置 60，归谁？
options: 位置 50 的数据库
位置 75 的数据库
位置 0 的数据库
位置 25 的数据库
why: 从 60 出发顺时针走，遇到的第一个节点在 75——key 归位置 75 的数据库。注意是「向前找下一个」，不是「找最近的」。
why_en: Walking clockwise from sixty, the first node you meet is at seventy-five, so that database owns the key.
options_en: The database at position 50.
The database at position 75.
The database at position 0.
The database at position 25.
q_en: With ring size 100 and nodes at 0, 25, 50, and 75, who owns a key at position 60?

q: 同样的环（节点在 0、25、50、75），某 key 哈希到位置 80，归谁？
options: 位置 75 的数据库
位置 50 的数据库
没有归属，报错
位置 0 的数据库（顺时针回绕）
why: 80 之后顺时针没有更大的节点位置了，于是回绕（wrap around）到环的起点——位置 0 的节点接住它。环是首尾相接的。
why_en: Past the last node the walk wraps around the ring, so a key at eighty belongs to the node at position zero.
options_en: The database at position 75.
The database at position 50.
No owner; it errors out.
The database at position 0, via clockwise wrap-around.

termDefinitions.meaning: 沿环走到末尾后，逻辑上接回环的起点继续查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Wrap-around means that after reaching the end of the ring, the walk logically continues from the start.

q_en: On the same ring, who owns a key at position 80?

q: 环上节点在 0、25、50、75，现在在位置 90 加入 DB5。哪些数据需要移动？
options: 所有数据都要重新分布，四台旧库和新库之间发生大规模互相搬迁
只有位置 0-25 之间、原本归 DB1 的那部分数据会搬到新库
只有哈希到 75-90 区间的 key 会移动——原本归 DB1，现在归 DB5
位置 50-75 之间的数据会被重新分配，原持有者 DB3 完全清空
why: 新节点只「切走」它逆时针方向到上一个节点之间的区间（75-90）；这些 key 原本回绕给 DB1，现在就近归 DB5，其余数据原地不动。
why_en: Only keys hashing between seventy-five and ninety move, since they previously wrapped to the node at zero and now belong to the new node.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    K["75-90 区间的 key"] -->|before| DB1["DB1 位置 0"]
    K -->|after DB5 joins| DB5["DB5 位置 90"]
    O["其余所有 key"] --> S["原地不动"]
options_en: All data gets redistributed; the four old databases and the new one all shuffle data around.
Only the data between positions 0 and 25 moves.
Only keys hashing into the 75-to-90 range move — they used to belong to DB1 and now belong to DB5.
Data between positions 50 and 75 gets reassigned and DB3 is emptied out entirely.
q_en: A new DB5 joins at position 90. Which data needs to move?

q: 在位置 90 加入 DB5，移动的数据量大约是多少？
options: 全部数据的约 50%，因为新库要跟旧库对半分担负载
约 DB1 的 60%（25 个单位里的 15 个），即全部数据的约 15%
全部数据的约 90%，因为几乎所有 key 的顺时针归属都变了
不到 1%，只有极少数刚好哈希到 90 这个精确点的 key 会动
why: 只动 75-90 这 15 个单位：占 DB1 跨度（25 单位）的 60%、占整个环的约 15%——对比取模哈希的「几乎全量」，这就是一致性哈希的价值。
why_en: Only about sixty percent of one node's keys, roughly fifteen percent of all data, moves, versus nearly everything under modulo hashing.
scenario: 环大小 100，节点在 0、25、50、75；在位置 90 新增 DB5 后，原本 75-90 这段 key 从 DB1 改归 DB5，其余区间不受影响。
options_en: About 50% of all data, since the new node should split load evenly with the old one.
About 60% of DB1's data (15 of its 25-unit span), roughly 15% of all data.
About 90% of all data, since nearly every key's clockwise owner changes.
Less than 1%, since only keys hashing to exactly position 90 would move.
q_en: Roughly how much data moves when DB5 joins at position 90?
scenario_en: The ring size is 100 with nodes at 0, 25, 50, and 75. After DB5 joins at position 90, keys from 75 to 90 move from DB1 to DB5.

q: 环上节点在 0、25、50、75，位置 25 的 DB2 宕机后，它的数据去哪？
options: 全部顺时针滑给下一个节点——位置 50 的 DB3；其他数据原地不动
均分给所有剩余节点，DB1、DB3、DB4 各接手三分之一
回绕给位置 0 的 DB1，因为它是环上最后一个节点
永久丢失，必须人工逐条从最近备份里恢复
why: 节点消失后，原本落在它区间的 key 继续顺时针走，全部落到下一个节点 DB3；环上其他区间完全不受影响。
why_en: When a node fails its keys simply continue clockwise to the next node, and everything else stays put.
options_en: All of it slides clockwise to the next node, DB3 at position 50; everything else stays put.
It splits evenly among all remaining nodes — DB1, DB3, and DB4 each take a third.
It wraps around to DB1 at position 0, since that is the last node on the ring.
It is permanently lost and must be restored record by record from the latest backup.
q_en: If DB2 at position 25 fails, where does its data go?

q: 没有虚拟节点时，DB2 宕机、数据全给了顺时针邻居 DB3，带来什么新问题？
options: DB3 的数据会整体损坏，必须动用最近一次全量备份逐条恢复重建
环在拓扑结构上直接断裂，其余节点之间的顺时针查找关系全部失效
DB1 的负载会显著下降，因为它不用再承担任何一个 key 的服务
DB3 承担了双倍负载，而 DB1、DB4 闲着——失效负载全砸在一个邻居身上
why: 朴素一致性哈希的软肋：节点失效时它的全部负载只由顺时针的那一个邻居接盘，负载瞬间翻倍——这正是虚拟节点要解决的。
why_en: Without virtual nodes a failed node dumps its entire load onto its single clockwise neighbor, doubling that node's load.
options_en: DB3's data becomes corrupted and must be rebuilt record by record from the latest full backup.
The ring topologically breaks apart and clockwise lookups between the remaining nodes all fail.
DB1's load drops noticeably because it no longer serves any key at all.
DB3 now carries double the load while DB1 and DB4 sit idle — the failed node's load lands entirely on one neighbor.
q_en: Without virtual nodes, what new problem appears when DB2 fails and DB3 takes all its data?

q: 虚拟节点（virtual nodes）是怎么实现的？
options: 为每个节点单独采购多台物理备用整机，接口层做故障转移热备份
把节点名加不同后缀（vn1、vn2…）分别哈希，让一台物理机出现在环上多个位置
提前把整个哈希环硬编码切分成固定的一百个等份格子，每个节点认领若干格
用虚拟化技术把每台物理机替换成若干独立运行的虚拟机实例
why: 一台物理节点 = 环上多个点：哈希「DB1-vn1」「DB1-vn2」等得到多个位置，各节点的虚拟节点自然交错混排在环上。
why_en: Each server is hashed under several name variants so it appears at many ring positions, naturally interleaving with other servers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["DB1 vnode A"] --> B["DB2 vnode A"]
  B --> C["DB1 vnode B"]
  C --> D["DB3 vnode A"]
options_en: Buy several extra physical standby machines per node and fail over at the interface layer.
Hash the node's name under different suffixes (vn1, vn2, ...) so one physical machine lands at multiple ring positions.
Pre-partition the whole ring into a hardcoded one hundred equal slots and have each node claim a share.
Use virtualization to replace each physical machine with several independently running virtual machines.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给一台物理服务器在环上生成多个哈希位置的技术，用来让负载分布更均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node technique hashes a physical server under several name variants so it occupies multiple ring positions for more even load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把哈希值空间首尾相接成一个环，数据和节点都映射到环上的位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash ring wraps the hash-value space into a circle onto which both data and nodes are mapped.

q_en: How are virtual nodes implemented?

q: 有了虚拟节点后，DB2 宕机时会发生什么？
options: DB2 的虚拟节点分别由不同节点接手，失效负载被均摊给所有幸存节点
所有数据仍然只会滑给它唯一的顺时针邻居，负载翻倍不变
整个哈希环都需要停机重新构建，所有节点重新计算环上位置
必须先由运维人工手动把数据迁移到目标节点
why: DB2 的虚拟节点散布在环上各处，每一段的顺时针邻居都不同，所以失效负载被自然摊薄——不再压垮单个邻居。
why_en: Because a failed node's virtual positions are scattered, each segment falls to a different survivor and the load spreads evenly.
options_en: DB2's virtual-node ranges are picked up by different nodes each, so the failed load spreads evenly across all survivors.
All of it still slides to its single clockwise neighbor, doubling that node's load unchanged.
The whole hash ring must be rebuilt offline while every node recomputes its position.
An operator must first migrate the data to the target node by hand.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给一台物理服务器在环上生成多个哈希位置的技术，用来让负载分布更均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node technique hashes a physical server under several name variants so it occupies multiple ring positions for more even load.

q_en: With virtual nodes, what happens when DB2 fails?

q: 加新节点时，虚拟节点带来什么好处？
options: 新节点上线后完全不需要接收任何数据，等下次扩容再说
新节点可以先加入环但延迟接收流量，等运维手动开启

# node_positions 已排序；找第一个 >= pos 的位置

node = ring_nodes[idx % len(ring_nodes)]  # 越界回绕到环起点

q: Redis Cluster 把 key 空间固定切成 16384 个槽，而不是切成 100 个或几百万个，这个数量级选择背后的设计考虑是什么？
options: 槽太少会让每槽覆盖太多 key、切分不精细；槽太多会让心跳传播的槽位图变笨重——16384 是折中
这只是历史遗留的随意选择，和心跳带宽、负载切分粒度都没有关系
槽数必须和物理节点数量完全相等，16384 意味着当年设计支持这么多节点
槽数越多每次写入越快，16384 恰好是让哈希计算耗时最短的数字
why: 16384 = 14 位槽位图，正好能塞进心跳包的合理大小；再大会让每次 gossip 传播的位图变笨重，再小则每个槽扛的 key 太多、负载切分不够细——这是 Redis 给出的折中点。
why_en: Redis picked 16384 slots as the sweet spot: enough granularity to split load finely, while keeping the per-node slot bitmap small enough to gossip in every heartbeat without bloating it.
scenario: Redis Cluster 用 CRC16(key) mod 16384 决定槽位，每个节点通过 gossip 协议向其他节点广播自己认领的槽位图。
options_en: Too few slots means each slot covers too many keys and load-splitting is too coarse; too many slots makes the gossiped slot bitmap unwieldy — 16384 is the middle ground.
It's just an arbitrary legacy choice unrelated to heartbeat bandwidth or split granularity.
The slot count must exactly equal the physical node count; 16384 was the era's design ceiling for nodes.
More slots always means faster writes; 16384 happens to minimize hash computation time.

CLUSTER SLOTS
# 返回各节点认领的槽区间，如 0-5460 -> node A

q: 一致性哈希的适用范围，正确的说法是？
options: 任何把数据分布到一组服务器的场景都适用——数据库、缓存、消息队列、应用服务器
只能用在数据库分片这一种场景，缓存和消息队列都不适用
只能用在 CDN 边缘节点内容缓存这一件事情上
只适合纯内存系统，任何涉及磁盘持久化的系统都不适用
why: 环上放的「节点」不限于数据库：缓存节点、broker、应用服务器都可以——本质是通用的「key → 服务器」映射方案。
why_en: Consistent hashing applies to any scenario distributing data across a cluster, whether databases, caches, message brokers, or app servers.
options_en: It applies anywhere data needs to spread across a set of servers — databases, caches, message brokers, even app servers.
It only applies to database sharding; caches and message brokers don't apply.
It only applies to picking a CDN edge node for content caching.
It only suits pure in-memory systems; anything touching disk persistence doesn't apply.
q_en: What is the correct scope of consistent hashing?

scenario: CDN 有 K 个内容 URL、N 个边缘节点；节点会扩缩容或上下线，不希望每次节点数变化都让大量缓存重新归属。
scenario_en: A CDN has K content URLs and N edge nodes. Nodes join and leave, and we do not want each membership change to remap most cached content.
q: CDN 内容映射该用简单取模还是一致性哈希？
q_en: Should CDN content mapping use simple modulo hashing or consistent hashing?
options: 用一个中心数据库记录每个 URL 具体存在哪个边缘节点上
每次请求都随机挑一个边缘节点去存放内容
按固定顺序轮询分配给各个边缘节点存放
一致性哈希：内容 URL 哈希到环上，就近顺时针归属边缘节点
why: 假设哈希均匀：取模从 N 加到 N+1，约 K×N/(N+1) 个 URL 会换节点；100 个节点加 1 个，接近 99% 会重映射。一致性哈希只让新节点接管一段环，平均搬 K/(N+1)。
why_en: With modulo hashing, adding one node remaps about K times N over N plus one keys, while consistent hashing moves only about K over N plus one keys.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点集合很小、几乎不变，简单取模或静态映射表也够用；一致性哈希主要赢在节点经常变化时。
options_en: A central database records exactly which edge node holds each URL.
Randomly pick an edge node to store the content each time.
Assign content to edge nodes in a fixed round-robin order.
Consistent hashing: hash the content URL onto the ring and assign it to the nearest clockwise edge node.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["简单取模 hash(url) % N"] --> B["N 变 N+1"] B --> C["多数 URL 换节点
约 K×N/(N+1) 要搬"] D["一致性哈希环"] --> E["新节点插入一段区间"] E --> F["只搬相邻区间
约 K/(N+1) 要搬"]
tradeoff: 简单取模（实现最简单但节点变化时大搬家）vs 一致性哈希（实现复杂些但迁移量小）

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定顺序依次把请求分配给各节点，不看 key 内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round-robin assigns requests to nodes in a fixed rotating order, ignoring the key's content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 hash(key) % N 选择节点；N 一变，旧 key 的余数关系也大多会变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo hashing picks a node with hash(key) % N; when N changes, most old keys map somewhere else.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 和节点放到同一个环上，key 归顺时针遇到的第一个节点；节点变化只影响相邻区间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing places keys and nodes on one ring, assigning each key to the next clockwise node so membership changes affect only nearby ranges.

optionMeanings: 中心表记录 URL 到边缘节点的映射，控制强但要集中查表。
随机存放不保证同一 URL 回到同一边缘节点。
轮询按顺序分配，不看 URL，无法保持内容归属。
一致性哈希把 URL 放到环上，顺时针边缘节点负责缓存。
optionDirectness: 适合小规模、强一致目录比低延迟更重要时。
适合无状态临时任务，不适合缓存内容定位。
适合请求分摊，不适合需要命中同一内容的 CDN 缓存。
适合边缘节点经常上下线且想保住大多数缓存时。
optionScenarioImpacts: 本题会让目录库成为查询瓶颈和故障点。
本题会让同一 URL 到处 miss，缓存价值变低。
本题节点变化时归属混乱，命中率不稳。
本题只搬新节点相邻区间，避免大面积缓存失效。
optionMeanings_en: A central table explicitly records URL-to-edge ownership; it gives control but adds a central lookup.
Random placement does not guarantee that the same URL returns to the same edge node.
Round-robin rotates assignments and ignores URL identity, so content ownership is unstable.
Consistent hashing places URLs on the ring and assigns each to the clockwise edge node.
optionDirectness_en: Fits small systems where a strongly consistent directory matters more than latency.
Fits stateless temporary work, not locating cached content.
Fits request spreading, not CDN cache hits for the same content.
Fits edge nodes that join and leave while most cached objects should stay put.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Here the directory database can become a lookup bottleneck and failure point.
Here the same URL misses across many nodes, reducing cache value.
Here content ownership remains unstable when node count changes.
Here only the adjacent range moves, avoiding widespread cache invalidation.

q: Kleppmann（DDIA）对「一致性哈希」这个词的提醒是？
options: 这个词已经被业界正式弃用，学术界改用别的术语来称呼这套原则
只有严格按最初学术论文一字不差实现的版本才真正配称为一致性哈希算法
这个词用得很宽泛：有些系统实为固定槽分区而非教科书环——核心是最小化再均衡的数据移动
所有自称使用一致性哈希的系统都精确复刻了教科书式的环结构
why: 别较真术语：实现可以是环、也可以是固定槽变体，核心原则始终是「节点变化时尽量少搬数据」。
why_en: The term is used loosely in practice; what matters is the principle of minimizing data movement during rebalancing, not the textbook ring.
options_en: The term has been formally deprecated and academics use a different name for this principle now.
Only an implementation that matches the original academic paper verbatim truly deserves the name consistent hashing.
The term is used loosely in practice: some systems claiming consistent hashing are really fixed hash-slot partitioning — what matters is minimizing data movement during rebalancing.
Every system that claims to use consistent hashing precisely replicates the textbook ring structure.

q: 把「从取模分片演进到一致性哈希 + 虚拟节点」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 选型：一致性哈希——数据与节点放同一个环上，顺时针定位
缓解：虚拟节点把每个节点打散到环上多个位置，失效负载均摊
需求：数据分片到多台实例，且节点会因扩容/故障增减
残留代价：节点失效时其全部数据砸给唯一的顺时针邻居，负载翻倍
问题：取模哈希在节点数变化时几乎全量 key 重新映射
why: 需求（动态节点）→ 问题（取模全量重排）→ 选型（哈希环）→ 代价（邻居接盘过载）→ 缓解（虚拟节点）。这条链就是面试的标准叙事。
why_en: Dynamic membership breaks modulo hashing, the ring localizes movement, its neighbor-overload cost is then fixed by virtual nodes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求：节点会增减"] --> P["问题：取模几乎全量重排"]
    P --> C["选型：哈希环+顺时针"]
    C --> K["代价：失效负载砸给单个邻居"]
    K --> M["缓解：虚拟节点均摊"]
tradeoff: 取模哈希（简单但节点变化时全量搬迁）vs 一致性哈希+虚拟节点（局部搬迁+失效负载摊薄）

q: 把「热点问题的识别与缓解」推理链排成正确顺序：
steps: 缓解：把热 key 复制到多个节点，读请求负载均衡（最常用）
现象：个别 key（如霉霉演唱会）流量是其他 key 的 100 倍
后果：承载热 key 的那个节点被流量打爆，成为热点
进阶：key 加盐打散，或自适应再均衡自动搬迁
认识：一致性哈希均衡的是 key 分布，不是流量
why: 现象（超热 key）→ 认识（哈希只均衡 key 不均衡流量）→ 后果（单节点被打爆）→ 缓解（复制读副本）→ 进阶（加盐/自适应）。
why_en: A wildly popular key overwhelms one node because hashing balances keys not traffic, mitigated first by replication and then by salting or adaptive rebalancing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个节点因承载了流量远超其他节点的 key 而被过度请求压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot spot is a node overwhelmed by disproportionate traffic because it holds an especially popular key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持有同一份数据只读拷贝的节点，用来分摊读请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica holds a read-only copy of the data used to spread out read traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给热 key 追加随机后缀拆成多个物理 key，分散到不同节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key-space salting appends a random suffix to a hot key so it spreads across multiple physical keys and nodes.

q_en: Put the reasoning chain for identifying and mitigating hot spots in order:

scenario: 面试官追问：「你的分布式缓存节点挂了一台，怎么保证既不丢缓存价值又不搬大量数据？」
q: 最完整的回答思路是？
options: 把那台挂掉的节点直接重启，数据就能自动完整恢复
一致性哈希只影响该节点区间 + 虚拟节点把冲击摊薄 + 副本直接顶上，无需搬数据
把整个缓存集群的数据全部推倒重建一遍才能继续用
把全部流量临时切换到数据库，彻底绕开缓存层
why: 三层递进：环把影响局部化、虚拟节点把冲击摊薄、复制让故障处理零搬迁——这正是「一致性哈希与复制配合实现容错」的关系。
why_en: Combine the ring's localized impact, virtual nodes spreading the load, and replication so failures are absorbed without moving data.
whenOtherWins: 若数据可容忍全部重建（纯缓存、回源成本低），也可以接受简单方案：挂了就让相应 key 未命中、自然回填。
options_en: Just restart the failed node and its data recovers automatically and completely.
Consistent hashing limits impact to that node's range, virtual nodes spread the hit, and replicas take over directly with no data movement.
Tear down and rebuild the entire cache cluster's data before it can be used again.
Temporarily route all traffic to the database, bypassing the cache layer entirely.
tradeoff: 组合方案（环局部化+虚拟节点摊薄+副本零搬迁）vs 简单粗暴方案（全量重建或直接打库）

termDefinitions.meaning: 给一台物理服务器在环上生成多个哈希位置的技术，用来让负载分布更均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node technique hashes a physical server under several name variants so it occupies multiple ring positions for more even load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一份数据的多个拷贝，分布在不同节点上用于容错。

q_en: What is the most complete answer path?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: one distributed-cache node failed, so how do you preserve cache value without moving a large amount of data?
optionMeanings: 重启只能恢复进程，不保证丢失节点上的缓存数据还在。
组合答案：哈希环限范围、虚拟节点摊压力、副本接管服务。
全量重建是把所有缓存价值清空后重新预热。
直接打库绕开缓存，会把故障压力转移给数据库。
optionDirectness: 适合进程假死且本地数据未丢的临时故障。
适合缓存仍有副本、且要控制故障冲击面的场景。
适合缓存可丢且回源成本很低的小系统。
只适合短时间应急降级，且数据库有足够余量。
optionScenarioImpacts: 本题若机器真的不可用，重启不一定可行，也没有解释少搬数据。
本题能让存活副本立刻服务，并把失效负载摊给多个节点。
本题会制造大量 miss 和回源，恢复期延迟升高。
本题可能把数据库打穿，缓存层的保护作用消失。
optionMeanings_en: Restarting restores a process, but it does not guarantee cached data on the failed node still exists.
The combined answer limits the range with the ring, spreads pressure with virtual nodes, and serves from replicas.
Full rebuild throws away cache value and warms everything again.
Bypassing the cache shifts the failure pressure to the database.
optionDirectness_en: Fits a temporary process hang where local data is still intact.
Fits when cache data has replicas and the failure blast radius must stay bounded.
Fits small systems where cache loss is acceptable and origin reads are cheap.
Only fits short emergency degradation if the database has enough headroom.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Here a real machine failure may not restart, and it does not explain low data movement.
Here survivors serve immediately and failed load is spread across several nodes.
Here many misses hit the origin and recovery latency rises.
Here the database may be overloaded, removing the cache layer’s protection.

q: 系统设计面试对数据建模的期望是什么？

清晰、能用、贴合系统需求的 schema
背出所有范式的定义
跳过数据建模直接画架构
options_en: Do a full normalization pass and draw a complete ER diagram, like a dedicated data-modeling interview.
A clear, workable schema that fits the system's requirements.
Recite the definitions of every normal form from memory.
Skip data modeling entirely and jump straight to the architecture diagram.
optionMeanings: 像数据工程面试一样做完整范式化和 ER 图——用数据库设计的全套工程规范
设计一个清晰、能用、贴合系统需求的 schema——重点是实用而非形式完美
把数据库范式（1NF、2NF、3NF...）的定义背下来
完全跳过数据建模这一步
optionMeanings_en: Do full normalization and ER diagrams like in a data engineering interview.
Design a clear, functional schema aligned with the system requirements — practicality over perfect form.
Memorize and recite all the definitions of database normalization forms.
Skip data modeling entirely.
optionDirectness: 这只适合数据库设计专场，不适合系统设计面试的时间盒
适合系统设计面试：先把需求、实体、查询路径说清楚
只在考数据库理论时有用，不能替代真实 schema 推理
架构评审前仍要说明数据怎么存、怎么关联
optionDirectness_en: This fits a database-design interview, not the system-design time box.
This fits system design: explain requirements, entities, and query paths.
This helps in database theory, not real schema reasoning.
You still need to explain what persists and how entities relate.
optionScenarioImpacts: 选这个会显得过度工程化，面试官会认为你没理解系统设计的缩放范围
你能展示自己理解系统需求并能快速设计可用的数据模型
背诵定义无法展示实际设计能力，且耗时且低效
没有数据持久化设计会导致系统设计方案不完整
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This looks over-engineered; the interviewer expects system-design scope, not formal database design rigor.
You demonstrate understanding of requirements and can quickly produce a usable data model.
Memorizing definitions does not show design ability and wastes time.
A system without a data model and persistence is incomplete.
why: 系统设计面试的门槛比专门的数据建模面试低得多：不需要全部范式化或完整 schema 图，「清晰、能用、贴合需求」就够了。
why_en: In a system design interview you just need a clear, functional schema aligned with the requirements, not a fully normalized diagram.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization stores each fact exactly once and links tables with foreign keys, preventing update-miss inconsistencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实体关系图，用方框和连线表示表与它们之间的关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ER diagram, or Entity-Relationship diagram, shows tables and how they relate to each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库的结构定义：有哪些表/集合、字段和它们的关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema is the structural definition of a database — its tables or collections, fields, and their relationships.

scenario: 面试中要为一个普通的社交/电商类系统选数据库，需求没有特殊信号（没有极端写入量、没有频繁变化的 schema）。
scenario_en: You are choosing a database for a typical social or e-commerce system, with no special signal such as extreme write volume or rapidly changing schema.
q: 默认应该选什么？
q_en: For a normal social or e-commerce system, what database should you choose by default?
options: 关系型数据库（推荐 PostgreSQL）
图数据库 Neo4j
宽列数据库 Cassandra
文档数据库 MongoDB
options_en: A relational database — PostgreSQL is the recommended default.
A graph database like Neo4j.
A wide-column database like Cassandra.
A document database like MongoDB.
optionMeanings: 关系型数据库（推荐 PostgreSQL）——支持 ACID、事务、复杂查询
Neo4j 是专门为图数据和关系查询优化的图数据库
Cassandra 是列族存储，为海量分布式写优化
MongoDB 是文档数据库，支持灵活 schema
optionMeanings_en: Relational database like PostgreSQL — supports ACID, transactions, and complex queries.
Neo4j is a graph database optimized for relationships and graph queries.
Cassandra is a wide-column store optimized for massive distributed writes.
MongoDB is a document database with flexible schema.
optionDirectness: 需求普通且 schema 稳定时，关系型覆盖事务和查询灵活性
只有核心查询是多跳关系遍历时，Neo4j 才值得引入
只有海量追加写或时序负载明显时，Cassandra 才占优
只有记录结构频繁变化、嵌套很深时，MongoDB 才占优
optionDirectness_en: Relational fits stable, ordinary requirements needing transactions and flexible queries.
Neo4j earns its keep only when deep relationship traversal is central.
Cassandra wins when massive append writes or time-series load is explicit.
MongoDB wins when record shapes change quickly or nest deeply.
optionScenarioImpacts: 选关系型最稳妥，兼顾事务与查询灵活性
选图库会显得在炫技，没有强信号就不必要
选宽列库预设了极高的写吞吐需求，普通系统用不上
选文档库预设 schema 频繁变化，但面试需求通常稳定
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Relational is the safest default — it balances transactions, query flexibility, and team familiarity.
Choosing a graph database looks like showing off; no strong signal makes it unnecessary.
Wide-column assumes extreme write throughput that a typical system doesn't need.
Document database assumes frequent schema changes, but most interview requirements are stable.
why: 普通社交/电商没有特殊信号时，关系型就是默认；没有强烈个人经验就用 PostgreSQL。
why_en: Resist exotic choices; a relational database like PostgreSQL is the default unless requirements clearly signal a specialized model.
whenOtherWins: 写入量巨大/时序 → 宽列；schema 频繁变化 → 文档库；纯 key 查找/缓存 → KV。有明确信号才切换。
tradeoff: 默认关系型的通用性与团队熟悉度 vs 特殊模型对某类查询的针对性优化

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持强一致事务与复杂查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database with strong transactional guarantees and rich query support.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主流图数据库，以节点和边存储数据、优化关系遍历。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Neo4j is a popular graph database that stores data as nodes and edges optimized for traversal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以节点和边存储数据、优化关系遍历查询的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A graph database stores data as nodes and edges and is optimized for traversing relationships.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式宽列数据库，为海量写入和时序数据优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a distributed wide-column database optimized for massive writes and time-series data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列族组织、每行列集合可不同的数据库，为海量写入和时序数据优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A wide-column database organizes data into column families where each row can have a different set of columns, optimized for massive writes and time-series data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主流文档数据库，以 JSON 风格文档存储数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a popular document database that stores data as JSON-like documents.

q: 关系型数据库的组织方式是？
q_en: How is data organized in a relational database?
options: 自由嵌套的 JSON 文档
节点和边
扁平的 key → value
固定schema表，外键+ACID事务
options_en: Freely nested JSON documents.
Nodes and edges.
A flat key-to-value mapping.
Fixed-schema tables with foreign keys and ACID transactions.
optionMeanings: JSON 风格的自由嵌套文档，没有固定 schema
节点和边的网络结构，针对关系查询
完全扁平的 key → value 映射
行是实体、列是属性、用外键维系关系、ACID 事务保证的表结构
optionMeanings_en: Self-nested JSON documents without a fixed schema.
A network of nodes and edges optimized for relationship queries.
A completely flat key-to-value mapping.
Tables where rows are entities, columns are attributes, foreign keys link relationships, and ACID transactions guarantee correctness.
optionDirectness: 这描述文档库：字段灵活、嵌套自然
这描述图库：关系遍历是一等公民
这描述 KV：只按 key 精确取值
这描述关系型：表结构固定，关系靠键和事务维护
optionDirectness_en: This describes document stores: flexible fields and natural nesting.
This describes graph stores, where traversal is the first-class operation.
This describes key-value stores: exact lookup by key.
This describes relational storage: fixed tables, keys, and transactions.
optionScenarioImpacts: 选这个说明你混淆了关系型和文档库的特性
选这个说明你混淆了关系型和图库的特性
选这个说明你混淆了关系型和 KV 存储的特性
你能准确说出关系型数据库的四个核心组成部分
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You confuse relational and document database characteristics.
You confuse relational and graph database characteristics.
You confuse relational and key-value storage characteristics.
You can clearly define relational as tables plus fixed schema plus foreign keys plus ACID.
why: 表 + 固定 schema + 外键 + ACID 是关系型的四要素；社交（用户/帖子/评论/点赞）和电商（用户/商品/订单/支付）都能自然映射。
why_en: Relational databases organize data into fixed-schema tables where rows are entities and columns are attributes, with foreign keys and ACID transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库事务的四个正确性保证：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability, the four guarantees a database transaction provides.

termDefinitions.meaning: 外键：一张表中指向另一张表主键的字段，用来维系表间关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key is a column that references another table's primary key to enforce a relationship.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库的结构定义：有哪些表/集合、字段和它们的关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema is the structural definition of a database — its tables or collections, fields, and their relationships.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种轻量的键值/嵌套数据格式，常用于文档数据库存储记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON, or JavaScript Object Notation, is a lightweight nested key-value format commonly used to store documents.

scenario: 非功能需求写明强一致：支付绝不能重复扣款、库存绝不能超卖。
scenario_en: A non-functional requirement says consistency is strict: payments must never double-charge and inventory must never oversell.
q: 最合适的存储保证来自？
q_en: Which storage guarantee best fits this requirement?
options: 文档数据库的灵活 schema
SQL 的 ACID 事务
KV 缓存的高速读取
宽列库的高写吞吐
options_en: A document database's flexible schema.
SQL's ACID transactions.
A key-value cache's fast reads.
A wide-column store's high write throughput.
optionMeanings: 文档库提供灵活的 schema 支持，允许字段随意变化
SQL 的 ACID 事务保证操作原子性、一致性、隔离性和持久性
KV 缓存提供超快的读取，但只支持精确 key 查询
宽列库为高吞吐写优化，适合追加写场景
optionMeanings_en: Document database flexibility allows fields to change freely.
SQL ACID transactions guarantee atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.
Key-value caching offers ultra-fast reads but only for exact-key lookups.
Wide-column databases optimize for high write throughput on append-only workloads.
optionDirectness: 字段快速变化时文档库有用，但它不保证扣款和库存原子性
支付和库存要一起成功或一起失败时，ACID 最合适
热读可放缓存，但资金和库存不能以缓存为真相源
写吞吐是目标时宽列有用，但强一致不是它的卖点
optionDirectness_en: Document stores help with changing fields, not payment or inventory atomicity.
ACID fits when payment and inventory must succeed or fail together.
Hot reads can use cache, but money and inventory cannot trust cache as truth.
Wide-column helps write throughput, but strong consistency is not its strength.
optionScenarioImpacts: 灵活 schema 与「不能重复扣款」需求无关——核心问题不是字段灵活性
ACID 事务直接解决「强一致」需求——支付和库存都需要原子操作
高速读取无法保证一致性——缓存可能返回过期数据
高吞吐写对一致性没帮助——反而容易造成分布式不一致
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Schema flexibility is unrelated to preventing double charges — the core issue is not field flexibility.
ACID transactions directly address the strong consistency requirement — payments and inventory both need atomic operations.
Speed without consistency is useless — caches may return stale data.
High throughput actually increases distributed inconsistency rather than preventing it.
why: 「不能重复扣款、不能超卖」正是 ACID 事务的用武之地：强一致作为非功能需求出现时，SQL 就是那个对的工具。
why_en: When strong consistency like no double charges or overselling is a requirement, SQL's ACID guarantees are the right tool.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据可接受最终一致（活动 feed、点赞数），就可以分散到为读优化的其他系统。
tradeoff: 强一致 ACID 事务保证 vs 更灵活/更高吞吐但一致性较弱的存储

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库事务的四个正确性保证：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability, the four guarantees a database transaction provides.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只支持按精确 key 查值的存储，查询能力有限但极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A key-value store only supports exact-key lookups, trading query power for extreme speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列族组织、每行列集合可不同的数据库，为海量写入和时序数据优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A wide-column database organizes data into column families where each row can have a different set of columns, optimized for massive writes and time-series data.

q: 面试里随口提出「跨多表 join 的复杂报表查询」会有什么风险？
q_en: What risk comes with casually proposing complex multi-table joins in an interview?
options: 多表 join 规模化后是性能陷阱，要主动给对策
没有任何风险，join 永远高效
会被认为不会写 SQL
数据库会拒绝执行
options_en: Multi-table joins become a performance trap at scale — call out a plan for them.
There's no risk at all; joins are always efficient.
It will make you look like you can't write SQL.
The database will refuse to execute it.
optionMeanings: 多表 join 在规模化后变成性能陷阱，需要主动说明对策（反范式、缓存、预计算）
多表 join 总是高效的，没有任何性能风险
提出复杂 join 查询会被认为你 SQL 技能欠缺
数据库会拒绝执行多表 join
optionMeanings_en: Multi-table joins become performance traps at scale and require proactive countermeasures like denormalization, caching, or precomputation.
Multi-table joins are always efficient with no performance risk.
Proposing complex join queries will be seen as weak SQL skills.
The database will refuse to execute multi-table joins.
optionDirectness: 报表必须 join 多张大表时，要同时给缓存或预计算方案
小表 join 可以便宜，数据量大后不能默认永远高效
SQL 能力和大规模 join 成本是两个独立问题
语法合法时数据库会执行，风险是延迟和资源消耗
optionDirectness_en: If reports join large tables, pair the idea with cache or precompute.
Small joins can be cheap, but large data makes 'always fast' unsafe.
SQL skill and large-scale join cost are separate concerns.
The database can run valid joins; latency and resources are the risk.
optionScenarioImpacts: 选这个说明你理解复杂查询的性能陷阱，并能主动给出解决方案
选这个显得天真——大规模数据下 join 确实会成问题
选这个是误会——复杂 join 本身不代表 SQL 不行，问题在规模化后的性能
选这个是技术误解——数据库可以执行任意 join，问题是性能成本
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You show you understand join performance risks at scale and can proactively propose solutions.
You sound naive — joins do become expensive at large scale.
This is a misunderstanding — complex queries show SQL skill; the issue is scaled performance.
This is technically wrong — databases can execute any join; the issue is the cost.
why: SQL 擅长复杂查询，但大规模下多表 join 变贵；提到这类查询时要顺手补上性能对策（反范式视图、缓存、预计算），否则显得没意识。
why_en: Multi-table joins become performance traps at scale, so mention denormalized views, caching, or precomputed results when you bring them up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关联字段把多张表的行拼接在一起的查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join is a query operation that combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了读性能主动在多处冗余存储同一份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization deliberately duplicates the same data in multiple places to speed up reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提前算好的汇总结果，读时直接取用不用现算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A precomputed aggregation is a summary calculated ahead of time so reads don’t have to compute it live.

q: 「关系型数据库不能扩展」这个说法，正确的评价是？
q_en: How should you evaluate the claim that relational databases cannot scale?
options: 完全正确，SQL 到百万用户必挂
SQL 确实无法做任何水平扩展
常被夸大：读副本/分片/缓存都能扩展 SQL
只有 NoSQL 才能上规模
options_en: Completely true — SQL always collapses once you hit a million users.
SQL genuinely cannot scale horizontally at all.
Often exaggerated: read replicas, sharding, and caching all scale SQL.
Only NoSQL can operate at that scale.
optionMeanings: 说关系型完全无法扩展、一定会在百万用户时挂掉
关系型数据库从根本上无法做任何形式的水平扩展
关系型可以通过读副本、分片、连接池、缓存等手段扩展；Facebook、Airbnb 都用关系型支撑大规模
只有 NoSQL 技术栈能支持大规模应用
optionMeanings_en: Relational databases absolutely cannot scale and will crash by a million users.
SQL can never do any form of horizontal scaling.
Relational can scale via read replicas, sharding, connection pooling, and caching; Facebook and Airbnb are built on relational foundations.
Only NoSQL can support large-scale systems.
optionDirectness: 百万级并不会让 SQL 自动失效，瓶颈要看查询和架构
读副本、分片和缓存都能给关系型系统扩展空间
关系型适合先作为默认，再按瓶颈加读写扩展手段
NoSQL 只在模型或规模信号明确时才值得替换默认 SQL
optionDirectness_en: A million users do not automatically break SQL; the bottleneck depends on queries and architecture.
Read replicas, sharding, and caching all give relational systems room to scale.
Use relational as the default, then add read or write scaling for bottlenecks.
Replace SQL with NoSQL only when the model or scale signal is clear.
optionScenarioImpacts: 这种绝对化说法会被认为是过度简化，没有理解关系型的实际能力
绝对化论断——忽视了关系型配合架构设计的扩展潜力
你展示了对关系型扩展方式的深入理解，显得成熟理性
这种说法是误导——NoSQL 有自己的问题，关系型在大厂仍是主流
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This absolute claim sounds simplistic and shows you don't understand relational's real capabilities.
Another absolute — you ignore how relational databases scale when paired with good architecture.
You demonstrate mature understanding of relational scaling techniques and cite real examples.
This claim misleads — NoSQL has its own tradeoffs, and major companies still rely on SQL.
why: 扩展性短板被夸大了：配合读副本、分片、连接池和缓存，关系型撑起了世界级大厂。扩展靠的是围绕数据库的架构，不只是数据库本身。
why_en: The scalability knock on SQL is exaggerated: with read replicas, sharding, pooling, and caching, companies like Facebook and Airbnb run on relational foundations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只读的数据库副本，用来分担读流量。

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行数据落在哪个分片上的字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard key is the field that determines which shard a row lives on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用数据库连接而不是每次新建，减少连接建立开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Connection pooling reuses database connections instead of opening a new one per request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 泛指非关系型数据库，如文档库、KV 存储、宽列库、图数据库。

options: 因为内存里放不下任何数据，只能常驻磁盘
数据落在磁盘上，只有搬进内存（RAM）才能被 CPU 处理
因为磁盘硬件本身不支持随机读取
为了保证事务的隔离性级别达标
why: 数据落在磁盘（如今多为 SSD），而 CPU 只能处理内存里的数据，所以每个查询都要把相关页从磁盘搬进 RAM。索引的价值就是减少要搬的页数。
why_en: Data lives on disk but can only be processed in memory, so every query loads pages from disk into RAM, and indexes minimize how many pages that takes.
options_en: Because memory cannot hold any data at all, so everything must stay on disk.
Data lives on disk and can only be processed once it is loaded into memory (RAM).
Because the disk hardware itself does not support random reads.
To guarantee the transaction isolation level is met.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随机存取内存，CPU 能直接处理的高速易失存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAM stands for Random Access Memory, the fast volatile storage the CPU can directly process.

termDefinitions.meaning: 中央处理器，执行程序指令的核心部件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, executes program instructions.

q_en: Why does every database query have to load data from disk into memory?

q: 关于 SSD 上「随机访问 vs 顺序访问」，正确的说法是？
options: SSD 上两者速度完全一样，没有差距
SSD 上随机访问反而比顺序访问更快
只有机械硬盘 HDD 才存在两者差距
SSD 上随机访问仍明显慢于顺序访问——常见误解是这差距已消失
why: 常见误解是 SSD 抹平了差距：其实差距只是比 HDD 小，随机访问依然明显更慢；HDD 上差距更悬殊，所以合理建索引至关重要。
why_en: Even on SSDs random access is still significantly slower than sequential access, a smaller gap than on HDDs but a very real one.
options_en: On SSDs the two have exactly the same speed, no gap at all.
On SSDs random access is actually faster than sequential access.
The gap only exists on HDDs, not on SSDs.
Even on SSDs, random access is still noticeably slower than sequential access — a common misconception says that gap disappeared.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固态硬盘，无机械部件的闪存存储介质，随机访问比机械硬盘快得多但仍慢于顺序访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSD stands for Solid State Drive, flash-based storage much faster at random access than spinning disks but still slower than sequential access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机械硬盘，靠磁头寻道读写的存储介质，随机访问比顺序访问慢得多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HDD stands for Hard Disk Drive, mechanical storage where random access is much slower than sequential access due to seek time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按不连续、不可预测的顺序读写数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random access means reading or writing data in a non-sequential, unpredictable order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按连续顺序读写数据，通常更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential access means reading or writing data in contiguous order, which is usually faster.

q_en: What is true about random access versus sequential access on SSDs?

q: 索引让查询变快的本质机制是什么？
options: 把所有数据压缩得更小，省磁盘空间
提供结构化路径，直接指出数据在哪些页，减少要读的页数
把整张表常驻内存，不必碰磁盘
并行扫描所有磁盘页，多线程加速
why: 索引是为搜索优化的独立数据结构：它告诉你目标数据具体在哪些页，从而不必逐页检查。就像用书的目录直接翻到相关页，而不是一页页找。
why_en: An index is a separate search-optimized structure that tells the database exactly which pages hold the target data, minimizing pages read from storage.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Root page"] --> B["Internal page"]
  B --> C["Leaf page"]
  C --> D["Row pointer"]
options_en: It compresses all the data to make it smaller, saving disk space.
It provides a structured path pointing directly to the pages holding the target data, reducing pages read.
It keeps the entire table resident in memory, never touching disk.
It scans all disk pages in parallel with multiple threads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库读写磁盘的最小单位，典型大小 8KB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A disk page is the smallest unit a database reads or writes on disk, typically eight kilobytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查找而维护的、独立于主表的结构化数据路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is a separate structured data path maintained purely to speed up lookups.

q_en: What is the core mechanism that makes an index speed up queries?

q: 索引不是免费的。它的代价包括哪些？（多选）
options: 额外磁盘空间，有时接近原始数据大小
每次插入/更新除了改主表，还要更新表上的每一个索引
多个索引会让一次写操作触发多次磁盘写
有索引后读取一定变慢
why: 索引的三重代价：占磁盘空间、写入时每个索引都要维护、多索引放大写开销。读取恰恰是索引加速的对象，不会因此变慢。
why_en: Indexes cost extra disk space and slow down writes because every insert or update must also update each index, turning one write into several disk writes.
options_en: It costs extra disk space, sometimes nearly as much as the original data.
Every insert or update must update the main table plus every index on it.
Multiple indexes turn a single write into several disk writes.
Reads always get slower once you add an index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入时同步更新索引结构的开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Index maintenance is the overhead of keeping index structures updated on every write.

q_en: Indexes are not free. What costs do they add? (Select all that apply.)

scenario: 一张日志表：持续高频插入新记录，但几乎从不查询旧数据。
q: 对这张表，关于索引的正确判断是？
options: 尽量多建索引以防万一，覆盖所有可能查询
必须建覆盖索引，避免任何回表
索引可能弊大于利：写多读少，维护开销盖过读收益
建哈希索引就能兼顾写入和查询
why: 写频繁、读极少的表是索引伤害大于收益的经典案例：每次插入都要维护索引，却几乎没人来读。这里少建甚至不建索引才对。
why_en: A write-heavy, rarely-read logging table is the classic case where index maintenance overhead outweighs the benefit.
whenOtherWins: 反过来，读多写少的表（用户资料、商品目录）索引收益远超维护成本，应该按查询模式建索引。
options_en: Add as many indexes as possible just in case, to cover every possible query.
You must add a covering index to avoid any table lookup.
Indexes may hurt more than help here: writes dominate, so maintenance overhead outweighs the read benefit.
A hash index alone can satisfy both writing and querying.
tradeoff: 索引维护成本 vs 查询收益

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

q_en: For this table, what is the right indexing judgment?
scenario_en: A log table receives high-frequency inserts, but old records are almost never queried.

scenario: 一张只有几百行的小配置表，被问要不要加索引。
q: 最合理的回答是？
options: 可以不加：表太小，索引维护成本可能超过一次顺序扫描
必须加索引，任何表都不能例外
加哈希索引，因为查找永远最快
加覆盖索引，提前避免所有回表
why: 几百行的小表全扫一遍非常便宜，索引的维护与遍历成本反而可能更高。索引的价值随数据量增长才显现。
why_en: For a tiny table a sequential scan is so cheap that maintaining and traversing an index can cost more than it saves.
whenOtherWins: 当表增长到几十万、上百万行且有明确过滤/排序模式时，就该按查询模式补上索引了。
options_en: Skip it: the table is so small that index maintenance can cost more than one sequential scan.
Always add an index — no table is an exception.
Add a hash index because lookups are always fastest.
Add a covering index up front to avoid any table lookup.
tradeoff: 索引维护成本 vs 顺序扫描成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 从头到尾依次读取表中每一行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential scan reads every row of a table from start to end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

q_en: What is the most reasonable answer for this tiny table?
scenario_en: You are asked whether to add an index to a tiny configuration table with only a few hundred rows.

q: 索引对内存占用的实际影响，下面哪个判断最准确？
options: 多一个索引，内存占用就直接翻一倍
索引完全不占用任何内存空间
内存影响是索引所有代价里最致命的
影响常被夸大：缓冲池管理已很智能，但仍要监控索引使用
why: 索引对内存的冲击常被高估——现代缓冲池管理已大幅缓解。但好习惯不变：监控索引使用率，删掉没有明显收益的索引。
why_en: The memory impact of indexes is often overblown thanks to smart buffer pool management, but you should still monitor usage and drop unnecessary indexes.
options_en: Adding one more index simply doubles memory usage.
Indexes take up no memory at all.
Memory impact is the single most fatal cost of indexes.
The impact is often overblown thanks to smart buffer pool management, but you should still monitor index usage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库在内存里缓存磁盘页的区域，减少重复磁盘读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The buffer pool is the in-memory area a database uses to cache disk pages and avoid repeated disk reads.

q_en: Which statement best describes how indexes affect memory usage?

q: 补全面试常考的索引家族：
text: 通用默认用 {{B 树}}；极端写入负载用 {{LSM 树}} 存储引擎；纯精确匹配可用 {{哈希}} 索引；经纬度邻近搜索用 {{地理空间}} 索引；全文搜索用 {{倒排}} 索引。
why: 五类索引各解一类问题：B 树是万金油，LSM 吃写入，哈希只做等值，地理空间管 2D 邻近，倒排管文本。面试先想清楚查询形态再选。
why_en: B-trees are the default, LSM trees serve write-heavy workloads, hash indexes do exact matches, geospatial indexes handle proximity, and inverted indexes power text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写的存储引擎，靠内存缓冲和后台合并优化写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a storage engine that turns random writes into sequential writes using an in-memory buffer and background merging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

termDefinitions.term: 地理空间索引 / geospatial index
termDefinitions.meaning: 理解二维空间邻近关系的索引，如 geohash、四叉树、R 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index understands 2D proximity, implemented via approaches like geohash, quadtrees, or R-trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

q_en: Fill in the common index families interviewers expect you to know:

q: B 树节点和二叉树节点的关键区别是？
options: B 树节点和二叉树一样最多两个子节点
B 树节点可以有数百个子节点，节点内是有序的键+指针数组
B 树节点只存指针，不存任何键
B 树本质上根本不是树结构
why: 二叉树每节点最多两个孩子，B 树节点能有数百个孩子，节点内是有序的键+指针数组。扇出大意味着树很矮，找数据只需极少次磁盘读。
why_en: Unlike binary trees, a B-tree node can have hundreds of children with an ordered array of keys and pointers, keeping the tree shallow to minimize disk reads.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Root page"] --> B["Internal page"]
  B --> C["Leaf page"]
  C --> D["Row pointer"]
options_en: A B-tree node, like a binary tree node, has at most two children.
A B-tree node can have hundreds of children, each holding a sorted array of keys and pointers.
A B-tree node stores only pointers, no keys.
A B-tree is not actually a tree structure at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个节点最多两个子节点的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A binary tree is a tree structure where each node has at most two children.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个树节点能指向的子节点数量，扇出越大树越矮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is how many children a tree node can point to; higher fanout means a shallower tree.

q_en: What is the key difference between a B-tree node and a binary-tree node?

q: B 树的结构性规则包括哪些？（多选）
options: 所有叶子节点必须在同一深度
每个节点可含 m/2 到 m 个键（m 为树的阶）
有 k 个键的节点恰好有 k+1 个子节点
节点内的键无需保持有序
why: B 树靠这些不变式保持平衡：叶子同深、节点键数在 m/2 到 m 之间、k 键对应 k+1 子。节点内的键必须有序——这正是范围查询高效的基础。
why_en: In a B-tree all leaves sit at the same depth, nodes hold between half-m and m keys, a node with k keys has exactly k plus one children, and keys stay sorted within each node.
options_en: All leaf nodes must sit at the same depth.
Each node can hold between m/2 and m keys, where m is the tree's order.
A node with k keys has exactly k+1 children.
Keys inside a node do not need to stay sorted.

termDefinitions.meaning: B 树的阶 m 决定了每个节点最多能有多少个键和子节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree's order, m, determines the maximum number of keys and children each node can have.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

q_en: Which structural rules does a B-tree maintain? (Select all that apply.)

q: B 树节点的大小通常被设计成正好匹配什么？
options: 一个磁盘页，典型为 8KB
一个 CPU 缓存行（64 字节）
一个内存页（4KB 固定）
整个表的大小
why: 8KB 是磁盘页这个硬件给定值，不是公式推导出来的；B 树节点对齐它，一次 I/O 正好读满一个节点，这是后续对比 LSM/哈希索引 I/O 效率的基准。
why_en: Eight kilobytes is a given hardware constant, not a derived number; aligning B-tree nodes to it means one I/O reads one full node, the baseline for later I/O comparisons.
scenario: 面试官追问：为什么 Postgres 把 B 树节点大小固定设计成这个数字，而不是随便选。
options_en: One disk page, typically eight kilobytes.
One CPU cache line, sixty-four bytes.
One fixed four-kilobyte memory page.
The size of the entire table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库读写磁盘的最小单位，典型大小 8KB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A disk page is the smallest unit a database reads or writes on disk, typically eight kilobytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对磁盘的一次读或写操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: I/O, or Input/Output, here means one read or write operation to disk.

termDefinitions.term: CPU 缓存行 / CPU cache line
termDefinitions.meaning: CPU 内部的小容量高速缓存行，一般 64 字节，远小于磁盘页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CPU cache line is a small, very fast on-chip cache unit, typically 64 bytes, far smaller than a disk page.

q_en: A B-tree node is usually sized to match what unit?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why PostgreSQL sizes B-tree nodes to this number instead of choosing an arbitrary size.

q: PostgreSQL 用 B 树按 id=350 找一条记录，通常需要读多少个磁盘页？
options: 几十页，逐层慢慢定位
上百页，接近全表扫描
只需 2-3 页：根节点、内部节点、叶节点各一次
必须读整张表才能确认
why: B 树扇出大、树矮，一次点查通常只读根、内部、叶共 2-3 页——这不是背诵数字，而是后面对比 LSM 读放大的基准线。
why_en: Thanks to high fanout, a B-tree point lookup typically reads only two to three pages — root, internal, leaf — the baseline for later LSM read-amplification comparisons.
scenario: 面试官问：B 树的高扇出到底能把一次点查的磁盘读次数压到多低。
options_en: Dozens of pages, locating it layer by layer.
Hundreds of pages, close to a full scan.
Only two to three pages: root, maybe one internal node, and one leaf node.
The entire table must be read to be sure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个树节点能指向的子节点数量，扇出越大树越矮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is how many children a tree node can point to; higher fanout means a shallower tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只查一个精确 key 的查询，例如按主键取一行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point lookup is a query for one exact key, such as fetching a row by primary key.

q_en: In PostgreSQL, how many disk pages does a B-tree lookup for id=350 usually read?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how low a B-tree's high fanout can push the disk-page reads for one point lookup.

q: 在 PostgreSQL 里建一张带 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY 和 email UNIQUE 的表，会自动发生什么？
options: 什么索引都不会自动建
自动建两个 B 树索引：主键和 email 各一个
自动创建两个哈希索引来处理
只给主键建索引，唯一约束靠全表扫描检查
why: Postgres 几乎处处用 B 树：主键、唯一约束、常规索引默认都是 B 树。B 树保持有序，同时支撑唯一性检查和范围查询。
why_en: PostgreSQL automatically creates two B-tree indexes for this table, one for the primary key and one for the unique email constraint.
options_en: No index gets created automatically at all.
Two B-tree indexes are created automatically: one for the primary key, one for email.
Two hash indexes get created automatically instead.
Only the primary key gets an index; the unique constraint is checked via full table scan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自增整数主键，PostgreSQL 里的常见写法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIAL PRIMARY KEY is PostgreSQL syntax for an auto-incrementing integer primary key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证某列（组合）在表中不出现重复值的约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A unique constraint guarantees a column or column set never has duplicate values in the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

q_en: What happens automatically when you create a PostgreSQL table with SERIAL PRIMARY KEY and email UNIQUE?

q: MongoDB 的索引（如 db.users.createIndex({"email": 1})）底层用的是？
options: 哈希表，靠哈希值定位
跳表，靠多层链表加速
LSM 树，靠顺序合并写入
B+ 树：B 树变体，数据全部存在叶节点
why: 即便是文档模型的 MongoDB，索引也用 B+ 树（数据全在叶节点的 B 树变体），把 email 值映射到文档位置。B 树家族无处不在。
why_en: Even document-model MongoDB uses B-plus trees, a B-tree variant storing all data in leaf nodes, to map indexed values to document locations.
options_en: A hash table, locating entries by hash value.
A skip list, using layered linked lists for speed.
An LSM tree, merging writes sequentially.
A B+ tree, a B-tree variant that stores all data in the leaf nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: B 树的变体，所有实际数据都存放在叶节点，内部节点只存路由键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B+ tree is a B-tree variant where all actual data lives in leaf nodes and internal nodes only store routing keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用多层链表实现快速查找和有序插入的概率性数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A skip list is a probabilistic layered linked-list structure that supports fast ordered search and insertion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档模型的 NoSQL 数据库，索引底层使用 B+ 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document-model NoSQL database whose indexes are implemented with B+ trees under the hood.

optionMeanings: 把值哈希到桶来定位的结构。
多层链表实现的有序跳跃结构。
把随机写转顺序写的日志合并树。
B 树变体，数据全存在叶节点。
optionScenarioImpacts: 适合纯内存等值查找，不是文档数据库索引的常见形态。
常见于内存有序集合，不属于磁盘索引家族。
适合写远多于读，不是 MongoDB 索引默认结构。
在文档模型上仍靠这层结构定位到具体文档。
optionDirectness: 答非所问：题目问的是有序索引家族，不是哈希。
跳表服务内存排序结构，不属于磁盘索引家族。
LSM 优化的是写入吞吐，不是索引查找结构。

why_en: IP handles routing and addressing by breaking data into packets and forwarding them with best-effort delivery to any destination address.

It encrypts the contents of the communication.

It maintains session state between client and server.

Domain name resolution.
HTML rendering.
Modulating the physical signal.

q: 把「浏览器输入 URL 到拿到网页」的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the browser-to-webpage request flow in the correct order.
steps: TCP 三次握手建立连接
DNS 把域名解析成 IP 地址
服务器处理请求并准备响应
客户端发送 HTTP GET 请求
TCP 四次挥手关闭连接
服务器发回 HTTP 响应
why: DNS 解析 → TCP 握手 → 发请求 → 服务器处理（多数工程师唯一控制的延迟）→ 回响应 → 挥手断开。一次「简单」请求背后是多轮包交换，层层都有延迟。
why_en: A web request resolves DNS, performs the TCP handshake, sends the HTTP request, waits for server processing, receives the response, and tears the connection down.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant D as DNS
    participant S as 服务器
    C->>D: 域名解析
    D-->>C: IP 地址
    C->>S: SYN / SYN-ACK / ACK（三次握手）
    C->>S: HTTP GET
    S-->>C: HTTP 响应
    C->>S: FIN / ACK / FIN / ACK（四次挥手）

q: 补全 TCP 三次握手：
q_en: Complete the TCP three-way handshake.
text: 客户端发 {{SYN}} 请求连接；服务器回 {{SYN-ACK}} 确认请求；客户端再发 {{ACK}} 完成连接建立。断开则用 FIN/ACK/FIN/ACK 四次挥手。
why: 三次握手建立、四次挥手拆除——每个不复用连接的请求都要重复这套流程，这是后面讨论持久连接和负载均衡的伏笔。
why_en: TCP opens with a SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK three-way handshake and closes with a four-way FIN and ACK exchange.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: SYN
    S-->>C: SYN-ACK
    C->>S: ACK
    Note over C,S: 连接已建立

q: TCP 连接是客户端和服务器都要维护的状态：这一事实带来什么设计影响？
q_en: What design consequence follows from TCP connection state living on both client and server?
options: 连接一旦建立就永远免费
状态只存在服务器端
不用 keep-alive 就要重建连接
TCP 连接不占用任何资源
why: 连接即状态，双方都要维护；不复用就得每请求重建，开销可观。设计实时更新类系统（持久连接）时这一点会反复出现。
why_en: Because a connection is state both sides maintain, every request repeats the costly setup unless you use keep-alive or multiplexing, which matters for realtime systems.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["请求 1"] --> B["建连"]
    B --> C["响应"]
    C --> D["断开"]
    D --> E["请求 2 再建连"]
    C -.keep-alive.-> F["复用连接"]
options_en: Once established, a connection is free forever.
The state only lives on the server side.
Without keep-alive you rebuild the connection every time.
A TCP connection consumes no resources at all.
optionMeanings: 假设连接免费：忽略了握手和维护状态的真实开销。
假设状态只在服务器：忽略了客户端同样要维护连接状态。
keep-alive/HTTP2 多路复用：让多个请求复用同一条连接、省去重复建连。
假设连接零资源占用：与 TCP 需要维护缓冲区、序号等状态矛盾。

q: 关于公网 IP，正确的说法是？

公网 IP 由 RIR（区域互联网注册机构）分配、全网可路由
公网 IP 只在局域网内有效
公网 IP 由 DNS 服务器分配
why: 私有网络里 IP 随便定，但要让互联网流量找到你，必须用 RIR 分配的可路由地址。互联网路由基础设施针对公网 IP 之间的转发做了优化。
why_en: Public IPs are allocated by regional internet registries and are routable, so the internet backbone knows for example that addresses starting with 17 belong to Apple.
options_en: Anyone can self-assign a public IP and have it routed by the whole internet.
Public IPs are allocated by a RIR and are globally routable.
A public IP only works inside a local network.
Public IPs are assigned by DNS servers.

q: UDP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does UDP have?
options: 无连接：没有握手和连接建立，开销小、延迟低
不保证送达：丢包不会有任何通知
不保证顺序：包可能乱序到达
自动去重，保证恰好一次投递
why: UDP 是「机枪式」spray and pray：在 IP 之上几乎不加功能，换来速度。无连接、可能丢、可能乱序，也没有重复保护——收到的就是一坨二进制加上来源/目的地址端口。
why_en: UDP is connectionless with no handshake, offers no delivery or ordering guarantees, and has lower latency precisely because it adds so little on top of IP.
options_en: Connectionless: no handshake or setup, so overhead and latency are lower.
No delivery guarantee: a lost packet triggers no notification.
No ordering guarantee: packets can arrive out of order.
Automatic deduplication with exactly-once delivery.

scenario: 设计 VoIP 语音通话：偶尔丢一个包只是音频轻微卡顿、对话依然可懂；重传丢失的包反而会用 ACK 堵塞网络。
scenario_en: You are designing a VoIP call: losing one audio packet causes a tiny glitch, but retransmitting it would block newer audio behind ACKs.
q: 传输层该选？
q_en: Which transport protocol should you choose for this VoIP audio call?
options: TCP，保证每个音频包都到
QUIC，等它普及
UDP：速度优先，客户端自己扛丢包
HTTP 轮询
why: 实时音视频、在线游戏、DNS 查询都是 UDP 的主场：应用能自行处理偶发丢包/乱序，低延迟远比完整重传值钱。
why_en: UDP fits VoIP because dropping an occasional packet is a minor hiccup, while retransmitting old audio would only clog the network.
whenOtherWins: 数据完整性关键的场景（支付、文件传输、几乎一切非实时业务）用 TCP——凡是 UDP 不合适的地方基本都是 TCP。
options_en: TCP, to guarantee every audio packet arrives.
QUIC, and wait for it to become mainstream.
UDP: speed over reliability, and the client absorbs the occasional loss.
HTTP polling.
tradeoff: UDP 低延迟可丢包 vs TCP 可靠重传
optionMeanings: TCP：可靠传输协议，握手建连、丢包重传。
QUIC：基于 UDP 的现代传输协议，性能好但采用面还不够广。
UDP：无连接、尽力而为，不重传不保序。
HTTP 轮询：客户端周期性发请求问有没有新数据。
optionDirectness: 方向错了：重传机制反而会让实时音频卡顿更久，牺牲了延迟去换不需要的可靠性。
粒度错了：QUIC 值得关注，但现在就全量依赖它超出了这题的约束——普及度不够。
抓住了关键差异：偶发丢包只是轻微卡顿，重传反而更糟——UDP 直接匹配这条约束。
时机错了：轮询天然有延迟，不是真正的实时推送，不适合语音流。

q: TCP 的「流（stream）」意味着什么？
q_en: What does it mean that TCP exposes a stream?
options: 数据以视频流形式传输
服务器可以不经请求推送数据
连接是无状态的
有状态连接：同流内消息保序，未确认会重传
why: TCP 流是有状态连接，给了我们谈「顺序」的基础：同流内消息保序，接收方必须 ACK，否则发送方重传。可靠、有序、有错误校验。
why_en: A TCP stream is a stateful connection where messages arrive in the order sent and unacknowledged messages are retransmitted until confirmed.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["发送端字节流"] --> B["TCP 分段"]
    B --> C["确认 ACK"]
    C -.丢包.-> D["重传"]
    C --> E["接收端按序读"]
options_en: Data is transmitted like a video stream.
The server can push data without being asked.
The connection is stateless.
A stateful connection: messages on the same stream stay ordered, and unacknowledged ones get retransmitted.

q: TCP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does TCP provide?
options: 面向连接：传数据前先建立专用连接
可靠投递：保证数据按序、无错到达
流量控制防止淹没接收方 + 拥塞控制适应网络拥堵
头部固定只有 8 字节
why: TCP 四大件：面向连接、可靠有序、流控、拥塞控制——这就是它比 UDP 慢的原因，也是互联网的主力马。8 字节头是 UDP 的，TCP 头是 20-60 字节。
why_en: TCP is connection-oriented with reliable in-order delivery, flow control, and congestion control, while the tiny eight-byte header belongs to UDP.
options_en: Connection-oriented: it establishes a dedicated connection before transferring data.
Reliable delivery: it guarantees data arrives in order and without errors.

q: 在系统设计常见协议中，WebRTC（Web 实时通信协议）有哪两个独特之处？

q: 补全 WebRTC 的三大基础设施角色：
q_en: Fill in the three infrastructure roles behind WebRTC.
text: {{信令服务器}}记录哪些 peer 可用及其连接信息；{{STUN}} 用「打洞」等技术帮 peer 获得公网可路由的地址和端口；{{TURN}} 是中继兜底——直连失败时把流量经中央服务器转发。
why: 多数客户端在 NAT 之后、不接受入站连接，直连没那么容易：信令服务器牵线，STUN 打洞，实在不行 TURN 中继。
why_en: A signaling server tracks available peers, STUN performs NAT hole punching to obtain routable addresses, and TURN relays traffic when direct connection fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 帮 peer 穿透 NAT、获得公网可路由地址的一套技术（如打洞）。

termDefinitions.meaning: 直连失败时用中央服务器中继流量的兜底方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TURN is the fallback that relays traffic through a central server when a direct peer-to-peer connection fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台内网设备共享一个公网 IP 的机制，也让它们默认不接受入站连接。

q: Redis Cluster 是客户端负载均衡的好例子，它如何运作？

有一个中央路由服务器分发所有请求

q: DNS 的 TTL 机制给「更新服务器列表」带来什么硬约束？
q_en: What hard constraint does DNS TTL create when updating server lists?
options: 远端 DNS 服务器会按 TTL 缓存解析记录
TTL 越长更新越快
TTL 不影响更新速度
TTL 只影响 HTTPS
why: TTL 是把双刃剑：允许各地 DNS 缓存（扩展性好），但也决定了摘掉一台坏服务器最长要等一个 TTL 才对所有客户端生效。
why_en: DNS entries are cached for their TTL by resolvers everywhere, so your updates cannot propagate to clients faster than that TTL.
options_en: DNS resolvers everywhere cache a record for its TTL.
A longer TTL makes updates propagate faster.
TTL doesn't affect update speed.
TTL only affects HTTPS.

q: Layer 4 负载均衡器的工作方式是？
q_en: How does a Layer 4 load balancer work?
options: 解析 HTTP 请求内容再路由
只做 DNS 解析
工作在传输层：只看 IP/端口做路由
在应用层重写每个请求
why: L4 LB 几乎不拆包，快而高效；建立的 TCP 连接具有粘性（同连接同后端），概念上就像客户端和那台服务器直连——这正是持久连接协议需要的。
why_en: A layer four load balancer routes on IP and port without inspecting content, acting as if the client had a direct persistent TCP connection to one backend.
options_en: It parses HTTP request content to route.
It only does DNS resolution.
It operates at the transport layer, routing only on IP and port.
It rewrites every request at the application layer.
optionMeanings: 解析 HTTP 内容路由：这是 L7 的行为。
只做域名解析：这是 DNS 的职责，不是负载均衡器的工作方式。
只凭 IP/端口路由、不看内容：L4 的真实工作方式。
在应用层重写每个请求：这也是 L7 一类的行为。
optionDirectness: 层次错了：解析请求内容是 L7 才做的事，L4 不拆到这一层。
方向错了：域名解析是 DNS 的职责，和负载均衡器转发请求是两回事。
抓住了关键差异：不拆包、只看 IP/端口，正是 L4 用速度换灵活性的地方。
层次错了：重写请求内容同样需要理解应用协议，属于 L7 范畴。

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里提供端到端保证（可靠性、顺序、流控）的传输层，主角是 TCP/UDP/QUIC。

q: Layer 7 负载均衡器的工作方式是？
q_en: How does a Layer 7 load balancer work?
options: 透传 TCP 包不做处理
终止连接，按 HTTP 内容路由
只按源 IP 路由
只能用于 UDP
why: L7 LB 接收的是应用层请求（如 HTTP GET）再转发请求本身：API 请求路由到一组服务器、网页请求到另一组（类似 API 网关），或按 cookie 把同一用户固定到同一后端。
why_en: A layer seven load balancer terminates connections and routes each application-level request based on its content such as URL, headers, or cookies.
options_en: It passes TCP packets through untouched.
It terminates the connection and routes on HTTP content.
It only routes by source IP.
It only works with UDP.
optionMeanings: 透传不处理：这是 L4 的行为，不是 L7。
终止连接、按内容路由：L7 的真实工作方式。
只按源 IP 路由：粒度比 L7 实际能力粗得多。
只能用于 UDP：与 L7 常见场景（HTTP）矛盾。
optionDirectness: 层次错了：透传不检查内容，是 L4 的做法，不是 L7。
抓住了关键差异：终止连接、理解应用协议、按内容路由，正是 L7 的分层位置。
粒度错了：L7 能看到的信息远不止源 IP，比如路径、header、cookie。
方向错了：L7 的典型场景就是 HTTP 类应用层流量，不是 UDP。

L7，因为功能更多
L4 负载均衡器：维持持久 TCP 连接

options_en: It doesn't matter, they're interchangeable.
You can only use DNS rotation.
L7, because it has more features.
A layer 4 load balancer, which keeps a persistent TCP connection.
tradeoff: L4 持久连接粘性 vs L7 按内容灵活路由
optionMeanings: 认为两种负载均衡器对这个场景没有差别。
把 DNS 轮转当成唯一手段。
L7：按内容路由更灵活，但连接语义不同。
L4：维持持久 TCP 连接，天然适合长连接协议。
optionDirectness: 状态错了：WebSocket 需要长连接粘在同一后端，两种 LB 的连接语义并不等价。
粒度错了：DNS 轮转解决的是入口分散，不解决单条长连接的粘性问题。
状态错了：L7 常见做法是终止再转发，不天然保证同一条 WebSocket 连接的粘性。
抓住了关键差异：L4 的透传式连接正好保住了 WebSocket 需要的持久会话。

q: L4 与 L7 负载均衡器的一句话对比是？
q_en: What is the one-line comparison between L4 and L7 load balancers?
options: L4 不看内容快转发；L7 按内容智能路由
L4 更智能，L7 更快
两者都终止 TCP 连接
L7 不支持 HTTP
why: 一条性能与智能的取舍线：L4 = 快、透传、连接粘性；L7 = 灵活、内容路由、代价是包检查的 CPU。按「要不要持久连接、要不要按内容分流」来选。
why_en: Layer four is fast and content-blind with persistent connections, while layer seven terminates connections and routes intelligently on request content at higher CPU cost.
options_en: L4 forwards fast without looking at content; L7 routes intelligently on content.
L4 is smarter, L7 is faster.
Both terminate the TCP connection.
L7 doesn't support HTTP.
tradeoff: L4 快但看不到内容 vs L7 智能但更耗 CPU
optionMeanings: L4 快、不看内容；L7 灵活、看内容：两者真实的能力/代价对照。
把两者的智能与速度描述对调。
认为两者都终止 TCP 连接。
认为 L7 不支持 HTTP。
optionDirectness: 抓住了关键差异：「看不看内容」正是决定速度与灵活性谁占优的那条轴。

状态错了：L4 通常不终止连接，效果更像透传。
方向错了：L7 恰恰是围绕 HTTP 等应用协议设计的，这是它的主场。

q: 负载均衡器靠什么实现自动故障转移（高可用的关键）？
q_en: How do load balancers implement automatic failover for high availability?
options: 人工值守切换
健康检查：TCP/L7 探测存活
重启所有服务器
把流量全部缓存
why: LB 不只分流量，还持续监控后端健康：服务器崩溃或断电就停止向它路由，恢复了再加回来。检测并绕开故障、无需人工干预——这是 LB 之于高可用的价值。
why_en: Load balancers run health checks, like TCP connection tests or HTTP checks expecting a 200, and automatically route around servers that fail until they recover.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    LB["LB"] -->|健康检查| A["Server A OK"]
    LB -->|健康检查失败| B["Server B"]
    B -.摘除.-> X["不接流量"]
    A --> U["用户请求"]
options_en: A human manually flips traffic over.
Health checks: a TCP or L7 probe for liveness.
Restart every server.
Cache all the traffic.
codeSample:
GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: backend-3

HTTP/1.1 200 OK   # 健康，继续接流量
HTTP/1.1 500      # 或超时无响应 -> 摘除该实例
optionMeanings: 人工值守：与「自动」故障转移的要求矛盾。
健康检查：TCP 层探测能否建连，或 L7 层探测 HTTP 响应码。
重启所有服务器：代价过大且会造成服务中断。
把流量全部缓存：无法检测后端是否存活。

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器定期探测后端是否存活/正常响应，失败就摘掉流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A health check is the load balancer periodically probing whether a backend is alive and responding correctly, pulling traffic if it fails.

q: 补全常见负载均衡算法：
q_en: Fill in the common load-balancing algorithms.
text: {{Round Robin}}：按顺序轮流分发；Random：随机分发；{{Least Connections}}：发给活跃连接最少的服务器；Least Response Time：发给响应最快的；{{IP Hash}}：按客户端 IP 决定服务器，可用于会话保持。
why: 无状态应用用轮询/随机就好——新服务器加入后自然开始分到流量；持久连接服务用最少连接；要会话粘性用 IP Hash。
why_en: Round robin cycles through servers, least connections picks the server with the fewest active connections, and IP hash maps a client to a consistent server for session persistence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定顺序轮流把请求分给每台服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round robin is a load-balancing algorithm that cycles through servers in a fixed order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把新请求发给当前活跃连接数最少的服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least connections is a load-balancing algorithm that sends each new request to whichever server currently has the fewest active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按客户端 IP 计算哈希决定路由到哪台服务器的负载均衡算法，可用于会话保持。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP hash is a load-balancing algorithm that hashes the client IP to pick a server, useful for session persistence.

scenario: 你的服务维护大量 SSE / WebSocket 持久连接，担心负载在服务器间越来越不均。
scenario_en: Your service holds many SSE or WebSocket connections, and you are worried that load will drift unevenly across servers.
q: 负载均衡算法该选？
q_en: Which load-balancing algorithm should you choose for many persistent connections?
options: 永远用轮询
IP Hash
最少连接
随机
why: 长连接不像短请求会自然消散：轮询下先起的服务器会一直背着旧连接。按活跃连接数分发能防止单机被长连接慢慢压满。
why_en: For services holding SSE or WebSocket connections use least connections, which prevents one server from gradually accumulating all the active connections.
whenOtherWins: 无状态短请求服务用轮询或随机即可——简单、且扩容加机器后流量自然流向新节点。
options_en: Always use round robin.
IP hash.
Least connections.
Random.
tradeoff: Least Connections 防止长连接堆积 vs Round Robin 简单够用
optionMeanings: 永远用轮询：忽略了长连接不会像短请求一样自然消散。
IP Hash：解决会话保持，不解决连接堆积。
Least Connections：按当前活跃连接数分发。
随机：同样不感知每台服务器已经背了多少条长连接。
optionDirectness: 状态错了：轮询不看每台服务器当前已经持有多少条连接，容易越堆越偏。
方向错了：IP Hash 解决的是同一客户端固定打到同一台服务器，不是负载不均问题。
抓住了关键差异：它直接感知当前连接数，专门针对长连接堆积这个问题。
状态错了：随机同样不参考存量连接数，长期下来也会失衡。

q: 什么是可用区（availability zone）模式？
q_en: What is the availability-zone deployment pattern?

每个用户一台专属服务器
只在一个国家部署

Give every user a dedicated server.

q: 光速给纽约-伦敦的往返延迟定了什么物理下限？
q_en: What round-trip latency lower bound does the speed of light impose between New York and London?
options: 约 1ms
往返理论最低约 56ms
约 500ms
没有物理下限，取决于带宽
why: 还没算任何处理时间，物理就先收走 56ms。这条硬约束是低延迟应用必须做地理分布的根本原因——你无法优化光速。
why_en: Light in fiber travels at about two thirds of light speed, so a New York to London round trip has a theoretical floor of roughly fifty-six milliseconds.
scenario: 设计一个跨大陆服务：客户端在纽约，一部分依赖部署在伦敦，需要估算物理延迟的下限。
scenario_en: You are designing a cross-continent service: the client is in New York and one dependency runs in London, so you need the physical latency floor.
options_en: About 1 millisecond.
The theoretical round-trip floor is about 56ms.
About 500 milliseconds.
There's no physical floor, it's all down to bandwidth.
