q: checkpoint barrier（屏障）是怎么工作的？
q_en: How does a checkpoint barrier work?
options: JobManager 逐台机器 SSH 上去手动打包内存下载
每个算子每秒各自独立拍快照，彼此互不协调
JobManager 向 source 发屏障，算子收齐后各自快照，全部完成即注册成功
由 sink 逐级反向发送确认信号来触发整个流程
options_en: The JobManager SSHes into each machine one by one to manually dump memory.
Every operator independently snapshots itself once a second with no coordination.
The JobManager sends a barrier from the sources; each operator snapshots once barriers arrive, and it registers once all finish.
The sink triggers the whole process by sending acknowledgements backward, one stage at a time.
optionMeanings: SSH 手动 dump
算子独立快照
barrier 协调快照
sink 反向触发
optionMeanings_en: The JobManager SSHes into each machine one by one to manually dump memory.
Every operator independently snapshots itself once a second with no coordination.
The JobManager sends a barrier from the sources; each operator snapshots once barriers arrive, and it registers once all finish.
The sink triggers the whole process by sending acknowledgements backward, one stage at a time.
why: 屏障像 watermark 一样随流而行，把「快照时刻」一致地传播到每个算子——状态序列化存入 backend，最终由 JobManager 登记。
why_en: The job manager injects a barrier at the sources, each operator snapshots its state once barriers arrive from all inputs, and the checkpoint completes when every operator finishes.

    S->>A: checkpoint barrier
    A->>Store: snapshot state
    A->>B: forward barrier
    B->>Store: snapshot state

q: 把 Flink 的故障恢复流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put Flink failure recovery in the correct order:
steps: 整个作业暂停：所有任务（含健康节点上的）都停下
JobManager 发现某 TaskManager 心跳消失，标记其失败
作业从 checkpoint 恢复处理，保证 exactly-once
取回最近的 checkpoint，把失败节点的任务重新分配到健康节点
各任务恢复状态，source 回退到 checkpoint 时的位点（如 Kafka offset）
why: 检测 → 全作业暂停 → 取 checkpoint + 重分配 → 恢复状态 + 回退 source → 继续处理。代价是恢复期间全作业不可用，但换来一致的状态边界。
why_en: Flink detects the failure, pauses the whole job, restores from one checkpoint, rewinds sources, and pays downtime to keep state consistent.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    D["检测：心跳丢失"] --> P["暂停整个作业"]
    P --> R["取最近 checkpoint\n重分配任务"]
    R --> S["恢复状态 + source 回退"]
    S --> G["恢复处理 (exactly-once)"]

q: 某个 TaskManager 挂了，为什么 Flink 要暂停「整个作业」，连健康节点上的任务也停？
q_en: When one TaskManager dies, why does Flink pause the entire job instead of letting healthy tasks continue?
options: Flink 把作业当整体，必须一起回到同一个 checkpoint
纯粹是为了让整个集群运行时更省电、降低成本
因为健康节点这时大概率其实也已经出现故障
这是 Kafka 这一层强制规定必须遵守的行为
options_en: Flink treats the job as one recovery unit, so it must roll back to the same checkpoint together.
Purely to make the whole cluster use less power and cost less while running.
Because the healthy nodes are probably also failing at that point.
Because Kafka itself mandates this recovery behavior.
optionMeanings: 把 checkpoint 当成全局恢复边界
把故障恢复误解成节能策略
把单点故障误解成集群级故障
把 Flink 的恢复策略归因给 Kafka
optionMeanings_en: The checkpoint is the global recovery boundary.
It mistakes failure recovery for a power-saving policy.
It assumes one worker failure implies a cluster-wide failure.
It attributes Flink recovery behavior to Kafka.
optionDirectness: 适合有状态作业要从同一快照恢复时。
只有讨论空闲资源节能时才相关。
只有有共同依赖或机房故障证据时才可能。
只有 Kafka 协议规则本身约束消费者时才成立。
optionDirectness_en: Use this when stateful tasks must restore from one snapshot.
Power saving is relevant only for idle-resource policies.
This fits only with evidence of a shared dependency or site failure.
This would fit only if Kafka protocol rules forced the consumer behavior.
optionScenarioImpacts: 所有 task 停在同一边界，避免新旧状态混跑。
会忽略真正风险：状态和输入位点不一致。
会把恢复范围误判成硬件排障。
会混淆数据源日志和 Flink 作业状态。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: All tasks stop at one boundary, avoiding mixed old and new state.
It misses the real risk: state and input positions diverging.
It turns a recovery decision into hardware troubleshooting.
It confuses the source log with Flink's job state.
why: Flink 的 checkpoint 是全局一致边界；TaskManager 挂后，健康任务如果继续推进，就会和失败分支落在不同输入位点。暂停全作业再一起回滚，牺牲恢复期可用性，换来状态和 source offset 对齐。
why_en: Flink checkpoints are global consistency boundaries, so a failed TaskManager pauses every task and rolls back together instead of letting healthy tasks outrun the failed branch.
whenOtherWins: 如果作业完全无状态且允许重复或乱序处理，局部继续可能更便宜，但这不再是 Flink checkpoint 恢复语义。
tradeoff: 全局一致恢复 vs 健康任务继续处理的可用性

q: 「source 回退到 checkpoint 位点」对 Kafka source 提出了什么要求？
q_en: What requirement does source rollback to a checkpoint place on a Kafka source?
options: 要求 Kafka topic 从此以后只能有一个分区
要求整个链路必须启用 Kafka 的事务功能
要求 topic 保留期够长，能覆盖回退到 checkpoint offset

It requires enabling Kafka transactions across the whole pipeline.
It requires retention long enough to still cover rewinding to the checkpointed offset.
It requires the consumer group's group id to be recreated every time.
optionMeanings: 单分区误解

retention 覆盖 offset

optionMeanings_en: It requires the Kafka topic to have only a single partition from then on.
It requires enabling Kafka transactions across the whole pipeline.
It requires retention long enough to still cover rewinding to the checkpointed offset.
It requires the consumer group's group id to be recreated every time.
why: 恢复时 Kafka 消费者要回到 checkpoint 时的 offset 重放数据；retention 太短、数据被清理，就回不去了。
why_en: Rewinding requires the Kafka topic to retain enough data to replay from the checkpointed offset.

options: 覆盖一切，包括第三方 API 调用产生的副作用

q: 事件时间（event time）与处理时间（processing time）的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between event time and processing time?
options: 事件时间是事件发生时刻；处理时间是系统处理它的机器时钟
两者在任何情况下都必然永远相等
处理时间算出来的结果天然会更准确
事件时间完全由 sink 一侧决定，与 source 无关
options_en: Event time is when the event happened; processing time is the machine clock when the system handles it.
The two are always necessarily equal under every circumstance.
Results computed by processing time are inherently more accurate.
Event time is entirely decided on the sink side, unrelated to the source.
optionMeanings: 事件发生时 vs 处理时
二者永远相等误解
处理时间更准误解
sink 决定事件时间误解
optionMeanings_en: Event time is when the event happened; processing time is the machine clock when the system handles it.
The two are always necessarily equal under every circumstance.
Results computed by processing time are inherently more accurate.
Event time is entirely decided on the sink side, unrelated to the source.
why: 乱序与延迟让两个时间域必然分叉：按事件时间算才能得到业务正确的窗口结果，watermark 就是事件时间的推进器。
why_en: Event time is when the event actually happened while processing time is when the system handles it, and separating the two domains is a key Flink pattern.
tradeoff: 事件时间的业务正确性 vs 处理时间的实现简单

q: 即使不用 Flink，也能借鉴它的哪些设计经验？（多选）
q_en: Which Flink design lessons are useful even when you do not use Flink?
options: 分离处理时间与事件时间；用 watermark 跟踪乱序事件流的进度
本地状态 + checkpoint 的状态管理模式，可迁移到其它有状态分布式系统
slot 式的资源隔离与共享
任何系统都应默认内置 CEP 引擎
options_en: Separate processing time from event time, and use watermarks to track progress through out-of-order events.
The local-state-plus-checkpoint pattern, transferable to other stateful distributed systems.
Slot-style resource isolation and sharing.
Every system should ship a built-in CEP engine by default.
optionMeanings: 时间域分离 + watermark
本地状态 + checkpoint
slot 资源模型
默认 CEP 误解
optionMeanings_en: Separate processing time from event time, and use watermarks to track progress through out-of-order events.
The local-state-plus-checkpoint pattern, transferable to other stateful distributed systems.
Slot-style resource isolation and sharing.

why: 时间域分离、watermark 进度跟踪、状态管理模式、exactly-once 技术、slot 资源隔离——这五条是 Flink 给分布式系统设计的「北极星」。
why_en: Flink teaches separating time domains, watermark-based progress tracking, local state with checkpointing, and slot-based resource isolation.

q: 把「为什么选 Flink」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the "why choose Flink" decision chain in the correct order:
steps: 选型：Apache Flink（托管状态 + checkpoint + watermark）
代价：集群部署/监控/扩缩容的运维负担与复杂度
需求：对连续数据做有状态的实时处理（窗口聚合、乱序处理、故障不丢状态）
缓解：确认真的需要实时；简单变换退回普通消费服务，必要时用托管服务
why: 需求（有状态实时）→ 选型（Flink）→ 代价（运维复杂度）→ 缓解（先质疑实时性、能简则简）。
why_en: Stateful real-time needs lead to Flink, whose operational complexity is mitigated by questioning real-time requirements and keeping simple paths simple.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是无状态逐条转换，普通 Kafka consumer 更轻；如果只是日级报表，批处理更省。
tradeoff: Flink 的有状态实时能力 vs 普通消费服务/批处理的低复杂度

scenario: 欺诈检测里，交易流需要补上账户信息（enrichment）后再判断。账户信息本身也是一条流。
scenario_en: In fraud detection, the transaction stream needs account information enrichment before evaluation, and account information is also a stream.
q: Flink 中最直接的做法是？
q_en: What is the most direct Flink approach here?
options: 每笔交易都同步发起一次账户服务的 API 调用
两条流按 accountId keyBy 后 connect，状态化补全
把整张账户表直接广播发送给所有客户端节点
干脆放弃补全，只依赖交易自身携带的字段
options_en: Synchronously call the account service's API for every single transaction.
Key both streams by account id, connect them, and enrich statefully.
Broadcast the entire account table out to every client node.
Just skip enrichment and rely only on fields the transaction already carries.
optionMeanings: 逐条同步 API
按 accountId connect 双流
广播账户表给客户端
不做 enrichment
optionMeanings_en: Synchronously call the account service's API for every single transaction.
Key both streams by account id, connect them, and enrich statefully.
Broadcast the entire account table out to every client node.

why: 双流按同键 connect + 状态化 process 是流内 enrichment 的标准手法，避免了对外部服务的逐条同步调用。

whenOtherWins: 账户数据极小且几乎不变时，作为静态维表加载或广播反而更简单。
tradeoff: 流内 connect 补全的低延迟 vs 同步 API 调用的简单直接

q: 把比赛事件随机分发到多台队列服务器上，会出什么问题？
q_en: What goes wrong if match events are randomly spread across queue servers?
options: 事件乱序：进球出现在开赛之前、球员为还没发生的犯规吃牌
整体吞吐反而下降，因为分区数变多需要重新协调

why: 队列各自独立消费，跨队列没有全局顺序：随机打散后同一场比赛的事件先后不可控——这正是要按实体分区的原因。
why_en: Randomly spreading events across queues destroys ordering, so a goal could appear before kickoff, which is exactly why related events must share one partition.

scenario: 1000 场比赛同时进行，事件量远超单机队列，但每场比赛内部的事件必须严格按发生顺序处理。
scenario_en: One thousand matches are live at once, traffic is beyond one queue server, and each match's events must stay in order.
q: 该怎么切分数据到多台队列服务器？
q_en: How should the data be split across queue servers?
options: 轮询平均分发到所有服务器，不管消息之间有没有关联
按比赛 ID 作为 key 分区：同一场比赛的事件永远进同一个分区
按事件到达的时间戳切片，假设同一时间段的事件天然相关
按事件类型（进球/黄牌）分流到不同服务器，假设同类事件该合并处理
why: Kafka 的根本思想之一：消息按分区策略分布，同 key 落同分区，分区内天然有序——既扩容又保序。
why_en: Partitioning by game ID keeps every event for one game in the same partition, preserving order while still scaling out.
whenOtherWins: 如果事件之间根本没有顺序依赖（纯统计计数），不带 key 随机分发反而分布最均匀。
tradeoff: 按 key 分区保住实体内顺序 vs 轮询/无 key 分发换来更均匀的负载

q: 补全常见的复制配置：
q_en: Fill in the common replication setup:
text: 复制因子（replication factor）为 {{3}} 是常见配置：每个分区共 3 个副本 = {{1}} 个 leader + {{2}} 个 follower；一台 broker 挂掉，数据仍在另外两台上。
why: RF=3 是耐用性和成本的常见平衡点：单 broker 故障后仍有两份数据，可以立刻提升一个 follower 顶上。
why_en: A replication factor of three means one leader plus two followers, so data survives a single broker failure and a follower can be promoted right away.

scenario: 业务要求多个 region 同时接受写入，并尽量本地低延迟提交。
q: 为什么普通 Postgres 不是天然强项？
options: Postgres 不能部署到云上

Postgres replica 不能读
Postgres 不支持任何事务
why: Postgres 可做跨 region 复制，但真正 active-active 多主会带来一致性和冲突解决问题。需要全球 ACID 可考虑 CockroachDB，最终一致可考虑 Cassandra/DynamoDB。

whenOtherWins: 如果写入可以集中在一个 primary region，其他 region 读 replica，Postgres 跨 region 部署仍可行。
options_en: Postgres cannot be deployed to the cloud.
Cross-region synchronous replication is slow and conflicts are hard to resolve.
A Postgres replica cannot serve reads.
Postgres does not support transactions at all.

scenario: 访问模式只是按 key 存取 value，没有 join、复杂 query、外键或事务需求。

why: Postgres 能做 key-value，但如果真的只需要简单 key lookup，Redis/DynamoDB/Cassandra 可能更轻或更易扩展。选型要匹配访问模式。
why_en: For truly simple key-value access, Postgres can be overkill because its transactional and query machinery adds unnecessary overhead.
whenOtherWins: 如果 key-value 数据还需要 SQL 查询、事务、关系约束或与其他表 join，Postgres 仍有价值。
options_en: Postgres cannot query by key.
Key-value workloads must use a relational database.
Redis cannot do any key-value work.
MVCC, WAL, and the query planner add overhead you do not need.

q: “NoSQL scales better, 所以不用 PostgreSQL”这句话的问题是什么？

q: Postgres durability 主要靠什么机制保证？

options_en: Relying only on the application's in-memory cache.
Relying entirely on the client to retry on its own.
WAL: flush the log first, so a crash can be recovered by replay.
Claiming it never needs to write to disk at all.

q: 在 latitude(纬度)一列上建 B-tree 索引,再查"2 公里内的司机",会取回什么?

q: 贯穿所有空间索引的统一思想是什么?

q: 空间树路线在"写入"上的软肋具体是什么?
q_en: What exactly is the write-side weakness of the spatial-tree route?
options: 写入操作会把整张表直接全部锁住
R-tree 重平衡矩形,BKD 批量重建
空间树的索引结构完全不支持删除
写入必须一条一条严格串行处理
why: 这就是"司机每秒动一次"的数据不该进空间树的原因:R-tree 每次更新要维护矩形嵌套,BKD 则要整批重建。
why_en: Rebalancing R-tree rectangles is real work and the BKD variant is essentially write-once, so neither loves churning data.
options_en: Writes end up locking the entire table completely.
R-tree rebalances rectangles; BKD rebuilds in batch.
Spatial tree indexes completely lack delete support.
Writes have to be processed one at a time, strictly serial.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把点打包进磁盘页大小的块、一次性批量构建的磁盘友好 k-d 树变体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BKD tree packs points into disk-page-sized blocks and is built once from a batch, making it disk friendly but essentially write-once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个搜索引擎,geo 字段底层用 BKD 树索引位置数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search engine whose geo fields are indexed with BKD trees.

scenario: 数据几乎全是持续移动的点:司机、用户设备、实时位置;写入洪流巨大,查询是"我附近有谁";多边形运算完全不需要。
scenario_en: The data is almost all continuously moving points: drivers, user devices, and real-time locations; writes are huge, queries ask "who is near me," and polygon math is unnecessary.
q: 选型与代价是?
q_en: What is the choice and its cost?
options: 编码格子(落普通索引):写廉价,但基本只懂点
PostGIS 加 GiST 空间扩展
每个城市各建一棵内存 k-d 树
全表扫描,外面再套一层缓存
why: 移动点要的是廉价写+快速候选生成,编码格子恰好只卖这两样;失去的多边形能力本来也用不上。
why_en: Encoded cells turn each driver move into a single integer update and scale to millions of writes per second, at the price of point-only data and ring queries.
whenOtherWins: 一旦需要"配送区是否包含该地址"这类几何判断,就必须引入空间树;两者可以并存、各管一摊。
options_en: Encoded cells on an ordinary index: cheap writes, but mostly limited to points.
PostGIS with the GiST spatial extension.
A separate in-memory k-d tree for every city.
A full table scan with a cache layered on top.
tradeoff: 编码键:廉价写、快速候选、只懂点 vs 空间树:几何语义、写更贵

text: 形状用{{空间树}},移动点用{{编码 cell}},并且永远、永远{{后过滤}}。

判断数据的形状:是多边形/道路等几何体,还是高频移动的点

q: 这个量级最支持下面哪条设计判断?
q_en: Which design judgment does this scale fact support?
options: 全球尺度该换 S2/H3 球面网格,而非平面 geohash
只要把 geohash 的精度多加几位字符就够
高纬度地区可以直接跳过索引,全表扫描兜底
这个数字只影响地图渲染效果,不影响索引选型
why: 111 公里到 0 的收缩说明同一级 geohash 格子在赤道是胖方块、在高纬是细长条,面积不一致会让候选集在不同纬度表现完全不同。要在全球尺度保持一致,必须换成 S2/H3 这类尊重球面的编码。
why_en: Longitude spans about 111km at the equator but shrinks toward zero at the poles, so flat geohash cells get uneven — that pushes global-scale indexes toward S2 or H3.
scenario: 地图服务要在伦敦、新加坡、雷克雅未克等不同纬度的城市统一做同城 5 公里邻近召回;已知一度经度的地面距离在赤道约 111 公里,向两极收缩趋近于 0。

Just add a few more characters to the geohash precision.
Skip indexing entirely at high latitudes and fall back to a full scan.

q: 关于各方案的 ID 位数,哪组数字正确?

options: geohash 每字符是 8 bit,S2 与 H3 都用 32 位 ID

q: 如果省略"精确距离后过滤"这一步,会出什么错?

q: 这个 fsync 频率的量级最支持哪条设计判断？

只要打开了 AOF 就等于零丢失，不需要额外设计

scenario: 你想要 Redis 的数据结构和接口，但它不只是缓存：已确认写入必须持久，failover 后也不能丢。
q: 最合适的选择是？
options: 开源 Redis 默认配置：最快，但确认写可能仍有丢失窗口

flowchart LR

MemoryDB 用 Redis 接口，但把自己当持久主库。

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS MemoryDB：兼容 Redis/Valkey API 的内存主数据库，成功写入会进入 Multi-AZ log。

termDefinitions.meaning: 读 primary 可以拿到最新成功写入，适合需要强一致的读取。

q_en: Given this requirement, what's the best choice?

q: 这个「槽数量在集群运行期间固定」的设计，最支持哪个判断？
options: 扩缩容 = 重新分配槽归属哪个节点，而不是重新对所有 key 哈希
每加一个节点，哈希函数本身都要跟着重新调整算法
槽的总数必须精确等于集群里的节点数量
槽总数会随着集群规模自动增加或减少
why: 槽数固定意味着扩缩容只是把一部分槽（连同其中的 key）挪给新节点，客户端和哈希函数完全不用变。
why_en: Because the slot count is fixed, scaling only reassigns which node owns a share of the slots, leaving the hash function and clients untouched.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["key"] --> B["CRC16"]
  B --> C["slot 0..16383"]
  C --> D["owning node"]
scenario: Redis Cluster 把整个 key 空间预先切成固定数量的哈希槽，加/减节点只是重新分配槽的归属，不重新计算哈希。
options_en: Scaling means reassigning which node owns which slots, not rehashing every key
Adding a node forces you to re-tune the hash function's algorithm itself

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希槽：Redis Cluster 把 key 空间切成的固定分片单位，每个槽归属一个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash slot is a fixed sharding unit that Redis Cluster splits the key space into, with each slot owned by one node.

q_en: Which conclusion does the fixed slot count during cluster operation best support?
scenario_en: Redis Cluster pre-splits the entire key space into a fixed number of hash slots; adding or removing nodes only reassigns which node owns which slots, without rehashing.

q: Redis Cluster 客户端如何找到 key 所在的节点？
options: 随便连一个节点，由它读懂请求内容后代为转发

客户端本地缓存 slot→node 映射，从 key 算出槽后直连目标节点
把每个请求广播到集群里所有节点，取第一个响应
why: 客户端把槽位表当电话簿：从 key 算槽、查本地映射、第一跳就打到正确节点；Redis 节点不会替你转发请求。
why_en: Clients cache the slot-to-node map, compute the slot from the key, and connect directly to the owning node because Redis will not forward requests.
options_en: Connect to any node and have it read the request and forward it on your behalf
Ask a separate external configuration-center service before every operation
Cache the slot-to-node map locally, compute the slot from the key, and connect directly to the owning node

It replies MOVED pointing at the right node, and the client refreshes its slot map and retries

q: Redis 主从复制的确认时序是？

q: 主节点崩溃、副本被提升后，最典型的数据后果是？

termDefinitions.meaning: Redlock：向多个独立 Redis 节点分别请求锁、拿到多数即算持有的算法。

q_en: What is the core idea behind the Redlock algorithm?

q: Kleppmann 对 Redlock 的著名批评指出：即使算法成立，仍会发生什么？
options: N 个节点里多数派永远无法达成，算法根本跑不起来
所有参与节点的时钟必须做到精确同步
客户端 GC 暂停或卡顿后，会拿着已经过期的锁继续操作
获取锁的吞吐量在多节点方案下太低，扛不住并发
why: 进程暂停、GC、网络延迟都可能让客户端在锁过期后才恢复动作——它自己不知道锁已易主，Redis 也拦不住它。
why_en: A paused or slow client can resume work after its lock already expired, and nothing in Redis stops it from acting.
options_en: A majority of the N nodes can never be reached, so the algorithm cannot even run
Every participating node's clock must be kept in perfect sync
A paused or slow client can resume acting after its lock has already expired
The lock's acquisition throughput is too low across multiple nodes to handle real concurrency

q: 防止「过期锁的持有者继续写坏数据」的标准手段是？
options: 让持有者每隔几秒就主动给锁续租延长时限

why: 递增的 fencing token 由存储层校验，旧持有者的写会被拒绝；Redis 本身没有内建这个机制。
why_en: A fencing token is an increasing number issued with each lock grant that the storage layer uses to reject stale writers, and Redis has nothing built in for it.
options_en: Have the holder proactively renew the lock's lease every few seconds to extend it
Just brute-force the lock's TTL to ten times longer as a safety net
Acquire two mutually independent locks at once as a double safeguard

scenario: 对每个 API key 做固定窗口限流：窗口内最多 N 次请求，超出返回 429 并带 Retry-After 头。

q: 补全 Stream 工作队列的命令分工：
text: 生产者用 {{XADD}} 追加条目；工作者通过消费组用 {{XREADGROUP}} 领取条目；超时未确认的条目可被其他工作者用 {{XCLAIM}}（或 XAUTOCLAIM）抢过来重做。

XGROUP CREATE jobs workers $ MKSTREAM
XADD jobs * kind email user 42
XREADGROUP GROUP workers worker-1 COUNT 1 STREAMS jobs >
# worker-1 dies before XACK; entry stays in PEL
XCLAIM jobs workers worker-2 60000 {entry-id}
XAUTOCLAIM jobs workers worker-2 60000 0-0 COUNT 10
XACK jobs workers {entry-id}

termDefinitions.meaning: XAUTOCLAIM：从某个起点开始扫描，并批量接管 idle 超时的 pending 条目。

idle 超时后，用 XCLAIM 转给其他 worker 重做
主节点重新广播任务，让所有 worker 抢处理
why: 未 XACK 的条目会留在 PEL，记录 owner 和 idle。idle 超阈值后，其他 worker 用 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管并重做。
why_en: Unacknowledged stream entries stay in the PEL, so another worker can claim an idle entry with XCLAIM or XAUTOCLAIM and retry it.
tradeoff: 故障恢复与至少一次处理 vs 重复执行风险
whenOtherWins: 若任务不能重复执行，业务层要加去重键或状态机；Redis 重新交付，但不保证只执行一次。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P[Producer XADD] --> S[(Redis Stream)]
    S --> G[Consumer group]
    G --> W1[worker1 XREADGROUP]
    W1 --> PEL[PEL: delivered, not XACKed]
    W1 -. crashes .-> PEL
    PEL -- idle exceeds threshold --> W2[worker2 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM]
    W2 --> R[redo work]
    R --> A[XACK removes from PEL]

rows: 其他 worker 发现超时

optionMeanings: 认为 worker 死亡会让任务消失。
认为 Redis 会管理你的 worker 进程。

Assumes Redis rebroadcasts the task.

Redis stores data; it does not restart app processes.
After the idle timeout, the task can be claimed and retried.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Streams：Redis 里的追加式消息日志，可用来做轻量工作队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Streams is an append-only message log in Redis that can act as a lightweight work queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: XREADGROUP：消费组里的 worker 用它领取还没分配的新任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XREADGROUP lets a worker read entries through a Redis consumer group.

termDefinitions.meaning: XACK：worker 处理成功后确认任务完成，并把条目移出 PEL。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK acknowledges that a stream entry was processed and removes it from the PEL.

termDefinitions.meaning: Pending Entries List（PEL）：记录已交付但还没有 XACK 的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Pending Entries List tracks entries that were delivered but not yet acknowledged.

termDefinitions.meaning: idle time：一条 pending 任务距离上次交付或认领已经过去多久。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idle time is how long a pending entry has gone without being claimed or acknowledged.

termDefinitions.meaning: XCLAIM：把超时未确认的 pending 条目改交给另一个 worker。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XCLAIM transfers a stale pending stream entry to another worker.

termDefinitions.meaning: XAUTOCLAIM：批量扫描并接管 idle 超时的 pending 条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XAUTOCLAIM scans and claims pending entries that have been idle too long.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一任务重复执行，最终结果仍然像执行一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means repeating the same job leaves the system in the same final state.

q_en: In a Redis Streams work queue, how does an unacknowledged task recover after the worker that claimed it crashes?
scenario_en: A producer writes tasks with XADD and workers claim them with XREADGROUP; a task only counts as done once it's processed successfully and XACKed.

q: XCLAIM 接管机制带来的副作用是？
options: 同一条目可能被处理两次——Redis 分不清「慢」和「死」，处理逻辑必须幂等
超时的条目会被 Redis 静默丢弃，不再投递
整个消费组的消费顺序会被完全打乱
接管机制强制一个消费组只能有一个 worker
why: 慢 worker 没死却被判超时的话，条目会被第二个 worker 重做——这是 at-least-once 语义，幂等是消费端的义务。
why_en: Redis cannot tell a slow worker from a dead one, so an entry can occasionally be processed twice and your handler must be idempotent.
options_en: An entry can be processed twice, since Redis cannot tell slow from dead, so handlers must be idempotent
A timed-out entry gets silently dropped by Redis and never redelivered
The entire consumer group's processing order gets completely scrambled
The takeover mechanism forces a consumer group to have only one worker

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一个操作重复执行多次，结果和只执行一次一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means running the same operation multiple times produces the same result as running it once.

q_en: What side effect comes from the XCLAIM takeover mechanism?

q: 把 Stream 当「可靠日志」用之前必须记住什么？
options: 条目的持久性只取决于你的 RDB/AOF 配置——默认下崩溃可能丢最近的条目
Stream 的写入总是同步落盘，绝不会丢失数据
Stream 会自动把条目复制一份镜像到 Kafka 集群
Stream 里写入的条目永远不可以被删除
why: Stream 再像日志，也逃不过 Redis 的持久化取舍：默认配置下崩溃丢最近写入——和页首的 durability 警告是同一件事。
why_en: Stream entries are only as durable as your persistence settings, so with defaults a crash can lose recent entries.
options_en: Entry durability depends entirely on your RDB/AOF settings, and a crash can lose recent entries under defaults
Stream writes are always synchronously flushed to disk and never lost
Streams automatically mirror a copy of every entry into a Kafka cluster
Once written, entries in a stream can never be deleted
q_en: What must you remember before treating a Stream as a 'reliable log'?
optionMeanings: Stream 的持久性和其它 key 一样，逃不开 RDB/AOF 的取舍。
同步落盘会拖慢每次写入，Redis 默认并不这样做。
Redis 没有内建到 Kafka 的自动镜像功能。
XDEL/XTRIM 都能删除 Stream 里的条目。

q: 什么时候该把 Redis Streams 换成 Kafka？
options: 只要队列规模比较小，就应该马上换掉
只要系统里已经部署了 Redis，就该顺便换掉
只要用到了消费组（consumer group）机制就该换
需要长期保留、多个独立消费者重放、以及一条都不能丢的持久有序吞吐时
why: Streams 适合已有 Redis、队列规模不大的场景（后台任务、通知扇出、工作分发）；长保留 + 重放 + 不可丢消息才值得付 Kafka 的运维成本。
why_en: Kafka earns its complexity when you need long retention, replay for many independent consumers, and durable ordered throughput where losing a message is unacceptable.
scenario: 你的设计已经在用 Redis Streams 做工作队列（后台任务、通知扇出），眼下数据量和独立消费者的数量都在持续增长。
options_en: You should switch the moment the queue is even moderately small
As soon as Redis happens to already be deployed in the system
As soon as you touch the consumer-group mechanism at all
When you need long retention, replay for many independent consumers, and durable ordered throughput where losing a message is unacceptable
tradeoff: 留在 Redis Streams 的低运维成本 vs 换 Kafka 换来的长保留与可靠重放
q_en: When should you switch from Redis Streams to Kafka?
scenario_en: Your design already uses Redis Streams as a work queue (background jobs, notification fan-out), and both data volume and the number of independent consumers keep growing.

q: Pub/Sub 和 Streams 的分工，一句话是？
options: Pub/Sub 会把消息持久化落盘，Streams 反而不落盘
Streams 服务「需要补课的消费者」；Pub/Sub 只投递给「此刻在线的听众」
两者的投递语义和可靠性完全等价，可以互换
Pub/Sub 天生持久可靠，更适合做工作队列
why: Streams 有历史可回读；Pub/Sub 即发即失、离线就错过——按「消费者要不要追赶历史」来选。
why_en: Streams serve consumers that must catch up on missed entries, while Pub/Sub only delivers to whoever is listening right now.
options_en: Pub/Sub persists messages to disk while Streams, oddly, does not
Streams serve consumers who need to catch up on history; Pub/Sub only delivers to whoever is listening right now
The two have fully equivalent delivery semantics and reliability, interchangeably
Pub/Sub is inherently durable and reliable, making it the better fit for work queues
tradeoff: Streams 的可回读历史 vs Pub/Sub 的即发即失
q_en: In one line, how do Pub/Sub and Streams divide responsibilities?

q: Redis Pub/Sub 的投递语义是？
options: 恰好一次投递，Redis 会去重保证不重不漏
至少一次投递，离线消息会重试到送达为止
至多一次：订阅者离线期间发布的消息永久错过
带事务性保证的投递，要么全送达要么全不送
why: 消息不落盘、不可重放：连接断开或不在线就收不到，这就是 at-most-once。
why_en: Redis Pub/Sub is at-most-once delivery, so a subscriber offline at publish time misses the message entirely.
options_en: Exactly-once delivery, with Redis deduplicating so nothing repeats or is missed
At-least-once delivery, retrying offline messages until they land
At-most-once: a subscriber offline at publish time permanently misses the message
Transactional delivery guarantees where messages either all arrive or none do
q_en: What are Redis Pub/Sub's delivery semantics?

q: 「集群 Pub/Sub 加节点不加容量」这个老印象，现在的事实是？
options: Redis 7 起的 sharded Pub/Sub 把频道按槽路由到分片，容量随集群扩展
这个限制至今仍然如此，Redis 团队从未改变过这个行为
Pub/Sub 这整个功能后来的版本已经被完全移除
只有付费的商业版 Redis Enterprise 才彻底解决了这个问题
why: 经典模式确实把每条消息广播到所有节点；Redis 7 的分片 Pub/Sub 让频道像 key 一样哈希到槽，扩节点就扩容量。
why_en: Since Redis 7, sharded Pub/Sub routes each channel to the shard owning its slot, so capacity scales with the cluster.
options_en: Since Redis 7, sharded Pub/Sub routes channels to shards by slot, so capacity scales with the cluster
That limitation still holds today; the Redis team has never changed this behavior
The entire Pub/Sub feature was removed completely in a later version
Only the paid Redis Enterprise commercial edition fully solved this
codeSample:
SSUBSCRIBE orders.123    # 按槽路由到拥有该频道的分片
SPUBLISH orders.123 msg  # 只广播给该分片上的订阅者

termDefinitions.meaning: SPUBLISH：分片 Pub/Sub 的发布命令，只把消息发给拥有该频道槽位的分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SPUBLISH is the sharded Pub/Sub publish command, sending a message only to the shard that owns the channel's slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSUBSCRIBE：分片 Pub/Sub 的订阅命令，像 key 一样把频道哈希到槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSUBSCRIBE is the sharded Pub/Sub subscribe command, hashing the channel to a slot just like a key.

q_en: The old assumption is 'adding cluster nodes doesn't add Pub/Sub capacity' — what's actually true now?

q: 使用一个 Pub/Sub 频道之前需要什么创建或配置步骤？
options: 执行 CREATE CHANNEL 命令
在 CONFIG SET 里注册频道
先创建一个 consumer group
什么都不用：有人发布或订阅这个名字，频道就存在了
why: 频道只是个名字：发布者往这个名字上发、订阅者在这个名字上听，不需要任何预先创建。
why_en: A channel is just a name that comes into existence when someone publishes or subscribes; there is nothing to create.
options_en: Run a CREATE CHANNEL command
Register the channel via CONFIG SET
First create a consumer group for it
Nothing: the channel exists the moment someone publishes or subscribes to that name
q_en: What setup or creation step do you need before using a Pub/Sub channel?

q: 一台订阅了 100 万个频道的服务器，需要多少条到 Redis 的连接？
options: 为每个频道单独开一条独立的 TCP 连接，总共 100 万条
严格按每个频道一条连接来计算连接开销
每个持有相关槽位的节点一条——连接开销按节点算，不按频道算
至少要开 16,384 条连接，正好对应哈希槽的数量
why: 一条到节点的连接承载它订阅的所有频道；sharded Pub/Sub 下只需连「拥有你频道槽位」的那几个节点。
why_en: A subscriber holds one connection per node, not per channel, and that single connection carries all its subscribed channels.
options_en: Open one dedicated TCP connection per channel, a million separate connections in total
Overhead is counted strictly at one connection per channel, regardless of node
One connection per node holding the relevant slots — the overhead scales with nodes, not channels
At least 16,384 connections, exactly matching the hash slot count
q_en: How many connections to Redis does a server subscribed to one million channels need?
optionMeanings: TCP 连接是有状态的传输层连接，为每个频道各开一条既昂贵又没必要。
把开销和频道数挂钩，忽略了一条连接能承载该节点的全部频道。
正确答案：开销只和节点数相关。
16,384 是槽数量，和需要的连接数无必然关系。

scenario: 聊天系统用 Pub/Sub 做实时投递，但产品要求用户重新上线后能补看离线期间错过的消息。
q: 正确的补法是？
options: 只是把 Pub/Sub 内部的消息缓冲区调得更大一些而已
想尽各种办法保证客户端的连接永远都不会意外断开或掉线
把全部实时投递流程都直接改成客户端定时轮询查询
Pub/Sub 之外再落一份可回放存储：Streams、Kafka/SQS 或 outbox 表
why: Pub/Sub 天生不持久，离线补课必须有一条持久化路径——Streams、消息队列或 outbox 表都行。
why_en: Pair Pub/Sub with a durable replayable path such as Redis Streams, a queue, or an outbox table so offline consumers can catch up.
whenOtherWins: 若消息只对「此刻在场」的人有意义（光标位置、正在输入提示），纯 Pub/Sub 反而是最省的正确答案。
options_en: Just make Pub/Sub's internal message buffer even bigger, nothing else
Find every possible way to guarantee client connections never accidentally drop or disconnect
Replace the entire real-time delivery flow directly with client-side timed polling
Pair Pub/Sub with a replayable store: Streams, Kafka or SQS, or an outbox table
tradeoff: Pub/Sub 的即时低延迟 vs 落一份可回放存储换来的离线补课能力

termDefinitions.meaning: outbox 模式：把要发的消息先写进数据库表，再由后台进程读出并投递，保证不丢消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The outbox pattern writes outgoing messages to a database table first, then a background process delivers them, guaranteeing none are lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS（Simple Queue Service）：AWS 的托管消息队列服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, or Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed message queue.

q_en: What's the correct fix?
scenario_en: A chat system uses Pub/Sub for real-time delivery, but product requires that users coming back online can catch up on messages they missed while offline.
optionMeanings: 缓冲区调大也留不住离线期间的消息，Pub/Sub 本质不持久化。
网络必然会断，「永不断线」不是可依赖的工程假设。
纯轮询能补历史，但延迟高、浪费资源，不如加一条持久通道。
Streams/Kafka/outbox 都能让离线用户回放错过的消息。

q: 「自制 Pub/Sub」（Redis 里存 topic → 订阅者地址集合，发布者自己逐个直发）相比原生 Pub/Sub 的缺点有哪些？（多选）
options: 网络跳数从 2 跳变成 3 跳
要给每个订阅者服务器现建 TCP 连接，最后一跳最贵
订阅者宕机后要靠心跳/TTL 清理注册表，复杂且啰嗦
发布的消息体大小会受到限制
why: 原生 Pub/Sub 复用已建立的长连接、两跳送达，频道没人订阅时自动消失；自制方案多一跳、连接冷启动，还得自己管注册表的生命周期。
why_en: The homegrown version adds a network hop, pays for new TCP connections to each subscriber, and needs heartbeats to clean up dead servers, unlike native Pub/Sub.
options_en: The network hop count goes from two hops to three
It must establish a fresh TCP connection to each subscriber server, and that last hop is the most expensive
A dead subscriber needs heartbeats or a TTL to clean up the registry, which is complex and chatty
The published message body size becomes limited

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP（传输控制协议）：建立连接后可靠传输字节流的协议，新建连接有握手开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP, or Transmission Control Protocol, is a connection-based reliable byte-stream protocol whose handshake adds setup cost.

q_en: Compared to native Pub/Sub, what are the drawbacks of a homegrown Pub/Sub built on Redis (storing topic-to-subscriber-address sets, with the publisher fanning out directly)? (multi-select)
optionMeanings: 自制方案多了一跳：发布者→Redis 注册表→目标服务器。
新建 TCP 连接有握手开销，原生 Pub/Sub 复用长连接没有这一跳。
注册表活性靠心跳/TTL 自己维护，原生频道靠订阅本身自动生死。
两种方案对消息体大小的限制其实差不多，不是自制方案独有的缺点。

q: 原生 Pub/Sub 里，一个频道的最后一个订阅者断开后会发生什么？
options: 频道会在内存里继续保留 24 小时才清理
频道从内存移除，之后对它的 publish 直接被丢弃
没有订阅者时，消息会开始堆积排队等待
publish 会向发布者返回一个错误提示
why: Redis 只为有活跃订阅者的频道占内存；没人听的频道就不存在，发了也就丢了——零清理成本。
why_en: When the last subscriber disconnects the channel vanishes from memory and later publishes to it are simply dropped.
options_en: The channel stays reserved in memory for 24 hours before cleanup
The channel is removed from memory and later publishes to it are simply dropped
With no subscribers, messages start queuing up waiting to be read
The publish call returns an error back to the publisher
q_en: In native Pub/Sub, what happens when a channel's last subscriber disconnects?

q: 100 节点的 Redis 缓存集群，某个商品突然爆红、流量占到全站一半，会发生什么？
options: 集群检测到热点后会自动触发一次槽再均衡
这份流量会被所有 100 台节点平均分摊
Redis 检测到热点后自动把这个 key 复制到多个节点
拥有这个 key 的那台节点负载暴涨、开始失败，其余 99 台闲着
why: key 哈希决定归属：一个 key 只住一台节点，节点再多也分不走单 key 的流量——这就是 hot key 问题（Memcached、DynamoDB 同样有）。
why_en: A single hot key lives on one node, so that node melts while the other ninety-nine idle, a problem Memcached and DynamoDB share.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Hot key"] --> B["One slot node hot"]
  B --> C["Replicas or key copies"]
  C --> D["Fan out reads"]
options_en: The cluster detects the hot spot and automatically triggers a slot rebalance
That traffic gets evenly shared across all one hundred nodes
Redis detects the hot spot and automatically replicates this key across nodes
The one node owning this key sees load spike and starts failing while the other ninety-nine sit idle
q_en: In a 100-node Redis cache cluster, a single product suddenly goes viral and its traffic hits half the whole site — what happens?

scenario: 少数几个爆款商品被海量读取，可以容忍秒级陈旧，希望大部分读请求根本不打到 Redis。
q: 最合适的缓解是？
options: 应用服务器进程内缓存这几个最热 key（配短 TTL）
单纯加大拥有热 key 的那台 Redis 节点的内存
把持久化模式从 RDB 换成 AOF
把集群的哈希槽总数从 16384 再调大
why: 客户端缓存把热读挡在应用层；代价是又多一层要保新鲜的缓存，所以只对小规模热 key 配短 TTL 使用。
why_en: Client-side caching keeps most hot reads from ever reaching Redis, at the cost of one more cache to keep coherent with short TTLs.
whenOtherWins: 业务不容忍任何陈旧（如库存扣减）、或热点又多又散时，客户端缓存不合适——考虑副本读或 key 副本。
options_en: Cache the handful of hottest keys in-process on the app servers, with a short TTL
Just give the Redis node that owns the hot key more memory
Switch the persistence mode from RDB to AOF
Increase the cluster's total hash slot count beyond 16384
tradeoff: 客户端缓存挡住热读 vs 多一层要保鲜的缓存一致性负担
q_en: What's the best mitigation?
scenario_en: A handful of viral products get read at massive volume, second-level staleness is tolerable, and you want most reads to never hit Redis at all.

scenario: 一个读热 key 想横向摊到多台节点上，读方代码可以配合改造。
q: 「key 副本」方案怎么做？
options: 只是把 key 的名字改得更短一点，指望能减少内存占用
同一份数据存成 product:123:1..10 多个 key 散到不同槽，读者随机挑后缀读
用 hash tag 反而把这些数据副本全部绑到同一个槽上
打开集群自带的代理转发模式，指望它来分摊流量
why: 带不同后缀的 key 哈希到不同节点，读流量被随机打散；代价是每次写要扇出到所有副本，读者还得知道哪些 key 被复制过。
why_en: Storing copies under suffixed keys spreads them across nodes and readers pick a random suffix, while every write must fan out to all copies.
whenOtherWins: 写频繁的 key 不适合（写扇出放大）；那种情况优先在数据模型上拆分，或用副本读扛读热。
options_en: Just shorten the key's name a little, hoping that alone uses less memory
Store the data under suffixed keys like product:123:1 through 10 spread across slots, readers pick a random suffix
Use a hash tag to pin all of these data copies onto that very same slot instead

q: 用读副本（read replicas）抗热 key，面试官爱追问的两个坑是？

why_en: Replicas only absorb load if clients are configured for replica reads, and they do nothing for a write-hot key since writes still hit the one primary.

Replica nodes simply cannot be deployed to a different region or availability zone

The mere existence of multiple replicas directly causes cluster split-brain

q: 哪些信号说明这个场景不该用 Redis？（多选）
options: 数据是唯一的真相源，一条都不能丢
工作集大到放内存不经济

why_en: Avoid Redis as a system of record, for working sets too big for RAM, or when you need joins and cross-key queries; sub-millisecond reads are exactly why you would use it.

q: 集群模式下多 key 操作（MSET、含多个 key 的 MULTI）的限制是？

q: 什么时候该选择时间序列数据库（TSDB）？
q_en: When should you choose a time-series database (TSDB)?
options: 只要数据里有 timestamp 字段就必须用 TSDB
当业务需要强事务和复杂外键约束时
当通用数据库在高写入、时间范围查询、保留策略和压缩上出现真实瓶颈时
当核心需求是跨全部 series 做 Top-K 排序时
why: 决定性约束是通用数据库先撑不住高写入、时间范围查询或保留/压缩需求；仅有 timestamp 字段不构成理由。先用 Postgres/DynamoDB 顶，顶不住再上专用系统。
why_en: A time-series database is worth adopting once a general-purpose database genuinely bottlenecks on write volume, time-range queries, or retention, not just because the data happens to have a timestamp.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询核心是跨海量 series 的全局排序或强事务/复杂 join，Postgres/DynamoDB 等通用方案通常更直接。
tradeoff: 专用 TSDB 的写入/压缩优化 vs 通用数据库的事务与关系能力
options_en: Any time your data has a timestamp field, you must use a TSDB.
When the business needs strong transactions and complex foreign keys.

scenario_en: A cloud monitoring system has 100,000 servers, each reporting 5 metrics every 10 seconds, which is about 50,000 points per second and 4.3 billion points per day.
q: 这个写入量级对存储引擎的设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does this write scale imply for the storage engine design?
options: 这个量级下单机 Postgres 加两个索引就能长期稳定支撑，不需要改变写入方式
这个量级只影响读延迟，写入可以随意排队，不需要特别设计
这个量级下随机原地更新和逐行索引维护会撑不住，写路径必须转向顺序追加和批量整理
只要磁盘足够大，这个量级对存储引擎设计没有实质影响
why: 50,000 点/秒、一天 43 亿点意味着随机 I/O 和逐行索引会先被拖垮；这正是 append-only + LSM 这类设计存在的原因。
why_en: At roughly 50,000 points per second and 4.3 billion points a day, random I/O and per-row indexing become the bottleneck, which is exactly why append-only and LSM-style engines exist.
options_en: At this scale, a single Postgres instance with two indexes can support it indefinitely without changing how writes work.
At this scale, only read latency is affected, so writes can queue freely without special design.
At this scale, in-place random updates and per-row index maintenance can't keep up, so the write path must shift to sequential appends with batched reorganization.
As long as disks are big enough, this scale has no real effect on storage engine design.

q: 把大规模指标按 timestamp、host、metric_name、value 存到一张普通 Postgres 行式表，会先在哪里出问题？
q_en: Where does a normal Postgres row table first break down for large-scale metrics stored as timestamp, host, metric_name, and value?
options: 只要给 host 和 metric_name 分别建索引，就能同时保证写入吞吐和查询延迟
问题只出现在磁盘空间上，不会影响写入吞吐或查询延迟
标签字符串按行重复存储，加上高写入下的索引维护，会同时拖慢写入并膨胀存储
只要把 value 列类型换成 REAL 而不是 DOUBLE PRECISION 就能解决
why: 决定性约束是每行都重复存 host/metric_name 字符串，且高写入下索引维护很重；加索引或换数据类型都治标不治本。
why_en: The real bottleneck is repeated label strings in every row plus heavy index maintenance under high write volume, which indexing alone or a smaller numeric type can't fix.
options_en: Adding separate indexes on host and metric_name alone is enough to guarantee both write throughput and query latency.
The problem only shows up in disk space; it doesn't affect write throughput or query latency.
Repeating label strings in every row plus heavy index maintenance under high write volume slows writes and bloats storage at the same time.
Switching the value column from DOUBLE PRECISION to REAL is enough to fix it.
codeSample:
CREATE TABLE metrics (
  timestamp TIMESTAMP,
  host VARCHAR(255),
  metric_name VARCHAR(255),
  value DOUBLE PRECISION

q: Append-only（只追加写）存储的核心思想是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea of append-only storage?
options: 每次写入都先扫描全表
新数据总是追加到文件末尾，避免原地随机更新
只允许删除，不允许写入
每个指标都单独创建数据库
why: 追加写把昂贵的随机 I/O 转成顺序 I/O，特别适合大量持续写入的指标流。代价是之后需要靠 compaction/index 让读取仍然可接受。
why_en: Append-only storage writes new points at the end of files, turning random writes into fast sequential writes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Metric point"] --> B["Memory buffer"]
  B --> C["Append segment"]
  C --> D["Compact later"]
options_en: Every write first scans the entire table.
New data is always appended to the end of a file, avoiding in-place random updates.
Only deletes are allowed, no writes.
Each metric gets its own separate database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在文件末尾追加新数据，不做原地更新的写入方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Append-only storage always writes new data to the end of a file instead of updating in place.

q: 在磁盘 I/O 模式上，append-only 写入相比传统原地更新的优势是什么？
q_en: For disk I/O, what advantage does append-only writing have over traditional in-place updates?
options: 它让每次写入都必须先随机寻址到旧 block 再修改
它省去定位旧数据、读、改、写的步骤，只在文件尾部顺序追加
它保证所有查询都不必再使用任何索引
它只能在纯内存数据库里生效，磁盘数据库用不了
why: 原地更新要先定位旧位置再读改写，产生随机 I/O；append-only 只在文件尾追加，把随机变顺序，代价是空间需要靠后台整理回收。
why_en: In-place updates need to locate, read, modify, and rewrite old data, causing random I/O, while append-only writes sequentially at the end and reclaims space later via background compaction.
tradeoff: 顺序追加换取写入吞吐 vs 原地更新换取即时空间复用
options_en: It forces every write to randomly seek to an old block and modify it first.
It skips locating, reading, modifying, and rewriting old data, appending sequentially at the end of the file instead.
It guarantees every query no longer needs any index.
It only works for pure in-memory databases, not disk-based ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对磁盘上分散位置的读写，需要额外寻址开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random I/O reads or writes scattered disk locations and pays extra seek overhead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按顺序连续读写磁盘位置，没有寻址开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential I/O reads or writes contiguous disk locations without seek overhead.

scenario: 为高吞吐指标流选型时，需要判断随机写和顺序写在机械硬盘上的量级差异。
scenario_en: When choosing storage for a high-throughput metric stream, you need to judge the order-of-magnitude gap between random and sequential writes on spinning disks.
q: 机械硬盘上，随机 I/O 相比顺序 I/O 的数量级差异大致是什么？
q_en: On spinning disks, roughly how different are random I/O and sequential I/O?
options: 随机 I/O 永远比顺序 I/O 快 100 倍
SSD 无论随机还是顺序都完全一样，二者无差别
机械硬盘随机操作通常只有百级 ops/s，顺序写吞吐可以高出一到两个数量级
磁盘 I/O 模式与数据库写入设计无关
why: 机械硬盘随机操作受限于磁头寻道，通常百级 ops/s；顺序写能到万级甚至更高。这个差距正是 append-only 设计存在的理由。
why_en: Spinning disks are limited to roughly hundreds of random operations per second because of head seeks, while sequential writes can reach far higher throughput, which is exactly why append-only design pays off.
options_en: Random I/O is always 100 times faster than sequential I/O.
SSDs perform identically whether access is random or sequential.
Spinning disks typically manage only hundreds of random ops per second, while sequential writes can be one to two orders of magnitude higher.
Disk I/O pattern has nothing to do with database write design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固态硬盘，没有机械寻道臂，但顺序访问仍比随机访问更友好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSD is flash-based storage with no mechanical seek arm, though sequential access is still friendlier than random access.

q: 把 LSM tree 写入路径按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the LSM tree write path in order:
steps: 后台 compaction 合并多个 SSTable，清理重复数据和 tombstone
新数据先写入内存中的有序 memtable
memtable 满后顺序刷盘成不可变的有序 SSTable
查询时可能需要检查 memtable 和多个磁盘文件
why: LSM 把前台随机写转为内存写和顺序刷盘，再把组织数据的成本放到后台 compaction。读取会承担检查多个文件的成本。
why_en: LSM trees write to a sorted memtable, flush immutable SSTables, compact them in the background, and may check multiple files on reads.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Write[Incoming points] --> Memtable[Sorted memtable]
Memtable --> SSTable[Immutable SSTable]
SSTable --> Compaction[Background compaction]
Compaction --> Larger[Large sorted files]
Query[Query] --> Memtable
Query --> SSTable

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写，再靠后台合并整理数据的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree turns random writes into sequential writes and reorganizes data later via background merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 刷盘后生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is the immutable sorted file an LSM tree writes when it flushes memory to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 中驻留内存的有序缓冲结构，接收最新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is the in-memory sorted buffer that absorbs the newest writes in an LSM tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 合并多个存储文件、清理重复和已删除数据的后台过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compaction is the background process that merges storage files and removes stale or deleted data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记某条数据已删除的占位记录，等 compaction 时才真正清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone is a marker recording that a value was deleted; it is physically removed only during compaction.

q: LSM（Log-Structured Merge Tree）的 memtable 为什么通常保持有序？
q_en: Why is the memtable in an LSM tree usually kept sorted?
options: 为了让所有写入都必须等待磁盘完成排序后才算成功
为了强制所有查询必须全表扫描，不能走索引
为了把每个 key 随机分散写到不同文件，避免热点
为了刷盘后直接生成有序 SSTable，方便二分查找、范围扫描和后续合并
why: 内存里排序成本低，刷盘时直接顺序写出有序文件；有序文件支持二分查找、范围扫描，也让后台 merge-sort compaction 更高效。
why_en: A sorted memtable flushes into a sorted SSTable, enabling binary search, efficient ranges, and merge-based compaction.
options_en: So that every write must wait for the disk to finish sorting before it's considered successful.
So that every query is forced to do a full scan instead of using an index.
So that each key is randomly scattered across different files to avoid hotspots.
So that flushing produces an already-sorted SSTable, enabling binary search, range scans, and later merge-based compaction.
optionMeanings: 误以为排序是为了拖慢写入确认速度。
误以为有序结构会禁止索引查询。
误以为有序是为了打散 key 分布。
有序 memtable 刷盘后直接是有序 SSTable。

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 中驻留内存的有序缓冲结构，接收最新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is the in-memory sorted buffer that absorbs the newest writes in an LSM tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 刷盘后生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is the immutable sorted file an LSM tree writes when it flushes memory to disk.

q: LSM tree（日志结构合并树）的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff of an LSM tree?
options: 牺牲所有写入能力，换取只读性能
牺牲部分读性能和写放大，换取高写入吞吐
牺牲压缩能力，换取更高空间占用
完全没有任何后台开销，因此性能只受磁盘限制
why: 读可能要查多个 SSTable，compaction 会重写数据产生写放大。它适合高写入场景，而不是所有 workload 的默认答案。
why_en: LSM trees trade some read cost and write amplification for much higher write throughput.
tradeoff: 高写入吞吐 vs 读放大与写放大
options_en: It gives up all write capability in exchange for read-only performance.
It trades some read performance and write amplification for much higher write throughput.
It gives up compression capability in exchange for higher space usage.
It has zero background overhead, so performance is limited only by disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写，再靠后台合并整理数据的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree turns random writes into sequential writes and reorganizes data later via background merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由于 compaction 反复重写数据，实际磁盘写入量大于逻辑写入量的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification means the actual bytes written to disk exceed the logical write size because compaction rewrites data multiple times.

q: 补全 delta encoding 的思想：
q_en: Complete the idea behind delta encoding:
text: Delta encoding 不反复存完整值，而是存相邻值之间的 {{difference}}；时间序列相邻点通常变化小，所以这些 delta 更容易被 {{compressed}}。
why: CPU、内存、流量等指标通常连续且变化平滑，delta 值比原始值小。配合可变长编码能显著降低存储。
why_en: Delta encoding stores differences between adjacent values, which compress well when time-series data changes gradually.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["t1 t2 t3"] --> B["deltas"]
  B --> C["delta of delta"]
  C --> D["compressed block"]
codeSample:
Raw values:     45.2  45.3  45.1  45.4
Delta encoded:  45.2  +0.1  -0.2  +0.3
# 只存差值，差值比原值小很多，更容易压缩

termDefinitions.meaning: 存相邻值之间的差而不是完整值的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta encoding stores the difference between adjacent values instead of the full value each time.

q: varint（variable-length encoding，变长整数编码）在 TSDB 压缩中解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does varint, or variable-length encoding, solve in TSDB compression?
options: 让所有字符串自动转换成图片格式存储
强制每条记录都补齐到固定 1MB 大小
让数值小的整数只占 1-2 字节，而不是固定 4/8 字节
让浮点数从此无法用任何方式存储
why: delta 往往是小数值，varint 能让小值占用 1-2 个字节。它放大了 delta encoding 的空间收益。
why_en: Variable-length encoding stores small deltas in fewer bytes instead of always using a fixed-width integer.
options_en: It automatically converts all strings into image format for storage.
It forces every record to pad out to a fixed 1MB size.
It lets small integers take only 1-2 bytes instead of a fixed 4 or 8 bytes.
It makes floating-point numbers impossible to store at all.
codeSample:
varint(1)        = 0x01            (1 byte)
varint(300)      = 0xAC 0x02       (2 bytes)
varint(1000000)  = 0xC0 0x84 0x3D  (3 bytes)
# 值越小，占用字节越少；delta 编码后大多是小数值

termDefinitions.meaning: 变长整数编码，用更少字节表示小数值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Varint is a variable-length integer encoding that stores small numbers in fewer bytes.

q: 时间戳 delta-of-delta（二阶差分）编码为什么对固定采样间隔特别有效？
q_en: Why is timestamp delta-of-delta encoding especially effective for fixed sampling intervals?
options: 因为 timestamp 不能被排序
因为相邻 timestamp 的间隔经常相同，二阶差分大量为 0
因为它会丢弃真实采样时间，只保留序号
因为所有 timestamp 都必须先转成字符串再比较
why: 如果每 10 秒采样一次，timestamp 的 delta 基本恒定，delta-of-delta 接近 0。大量 0 非常容易压缩。
why_en: Delta-of-delta compression works well because regular sampling intervals make second-order timestamp deltas mostly zero.
options_en: Because timestamps cannot be sorted.
Because the interval between adjacent timestamps is often constant, so second-order deltas are mostly zero.
Because it discards the real sample time and keeps only a sequence number.
Because every timestamp must first be converted to a string before comparison.
codeSample:
Raw timestamps:   1000  1010  1020  1030  1040
Deltas:              10    10    10    10
Delta-of-delta:            0     0     0
# 间隔恒定 → 二阶差分几乎全 0 → 极易压缩

termDefinitions.meaning: 对增量再做一次差分的二阶编码，常用于规律采样的时间戳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta-of-delta encoding takes the difference of deltas, which collapses to near zero for regularly spaced timestamps.

q: TSDB 对浮点值常用 XOR 压缩的直觉是什么？
q_en: What is the intuition behind XOR compression for floating-point values in a TSDB?
options: 浮点数在时间序列里完全无法做任何压缩处理
XOR 运算会把所有数值变成同一个常数输出
XOR 压缩只对文本字符串生效，对浮点数无效
相邻浮点值接近时，XOR 后多数 bit 是 0，只需存差异部分
why: 相邻指标值通常很接近，二进制表示也有大量相同位。XOR 后只保留有意义的差异位，能显著减少空间。
why_en: XOR compression exploits similar adjacent floating-point values because their XOR contains many zero bits.
options_en: Floating-point values in time series can't be compressed at all.
XOR turns all values into the same constant output.
XOR compression only works on text strings, not floats.
When adjacent float values are close, XORing them leaves mostly zero bits, so only the differing part needs to be stored.

termDefinitions.meaning: 利用相邻浮点数按位异或后大量为 0 位来压缩数值的技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XOR compression exploits the fact that XORing similar adjacent floating-point values leaves mostly zero bits.

scenario: 监控系统每条指标点只有 timestamp 和一个 float，理论上很小，但落到普通行式表后磁盘占用远超预期。
scenario_en: Each monitoring point only has a timestamp and one float, so the raw payload is tiny, but disk usage grows far beyond expectation in a normal row store.
q: 为什么一条普通指标点的原始信息很小，但行式存储仍可能很浪费？
q_en: Why can a normal metric point be tiny in raw form but still waste space in row storage?
options: 因为每条指标都会被数据库自动复制成完整的一段视频文件保存
因为原始数值本身只有十几字节，但每行还反复存 host、metric_name 等标签字符串
因为 timestamp 这个字段本身在磁盘上要占用大约 10MB 空间
因为浮点数类型在关系数据库里天生完全无法进行任何压缩
why: 实际数值部分很小，空间膨胀多来自重复标签和行式元数据。TSDB 通过 series-oriented 存储和压缩减少这种重复。
why_en: The raw timestamp and value are small, but row stores waste space by repeating labels and row metadata for every point.
options_en: Because every point gets automatically duplicated into a full video file by the database.
Because the raw value itself is only a dozen or so bytes, but every row still repeats label strings like host and metric_name.
Because the timestamp field alone takes about 10MB of disk space.
Because floating-point types in relational databases inherently cannot be compressed at all.

q: Time-based partitioning 在 TSDB 中的含义是什么？
q_en: What does time-based partitioning mean in a TSDB?
options: 按用户名哈希把数据随机拆分成数量不受控的表
把所有历史数据永远放进一个不可删除的大文件
按时间窗口把数据切成不同 partition/chunk，比如按天或按周划分
只根据 metric 的数值大小做分区，不看时间
why: 时间序列查询天然带时间范围，按时间窗口组织能让写入、读取和保留策略都更简单。不同 partition 可以在同机或多机上。
why_en: Time-based partitioning groups points into time-windowed chunks such as daily or weekly partitions.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Time range"] --> B["Day partition"]
  A --> C["Week partition"]
  B --> D["Drop old partition"]
options_en: Randomly hash-splitting data by username into an unbounded number of tables.
Keeping all historical data forever in one file that can never be deleted.
Splitting data into partitions or chunks by time window, such as daily or weekly.
Partitioning only by the metric's numeric value, ignoring time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间窗口（如按天/周）把数据切成不同 partition/chunk。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-based partitioning groups data into chunks by time window, such as daily or weekly.

q: Time-based partitioning 带来哪些收益？
q_en: What benefits does time-based partitioning provide?
options: 所有高基数标签都会自动变低基数
新写入集中到当前时间 partition
保留策略可直接 drop 旧 partition
时间范围查询可以跳过不相关 partition
why: 按时间组织同时优化写入局部性、查询裁剪和数据过期。它不能解决 tag cardinality 爆炸。
why_en: Time partitions localize writes, prune reads by time range, and make retention as simple as dropping old partitions.
options_en: All high-cardinality tags automatically become low-cardinality.
New writes concentrate on the current time partition.
Retention can simply drop entire old partitions.
Time-range queries can skip irrelevant partitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间窗口（如按天/周）把数据切成不同 partition/chunk。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-based partitioning groups data into chunks by time window, such as daily or weekly.

q: 为什么 TSDB 的保留策略通常比在巨表上 DELETE 旧行更便宜？
q_en: Why is TSDB retention usually cheaper than deleting old rows from a huge table?
options: 因为所有历史数据会在保留期到期后自动变成 0 字节但仍保留行
因为保留策略执行时完全不需要读取任何元数据
因为 TSDB 设计上永远不会删除任何数据
因为旧数据按时间分区存放，可直接删除整段旧文件
why: drop partition 是元数据/文件级操作，避免在巨表里扫描并删除海量旧行。监控数据常有明确生命周期，所以这个收益很大。
why_en: Retention is cheap because old time partitions can be dropped instead of deleting rows from a massive table.
options_en: Because all historical data automatically shrinks to 0 bytes at expiry but rows remain.
Because executing retention needs no metadata lookup at all.
Because a TSDB is designed to never delete any data.
Because old data lives in its own time partition, so retention can simply drop that entire file.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间窗口（如按天/周）把数据切成不同 partition/chunk。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-based partitioning groups data into chunks by time window, such as daily or weekly.

scenario: 一次按 series 查询要检查多个 SSTable，直接挨个读盘代价很高，需要先低成本排除不可能的文件。
scenario_en: A query for one series may need to check several SSTables, so reading each file from disk first is too expensive.
q: Bloom filter（布隆过滤器）在 LSM/TSDB 读取路径中的作用是什么？
q_en: What role does a Bloom filter play in the LSM/TSDB read path?
options: 保证所有聚合查询完全不需要读取任何磁盘数据
不读磁盘就能判断某个 SSTable 一定没有目标 series，或者可能有
把所有压缩算法都替换成 Bloom filter 一种方案
把所有 false positive 结果都变成 false negative
why: Bloom filter 可以快速跳过不含目标 key 的文件。它可能误报“也许有”，但不会误报“肯定没有”。
why_en: A Bloom filter lets the database skip SSTables that definitely do not contain a queried series without disk reads.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Query series"] --> B["Block bloom"]
  B --> C{"Maybe present?"}
  C -->|"no"| D["Skip block"]
  C -->|"yes"| E["Read block"]
options_en: It guarantees every aggregation query needs zero disk reads at all.
Without touching disk, it tells you an SSTable definitely does not contain a series, or maybe does.
It replaces every compression algorithm with a single Bloom filter.
It turns every false positive result into a false negative.
optionMeanings: 误以为 Bloom filter 能让聚合完全跳过磁盘读取。
它是用来低成本排除不相关 SSTable 的快速判断。
混淆了 Bloom filter 和压缩算法这两类机制。
把两种误差的方向（漏报/误报）弄反了。
optionScenarioImpacts: 实际匹配的 SSTable 仍然需要真正读盘确认。
能把要检查的候选 SSTable 数量大幅减少。
Bloom filter 不压缩数据，只做成员判断。
false positive 只多读一次，false negative 才是真正致命的。
optionDirectness: 命中文件很少、文件数也少时，直接读盘还能接受。
文件很多且多数不含目标 series 时，Bloom filter 最有价值。
需要降低存储体积时应选压缩算法，不是 Bloom filter。
读路径宁可多读也不能漏读，所以 no false negative 是底线。
codeSample:
Query: series host=server-42
SSTable-1 bloom: “not here”   → skip (0 磁盘读)
SSTable-2 bloom: “not here”   → skip (0 磁盘读)
SSTable-3 bloom: “maybe here” → 读盘校验
# 只有 “maybe” 才真正触发磁盘 I/O

termDefinitions.meaning: 概率型数据结构，能确定判断“一定没有”，“可能有”时需要进一步确认。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic structure that can say a key is definitely absent, while a maybe-present result needs further checking.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 刷盘后生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is the immutable sorted file an LSM tree writes when it flushes memory to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: false positive 指误报“可能有”但实际没有；false negative 指漏报“没有”但实际有。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive wrongly reports maybe-present when the key is absent; a false negative wrongly reports absent when the key is actually present.

q: Bloom filter 的 false positive / false negative 特性是什么？
q_en: What are the false positive and false negative properties of a Bloom filter?
options: 它有时会漏掉真实存在的 key，即产生 false negative
它保证零误差，既没有 false positive 也没有 false negative
它可能误报“也许有”但实际没有；绝不会漏报“没有”但实际有
它只能用于对 key 做精确计数，不能做成员判断
why: Bloom filter 的核心保证是 no false negatives。false positive 只会导致多读一次文件，不会漏结果。
why_en: Bloom filters can have false positives but no false negatives, so they may cause extra reads but do not miss existing keys.
tradeoff: 多读几次文件（false positive）vs 绝不漏掉真实数据（no false negative）
options_en: It sometimes misses keys that really exist, producing a false negative.
It guarantees zero error, with neither false positives nor false negatives.
It may falsely say maybe-present when absent, but never falsely says absent when the key is actually present.
It can only be used for exact key counting, not membership checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 概率型数据结构，能确定判断“一定没有”，“可能有”时需要进一步确认。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic structure that can say a key is definitely absent, while a maybe-present result needs further checking.

termDefinitions.meaning: false positive 指误报“可能有”但实际没有；false negative 指漏报“没有”但实际有。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive wrongly reports maybe-present when the key is absent; a false negative wrongly reports absent when the key is actually present.

scenario: 为百万级 series、几十个 SSTable 的 TSDB 评估 Bloom filter 的内存开销是否划算。
scenario_en: You are evaluating whether Bloom filter memory cost is worthwhile for a TSDB with millions of series and dozens of SSTables.
q: 一个调优良好的 Bloom filter，典型的内存开销和误报率大致是什么量级？
q_en: What order of memory cost and false positive rate is typical for a well-tuned Bloom filter?
options: 必须每个 key 占用 10KB 才能正常工作
约 10 bits/key 就能做到约 1% 的 false positive 率
false positive 率永远是 100%，形同虚设
只能用于少于 10 个 key 的小文件
why: 这不是要死记硬背的精确值，但说明 Bloom filter 用很少内存就能跳过大量无关 SSTable，是数量级上的直觉。
why_en: A practical Bloom filter can use around 10 bits per key for about a 1 percent false positive rate.
options_en: It must use 10KB per key to work at all.
About 10 bits per key can achieve roughly a 1 percent false positive rate.
The false positive rate is always 100 percent, making it useless.
It only works for small files with fewer than 10 keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 概率型数据结构，能确定判断“一定没有”，“可能有”时需要进一步确认。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic structure that can say a key is definitely absent, while a maybe-present result needs further checking.

q: Downsampling / rollup 在 TSDB 中解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem do downsampling and rollups solve in a TSDB?
options: 让所有原始数据永远保持最高分辨率并无限复制
把时间戳删除，使数据无法按时间查询
把老数据降到更粗粒度，减少历史查询需要扫描的数据量
只用于加密用户密码
why: 近期数据常需要高分辨率，历史数据通常只看趋势。rollup 用更粗的时间桶保存预聚合结果，换取更快历史查询和更低存储。
why_en: Downsampling stores lower-resolution rollups for older data so historical queries scan far fewer points.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Raw points"] --> B["1m buckets"]
  B --> C["5m rollup"]
  C --> D["Long range query"]
options_en: Keep all raw data at maximum resolution forever with unlimited replication.
Delete timestamps so data can no longer be queried by time.
Reduce older data to coarser granularity so historical queries scan far less data.
It is only used to encrypt user passwords.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把细粒度历史数据预聚合成更粗时间桶，牺牲精度换存储和查询效率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollup pre-aggregates fine-grained history into coarser time buckets, trading precision for storage and query speed.

q: Rollup 通常会为每个时间桶预聚合哪些值？
q_en: What values does a rollup usually pre-aggregate for each time bucket?
options: 完整用户会话视频
min
max
sum/count
why: min、max、sum、count 能支持平均值、范围和趋势类查询。它们不需要保留每个原始点就能回答多数历史 dashboard 问题。
why_en: Rollups usually store aggregates such as min, max, sum, and count for each time bucket.
options_en: A complete recording of the user's session video.
min
max
sum/count

termDefinitions.meaning: 把细粒度历史数据预聚合成更粗时间桶，牺牲精度换存储和查询效率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollup pre-aggregates fine-grained history into coarser time buckets, trading precision for storage and query speed.

scenario: Dashboard 把一天历史数据用 5 分钟粒度的 rollup 展示，而不是原始 10 秒采样点。
scenario_en: A dashboard shows one day of history using 5-minute rollups instead of raw 10-second samples.
q: 相比直接扫描原始 10 秒采样点，用 5 分钟 rollup 回答“过去一天趋势”的查询，设计上带来了什么？
q_en: Compared with scanning raw 10-second samples, what does a 5-minute rollup change for a past-day trend query?
options: 扫描的数据点数量完全不变，只是换了一种展示方式
查询需要扫描的数据点数量级下降，历史大范围查询明显更快，但会牺牲一部分时间精度
rollup 会让查询变慢，因为要先做聚合计算
rollup 只影响存储成本，不影响查询要扫描多少数据
why: 原始 10 秒采样一天有 8,640 点，5 分钟 rollup 只有 288 个桶，两个数量级的差距直接决定长范围查询要扫多少数据。
why_en: Raw 10-second sampling produces 8,640 points a day while 5-minute rollups produce only 288 buckets, and that order-of-magnitude gap is what makes long-range queries fast.
options_en: The number of points scanned stays exactly the same; only the display changes.
The number of points to scan drops by orders of magnitude, making large historical queries much faster at the cost of some time resolution.
Rollups make queries slower because they require upfront aggregation.
Rollups only affect storage cost, not how much data a query scans.

scenario: 面试官说要保存 1 年 10 秒级指标，但多数 dashboard 只看长期趋势。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks to keep one year of 10-second metrics, but most dashboards only show long-term trends.
q: 更成熟的回应是什么？
q_en: What is a more mature response?
options: 直接照单全收，保存全部原始点一整年，不讨论任何成本
直接把最近 24 小时的数据也删掉以省空间
建议近期保留细粒度，老数据降采样成分钟级 rollup，并向面试官确认是否可接受
把所有历史数据都压缩成只剩最后一个点
why: 这是需求谈判：先指出原始数据量巨大，再提出保留精度与成本之间的折中。即使面试官不同意，也能体现你会主动识别未来瓶颈。
why_en: A strong interview answer negotiates raw retention by keeping fine resolution for recent data and rolling up older data.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务确实需要长期逐点审计或法务追溯，就必须保留原始点，并相应扩容存储与查询方案。
tradeoff: 精度换成本的降采样提案 vs 原样保留全部原始点
options_en: Just accept it as-is and store every raw point for a full year without discussing cost.
Delete even the most recent 24 hours of data to save space.
Propose keeping fine resolution for recent data and rolling older data up to minute-level buckets, then confirm with the interviewer whether that's acceptable.
Compress all historical data down to just the last point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把细粒度历史数据预聚合成更粗时间桶，牺牲精度换存储和查询效率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollup pre-aggregates fine-grained history into coarser time buckets, trading precision for storage and query speed.

q: Block-level metadata 在 TSDB 查询中有什么用？
q_en: What is block-level metadata used for in TSDB queries?
options: 强制数据库把每个 block 都完整读一遍，不允许跳过
把所有 metric name 随机替换成一串数字
只在处理用户登录鉴权请求时才会被用到
记录每个 block 的 min/max，用来跳过不可能匹配的 block
why: 如果查询条件与 block 的 min/max 范围不相交，数据库可以直接 prune。它和时间分区一起减少无效扫描。
why_en: Block metadata such as min and max values lets the engine prune blocks that cannot match a query.
options_en: Force the database to fully read every block, never allowing a skip.
Randomly replace every metric name with a number.
It is only used when handling user login authentication.
Record each block's min and max so queries can skip blocks that cannot match.
codeSample:
block_0.min_ts=1700000000  block_0.max_ts=1700003600
block_0.min_val=0.0        block_0.max_val=4.8
# 查询 value > 10 时，跳过 max_val=4.8 的 block_0，无需读盘

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录每个数据 block 的 min/max 等统计信息，用于跳过不可能匹配的 block。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Block-level metadata records stats like min and max per block so queries can skip blocks that cannot match.

q: 补全 TSDB 的基本数据模型：
q_en: Complete the basic TSDB data model:
text: TSDB 通常把数据组织成 {{measurement/metric}}、可索引的 {{tags}}、实际数值 {{fields}} 和 {{timestamps}}。
why: measurement 类似表名，tags 是筛选维度，fields 是被测值，timestamp 定义时间位置。这个区分决定查询是否高效。
why_en: Time-series data is usually modeled as measurements, tags, fields, and timestamps.
codeSample:
cpu_usage,host=server-1,region=us-west value=45.2 1699999200000000000
# measurement=cpu_usage，tags=host+region，field=value，timestamp=末尾纳秒

termDefinitions.meaning: 类似表名，标识一种指标类型，比如 cpu_usage。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A measurement is like a table name identifying a metric type, such as cpu_usage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可索引的元数据维度，用于过滤，比如 host、region。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tag is indexed metadata used for filtering, such as host or region.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际测量值，通常不建索引，比如 value。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A field is the actual measured value, usually not indexed, such as value.

q: 在 TSDB 中，tags 和 fields 最关键的区别是什么？
q_en: In a TSDB, what is the key difference between tags and fields?
options: fields 才是用于过滤的索引元数据，tags 只能存浮点数值
tags 是可索引的过滤元数据；fields 是实际测量值，通常不建索引
tags 和 fields 在存储和查询上完全没有区别，可以互换使用
fields 只能用来存时间戳，不能存其他测量值
why: 把常用过滤维度放 tags 可以利用索引；把高基数或只需存储的值放 fields 可以避免 series 爆炸。建模错误会严重影响性能。
why_en: Tags are indexed metadata for filtering, while fields are the measured values and are usually not indexed.
tradeoff: tags 建索引换来快速过滤 vs fields 不建索引避免 series 爆炸
options_en: Fields are actually the indexed metadata for filtering, while tags can only store floating-point values.
Tags are indexed metadata for filtering; fields are the actual measured values and are usually not indexed.
Tags and fields are completely interchangeable for storage and querying.
Fields can only store timestamps, not other measured values.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可索引的元数据维度，用于过滤，比如 host、region。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tag is indexed metadata used for filtering, such as host or region.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际测量值，通常不建索引，比如 value。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A field is the actual measured value, usually not indexed, such as value.

q: TSDB 里一个 series 通常由什么唯一确定？
q_en: What usually uniquely identifies a series in a TSDB?
options: 客户端发起请求时 IP 地址的最后一段数字
数据库进程本次启动的系统时间戳
measurement 加上一组具体 tag 值的唯一组合
series 里数值最大的那一个点
why: 例如 cpu_usage + host=server-1 + region=us-west + env=prod 会形成一个 series。相同 series 的点通常被物理上放在一起。
why_en: A series is typically the unique combination of a measurement and its tag values.
options_en: The last segment of the client's IP address at request time.
The system timestamp of when the database process last started.
The unique combination of a measurement plus a specific set of tag values.
Whichever point in the series happens to have the largest value.

termDefinitions.meaning: measurement 加上一组具体 tag 值构成的一条时间序列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A series is one time-ordered stream identified by a measurement plus a specific set of tag values.

q: 把典型 TSDB 写入/存储引擎步骤按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the typical TSDB write/storage engine steps in order:
steps: buffer 达到阈值后刷盘成不可变压缩文件
数据写入 WAL 以便崩溃恢复
后台 compaction 合并小文件、减少查询要检查的文件数
数据进入按 measurement/tag 组织的内存 buffer
why: WAL 负责 durability，buffer 负责吸收新写入，flush 生成压缩文件，compaction 再优化读取路径。这个组合就是很多 TSDB 的核心写路径。
why_en: A TSDB often writes to the WAL, buffers points in memory, flushes compressed immutable files, and compacts them in the background.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Point[Metric point] --> WAL[WAL]
Point --> Buffer[In-memory buffer]
Buffer --> File[Compressed immutable file]
File --> Compact[Background compaction]
Compact --> QueryFiles[Query-optimized files]

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入先落地的日志，用于崩溃后恢复未持久化的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WAL is an append-only log written before data is applied, used to recover uncommitted writes after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 中驻留内存的有序缓冲结构，接收最新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is the in-memory sorted buffer that absorbs the newest writes in an LSM tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 合并多个存储文件、清理重复和已删除数据的后台过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compaction is the background process that merges storage files and removes stale or deleted data.

q: TSDB 数据文件末尾的 series index 通常记录什么？
q_en: What does the series index at the end of a TSDB data file usually record?
options: 系统里全部用户账号的密码明文备份记录
series key 映射到对应 block 的偏移量
每个 HTTP 请求头里携带的完整字段内容
训练机器学习模型过程中产生的 GPU 日志
why: 文件 index 让查询特定 series 时可以先定位 block，再读数据，而不是从头扫描整个文件。文章强调这通常只需要少量 seek。
why_en: The file index maps series keys to the block offsets containing their data.
options_en: A plaintext backup of every user account's password.
A mapping from series key to the block offset containing its data.
The full header fields carried on every HTTP request.
GPU logs produced while training a machine learning model.
codeSample:
INDEX（文件尾部）:
  "cpu_usage,host=server-1,region=us-west" → block 0
  "cpu_usage,host=server-2,region=us-west" → block 1
# 查 series 只需 2 次 seek：先查 index，再读对应 block

termDefinitions.meaning: 文件尾部维护的 series key 到 block offset 的映射表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A series index is the mapping at the end of a data file from series key to block offset.

q: 把 TSDB 查询执行路径按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the TSDB query execution path in order:
steps: 从内存 buffer 和磁盘文件读取并合并结果
根据 tag filter 在 tag index 中定位匹配 series
边读边做聚合，而不是先把所有点加载进内存
根据时间范围选择相关 partitions/chunks
why: 查询先用时间范围和标签索引缩小候选数据，再合并最新内存数据和磁盘数据。聚合通常是 streaming 的，减少内存压力。
why_en: Query execution prunes partitions by time, finds series via tag indexes, merges buffer and disk data, and streams aggregations.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Query tags and time"] --> B["Tag index"]
  B --> C["Series ids"]
  C --> D["Time blocks"]
  D --> E["Aggregate"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 tag 值映射到匹配 series 集合的内存索引，类似倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tag index maps tag values to the set of matching series, similar to an inverted index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 边读取数据边累积聚合结果，不必先把全部数据加载进内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Streaming aggregation accumulates results as data is read instead of loading everything into memory first.

q: TSDB 的 tag index 和 Elasticsearch 的 inverted index 在直觉上有什么相似？
q_en: What is the intuitive similarity between a TSDB tag index and an Elasticsearch inverted index?
options: 两者的作用都只是对浮点数值做压缩编码而已
都把可过滤的值映射到包含它的对象集合
两者都完全不支持对多个条件做集合交集
两者都只能运行在浏览器前端环境里，不能用于服务端
why: TSDB tag index 可以把 region=us-west 映射到相关 series，把 env=prod 映射到另一组 series，再取交集。它避免扫描全部数据块。
why_en: A tag index maps tag values to matching series, much like an inverted index maps terms to documents.
options_en: Both of them only compress floating-point values.
Both map a filterable value to the set of objects that contain it.
Neither supports intersecting multiple filter conditions.
Both only run inside a browser front end, never on a server.
codeSample:
Tag index:  region=us-west → [Series1, Series2]
Inverted:   "claude"      → [doc7, doc19]
# 同一套思路：value → 匹配对象集合，再做交集

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 tag 值映射到匹配 series 集合的内存索引，类似倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tag index maps tag values to the set of matching series, similar to an inverted index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 token 映射到包含它的文档集合的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps tokens to the set of documents that contain them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于倒排索引的搜索与分析引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search and analytics engine built on an inverted index.

q: 查询 region='us-west' AND env='prod' 时，tag index 通常会怎么用？
q_en: How would a tag index usually handle a query like region='us-west' AND env='prod'?
options: 不看任何索引，直接随机读取所有 block 逐个比对
先把 env 这个 tag 从索引里整个删除再查询
只检查 value 字段是否大于 0，忽略两个 tag 条件
分别查两个 tag 各自的 series 集合，再取交集
why: 集合交集能快速得到同时满足多个 tag 条件的 series。之后只需要读取这些 series 对应的 block。
why_en: A multi-tag query intersects the series sets for each tag predicate before reading data blocks.
options_en: Ignore every index and randomly scan every block one by one.
Delete the env tag from the index entirely before querying.
Only check whether the value field is greater than 0, ignoring both tag conditions.
Look up the series set for each tag separately, then intersect the two sets.
codeSample:
region=us-west → [Series1, Series2]
env=prod       → [Series1, Series2, Series3]
交集 = [Series1, Series2]  # 只需读这两个 series 对应的 block

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 tag 值映射到匹配 series 集合的内存索引，类似倒排索引。

q: 为什么 series-oriented 存储比普通行式表更适合指标查询？
q_en: Why is series-oriented storage better suited to metric queries than a normal row table?
options: 它让所有数据都不再需要保存时间戳字段
它会彻底禁止用户按任何 tag 做过滤查询
同一 series 的点物理上更集中，查询时更少分散读取
它规定整个数据库里每个 series 只能存一条数据
why: 监控查询常围绕某些 host/service/region 的时间范围。把相关点放在连续 block 中，能减少随机读取并提升压缩率。
why_en: Series-oriented storage colocates related points, reducing scattered reads and improving compression for time-range queries.
tradeoff: 同 series 物理集中换取更少分散读取 vs 行式表按插入顺序存储更简单
options_en: It means data no longer needs to store a timestamp field at all.
It completely bans filtering by any tag.
Points from the same series sit closer together physically, so querying it touches fewer scattered reads.
It restricts the whole database to storing only one point per series.

termDefinitions.meaning: measurement 加上一组具体 tag 值构成的一条时间序列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A series is one time-ordered stream identified by a measurement plus a specific set of tag values.

q: TSDB 查询 mean(value) GROUP BY time(5m) 时，为什么通常不需要先把所有点加载到内存？
q_en: Why does a TSDB query like mean(value) GROUP BY time(5m) usually not need to load all points into memory first?
options: 平均值不需要任何输入数据
聚合可以边读取边累积 sum/count/min/max
磁盘会自动返回最终答案
tag index 会直接存所有聚合结果
why: 聚合函数可以流式计算，只保留每个桶的中间状态。这样查询大时间范围时内存压力更可控。
why_en: Aggregations can be streamed by maintaining bucket state such as sum and count as points are read.
options_en: The average requires no input data at all.
Aggregation can accumulate sum, count, min, and max while streaming through the data.
The disk automatically returns the final answer.
The tag index directly stores every aggregation result.
codeSample:
SELECT mean(value) FROM cpu_usage
WHERE host = 'server-1' AND time > now() - 1h
GROUP BY time(5m)

termDefinitions.meaning: 边读取数据边累积聚合结果，不必先把全部数据加载进内存。

q: TSDB 查询快的两个 locality 直觉是什么？
q_en: What are the two locality intuitions behind fast TSDB queries?
options: 用户密码局部性和 CSS 局部性
随机分区局部性和全表扫描局部性
只写不读局部性和只读不写局部性
时间局部性和 series 局部性

why_en: Time-series databases exploit both time locality and series locality to minimize disk access.
options_en: Password locality and CSS locality.
Random partition locality and full-table-scan locality.
Write-only locality and read-only locality.
Time locality and series locality.

q: TSDB 中 cardinality 指的是什么？
q_en: What does cardinality mean in a TSDB?
options: 磁盘上文件的权限数量
每秒 CPU 指令数
唯一 tag 组合，也就是 series 的数量
SQL join 的列数
why: series 数量由 measurement 和 tag 组合决定。cardinality 高会让内存 tag index 和元数据膨胀。
why_en: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, or series, that the database must track.
options_en: The number of file permission bits on disk.
The number of CPU instructions executed per second.
The number of unique tag combinations, i.e., the number of series.
The number of columns in a SQL join.

q: 为什么 user_id、request_id 这类高基数值通常不应该作为 TSDB tag？
q_en: Why should high-cardinality values like user_id or request_id usually not be TSDB tags?
options: 它们在写入时完全没办法被序列化成字节
它们会造出海量唯一 series，压垮内存索引并拖慢查询
它们的取值格式一定不允许是字符串类型
它们会导致所有数据的时间戳顺序颠倒
why: TSDB 会为每个唯一 tag 组合维护索引和元数据。把高基数值放 tag 会迅速耗尽内存，失去性能收益。
why_en: High-cardinality values like user IDs create too many series and can overwhelm the in-memory index.
options_en: They simply cannot be serialized into bytes when written.
They create massive numbers of unique series, overwhelming the in-memory index and slowing queries.
Their values are never allowed to be strings.
They cause every timestamp to be reversed in order.

scenario: 你必须随指标记录 request_id，但查询很少按 request_id 过滤。

q: 在 TSDB 中更适合把 request_id 放在哪里？
q_en: Where should request_id go in a TSDB?
options: 放 tag，因为所有字段都应该建索引
放 timestamp，替代原始采样时间
放 measurement name，让每个请求单独建一个 measurement
放 field，避免高基数 tag 造成 series 爆炸

whenOtherWins: 如果某个维度低基数且经常用于过滤，比如 region/env/service，放 tag 才能利用索引。

Put it in a field, avoiding a high-cardinality tag that explodes the series count.

q: 补全 TSDB 的关键数据假设：
q_en: Complete the key TSDB data assumptions:
text: TSDB 的高性能依赖一些假设：tags 的 cardinality 较 {{low}}，采样时间较 {{regular}}，相邻数据点的 delta 较 {{small}}。

scenario: 面试官问，把写入、时间分区、压缩、索引这些优化叠加后，TSDB 相比通用数据库大概能快多少。

q: 对目标 workload 而言，TSDB 相比通用数据库的性能收益大致是什么量级？
q_en: For the target workload, what order of performance gain can a TSDB have over a general-purpose database?

永远慢 100x，专用系统反而更差

options_en: It's always only 1 percent faster, barely noticeable.

It typically delivers one to two orders of magnitude better performance, roughly 10 to 100x.

q: 是否应该因为数据带时间就默认上 TSDB？

options: 应该，只要数据字段里出现时间就必须优先考虑 TSDB
应该，因为 TSDB 能自动帮你处理所有排序和聚合逻辑

options_en: Yes, whenever a field contains time you must prioritize a TSDB.

scenario: 云监控平台持续接收 CPU、内存、磁盘、网络指标，用户主要看最近一小时/一周图表和告警。

q: 为什么 TSDB 比普通行式表更贴合？
q_en: Why does a TSDB fit better than a normal row table?

q: TSDB 查询时为什么通常要同时看内存 buffer 和磁盘文件？
q_en: Why does a TSDB query usually check both the in-memory buffer and disk files?
options: 磁盘上的文件永远是空的，不会保存任何数据
内存 buffer 里只会缓存用户的头像图片

The in-memory buffer only caches user avatar images.
The newest data may still be in the in-memory buffer while older data has already been flushed to disk.

q: “writes are optimized to assist reads” 在 TSDB 里的意思更接近哪一个？
q_en: What does "writes are optimized to assist reads" mean in a TSDB?

写入时故意把数据打乱顺序，让查询变得更难
写入时只保留每个 series 最后一个值，其余全部丢弃
写入按 series/time 组织并压缩，让后续查询少读更顺序
