Not direct: inverts who should own service discovery.

q: 把 ZooKeeper 的应用级 leader 选举配方排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put ZooKeeper's application-level leader election recipe in the correct order.
steps: 序号最小的服务器成为 leader
每台服务器在指定路径下创建顺序+临时节点
leader 故障 → 它的节点消失，下一个序号的服务器收到通知接任
其余服务器各自 watch「比自己小的下一个序号」的节点
why: 创建顺序临时节点 → 最小序号当 leader → 各自 watch 前一个 → 前面的消失就接班。自动故障转移，同一时刻只有一个 leader。
why_en: Each server creates a sequential ephemeral node, the lowest number leads, everyone watches the next lower node, and when the leader dies the next in line takes over.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["node-0001 (leader)"] -.被 watch.- B["node-0002"]
    B -.被 watch.- C["node-0003"]
    A -- 崩溃消失 --> B2["node-0002 成为新 leader"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序+临时节点：同时具备顺序节点的递增编号和临时节点的会话绑定特性，是选举与锁配方的原料。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential ephemeral node combines an auto-incrementing suffix with session-bound auto-deletion, the building block for election and lock recipes.

q: 选举配方里，为什么 Server 3 watch 的是 node-0000000002（前一个），而不是 leader 的 node-0000000001？
q_en: In the election recipe, why does Server 3 watch node-0000000002 instead of the leader node?
options: watch leader 节点是为了持续监控它的 CPU 和内存性能
两种 watch 方式在效果上完全等价，选哪个都可以
因为单个客户端在 ZooKeeper 上能注册的 watch 数量有硬性上限
链式监听：每人只盯前一位，任何节点消失只惊动它的下一位，通知量最小
options_en: Watching the leader's node is meant to monitor its CPU and memory usage.
The two watch strategies are functionally equivalent, so either works fine.
There is a hard cap on how many watches a single client can register.
A chain: each server watches only the next lower node, so a failure notifies exactly one successor.
why: 链式 watch 让每次变动只通知一个等待者，避免全体涌向同一节点；谁的前任消失谁递补。
why_en: Each server watches only the next lower node, forming a chain so a failure notifies exactly one successor instead of everyone.

q: 哪些真实系统用过 ZooKeeper 的这种 leader 选举模式？
q_en: Which real systems have used this ZooKeeper leader election pattern?
options: HBase 的 schema 变更协调，以及早期 Kafka 用它选出管理分区领导权的 controller broker
Redis 的主从故障切换机制，同样是靠这套顺序临时节点选举模式挑出新主节点
Nginx 做请求负载均衡的时候，也是用它在多个后端实例间选一个当前活跃节点
Git 在合并多个分支的时候，也是用它决定哪一条分支的提交历史应该优先保留
options_en: HBase's schema-change coordination, and early Kafka's controller broker that manages partition leadership.
Redis also uses this exact sequential-ephemeral election recipe to pick its new primary during failover.
Nginx also uses it to elect one active backend instance among several for request load balancing.
Git also uses it to decide which branch's commit history should be kept as priority during a merge.
why: HBase 靠它保证一台服务器协调 schema 变更；KRaft 之前的 Kafka 用它选 controller——经典的「同一时刻只有一个人干关键活」。
why_en: HBase coordinates schema changes and pre-KRaft Kafka elected its controller broker using this ZooKeeper pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: HBase：构建在 Hadoop 之上的分布式列式数据库，历史上用 ZooKeeper 做协调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HBase is a distributed column-family database built on Hadoop that has historically used ZooKeeper for coordination.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：分布式消息队列/事件流平台，早期版本依赖 ZooKeeper 管理集群元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and event-streaming platform whose early versions relied on ZooKeeper for cluster metadata.

termDefinitions.meaning: controller broker：Kafka 集群中被选出、专门负责管理分区 leader 分配的那台 broker。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The controller broker is the elected Kafka broker responsible for managing partition leader assignment.

optionMeanings: HBase 与早期 Kafka 都用顺序临时节点选举实现单点协调。
Redis 主从切换的哨兵机制并非基于 ZooKeeper 选举配方。
Nginx 的负载均衡是请求分发算法，不涉及 leader 选举。
Git 合并靠提交图和合并策略，与分布式选举无关。
optionScenarioImpacts: 两个系统都借助临时节点的会话特性做崩溃自动检测。
Redis Sentinel/Cluster 有自己的一套投票机制，不依赖 ZK。
Nginx 本身是无状态转发，没有『谁是 leader』这个概念。
分支合并是版本控制里的操作，和运行时协调服务不是一回事。
optionDirectness: 最直接：这是文章点名的两个真实案例。
不直接：混淆了不同系统各自的容错机制。
不直接：张冠李戴，负载均衡不是选举。
不直接：跨领域概念混用，Git 不做运行时协调。
optionMeanings_en: HBase and early Kafka both used sequential ephemeral nodes for single-coordinator election.
Redis failover uses Sentinel/Cluster voting, not the ZooKeeper election recipe.
Nginx load balancing is a request-distribution algorithm, not leader election.
Git merging relies on commit graphs and merge strategies, unrelated to distributed election.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Both systems lean on ephemeral-node session semantics for automatic crash detection.
Redis has its own voting mechanism and does not depend on ZooKeeper.
Nginx is stateless request forwarding with no notion of a leader.
Branch merging is a version-control operation, unrelated to runtime coordination.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: these are the two real-world cases the article names.
Not direct: conflates unrelated fault-tolerance mechanisms.
Not direct: confuses load balancing with leader election.
Not direct: mixes in an unrelated version-control concept.

scenario: 多个支付 worker 都想处理同一笔 payment，但同一时刻只能有一个 worker 进入临界区。worker 可能崩溃，所以锁必须能自动释放。
scenario_en: Multiple payment workers want to process the same payment, but only one worker may enter the critical section at a time. Workers can crash, so the lock must release automatically.
q: ZooKeeper 分布式锁的配方是？
q_en: What is the ZooKeeper distributed-lock recipe?
options: 所有客户端抢写同一个固定节点，成功者持锁
每个客户端建临时顺序节点，最小号持锁
由 ensemble leader 手动挑一个客户端发锁
按客户端本地时间戳排序，最早者持锁
options_en: All clients race to write the same fixed node; whoever succeeds holds the lock.
Each client creates an ephemeral sequential node; the lowest number holds the lock.
The ensemble leader manually chooses one client and grants the lock.
Sort by each client's local timestamp; the earliest one holds the lock.
why: 把锁想成排队拿号：每个客户端拿一个会自动递增、会话结束会消失的节点号。号最小的人持锁；其他人只 watch 自己前一个号，前一个消失后再检查是否轮到自己。
why_en: Think of the lock as taking a queue ticket: each client creates an ephemeral sequential node, the lowest ticket holds the lock, and everyone else watches only the previous ticket.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是同一进程内互斥，用本地 mutex；如果是高频短锁，Redis 或数据库条件写通常更轻。
tradeoff: 公平排队+崩溃自动释放 vs 每次加解锁都走 ZooKeeper 写路径
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Client creates lock-0007"] --> B["List lock queue"]
  B --> C{"Am I smallest?"}
  C -->|"yes"| D["Enter critical section"]
  C -->|"no"| E["Watch lock-0006"]
  E --> F["0006 deleted or session expired"]
  F --> B
optionMeanings: 大家同时争同一个固定节点。
每个客户端拿一个 ZooKeeper 分配的排队号。
误以为 ZooKeeper leader 直接管理业务锁。
用各机器自己的时钟决定先后。
optionScenarioImpacts: 锁释放时可能所有等待者一起醒来，形成惊群。
只唤醒下一位；持锁者崩溃时临时节点自动消失。
ensemble leader 负责共识写入，不负责业务层发锁。
机器时钟会漂移，跨机器顺序不可靠。
optionDirectness: 不直接；能做简单抢占，但不如排队 watch 可控。
最直接；它同时解决排队、公平和崩溃释放。
不直接；这是把内部 leader 和业务锁混淆。
不直接；本地时间不能做分布式全序。
optionMeanings_en: Everyone races on one fixed node.
Each client takes a ZooKeeper-assigned queue ticket.
It assumes the ZooKeeper leader directly manages application locks.
It orders clients by their own local clocks.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: When the lock releases, all waiters may wake up and stampede.
Only the next waiter wakes; if the holder crashes, its ephemeral node disappears.
The ensemble leader coordinates writes, not application-level lock grants.
Machine clocks drift, so local timestamps cannot define a reliable global order.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; it can race, but queueing with watches is more controlled.
Most direct; it covers queueing, fairness, and crash release.
Not direct; it confuses the internal leader with application locks.
Not direct; local time cannot provide distributed total order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一时刻只能由一个 worker 执行的代码段，例如处理同一笔 payment。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A critical section is code that only one worker may execute at a time, such as processing one payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 临时顺序节点：名字带递增编号，创建者会话结束时自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ephemeral sequential node has an increasing suffix and is deleted when its creator session ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只监听自己前一个排队节点。这样释放锁时只唤醒下一位，避免全部等待者一起抢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Watching the predecessor means listening only to the queue node just before yours, so only the next waiter wakes.

q: ZooKeeper 锁不适合什么场景？该用什么替代？
q_en: When is a ZooKeeper lock a poor fit, and what should replace it?
options: 只要持锁时间超过几分钟，就应该换成本地内存锁替代
任何生产场景都不该用 ZooKeeper 锁，风险太高
高频加解锁（每秒数百次）；这种场景考虑 Redis 锁或数据库事务
跨机房场景不适合，应该改成每个机房各自独立加锁
options_en: Any hold time over a few minutes should switch to a local in-memory lock.
ZooKeeper locks should never be used in any production scenario at all.
High-frequency locking, hundreds of times per second, where Redis locks or database transactions fit better.
Cross-datacenter locking is unsuitable, so each datacenter should lock independently instead.
why: 每次加解锁都是走共识的写操作，高频场景撑不住；高频轻量锁交给 Redis 或数据库。
why_en: ZooKeeper locks are not built for hundreds of acquisitions per second, where Redis locks or database transactions fit better.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 锁：用 SETNX/TTL 等 Redis 命令实现的轻量分布式锁，吞吐高但依赖超时管理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis lock is a lightweight distributed lock built with commands like SETNX and TTL, offering high throughput but relying on timeout management.

scenario: 金融交易的关键操作需要分布式锁：正确性压倒性能，锁可能持有数小时，持锁进程崩溃必须被可靠检测。
scenario_en: A financial transaction workflow needs a distributed lock. Correctness matters more than throughput, the lock may be held for hours, and a crashed holder must be detected reliably.
q: 选 ZooKeeper 锁还是 Redis 锁？
q_en: Should you choose a ZooKeeper lock or a Redis lock?
options: ZooKeeper 锁：一致性保证更强，临时节点自动检测崩溃，长锁不依赖小心翼翼的超时管理
Redis 锁：吞吐更高、延迟更低，看起来很适合这种长时间持有的场景
两者随便选一个都可以，反正最终业务结果都是一样的
干脆不加锁，靠业务失败之后重试来兜底数据一致性
options_en: ZooKeeper locks — stronger consistency, ephemeral nodes detect crashes automatically, no fragile timeout tuning for long holds.
Redis locks — higher throughput and lower latency, which looks like a fit for this long-hold scenario.
Either one is fine to pick, the final business outcome ends up the same.
Skip locking entirely and just rely on retry-after-failure to backstop consistency.
why: Redis 锁赢在性能与简单（Ticketmaster/Uber 场景）；但正确性优先 + 长持有 + 崩溃自动释放的需求下，ZK 的会话机制远比 Redis 的超时+心跳可靠。
why_en: Choose ZooKeeper locks when correctness trumps performance and locks are long-lived, since ephemeral nodes detect crashes more robustly than Redis timeouts.
whenOtherWins: 高频短锁场景（秒杀、抢票）Redis 性能更占优，Ticketmaster、Uber 都选了它。
tradeoff: ZooKeeper 锁的强一致 + 会话式崩溃检测 vs Redis 锁的高吞吐 + 手动超时管理

rows: 会话超时自动删除节点

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 锁：常用 SET key value NX EX ttl 实现，靠 TTL 超时兜底释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis lock is typically built with SET NX EX and relies on a TTL timeout as its safety net for release.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum（多数派）：ZooKeeper 写操作需要 ensemble 过半服务器确认后才算成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the majority of ensemble servers whose acknowledgment a ZooKeeper write needs before it succeeds.

optionMeanings: 选 ZooKeeper：靠会话和临时节点保证强一致与自动崩溃检测。
选 Redis：靠 TTL 实现，吞吐更高但一致性较弱。
认为两个方案在这个场景下等价。
放弃加锁，改用重试兜底。
optionScenarioImpacts: 锁持有数小时也不怕漏检崩溃，会话超时是可靠信号。
TTL 需要精确设置成远超预期持锁时长，否则锁会提前失效引发并发写。
金融交易场景一旦并发写入，后果是资金错误，不能『随便选』。
没有锁保护的并发交易可能导致重复扣款或超卖资金。
optionDirectness: 最直接：完全匹配『正确性优先、长持有、可靠崩溃检测』。
不直接：性能优先在这个场景权重最低。
不直接：回避了做决策，掩盖了真实取舍。
不直接：重试不能替代互斥这一根本需求。
optionMeanings_en: Choose ZooKeeper: sessions and ephemeral nodes give strong consistency and automatic crash detection.
Choose Redis: TTL-based, higher throughput but weaker consistency guarantees.
Treat both options as equivalent for this scenario.
Skip locking and rely on retries instead.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Locks can sit for hours without missing a crash, since session expiry is a reliable signal.
The TTL must be set far longer than the expected hold time, or the lock expires early and lets in concurrent writes.
In finance, a concurrent write means real monetary error, not something to leave to chance.
Unprotected concurrent transactions risk duplicate charges or overspending funds.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: matches correctness-first, long-hold, reliable-crash-detection exactly.
Not direct: throughput is the lowest priority in this scenario.
Not direct: avoids the decision and hides the real tradeoff.
Not direct: retries cannot substitute for mutual exclusion.

q: ZooKeeper 内部靠什么协议达成共识？
q_en: Which protocol does ZooKeeper use internally for consensus?
options: Raft 协议，据说和 etcd 内部所使用的共识协议完全是同一套实现
ZAB（ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast）：让全体服务器在故障下仍对系统状态达成一致
Gossip 协议，节点之间随机两两交换状态信息、逐步扩散全局视图
关系型数据库里常见的两阶段锁协议，专门用来处理并发事务控制
options_en: Raft, supposedly the exact same implementation of the consensus protocol that etcd uses internally.
ZAB, ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast, which lets all servers agree on system state despite failures.
Gossip, where nodes randomly exchange state with each other in pairs to gradually spread a global view.
Two-phase locking, the classic relational-database protocol for concurrent transaction control.
why: 有趣的反讽：ZK 帮别人解决协调问题，自己得先解决自己的——答案就是 ZAB 协议。
why_en: ZooKeeper runs the ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast protocol so all its servers agree on system state despite failures.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZAB：ZooKeeper 内部使用的共识协议，负责 leader 选举与写操作的原子广播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZAB, ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast, is the consensus protocol ZooKeeper's own servers use for leader election and atomic write propagation.

termDefinitions.meaning: Raft：一种被广泛使用的分布式共识协议，etcd 等系统基于它实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Raft is a widely used distributed consensus protocol that systems like etcd are built on.

termDefinitions.meaning: Gossip 协议：节点间随机两两交换状态、逐步扩散信息的去中心化通信方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gossip protocols spread state by having nodes randomly exchange information with each other in a decentralized way.

q: ZAB 协议的两个主要阶段是？
q_en: What are the two main phases of the ZAB protocol?
options: 大数据批处理里常见的映射（Map）和归约（Reduce）两个阶段
存储引擎设计里常见的压缩和解压这两个流程阶段
先选出 leader 协调者，再由它做原子广播：写请求经 leader 广播，多数派确认才算成功
网络传输协议里常见的加密和解密这两个流程阶段
options_en: Map and Reduce, the familiar two phases from big-data batch processing.
Compress and decompress, the two phases common in storage engine design.
First elect a leader coordinator, then it does atomic broadcast: writes go through the leader and commit once a majority confirms.
Encrypt and decrypt, the two phases common in network transport protocols.
why: 先选主，再由主广播所有写并等 quorum 确认——两阶段合起来保证故障下的一致视图。
why_en: ZAB has leader election followed by atomic broadcast, where writes go through the leader and commit once a majority persists them.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Leader election"] --> B["Discovery"]
  B --> C["Sync"]
  C --> D["Broadcast writes"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子广播：leader 把一条写操作发给所有 follower，且保证要么大家都按同一顺序应用，要么不生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Atomic broadcast is the leader sending a write to all followers with the guarantee that everyone applies it in the same order, or not at all.

q: ZK 内部的 leader 选举标准，与应用层「最小顺序节点当 leader」的配方有什么有趣的差别？
q_en: How does ZooKeeper's internal leader election differ from the application recipe?
options: 两者的判断标准其实完全一样，内部选举和应用层都是序号最小的那个胜出
内部选举优先「事务历史最新」的服务器，历史相同时选 ID 最高的——方向恰好与应用层「最小序号获胜」相反
内部选举其实是按服务器主机名做字典序排序，直接取排在最前面的那一台
内部选举的结果其实完全由运维人员手工写进配置文件里去指定
options_en: Both use the exact same rule internally and at the application layer: the lowest sequence number wins.
Internally the server with the most up-to-date transaction history wins, ties broken by highest ID, the opposite of the application-layer rule.
Internal election actually just sorts servers by hostname in dictionary order and picks the first one.
The internal election result is actually entirely hand-written by an operator into a config file.
why: 内部要的是「数据最全的节点当 leader」（防丢更新），平局取最高 ID；应用层配方取最小序号——内部机制与其上构建的模式可以完全不同。
why_en: Internally ZooKeeper elects the server with the most up-to-date transaction history, preferring the highest ID on ties, the opposite of the lowest-sequence application recipe.
tradeoff: 内部选举「数据最全者优先」（防丢写）vs 应用层配方「最小序号优先」（排队公平）

q: ZAB 与 Paxos / Raft 的关系是？
q_en: How are ZAB, Paxos, and Raft related?
options: 三者的目标和实现完全不相关，只是名字看起来像
ZAB 只是对 Raft 协议做了一层简单封装
ZAB 的功能已经被 Paxos 完全取代，现在没人用了
同类目标：都是分布式共识协议；ZAB 早于 Raft，实现细节不同但高层目标一致
options_en: The three are unrelated in goal and implementation; they just sound similar.
ZAB is just a thin wrapper around the Raft protocol.
ZAB has been completely superseded by Paxos and nobody uses it now.
Same family: all are distributed consensus protocols; ZAB predates Raft and differs in details but shares the high-level goal.
why: ZAB、Paxos、Raft 都解决「多副本对状态达成一致」；面试里可以把 ZAB 类比成 ZK 自家的共识协议。
why_en: ZAB predates Raft and differs in implementation, but like Paxos and Raft it achieves distributed consensus.

termDefinitions.meaning: Paxos：最早提出的分布式共识协议之一，理论严谨但实现较复杂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Paxos is one of the earliest distributed consensus protocols, theoretically rigorous but notoriously hard to implement.

q: 补全 ZooKeeper 的一致性保证：
q_en: Fill in ZooKeeper's consistency guarantees.
text: 五大保证：{{顺序一致性}}（同一客户端的更新按发送顺序生效）、{{原子性}}（更新要么全成要么全败）、{{单一系统映像}}（连哪台服务器看到的视图一致）、{{持久性}}（确认过的更新不会丢）、及时性（客户端视图在有界时间内更新）。
why: 这五条是 ZK 可以被信任为「协调真相源」的原因；实现上全靠写走 leader 的全序 + quorum 持久化。
why_en: ZooKeeper guarantees sequential consistency, atomicity, a single system image, durability, and timeliness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序一致性：同一客户端发出的多个更新，所有服务器都按发送顺序应用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential consistency means updates from one client are applied by every server in the order that client sent them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单一系统映像：无论客户端连到 ensemble 里哪台服务器，同步后看到的数据视图都一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single system image means a client sees the same data view regardless of which ensemble server it connects to, once synced.

q: 从 follower 读数据可能读到旧值。需要最强一致的读时怎么办？
q_en: Follower reads can be stale. What should you do when you need the strongest read consistency?
options: 把所有读请求都强制改发给 leader 一台机器处理
读前先调用 sync 操作，确保该服务器已与 leader 同步再读
同一份数据读三次，取出现次数最多的那个结果
这个问题无解，只能接受可能读到旧数据
options_en: Force every read request to go only to the leader.
Call sync before reading, ensuring the server has caught up with the leader first.
Read the same value three times and take the majority result.
There is no fix — you just accept that reads may be stale.
why: follower 平时不为每次读询问 leader，所以可能滞后；sync 强制先追平再读，换来最新数据。
why_en: Follower reads can be stale, so clients call sync before reading when they need the most up-to-date view.

termDefinitions.meaning: sync：一个强制 follower 先追平 leader 最新状态、再返回读结果的操作，用于换取最强一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: sync is an operation that forces a follower to catch up with the leader's latest state before serving a read, trading latency for the strongest consistency.

scenario: 选型时要判断 ZooKeeper 是否适合当前系统：读多写少的服务发现场景，还是写多读少的日志采集场景。
scenario_en: During technology selection, you need to decide whether ZooKeeper fits this workload: read-heavy service discovery or write-heavy log collection.
q: ZooKeeper 架构最适合怎样的读写比例？
q_en: What read/write ratio is ZooKeeper architecture best suited for?
options: 写多读少：大部分请求是更新配置或路由信息
读写各占一半，二者请求量基本相当
读远多于写，约 10:1 的读写比
只有读请求，几乎不产生任何写请求
options_en: Write-heavy: most requests update config or routing information.
Roughly even split between reads and writes.
Read-dominant, around a ten-to-one read-to-write ratio.
Read-only, with almost no write requests at all.
why: 读由任意节点从内存直接服务（快、不用等 quorum），写必须过 leader 走 ZAB 等多数派确认（贵）——架构天生偏向读主导负载，约 10:1 是经验值，决定了该不该用 ZK 承载你的负载。
why_en: ZooKeeper excels at read-dominant workloads around ten reads per write, since any server serves reads but all writes go through the leader.

q: ZooKeeper 会话（session）机制的要点是？
q_en: What are the key points of ZooKeeper sessions?
options: 会话一旦建立成功就永不过期，客户端可以一直保持连接下去
会话本质上就是一条 TCP 连接，这条连接一断会话就立刻失效
会话完全由 ensemble 的 leader 手动维护，客户端不参与任何交互
客户端建立带超时（典型 10-30 秒）的会话，靠心跳维持；断连后可换服务器恢复会话，过期则清理其临时节点和 watch
options_en: Once established, a session never expires and the client can stay connected forever.
A session is essentially just one TCP connection, and it dies the instant that connection drops.
Sessions are entirely managed by the ensemble leader with no client-side involvement at all.
Clients hold a heartbeat-maintained session with a typical 10-30 second timeout; expiry cleans up its ephemeral nodes and watches.
why: 会话是临时节点和故障检测的地基：心跳没到、超时到期，就视为客户端死亡并自动清理它的痕迹。
why_en: Clients hold heartbeat-maintained sessions with a ten-to-thirty-second timeout, and expiry deletes their ephemeral nodes and watches.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Client session"] --> B["Heartbeat"]
  B --> C{"Timeout?"}
  C -->|"no"| A
  C -->|"yes"| D["Delete ephemeral nodes"]

termDefinitions.meaning: session（会话）：客户端与 ZooKeeper 之间靠心跳维持的逻辑连接，可以跨越多次 TCP 重连而存续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session is a heartbeat-maintained logical connection between client and ZooKeeper that can survive multiple TCP reconnects.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP：一种保证有序、可靠传输的底层网络协议；ZooKeeper 会话建立在 TCP 连接之上，但会话本身能跨越重连存续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is the underlying reliable, ordered transport protocol; a ZooKeeper session sits on top of a TCP connection but can outlive a single reconnect.

optionMeanings: 认为会话没有过期机制。
把会话等同于底层 TCP 连接本身。
认为客户端在会话机制里毫无参与。
会话有超时、靠心跳续期，可跨连接恢复，过期触发清理。
optionScenarioImpacts: 崩溃的客户端永远占着它注册的临时节点，故障检测彻底失效。
网络抖动引发的短暂断连会被误判为客户端死亡，引发不必要的切换。
无法解释为什么客户端要发心跳、为什么能在超时前换机重连。
既能容忍网络抖动（超时内重连即可恢复），又能在真崩溃时清理干净。
optionDirectness: 不直接：违背『超时清理』这一故障检测基础。
不直接：混淆了传输层连接和会话这两个概念。
不直接：会话机制本就需要客户端心跳配合。
最直接：完整覆盖超时、心跳、恢复、过期清理四个要点。
optionMeanings_en: Claims sessions never expire.
Equates a session with the underlying TCP connection itself.
Claims the client plays no role in session handling.
Sessions time out, renew via heartbeat, can recover across reconnects, and clean up on expiry.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A crashed client would hold its ephemeral nodes forever, breaking failure detection entirely.
A brief network blip gets misread as client death, triggering needless failover.
Fails to explain why clients heartbeat or how they can reconnect to a new server before timeout.
Tolerates network blips (reconnect within timeout) while still cleaning up after real crashes.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: contradicts the timeout-based cleanup that failure detection relies on.
Not direct: conflates the transport-layer connection with the session concept.
Not direct: session handling inherently needs client heartbeats.
Most direct: covers timeout, heartbeat, recovery, and expiry cleanup fully.

q: 会话超时（session timeout）设置的两难是？
q_en: What tradeoff does the ZooKeeper session timeout setting create?
options: 设太短：临时网络抖动就误判死亡引发不必要的失效/切换；设太长：真故障要等很久才被发现
无论把这个值设得再长或者再短，实际观察到的效果完全一样
会话超时值只会小幅影响服务器进程的内存占用大小
会话超时值只会影响 ZooKeeper 每天写出的日志文件总量
options_en: Too short causes false failovers on network blips; too long delays detecting real failures.
Setting the value longer or shorter produces exactly the same observed effect either way.
The timeout value only has a minor effect on how much memory the server process uses.
The timeout value only affects how much log file volume ZooKeeper writes out per day.
why: 这是所有故障检测的通用权衡：灵敏 vs 稳定。10-30 秒的典型值就是在两者间折中。
why_en: A short session timeout causes false failovers on network blips, while a long one delays detecting real failures.

q: ZooKeeper 靠什么保证「确认过的更新永不丢失」？
q_en: How does ZooKeeper make sure acknowledged updates are not lost?
options: 把每一次写操作产生的数据都顺手额外同步一份到远端云对象存储服务里去
每个状态变更先写持久化的事务日志（WAL，须先落盘再响应）；周期性做内存数据库快照，重启时加载快照+重放日志恢复
只要在三台服务器各自的内存里都稳定保留一份副本数据就已经足够可靠
让每一个连接进来的客户端都在本地缓存一份完整数据作为额外的备份手段
options_en: Every write also gets an extra sync out to a remote cloud object storage service.
Each change is first written to a persistent write-ahead transaction log, then periodic snapshots speed up recovery by replaying the log.
Keeping one steady in-memory replica on each of three servers is already reliable enough.
Every connected client also keeps a full local cache of the data as an extra backup measure.
why: WAL + 快照是经典持久化组合：日志保证不丢，快照加速恢复。官方强调事务日志是 ZK 最性能攸关的部分，建议独立日志盘。
why_en: Every change is synced to a write-ahead transaction log before responding, and periodic snapshots speed up recovery on restart.

termDefinitions.meaning: WAL（预写日志）：先把变更写进持久化日志、确认落盘后才响应客户端的技术，保证崩溃不丢已确认的更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records a change durably before responding to the client, guaranteeing acknowledged updates survive a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 快照：内存数据库某一时刻的完整落盘副本，重启时先加载快照再重放之后的日志，加速恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A snapshot is a point-in-time on-disk copy of the in-memory database; restart loads it first and then replays the log for faster recovery.

q: 为什么内存交换（swapping）对 ZooKeeper 性能是灾难性的？
q_en: Why is swapping disastrous for ZooKeeper performance?
options: swap 会直接损坏磁盘上已经持久化的事务日志数据
swap 发生时 ZooKeeper 会强制断开所有已连接的客户端
ZK 的所有操作是全序执行的：一个请求因 swap 卡在磁盘，后面排队的所有请求都被拖住
swap 只会让 watch 通知机制暂时失效几秒钟
options_en: Swapping directly corrupts the transaction log already persisted on disk.
Swapping forces ZooKeeper to disconnect every connected client immediately.
All operations execute in total order: one request stuck on disk due to swap delays every request queued behind it.
Swapping only makes the watch notification mechanism briefly stop working for a few seconds.
why: 全序流水线意味着「一人慢全队慢」；堆大小要保证数据集全在内存、绝不触发 swap。
why_en: Because all operations are totally ordered, one request hitting swap delays every queued request behind it.

q: 网络分区导致任何一组服务器都凑不齐多数派时，ZooKeeper 会怎样？
q_en: What does ZooKeeper do when no network partition can form a majority?
options: 分区两边的服务器各自继续独立处理写请求，等分区恢复后再合并数据
自动在云上现拉起几台新的服务器节点来补足所需的多数派
由系统随机挑其中一边的服务器组，继续处理这一边的写请求
停止处理写请求直到分区恢复——宁可不可用也要避免 split-brain（脑裂）
options_en: Both sides of the partition keep processing writes independently and merge the data after it heals.
It automatically spins up a few new servers in the cloud to restore a majority.
The system randomly picks one side of the partition to keep processing its writes.
It stops processing writes until the partition heals, choosing unavailability over split-brain.
why: 没有多数派就不写，防止系统两半各持一套「真相」；这是 CP 系统的典型选择。
why_en: Without a majority ZooKeeper refuses writes until the partition heals, preventing split-brain disagreement.

termDefinitions.meaning: split-brain（脑裂）：网络分区后系统两半各自独立接受写入，产生两份互相矛盾的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Split-brain is when a network partition lets both halves of a system independently accept writes, producing two conflicting copies of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: CP 系统：在 CAP 权衡中优先保证一致性和分区容忍、宁可牺牲可用性的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CP system is one that, in the CAP tradeoff, prioritizes consistency and partition tolerance even at the cost of availability.

q: 把「聊天服务器崩溃后 ZooKeeper 的自动处理」排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put ZooKeeper's automatic handling of a crashed chat server in the right order.
steps: 其它 watch 这些节点的服务器收到通知，更新路由表、把用户标记下线
Server 2 崩溃
它创建的所有临时节点被自动删除（服务器注册节点 + 名下用户节点）
Server 2 的 ZK 会话超时（典型 10-30 秒后）
why: 崩溃 → 会话超时 → 临时节点消失 → watcher 收通知并响应。全程无需人工干预——这是 ZK 最强大的特性之一。
why_en: After a crash the session times out, its ephemeral nodes are deleted, and watching servers get notified and update their routing automatically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Server 2 崩溃"] --> T["会话超时"]
    T --> D["临时节点自动删除"]
    D --> N["watcher 收到通知\n更新路由/标记下线"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 会话超时：客户端超过约定时间没有发送心跳，ZooKeeper 判定其会话失效并清理其临时节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session timeout is when a client misses heartbeats for the agreed window, so ZooKeeper marks its session expired and cleans up its ephemeral nodes.

q: 今天哪些系统仍然依赖 ZooKeeper？
q_en: Which systems still depend on ZooKeeper today?
options: Apache 生态核心组件：HBase、Hadoop、Storm、Pulsar 等；ClickHouse 复制协调也依赖它
有人误以为 Kubernetes 的核心调度组件是直接构建在 ZooKeeper 协调服务之上的
几乎所有主流的云托管数据库和缓存产品线，据说如今都还依赖它来做协调
有人认为已经完全没有任何生产系统还在实际使用 ZooKeeper 了
options_en: Core Apache-ecosystem components: HBase, Hadoop, Storm, Pulsar and more; ClickHouse also relies on it for replication coordination.
Some mistakenly believe Kubernetes' core scheduler is built directly on top of the ZooKeeper coordination service.
Some claim nearly every mainstream cloud-managed database and cache product line today still depends on it.
Some believe there is no production system left anywhere that actually still uses ZooKeeper.
why: ZK 在 Apache 生态依然是台柱；ClickHouse 的复制部署也要求它。它老了，但没退休。
why_en: ZooKeeper remains central to HBase, Hadoop, SolrCloud, Storm, NiFi, and Pulsar, and ClickHouse requires it for replication coordination.

q: Kafka 摆脱 ZooKeeper 的举动（KRaft）说明了什么趋势？
q_en: What trend does Kafka's move away from ZooKeeper with KRaft show?
options: 说明共识协议这类机制在分布式系统里已经变得不再重要
说明所有系统今后都应该反过来外挂一个 ZooKeeper 集群才对
转向「自带内置共识协议的自包含系统」：KRaft 消除了外部协调服务带来的运维复杂度、扩展瓶颈和故障点
说明 Kafka 已经彻底放弃了分布式架构，改回单机部署模式
options_en: It shows consensus mechanisms like this no longer matter in distributed systems.
It shows every system should now instead bolt on an external ZooKeeper cluster.
A shift toward self-contained systems with built-in consensus: KRaft removes the ops complexity, scaling bottlenecks, and failure points of an external coordinator.
It shows Kafka has completely abandoned distributed architecture and gone back to single-node deployment.
why: 多年依赖后，Kafka 用内置 Raft 元数据模式替换 ZK——外部协调服务正在被内嵌共识取代，这是大势。
why_en: Kafka's move to KRaft reflects a broader trend toward self-contained systems with built-in consensus instead of external coordination services.

termDefinitions.meaning: KRaft：Kafka 内置的基于 Raft 的元数据管理模式，用来取代外部 ZooKeeper 依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KRaft is Kafka's built-in Raft-based metadata mode that replaces its former dependency on external ZooKeeper.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：分布式消息队列/事件流平台，曾长期用 ZooKeeper 管理集群元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and event-streaming platform that long relied on ZooKeeper for cluster metadata.

optionMeanings: 认为共识协议整体已经过时。
认为所有系统都该反过来依赖 ZooKeeper。
Kafka 用内置 Raft（KRaft）取代外部 ZooKeeper 协调。
误以为 KRaft 是放弃分布式的信号。
optionScenarioImpacts: 但 KRaft 恰恰是用另一种共识协议（Raft）替代，说明共识依然核心。
现实相反：Kafka 正在移除对 ZooKeeper 的外部依赖。
运维只需管理 Kafka 自身进程，不再需要单独运维一套 ZK 集群。
KRaft 之后 Kafka 依旧是多 broker 分布式集群，只是元数据管理方式变了。
optionDirectness: 不直接：与 KRaft 本身就是共识协议的事实矛盾。
不直接：方向与实际趋势完全相反。
最直接：准确描述了 KRaft 消除外部协调依赖的动机和效果。
不直接：混淆了元数据管理方式变化和架构模式变化。
optionMeanings_en: Claims consensus protocols are obsolete overall.
Claims every system should now depend on ZooKeeper instead.
Kafka replaces external ZooKeeper coordination with built-in Raft (KRaft).
Mistakes KRaft for Kafka abandoning distributed architecture.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: But KRaft replaces it with another consensus protocol, Raft, so consensus is still core.
The reality is the opposite: Kafka is removing its external ZooKeeper dependency.
Operators now only manage Kafka's own processes, no separate ZooKeeper cluster.
Post-KRaft Kafka is still a multi-broker distributed cluster; only metadata management changed.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: contradicts the fact that KRaft is itself a consensus protocol.
Not direct: the direction is the opposite of the real trend.
Most direct: accurately captures why KRaft removes the external coordination dependency.
Not direct: conflates a metadata-management change with an architectural retreat.

q: etcd 相对 ZooKeeper 的定位是？
q_en: How is etcd positioned relative to ZooKeeper?
options: 很多人误以为 etcd 只是把 ZooKeeper 原封不动地用 Java 语言重新实现了一遍而已
云原生世界的协调新贵：强一致分布式 KV，现代 HTTP/JSON 与 gRPC API，是 Kubernetes 的底座
很多人以为 etcd 只能拿来做服务发现，完全不支持用它存放配置数据
很多人误以为 etcd 本质是最终一致的存储系统，不提供任何强一致性保证
options_en: Many mistakenly believe etcd is just ZooKeeper reimplemented in Java, unchanged, one to one.
The cloud-native coordinator: a strongly consistent distributed key-value store with modern HTTP/JSON and gRPC APIs, the base of Kubernetes.
Many believe etcd can only be used for service discovery and does not support storing configuration at all.
Many mistakenly believe etcd is fundamentally an eventually consistent store with no strong consistency guarantee.
why: etcd 与 ZK 解决同类问题（配置管理、服务发现），但 API 更现代、与云原生生态深度绑定。
why_en: Etcd offers strongly consistent key-value coordination with modern HTTP and gRPC APIs and powers Kubernetes.
tradeoff: etcd 的现代云原生 API + Kubernetes 深度集成 vs ZooKeeper 的 Apache 生态成熟度 + 更丰富的原生配方（选举/锁）

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd：基于 Raft 协议的强一致分布式键值存储，是 Kubernetes 的核心元数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a strongly consistent distributed key-value store built on Raft that serves as Kubernetes' core metadata store.

termDefinitions.meaning: gRPC：Google 开源的高性能 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和 Protocol Buffers。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance remote-procedure-call framework built on HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP/JSON：用标准 HTTP 请求携带 JSON 格式数据的接口风格，浏览器和多数语言都能直接用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/JSON is an API style using standard HTTP requests with JSON payloads, directly usable from browsers and most languages.

optionMeanings: 误以为 etcd 是 ZooKeeper 的语言移植版。
etcd：现代 API、强一致 KV，是 Kubernetes 的底座。
低估了 etcd 的配置存储能力。
误判 etcd 的一致性模型为最终一致。
optionScenarioImpacts: 两者协议、数据模型、API 完全不同，不是简单的语言移植。
云原生团队选它做配置中心和服务发现的统一存储。
etcd 的 KV 接口天然适合存配置，且是很多平台配置中心的底层实现。
etcd 基于 Raft，和 ZAB 一样提供强一致写，不是最终一致。
optionDirectness: 不直接：混淆了『解决同类问题』和『同一个实现』。
最直接：准确概括了 etcd 的 API、一致性模型与定位。

Consul 不做健康检查，这方面反而不如 ZooKeeper

q: ZooKeeper 的「热点问题（hot spotting）」指什么？
q_en: What does ZooKeeper hot spotting mean?
options: 服务器 CPU 长期处于持续高负载运行状态，触发了系统自动降频保护机制
大量客户端 watch 同一个 ZNode（选举、锁的常态）时，通知流量可能压垮服务器——热门节点成为瓶颈
系统会自动把被频繁访问的热数据迁移到内存容量更大的机器上去
磁盘上的某个存储扇区因为被反复频繁写入而提前发生物理损坏
options_en: Servers throttle their own CPU frequency after sustained continuous high load.
When many clients watch the same znode, common in election or locks, notification traffic can overwhelm servers — popular nodes become bottlenecks.
The system automatically migrates frequently accessed hot data onto machines with larger memory capacity.
A specific storage sector wears out and fails early from being written to over and over.
why: 想象聊天例子里百万用户同时上线：同一节点的海量 watch 通知是规模化的天花板之一。
why_en: When many clients watch the same znode, notification traffic can overwhelm the servers and popular nodes become bottlenecks.

termDefinitions.meaning: hot spotting（热点问题）：大量请求或 watch 集中在同一个节点上，导致该节点及其所在服务器成为瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hot spotting is when a large volume of requests or watches concentrate on a single node, turning it and its server into a bottleneck.

q: ZooKeeper 的主要局限有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are ZooKeeper's main limitations? (Select all that apply.)
options: 写昂贵：必须经 leader 传播到多数派
内存存储模型限制容量：ZNode 要 <1MB、数据集须装进内存
运维复杂：JVM 参数、磁盘布局、超时与连接监控——「用起来简单，运维起来复杂」
不支持 watch 通知，只能靠轮询感知变化
options_en: Writes are expensive: they must propagate through the leader to a majority.
Capacity is memory-bound: znodes must stay under one megabyte and the dataset must fit in memory.
Operationally complex: JVM tuning, disk layout, timeout and connection monitoring — simple to use, complex to operate.
It does not support watch notifications, so changes can only be detected by polling.
why: 存大量数据、扛超高写入、或想最小化运维时，都该考虑替代方案；watch 恰恰是它的招牌能力，不是局限。
why_en: ZooKeeper writes are expensive through leader and quorum, capacity is memory-bound with small znodes, and it is simple to use but complex to operate.

termDefinitions.meaning: JVM：运行 Java 程序的虚拟机；ZooKeeper 用 Java 实现，堆大小等 JVM 参数需要仔细调优。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The JVM is the runtime that executes Java programs; ZooKeeper is written in Java, so JVM settings like heap size need careful tuning.

scenario: 设计 Facebook Live Comments / YouTube Live Chat：百万观众看同一直播，希望同一直播间的 websocket 连接尽量集中到同一台（组）服务器以减少跨服务器通信。
scenario_en: You are designing Facebook Live Comments or YouTube Live Chat. Millions of viewers watch the same stream, and you want connections for one room concentrated on the same server group to reduce cross-server traffic.
q: ZooKeeper 在这里扮演什么角色？
q_en: What role does ZooKeeper play in this live-chat routing design?
options: 让 ZooKeeper 直接充当消息队列，转发全部实时评论的消息本体内容
把每一条历史评论的完整内容都存进 ZooKeeper 里，方便日后回放
作为 API 网关的协调点：维护「哪个房间/直播由哪台服务器负责」的映射；服务器带容量注册，新连接按房间查 ZK 定向
给每一条实时评论单独加一把分布式锁，用来防止重复展示
options_en: Have ZooKeeper act directly as the message queue forwarding every live comment's payload content.
Store the full content of every historical comment inside ZooKeeper for later replay.
Act as the API gateway's coordination point, mapping which server handles which room, with capacity-aware registration and routing.
Put an individual distributed lock on each live comment to prevent it from being shown twice.
why: 这是「智能路由/同房间同服务器（colocation）」的高级用法——Staff+ 或深度分布式面试的加分项。
why_en: ZooKeeper coordinates smart routing by mapping rooms to servers so a gateway can colocate all viewers of a stream on the same server group.
whenOtherWins: 普通规模的聊天用 pub/sub 广播就能绕开大部分协调问题，不必上这套。
tradeoff: ZK 做房间→服务器的协调映射（轻量、可扩展）vs 把评论本体也塞进 ZK（违反小数据原则、写爆）

termDefinitions.meaning: colocation（同机集中路由）：把同一房间/直播的所有连接尽量路由到同一台或同一组服务器，减少跨服务器通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Colocation routing means directing all connections for the same room or stream to the same server or server group, minimizing cross-server chatter.

q: 设计「分布式消息队列」时，ZooKeeper 可以作为共识大脑承担哪些职责？（多选）
q_en: In a distributed message queue, which responsibilities can ZooKeeper handle as the consensus brain? (Select all that apply.)
options: broker 注册与发现、topic 元数据（分区数、副本因子）存储
每个分区的 leader 选举（顺序临时节点保证单一 leader）
consumer group 成员关系与分区分配，broker 故障经临时节点触发分区重分配
存储全部消息本体，让 broker 直接从 ZK 读写消息内容
options_en: Broker registration and discovery, plus topic metadata like partition count and replication factor.
Per-partition leader election, using sequential ephemeral nodes to guarantee a single leader.
Consumer group membership and partition assignment, with broker failure triggering reassignment via ephemeral nodes.
Storing the full message payloads so brokers read and write message content directly from ZooKeeper.
why: KRaft 之前的 Kafka 正是这么用 ZK 的；HBase、Hadoop、Solr 也是类似模式。消息本体走 broker 自己的日志存储，绝不放 ZK。
why_en: In a distributed queue design ZooKeeper handles broker registration, topic metadata, partition leader election, consumer membership, and failure detection, never the message payloads.
tradeoff: ZK 管协调元数据（小、强一致）vs broker 自管消息日志（大、高吞吐）——两者不能互换

termDefinitions.meaning: broker：消息队列集群里负责接收、存储、转发消息的服务器节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broker is a server node in a message-queue cluster responsible for receiving, storing, and forwarding messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: consumer group（消费组）：一组共同消费同一批分区、彼此分摊负载的消费者客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumer clients that jointly consume a set of partitions, sharing the load among themselves.

scenario: 分布式文件系统需要「目录及其文件」的嵌套锁获取，要防死锁，还要能监控整个锁层级的变化。
scenario_en: A distributed file system needs nested locks for directories and files. It must avoid deadlocks and watch changes across the whole lock hierarchy.
q: 为什么这里 ZooKeeper 严格优于 Redis？
q_en: Why is ZooKeeper strictly better than Redis in this case?
options: 因为部署 ZooKeeper 集群的机器成本比部署 Redis 更加便宜
ZK 的层级命名空间天然表达父子锁结构，能同时 watch 多个节点监控整个锁层级；Redis 缺少层级与联动通知
因为 Redis 这个产品根本就没有实现过分布式锁的能力
因为 ZooKeeper 锁的整体写入吞吐量比 Redis 锁要高得多
options_en: Because running a ZooKeeper cluster costs less hardware than running Redis.
ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace naturally expresses parent-child lock structure and can watch multiple nodes across the whole hierarchy; Redis lacks that hierarchy and linked notification.
Because Redis as a product has never implemented any distributed-lock capability.
Because ZooKeeper locks have much higher overall write throughput than Redis locks.
why: 资源有父子关系、锁获取要尊重层级时，ZK 的树形结构 + 多点 watch 是量身定制；Redis 锁是平面的。
why_en: ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace and multi-node watches express nested directory-file locks with deadlock prevention, which flat Redis locks cannot.
whenOtherWins: 普通的单资源短锁（订单、座位）Redis 又快又简单，是默认选择。
tradeoff: ZooKeeper 的层级命名空间+多点 watch（表达父子锁结构）vs Redis 的平面 key 空间（无天然层级）

The overriding constraint here is correctness and hierarchy expression, not throughput.

不管遇到什么场景，面试全程都绝口不提 ZooKeeper 这个词

q: 一次写请求（如注册 Bob 的 ZNode）在 ensemble 内部的流转是？
q_en: How does a write request, such as registering Bob's ZNode, flow through the ensemble?
options: 任意一台 follower 收到写请求后直接写本地磁盘，就可以立刻返回写成功
请求到 leader → leader 向所有 follower 广播变更 → 多数派确认已接受并保存 → leader 确认写成功
客户端把同一条写请求原样同时发送给 ensemble 里的每一台服务器
每台服务器先各自把数据写到本地磁盘，之后再统一去问 leader 这次写是否有效
options_en: Any follower that receives the write just writes to its local disk and returns success right away.
The request reaches the leader, which broadcasts the change to followers, and it succeeds once a majority has accepted and saved it.
The client sends the exact same write request to every single server in the ensemble at once.
Every server first writes to its own local disk, then afterward asks the leader whether that write was valid.
why: 写必须过 leader 并拿到 quorum 确认——这正是写比读贵、但一致性有保障的原因。
why_en: A write goes to the leader, which broadcasts it to followers and confirms success once a majority has accepted and saved it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Client write"] --> B["Leader proposal"]
  B --> C["Quorum ack"]
  C --> D["Commit"]
  D --> E["Watch events"]

scenario: 团队在讨论要不要把一份几 MB 大小的完整用户资料 JSON 直接存进一个 ZNode，还是只存一个指向对象存储的引用；ZooKeeper 的设计前提是 ZNode 只放协调元数据，不放大文件。
scenario_en: The team is deciding whether to store a multi-MB user profile JSON directly in one ZNode or store only a pointer to object storage. ZooKeeper is meant for coordination metadata, not large files.
q: 遵循这个设计边界，单个 ZNode 承载的数据量上限应该设为？
q_en: Under this design boundary, what data-size limit should a single ZNode follow?
options: 1KB，比官方建议严格得多，几乎存不下任何真实配置
10MB，远超官方建议，容易在快照/日志里造成额外压力
1MB，符合官方建议：ZNode 只放小量协调数据，数据集要能整个装进内存
1GB，把 ZNode 当文件存储用，完全违背 ZooKeeper 的设计前提
options_en: 1KB, far stricter than the guideline, barely enough for any real config.
10MB, well past the guideline, adding extra pressure to snapshots and logs.
1MB, matching the guideline: znodes hold only small coordination data and the dataset must fit in memory.
1GB, treating a znode like file storage, which defeats ZooKeeper's whole design premise.
why: ZNode 定位是小协调数据：保持在 1MB 以下，整个数据集要能装进内存；超过这个量级就该把大对象放对象存储/DB，ZNode 只存一个引用指针。
why_en: Keep each znode under one megabyte and ensure the whole dataset fits in memory; anything bigger belongs in object storage with just a reference stored in the znode.

scenario: 配置聊天服务器的 ZooKeeper 客户端会话超时参数，要在「网络抖动误判」和「故障发现太慢」之间找平衡。
scenario_en: You are configuring the ZooKeeper client session timeout for chat servers and need to balance false failure detection from network jitter against slow real-failure detection.
q: ZooKeeper 会话超时的典型配置区间是？
q_en: What is the typical ZooKeeper session timeout range?
options: 10-30 毫秒，几乎任何一次网络抖动都会触发误判
10-30 秒，兼顾故障发现速度和抗网络抖动能力
10-30 分钟，故障发现会慢到影响用户体验
10-30 小时，几乎等于关闭了故障检测能力
options_en: 10-30 milliseconds, where almost any network blip triggers a false failure.
10-30 seconds, balancing fast failure detection against tolerance for network blips.
10-30 minutes, slow enough to noticeably hurt user experience during a real failure.
10-30 hours, which effectively disables failure detection.
why: 10-30 秒是「误报 vs 检测速度」的常见折中——短于此网络抖动就会引发误判切换，长于此真故障要等太久才被发现，而这个窗口也正是临时节点消失、下游 watcher 收到通知的时间量级。
why_en: Session timeouts are typically ten to thirty seconds, balancing false-positive failovers against how long real failure detection via ephemeral nodes takes.

q: 补全 ZooKeeper 的三大基础原语：
q_en: Fill in ZooKeeper's three basic primitives.
text: ZooKeeper 靠三个简单原语组合出所有协调能力：{{ZNode}}（层级命名空间中的数据节点）、可靠的服务器 {{ensemble}}（多数派容错）、{{watch}}（变更实时通知）。
why: 数据模型 + 可靠集群 + 通知机制——三件套组合出配置管理、服务发现、选举与锁的全部配方。
why_en: ZooKeeper combines znodes in a hierarchical namespace, a reliable server ensemble, and watches for change notification.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZNode：层级命名空间里的一个数据节点，能存少量数据、能有子节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A znode is a node in the hierarchical namespace that can hold a small amount of data and have children.

termDefinitions.meaning: ensemble：一组协同工作、以多数派（quorum）容错的 ZooKeeper 服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ensemble is the group of ZooKeeper servers working together with majority-based fault tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: watch：客户端登记在 ZNode 上的一次性变更通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watch is a one-time change notification a client registers on a znode.

Core concepts are technology-agnostic building blocks — caching, sharding, consistency — that show up in almost every design problem; interviewers assume you know them and will probe once you propose a specific technology.
Core concepts only show up in academic courses, not real work.
There is no difference; learning one technology means you already know the concepts.

why_en: Cache only data that is read frequently and changes rarely; caching data that changes every request adds latency and complexity for nothing.

q: 什么信号说明你可能真的需要分片？（多选）
q_en: Which signals mean you may actually need sharding? Select all that apply.
options: 存储逼近单实例上限（单个 Postgres 到 TB 量级封顶）
写吞吐到顶（数万写/秒）
读吞吐连读副本都扛不住
用户数刚过一万
options_en: Storage nears a single instance's limit, like a Postgres instance capping out in the terabytes.
Write throughput hits its ceiling, tens of thousands of writes per second.
Read throughput that even read replicas cannot handle.
The user count just crossed ten thousand.
optionScenarioImpacts: 提示要按存储上限规划分片，不是凭感觉
单库写路径成为瓶颈，是最常见的真实触发点
说明加读副本这条路已经走到头，该水平切分了
用户数不是负载指标，跟数据库扛不扛得住无关
why: 分片的三个触发条件：存储、写吞吐、副本也救不了的读吞吐；用户数本身不是理由，要看负载数字。
why_en: Shard when you hit storage limits, write throughput limits, or read throughput that even replicas cannot handle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

q: 分片时最重要的决策是什么？以 Instagram 为例说明取舍。
q_en: What is the most important sharding decision, and how does Instagram illustrate it?
options: 选数据库品牌
选机房位置
选 shard key
选分片数量
options_en: Choosing the database vendor.
Choosing the data center location.

Choosing the shard key: sharding by user id keeps a user's data on one shard so user-scoped queries are fast, but global queries like trending posts must hit every shard and aggregate, which gets expensive.
Choosing the number of shards.
why: shard key 决定数据怎么分布、什么查询快什么查询贵，牵动整个设计——这是分片的第一决策。
why_en: The shard key is the most important decision: sharding Instagram by user id makes user-scoped queries fast but global queries expensive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落在哪个分片上的字段，牵动整个分片设计的查询快慢分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key decides which shard a row lands on, and it drives which queries end up fast versus expensive across the whole design.

q: hash 分片与 range 分片的取舍是？
q_en: What is the tradeoff between hash sharding and range sharding?
options: hash 均匀防热点；range 易过热
range 永远更均匀
hash 支持高效范围扫描
两者没有差别
options_en: Hash-based sharding, hashing the key then taking a modulo, distributes evenly and avoids hot spots, so it's what most systems use; range-based fits naturally partitioned access like multi-tenant SaaS but risks hot ranges.
Range-based is always more even.
Hash-based supports efficient range scans.
The two make no difference.
optionMeanings: 准确的取舍描述
方向反了
能力错配
无差异错误认知
optionDirectness: hash 分片适合均匀分布，range 分片适合范围扫描但要防热点。
时间递增写入用 range 很容易把最新分片打热。
hash 打散顺序，不能天然支持连续范围扫描。
负载均匀度和范围查询能力正是两者的差别。
optionDirectness_en: Hash sharding spreads load evenly; range sharding supports scans but needs hotspot control.
Range sharding with increasing timestamps can overheat the newest shard.
Hashing destroys order, so it does not naturally support contiguous range scans.
Load balance and range-query support are exactly where the two differ.
why: 还有目录式分片（查表定位）：灵活但每个请求多一跳依赖和延迟，面试里很少值得提。
why_en: Hash-based sharding distributes evenly and avoids hot spots, while range-based suits naturally partitioned access but risks hot ranges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 取哈希再取模来分配分片的方式，分布均匀、防热点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash-based sharding hashes the shard key and takes a modulo to assign a shard, distributing load evenly and avoiding hot spots.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 key 的区间连续分配分片的方式，适合天然分区的访问模式但容易局部过热。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Range-based sharding assigns contiguous key ranges to shards, fitting naturally partitioned access but risking hot ranges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一张查找表记录每条数据在哪个分片的方式，灵活但每次请求多一跳依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table to record which shard holds each item, flexible but adding an extra hop of dependency per request.

tradeoff: 分布均匀防热点 vs 保留天然区间局部性

q: 「10K 写/秒 + 100GB 数据就提议分片」的问题是？
q_en: What is wrong with proposing sharding at 10K writes per second and 100GB of data?
options: 没问题，早分片早安心
分片会降低可用性所以永远不该分
应该先换 NoSQL
过早分片，先做容量数学
options_en: No problem, sharding early means peace of mind.
Sharding lowers availability so it should never be done.
You should switch to NoSQL first.
It's premature — a well-tuned single database with read replicas handles far more than most people think; do the capacity math first and only shard when the numbers demand it.
why: 分片的最大错误是动手太早：10K 写/秒、100GB 离单库上限还很远，提前分片就是无谓地引入巨大复杂度。
why_en: The biggest sharding mistake is doing it too early; at ten thousand writes per second and a hundred gigabytes you do not need it yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.

q: 分片引入的新问题有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What new problems does sharding introduce? Select all that apply.
options: 跨分片事务几乎不可能——需要分布式事务或 saga，复杂且慢
热点分片：某个分片流量畸高（Taylor Swift 所在的分片被打爆，其他闲着）
resharding 痛苦：加分片要搬移海量数据
分片后不再需要考虑数据一致性问题
options_en: Cross-shard transactions become nearly impossible, needing distributed transactions or sagas, which are complex and slow.
Hot shards: one shard's traffic spikes far above the rest, like the shard holding Taylor Swift's data getting hammered while others sit idle.
Resharding is painful: adding a shard means moving massive amounts of data.
Sharding means you no longer need to think about data consistency.
optionScenarioImpacts: 跨分片边界的写操作会显著变慢、变复杂，甚至无法原子提交
单个分片被打爆时，扩容其他分片没有用，压力集中在一处
改分片数量意味着一次昂贵的数据重分布，不能说改就改
分片不解决一致性问题，反而让跨片一致性更难保证
why: 分片换来扩展性，同时带来跨片事务、热点、再分片三大痛；设计分片边界时要主动规避跨片操作。
why_en: Sharding makes cross-shard transactions nearly impossible, creates hot spots, and makes resharding a painful mass data migration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一串本地事务加补偿动作模拟跨分片/跨服务事务的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A saga simulates a cross-shard or cross-service transaction with a sequence of local transactions plus compensating actions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多个数据库/分片协调、要求要么全部提交要么全部回滚的事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed transaction coordinates commits across multiple databases or shards so they all succeed or all roll back together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个分片因为数据/流量倾斜而承受远高于其他分片的负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot shard carries far more load than the others because of skewed data or traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 改变分片数量或边界、需要重新搬移数据的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resharding is changing the number or boundaries of shards, which requires moving data around.

scenario: 面试进行到扩展性讨论，你想引入数据库分片。
scenario_en: In the scalability discussion, you want to introduce database sharding.
q: 正确的话术顺序是？
q_en: What is the right way to explain a sharding proposal in an interview?
options: 直接宣布「我们分 16 个片」
先证明必要性，再给 key 和取舍
说「大厂都分片所以我们也分」
让面试官决定要不要分
options_en: Just announce, "we'll shard into sixteen pieces."
First justify why a single database with read replicas is not enough with capacity math, then state the shard key, and explain the tradeoff of which queries get fast and which get slow.
Say, "big companies all shard, so we should too."
Let the interviewer decide whether to shard.
optionMeanings: 跳过论证
完整论证链条
诉诸权威
推卸决策
optionDirectness: 没证明单库到顶就先分片，会显得过早引入复杂度。
先给容量理由，再给 shard key，再说跨片代价和缓解。
引用大厂经验只能作背景，不能替代本题负载判断。
候选人要主动给决策和取舍，不能把选择交回面试官。
optionDirectness_en: Proposing sharding before proving the single DB is capped looks like premature complexity.
Give the capacity reason, then the shard key, then cross-shard costs and mitigations.
Big-company examples can be background, but they cannot replace workload math for this prompt.
The candidate should state the decision and tradeoff instead of handing it back to the interviewer.
why: 考官要的就是这条完整逻辑：先证明必要性，再给 key 和 tradeoff；多数面试到这一步就够了。
why_en: Justify why a single database will not work, state your shard key, and explain which queries get fast and which get slow.
whenOtherWins: 容量数学显示单库加副本就能扛时，「不分片」才是正确答案——把复杂度留给真正需要的地方。
tradeoff: 先证明必要性再动手 vs 直接报分片数节省时间

q: 把「Instagram 按 user_id 分片」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the Instagram user_id sharding decision chain in the right order.
steps: 代价：全局查询（全站热门帖）要打所有分片聚合，跨分片事务几乎不可能
需求：写入与存储超出单库上限，读副本也扛不住
缓解：设计分片边界避免跨片事务，全局查询走离线聚合/独立服务
选型：按 user_id 做 hash 分片，用户的帖子/点赞/评论同片
why: 需求（单库到顶）→ 选型（user_id 哈希分片）→ 代价（全局查询贵、跨片事务难）→ 缓解（边界设计 + 离线聚合）。
why_en: Outgrowing one database leads to hashing by user id, which makes global queries expensive, mitigated by shard-boundary design and offline aggregation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落在哪个分片上的字段，牵动整个分片设计的查询快慢分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key decides which shard a row lands on, and it drives which queries end up fast versus expensive across the whole design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 取哈希再取模来分配分片的方式，分布均匀、防热点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash-based sharding hashes the shard key and takes a modulo to assign a shard, distributing load evenly and avoiding hot spots.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多个数据库/分片协调、要求要么全部提交要么全部回滚的事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed transaction coordinates commits across multiple databases or shards so they all succeed or all roll back together.

diagram:
flowchart LR R["需求：单库到顶
写/存储超限"] --> C["选型：user_id 哈希分片"] C --> K["代价：全局查询贵
跨片事务难"] K --> M["缓解：边界设计
离线聚合"]
tradeoff: user_id 分片下用户查询变快 vs 全局聚合查询变贵

q: 用 hash(key) % N 分配服务器，增删一台服务器会发生什么？
q_en: With hash(key) modulo N server assignment, what happens when you add or remove a server?
options: N 变了，几乎所有 key 重新映射
只有新服务器的数据要动
什么都不会发生
数据自动均匀迁移，无成本
options_en: N changes, so almost every key maps to a different server — most data must move, a disaster at millions of entries.
Only the new server's data needs to move.
Nothing happens at all.
Data automatically migrates evenly at no cost.
why: 取模分布对 N 极度敏感；这正是一致性哈希要解决的问题。
why_en: With modulo hashing, adding or removing a server changes N so almost every key remaps and most data must move.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 key 的哈希值对服务器数 N 取余来决定归属的最简单分布方式，对 N 的变化极度敏感。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo hashing takes a key's hash mod the server count N to decide ownership, and it's extremely sensitive to any change in N.

codeSample:
server_index = hash(key) % N
# N: 10 -> 11 remaps almost every existing key

q: 一致性哈希的工作方式是？
q_en: How does consistent hashing work?
options: 按 key 首字母分配服务器
维护一张全局路由表
服务器和 key 哈希到虚拟环上
每次请求广播到所有节点
options_en: Assign servers by a key's first letter.
Maintain one global routing table.
Both servers and keys hash onto a virtual ring, and a key belongs to the next server found clockwise; adding a node only moves the keys between it and its neighbor.
Broadcast every request to all nodes.
optionMeanings: 朴素前缀分配
目录式分片的做法
环形局部化分配
全节点广播
optionDirectness: 按首字母切分只适合玩具例子，现实分布很容易倾斜。
目录式分片适合灵活迁移，但每次路由多查目录。
一致性哈希用环把增删节点影响限制在邻近区间。
广播适合发现或同步少量元数据，不适合定位数据归属。
optionDirectness_en: First-letter splitting only fits toy examples; real distributions skew badly.
Directory sharding supports flexible moves, but every route depends on a directory lookup.
Consistent hashing uses a ring to localize node add/remove impact to nearby ranges.
Broadcast can discover or sync small metadata, not locate data ownership.
why: 环结构把增删节点的影响局部化：移除节点时也只有它的 key 迁给环上的下一台。Memcached/Redis Cluster、Cassandra/DynamoDB、部分 LB 和 CDN 都在用。
why_en: Consistent hashing places servers and keys on a ring where each key belongs to the next server clockwise, so only a small range moves when nodes change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务器和 key 都映射到一个虚拟环上，增删节点只影响环上局部一小段 key 的分布算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps servers and keys onto a virtual ring so adding or removing a node only affects a small local range of keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希里承载服务器和 key 哈希值的环形结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The virtual ring is the circular structure that holds the hashed positions of servers and keys in consistent hashing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一张查找表记录每条数据在哪个分片的方式，灵活但每次请求多一跳依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table to record which shard holds each item, flexible but adding an extra hop of dependency per request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的分布式内存缓存系统，常用一致性哈希分布 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memcached is a common distributed in-memory cache that often uses consistent hashing to distribute keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 宽列分布式数据库，用一致性哈希做分片，强调高写入吞吐和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column distributed database that uses consistent hashing for sharding and emphasizes high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content on edge servers close to users.

scenario: 线上缓存/分片集群要弹性伸缩，纠结该用简单取模还是一致性哈希分配节点。
scenario_en: An online cache or shard cluster needs elastic scaling, and you are choosing modulo hashing or consistent hashing.
q: 10 台服务器的集群加 1 台：简单取模 vs 一致性哈希，各要移动多少数据？
q_en: In a 10-server cluster adding one server, how much data moves with modulo hashing versus consistent hashing?
options: 都是 50%
取模 ~90% vs 一致性哈希 ~10%
取模 ~10% vs 一致性哈希 ~90%
都不用移动
options_en: Both about fifty percent.
About ninety percent with modulo versus about ten percent with consistent hashing.
About ten percent with modulo versus about ninety percent with consistent hashing.
Neither needs to move any data.
why: 这组数字就是一致性哈希的价值：动态增删节点不再引发海量数据迁移，这个比例直接决定了扩缩容操作是否安全、可以随时做。
why_en: Adding one server to ten means moving about ninety percent of data with modulo hashing but only about ten percent with consistent hashing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 key 的哈希值对服务器数 N 取余来决定归属的最简单分布方式，对 N 的变化极度敏感。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo hashing takes a key's hash mod the server count N to decide ownership, and it's extremely sensitive to any change in N.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务器和 key 都映射到一个虚拟环上，增删节点只影响环上局部一小段 key 的分布算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps servers and keys onto a virtual ring so adding or removing a node only affects a small local range of keys.

codeSample:
# modulo: nearly all keys remap when N changes
server = hash(key) % N

# consistent hashing: only the range between the
# new node and its neighbor on the ring moves

scenario: 面试中讨论分布式缓存的弹性扩缩容：要按负载动态加减缓存节点或数据库分片。
scenario_en: In an interview about distributed cache scaling, nodes or shards may be added and removed based on load.
q: 关于一致性哈希，说到什么程度合适？
q_en: How much detail should you give about consistent hashing in an interview?
options: 现场手推环算法的数学证明
完全不提
点到为止，除非追问才展开
背诵虚拟节点的实现代码
options_en: Derive the ring algorithm's math proof on the spot.
Don't mention it at all.
Say just enough: "we'll use consistent hashing to distribute data across nodes so scaling doesn't trigger massive data migration," and expand only if asked.
Recite the virtual-node implementation code from memory.
why: 考官通常只想确认你知道这项技术；弹性伸缩场景点名它的作用即可，别自己展开长篇原理。
why_en: In interviews just say you will use consistent hashing to distribute data across nodes; explain the internals only if asked.
whenOtherWins: 若考官明确追问工作原理，再讲环、顺时针归属和局部迁移这套机制。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务器和 key 都映射到一个虚拟环上，增删节点只影响环上局部一小段 key 的分布算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps servers and keys onto a virtual ring so adding or removing a node only affects a small local range of keys.

tradeoff: 点到为止展示知识面 vs 深入原理占用宝贵面试时间

q: CAP 定理的准确表述是？
q_en: What is the accurate statement of the CAP theorem?
options: 三个都能同时拿到
只能同时满足两个；实际是 C vs A
CAP 只描述强一致系统，不适用于最终一致系统
只适用于单机数据库
options_en: All three can be had at once.

You can satisfy only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once; since partitions are unavoidable in distributed systems, the real choice is between consistency and availability.
CAP only describes strongly consistent systems, not eventually consistent ones.
It only applies to single-machine databases.
optionMeanings: 三者兼得的误解
准确的三选二表述
一致性模型范围的误解
系统层级适用范围的误解
optionDirectness: 网络分区不可避免时，系统不能同时保证强一致和全可用。
CAP 的面试重点是分区发生时，在一致性和可用性之间选。
CAP 讨论分布式系统的分区场景，不限定某一种一致性术语。
单机系统不面对网络分区，CAP 不是主要分析框架。
optionDirectness_en: When partitions happen, a system cannot guarantee strong consistency and full availability together.
The interview point of CAP is choosing consistency or availability during a partition.
CAP is about distributed partition scenarios, not one narrow consistency term.
Single-node systems do not face network partitions, so CAP is not the main frame.
why: C = 所有节点看到相同数据，A = 每个请求都有响应，P = 网络断裂时系统仍工作；P 是前提，真正的选择题是 C vs A。
why_en: CAP says you can have only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance, and since partitions are unavoidable you really choose between consistency and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络连接在节点间断开时系统仍要能工作的要求，在分布式系统里几乎不可避免要满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partition tolerance requires the system to keep working even when network links between nodes fail, and in practice it's unavoidable.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["Partition happens"] --> Choice{"Choose?"}
    Choice --> C["Consistency: reject stale"]
    Choice --> A["Availability: serve stale"]

q: 网络分区发生时，「选一致性」和「选可用性」的系统各自表现为？
q_en: During a network partition, how do consistency-first and availability-first systems behave?
options: 两者都直接宕机
两者都继续服务且数据一致
选 C 的系统所有节点数据分歧；选 A 的系统拒绝请求
选 C 拒绝服务；选 A 继续响应会分歧
options_en: Both go straight down.
Both keep serving with consistent data.
A consistency-first system has diverging data on every node; an availability-first system refuses requests.

Consistency-first: some nodes refuse to serve rather than risk returning stale data; availability-first: every node keeps responding, data may diverge temporarily, and it converges once the partition heals.
optionMeanings: 双双宕机的误解
鱼与熊掌兼得的误解
行为对调
准确的行为描述
optionDirectness: 选 C 的系统可能拒绝请求，选 A 的系统仍会响应。
分区时无法同时让所有副本一致又让所有请求成功。
把 C 和 A 的行为说反，会导致后续取舍全错。
分区期间，C 牺牲响应，A 牺牲短期一致。
optionDirectness_en: A C-first system may reject requests; an A-first system still responds.
During a partition, you cannot keep every replica consistent and every request successful.
Swapping C and A behavior breaks the later tradeoff analysis.
During the partition, C sacrifices responses and A sacrifices short-term consistency.
why: 选 C = 宁可拒绝服务也要数据正确；选 A = 宁可短暂不一致也要有响应。这是分区期间的行为差异。
why_en: A consistency-first system refuses requests rather than serve stale data during a partition, while an availability-first system keeps responding and converges later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

tradeoff: 拒绝请求保正确 vs 继续响应容忍分歧

scenario: 设计社交 feed、推荐系统或分析仪表盘，被问一致性模型怎么选。
scenario_en: You are designing a social feed, recommendation system, or analytics dashboard and need to choose a consistency model.
q: 安全的默认答案是？
q_en: What is the safer default consistency answer for feeds, recommendations, or analytics?
options: 可用性优先，最终一致
全系统强一致
弱一致，不保证收敛
线性一致
options_en: Availability-first with eventual consistency — users tolerate a feed that's two seconds stale, but not an app that won't open.
Strong consistency across the whole system.
Weak consistency, with no convergence guarantee.
Linearizable consistency.
why: 大多数系统默认选可用性：最终一致保证「无新更新时所有节点终将收敛」，对 feed/推荐/分析完全够用。
why_en: For most systems availability is the right default: users tolerate a slightly stale feed but not a down app, so eventual consistency works.
whenOtherWins: 题目一旦涉及钱、库存、订限量资源（订座），就要切到强一致。

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不承诺节点数据会收敛、也不保证顺序的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weak consistency makes no guarantee that replicas will ever converge or that updates are seen in order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最严格的一致性模型，所有操作看起来像按一个全局顺序瞬时发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability is the strictest consistency model, making all operations appear to happen instantly in one global order.

tradeoff: 可用性默认（最终一致） vs 强一致带来的协调延迟

scenario: 库存计数、银行账户余额、Ticketmaster 座位预订——读到几秒前的旧数据就会超卖 / 放过欺诈 / 重复订座。
scenario_en: Inventory counts, bank balances, or ticket seats can oversell, allow fraud, or double-book if reads are stale by a few seconds.
q: 一致性模型该选？
q_en: Which consistency model should you choose for stale-read-sensitive paths?
options: 最终一致
弱一致
强一致（防超卖）
不需要一致性
options_en: Eventual consistency.
Weak consistency.
Strong consistency, because stale data causes real financial loss.
No consistency guarantee needed.
why: 强一致的适用判据是「陈旧读会造成实际业务损失」；同一应用可混用：电商的商品描述/评论最终一致、库存/下单强一致。
why_en: Choose strong consistency when stale reads cause real business harm, like overselling inventory, fraud, or double-booked seats.
whenOtherWins: 同系统里的展示型数据（描述、评论晚 5 秒出现没人在乎）继续用最终一致即可。

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

tradeoff: 数据实时正确（防超卖/防欺诈） vs 协调延迟和可用性下降

q: 最终一致（eventual）与弱一致（weak）的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between eventual consistency and weak consistency?
options: 最终一致承诺收敛；弱一致不承诺
两者是同义词
弱一致更强
最终一致等于强一致
options_en: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes eventually converge to the same state; weak consistency makes no such convergence guarantee.
The two are synonyms.
Weak consistency is the stronger guarantee.
Eventual consistency is the same as strong consistency.
optionMeanings: 准确的收敛承诺差异
混淆两个概念
强弱颠倒
混淆两种模型
optionDirectness: eventual consistency 至少承诺没有新写入后会收敛。
把 eventual 说成 weak，会丢掉收敛承诺这个重点。
weak consistency 的保证更少，不是更强。
strong consistency 要求读到最新写，比 eventual 更严格。
optionDirectness_en: Eventual consistency at least promises convergence after new writes stop.
Calling eventual consistency weak loses the convergence guarantee.
Weak consistency has fewer guarantees, not stronger ones.
Strong consistency requires reading the latest write, which is stricter than eventual consistency.
why: 「最终」是一个有内容的承诺——会收敛；弱一致什么都不承诺。面试别把两个词混用。
why_en: Eventual consistency guarantees all nodes converge given enough time without updates, while weak consistency makes no convergence guarantee at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不承诺节点数据会收敛、也不保证顺序的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weak consistency makes no guarantee that replicas will ever converge or that updates are seen in order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

tradeoff: 承诺最终收敛 vs 不承诺任何收敛

q: PACELC 定理补充了 CAP 的什么盲区？
q_en: What blind spot in CAP does PACELC cover?
options: 分区时选延迟
CAP 适用于单机
网络永远不会分区
平时其实是一致性 vs 延迟的取舍
options_en: During a partition, choose latency.
CAP applies to single machines.
Networks never partition.

CAP only describes behavior during partitions, which are rare; day to day the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency, since strong consistency is slower even on a healthy network because nodes must coordinate before responding.
why: PACELC：分区（P）时选 A 或 C；否则（E）选延迟（L）或一致性（C）。日常运行中强一致的代价是协调延迟。
why_en: PACELC notes that outside rare partitions the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency, since strong consistency requires coordination before responding.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 的补充：分区时选可用性或一致性，其他时候（日常）选延迟或一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PACELC extends CAP: during a Partition choose Availability or Consistency, Else choose Latency or Consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

q: 把「订票系统选强一致」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the strong-consistency decision chain for a ticket-booking system in the right order.
steps: 选型：对这些关键路径选择强一致
需求：库存/余额/订座——读到陈旧数据会超卖、放过欺诈或重复订座
缓解：只对关键路径强一致，描述、评论等展示数据用最终一致
代价：分区时部分请求被拒，且日常延迟更高（节点需先协调）
why: 需求（陈旧读有真实代价）→ 选强一致 → 代价（可用性与延迟）→ 缓解（按路径混用一致性模型）。
why_en: Stale reads costing real money lead to strong consistency, whose availability and latency costs are contained by applying it only to critical paths.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same up-to-date data at all times, at the cost of higher latency or lower availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    Loss["Stale read causes loss"] --> Strong["Strong consistency"]
    Strong --> Cost["Higher latency / lower availability"]
    Cost --> Mix["Use only on critical path"]
tradeoff: 关键路径强一致防超卖 vs 非关键路径最终一致保可用性/延迟

q: 脑子里装着 2010 年代的硬件数字做设计，会导致什么？
q_en: What happens if you design with outdated 2010s hardware numbers in mind?
options: 设计更保守更安全
过早提出分片和缓存
没有影响
面试官会觉得你经验老到
options_en: The design becomes more conservative and safer.
You propose sharding and caching far earlier than necessary — a modern tuned database handles tens of thousands of QPS, and a single Redis handles hundreds of thousands of ops per second.
It has no effect.
The interviewer will think you're seasoned.
why: 现代硬件比多数候选人以为的强得多；用老数字就会为不存在的瓶颈加复杂度。
why_en: Using 2010-era numbers makes you propose sharding and caching far earlier than needed, since modern servers handle tens of thousands of queries per second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统每秒处理的查询数，常用来估算需要多少台服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is the number of queries a system handles per second, often used to estimate how many servers you need.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

q: 补全延迟阶梯（影响几乎所有设计决策）：
q_en: Fill in the latency ladder that shapes almost every design decision.
text: 内存访问约{{纳秒}}级；SSD 读取约{{微秒}}级；数据中心内网络调用约 {{1-10}} 毫秒；跨大洲调用要几十到几百毫秒。
why: 「要不要加缓存」「值不值得做地理分布」的判断，本质都来自这几级延迟差。
why_en: Memory takes nanoseconds, SSD reads microseconds, in-datacenter network calls one to ten milliseconds, and cross-continent calls tens to hundreds.
tradeoff: 本地内存访问延迟 vs 跨大洲网络调用延迟

scenario: 数据量还在增长，团队在纠结现在要不要把 Postgres 拆分片。
scenario_en: Data volume keeps growing, and the team is deciding whether to split Postgres into shards now.
q: 单个 Postgres 实例大约能舒适地承载多少存储？什么量级才该考虑分片？
q_en: Roughly how much storage can one Postgres instance comfortably hold, and when should sharding enter the conversation?
options: 舒适到几个 TB；分片门槛更高
只能存 10GB
1TB 就必须分片
存储无上限
options_en: A few terabytes comfortably; sharding is needed only in the tens to hundreds of terabytes — proposing it at 500GB is needless complexity.
Only 10GB.
Sharding is mandatory at 1TB.
Storage has no upper limit.
why: 存储容量是分片决策的核心数字之一；数据量远低于单库上限时提出分片会被视为乱加复杂度。
why_en: A single Postgres handles a few terabytes comfortably, so you do not need sharding until tens or hundreds of terabytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储容量单位，1 TiB ≈ 1024 GB，用来衡量单库存储上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TiB (tebibyte) is a storage unit of about 1024 GB, used to gauge a single database's storage ceiling.

scenario: 要判断单个数据库实例还能不能撑住业务增长，什么信号说明该扩容了。
scenario_en: You need to decide whether one database instance can keep handling growth, and which signals trigger expansion.
q: 数据库的关键量级与扩容触发点（记忆锚点）是？
q_en: What database scale anchors and expansion triggers should you remember?
options: 最多 100 TPS，10GB 存储
约 5 万 TPS；触发点看写吞吐/延迟
无限 TPS
1000 TPS 就必须分库
options_en: At most 100 TPS and 10GB of storage.

Up to about fifty thousand TPS, sub-five-millisecond cached reads, and 64 TiB-plus storage; consider action when writes pass ten thousand TPS, uncached reads exceed five milliseconds, or you need geographic distribution.
Unlimited TPS.
You must shard at 1000 TPS.
why: 这组数字回答「单库还能不能扛」；没超过触发点就别急着分片或换存储。
why_en: A database handles up to about fifty thousand transactions per second with sub-five-millisecond cached reads, with scale triggers at ten thousand write TPS or slow uncached reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库每秒能处理的事务数，是判断单库还能不能扛的核心指标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS is the number of transactions a database can process per second, a key signal for whether a single instance can still keep up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储容量单位，1 TiB ≈ 1024 GB，用来衡量单库存储上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TiB (tebibyte) is a storage unit of about 1024 GB, used to gauge a single database's storage ceiling.

scenario: 线上 Redis 集群做容量规划，要知道什么信号说明该扩容或优化。
scenario_en: You are capacity-planning a Redis cluster and need signals for expansion or optimization.
q: 缓存（Redis 级别）的关键量级与告警触发点是？
q_en: What Redis-scale cache anchors and alert triggers should you remember?
options: 延迟 100ms、1k ops/s
延迟 1 秒、10k ops/s
~1ms、10万+ ops/s
没有任何上限
options_en: 100ms latency, 1k ops per second.
1 second latency, 10k ops per second.
About 1ms latency, over 100k ops per second, memory up to about 1TB; watch for hit rate below eighty percent, latency above one millisecond, or memory above eighty percent.
No upper limit at all.
why: 用这组数字判断「单个缓存实例够不够」以及何时该扩缓存集群。
why_en: A cache serves in about a millisecond at over a hundred thousand operations per second up to about a terabyte of memory, with hit rate below eighty percent as a key trigger.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

scenario: 消息队列（如 Kafka）做容量规划，要知道什么信号说明该给 broker 扩容。
scenario_en: You are capacity-planning a Kafka-like message queue and need signals for broker expansion.
q: 消息队列的关键量级是？
q_en: What message-queue scale anchors should you remember?
options: 每 broker 每秒 100 条
每秒 1 万条是极限
端到端延迟至少 1 秒
单 broker ~100万条/秒
options_en: One hundred messages per second per broker.
Ten thousand per second is the ceiling.
At least one second of end-to-end latency.

A single broker can reach about a million messages per second with sub-five-millisecond end-to-end latency and storage up to 50TB; scale when nearing eight hundred thousand per second or consumer lag keeps growing.
why: 消息队列吞吐远比直觉高；真正要盯的是接近吞吐上限、分区数（~20 万/集群）和不断增长的 consumer lag。
why_en: A message queue broker handles up to a million messages per second with sub-five-millisecond latency, with growing consumer lag as a key scale trigger.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者处理进度落后于消息队列写入进度的差值，持续增长说明消费能力跟不上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consumer lag is how far a consumer's processing position trails the queue's write position; a growing lag means consumers can't keep up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息队列里把一个 topic 拆成的并行处理单元数量，决定了消费并行度的上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partition count is how many parallel units a topic is split into, capping how much consumer parallelism is possible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息队列集群里实际存储和转发消息的服务器节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broker is a server node in a message-queue cluster that actually stores and forwards messages.

q: 中级候选人挂掉系统设计面试最常见的原因是？
options: 算 QPS/DAU 时出了算术错误
选用了不够『潮』的数据库
没能交付出一个可运行的完整系统
白板图画得不够美观
options_en: Made an arithmetic mistake estimating QPS or DAU.
Picked a database that felt unfashionable.
Failed to deliver a working, complete system.
The whiteboard diagram wasn't pretty enough.
why: 最容易自毁的方式是没能交付出可工作的系统；这是中级候选人最常见的挂点，表面上常被误诊为『时间管理』问题。
why_en: The single easiest way to fail is not delivering a working system, which mid-level candidates most often misdiagnose as a time-management problem.
optionMeanings: 把失利归因于估算数字算错，一种常见误解
把失利归因于数据库选型不够新潮
指方案从未落成一个能跑通的整体架构
把失利归因于画图美观度
optionScenarioImpacts: 算术小错通常能当场纠正，不是致命伤
选型有争议时考官通常接受多种数据库
半成品设计让考官无法评估你端到端的判断力
美观从不是评分项，考官在意逻辑而非配色
optionMeanings_en: Blames failure on a miscalculated number, a common misread.
Blames failure on the database choice feeling outdated.
Means the design never became one runnable end-to-end system.
Blames failure on how tidy the diagram looks.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A small arithmetic slip is usually fixable on the spot.
Interviewers generally accept several reasonable databases.
An unfinished design leaves the interviewer nothing end-to-end to judge.
Neatness was never a scored dimension.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统每秒处理的查询次数，衡量负载的常用单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is the number of queries a system handles per second, a standard load metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每天实际使用产品的独立用户数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU is the count of unique users who use the product on a given day.

q_en: What is the most common reason mid-level candidates fail system design interviews?

是面试给的时间本身不够
是面试官计时不准确

You really do need to talk faster.
The interview simply doesn't allocate enough time.
The interviewer's timing is inaccurate.

why_en: The issue is rarely that you must work twice as fast; usually you just need to focus on the right things.
optionMeanings: 把『慢』重新定义为『没聚焦重点』
把『慢』归因于语速这个表层现象
把『慢』归因于外部时间预算

光说得快不会让设计更完整，只会更乱
45 分钟对所有候选人一样长，抱怨没用
计时误差不会系统性地拖垮候选人

Blames slowness on the surface symptom of talking pace.
Blames slowness on the fixed external time budget.
Blames slowness on the interviewer's timing tool.

Talking faster alone won't make the design more complete.
Everyone gets the same forty-five minutes, so this isn't fixable.

q: 跟随交付框架（Delivery Framework）的好处有哪些？（多选）
