线性搭建方案，不容易迷路、不容易卡死
保证一定拿到 offer
options_en: Keeps you focused on what the interviewer cares about most.
Gives you a clear fallback path when you freeze up under nerves.
Builds the solution linearly, so you rarely get lost or stuck.
Guarantees you'll get the offer.
why: 框架 = 一套推荐的步骤与时间分配：让你聚焦重点、慌乱时有轨道可退、并线性搭建方案——但它不是 offer 保票。
why_en: The framework keeps you focused on what matters, gives you a track to fall back on when nervous, and helps you build the solution linearly.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    F["Framework"] --> P["Focus"]
    F --> R["Fallback path"]
    F --> C["Complete system"]
optionMeanings: 框架把注意力锚定在考官的评分点上
框架提供固定步骤，慌乱时可以照抄流程
框架按顺序搭建，避免同时改十个地方
误把『有方法论』等同于『必过』
optionScenarioImpacts: 省下判断『该讲什么』的决策成本
紧张时仍能按部就班完成设计
每一步都建立在前一步之上，减少推倒重来
过度依赖框架会让人忽视实际设计质量
optionMeanings_en: The framework anchors attention on what interviewers score.
It supplies fixed steps to follow when you panic.
It builds sequentially so you avoid touching ten things at once.
Confuses having a method with a guaranteed pass.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Saves the cost of deciding what to cover next.
Lets you keep moving methodically even when nervous.
Each step builds on the last, reducing rework.
Over-relying on it can blind you to actual design quality.
q_en: What are the benefits of following the Delivery Framework? (Select all that apply)

scenario: 面试只有 35-45 分钟，你要在开口前决定每个环节大概花多久，才不会前面磨蹭、后面来不及深挖。
q: 补全交付框架各环节的建议用时：
text: 需求 ~{{5}} 分钟 → 核心实体 ~{{2}} 分钟 → API ~{{5}} 分钟 →（可选：数据流 ~5 分钟）→ 高层设计 ~{{10-15}} 分钟 → 深挖 ~{{10}} 分钟。
why: 这套预算把 35-45 分钟切成五段，高层设计占比最大；数字不用死记，用途是提醒你『需求和实体别磨太久，把时间留给深挖』。
why_en: The framework budgets about five minutes for requirements, two for core entities, five for the API, ten to fifteen for high-level design, and ten for deep dives, so you protect time for the deep dives.
q_en: Fill in the recommended time budget for each Delivery Framework stage:
scenario_en: The interview is only 35 to 45 minutes, so you need a rough time budget before speaking or you will lose the deep-dive window.

q: 把交付框架的五个主环节按面试推进顺序排列：
steps: 高层设计（画框图，逐个 endpoint 搭建）
需求（功能性 + 非功能性）
深挖（加固设计以满足非功能需求）
API 或系统接口（定义契约）
核心实体（列出系统的关键名词）
why: 需求 → 核心实体 → API → 高层设计 → 深挖；数据处理型系统可在 API 后插入可选的『数据流』环节。
why_en: The delivery framework runs requirements, core entities, API, high-level design, and finally deep dives, with an optional data-flow step for data-processing systems.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求 ~5min"] --> E["核心实体 ~2min"]
    E --> A["API ~5min"]
    A -.-> D["数据流（可选）~5min"]
    A --> H["高层设计 ~10-15min"]
    D -.-> H
    H --> DD["深挖 ~10min"]
q_en: Put the five main Delivery Framework stages in interview order:

q: 功能性需求（functional requirements）的标准句式是？
options: "The system should be..."（系统应当具备…）
"Users/Clients should be able to..."（用户/客户端应能…）
"We will use..."（我们将使用…）
"The database must..."（数据库必须…）
options_en: "The system should be..."
"Users/Clients should be able to..."
"We will use..."
"The database must..."
why: 功能需求描述系统的核心特性，句式是『用户/客户端应能做 X』；它是需求环节第一个要跟考官对齐的内容。
why_en: Functional requirements are the "users should be able to" statements that capture the core features of the system.
optionMeanings: 这是非功能需求的句式，描述系统品质而非动作
这是功能需求的标准句式，描述用户能做的动作
这是技术选型陈述，不是需求陈述
这是对某个组件的约束，不是面向用户的需求
optionScenarioImpacts: 用它列需求会漏掉『用户能做什么』这条主线
直接产出可对齐优先级的功能清单
过早锁定实现细节，跳过了需求收集
把需求和某个组件强绑定，缩小了设计空间
optionMeanings_en: This phrasing describes system qualities, i.e. non-functional requirements.
This is the canonical functional-requirement phrasing describing user actions.
This states an implementation choice, not a requirement.
This constrains one component rather than stating a user-facing need.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Using this misses the core 'what can users do' thread.
Produces a feature list you can directly prioritize with the interviewer.
Locks in implementation details before requirements are even gathered.
Ties the requirement to one component, narrowing the design space.
q_en: What is the standard phrasing for a functional requirement?

q: 收集功能需求的正确姿势是？
options: 自己闷头列完再一次性宣布
被动等待面试官主动报需求
把题目原文照抄一遍当需求
像对产品经理一样提针对性问题，和考官来回对齐优先级
options_en: Silently list everything yourself and announce it all at once.
Passively wait for the interviewer to hand you the requirements.
Copy the prompt's wording verbatim as your requirements.
Ask targeted questions like a product manager and align priorities with the interviewer.
why: 需求环节常是与考官的 back-and-forth：用针对性提问逼出核心功能，并排出优先级。
why_en: Gather functional requirements by asking targeted questions as if talking to a product manager, iterating with the interviewer toward a prioritized feature list.
optionMeanings: 把需求收集当成个人任务，跳过了对齐环节
把主动权完全交给考官，自己不驱动
把已知信息复述一遍，没有产出新判断
用提问驱动，暴露隐藏假设并排优先级
optionScenarioImpacts: 考官看不到你怎么筛选和排序需求的思路
对话冷场，考官很难评估你的沟通与推理
浪费开场时间，考官得不到任何新信息
对齐后的清单成为后续设计的共同锚点
optionMeanings_en: Treats gathering requirements as a solo task, skipping alignment.
Hands all initiative to the interviewer instead of driving it.
Restates known information without producing new judgment.
Drives with questions that surface hidden assumptions and set priority.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer never sees how you filter and prioritize.
The conversation stalls, making it hard to assess your reasoning.
Wastes opening time without adding new information.
The aligned list becomes the shared anchor for the rest of the design.
q_en: What is the right way to gather functional requirements?

scenario: 真实产品（如 Twitter、Amazon）动辄有上百个功能，但 45 分钟的面试不可能把它们都设计一遍。
q: 面对上百个真实功能，你应该识别并聚焦前几个核心功能？
options: 10 个以上，尽量全
前 3 个左右
只挑 1 个
全部列出再筛选
options_en: Ten or more, aim for full coverage.
Roughly the top three.
Just one feature.
List every single one, then filter.
why: 你的职责是从上百个功能里挑出并优先处理 top 3 左右；这份小清单撑起接下来整场面试的设计，多了拖慢节奏、少了撑不起系统。
why_en: Your job is to identify and prioritize roughly the top three core features out of the hundreds the real product has, since that short list has to carry the rest of the interview.
q_en: When a real product has hundreds of features, how many core features should you focus on?
scenario_en: Real products like Twitter or Amazon have hundreds of features, but a 45-minute interview cannot design all of them.

q: 把功能需求列得又长又全的后果是？
options: 弊大于利——顶级大厂直接评估『聚焦重点』的能力
显得准备充分，通常会加分
对后续设计没有影响
可以直接跳过深挖环节
options_en: It backfires — top companies directly evaluate your ability to focus.
It looks thorough and usually earns bonus points.
It has no effect on the rest of the design.
It lets you skip the deep-dives step entirely.
why: 长清单会拖垮后面所有环节；不少 FAANG 把『能否聚焦最重要的事』作为直接评估项。
why_en: A long requirements list hurts more than it helps, since top companies directly evaluate your ability to focus on what matters.
optionMeanings: 长清单被当作『不会取舍』的负面信号
误以为需求越多越显得认真
误以为需求环节和后续设计彼此独立
误以为需求收集能替代后面的加固环节
optionScenarioImpacts: 每多一条需求，后面就要多验证一条，时间被稀释
考官反而会追问『这些里哪个最重要』，暴露没有取舍
实际上臃肿的需求清单会拖慢 API 和高层设计
深挖环节仍然要单独跑，需求详略换不来它
optionMeanings_en: A long list reads as a negative signal for prioritization skill.
Mistakenly assumes more requirements looks more thorough.
Mistakenly assumes the requirements step is independent of the rest.
Mistakenly assumes gathering requirements can replace hardening later.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Every extra requirement adds something to verify later, diluting time.
Interviewers will probe which one actually matters most, exposing the lack of choice.
A bloated list slows down the API and high-level design that follow.
Deep dives still have to run separately; detail here doesn't buy it back.
q_en: What happens if you list every possible functional requirement?

q: 设计 Twitter 时合理的核心功能需求有哪些？（多选）
options: 用户应能发推文
用户应能关注其他用户
用户应能看到所关注用户的推文
用户应能购买广告位
options_en: Users should be able to post tweets.
Users should be able to follow other users.
Users should be able to see tweets from users they follow.
Users should be able to purchase ad placements.
why: 发推、关注、看关注流是 Twitter 的 top 3 核心功能；广告投放不是面试 45 分钟里该抓的重点。
why_en: For Twitter the core functional requirements are posting tweets, following users, and seeing tweets from followed users.
optionMeanings: 发推是 Twitter 最基本的写路径
关注定义了用户之间的图关系
看关注流是发推之后的核心读路径
广告是变现功能，不是核心产品体验
optionScenarioImpacts: 没有发推，整个系统没有内容来源
没有关注，feed 无法定义『该展示谁的内容』
没有 feed 读取，发推和关注就没有出口
广告涉及计费、竞价，是完全独立的子系统
optionMeanings_en: Posting is the most basic write path.
Following defines the graph relationship between users.
Viewing the feed is the core read path after posting.
Ads are a monetization feature, not the core product experience.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Without posting there is no content source at all.
Without following, the feed has no way to decide whose content to show.
Without feed reads, posting and following have no output.
Ads involve billing and bidding, an entirely separate subsystem.
q_en: Which core functional requirements are reasonable for designing Twitter? (Select all that apply)

q: 非功能性需求（non-functional requirements，NFR）描述的是什么？
options: 系统的功能清单
团队的开发流程
对用户重要的系统品质
运维值班安排
options_en: The list of system features.
The team's development process.
System qualities that matter to users.
The on-call rotation schedule.
why: 非功能需求刻画系统品质：可用性、扩展性、延迟等，句式是 "The system should (be able to)..."。
why_en: Non-functional requirements are statements about system qualities that matter to users, phrased as "the system should be" statements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刻画系统品质（延迟/可用性/扩展性等）而非具体动作的需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-functional requirement describes a system quality like latency or availability, not a user action.

optionMeanings: 这是功能需求的定义，不是非功能需求
这是团队管理话题，和系统品质无关
这正是非功能需求：品质而非功能
这是运维话题，不属于需求环节
optionScenarioImpacts: 混淆两者会让延迟/可用性这类品质无处安放
写进需求文档也不会被考官采纳
为后面的深挖环节提供可验证的品质目标
值班安排和设计决策无直接关系
optionMeanings_en: This defines functional requirements, not non-functional ones.
A team-management topic unrelated to system qualities.
This is exactly what a non-functional requirement is: a quality, not a feature.
An operations topic, not part of requirements gathering.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Confusing the two leaves qualities like latency with nowhere to live.
Writing this down won't be accepted as a requirement by the interviewer.
Gives the deep-dives step a verifiable quality target.
On-call scheduling has no direct bearing on design decisions.
q_en: What do non-functional requirements, or NFRs, describe?

q: 「系统应该低延迟」这条非功能需求的问题在哪？
options: 延迟根本不属于非功能需求
太空泛，需结合语境量化
这样写没问题，直接照抄即可
低延迟只和前端渲染有关
options_en: Latency isn't even a non-functional requirement.
It's too vague; it should be scoped and quantified.
It's fine as written; just copy it in as-is.
Low latency only concerns front-end rendering.
why: 好的 NFR 要放进系统语境并尽量量化：指出最需要低延迟的部分、给出目标值，否则这句话没有信息量。
why_en: Saying the system should be low latency is meaningless; a useful requirement names the part that matters and quantifies it, like search under 500 milliseconds.
optionMeanings: 把延迟错误地排除在 NFR 范畴之外
指出『空泛』才是问题所在
误把模板句当成已经写好的需求
把延迟问题限缩到某一层，缩小了范围
optionScenarioImpacts: 延迟其实是最典型的 NFR 之一，排除它会漏掉重点
量化后才能在深挖环节验证方案是否达标
空泛陈述留给后面无法验收的隐患
后端查询/网络传输同样贡献延迟，不止前端
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly excludes latency from the NFR category.
Names vagueness as the actual problem.
Mistakes a template sentence for an already-usable requirement.
Narrows latency to one layer, shrinking the real scope.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Latency is one of the most typical NFRs, so excluding it misses the point.
Quantifying it lets the deep dives later verify whether the design meets it.
A vague statement leaves nothing checkable at the end.
Backend queries and network transfer add latency too, not just the front end.
q_en: What is wrong with saying only that the system should have low latency?

q: 补全 Twitter 的非功能需求示例：
text: 系统应高可用，{{可用性}}优先于{{一致性}}；应能扩展到支撑 {{100M}}+ 日活用户；feed 渲染延迟应低于 {{200ms}}。
why: 这三条示范了 NFR 的正确写法：点名 CAP 取舍、给出规模数字、给出量化延迟目标——每条都能在深挖环节被验收。
why_en: Twitter's example requirements prioritize availability over consistency, scale past one hundred million daily active users, and render feeds in under two hundred milliseconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统在网络分区时只能同时保证一致性与可用性中的一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can guarantee only consistency or availability, not both, during a network partition.

q_en: Fill in the Twitter non-functional requirement examples:

q: 非功能需求检查清单中包含哪些维度？（多选）
options: CAP 取舍与环境约束（电池/内存/带宽）
扩展性（突发流量、读写比）与延迟
持久性、安全、容错、合规
团队人数与代码风格
options_en: CAP trade-off and environment constraints (battery, memory, bandwidth).
Scalability (bursty traffic, read/write ratio) and latency.
Durability, security, fault tolerance, compliance.
Team headcount and coding style.
why: 清单共八项：CAP、环境约束、扩展性、延迟、持久性、安全、容错、合规——从中挑出与本系统最相关的 3-5 条。
why_en: The checklist covers CAP trade-offs, environment constraints, scalability, latency, durability, security, fault tolerance, and compliance.
optionMeanings: 涵盖分布式取舍与运行环境的物理限制
涵盖流量形状和响应速度两个维度
涵盖『数据能不能丢/系统能不能扛住故障/合不合规』
属于团队管理，不属于系统品质
optionScenarioImpacts: 移动端项目尤其要考虑电池和带宽约束
决定该扩读还是扩写、要不要应对流量洪峰
决定要不要引入多副本、加密、审计日志
写进 NFR 也不会影响系统架构
optionMeanings_en: Covers distributed trade-offs and physical runtime limits.
Covers traffic shape and response speed.
Covers whether data can be lost, failures survived, or rules met.
An organizational topic, not a system quality.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Mobile projects especially need battery and bandwidth limits considered.
Decides whether to scale reads or writes and handle traffic spikes.
Decides whether to add replicas, encryption, or audit logging.
Writing it into the NFRs wouldn't change the architecture at all.
q_en: Which dimensions belong in the non-functional requirement checklist? (Select all that apply)

q: 用 CAP 定非功能需求时，正确的问法是？
options: 「优先一致性还是可用性？」（P 是前提）
「要 C、A、P 里的哪两个？」三选二随便选
「能不能三个都要？」
CAP 与非功能需求无关
options_en: "Consistency or availability?" (P is already a given).
"Which two of C, A, P do we want?" — just pick any two.
"Can we have all three?"
CAP has nothing to do with non-functional requirements.
why: 分布式系统必须容忍分区，所以 P 不是选项而是前提；真正要回答的是这套系统更看重一致性还是可用性。
why_en: Partition tolerance is a given in distributed systems, so the real CAP question is whether to prioritize consistency or availability.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["Partition is given"] --> Q{"Need newest data?"}
    Q -->|Yes| C["Prefer consistency"]
    Q -->|No| A["Prefer availability"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统在网络分区下只能同时保证一致性与可用性中的一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In a network partition a distributed system can guarantee only consistency or availability, not both.

optionMeanings: 把 P 当作前提，问题聚焦在 C 与 A 的取舍
误把 CAP 当成『任选两个』的组合题
误以为分布式系统能同时拿到三项保证
误以为 CAP 只是理论，不影响需求
optionScenarioImpacts: 得到的答案能直接指导后续的一致性模型选型
『三选二随便选』掩盖了分区容错不可放弃这个事实
网络分区一旦发生就必须在 C/A 间二选一，不能都要
跳过这一步会让后续可用性设计失去依据
optionMeanings_en: Treats P as a given and focuses the real question on C versus A.
Wrongly treats CAP as 'pick any two out of three'.
Wrongly assumes a distributed system can guarantee all three at once.
Wrongly assumes CAP is purely theoretical and doesn't affect requirements.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The answer directly guides which consistency model you pick later.
'Pick any two' hides the fact that partition tolerance can't be given up.
Once a partition happens you must choose between C and A, not both.
Skipping this leaves later availability decisions with no grounding.
q_en: What is the right CAP question when defining non-functional requirements?

q: 评估「扩展性」这条非功能需求时，除了总量还要特别考虑什么？
options: 机房的物理选址
编程语言的运行时性能
服务器的品牌型号
突发流量（高峰/节假日）以及读写比
options_en: The physical location of the data center.
The programming language's runtime performance.
The server hardware brand and model.
Bursty traffic (peak hours or holidays) and the read/write ratio.
why: 所有系统都要扩展，值得写进 NFR 的是「独特的扩展需求」：某时段的 bursty 流量、大事件洪峰、以及读写比例。
why_en: For scalability, consider unique needs like bursty traffic at certain times, event spikes, and whether reads or writes need to scale more.
optionMeanings: 选址属于基础设施决策，不是需求环节要回答的
语言性能是实现细节，不是架构层面的扩展性
硬件品牌不影响架构该怎么扩
指出流量形状和读写比才是扩展性里有信息量的部分
optionScenarioImpacts: 写进 NFR 也不会改变要不要分片、要不要缓存的判断
换一种语言不会改变水平扩展的架构决策
品牌不会影响是否需要读写分离或分片
决定了该扩读还是扩写、要不要为峰值预留缓冲
optionMeanings_en: Site selection is an infrastructure decision, not a requirements question.
Runtime performance is an implementation detail, not architectural scalability.
Hardware brand doesn't change how the architecture should scale.
Names traffic shape and read/write ratio as the informative part of scalability.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Writing this into the NFRs won't change sharding or caching decisions.
Switching languages won't change the horizontal-scaling architecture.
Brand doesn't affect whether you need read replicas or sharding.
Decides whether to scale reads or writes and whether to buffer for peaks.
q_en: When evaluating scalability as an NFR, what should you consider besides total volume?

q: 「持久性」要求因业务而异，教科书式的对比是？
options: 游戏内进度不能丢，银行流水可以丢
社交网络可容忍少量数据丢失，银行系统绝对不行
所有系统都不能丢任何一条数据
持久性只取决于磁盘型号
options_en: Game progress can never be lost, but bank ledgers can be.
A social network can tolerate some data loss; a banking system cannot.
No system can ever afford to lose a single record.
Durability depends only on the disk model.
why: 持久性该问『丢数据的代价有多大』：社交网络丢一条动态可以忍，银行丢一笔交易不可接受，这是延迟成本 vs 数据丢失成本的取舍。
why_en: A social network might tolerate some data loss, but a banking system cannot, which is the classic durability contrast.
tradeoff: 社交场景『容忍少量丢失换更简单/更快的写路径』 vs 金融场景『零丢失优先，接受更重的写路径』
optionMeanings: 把顺序反了：金融数据才是绝对不能丢的一方
正确点名了两种业务对丢数据代价的真实差异
忽略了业务代价的差异，把所有系统一刀切
把持久性错误地归因于单一硬件因素
optionScenarioImpacts: 按这个反例设计会让银行系统的写路径过于脆弱
据此可以决定同步写盘/多副本确认的力度
对所有系统都上最高持久性，会不必要地拖慢写入
只换磁盘型号解决不了副本数和写确认策略的问题
optionDirectness: 只在故意反转业务风险的反例里成立，用来暴露判断方向错了。
适合说明持久性随业务损失变化：社交内容可少量丢，资金流水不能丢。
适合极高合规或资金场景，但拿来套所有系统会把成本拉满。
只讨论硬件时会漏掉复制因子、写确认和备份策略这些真正杠杆。
optionMeanings_en: Gets it backwards: financial data is the side that must never be lost.
Correctly names the real difference in loss-cost between two businesses.
Ignores the difference in business cost and treats every system the same.
Wrongly attributes durability to a single hardware factor.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Designing off this reversed example makes a bank's write path too fragile.
This determines how much synchronous replication and write-ack you need.
Applying max durability everywhere needlessly slows down every write.
Swapping disks alone can't fix replica count or acknowledgment policy.
optionDirectness_en: This only works as a reversed-risk counterexample that exposes the wrong judgment.
Use this to show that durability depends on business loss: social posts may tolerate loss, bank ledgers cannot.
This fits strict financial or compliance cases, but applying it everywhere makes cost explode.
Hardware-only thinking misses the real levers: replication factor, write acknowledgments, and backups.
q_en: What is the textbook contrast for durability requirements across businesses?

scenario: 非功能需求检查清单一共有 CAP、环境约束、扩展性、延迟、持久性、安全、容错、合规八项。
q: 从这八项检查清单里，最终应挑出几条与系统最相关的非功能需求？
options: 全部 8 条都写
只挑 1 条
10 条以上
options_en: Write down all eight.
Pick just one.
Three to five.
More than ten.
why: 识别与本系统最相关的 top 3-5 条 NFR；全写会稀释深挖环节的火力，只写一条又撑不起完整的品质画像。
why_en: Identify the three to five non-functional requirements most relevant to your system.
q_en: From the eight NFR checklist items, how many should you finally choose for the system?
scenario_en: The NFR checklist has eight items: CAP, environment constraints, scalability, latency, durability, security, fault tolerance, and compliance.

scenario: 面试开场刚定完需求，很多备考指南建议此时先做一轮 back-of-the-envelope 容量估算（存储、DAU、QPS）。
q: 本框架推荐的做法是？
options: 必须先算完存储、DAU、QPS 再动手设计
向面试官说明：跳过开场估算，需要时再算
让面试官替你把数字算出来
整场面试完全不做任何计算
options_en: Finish estimating storage, DAU, and QPS before doing anything else.
Tell the interviewer you'll skip upfront estimation and do the math only when needed.
Ask the interviewer to do the numbers for you.
Do no calculations at all during the whole interview.
why: 开场估算常是无用功——大型分布式系统直接假设即可；只有当数字会改变设计决策时才当场做数学。
why_en: Tell the interviewer you will skip upfront estimation and do the math during the design only when it directly influences a decision.
whenOtherWins: 当结果直接决定架构时必须算：比如 TopK 热门话题要估话题总数，才能决定 min-heap 用单实例还是要分片。
tradeoff: 开场就估算『看似严谨但常无信号』 vs 按需估算『省时间，只在改变设计时才算』
optionMeanings: 把估算当成开场必做的固定仪式
把估算改成按需触发的工具
把估算责任转嫁给考官
把估算完全排除在设计过程之外
optionScenarioImpacts: 算完常常只得到『嗯，很大』，挤占了后面的时间
只在数字会改变架构决策时才停下来算
考官不会替你完成本该属于你的判断
遇到真正需要估算的场景（如分片阈值）时会卡住
optionDirectness: 只有数字会马上改变设计时，开场估算才值得抢占这段时间。
适合大多数面试开局：先推进架构，等某个选择被数字卡住再算。
面试官可以帮你澄清假设，但容量判断仍要由候选人负责。
只有完全没有数字会影响决策时才可不算；现实里深挖常会用到估算。
optionMeanings_en: Treats estimation as a mandatory opening ritual.
Turns estimation into a tool triggered only when needed.
Shifts the estimation responsibility onto the interviewer.
Excludes estimation from the design process entirely.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Often ends in just 'okay, it's a lot', eating into later time.
Only pauses to calculate when a number would change the architecture.
The interviewer won't do your judgment work for you.
You'll stall when a scenario genuinely needs a number, like a sharding threshold.
optionDirectness_en: Early estimation is worth the time only when the number immediately changes the design.
This fits most interview openings: move the architecture forward and calculate when a choice needs a number.
The interviewer can help clarify assumptions, but the candidate owns the capacity judgment.
You can avoid math only if no number affects any decision; deep dives often still need estimates.
q_en: What does this framework recommend for early back-of-the-envelope estimates?
scenario_en: Right after requirements, many prep guides suggest doing back-of-the-envelope estimates for storage, DAU, and QPS.

q: 算了一通存储/DAU/QPS，结论只是「嗯，很大」，考官从中得到了什么信号？
options: 对系统规模的深刻理解
扩展性方面的具体设计信号
对估算能力的认可
除了『你会基础算术』以外什么都没有
options_en: Deep insight into the system's scale.
A concrete design signal about scalability.
Credit for your estimation ability.
Nothing except proof that you can do basic arithmetic.
why: 不影响设计的估算是表演式计算；考官点明这种算术除了证明会加减乘除毫无信号。
why_en: Calculating storage and QPS just to conclude it is a lot gives the interviewer nothing except proof you can do arithmetic.
optionMeanings: 误以为算出大数字就等于理解了系统
误以为任何估算天然会指向具体架构选择
误以为面试考的是算术熟练度
指出这类计算唯一证明的就是基础运算能力
optionScenarioImpacts: 『很大』这个结论不会改变任何一个组件的选型
没有落到『所以要分片/要缓存』这类具体动作，就没有信号
考官真正在意的是判断力，不是心算速度
这类计算挤占了本可以用于设计的时间
optionMeanings_en: Mistakenly assumes a big final number equals real system understanding.
Mistakenly assumes any estimate naturally points to a concrete architecture choice.
Mistakenly assumes the interview is testing arithmetic fluency.
Names the only thing this kind of math actually proves.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Concluding 'it's a lot' changes no component choice at all.
Without landing on a concrete action like sharding, there's no signal.
What interviewers actually care about is judgment, not mental-math speed.
This kind of calculation eats into time that could go toward the design.
q_en: If your storage, DAU, and QPS math only concludes “it is large,” what signal does the interviewer get?

scenario: 你在设计一个 TopK 热门话题系统：需要在内存里维护『当前最热的 K 个话题』。
q: 什么时候当场估算才是「必要」的？
options: 话题总数决定要不要分片
每场面试开始时都必须先估算一次
只在结束时总结陈述用
面试官心情好的时候顺便算一下
options_en: When the topic count decides whether to shard.
At the very start of every interview, no matter the system.
Only as a closing summary at the end.
Whenever the interviewer happens to be in a good mood.
why: TopK 例子：话题总数决定单个数据结构实例是否装得下，直接改变架构——这类计算才值得当场做。
why_en: Estimation matters when it changes the design, like estimating topic counts in a top-k system to decide between a single min-heap and a sharded one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在候选集合里持续维护排名前 K 的元素的问题模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K is the problem of continuously tracking the highest-ranked K elements in a set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆顶始终是最小值的二叉堆，常用来维护当前的 K 个最大候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a binary heap whose root is always the smallest element, often used to track the current top-K candidates.

optionMeanings: 点名了一个数字会直接切换架构方案的真实例子
把估算当成固定的开场仪式，与设计脱节
把估算变成收尾装饰，不影响任何决策
把估算的触发条件变成随机、不可控的因素
optionScenarioImpacts: 话题数超过单机容量就必须引入分片和聚合
大多数系统里这个数字根本不改变架构
总结阶段估算不会反过来修改已经画好的设计
以心情为准的估算无法在真实面试里复现
optionMeanings_en: Names a real example where one number flips the entire architecture.
Treats estimation as a fixed opening ritual disconnected from the design.
Turns estimation into a closing decoration that changes no decision.
Makes the trigger for estimating random and uncontrollable.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Once topic count exceeds single-machine capacity you must shard and aggregate.
In most systems this number never changes the architecture at all.
Estimating at the summary stage can't retroactively change a finished design.
A mood-based trigger can't be reproduced in a real interview.
q_en: When is it actually necessary to estimate during the interview?
scenario_en: You are designing a TopK trending-topics system that keeps the current hottest K topics in memory.

q: 「核心实体」环节（约 2 分钟）要做什么？
options: 写出完整的数据库 schema 与所有字段类型
先画出最终版架构图
列出核心实体清单（第一稿）
把建表 SQL 写完整
options_en: Write out the complete database schema with every column type.
Draw the final architecture diagram first.
List the core entities as a first draft.
Write the complete CREATE TABLE SQL.
why: 先用一个简短的 bulleted list 列核心实体：定义术语、理解核心数据，作为 API 与数据模型的地基。
why_en: Spend about two minutes listing the core entities your API will exchange and your system will persist, framed as a first draft.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Actors["Actors"] --> Nouns["Core nouns"]
    Nouns --> API["API resources"]
    API --> Data["First data model"]
optionMeanings: 把两分钟的草稿环节当成完整数据建模来做
把顺序完全颠倒，架构本该在实体之后画
把实体清单定位为可迭代的第一稿
把 DDL 细节提前到还没确定字段的阶段
optionScenarioImpacts: 两分钟根本写不完完整 schema，会挤占 API 时间
没有实体和 API，架构图无从画起
后续在高层设计里发现新字段时可以随时补充
字段还没定案时写 SQL 大概率要推倒重写
optionMeanings_en: Turns a two-minute sketch step into full data modeling.
Reverses the order — architecture should come after entities, not before.
Frames the entity list as an iterable first draft.
Pushes DDL detail ahead of the point where fields are even settled.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Two minutes can't finish a full schema, eating into API time.
Without entities and an API there's nothing to draw an architecture from.
New fields discovered during high-level design can be added later.
Writing SQL before fields are settled usually gets rewritten anyway.
q_en: What should you do in the roughly two-minute core entities stage?

q: 为什么核心实体环节不直接写完整数据模型？
options: 因为数据模型不重要，可有可无
因为『不知道不知道什么』，先小清单迭代
因为面试官从来不看数据模型
因为手写字段太耗时
options_en: Because the data model doesn't really matter.
Because you don't know what you don't know; start small and iterate.
Because interviewers never look at the data model.
Because writing out fields by hand takes too long.
why: 过早锁死 schema 会被后面的发现推翻；等高层设计里清楚了每个请求改什么状态，再补各实体的关键字段。
why_en: You don't know what you don't know yet, so start with a small entity list and add fields once the high-level design clarifies what each request updates.
optionMeanings: 误把『暂缓』理解成『不重要』
指出提前锁定 schema 的真实代价：会被推翻
误以为数据模型对评分毫无影响
把根本原因简化成书写速度问题
optionScenarioImpacts: 如果真不重要，深挖环节就不需要回头标注字段了
先粗后细能避免高层设计阶段大改数据模型
很多面试官恰恰通过数据模型考察建模能力
就算打字再快，提前锁死的字段还是会被推翻
optionMeanings_en: Mistakes 'defer it' for 'it doesn't matter'.
Names the real cost of locking a schema too early: it gets overturned.
Wrongly assumes the data model has no bearing on scoring.
Reduces the real reason to a typing-speed problem.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: If it truly didn't matter, deep dives wouldn't need to revisit fields.
Starting coarse and refining avoids a big data-model rewrite later.
Many interviewers specifically probe modeling skill through the data model.
Even fast typing doesn't save a schema locked in too early from being overturned.
q_en: Why should the core entities stage not become a full data model?

q: 识别核心实体时，值得自问的问题有哪些？（多选）
options: 系统里的参与者（actors）是谁？他们有重叠吗？
满足功能需求需要哪些名词/资源？
实体名字起得清晰吗？
实体将来要部署在哪个可用区？
options_en: Who are the actors in the system? Do they overlap?
What nouns or resources are needed to satisfy the functional requirements?
Are the entity names clear and well chosen?
Which availability zone will each entity be deployed to?
why: 找实体 = 找 actor + 找满足功能需求的名词；有的考官还会借命名质量观察你的基本功。部署位置不是这一步的事。
why_en: Ask who the actors are and which nouns are needed to satisfy the functional requirements, and choose good names for them.
optionMeanings: 从『谁在用系统』倒推出实体
从『功能需求需要什么名词』正推出实体
把命名质量当作观察基本功的信号
把部署位置这类运维决策提前到实体环节
optionScenarioImpacts: actor 重叠时（如 User 既是发帖者也是关注者）能减少重复实体
直接从需求清单映射出实体清单，减少遗漏
命名模糊（如 Data、Info）会被考官视为负面信号
可用区属于部署阶段，这时候讨论为时过早
optionMeanings_en: Works backward from who uses the system to find entities.
Works forward from what nouns the requirements need to find entities.
Treats naming quality as a signal of engineering fundamentals.
Pulls a deployment decision forward into the entities step.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Overlapping actors, like a User who both posts and follows, avoid duplicate entities.
Maps the requirements list directly onto an entity list, reducing omissions.
Vague names like Data or Info read as a negative signal to interviewers.
Availability zones belong to deployment, far too early to raise here.
q_en: Which questions are useful when identifying core entities? (Select all that apply)

q: Twitter 例子的核心实体清单是？
options: User、Tweet、Follow
Server、Database、Cache
Post、Comment、Like、Share、Ad、DM
只有 Tweet 一个实体
options_en: User, Tweet, Follow.
Server, Database, Cache.
Post, Comment, Like, Share, Ad, DM.
Just Tweet, and nothing else.
why: 三个实体就够撑起核心功能：User 发 Tweet、User 之间 Follow；组件（服务器/缓存）不是业务实体。
why_en: For Twitter the core entities are simply the user, the tweet, and the follow relationship.
optionMeanings: 三个业务名词精确覆盖了发推与关注两条主线
把基础设施组件误当成业务实体
把六种功能都当成独立实体，超出了 top 3 的范围
遗漏了 Follow 这个支撑 feed 的关系实体
optionScenarioImpacts: 三个实体已经能撑起发推、关注、看 feed 三个核心功能
服务器和缓存属于高层设计的组件，不该出现在实体清单
过多实体会让两分钟的环节严重超时
没有 Follow，就定义不出『该展示谁的推文』
optionMeanings_en: Three business nouns exactly cover posting and following.
Mistakes infrastructure components for business entities.
Treats six separate features as entities, well beyond the top three.
Misses Follow, the relationship entity that underpins the feed.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Three entities are already enough to support posting, following, and feed reads.
Servers and caches are high-level-design components, not entities.
Too many entities would badly overrun the two-minute step.
Without Follow there's no way to define whose tweets to show.
q_en: What is the core entity list for the Twitter example?

q: API / 系统接口环节的目的？
options: 展示你会写代码
确定服务器数量
选择云厂商
定义系统与用户的契约
options_en: To demonstrate that you can write code.
To determine how many servers you need.
To pick a cloud vendor.
To define the contract between the system and its users.
why: 先定契约再画架构：API 保证你的设计对得上需求，之后高层设计可以逐 endpoint 搭建。
why_en: The API defines the contract between your system and its users, usually mapping to the functional requirements and guiding the high-level design.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Req["Functional reqs"] --> API["API contract"]
    API --> HLD["High-level design"]
    HLD --> Deep["Deep dive"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统对外暴露的调用契约，规定客户端能发起哪些请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the contract a system exposes, defining which requests a client can make.

optionMeanings: 把这一步误当成代码能力展示
把这一步误当成容量规划
把这一步误当成基础设施选型
点出契约先行、再指导高层设计的正确目的
optionScenarioImpacts: 写代码留给深挖里的伪代码/具体命令，不是这一步
服务器数量属于估算或深挖，不属于契约环节
云厂商选择几乎不出现在这套框架里
先有契约，高层设计才有『要满足什么』的边界
optionMeanings_en: Mistakes this step for a coding-skill demonstration.
Mistakes this step for capacity planning.
Mistakes this step for infrastructure vendor selection.
Names the real goal: contract first, then guide the high-level design.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Actual code belongs to the deep-dive pseudocode or commands, not here.
Server count belongs to estimation, not contract design.
Vendor choice almost never appears in this framework.
With the contract set, high-level design has a clear boundary of what to satisfy.
q_en: What is the purpose of the API or system interface stage?

scenario: 普通产品型系统设计面试，客户端形态单一，也没有特殊的服务间性能诉求，要快速选定 API 协议。
q: 默认应该选哪种 API 协议？
options: REST
GraphQL
gRPC
SOAP
options_en: REST.
GraphQL.
gRPC.
SOAP.
why: 别过度思考协议选择：没有特殊理由就默认 REST，它简单、通用、考官零解释成本。
why_en: Default to REST, which uses HTTP verbs for CRUD on resources, unless you have a specific reason not to.
whenOtherWins: 客户端多样、数据需求差异大 → GraphQL；内部服务间通信、性能关键 → RPC/gRPC；对接遗留企业系统 → SOAP。
tradeoff: REST『通用、零解释成本』 vs 专用协议『更贴合特定约束，但引入额外复杂度』

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源做增删改查的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that uses HTTP verbs to perform CRUD operations on resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端可以精确声明所需字段的查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets the client specify exactly which fields it needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 开源的高性能 RPC 框架，常用于服务间通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance remote-procedure-call framework, often used for service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 XML 的老式企业级 Web 服务协议，报文冗长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOAP is an older XML-based enterprise web-service protocol with verbose messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对资源的四种基本操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRUD stands for the four basic operations: create, read, update, and delete.

optionMeanings: 资源化 + HTTP 动词，业界最通用的默认选择
客户端自定义查询形状的协议
面向动作、序列化高效的内部通信协议
基于 XML 信封的老式企业协议
optionScenarioImpacts: 考官几乎不需要额外解释就能读懂你的接口
本场景客户端单一，引入 GraphQL 的复杂度换不来收益
本场景不是服务间调用，用不上它的性能优势
现代产品面试几乎不会以 SOAP 为默认选择
optionDirectness: 适合客户端形态简单、没有特殊协议收益时，REST 的解释成本最低。
适合多端字段差异大时；单一客户端下通常只是增加 schema 层。
适合内部高性能调用；对普通外部产品 API 往往解释成本更高。
适合遗留企业集成；新系统默认选它会带来不必要复杂度。
optionMeanings_en: Resource-oriented HTTP verbs, the industry's default choice.
A protocol where clients shape their own query.
An action-oriented protocol with efficient serialization for internal calls.
An older XML-envelope enterprise protocol.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer can read your API with almost no extra explanation.
With one client type, GraphQL's added complexity buys little here.
This isn't a service-to-service scenario, so its speed edge goes unused.
Modern product interviews almost never default to SOAP.
optionDirectness_en: Use REST when the client shape is simple and no special protocol benefit outweighs its low explanation cost.
Use GraphQL when client field needs differ a lot; for one client it usually adds schema overhead.
Use gRPC for high-performance internal calls; for a normal product API it costs more to explain.
Use SOAP for legacy enterprise integration; defaulting to it in a new system adds needless complexity.
q_en: Which API protocol should you choose by default?
scenario_en: You are designing a normal product interview system with one main client type and no special service-to-service performance constraint.

scenario: 系统要同时服务移动端、网页端、手表端等多种客户端，各端需要的数据字段差异很大，担心接口返回太多或太少数据。
q: 最匹配的 API 风格是？
options: REST 固定返回全部字段
为每种客户端各复制一套 REST API
GraphQL——客户端精确声明要什么数据
改用 FTP 传输数据
options_en: REST that always returns every field.
Duplicate a separate REST API for each client type.
GraphQL — clients specify exactly what data they want.
Switch to FTP for data transfer.

scenario: 按 REST 惯例为 Twitter 设计「发推」接口，当前用户由请求头里的认证 token 识别。
q: 哪个 endpoint 设计最符合惯例？

POST /v1/tweet?user_id=123&text=hello
GET /v1/createTweet

GET /v1/createTweet.
POST /v1/tweets with a body containing { "user_id": string, "text": string }.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源做增删改查的 API 风格。

scenario: 发推接口把当前用户写在请求体的 user_id 字段里，服务端直接读取这个字段当作作者。
q: 让客户端在请求体里传 user_id 来标识「当前用户」，隐患是什么？
options: 请求体会变大，浪费带宽
JSON 解析速度变慢
接口无法做 HTTP 缓存
任何人都能伪造别人的身份发帖
options_en: The request body gets larger, wasting bandwidth.
JSON parsing becomes slower.
The endpoint can no longer use HTTP caching.
Anyone can forge another user's identity and post as them.
why: 身份来自认证而非输入：始终从 auth token 推导当前用户，否则请求体里的 user_id 可被随意篡改冒充。
why_en: Never take the current user's identity from the request body; derive it from the authentication token, or anyone can impersonate anyone.
codeSample:
# 不安全：身份来自可篡改的请求体
POST /v1/tweets
body: { "user_id": "123", "text": "hi" }

# 安全：身份来自认证 token
POST /v1/tweets
Authorization: Bearer <token>
body: { "text": "hi" }   # user 从 token 解出

why_en: Go through your API endpoints one by one and build up the design sequentially to satisfy each of them.
whenOtherWins: 数据处理型系统（如爬虫）按 data flow 的步骤顺序推进更自然，而不是按 endpoint。
tradeoff: 逐 endpoint 搭建『天然贴合需求，但节奏依赖 API 清晰度』 vs 一次性堆全部组件『看似全面，实际容易偏离需求』
optionMeanings: 把『覆盖全面』误当成推进方式
把数据库当成设计的起点而非终点
把深挖阶段的加固内容提前搬进高层设计
把 API 清单当作驱动设计的顺序表
optionScenarioImpacts: 很多组件到最后用不上，等于提前浪费时间画蛇添足
容易先陷入表结构细节，反而忘了先满足接口需求
多机房容灾属于非功能需求的深挖内容，过早引入会拖慢节奏
每加一个组件都能直接对应一条需求，不容易偏题
optionDirectness: 适合最后做查漏补缺；一开始全摆上去容易堆出无用组件。
适合存储是核心难点的题；多数题先从数据库开画会丢请求路径。
适合深挖可用性和容灾；高层设计起点应先跑通核心 API。
适合大多数产品题：每个 endpoint 推出需要的组件，范围不容易跑偏。
optionMeanings_en: Mistakes 'cover everything' for a way to make progress.
Starts from the database as the beginning rather than the end.
Pulls deep-dive hardening content forward into high-level design.
Uses the API list as the ordered driver of the design.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Many components end up unused, wasting time drawing things you don't need.
You get stuck in table-structure detail and forget to satisfy the endpoints first.
Multi-region resilience is deep-dive, non-functional content; pulling it forward stalls momentum.
Each added component maps directly to a requirement, keeping the design on track.
optionDirectness_en: Listing every component fits a final checklist, but at the start it creates unused pieces.
Starting from storage fits database-centric problems; most product designs need the request path first.
Global disaster recovery fits an availability deep dive; high-level design should first run the core API.
Endpoint-by-endpoint design fits most product systems because each API reveals the components it needs.
q_en: What is the safest way to move through high-level design?
scenario_en: You are entering high-level design with a blank canvas and want a path that does not miss requirements.

q: 高层设计阶段过早堆复杂度（缓存、队列全上）最常见的下场是？
options: 永远到不了完整方案，时间被复杂度提前耗尽
设计更完善，通常会加分
反而节省了深挖环节的时间
面试官会主动替你简化设计
options_en: You never reach a complete solution because complexity eats the clock early.
The design looks more thorough and usually earns bonus points.
It actually saves time in the deep-dives step.
The interviewer will step in and simplify the design for you.
why: 这是极常见的失败：复杂度上得太早导致做不完。正确做法是发现可优化点时口头点一句、写个便签，然后继续推进。
why_en: Layering on complexity too early is why candidates never finish; keep the design simple, note improvement areas, and defer them to the deep dives.
optionMeanings: 指出提前堆料导致做不完的真实后果
误以为堆砌组件本身就是加分项
误以为提前处理复杂度能压缩深挖时间
误以为考官会主动帮你收敛设计
optionScenarioImpacts: 简单设计先跑通全部功能需求，复杂度留到深挖分批处理
考官更在意是否先满足了核心功能，而不是组件数量
深挖环节本就需要单独时间逐条对照 NFR，省不掉
考官通常只提问和观察，不会替你简化设计
optionMeanings_en: Names the real cost: piling on early means never finishing.
Wrongly assumes piling on components is itself a bonus.
Wrongly assumes handling complexity early shrinks the deep-dive time needed.
Wrongly assumes the interviewer will simplify the design for you.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A simple design clears all functional requirements first, saving complexity for deep dives.
Interviewers care more about meeting core functionality than component count.
Deep dives still need their own time to check off each NFR; it can't be pre-saved.
Interviewers mostly observe and probe; they won't simplify the design for you.
q_en: What usually happens when you add caches, queues, and other complexity too early?

q: 画高层设计时，嘴上应该同步讲什么？
options: 报出每个组件的品牌型号
数据如何流经系统：每一步哪些状态发生变化
背诵组件的发布年份
保持安静，专心画图就好
options_en: Call out the brand and model number of every component.
How data flows through the system: what state changes at each step.
Recite the release year of each component.
Stay silent and just focus on drawing.
why: 边画边讲思路：显式说明请求路径上的数据流与状态变更，请求到达持久层时顺手在库旁标注关键字段。
why_en: Talk through how data flows through the system and what state changes with each request, from the API call to the response.
optionMeanings: 把讲解重点放在品牌这种无关信息上
点出数据流与状态变更这条正确讲解主线
把讲解重点放在发布年份这种无关信息上
把讲解环节整体省略掉
optionScenarioImpacts: 品牌信息对判断架构是否正确毫无帮助
考官能实时跟上你的每一步决策依据
发布年份不会影响任何设计判断
考官只能看图猜测，无法评估你的思路
optionMeanings_en: Puts the narration focus on irrelevant brand information.
Names the correct thread: data flow and state changes.
Puts the narration focus on irrelevant release-year trivia.
Drops the narration step entirely.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Brand information does nothing to help judge whether the architecture is correct.
The interviewer can follow your reasoning at every step in real time.
Release year has no bearing on any design decision.
The interviewer is left guessing from the diagram alone, with no communication signal.
q_en: What should you explain out loud while drawing the high-level design?

q: 在图上给数据库标注 schema 时，正确的详略度是？
options: 每个表的所有列都写全，并标注类型
完全不写任何字段
只记录与设计特别相关的列，类型也不用标
只写主键，其余全部省略
options_en: Write out every column of every table, with types.
Write no fields at all.
Note only the columns relevant to your design, and skip types.
Write only the primary key and omit everything else.
why: 别浪费时间抄显而易见的 schema；把字段写在数据库组件旁边、只写设计相关的，方便随设计演进而更新。
why_en: Document only the columns that matter to your design next to the database, skipping obvious fields and types the interviewer can infer.
optionMeanings: 把这一步当成完整建表任务
把这一步的信息量直接清零
点出『只写设计相关字段』这个正确详略度
把详略度压缩到只剩主键，丢失设计相关字段
optionScenarioImpacts: email/密码哈希这类显而易见的字段会占用大量画图时间
深挖时想引用某个字段却发现图上完全没有记录
考官一眼就能看到你认为重要的字段，且方便随设计更新
像『分片键』『索引字段』这类关键信息反而被漏掉
optionMeanings_en: Treats this step as a complete table-definition task.
Reduces the information content of this step to zero.
Names the right level of detail: only design-relevant columns.
Compresses detail down to just the primary key, dropping relevant fields.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Obvious fields like email or password hash eat up drawing time for no benefit.
You want to reference a field during deep dives but the diagram never recorded it.
The interviewer immediately sees what you consider important, and it's easy to update.
Key design fields like a shard key or index column get dropped too.
q_en: How much schema detail should you write next to the database in the diagram?

q: 关于面试用的白板软件（如 Excalidraw），建议是？
options: 提前问招聘协调人用什么软件，并预先练熟
现场再摸索学习就行
坚持要求改用纸笔
软件用什么不重要，无需准备
options_en: Ask your recruiting coordinator ahead of time which tool you'll use, and practice it.
Figure it out live during the interview.
Insist on switching to pen and paper instead.
The tool doesn't matter, so no need to prepare.
why: 别把宝贵时间浪费在跟工具搏斗上：提前向招聘协调人确认软件并练习到顺手。
why_en: Ask your recruiter which whiteboarding software you'll use and practice with it ahead of time so you're not fumbling in the interview.
optionMeanings: 把工具熟练度当成可以提前消除的变量
把学习工具的成本转嫁到面试当场
把工具选择权强加给面试流程
误以为工具生疏不会拖慢设计节奏
optionScenarioImpacts: 提前练熟后，画图动作不会占用设计思考的带宽
现场摸索快捷键会挤占本该用于设计的分钟数
多数公司的面试流程是固定的，临时换工具通常不被允许
找快捷键、拖控件的卡顿会被算进你的 45 分钟
optionMeanings_en: Treats tool familiarity as a variable you can remove in advance.
Shifts the cost of learning the tool into the interview itself.
Tries to impose your own tool choice on the interview process.
Wrongly assumes tool unfamiliarity won't slow down delivery.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Practicing beforehand means drawing never competes with design thinking.
Learning shortcuts live eats into minutes that should go to designing.
Most companies run a fixed process; swapping tools last-minute usually isn't allowed.
Fumbling for shortcuts and dragging shapes counts against your forty-five minutes.
q_en: What should you do about interview whiteboard tools like Excalidraw?

q: 深挖（Deep Dives）环节要用剩余 ~10 分钟做哪些事？（多选）
options: 确保设计满足所有非功能需求
处理边界情况、识别并解决瓶颈
根据面试官的追问改进设计
推翻高层设计重画一遍
options_en: Make sure the design meets every non-functional requirement.
Handle edge cases and identify and fix bottlenecks.
Improve the design based on the interviewer's probing questions.
Scrap the high-level design and redraw it from scratch.
why: 深挖 = 加固既有设计：对照 NFR 逐条满足、补边界、消瓶颈、回应探询——不是推倒重来。
why_en: Deep dives harden the design by meeting the non-functional requirements, addressing edge cases and bottlenecks, and improving based on interviewer probes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    NFR["NFRs"] --> Bottleneck["Bottlenecks"]
    Bottleneck --> Edge["Edge cases"]
    Edge --> Improve["Improve design"]
    Improve --> Signals["Answer probes"]
optionMeanings: 把每条 NFR 转化成一段针对性的加固讨论
找出高层设计里没扛住压力或没覆盖到的地方
把考官的追问当成设计还有薄弱环节的信号
把深挖误当成重新设计的机会
optionScenarioImpacts: 缺一条 NFR 没被讨论，就等于这条需求没被验收
瓶颈不解决，非功能需求（如扩展性）就无法真正满足
顺着追问改进能精准命中考官想看的信号
推倒重来会让原本已验证过的高层设计失去价值
optionMeanings_en: Turns each NFR into a targeted hardening discussion.
Finds where the high-level design can't take load or leaves gaps.
Treats interviewer follow-ups as a signal of remaining weak spots.
Mistakes deep dives for a chance to redesign from scratch.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: An NFR that never gets discussed is effectively never verified.
Unfixed bottlenecks mean a non-functional requirement like scalability isn't truly met.
Following the probes precisely targets the signal the interviewer wants.
Starting over discards the value of a high-level design that was already validated.
q_en: What should you do with the remaining roughly ten minutes for deep dives? (Select all that apply)

q: 深挖环节里，junior 与 senior 候选人的差异是？
options: junior 必须比 senior 讲得更多
senior 可以直接跳过深挖环节
两者的主动性要求完全一样
junior 靠考官引导，senior 主动带节奏
options_en: Junior candidates must talk more than senior ones.
Senior candidates can skip the deep-dives step entirely.
Both levels are expected to show identical proactivity.
Juniors lean on interviewer guidance; seniors lead proactively.
why: 主动性与级别成正比：越资深越要自己发现问题、带节奏，而不是等考官喂点。
why_en: Junior candidates can expect the interviewer to point out weak spots, while senior candidates should identify them and lead the deep dives themselves.
tradeoff: junior『被动应答，考官引导』 vs senior『主动识别薄弱点，自己带节奏』
optionMeanings: 把差异错误地归结为说话总量
把资深误解为可以豁免这一环节
忽略了主动性这个真正的区分维度
点出主动权归属这条真正的区分维度
optionScenarioImpacts: 说话多少不是考官评估资深度的方式
跳过深挖会导致 NFR 完全没被验收
考官会用同一套标准衡量不同级别的主动性，其实标准是分级的
junior 靠考官引导，senior 靠自己主导，两者评分预期不同
optionDirectness: 适合描述发言风格，不适合区分级别；级别差异主要看主动性。
只有面试流程已明确不考深挖时才可能跳过，系统设计通常不会这样。
适合低级别校准；级别越高，越期待你自己提出问题和取舍。
适合真实面试预期：junior 可被引导，senior 要主动发现瓶颈。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly reduces the difference to how much each person talks.
Misreads seniority as an exemption from this step.
Ignores proactivity, the actual differentiating dimension.
Names the real differentiator: who is expected to lead.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Talking more or less isn't how interviewers assess seniority.
Skipping deep dives means the NFRs never get verified at all.
Interviewers apply a leveled standard, not one uniform bar, for proactivity.
Juniors lean on interviewer guidance while seniors lead; the scoring bar differs accordingly.
optionDirectness_en: Talk volume describes style, not level; level is mostly about proactivity.
Skipping deep dives fits only a process that explicitly does not test them, which system design usually does.
Equal proactivity fits junior calibration; higher levels are expected to raise issues themselves.
This matches real interview expectations: juniors can be guided, seniors should surface bottlenecks.
q_en: How do junior and senior candidates differ in the deep-dive stage?

q: 深挖环节滔滔不绝、盖住面试官说话的代价是？
options: 显得更主动，通常会加分
错过考官想收集的特定信号，还会拉低沟通协作评分
对最终评估没有影响
可以借机多讲一个备选方案
options_en: It looks proactive and usually earns bonus points.
You miss the specific signals the interviewer wants and hurt your communication score.
It has no effect on the final evaluation.
It's a chance to squeeze in one more alternative design.
why: 考官往往带着特定信号清单来提问；你说个不停就把机会说没了。主动和留白要平衡。
why_en: Talking over your interviewer makes you miss the specific signals they need and hurts your communication and collaboration evaluation.
optionMeanings: 把『说得多』和『主动』直接划上等号
点出错失信号+拉低沟通分这个真实代价
误以为发言量不影响任何评分维度
把说个不停包装成『讲方案更全面』
optionScenarioImpacts: 考官其实更看重能否留出提问空间，而非发言总量
考官带着明确的评估清单，插不上话就拿不到那部分信号
沟通协作是明确写在评分项里的独立维度
备选方案挤占的是考官原本要探的问题时间
optionMeanings_en: Equates 'talking a lot' directly with 'being proactive'.
Names the real cost: missed signals plus a lower communication score.
Wrongly assumes talk volume affects no scoring dimension.
Dresses up nonstop talking as 'covering the design more thoroughly'.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Interviewers actually value room to probe more than sheer talk volume.
Interviewers carry a specific checklist; no room to ask means missed signal.
Communication and collaboration is an explicit, separately scored dimension.
The extra alternative crowds out the time the interviewer wanted to probe.
q_en: What is the cost of talking nonstop and covering the interviewer during deep dives?

q: Twitter 例子中，深挖环节「最有趣的问题」是？
options: 用户注册流程该怎么设计
推文的字数校验规则
低延迟 feed：读扩散 vs 写扩散
机房该选址在哪里
options_en: How to design the user registration flow.
The tweet character-count validation rule.
Low-latency feed: fanout-on-read vs fanout-on-write.
Where to locate the data center.
why: 100M+ DAU 引出水平扩展/缓存/分片，而低延迟 feed 才是 Twitter 最有意思的深挖：读扩散 vs 写扩散加缓存。
why_en: For Twitter the most interesting deep dive is low-latency feed fetching, discussing fanout-on-read versus fanout-on-write plus caching.
tradeoff: fanout-on-write『写时推送，读取快但发帖贵』 vs fanout-on-read『读时聚合，写入便宜但大 V 读取慢』
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Feed["Low-latency feed"] --> Read["Fanout on read"]
    Feed --> Write["Fanout on write"]
    Read --> Cache["Cache hot reads"]
    Write --> Queue["Async fanout"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 读时才聚合所有关注对象的内容，写入便宜、读取慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout-on-read aggregates followed users' content at read time, keeping writes cheap but reads slower.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布时就把内容推送进每个粉丝的收件箱，读取快、写入更贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout-on-write pushes content into every follower's inbox at post time, making reads fast but writes more expensive.

optionMeanings: 误把一个次要的账户功能当成核心深挖点
误把一个简单的输入校验当成核心深挖点
点出真正撑起 100M+ DAU 低延迟需求的核心问题
误把与产品体验无关的基础设施选址当成核心深挖点
optionScenarioImpacts: 注册流程和『低延迟 feed』这条 NFR 没有直接关系
字数校验是一行代码就能实现的边界检查，没有架构含量
这条深挖直接决定了 Twitter 能不能撑住海量粉丝的大 V 发帖
选址属于运维/合规话题，不是这道题要深挖的架构权衡
optionMeanings_en: Mistakes a minor account feature for the core deep dive.
Mistakes a simple input check for the core deep dive.
Names the real problem underlying the hundred-million-DAU, low-latency requirement.
Mistakes unrelated infrastructure siting for the core deep dive.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Registration flow has little direct connection to the low-latency-feed NFR.
Character-count validation is a one-line boundary check with no architectural weight.
This deep dive directly determines whether Twitter can serve celebrities with huge follower counts.
Data-center siting is an operations/compliance topic, not this problem's architectural trade-off.
q_en: In the Twitter example, what is the most interesting deep-dive problem?

q: 补全深挖环节的四件事：
text: 深挖时：确保满足{{非功能需求}}、处理{{边界情况}}、识别并解决{{瓶颈}}、根据面试官的{{探询}}改进设计。
why: 这四件事就是『加固设计』的定义；每条非功能需求都应能对应到一段深挖讨论，而不是被口头带过。
why_en: Deep dives ensure the non-functional requirements are met, edge cases are handled, bottlenecks are fixed, and the design improves from interviewer probes.
q_en: Fill in the four jobs of the deep-dive stage:

q: 按正确顺序排列 system design 面试准备的基础阶段：
q_en: Put the foundation stages for system design interview prep in the right order:
steps: 选择一个 delivery framework，作为面试当天的线性路线图
理解 system design interview 到底考什么，可先看 intro 或 mock interview
学习 core concepts、key technologies、common patterns，建立知识地图
why: 先理解面试形态，再选 delivery framework 固定推进顺序，最后补 core concepts 等知识地图；顺序错了容易只背孤立组件。
why_en: Learn the interview format first, then pick a delivery framework, and only then fill in the core-concepts knowledge map.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["1 Intro"] --> B["2 Delivery"]
    B --> C["3 Concepts"]
    C --> D["Practice"]
tradeoff: 先搭路线图 vs 直接刷知识点

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定按顺序推进设计的答题框架，例如需求→接口→数据模型→高层设计→深潜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed step-by-step structure for walking through a system design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试，练习临场表达。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock interview is a timed practice session with another person that simulates the real interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念，例如一致性、缓存、扩展性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core concepts are the reusable system-design ideas such as consistency, caching, and scalability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件，例如数据库、消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key technologies are the concrete components such as databases and message queues used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路，例如读写分离、扇出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common patterns are recurring architecture strategies that show up across many designs.

scenario: 你从没做过 system design interview，连流程和预期都不清楚。
scenario_en: You have never done a system design interview, and you do not yet know the flow or expectations.
q: 准备的第一步最应该是什么？
q_en: What should be the first preparation step?
options: 跳过基础，直接背 30 套完整题解
先读 intro 或看一次 mock interview
只刷 LeetCode 算法，不看设计内容
直接挑战 ChatGPT 这类最难的题
options_en: Skip the basics and memorize thirty full solutions.
Read the intro or watch one mock interview first.
Only grind LeetCode algorithm problems.
Jump straight into the hardest problem, like ChatGPT.
why: 没做过这类面试时，先建立面试形态的整体画面最重要：面试官怎么问、你怎么澄清需求、设计怎么逐步展开。
why_en: If you have never done a system design interview, learn the format and expectations before memorizing full solutions.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经熟悉面试流程，下一步该练 delivery framework 和刻意练习，而不是重复看 intro。

Skip practicing problems and go straight to a mock.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You get stuck on an unfamiliar framework and heavy constraints at once.
You can get comfortable with the framework before adding difficulty.
With no reference solution, beginners struggle to spot their own gaps.

optionDirectness_en: Fits someone with a framework already; beginners face too many variables.
Fits confidence building because the complexity stays manageable.

Fits live rehearsal, but it is too early before framework practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 题目附带的完整书面题解文章。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-up is the full written solution article that comes with a question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock is a timed practice interview with another person.

scenario: 你在 HelloInterview 的题单里发现，一部分题在正文 common questions，另一部分只出现在 More Practice 区。
scenario_en: In the HelloInterview question list, some problems are in common questions, while others only appear in the More Practice section.
q: Common questions 表和 More Practice 表的主要区别是什么？
q_en: What is the main difference between Common questions and More Practice?
options: More Practice 里的题全部是 easy 难度
Common questions 完全不能用来练习
只有 Common questions 附带 write-up
两个题单在内容和形式上完全没有差别
options_en: Every problem in More Practice is easy difficulty.
Common questions cannot be used for practice at all.
Only common questions come with a write-up.
The two lists have no difference in content or format.
why: 正文题单带书面题解，是主线练习材料；More Practice 是补充题库，强调引导练习和 AI 反馈，不一定有完整文章。
why_en: Common questions include a written guide, while More Practice adds extra guided problems that may not have a full write-up.
tradeoff: 带书面题解的主线材料 vs 靠引导反馈的补充题库
optionMeanings: 把区别错误归因为难度分布。
把区别错误归因为能不能练习。
两个题单在“是否配书面题解”上不同。
否认两个题单存在结构差异。
optionScenarioImpacts: 两个题单其实都横跨 easy 到 hard。
两个题单都能拿来做 guided practice。
决定你该先读文章还是直接上手引导练习。
会让你误用某个题单的学习方式。
optionDirectness: 适合按难度选题；这里问的是题单形式差异。
适合判断能否练习；两个题单其实都能练。
适合决定学习方式；有 write-up 就先读后复盘。
适合完全相同的资源；这两个区块形式不同。
optionMeanings_en: Misattributes the difference to difficulty distribution.
Misattributes the difference to whether practice is possible.
The two lists differ in whether a written solution exists.
Denies that a structural difference exists.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Both lists actually span easy through hard.
Both lists support guided practice either way.
It decides whether you read an article first or jump into guided practice.
It leads you to misuse one of the two lists.
optionDirectness_en: Fits difficulty-based selection; this question asks about format.
Fits whether practice is possible; both lists can be practiced.
Fits choosing a study mode because write-ups change the workflow.
Fits identical resources, but these two sections differ in format.

termDefinitions.meaning: 题目附带的完整书面题解文章。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-up is the full written solution article that comes with a question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分步骤引导、边做边给反馈的练习工具。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 练习过程中由 AI 即时给出的评价和建议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI feedback is real-time evaluation and suggestions generated during practice.

scenario: 你已经能独立完成 Bitly 和 Dropbox，但 medium 题会卡在深潜和 tradeoff。
scenario_en: You can complete Bitly and Dropbox on your own, but medium problems still trip you up on deep dives and tradeoffs.
q: 下一步最合理的练习目标是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable next practice target?
options: 换 Ticketmaster、Tinder 这类 medium 题练深潜
回头重新只看 intro 入门介绍文章
跳过 medium，直接冲 ChatGPT 这类 hard 题
感觉太难，直接停止刷题练习
options_en: Move to medium problems like Ticketmaster and Tinder to practice deep dives.
Go back to only reading the intro article.
Skip medium and jump straight to a hard problem like ChatGPT.
Feel discouraged and stop practicing altogether.
why: 难度要逐步递进：easy 建框架，medium 练真实 tradeoff，hard 再练复杂约束。
why_en: A good progression moves from easy framework practice into medium tradeoffs before tackling hard production complexity.
whenOtherWins: 如果连 easy 题都讲不完整，应先继续打磨框架，而不是急着升级难度。
tradeoff: 循序渐进升级难度 vs 跳级挑战更难的题
optionMeanings: 用中等难度题练需求到深潜的过渡。
退回最基础的入门材料。
跳过中间难度直接挑战最难题。
把卡壳当成停止的理由。
optionScenarioImpacts: 正好对上“卡在深潜和 tradeoff”这个具体缺口。
已经会框架了，重看 intro 补不上深潜缺口。
缺口还没补，hard 题会叠加更多复杂约束。
缺口永远得不到练习机会。
optionDirectness: 适合补深潜和取舍短板；难度刚好上一个台阶。
适合重新了解面试形式；补不上 medium 的深潜缺口。
适合高手压测；当前缺口还没补完会更卡。
适合临时休息；不能解决已经暴露的能力缺口。
optionMeanings_en: Use medium-difficulty problems to practice the deep-dive transition.
Retreat to the most basic introductory material.
Skip the middle tier and jump to the hardest problems.
Treat getting stuck as a reason to quit.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It targets exactly the deep-dive and tradeoff gap described.
You already know the framework; the intro won't fix deep-dive gaps.
The gap is still open, and hard problems stack even more constraints.
The gap never gets a chance to close.
optionDirectness_en: Fits the deep-dive and tradeoff gap with one step up in difficulty.
Fits reviewing interview format, not fixing medium-level deep dives.
Fits expert stress tests; this learner's current gap is still open.
Fits taking a break, but it does not close the exposed gap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 针对某个组件或场景做更细的设计展开。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is a detailed exploration of one component or scenario in the design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案之间必须取舍的对比关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tradeoff is the balance you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

q: 补全练习系统设计题的关键规则：
q_en: Fill in the key rule for practicing system design questions:
text: 先{{自己尝试}}，再看{{answer key}}；最后通过{{peer mock}}训练在时间压力下讲出设计。
why: 这条规则把输入学习变成输出训练：先产出，再对照，最后计时讲出来，三步都不能跳。
why_en: The rule turns passive input into active output: attempt first, compare against the answer, then rehearse it under time pressure.
tradeoff: 先产出后对照 vs 先看答案后模仿

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

scenario: 你把某道题的 answer key 从头读到尾，觉得完全看懂了，但没有自己动手画过。
scenario_en: You read a question's answer key end to end and feel you understand it, but you have not drawn the design yourself.
q: 只看题解、不自己画设计，最容易造成什么问题？
q_en: What problem does reading the solution without drawing your own design most often cause?
options: 自动获得口头表达能力
自动知道所有 tradeoff
面试时完全不需要澄清需求
产生“看懂了”等于“会讲会设计”的错觉
options_en: You automatically gain verbal explanation skills.
You automatically know every tradeoff involved.
You no longer need to clarify requirements in the interview.
You get the illusion that understanding equals being able to design and explain it.
why: 阅读答案时结构和取舍已经被作者组织好了；面试现场你必须自己组织，这是两种不同能力。
why_en: Reading a solution can create a false sense of mastery because the author already organized the structure and tradeoffs for you.
optionMeanings: 假设阅读自动训练口头表达。
假设阅读自动覆盖所有取舍场景。
假设阅读能替代需求澄清练习。
把“读懂”错当成“能独立复现”。
optionScenarioImpacts: 表达能力要靠开口讲才能训练，阅读练不到。
换个约束，取舍就会不同，阅读记不住所有变体。
澄清需求是主动提问的技能，读答案不涉及。
面试现场要自己搭结构，读的时候没练过这步。
optionDirectness: 适合已经反复口述的人；单次阅读不会自动给你表达力。
适合固定场景复盘；换约束后仍要重新判断取舍。
适合题面已完全明确；真实面试仍要主动澄清。
适合描述被动阅读风险；它解释了为什么要先自己画。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes reading automatically trains verbal explanation.
Assumes reading automatically covers every tradeoff scenario.
Assumes reading replaces the skill of clarifying requirements.
Mistakes 'I understood it' for 'I can reproduce it myself.'
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Speaking skill only grows by speaking out loud, not by reading.
Change the constraint and the tradeoff changes; reading can't cover every variant.
Clarifying requirements is an active questioning skill reading doesn't touch.
In the real interview you must build the structure yourself, a step reading skips.
optionDirectness_en: Fits someone who already rehearsed aloud; reading once does not build speech.
Fits fixed-scenario review; tradeoffs still change when constraints change.
Fits fully specified prompts; real interviews still require clarification.
Fits the passive-reading risk and explains why drawing first matters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

scenario: 你练题时经常一会儿讲数据库、一会儿讲缓存、一会儿又回到需求，最后时间不够。
scenario_en: When practicing, you keep jumping from database to cache back to requirements, and you run out of time.
q: 应该如何修正这个跳题问题？
q_en: How should you fix this topic-jumping problem?
options: 继续想到哪讲到哪，不用框架
只画最终架构图，跳过前面阶段
固定用 delivery framework，按阶段控制范围
跳过 requirements，直接讲架构
options_en: Keep improvising, jumping topics without a framework.
Only draw the final architecture diagram, skip earlier stages.
Commit to a delivery framework and control scope stage by stage.
Skip requirements and jump straight into architecture.
why: 框架的价值就是让你线性推进、防止 scope creep；系统设计是逐步收敛问题，不是脑暴组件。
why_en: A delivery framework keeps your answer linear and prevents scope creep during a fast-paced interview.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经能自然组织答案，框架可以隐藏在表达里；但练习阶段仍应显式使用它。
tradeoff: 固定阶段推进 vs 想到哪讲到哪
optionMeanings: 让讨论顺序完全跟着联想走。
把设计压缩成只剩最终结果。
用固定阶段顺序逼自己不跑题。
跳过需求，直接从组件开始想。
optionScenarioImpacts: 正是这种跳跃导致时间不够用完。
没有前面阶段支撑，架构图也讲不清为什么这么画。
每个阶段有时间边界，跳来跳去的问题被结构消除。
没有需求锚点，很容易设计出偏题的系统。
optionDirectness: 适合自由脑暴早期；计时面试里会继续失控。
适合最后汇总结果；缺少前置阶段就讲不清依据。
适合防止跳题；阶段顺序会给每段讨论设边界。
适合需求已明确的复盘；正式回答不能跳过需求。
optionMeanings_en: Let the discussion order follow free association.
Compress the design down to just the final result.
Use a fixed stage order to force yourself to stay on track.
Skip requirements and start thinking from components.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This jumping is exactly what is eating your time now.
Without earlier stages, you can't justify why the diagram looks that way.
Each stage has a time boundary, so the jumping-around problem is structurally removed.
Without a requirements anchor, it's easy to design the wrong system.
optionDirectness_en: Fits early brainstorming; a timed interview keeps drifting this way.
Fits final summarization, but the diagram needs earlier justification.
Fits the jumping problem because stages set boundaries for each part.
Fits review after requirements are known; a real answer cannot skip them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试开始时明确的功能性和非功能性需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requirements are the functional and non-functional constraints you clarify at the start.

q: 先读 Core Concepts / Key Technologies / Patterns 的收益是什么？（多选）
q_en: What are the benefits of reading Core Concepts, Key Technologies, and Patterns first? (Select all that apply.)
options: 知道系统设计题常见组件和模式的边界
做题时能复用已有概念，而不是每题从零发明
帮助建立学习范围
保证不用再练任何题
options_en: You learn the boundaries of common components and patterns.
You can reuse existing concepts instead of reinventing them each time.
It helps you scope what you need to study.
It guarantees you never have to practice a question.
why: 基础材料不是替代练题，而是给练题提供词汇和取舍框架；没有基础，题解容易变成死记硬背。
why_en: The foundations give you reusable vocabulary and a tradeoff framework, but they do not replace active practice.
optionMeanings: 了解常见组件/模式各自适用的边界。
把学过的概念当工具直接复用。
明确该学到多深、多广。
假设读完基础就不用再练题。
optionScenarioImpacts: 遇到新题能快速判断该用哪类组件。
省去每题重新发明轮子的时间。
避免漫无目的地乱看资料。
会让你误以为可以跳过输出训练。
optionDirectness: 用来知道组件和模式什么时候适用。
用来把已有概念带进新题，减少从零发明。
用来控制学习范围，避免无目的乱看。
只在不考输出时成立；系统设计仍要练题。
optionMeanings_en: You learn where each common component or pattern applies.
You reuse concepts you've already learned as tools.
It clarifies how deep and how broad to study.
It assumes finishing the foundations means skipping practice.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You can quickly judge which component fits a new problem.
It saves you from reinventing the wheel on every question.
It keeps you from wandering aimlessly through material.
It falsely suggests you can skip output training.
optionDirectness_en: Use this to know when components and patterns apply.
Use this to bring known concepts into new problems.
Use this to scope study instead of wandering through material.
Only works if output is not tested; system design still requires practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.

scenario: 你已经练过几道题，准备进入 mock 阶段，想让反馈更贴近目标面试。
scenario_en: You have practiced several questions and are ready for mocks, but you want feedback that matches your target interview.
q: peer mock 对象怎么选更好？
q_en: Who is the better person to choose for a peer mock?
options: 只找完全不了解 system design 的人
优先找目标公司或相近风格的工程师
只对着镜子读答案
只用随机题目生成器，不要反馈
options_en: Find someone with no system design background at all.
Prioritize an engineer from the target company or a similar interview style.
Just read the answer out loud to a mirror.
Use a random question generator with no feedback.
why: 目标公司员工更熟悉该公司的面试节奏和评价偏好；反馈越贴近目标环境，练习价值越高。
why_en: A peer from the target company is more likely to give feedback aligned with that company's interview style.
whenOtherWins: 找不到目标公司的人时，找有系统设计面试经验的工程师，重点是拿到真实追问。
tradeoff: 贴近目标公司的真实反馈 vs 容易约到的泛泛反馈
optionMeanings: 找完全没有相关背景的人陪练。
找了解目标评分标准的人给反馈。
自己对自己复述，没有外部反馈。
只刷题，主动放弃反馈环节。
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方提不出有价值的技术追问。
追问方式和评分口味更接近真实面试官。

optionDirectness: 适合练普通表达；技术追问和评分反馈会很弱。

适合自我朗读热身；缺少外部追问和纠偏。
适合扩充题量；不能替代有人反馈的 mock。
optionMeanings_en: Pair with someone who has no relevant background at all.
Find someone who knows the target grading style to give feedback.
Recite your own answer to yourself, with no outside feedback.
Only drill questions and deliberately skip the feedback step.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They can't ask technically meaningful follow-up questions.
Follow-up questions and grading feel closer to the real interviewer.
No one can point out the requirement or tradeoff you missed.
Without feedback, your blind spots stay hidden.
optionDirectness_en: Fits general speaking practice; technical follow-up will be weak.
Fits target-company prep because the feedback matches the real style.
Fits a warm-up read-through, but it lacks outside probing.
Fits adding question volume, not replacing a feedback-based mock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

q: “读懂题解”和“面试中讲出设计”的最大区别是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest difference between understanding a write-up and explaining a design in an interview?
options: 讲出设计要在时间压力下自己组织结构和取舍
读懂题解更难，因为不需要表达
两者完全一样
讲出设计不需要任何技术判断
options_en: Explaining a design out loud means organizing structure and tradeoffs yourself, under time pressure.
Reading a write-up is harder because it requires no explanation.
The two are exactly the same skill.
Explaining a design requires no technical judgment at all.
why: 面试是实时沟通：要澄清需求、排序问题、画图、解释取舍并响应追问；阅读只是输入的一部分。
why_en: Speaking a design out loud requires actively organizing structure, tradeoffs, and communication under time pressure.
tradeoff: 主动组织表达 vs 被动接收阅读
optionMeanings: 把讲设计当成主动输出加沟通的任务。
颠倒了阅读和表达的难度关系。
否认输入和输出是两种技能。
错误地剥离了技术判断这一核心。
optionScenarioImpacts: 对应面试官真正在评估的能力。
表达通常比阅读更难，不是更容易。
会让人误以为看懂题解就等于会面试。
面试恰恰全程都在考技术判断。
optionDirectness: 适合描述现场面试能力；它强调自己组织和限时表达。
适合只比较阅读负担；没有覆盖面试输出难点。
适合低风险复习；真实面试和阅读不是同一任务。
适合非技术展示；系统设计仍然围绕技术判断。
optionMeanings_en: Treats explaining a design as active output plus communication.
Reverses the actual difficulty relationship between reading and speaking.
Denies that input and output are different skills.
Incorrectly strips out technical judgment as the core.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It matches what the interviewer is actually evaluating.
Speaking is usually harder than reading, not easier.
It wrongly implies understanding a write-up equals being interview-ready.
Technical judgment is exactly what's being tested throughout.
optionDirectness_en: Fits live interview skill because it stresses organizing under time.
Fits comparing reading load, not the hard part of interview output.
Fits low-risk review; real interviews and reading are different tasks.
Fits nontechnical presentation, but system design centers on judgment.

scenario: 主线 common questions 题单大约有 30 道，分布在 easy（约 4 道）、medium（约 13 道）、hard（约 13 道）三档。
scenario_en: The main common questions list has about 30 problems across easy, medium, and hard tiers: roughly 4 easy, 13 medium, and 13 hard.
q: 这个题量和难度分布，最支持哪条备考策略？
q_en: What prep strategy does this problem count and difficulty split support?
options: 跳过 medium，直接从 easy 冲到 hard
题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上
只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题
在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档
options_en: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
Only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
Sample practice across all three difficulty tiers instead of only one.
why: 约 30 道题在三档间分布均衡，说明常见面试难度本身就是均衡分布的；两周内做不完全部，应按难度分层抽样，而不是只啃一档或反复刷同一批题。
why_en: With about thirty problems split evenly across easy, medium, and hard, the right move in a short window is to sample every tier, not just one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文章正文列出的主线练习题单，带书面 write-up。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common questions are the main practice list in the article, each with a written guide.

scenario: 你独立完成一题后，对比 answer key 发现自己的高层架构不同。
scenario_en: After completing a problem independently, you compare with the answer key and find that your high-level architecture is different.
q: 最有价值的复盘方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most useful way to review the difference?
options: 直接把自己写的完整答案删除重做一遍
只核对两边用的组件名称是否一致
跳过复盘环节，直接进入下一道练习题
比较背后的 requirements 和 tradeoffs
options_en: Delete your own complete answer and redo it from scratch.
Only check whether the component names on both sides match.
Skip the review step and go straight to the next practice question.
Compare the requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference.
why: 系统设计通常没有唯一图；复盘要找出作者为什么选了某个组件、你漏了哪个约束、哪些取舍没讲清。
why_en: The useful review compares requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference, not the memorization of one architecture diagram.
whenOtherWins: 如果你的方案违反了硬性需求或指标，那不是风格差异，是需要修正的设计错误。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Mine["My design"] --> Gap["Find gaps"]
    Key["Answer key"] --> Gap
    Gap --> Req["Requirements"]
    Gap --> Trade["Tradeoffs"]
    Gap --> Deep["Deep dives"]
tradeoff: 复盘约束和取舍 vs 复盘表面架构图
optionMeanings: 把不同结果当成完全失败处理。
只核对名词，不核对决策依据。
放弃从这道题里学习的机会。
把差异当成理解取舍的线索去追问。
optionScenarioImpacts: 丢掉了本可以对比学习的素材。
组件名一样，决策逻辑可能完全没学到。
同样的缺口会在下一题重复出现。
能定位自己漏掉的约束或没考虑的取舍。
optionDirectness: 适合方案明显错误时重做；这里先要理解差异来源。
适合快速核对表面组件；不能解释为什么选它们。
适合赶进度；会错过这道题给你的反馈。
适合复盘设计判断；差异会指向漏掉的约束。
optionMeanings_en: Treat a different result as total failure.
Only check naming, not the reasoning behind decisions.
Give up the chance to learn from this question.
Treat the difference as a clue to chase down the reasoning.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You throw away material you could have learned from.
Matching names doesn't mean you learned the decision logic.
The same gap will resurface on the next question.
You can pinpoint the missed constraint or unconsidered tradeoff.
optionDirectness_en: Fits clearly broken designs; here you first need the source of the gap.
Fits surface-level component checks, not why those components were chosen.
Fits moving fast, but it throws away the feedback from this question.
Fits reviewing design judgment because differences point to missed constraints.

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 设计必须满足的硬性限制条件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constraints are the hard limits a design must satisfy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案之间必须取舍的对比关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tradeoffs are the balances you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

q: 补全准备路线的三个基础动作：
q_en: Fill in the three foundation steps in the preparation path:
text: 理解{{system design interview}}是什么，选择{{Delivery Framework}}，再学习{{Core Concepts}}、{{Key Technologies}}和{{Common Patterns}}。
why: 三步构成从面试形态到表达框架、再到知识地图的基础路线；缺一步，后面练习容易失焦。
why_en: The foundation is understanding the interview format, choosing a delivery framework, and then filling in core concepts, technologies, and patterns.
tradeoff: 先搭完整基础 vs 边练边补概念

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路。
