scenario: endpoint server 主要资源是打开的连接数，每条连接工作量类似。
scenario_en: The endpoint server's main resource is open connection count, and each connection does roughly similar work.
q: 负载均衡策略用什么最直观？
q_en: Which load-balancing strategy is the most direct fit?
options: 按请求的 URL path 做随机切分，和连接数无关
least connections（挑连接数最少的 server）
把所有长连接固定发给最开始那一台 server 处理
按 HTML 静态文件的大小来分配后续流量
why: 连接数本身就是资源消耗的主指标。least-connections 能避免某台 server 因历史长连接过多而成为热点。
why_en: Least-connections load balancing fits endpoint servers whose main resource is open connection count.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个连接负载差异很大，还要结合消息 QPS、CPU 和 per-topic 热度。
options_en: Randomly split traffic by the request's URL path, unrelated to connection count.
Least connections — route to whichever server currently holds the fewest connections.
Pin all long-lived connections to whichever server handled the very first request.
Allocate subsequent traffic based on the size of an HTML static file.
tradeoff: 按真实资源消耗均衡 vs 与连接数无关的路由规则
optionMeanings: URL path 和连接负载没有必然关系。
连接数就是资源消耗的主指标，直接按它均衡最直观。
固定一台会让它成为热点，完全没有均衡。
文件大小和长连接的资源消耗无关。

q: 实时系统中 zombie connection 指什么？
q_en: What is a zombie connection in a realtime system?
options: CDN 边缘节点上的缓存内容已经过期
数据库表里出现了同一条数据的重复行
一端以为连接还活着，但另一端已经断开或清理
同一个用户同时用多台设备登录
why: 移动网络、WiFi 切换和服务器重启都可能让连接状态不一致。Heartbeat/ping-pong 用来快速发现死连接。
why_en: A zombie connection is one side believing a connection is alive after the other side has lost or cleaned it up.
options_en: Cached content expiring at a CDN edge node.
Duplicate rows appearing in a database table.
One side believes the connection is still alive while the other side has already dropped or cleaned it up.
One user being logged in from multiple devices.
optionMeanings: 这是缓存失效问题，和连接状态无关。
这是数据一致性问题，和连接状态无关。
一端以为连接还活着，另一端其实已清理，这就是 zombie。
这是多设备场景，本身不是连接故障。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge servers that caches content close to users.

q: 断线重连设计通常需要哪些能力？（多选）
q_en: What capabilities does reconnect design usually need? (Select all that apply.)
options: heartbeat 检测断线
client reconnect with backoff
sequence number / last event ID 用来补发漏消息
断线期间消息直接丢弃且不记录
why: 真实网络一定会断。可靠实时系统要检测、重连、并根据客户端最后收到的位置补齐 gap。
why_en: Reliable realtime systems need heartbeats, reconnect backoff, and sequence IDs to replay missed updates.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: heartbeat
    S-->>C: ack
    Note over C,S: 网络断开
    C->>S: reconnect + last_seq
    S-->>C: replay missed
options_en: Heartbeats detect that a connection has died.
The client reconnects with backoff to avoid a reconnect storm.
A sequence number or last event ID lets the server know what to replay.
Drop messages during a disconnect and never record them.
optionMeanings: heartbeat 定期探测，快速发现连接已经死掉。
client reconnect with backoff 避免风暴式重连打垮服务器。
sequence number/last event ID 让服务器知道该补发哪一段。
反例：直接丢弃且不记录，重连后用户就永久漏消息。

termDefinitions.meaning: 给消息编号，客户端和服务器都能用它对齐看到哪了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number labels each message so client and server can agree on how far the client has read.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSE 事件自带的编号；重连时浏览器自动带上它，服务器据此补发漏掉的事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-Event-ID is the SSE event identifier the browser resends on reconnect so the server can replay missed events.

scenario: WebSocket 断开 20 秒后重连，客户端需要收到断线期间的消息。
scenario_en: A WebSocket disconnects for 20 seconds and then reconnects; the client still needs the messages sent during the gap.
q: 服务端应如何支持？
q_en: How should the server support this?
options: 让客户端在成功重连之后自己凭空猜测断线期间究竟收到过什么样的消息
直接放弃处理，明确告诉用户断线期间产生的所有消息都已经永久丢失了
只依赖 TCP 协议本身在传输层自动帮你保存断线期间产生的全部消息内容
维护 per-user 消息队列或 Redis Streams，按 sequence number 补发错过的消息
why: WebSocket 本身不替你保存断线消息。需要可查询的消息日志和 last_seen cursor。
why_en: WebSocket reconnection needs a durable message log or queue plus a last-seen cursor to replay missed messages.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务允许丢失临时 presence/typing indicator，可以不补发这些 ephemeral events。
options_en: Let the client, after successfully reconnecting, guess out of thin air what messages it might have missed.
Simply give up and tell the user that every message sent during the disconnect is permanently lost.
Rely solely on the TCP transport layer to automatically save every message sent during a disconnect.
Maintain a per-user message queue or Redis Streams and replay missed messages by sequence number.
tradeoff: 多维护一份可查询的消息日志 vs 断线期间完全无补发能力
optionMeanings: 猜测内容既不可靠，也不是工程方案。
放弃补发会让用户体验很差，且并非唯一选项。
TCP 只管这条连接内的字节顺序，不会替你持久化消息。
per-user 消息日志 + sequence number 是补发的标准做法。
codeSample:
XADD user:42:events * type message text "hi"
XREAD COUNT 50 STREAMS user:42:events 1699999999-0
# XADD 把事件追加进该用户的 stream
# 重连时带上 last_seen id，XREAD 从那之后读取补发

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里的一种追加日志结构，支持按位置读取和补发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Streams is an append-only log data structure in Redis that supports reading from a given position for replay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给消息编号，客户端和服务器都能用它对齐看到哪了。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number labels each message so client and server can agree on how far the client has read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

q: 实时系统里的 celebrity problem 是什么？
q_en: What is the celebrity problem in realtime systems?
options: 一个高关注用户的更新需要同时推给数百万客户端，naive fanout 可能压垮系统
用户在设置页面填写的显示名字超过了后端字段长度限制
WebSocket 协议在设计上本身就无法传输任何文本类型的消息
系统里恰好所有用户账号在这一时刻都处于离线状态
why: 名人发帖、直播评论、大促库存等会制造极端 fanout。不能简单对每个 follower 单独同步推送。
why_en: The celebrity problem is massive fanout when one user's update must reach millions of clients at once.
options_en: One highly followed user's update must reach millions of clients at once, and naive fanout can crash the system.
The display name a user entered on the settings page exceeds the backend's field length limit.
The WebSocket protocol, by design, is fundamentally unable to transmit any text-type message.
Every single user account in the system happens to be offline at this exact moment.
optionMeanings: 百万级 fanout 是 celebrity problem 的核心：naive 推送会打垮系统。
这是字段校验问题，和 fanout 规模无关。
WebSocket 能传文本，这个说法本身就错了。
离线状态不是 fanout 压力的成因。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条更新要分发给大量接收者，接收者数量越大分发压力越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is delivering one update to a large number of recipients; more recipients means more delivery pressure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that lets client and server exchange messages both ways over one persistent connection.

q: 处理单个更新 fanout 给数百万用户时，可考虑哪些策略？（多选）
q_en: Which strategies can handle one update fanning out to millions of users? (Select all that apply.)
options: 缓存更新一次，通过层级/区域分发推给本地连接
批量聚合和分层广播，避免单组件直接打满
对非关键实时性允许稍微延迟或抽样
同步逐个写入所有用户连接且不做限流
why: 极端 fanout 要把压力分层、批处理或缓存。完全同步逐个推送会产生热点。
why_en: Massive fanout needs caching, hierarchical distribution, batching, and sometimes relaxed freshness.
diagram:
flowchart TB
    A["热点更新"] --> B["聚合/限流"]
    B --> C["区域 fanout"]
    C --> D["Endpoint servers"]
    D --> E["大量客户端"]
options_en: Cache the update once and distribute it through regional or hierarchical layers of local connections.
Batch and broadcast hierarchically so no single component takes the full hit.
Allow slight delay or sampling where strict realtime is not critical.
Synchronously write to every user connection one by one with no throttling.
optionMeanings: 缓存更新一次，按区域/层级分发给本地连接，减少重复计算。
批量聚合 + 分层广播，避免单组件被瞬间打满。
非关键实时性允许延迟或抽样，用宽松度换稳定性。
反例：同步逐个写入且不限流，正是会被打垮的做法。

q: 分布式实时更新为什么会遇到 message ordering 问题？
q_en: Why do distributed realtime updates run into message ordering problems?
options: JSON 这种数据交换格式在设计上完全无法表达任何顺序字段
不同 server/partition/network path 处理消息，发送顺序和到达顺序可能不一致
客户端在系统运行的任意时刻永远只能收到一条服务器消息
load balancer 会在转发过程中自动帮所有消息重新排好顺序
why: 多个 server 并行处理时，消息可能乱序。关键流需要明确排序域和顺序来源。
why_en: Distributed realtime systems can reorder messages when different servers or paths process them concurrently.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["msg 1"] --> S1["Server A"] --> C["Client"]
    B["msg 2"] --> S2["Server B"] --> C
    S2 -.可能先到.-> C
    O["single sequencer"] -->|统一编号| C
options_en: JSON, as a data interchange format, is by design fundamentally unable to represent any ordering field.
Different servers, partitions, or network paths process messages, so send order and arrival order can differ.
A client, at any moment while the system is running, can only ever receive one server message.
The load balancer automatically re-sorts every message into the correct order while forwarding it.
optionMeanings: JSON 本身能表达顺序字段，这不是根因。
不同 server/路径并行处理，天然可能打乱到达顺序。
客户端能收多条消息，这个前提不对。
LB 不做消息排序，这是应用层要解决的问题。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种轻量级的结构化数据格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON is a lightweight structured data format.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple backend servers.

scenario: 在线拍卖中，同一个 item 的出价顺序必须明确，总顺序比水平扩展更重要。
scenario_en: In an online auction, bids for the same item need a clear total order, and that order matters more than horizontal scale.
q: 更务实的排序策略是什么？
q_en: What is the more pragmatic ordering strategy?
options: 完全依赖每个客户端设备本地时钟给自己的出价打时间戳
让每一台 server 各自独立、随机决定收到消息的处理先后顺序
把同一 item 的消息 funnel 到单个 server/partition 打顺序号
干脆不记录任何一次出价之间的先后顺序关系
why: 产品类面试里，单 host/partition 负责同一实体通常比 vector clocks 更简单可靠。它用可控扩展换明确顺序。
why_en: For product systems, funneling one entity's messages through one server or partition gives a simple total order.
whenOtherWins: 深层基础设施或多主复制系统才更常讨论 vector clocks、logical clocks 等复杂技术。
options_en: Rely entirely on each client device's local clock to timestamp its own bids.
Let every server independently and randomly decide the processing order of messages it receives.
Funnel one item's messages through a single server or partition that stamps a sequence number.
Simply don't record the ordering relationship between any bids at all.
tradeoff: 牺牲一点水平扩展换来简单的总顺序 vs 全局分布式排序的实现复杂度
optionMeanings: 客户端时钟不可信，会导致乱序甚至作弊。
随机顺序无法保证同一 item 出价的先后关系。
单 server/partition 天然给出一个总顺序，简单可靠。
拍卖场景明确需要顺序，不记录直接违反需求。

q: 什么时候才更可能讨论 vector clocks / logical timestamps？
q_en: When are vector clocks or logical timestamps more likely to come up?
options: 消息只经过单机队列顺序处理的场景
是普通在线拍卖这类产品设计题的默认首选方案
只是每 5 秒刷新一次 dashboard 数字的场景
深层分布式基础设施或多源并发更新，需要表达消息因果关系
why: 大多数产品设计题优先用单 partition 建立顺序。Vector clocks 更适合深 infra 和冲突解析。
why_en: Vector clocks are more common in deep infrastructure problems than in ordinary product realtime designs.
options_en: Messages processed sequentially through a single-machine queue.
The default first choice for an ordinary online-auction product design question.
A dashboard that just refreshes a number every five seconds.
Deep distributed infrastructure or multi-source concurrent updates that need to express causal relationships between messages.
tradeoff: 表达因果关系的通用性 vs 单 partition 方案的简单性
optionMeanings: 单机队列本身处理顺序天然有保证，无需额外机制。
产品设计题里默认优先用单一节点建立顺序，这个说法反了。
低频刷新场景完全用不上任何排序机制。
多源并发写入、需要表达先后因果时才用得上这类机制。

termDefinitions.meaning: 每台节点维护一个计数器向量，用来判断分布式事件之间的因果先后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector clock is a per-node counter vector used to determine the causal order between distributed events.

scenario: 面试官追问：在线拍卖这类产品设计题里，什么情况下才真的需要引入更复杂的分布式排序机制。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks when an online-auction style product design would truly need a more complex distributed ordering mechanism.

scenario: 设计 WhatsApp 类聊天，需要消息即时送达、typing、presence，并处理断线补发。
scenario_en: You are designing WhatsApp-style chat with instant delivery, typing, presence, and replay after disconnects.
q: 合理主线是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable main architecture path?
options: WebSocket 双向连接 + Pub/Sub 路由 + 消息日志支持 reconnect replay
把所有消息汇总起来做成一份每日邮件摘要发给用户查看

每条评论都同步、逐个直接推给每一位观众

WebSocket 实际上完全做不到任何形式的双向通信，只能单向推送
WebSocket 无论在什么场景下实现起来都必然比 polling 更加简单

q: 为什么内容型应用里「读扩展」几乎总是先于「写扩展」成为问题？
q_en: Why do content-heavy apps usually hit read scaling before write scaling?
options: 因为写操作天生比读操作慢
因为数据库默认不支持并发读
因为写产生数据、读消费数据，读流量增长远快于写流量
因为读操作无法用索引优化
why: 打开 Instagram 首页就是 100+ 次读（图片元数据、用户信息、点赞数、评论预览），而你一天可能只发一张照片（一次写）。读消费数据，天然比写多得多。
why_en: Writes create data while reads consume it, so in content-heavy applications read traffic grows far faster than write traffic.
options_en: Writes are inherently slower than reads.
Databases don't support concurrent reads by default.
Writes create data while reads consume it, so read traffic grows far faster than write traffic.
Reads can't be optimized with indexes.

q: 这种数量级对扩展重点选择有什么直接影响？
q_en: What does that order of magnitude imply for scaling priorities?
options: 应该优先攻克写路径的扩展
读路径收益远大于写路径，应优先做读扩展
读写应该同等力度、一起扩展
这说明写操作本身有性能缺陷，需要重构
why: 读写比到 100:1 说明大部分流量是读；索引、缓存、副本这类读优化手段的边际收益远超写路径，应该先攻克读扩展。
why_en: A hundred-to-one read-write ratio means most traffic is reads, so read-side techniques like indexing and caching pay off far more than write-path work.
scenario: 面试官提到某内容应用的读写比大约是 100:1——一条帖子发一次却被读一百次。
scenario_en: The interviewer says a content app has about a 100:1 read-write ratio: one post is written once but read a hundred times.
options_en: Prioritize scaling the write path first.
Read-path techniques pay off far more than write-path work, so scale reads first.
Scale reads and writes with equal effort.
This means the write operations themselves are broken.

q: 读流量把数据库压垮时，为什么通常「不是能调试解决的软件问题」？
q_en: Why is a database overwhelmed by read traffic usually not just a debuggable software bug?
options: 因为数据库代码是闭源的
因为 SQL 优化器不可控
因为一定是网络层的问题
因为撞上了物理极限：CPU/内存/磁盘都有硬上限
why: CPU、内存、磁盘 I/O 都是物理约束，到顶后再聪明的代码也无济于事，只能靠架构手段（索引、副本、缓存）绕开。
why_en: At scale you hit physics: CPU instructions per second, memory capacity, and disk I/O are hard limits that more code cannot overcome.
options_en: It's because database code is closed-source.
It's because the SQL optimizer is out of your control.
It's because it must be a network-layer problem.
It's because you've hit a physical limit: CPU, memory, and disk I/O all have hard ceilings.

why_en: Read scaling progresses from optimizing within the database, to scaling horizontally with replicas, to adding external caching layers.

q: 数据库索引本质上是什么？
q_en: What is a database index at its core?
options: 一张有序的查找表，指向数据行
数据的完整副本
一段查询结果缓存
一种数据压缩算法
why: 索引 = 有序查找结构 + 行指针，像书后的索引直接告诉你该看哪几页。没有索引，数据库只能全表扫描逐行找匹配。
why_en: An index is a sorted lookup table pointing to rows, like a book index that tells you exactly which pages to check.
options_en: A sorted lookup structure that points to rows.
A complete copy of the data.
A cache of query results.
A data compression algorithm.

q: 无索引全表扫描 vs 有索引查找，复杂度和量级差别是？
q_en: What is the complexity difference between a full table scan and an indexed lookup?
options: O(n) vs O(n)，没有差别
都变成 O(1)
O(n) 降到 O(log n)
O(n²) 降到 O(n)
why: 索引把线性扫描变成对数查找：100 万行的表大约只需 20 次索引比较就能定位，这是读优化里性价比最高的一步。
why_en: An index turns a linear scan into a logarithmic lookup, roughly twenty index checks instead of scanning a million rows.
scenario: users 表有 1000 万行，按 email 精确匹配查询；你要判断加索引后复杂度能改善多少。
scenario_en: The users table has 10 million rows and queries look up users by exact email match; you need to judge how much an index improves complexity.
options_en: O(n) versus O(n), no difference.
Both become O(1).
O(n) drops to O(log n).
O(n squared) drops to O(n).

提升是数量级的（10-100倍），常是最快的第一步
提升虽大但只影响写，不影响读扩展
两者没有区别，应直接上分布式存储
why: SSD 没有机械寻道，随机 I/O 比机械盘快 10-100 倍，是买读扩展喘息空间最快的一步。
why_en: SSDs eliminate mechanical seek time, giving roughly ten to one hundred times faster random I/O, often the fastest way to buy read-scaling headroom.
scenario: 现有系统随机读遇到磁盘瓶颈，你在评估把机械盘换成 SSD 能带来多大的杠杆。
scenario_en: Random reads are bottlenecked on spinning disks, and you are evaluating how much leverage SSDs would add.
options_en: The gain is modest (one to two times), not worth it as a scaling move.
The gain is an order of magnitude (ten to one hundred times), often the fastest first step.
The gain is real but only helps writes, not reads.
There's no real difference; go straight to distributed storage.

q: 「范式化 (normalization)」的目的是什么？
q_en: What is the purpose of normalization?
options: 让查询更快
让写入吞吐更高
把数据拆到多张表以减少冗余
自动生成索引
why: 范式化省存储、避免重复数据，但让查询更复杂：展示一个订单摘要可能要 join 用户、订单、商品多张表。
why_en: Normalization splits data across tables to reduce redundancy, at the cost of needing joins to bring related data back together.
options_en: Make queries faster.
Increase write throughput.
Split data across multiple tables to reduce redundancy.
Automatically generate indexes.

scenario: 电商订单摘要页每秒被读几千次，目前要 join users、orders、order_items、products 四张表才能拼出，系统读远多于写。
scenario_en: An e-commerce order-summary page gets thousands of reads per second and currently joins users, orders, order_items, and products; reads far outnumber writes.
q: 最直接的读优化是？
q_en: What is the most direct read optimization?
options: 建一张冗余的订单摘要单表（反范式化）
给四张表各配一台服务器
把 join 移到应用层执行
每次查询前先开启事务
why: 反范式化把用户名、商品名、价格冗余存进订单摘要表，昂贵的多表 join 变成单表点查——用存储换读速度。
why_en: Denormalization stores redundant copies so an expensive multi-table join becomes a simple single-table query, trading storage for read speed.
diagram:
flowchart TB
    A["原始读路径"] --> B["users + orders + order_items + products"]
    B --> C["每次页面加载都 join"]
    D["反范式写路径"] --> E[("order_summary")]
    E --> F["页面单表读取"]
whenOtherWins: 若写入频繁、数据总在变，多处更新的复杂度可能不划算——反范式前先看读写比。
options_en: Create a redundant order-summary table (denormalize) so one query returns everything.
Give each of the four tables its own server.
Move the join logic into the application layer.
Open a transaction before every query.
tradeoff: 存储与写复杂度 vs 查询速度

termDefinitions.meaning: 故意存储冗余数据以减少查询时的 join，用存储换读取速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization deliberately stores redundant data to avoid joins, trading storage for read speed.

q: 反范式化之后，用户改名会发生什么？
q_en: What happens after denormalization when a user changes their name?
options: 什么都不用做
必须更新所有冗余副本，写路径变复杂
数据库会自动同步所有副本
改名操作会被数据库拒绝
why: 冗余数据意味着写时多处更新；好在「改名」远比「看订单」少发生，读多写少时这笔账划算。
why_en: With denormalized data a name change must update every redundant copy, which is acceptable because such writes are rare compared to reads.
options_en: Nothing needs to be done.
Every redundant copy of the name must be updated, complicating the write path.
The database automatically syncs all copies.
The rename would be rejected by the database.

q: 补全反范式化的本质权衡：
q_en: Complete the core denormalization tradeoff.
text: 反范式化用更多{{存储}}和更复杂的{{写入}}，换取更快的{{读取}}；决定之前先看{{读写比}}。
why: 这是「为读优化、牺牲写」的经典例子；写频繁时复杂度可能不值得。
why_en: Denormalization trades extra storage and more complex writes for faster reads, so always check the read-write ratio first.

scenario: 商品页每次加载都要跨 products 和 reviews 两张表计算平均评分，聚合查询昂贵且结果不常变化。
scenario_en: A product page recomputes average ratings across products and reviews on every load; the aggregation is expensive and the result changes slowly.
q: 最合适的手段是？
q_en: What is the best technique here?
options: 每次页面加载都现场计算
把评分数据全部删掉
加更多应用服务器
物化视图：后台预计算并存储，页面直读现成值
why: 物化视图把昂贵聚合「算一次、读多次」，对跨大数据集的分析型查询尤其有效。
why_en: A materialized view precomputes an expensive aggregation once via a background job so every page load just reads the stored result.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P[(products)] --> J["后台 refresh"]
    R[(reviews)] --> J
    J --> MV[("product_ratings 物化视图")]
    Page["商品页"] --> MV
whenOtherWins: 若聚合结果必须实时精确反映最新一条评论，预计算的刷新延迟可能不可接受，只能现算或增量更新。
options_en: Recompute it on every page load.
Delete all the rating data.
Add more application servers.
Materialized view: a background job precomputes the average and pages just read the stored value.
tradeoff: 预计算与新鲜度 vs 实时计算成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 把聚合查询的结果预先计算并存成实体表，读时无需重新计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A materialized view precomputes and stores an aggregation's result so reads skip recomputation.

scenario: 要把「商品平均评分」从每次页面加载现算，改成预计算好供直接读取。
scenario_en: You want to replace live calculation of average product ratings on every page load with a precomputed value that pages can read directly.
q: 哪条 SQL 是正确的做法？
q_en: Which SQL statement is the right move?
options: SELECT p.id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.id;
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW product_ratings AS SELECT p.id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.id;
CREATE INDEX idx_reviews_product_rating ON reviews(product_id, rating) WHERE rating IS NOT NULL;
DELETE FROM reviews WHERE rating IS NULL OR rating NOT BETWEEN 1 AND 5;
why: 物化视图把 join+GROUP BY 的结果落成实体数据，读时零计算；索引帮不了聚合全表的场景。
why_en: The materialized view stores the join and group-by result so reads skip the computation entirely.
codeSample:
-- 每次页面加载都执行会很贵：
SELECT p.id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating
FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id
GROUP BY p.id;

-- 预计算并存储（后台任务定期 REFRESH）：
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW product_ratings AS
SELECT p.id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating
FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.id = r.product_id
GROUP BY p.id;
whenOtherWins: 数据量小或查询本身便宜时，直接查询即可，不必背上物化视图的刷新维护。
options_en: Query the join and average live on every page load.
Create a materialized view that precomputes the per-product average rating from the join.
Create a partial index on reviews by product and rating, excluding nulls.
Delete review rows with a null or out-of-range rating.
tradeoff: 预计算聚合 vs 每次实时 join+GROUP BY

q: 这个阈值信号最支持哪个判断？
q_en: What judgment does this threshold signal support?
options: 远低于任何需要关注的阈值
已经严重超标，必须立刻分片
接近 5-10 万/秒的经验阈值，该扩展或加缓存了
说明索引配置有问题，该重建索引
why: 5-10 万读/秒是粗略经验值，实际取决于读模式、数据模型和硬件；面试里粗估足以支撑「该扩展了」这个判断。
why_en: As a rule of thumb, a well-indexed single database needs horizontal scaling or a cache beyond roughly fifty to one hundred thousand reads per second.
scenario: 线上监控显示，已经加好索引的单库读 QPS 持续攀升，正朝着经验阈值靠近。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows a well-indexed single database's read QPS keeps climbing toward the rule-of-thumb threshold.
options_en: Far below any threshold worth worrying about.
Already way over budget, must shard immediately.
Close to the 50,000-100,000 reads/sec rule of thumb — time to scale horizontally or add a cache.
This means the indexes are misconfigured and need rebuilding.

q: 读副本 (read replica) 架构中，读和写分别去哪？
q_en: In a read-replica architecture, where do reads and writes go?
options: 所有写都去主库，读可以去任意副本
读写都去主库
写去副本、读去主库
读写随机分配到任意节点
why: 副本从主库复制数据；写集中在主库，读分散到副本——这就是读吞吐的水平扩展。
why_en: Read replicas copy data from the primary, all writes go to the primary, and reads spread across the replicas.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    W["写请求"] --> P[(主库 Primary)]
    P -->|复制| R1[(副本 1)]
    P -->|复制| R2[(副本 2)]
    Rd["读请求"] --> R1
    Rd --> R2
options_en: All writes go to the primary; reads can go to any replica.
Both reads and writes go to the primary.
Writes go to replicas, reads go to the primary.
Reads and writes are randomly assigned to any node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从主库复制数据的只读数据库副本，用来分摊读流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the database that offloads read traffic from the primary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理所有写入的数据库节点，是数据的权威来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary is the database node that handles all writes and is the source of truth.

q: 除了分摊读吞吐，读副本还附赠什么好处？
q_en: Besides spreading read throughput, what extra benefit do read replicas give?
options: 更强的写一致性
冗余容灾：故障时可提升副本当新主库
更便宜的存储
自动分片
why: 副本天然是数据的额外拷贝：主库挂掉时提升一个副本接任，停机时间大幅缩短。
why_en: Beyond spreading read load, replicas add redundancy because a replica can be promoted to primary if the primary fails.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    P[(Primary)] -->|复制| R1[(Replica A)]
    P -->|复制| R2[(Replica B)]
    P -.-> X["Primary down"]
    R1 -->|promote| N[(New Primary)]
    Traffic["读写流量"] --> N
options_en: Stronger write consistency.
Failover redundancy: a replica can be promoted to primary if it fails.
Cheaper storage.
Automatic sharding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个副本切换成新的主库，通常发生在主库故障时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Promoting a replica means switching it to become the new primary, typically after the old primary fails.

q: 补全标准复制架构：
q_en: Complete the standard replication architecture.
text: Leader-Follower 复制：{{主库(Leader)}} 处理写入，多个{{副本(Follower)}} 处理读取；复制可以是{{同步}}的（慢但一致）或{{异步}}的（快但可能读到旧数据）。
why: 这是读扩展的标准复制拓扑；同步 vs 异步的取舍是面试必问点。
why_en: In leader-follower replication the leader handles writes and followers handle reads, with synchronous replication being consistent but slow and asynchronous being fast but possibly stale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制拓扑：一个主节点(leader)处理写，多个从节点(follower)处理读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In leader-follower replication, one primary handles writes while several followers handle reads.

q: 同步复制 vs 异步复制，核心权衡是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff between synchronous and asynchronous replication?
options: 成本 vs 存储空间
两者没有实质区别
异步复制的一致性更强
同步一致但写延迟高；异步快但副本可能落后
why: 同步 = 等副本确认才算写完，慢但一致；异步 = 主库写完即返回，快但有陈旧窗口。这是复制延迟问题的根源。
why_en: Synchronous replication guarantees consistency at the cost of write latency, while asynchronous replication is faster but replicas can serve stale data.
options_en: Cost versus storage space.
There's no real difference between them.
Asynchronous replication has stronger consistency.
Synchronous stays consistent but writes are slower; asynchronous writes fast but replicas can briefly lag.
tradeoff: 一致性 vs 写入延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入要等待副本确认后才算完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Synchronous replication waits for replica acknowledgment before a write completes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库写完立即返回，副本稍后才追上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Asynchronous replication returns as soon as the primary commits, and replicas catch up afterward.

q: 复制延迟 (replication lag) 最经典的用户可见症状是？
q_en: What is the classic user-visible symptom of replication lag?
options: 写入数据永久丢失
自己刚提交的修改，刷新后看不到
数据库直接崩溃
所有读请求都变慢
why: 写进主库后传播到副本需要时间，期间从落后副本读就是旧值。缓解：read-your-writes——该用户的读走主库或粘住已更新的副本。
why_en: With replication lag a user may not see their own change because the read hit a replica that has not caught up, mitigated with read-your-writes routing.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant P as Primary
    participant R as Lagging Replica
    U->>P: update profile
    P-->>U: OK
    U->>R: refresh page
    R-->>U: old profile
    Note over U,R: read-your-writes routes this user to primary
options_en: Written data is permanently lost.
A user can't see their own just-submitted change after refreshing.
The database crashes outright.
All read requests become slow.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库写入传播到副本需要的时间差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication lag is the delay between a write on the primary and its propagation to replicas.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证用户能立刻看到自己刚提交的写入的一致性策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-writes is a consistency guarantee that a user immediately sees their own just-submitted write.

q: 读副本和分片 (sharding) 在「数据集大小」上的关键区别是？
q_en: How do read replicas and sharding differ on dataset size?
options: 副本复制整份数据，不缩小单机数据集；分片才切开数据
副本会缩小数据集，分片不会
两者都能缩小每台机器的数据集
两者都与数据集大小无关
why: 当数据大到「索引良好的查询也慢」时，副本帮不上忙（每台还是全量数据），要靠分片把数据集切小、同时分摊读负载。
why_en: Replicas copy the full dataset to each server, while sharding splits the data so each database handles a smaller, faster subset.
options_en: Replicas copy full data and don't shrink per-node data; sharding actually splits the data.
Replicas shrink the dataset, sharding doesn't.
Both shrink the per-node dataset.
Neither relates to dataset size.
tradeoff: 数据集大小分摊 vs 读吞吐分摊

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据切分到多个数据库，每个只存一部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple databases so each holds only a portion.

q: 「功能分片 (functional sharding)」是按什么来切分数据的？
q_en: What does functional sharding split data by?
options: 按行的哈希值
按时间范围
按业务域切分：用户库、商品库各自独立
按随机数均匀分配
why: 功能分片按业务域而不是按记录切分：资料请求只查更小的用户库，商品搜索只打商品库。
why_en: Functional sharding splits data by business domain, putting user data in one database and product data in another so each query hits a smaller database.
options_en: By the hash of the row.
By time range.
By business domain: user data in one database, product data in another.
By random uniform distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按业务域切分数据库，比如用户库和商品库分开。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Functional sharding splits databases by business domain, such as separating user data from product data.

scenario: 全球化产品：美国和欧洲用户各自主要访问本地区的数据，跨洲读取延迟高，单库压力也大。
scenario_en: In a global product, US and European users mostly read data from their own regions; cross-continent reads are slow and the single database is overloaded.
q: 最合适的分片方式是？
q_en: Which sharding strategy fits best?
options: 按用户 ID 哈希随机分片
地理分片：数据按区域放本地库，就近读分摊负载
按表大小轮流分片
不分片，只加内存
why: 地理分片对全球读扩展特别有效：就近服务降低延迟，同时没有任何单库承担全部流量。
why_en: Geographic sharding stores each region's data near its users, cutting latency while spreading load across databases.
whenOtherWins: 若访问没有地域局部性（任何用户随机读全球数据），地理分片收益小，哈希分片分布更均匀。
options_en: Hash-shard randomly by user ID.
Geo-shard: keep each region's data in a local database close to its users.
Rotate shards by table size.
Don't shard, just add more memory.
tradeoff: 地理局部性收益 vs 分布不均匀风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 按地理区域切分数据库，让用户读取本地数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geographic sharding splits databases by region so users read from a nearby database.

q: 对「读扩展」而言，分片的正确定位是？
q_en: How should sharding be positioned for read scaling?
options: 分片是读扩展的首选方案
分片没有运维成本
分片和缓存的效果完全等价
分片是写扩展手段、运维复杂；读扩展优先用缓存
why: 分片对读的帮助是「数据集变小 + 负载分摊」，但复杂度高；读扩展优先考虑缓存和副本。
why_en: Sharding is primarily a write-scaling technique with real operational complexity, and for most read problems caching is easier and more effective.
options_en: Sharding is the go-to option for read scaling.
Sharding has no operational cost.
Sharding and caching have identical effects.
Sharding is mainly a write-scaling tool with real ops cost; caching is usually easier for reads.

q: 缓存对读扩展特别有效，利用的是什么访问规律？
q_en: What access pattern makes caching so effective for read scaling?
options: 高度倾斜的访问模式：海量用户反复读同一批热数据
所有 key 被均匀访问
数据从不会被重复读取
写请求远多于读请求
why: 多数应用的访问高度倾斜——你在反复向数据库要一模一样的数据（爆款推文、热门商品），缓存把这些结果放进内存直接回。
why_en: Most applications have highly skewed access patterns where millions read the same rarely-changing data, which caches exploit by serving it from memory.
options_en: A highly skewed access pattern: millions of users repeatedly read the same hot data.
Every key is accessed uniformly.
Data is never read more than once.
Writes far outnumber reads.

q: 缓存命中 vs 优化良好的数据库查询，响应时间量级对比是？
q_en: What is the response-time order of magnitude for a cache hit versus an optimized database query?
options: 都在 100ms 以上
缓存亚毫秒级 vs 数据库几十毫秒
数据库通常更快
两者都在 1 微秒以内
why: 缓存从 RAM 直接返回预计算结果；数据库要读盘 + 执行查询。亚毫秒 vs 几十毫秒是量化「为什么加缓存」的关键数字。
why_en: A cache serves precomputed results from RAM in under a millisecond, versus tens of milliseconds for even a well-optimized database query.
scenario: 设计一个高读流量的资料页，你在决定要不要在数据库前面加一层缓存。
scenario_en: You are designing a high-read profile page and deciding whether to put a cache in front of the database.
options_en: Both are over 100 milliseconds.
Cache hits are sub-millisecond versus tens of milliseconds for the database.
The database is usually faster.
Both are under 1 microsecond.

q: 应用层缓存（Redis / Memcached）的标准读流程是？
q_en: What is the standard read flow for an application cache such as Redis or Memcached?
options: 先查数据库，再顺手更新缓存
读和写都只经过缓存
应用先查缓存，命中直接返回；未命中再查库并回填
缓存后台自动与数据库同步
why: 缓存位于应用和数据库之间：命中 = 亚毫秒返回；未命中 = 查库 + 回填。热门数据自然留在缓存里。
why_en: The application checks the cache first, and on a miss queries the database and populates the cache for future requests.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["App"] --> C{"Cache hit?"}
    C -->|yes| Out["Return value"]
    C -->|no| DB[(Database)]
    DB --> Fill["Set cache"]
    Fill --> Out
options_en: Query the database first, then update the cache as an afterthought.
Both reads and writes only ever touch the cache.
The app checks cache first; on a hit it returns directly, on a miss it queries the database and fills the cache.
The cache automatically syncs with the database in the background.

q: 在带 TTL 的缓存下，热门与冷门数据会自然形成什么分布？
q_en: With TTL-based caching, how do hot and cold items naturally distribute?
options: 热门数据常驻缓存；冷门数据到期自然退出
所有数据永久留在缓存
冷门数据常驻、热门数据被优先淘汰
缓存内容与访问模式无关
why: 这个模式的妙处：受欢迎的数据（如名人主页）自动留在缓存，不常访问的读到才进缓存、TTL 到期自然回落到数据库。
why_en: Popular data naturally stays cached through constant access while rarely-used data expires after its TTL and falls back to the database.
options_en: Popular data stays cached from constant access; cold data expires after its TTL.
All data stays in the cache permanently.
Cold data stays resident while hot data gets evicted first.
Cache contents have nothing to do with access patterns.

q: 补全五种常见的缓存失效策略：
q_en: Fill in the five common cache invalidation strategies.
text: 五种失效策略：基于时间的 {{TTL}} 过期；写库时立即更新/删除缓存的 {{write-through}} 失效；把失效事件排队异步处理的 {{write-behind}} 失效；按 {{标签(tag)}} 批量失效相关条目；把 {{版本号}} 编进缓存 key 的版本化失效。
why: 失效是缓存的头号难题；五种策略在「实现复杂度 vs 陈旧窗口 vs 写延迟」上各有取舍。
why_en: The five invalidation strategies are TTL expiry, write-through, write-behind, tagged invalidation, and versioned keys.

scenario: 缓存的是推荐分数这类不太关键、更新模式可预测的数据；实现要尽量简单，能容忍到期前的陈旧。
scenario_en: The cached value is a non-critical recommendation score with predictable updates; the implementation should be simple and stale values before expiry are acceptable.
q: 选哪种失效策略最合适？
q_en: Which invalidation strategy fits best?
options: 分布式锁串行化更新
写时同步失效 (write-through)
只靠 TTL 定时过期
版本化 key
why: TTL 实现最简单，适合更新模式可预测、能容忍到期前陈旧的次要数据——推荐分数正是典型。
why_en: Plain TTL expiration is the simplest strategy and fits non-critical data with predictable update patterns like recommendation scores.
whenOtherWins: 对用户资料、库存这类关键数据，只靠 TTL 的陈旧窗口太大，必须叠加写时主动失效。
options_en: Serialize updates with a distributed lock.
Synchronous write-through invalidation.
Rely solely on TTL expiration.
Versioned cache keys.
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 陈旧容忍度

q: 同步失效 vs 异步失效，核心区别是？
q_en: What is the core difference between synchronous and asynchronous invalidation?
options: 前者异步、后者同步
同步失效保一致但拖慢写；异步失效写快但有陈旧窗口
两者都不影响写延迟
write-behind 的一致性更强
why: 又是「写延迟 vs 陈旧窗口」的权衡：同步失效保一致但要小心错误处理，异步失效快但有陈旧窗口。
why_en: Synchronous invalidation updates or deletes cache entries during the write path for consistency at the cost of write latency, while asynchronous invalidation queues events and briefly risks stale reads.

rows: 写时立即更新/删除缓存
更大，直到 worker 处理

options_en: The former is asynchronous, the latter synchronous.
Synchronous invalidation updates or deletes cache during the write for consistency but slows writes; asynchronous invalidation queues the event, writing fast but risking a stale window.
Neither affects write latency.
Write-behind has stronger consistency.
tradeoff: 写延迟 vs 陈旧窗口

scenario: 缓存里有大量与「用户 123 的帖子」相关的条目（列表页、详情页、聚合页），一次帖子改动要让它们全部失效。
scenario_en: The cache has many entries related to user 123's posts, including list pages, detail pages, and aggregate pages; one post update must invalidate all of them.
q: 最合适的失效策略是？
q_en: Which invalidation strategy fits best?
options: 标签失效：按标签一键失效所有关联条目
逐个记住所有 key 再一一删除
把这些条目的 TTL 都设成 1 秒
干脆不缓存这些数据
why: 标签失效专治「一份数据牵连多个缓存条目」的复杂依赖（如给相关条目挂 user:123:posts 标签），代价是要维护标签与条目的关系。
why_en: Tagged invalidation associates entries with tags so one change can invalidate every related entry, at the cost of maintaining tag relationships.
whenOtherWins: 若只是单实体缓存（一条记录一个 key），版本化 key 更简单，不用维护标签关系。
options_en: Tagged invalidation: tag related entries and invalidate them all at once by tag.
Remember every key individually and delete them one by one.
Set all these entries' TTL to one second.
Just stop caching this data.

q: 「版本化 key (versioned keys)」失效策略的机制是？
q_en: How do versioned cache keys work?
options: 定期全量清空缓存
给每个 key 加分布式锁
把同一数据写两份互为备份
版本号编进 key；更新递增，旧 key 失效
why: 版本化不删除旧缓存，而是换 key 让旧条目变得不可达——简单可靠，但需要跟踪版本号。
why_en: Versioned keys include a version number in the cache key and increment it on update, so old entries become unreachable instead of being deleted.
options_en: Periodically flush the entire cache.
Add a distributed lock to every key.
Write the same data twice as a backup.
Bake a version number into the cache key; bumping it on update leaves the old key unreachable.

scenario: 生产系统要定失效方案：既有用户资料、库存这类关键数据，也有推荐分数这类次要数据。
scenario_en: You need a production invalidation plan for both critical data like profiles and inventory and secondary data like recommendation scores.
q: 工程上最常见的组合是？
q_en: What combination is most common in production?
options: 全部只靠长 TTL
全部用写时失效、不设任何 TTL
短 TTL 兜底，关键数据主动失效
所有数据都不缓存
why: 多数生产系统组合使用：TTL 兜底保证最终会刷新，主动失效保证关键数据及时更新。
why_en: Production systems combine short TTLs of five to fifteen minutes as a safety net with active invalidation for critical data.
whenOtherWins: 若全部数据的陈旧容忍都宽松且一致，只靠 TTL 是最简单的方案。
options_en: Use only long TTLs everywhere.
Use write-time invalidation everywhere with no TTL at all.
Short TTL as a safety net, with active invalidation layered on top for critical data.
Don't cache any data at all.
tradeoff: 简单统一 vs 按数据分层保护

scenario: 需求文档写明：搜索结果的陈旧不得超过 30 秒，用户资料可容忍 5 分钟陈旧。
scenario_en: The requirements say search results may be stale for at most 30 seconds, while user profiles may be stale for 5 minutes.
q: 缓存 TTL 应该怎么定？
q_en: How should you choose cache TTLs?
options: 由陈旧性需求驱动：搜索 30 秒、资料 5 分钟
统一设 1 小时省事
全部设 1 秒，越短越好
随便设一个值，出问题再调
why: 理想的 TTL 由非功能需求的 staleness 上限直接给出：这让一致性保证有界，缓存决策不用拍脑袋。
why_en: Drive TTLs from your staleness requirements, so a thirty-second staleness budget means exactly a thirty-second TTL.
whenOtherWins: 若需求是「写后立即可见」，多短的 TTL 都不够，要改用主动失效或版本化 key。
options_en: Drive it directly from staleness requirements: 30 seconds for search, 5 minutes for profiles.
Set one hour everywhere for simplicity.
Set one second everywhere — shorter is always better.
Pick an arbitrary value and adjust later if it breaks.
tradeoff: 一致性保证 vs 缓存收益

q: 关于现代 CDN 的能力，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about modern CDNs is correct?
options: 只能缓存静态文件，不支持任何动态数据
必须自建全球边缘机房才能用
缓存内容不能设置过期时间
除静态资源外，也能缓存动态内容
why: CDN 起家于静态资源，但现代 CDN 也缓存动态内容，把缓存从你的机房延伸到全球边缘节点。
why_en: Modern CDNs cache dynamic content such as API responses and query results, not just static assets.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    U["User"] --> E["Nearest CDN edge"]
    E -->|hit| U
    E -->|miss| O["Origin / API"]
    O --> E
options_en: It can only cache static files and never handles dynamic data.
It requires building your own global edge data centers.
Cached content can never have an expiration set.
Beyond static assets, modern CDNs also cache dynamic content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers located near users.

q: 东京用户访问弗吉尼亚源站 vs 就近的东京边缘节点，延迟量级变化是？
q_en: What latency change do you expect from a Virginia origin to a Tokyo edge node?
options: 约 200ms 降到 10ms 以内
没有变化
从 1 秒降到 500ms
从 10ms 升到 200ms
why: 地理分布是 CDN 的核心价值：跨洲往返约 200ms，就近边缘 10ms 以内，且命中的请求完全不打源站。
why_en: Edge caching cuts response times from around two hundred milliseconds cross-continent to under ten milliseconds locally.
scenario: 服务部署在美国弗吉尼亚，东京用户抱怨页面慢，你在评估是否要上 CDN 边缘节点。
scenario_en: The service is hosted in Virginia and Tokyo users complain about slow pages; you are evaluating CDN edge nodes.
options_en: From about 200 milliseconds down to under 10 milliseconds.
No change at all.
From 1 second down to 500 milliseconds.
From 10 milliseconds up to 200 milliseconds.

q: 读密集应用配好 CDN 缓存后，源站负载大致能降多少？
q_en: Roughly how much can a well-configured CDN reduce origin load in a read-heavy app?
options: 90% 或更多
基本不变
正好一半
why: 商品页、公开资料、搜索结果这类多人共读的内容都能边缘化，命中的请求完全不到源站，降 90%+ 很常见。
why_en: For read-heavy applications CDN caching can offload ninety percent or more of origin traffic.
scenario: 读密集应用给公开内容加上 CDN 边缘缓存后，你要向团队量化能省下多少源站压力。
scenario_en: After adding CDN edge caching for public content in a read-heavy app, you need to quantify the origin-load reduction.
options_en: About 10%.
90% or more.
Essentially unchanged.
Exactly half.

scenario: 决定哪些内容进 CDN：候选有公开帖子、商品目录、搜索结果、用户私信、个人偏好设置。
scenario_en: You are deciding what should go into the CDN: public posts, product catalogs, search results, private messages, and personal settings.
q: 正确的取舍是？
q_en: What is the right CDN caching tradeoff?
options: 全部进 CDN，越多越好
只缓存私信，因为它最敏感
全都不进 CDN
公开内容进 CDN，私有数据不进
why: CDN 只对「多用户共读」的内容有意义；私信、个人设置这类单用户数据只有本人访问，放 CDN 没有命中率收益。
why_en: CDNs only make sense for content many users share, so cache public posts and catalogs but never user-specific data that only one person requests.
whenOtherWins: 单用户数据要提速应放应用层缓存或客户端缓存，而不是共享型的 CDN。
options_en: Put everything in the CDN, the more the better.
Only cache private messages since they're the most sensitive.
Don't use a CDN for anything.
Cache public posts, catalogs, and search results; skip single-user data like DMs and settings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠近用户的 CDN 节点，命中时直接返回内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge server is a CDN node near users that returns cached content directly.

scenario: 面试进入扩展性讨论环节，你的系统是读密集型。
scenario_en: The interview has moved into scalability, and your system is read-heavy.
q: 最加分的切入方式是？
q_en: What is the strongest way to start the scalability discussion?
options: 直接宣布「加 Redis 和 CDN」
主动指出读瓶颈，按查询优化到缓存副本展开
等面试官点名再讨论
先谈微服务拆分
why: 强候选人主动识别读瓶颈：画 API 时就在会被打爆的端点停下来量化问题（如「资料页每天数十亿读」），然后按查询优化 → 缓存/副本的顺序展开。
why_en: Strong candidates proactively flag high-volume endpoints, quantify the read load, and then work through query optimization before caching and replicas.
whenOtherWins: 若系统是写密集（如 Uber 位置上报），应先谈写扩展而不是读扩展。
options_en: Just announce 'add Redis and a CDN'.
Proactively call out read bottlenecks at high-traffic endpoints, then work through query optimization before caching and replicas.
Wait for the interviewer to bring it up.
Start by talking about microservice decomposition.

scenario: 设计 Bitly：一条短链创建一次却可能被点击数百万次，长短链映射一旦生成从不改变。
scenario_en: Designing Bitly: a short link is created once, may be clicked millions of times, and the long-to-short mapping never changes.
q: 缓存策略应该是？
q_en: What caching strategy fits Bitly?
options: 短 TTL 频繁刷新
不缓存，防止陈旧
Redis 激进缓存不过期，配 CDN 扛流量
只缓存热门链接 1 分钟
why: 极端读写比 + 不可变数据 = 缓存梦想场景：不设过期也不会陈旧，命中率极高。
why_en: Bitly is a caching dream because the mapping never changes, so cache it aggressively with no expiration and let the CDN absorb global traffic.
whenOtherWins: 只要数据可能变（比如允许修改目标地址），「永不过期」就不成立，必须引入失效机制。
options_en: Refresh with a short TTL frequently.
Don't cache at all, to avoid staleness.
Cache the mapping aggressively in Redis with no expiration, backed by a CDN for global traffic.
Only cache popular links for one minute.
tradeoff: 激进缓存命中率 vs 数据不可变前提

scenario: 设计 Ticketmaster：开票瞬间几千人狂刷同一活动页；页面包含活动详情、场馆信息、座位图，也包含实时座位余量。
scenario_en: Designing Ticketmaster: at sale time thousands of users refresh the same event page; it includes event details, venue info, seat maps, and live seat availability.
q: 正确的缓存边界是？
q_en: Where should the caching boundary be?
options: 稳定内容激进缓存，余量近似，购买查权威库存
整页全部缓存 10 分钟
全部不缓存，保证绝对正确
把座位余量也缓存 60 秒
why: 关键是划清「可缓存内容」和「必须强一致的库存路径」：活动详情、场馆、座位图可激进缓存，余量只做短 TTL 近似展示。购买路径必须查权威库存，用锁或事务原子预留。
why_en: Cache stable event details aggressively; seat availability can be approximate for display, but checkout must read authoritative inventory and reserve atomically.
whenOtherWins: 若展示允许近似余量（如「少量余票」标签），可短缓存近似值，但下单扣减路径必须强一致。
options_en: Cache stable content like event and venue details aggressively; keep seat counts approximate with a short TTL, and require checkout to read authoritative inventory with an atomic reservation.
Cache the entire page for 10 minutes.
Cache nothing at all to guarantee correctness.
Cache seat availability too, for 60 seconds.
tradeoff: 缓存吞吐 vs 库存强一致性

scenario: 设计 Facebook 信息流：读极其密集，用户通常只看头几条。
scenario_en: Designing a Facebook feed: reads are extremely heavy, and users usually only look at the first few items.
q: 读扩展的关键手法是？
q_en: What is the key read-scaling technique?
options: 每次请求全量现算 feed
把整个 feed 一次性发给客户端
不缓存任何帖子以保证新鲜
预计算 feed，缓存近期帖子，用分页避免全量加载
why: 关键洞察：用户通常只读头几条，所以激进缓存近期内容回报巨大；预计算 + 分页避免每次现算和全量传输，把资源砸在头部内容上。
why_en: Pre-compute feeds for active users, cache recent posts, and paginate, because users typically only read the first few items.
whenOtherWins: 规模小或 feed 要求绝对实时时，请求时现算更简单，预计算反而是浪费。
options_en: Recompute the whole feed from scratch on every request.
Send the entire feed to the client in one shot.
Cache no posts at all to guarantee freshness.
Precompute feeds for active users, cache recent posts, and paginate instead of loading everything at once.
tradeoff: 预计算与缓存成本 vs 实时全量计算

scenario: 设计 YouTube：每次打开首页都要查推荐视频、频道信息、播放量；标题/描述/缩略图很少变化。
scenario_en: Designing YouTube: each home-page load needs recommended videos, channel info, and view counts; titles, descriptions, and thumbnails rarely change.
q: 合理的读扩展组合是？
q_en: What is a reasonable read-scaling mix?
options: 播放量必须每次播放都实时精确更新
激进缓存元数据；播放量最终一致；缩略图走 CDN
元数据不缓存，缩略图放数据库
全站强一致，禁止任何缓存
why: 元数据很少变 → 激进缓存；播放量不需要精确实时 → 最终一致批量更新；缩略图是静态媒体 → CDN。按数据特性分层处理。
why_en: Cache video metadata aggressively, let view counts be eventually consistent with periodic updates, and serve thumbnails from a CDN.
whenOtherWins: 若计数用于计费等要求精确的场景，就不能用最终一致的缓存计数。
options_en: View counts must update in real time on every single play.
Cache metadata aggressively; let view counts be eventually consistent; serve thumbnails via CDN.
Don't cache metadata, store thumbnails in the database.
Enforce strong consistency site-wide and forbid all caching.
tradeoff: 缓存新鲜度分层 vs 全站强一致

q: 哪些场景「不该」把读扩展当作主攻方向？（多选）
q_en: Which scenarios should not make read scaling the main focus? Select all that apply.
options: Uber 司机位置追踪：每几秒上报一次位置，读写比只有 2:1 甚至 1:1
面试官限定「为 1000 个用户设计」的小规模系统
Google Docs 这类实时协作系统：每次击键都要立即对他人可见
Bitly 短链接跳转服务
why: 写密集系统先做写扩展；小规模一个索引良好的单库就能扛几千 QPS；实时协作要的是实时更新，缓存反而有害。Bitly 恰恰是读扩展的梦想场景。
why_en: Skip read scaling for write-heavy systems, small-scale designs a single indexed database can handle, and real-time collaboration where caching actively hurts.
options_en: Uber driver location tracking: pings every few seconds, read-write ratio only 2:1 or even 1:1.
An interviewer-specified small system for 1000 users.
Google Docs-style real-time collaboration where every keystroke must be visible immediately.
Bitly-style URL shortener redirects.
tradeoff: 写扩展优先 vs 读扩展优先

q: 「读扩展」的真正目标是什么？
q_en: What is the real goal of read scaling?
options: 让所有请求都更快
彻底消灭数据库
减少数据库读负载；低延迟是另一类问题
提高写入吞吐
why: 读扩展解决的是「数据库被读垮」；「延迟不够低」是另一个问题、另一套解法，别混为一谈。
why_en: Read scaling is about reducing database load, and pure latency problems call for different solutions like edge computing.
options_en: Make every request faster.
Eliminate the database entirely.
Reduce the read load the database carries; pure latency problems are a different kind of issue.
Increase write throughput.

q: 1000 万用户后「按 email 登录」的查询拖到 30 秒、DB CPU 100%，最可能的原因是？
q_en: At 10 million users, email login takes 30 seconds and DB CPU is 100%; what is the likely cause?
options: 网络故障
缺索引导致每次登录都全表扫描千万行数据
内存条损坏
SQL 语法写错了
why: 无索引 = 每个查询全表扫盘；join 会再乘一层（先扫 users 再扫 orders，数十亿次行比较）。解法很直接：给频繁查询的列加索引。
why_en: Without an index every login scans all ten million rows, about two gigabytes of data per lookup, multiplied by concurrent logins.
options_en: A network outage.
Missing an index forces a full table scan on every login across all ten million rows.
Faulty RAM.
A SQL syntax error.

scenario: users 表 1000 万行，按 email 查询走的是全表扫描 (Seq Scan)，登录高峰时数据库 CPU 打满。
scenario_en: The users table has 10 million rows; email lookups are doing a full table scan, and login spikes max out database CPU.
q: 正确的修复是？
q_en: What is the right fix?
options: CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);
VACUUM FULL users;
SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 1;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email_backup TEXT;
why: 在 email 列上建索引，把千万行扫描变成几次索引查找；EXPLAIN 里 Seq Scan 变成 Index Scan、成本骤降就是证据。
why_en: Creating an index on the email column turns the full table scan into a few index lookups, visible in EXPLAIN as the plan switches to an index scan.
whenOtherWins: 若查询是 status + created_at 的组合过滤，需要对应的复合索引，单列 email 索引帮不上。
options_en: Create an index on the email column.
Run a full vacuum on the users table.
Select one row with a limit clause.
Add a new email_backup text column.
tradeoff: 查询延迟 vs 索引维护成本

q: 复合索引 (status, created_at) 能加速哪些查询？
q_en: Which queries can a compound index on status and created_at speed up?
options: 只加速单独按 created_at 过滤或排序的查询，跟 status 无关，因为它不在索引最左侧
只要用到 status 或 created_at 任意一列的查询都能被这个复合索引加速
只加速直接用 id 主键做等值匹配的点查，其它列都用不上
能加速 status 及联合 status+created_at 过滤，仅 created_at 不行
why: 复合索引按列顺序（最左前缀）生效：先按 status 排、再按 created_at 排，所以跳过 status 就用不上。列顺序很重要。
why_en: Column order matters in a compound index: an index on status and created_at helps status filters and combined filters, but not created_at alone.
options_en: It only speeds up queries filtering or sorting by created_at alone, unrelated to status, since it's not the leftmost column.
Any query touching status or created_at, in any combination, gets accelerated by this compound index.
It only speeds up point lookups on the id primary key, not other columns.
It speeds up status filters and combined status-plus-created_at filters; created_at alone gets no benefit.

q: 名人发帖后，单个缓存 key 从 5 万 QPS 冲到 50 万 QPS 并开始超时——这是什么问题？
q_en: A celebrity post pushes one cache key from 50k to 500k QPS and timeouts; what problem is this?
options: 热 key 打满单个缓存节点
缓存穿透
复制延迟
磁盘 I/O 瓶颈
why: 数据在内存不代表无限吞吐：把同一份数据序列化并通过网络发送 50 万次/秒，单台服务器就是扛不住。
why_en: This is the hot-key problem: one key gets all the traffic and overwhelms a single cache server's CPU and network even though the data is in memory.
options_en: The hot-key problem: one key's flood overwhelms a single node.
Cache penetration.
Replication lag.
A disk I/O bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问、可能压垮单个节点的缓存 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a cache key receiving unusually high traffic that can overwhelm a single node.

q: 请求合并 (request coalescing) 能把「百万用户同时要同一个 key」的后端压力降到多少？
q_en: How far can request coalescing reduce backend load when a million users ask for the same key?
options: 降到零请求，完全不查后端
恰好 N 个请求，N 是服务器数
降到大约一半
不变，仍是百万级
why: 合并把「无上限的相同请求」压缩成「每台应用服务器一个」：百万用户等同一个结果，后端只看到 N 次查询。
why_en: Request coalescing reduces backend load from potentially unlimited to exactly one request per application server doing the coalescing.
diagram:
flowchart LR U1["用户 x 100 万"] --> A1["应用服务器 1
合并为 1 个在途请求"] U1 --> A2["应用服务器 2
合并为 1 个在途请求"] A1 --> B[(后端 / 缓存)] A2 --> B B -.->|共 N 个请求| B
options_en: It drops to zero requests, never touching the backend.
Exactly N requests, where N is the number of servers.
It drops to roughly half.
It stays unchanged at the million level.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一 key 的多个并发请求合并成一次后端调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Request coalescing merges multiple concurrent requests for the same key into a single backend call.

q: 这段请求合并代码里，inflight 字典的作用是？
q_en: What role does the inflight map play in this request-coalescing code?
options: 缓存最终结果，供之后所有请求长期使用
限制全局并发数
记录哪个 key 在途，后来者共享 Future
统计每个 key 的 QPS
why: inflight 是 key → Future 的映射：第一个请求负责真正取数，后续同 key 请求共享那个 Future 的结果，取完即删。
why_en: The inflight map tracks keys already being fetched so concurrent requests await the same future instead of issuing duplicate backend calls.
codeSample:
class CoalescingCache:
    def __init__(self):
        self.inflight = {}  # key -> Future

    async def get(self, key):
        if key in self.inflight:          # 已有请求在取
            return await self.inflight[key]
        future = asyncio.Future()
        self.inflight[key] = future
        try:
            value = await fetch_from_backend(key)
            future.set_result(value)
            return value
        finally:
            del self.inflight[key]
scenario: 你在实现请求合并 (request coalescing) 来抵御热点 key 的并发洪峰，下面是核心 Python 代码。
scenario_en: You are implementing request coalescing to handle a concurrent flood on a hot key; this is the core Python code.
options_en: Cache the final result for all future requests long-term.
Limit the global concurrency count.
Track which keys already have a request in flight so later callers await the same future.
Count QPS per key.

scenario: 已做请求合并，但单 key 仍有 50 万 QPS 持续流量，超出单台缓存节点约 5 万 QPS 的能力。
scenario_en: Request coalescing is already in place, but one key still has sustained 500k QPS, above a single cache node's roughly 50k QPS capacity.
q: 下一步该怎么办？
q_en: What should you do next?
options: 把 TTL 加长
换一台更贵的缓存机器
关闭缓存直连数据库
缓存 key 扇出：复制多份分摊到多节点
why: 合并解决「重复请求」，扇出解决「单 key 持续洪峰」：把一个热 key 拆成多份副本分摊到多台节点。
why_en: Cache key fanout stores identical copies under multiple keys so clients randomly pick one, spreading the hot key's load across servers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Clients"] --> Pick["random shard key"]
    Pick --> K1["feed:taylor:1"]
    Pick --> K2["feed:taylor:2"]
    Pick --> K10["feed:taylor:10"]
    K1 --> N1["Cache node A"]
    K2 --> N2["Cache node B"]
    K10 --> N3["Cache node C"]
whenOtherWins: 若洪峰只出现在过期重建的瞬间而非持续流量，请求合并或提前刷新就够了，不必付扇出的内存与失效成本。
options_en: Extend the TTL.
Move to a more expensive cache machine.
Turn off the cache and hit the database directly.
Cache key fanout: store copies under several keys and let clients randomly pick one to spread the load.
tradeoff: 多副本分摊负载 vs 内存与失效成本

termDefinitions.term: 缓存 key 扇出 / cache key fanout
termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一数据复制到多个 key 上分散热点流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache key fanout duplicates data under multiple keys to spread hot-key traffic.

q: 缓存 key 扇出（一份数据存十个 key）的代价是什么？
q_en: What is the cost of cache key fanout?
options: 读延迟大幅上升
命中率必然下降
内存占用成倍增加，失效要清掉所有副本
写入会被阻塞
why: 扇出用冗余换可用性：多份拷贝多占内存、失效要全清；但在热 key 威胁可用性时，这点冗余是保命的小代价。
why_en: Fanout costs extra memory for duplicate copies and makes invalidation harder since every copy must be cleared, a small price for staying online.
options_en: Read latency rises sharply.
Hit rate is bound to drop.
Memory usage multiplies since data is duplicated, and invalidation must clear every copy.
Writes get blocked.

q: 缓存击穿/惊群 (cache stampede) 的根本触发机制是？
q_en: What triggers a cache stampede?
options: 过期是二元的：一瞬间全部涌向数据库
数据库本身太慢
TTL 设置得太长
缓存容量不足
why: 越热门的条目雪崩越大、重建越贵（10 表 join、外部 API）伤害越大——等于自己对自己发起 DDOS，10 万并发同一瞬间涌向数据库。
why_en: Cache expiration is binary, so the instant a hot entry expires every concurrent request misses at once and floods the database like a self-inflicted DDoS.
options_en: Cache expiry is binary — one moment it's there, the next it's gone, so every concurrent request misses at once.
The database itself is too slow.
The TTL was set too long.
The cache doesn't have enough capacity.

termDefinitions.term: 缓存击穿 / 惊群 / cache stampede
termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存过期瞬间大量并发请求同时未命中、一起打向数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede happens when many concurrent requests miss at the exact instant a cache entry expires.

q: 用分布式锁防击穿（只许第一个请求重建，其他人等待）的主要缺点是？
q_en: What is the main downside of using a distributed lock to stop a stampede?
options: 数据库负载完全不降
缓存永远无法更新
锁本身占用太多内存
若重建失败或太慢，成千上万等待者一起超时
why: 锁保护了后端，但把风险转嫁给等待者：重建一慢，全体请求挂起超时，需要复杂的超时与兜底逻辑，高负载下很脆弱。
why_en: With a distributed lock a slow or failed rebuild leaves thousands of waiting requests to time out, making the approach fragile under load.
options_en: Database load doesn't drop at all.
The cache can never be updated again.
The lock itself uses too much memory.
If the rebuild fails or is slow, thousands of waiters time out together, requiring fragile fallback logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨进程/服务器协调的锁，只让一个请求执行重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across processes so only one request performs the rebuild.

scenario: 首页缓存 10 万 QPS、1 小时 TTL；你想避免到点集体未命中，又不想引入锁的脆弱性。
scenario_en: A homepage cache gets 100k QPS with a one-hour TTL; you want to avoid a synchronized miss without the fragility of locks.
q: 更聪明的做法是？
q_en: What is the smarter approach?
options: 把 TTL 缩短到 10 分钟
概率化提前刷新：越接近过期触发概率越高，重建摊开
过期后让所有请求直接打数据库
每次读都强制刷新一遍
why: 概率化提前刷新把「同一瞬间的 10 万次重建」摊成「十几分钟里的零星刷新」，多数用户仍拿缓存、少数触发后台刷新。
why_en: Probabilistic early refresh gives each request a growing chance to refresh the entry as expiry nears, spreading rebuilds over minutes instead of one instant.
whenOtherWins: 对绝不容许击穿的最关键数据，用后台定时刷新彻底不让用户触发重建。
options_en: Shorten the TTL to 10 minutes.
Probabilistic early refresh: the closer an entry is to expiry, the higher the chance each request triggers a background refresh.
Let every request hit the database directly after expiry.
Force a refresh on every single read.
tradeoff: 确定性防击穿 vs 分散刷新概率

termDefinitions.term: 概率化提前刷新 / probabilistic early refresh
termDefinitions.meaning: 越接近过期，请求触发后台刷新的概率越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Probabilistic early refresh gives requests a growing chance to trigger a background refresh as an entry nears expiry.

scenario: 最关键的首页缓存：不能冒任何击穿风险，也不接受概率化方案的不确定性。
scenario_en: This is the most critical homepage cache: no stampede risk is acceptable, and probabilistic behavior is not acceptable.
q: 该用什么方案？
q_en: Which approach should you use?
options: 后台持续提前刷新，用户永不触发重建
把 TTL 设得更长
分布式锁
放弃缓存这个条目
why: 后台持续刷新是最强保险：用户请求永远命中新鲜缓存。代价是基础设施复杂度和「刷新了没人读的数据」的浪费，只留给最关键内容。
why_en: A background process continuously refreshes critical entries before expiry so users never trigger rebuilds, at the cost of extra infrastructure and wasted refreshes.
whenOtherWins: 普通热度的数据用概率化提前刷新就够了，专职后台刷新的成本不值得。
options_en: A background process keeps refreshing entries before they expire, so users never trigger a rebuild.
Just set a longer TTL.
Use a distributed lock.
Stop caching this entry.

q: 「写完数据库就删缓存」这种朴素失效方式有哪些真实问题？（多选）
q_en: What real problems does naive delete-cache-after-write create? Select all that apply.
options: 该删哪些缓存说不清：应用缓存、CDN、浏览器缓存都可能存着旧值
失效请求本身可能失败
删除之后、新值写入之前，另一个请求可能读到旧数据并把它重新缓存回去（竞态条件）
删除操作会锁住整张表
why: 多层缓存、失效失败、删后重缓存竞态——这三个坑让「直接删」在需要立即可见的场景不可靠，于是才有版本化方案。
why_en: Naive delete-on-write fails because caches live in many layers, invalidations can fail, and a racing read can re-cache stale data right after the delete.
options_en: It's unclear which caches to clear — app cache, CDN, and browser cache may all hold stale values.
The invalidation request itself can fail.
Between the delete and the new write, another request can re-cache the stale value — a race condition.
The delete operation locks the entire table.

q: 缓存版本化 (cache versioning) 的读写流程是？
q_en: What is the read/write flow for cache versioning?
options: 每次读都直接查数据库
写时向所有缓存层广播失效消息
版本号存在缓存里、由缓存自增
版本号存数据库，随更新递增；读时用版本拼 key
why: 核心是「不删除、改路由」：旧缓存条目从不被删，只是版本一变就没人再读它；CDN 和浏览器缓存也随 key/URL 变化自然过期。
why_en: Each record's version lives in the database and increments in the same transaction, so reads build a versioned cache key and old entries simply become unreachable.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["读请求"] --> V["取版本号
(版本 key 或 DB)"] V --> K["拼 key: event:123:v42"] K --> C{"缓存命中?"} C -->|是| Out["返回"] C -->|否| DB[(数据库)] --> F["回填 v42"] --> Out
options_en: Every read hits the database directly.
Writes broadcast invalidation messages to every cache layer.
The version number lives in the cache and increments itself.
The version lives in the database and increments in the same transaction; reads build the cache key from that version.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把版本号编进缓存 key，更新后旧 key 自然不可达。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Versioned keys embed a version number in the cache key so old keys become unreachable after an update.

q: 为什么版本化能整类地绕开失效竞态？
q_en: Why does versioning avoid a whole class of invalidation races?
options: 因为它给每次读加了全局锁
因为版本递增是原子的，旧缓存被绕开而非删除
因为缓存从此永不过期
因为它禁止了并发写入
why: 没有删除就没有「删了又被写回旧值」的竞态；版本变化原子发生，读者自动切到新 key，无需广播失效。
why_en: Version changes are atomic in the database so keys never collide and readers move to the new key automatically, eliminating the whole class of invalidation races.
options_en: Because it adds a global lock to every read.
Because version increments are atomic in the database, so old cache entries are bypassed rather than deleted.
Because the cache never expires anymore.
Because it forbids concurrent writes.

q: 缓存版本化的代价包括？
q_en: What costs come with cache versioning?
options: 多一次查找、旧版本堆积，只适合单实体缓存
读性能下降十倍
数据库写吞吐减半
版本号溢出会导致系统故障
why: 版本化的三笔账：多一跳查版本、旧条目靠 TTL 清、只覆盖单实体缓存——计算型数据的失效要另想办法（如删除项缓存）。
why_en: Versioning costs an extra lookup per read, lets old versions accumulate until TTLs clean them, and only really fits single-entity caches.
options_en: Every read needs two cache lookups, old versions accumulate, and it only fits single-entity caches.
Read performance drops tenfold.
Database write throughput is cut in half.
Version-number overflow crashes the system.

scenario: 内容审核场景：帖子被删除后必须立刻从所有已缓存的 feed 中消失，但逐一失效所有包含它的 feed 缓存太贵。
scenario_en: In a content-moderation flow, deleted posts must disappear from all cached feeds immediately, but invalidating every feed containing the post is too expensive.
q: 高效的折中方案是？
q_en: What is the efficient compromise?
options: 清空全部 feed 缓存
把 feed 缓存 TTL 降到 1 秒
停止缓存所有 feed
维护小的「已删除条目缓存」，出 feed 时过滤
why: 小而快的删除项缓存让你立即遮蔽被删内容、继续服务「大体正确」的缓存数据，复杂结构的真正失效异步完成。
why_en: A small deleted-items cache filters recently removed IDs at serve time so cached feeds stay usable while the expensive invalidation happens in the background.
whenOtherWins: 单实体数据（用户资料、活动详情）用版本化 key 更干净；删除项缓存专攻计算型/聚合缓存的快速遮蔽。
options_en: Wipe the entire feed cache.
Drop the feed cache TTL to one second.
Stop caching feeds altogether.
Keep a small deleted-items cache of recently removed post IDs and filter them out when serving feeds.
tradeoff: 即时遮蔽 vs 后台彻底失效

termDefinitions.term: 已删除条目缓存 / deleted items cache
termDefinitions.meaning: 一份记录近期被删除或隐藏内容 ID 的小缓存，用于过滤。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deleted-items cache is a small cache of recently removed or hidden IDs used to filter results.

q: 全球 CDN 场景下的缓存失效有什么额外难点与对策？
q_en: What extra challenge does cache invalidation have with a global CDN, and what is the response?
options: CDN 失效瞬间全球生效，无需特殊处理
要清数百个边缘节点，传播有延迟；关键更新可跳过 CDN
CDN 不支持任何形式的失效
只能等所有边缘节点的 TTL 自然过期
why: CDN 失效是「清几百个边缘」而非一个缓存，传播要时间；所以关键数据宁可不进 CDN，次要数据靠边缘短 TTL + 应用层长 TTL 分层。
why_en: Invalidating a CDN means clearing hundreds of edge locations with propagation delay, so critical updates may bypass CDN caching entirely via cache headers.
options_en: CDN invalidation takes effect globally in an instant with no special handling.
You must clear hundreds of edge nodes with propagation delay; critical updates can bypass the CDN via cache headers.
CDNs don't support any form of invalidation.
You can only wait for every edge node's TTL to expire naturally.

q: 把「场馆地址更新必须立即可见」的缓存决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the cache decision chain for venue address updates that must be visible immediately in order.
steps: 缓解：给旧版本条目设 TTL 兜底清理，接受每次读多一跳
需求：更新后立刻可见，而数据缓存在 Redis / CDN / 浏览器多层，直接删缓存有竞态
代价：每次读要先取版本号再取数据，旧版本条目会堆积
选型：缓存版本化——版本号入库、同事务递增、key 携带版本
why: 需求（立即可见 + 多层缓存）→ 选型（版本化 key）→ 代价（双查找、旧条目堆积）→ 缓解（TTL 清理）。决策链四段式。
why_en: The chain runs requirement, choice, cost, mitigation: immediate visibility across cache layers leads to versioned keys, whose double lookup and accumulation are bounded by TTL cleanup.

q: 补全 Bitly 缓存策略的推理：
q_en: Complete the reasoning for Bitly's cache strategy.
text: Bitly 是缓存的梦想场景：长短链映射{{不可变}}（创建后从不改变）、读写比{{极端悬殊}}（建一次、读百万次），所以可以激进缓存甚至{{不设过期}}，数据库只接冷门链接的未命中。
why: 「不可变 + 读爆炸」意味着缓存零陈旧风险、命中率极高——这是判断「能多激进地缓存」的标尺。
why_en: Because the mapping is immutable and read millions of times per write, Bitly can cache aggressively with no expiration at all.

scenario: 同一个系统里：用户资料可容忍 5 分钟陈旧，活动场馆地址更新必须立即可见。
scenario_en: In one system, user profiles may be stale for 5 minutes, while event venue address updates must be visible immediately.
q: 正确的整体缓存设计原则是？
q_en: What is the right overall caching design principle?
options: 全站统一 5 分钟 TTL 省事
全站都用最强的失效方案以防万一
按数据设计：不同数据一致性需求不同，别一刀切
干脆都不缓存
why: 缓存策略应围绕各类数据的一致性需求分层设计；一刀切要么太贵、要么太陈旧。
why_en: Design caching around each data type's consistency needs instead of applying one approach everywhere.
whenOtherWins: 若系统里所有数据的陈旧容忍确实一致，统一策略当然更简单。
options_en: Use one uniform 5-minute TTL everywhere for simplicity.
Apply the strongest invalidation strategy everywhere just in case.
Design per data type: different data has different consistency needs, so don't apply one approach everywhere.
Just don't cache anything.
tradeoff: 统一简单 vs 按需分层保护

q: 写入吞吐撞到单机极限时，最典型的三个硬件瓶颈是？
q_en: When write throughput hits a single machine's ceiling, what are the three classic hardware bottlenecks?
options: 内存容量、GPU、显存
磁盘 I/O、CPU、网络带宽
DNS、TLS 握手、负载均衡器
线程数、文件句柄、连接池
options_en: Memory capacity, GPU, and video RAM
Disk I/O, CPU, and network bandwidth
DNS, the TLS handshake, and the load balancer
Thread count, file handles, and the connection pool
why: 写入受限于磁盘 I/O、CPU 和网络带宽三堵墙；面试里谈扩展写入前，先确认到底撞的是哪一堵。
why_en: Writes are bottlenecked by disk I/O, CPU, and network bandwidth, so confirm which wall you're actually hitting before proposing any redesign.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理器，执行计算指令；写入路径上的序列化、校验、事务处理都要占用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, runs computation, and write-path work like serialization and transaction handling consumes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据落盘的读写操作，机械寻道或 SSD 写放大都会拖慢它，是写入最常见的瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Disk I/O is the read/write traffic to storage, and mechanical seeks or SSD write amplification make it the most common write bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器，擅长并行计算，不是典型数据库写入路径的瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU, or Graphics Processing Unit, is built for parallel compute and is not a typical bottleneck on a database write path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 建立加密连接时的一次性协商，不会随每次写入重复发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The TLS handshake is the one-time negotiation that sets up an encrypted connection, not something repeated on every write.

q: 在「扩展难度」这个维度上，为什么写扩展通常比读扩展更棘手？
q_en: On the axis of "how hard is it to scale", why is scaling writes usually harder than scaling reads?
scenario: 面试官已经问完读扩展（副本、缓存），现在追问「写呢」，想看你是否理解两边难度不对称。
scenario_en: The interviewer already covered read scaling (replicas, caching) and now asks "what about writes", checking whether you see the asymmetry.
options: 读侧有副本、缓存等成熟工具，写侧突发、高吞吐、强竞争更难扩
写请求的网络包大小天生比读请求大很多
读请求几乎不占用 CPU 和内存资源
写扩展没有专门工具，只能整体换掉数据库
options_en: Reads have mature tools like replicas and caching, while bursty, high-throughput, contention-heavy writes are much harder
Write request payloads are inherently much bigger than read payloads
Read requests barely use any CPU or memory
There are no dedicated tools for scaling writes, so you must replace the database entirely
why: 读侧有读副本、缓存等成熟套路；写侧面对突发、高吞吐和竞争，一次错误选择还可能让情况更糟，所以面试官爱在这里追问。
why_en: Reads scale with familiar tools like replicas and caching, while bursty, high-contention writes are much harder and invite interviewer probing.
tradeoff: 读扩展的现成工具箱 vs 写扩展的突发/竞争难度

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库的只读拷贝，用来分摊读流量，不承担写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a read-only copy of the database used to absorb read traffic, not writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理器，执行计算指令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, runs computation.

q: 补全扩展写入的四大策略：
q_en: Fill in the four write-scaling strategies:
text: 扩展写入的四大策略：{{垂直扩展}}与数据库选型、{{分片}}与分区、用队列和{{load shedding}}处理突发、{{批处理}}与层级聚合。
text_en: The four write-scaling strategies: {{vertical scaling}} and database choices, {{sharding}} and partitioning, queues and {{load shedding}} for bursts, and {{batching}} with hierarchical aggregation.
why: 这四招组合起来，能把写入扩展到单台未优化的数据库/服务器远达不到的量级；面试时按这个顺序逐层升级。
why_en: The four write-scaling strategies are vertical scaling with database choices, sharding and partitioning, queues with load shedding for bursts, and batching with hierarchical aggregation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统过载时主动丢弃部分不重要的写入，保住整体可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding is deliberately dropping some low-value writes when the system is overloaded, to keep the rest of it available.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一份数据横向拆到多台服务器，每台只处理一部分写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across multiple servers so each one only handles a portion of the writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给单台机器换更强的硬件来提升上限，例如更多 CPU 核或更高网络带宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical scaling means giving one machine stronger hardware, such as more CPU cores or more network bandwidth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多条写入合成一批提交，减少每条写入都单独付出的事务和刷盘开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batching combines multiple writes into one submission, reducing per-write transaction and flush overhead.

scenario: 面试官问「写入怎么扩展」，你还没算过当前写入 QPS，也没确认单机是否真的撑不住。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks "how would you scale writes", but you haven't yet computed the current write QPS or confirmed a single machine can't handle it.
q: 第一步应该做什么？
q_en: What should be your first move?
options: 直接上 Kafka 队列
立刻按 userID 分片
先做粗略估算，确认写吞吐是否超出现代单机硬件的能力
换成 Cassandra
options_en: Immediately add a Kafka queue in front of the database
Immediately shard by userID
Do a rough back-of-the-envelope estimate to confirm write throughput actually exceeds modern single-machine hardware
Immediately switch the database to Cassandra
why: 先做 back-of-the-envelope：算出实际写吞吐，对照硬件上限，确认真的撞墙了再加复杂度。这向面试官证明你不会过早架构化。
why_en: First do quick back-of-the-envelope math to check whether the write volume actually exceeds modern hardware before adding any architectural complexity.
whenOtherWins: 如果估算显示写入量确实远超单机（比如百万级 QPS），就直接进入分片、队列等横向策略，不必在垂直扩展上纠缠。
tradeoff: 先估算再动手 vs 直接上架构复杂度
optionMeanings: Kafka 是消息队列，用来缓冲突发写入，不解决稳态容量问题。
分片是把写入横向拆到多台机器的手段。
这是面试里常用的快速估算法，不写代码、不建架构就能判断量级。
Cassandra 是为高写吞吐做了取舍的宽列数据库。
optionScenarioImpacts: 还没算清楚容量就上队列，等于用缓冲掩盖未知问题。
还没确认瓶颈就分片，会让系统平白多出运维复杂度。
先确认真实撞墙没有，才知道后面该不该加复杂度。
换库前得先知道现有硬件到底撑不撑得住。

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户的唯一标识符，常被选作分片或分区的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: userID is a user's unique identifier, commonly chosen as the sharding or partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里快速估算量级的简化计算，用来判断是否真的需要复杂架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Back-of-the-envelope math is a quick order-of-magnitude estimate used to check whether you actually need a more complex architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库，靠追加写而非原地更新拿到写性能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database that trades read performance for write throughput by appending data instead of updating in place.

scenario: 你算出目标写入量约为每秒数万次简单写，正打算判断这在不在单机能力范围内，再决定要不要分片。
scenario_en: You calculated a target load of roughly tens of thousands of simple writes per second and need to judge whether that fits on one machine before deciding to shard.
q: 拿什么单机硬件基准来对照，才不会过早下「必须分片」的结论？
q_en: Which single-machine hardware baseline should you compare against so you don't prematurely conclude "we must shard"?
options: 现代云单机常见 200 核 CPU、10Gbit 网卡，这只是对照估算的基准，不是要背的数字
很多人还停留在 4-8 核、机械硬盘的旧印象，误以为几万写/秒就必须立刻分片
云厂商机器和十年前自建机房的规格完全一样，可以直接套用旧的容量经验
硬件规格无所谓，写入量一多就该先加消息队列做缓冲
why: 这是给定的硬件锚点，不是公式推导结果：把你算出的写入 QPS 和约 200 核、10Gbit 网卡的现代单机对照，再决定是否真的要分片。
why_en: Treat 200 cores and a 10Gbit NIC as a sizing anchor, then compare your estimated write QPS against it before jumping to sharding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理器，执行计算指令；写入路径上的序列化、校验、事务处理都要占用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, runs computation, and write-path work like serialization and transaction handling consumes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒可传输约 10 千兆比特数据的网络接口，决定了单机能吞吐多少写入流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A 10Gbit NIC, or Network Interface Card, moves about ten gigabits of data per second and caps how much write traffic one machine can absorb.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，用于缓冲突发写入，不是硬件规格问题的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue used to buffer write bursts, not an answer to a hardware-sizing question.

options_en: Modern cloud machines commonly reach 200 CPU cores and 10Gbit NICs — this is just a baseline to compare your estimate against, not a number to memorize
Many people still picture 4-8 cores and a spinning disk, so they assume tens of thousands of writes/sec must mean sharding right away
Cloud provider machines have the exact same specs as a decade-old self-hosted data center, so old capacity assumptions still apply
Hardware specs don't matter — once write volume rises at all, just add a message queue to buffer it

scenario: 你已经论证过现代硬件能扛住当前写入量，但面试官不断把规模往上加码，逼你转向横向扩展。
scenario_en: You already argued modern hardware can absorb the current write load, but the interviewer keeps raising the scale to push you toward horizontal scaling.
q: 正确的应对是？
q_en: What's the right way to respond?
options: 坚持和面试官辩论硬件足够
提出垂直扩展的理由后顺势转向横向方案，不要来回拉锯
拒绝回答横向扩展的问题
假装没听到规模变化，继续讲垂直扩展
options_en: Keep arguing with the interviewer that the hardware is sufficient
State the case for vertical scaling once, then move on to horizontal strategies without going back and forth
Refuse to answer the horizontal-scaling question
Ignore the scale change and keep talking about vertical scaling
why: 很多面试官的评分卡就是考横向扩展，会不断移动球门柱。该做的是先展示垂直扩展的判断力，然后见好就收、转向其他扩展手段。
why_en: Make the case for vertical scaling once, but if the interviewer keeps raising the scale, move on to horizontal strategies instead of arguing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给单台机器换更强的硬件（更多核、更大内存/网卡）来扛更高负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical scaling means giving one machine stronger hardware (more cores, memory, or network capacity) to handle more load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 增加更多机器分摊负载，例如分片、多副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling means adding more machines to share the load, such as sharding or replication.

scenario: 系统写多读少，团队在纠结要不要把主存储从传统关系型数据库换成 Cassandra 来提升写吞吐。
scenario_en: The workload is write-heavy, and the team is debating whether to switch the primary store from a traditional relational database to Cassandra for higher write throughput.
q: Cassandra 写吞吐远超传统关系型数据库，核心机制是？
q_en: Cassandra's write throughput far exceeds a traditional relational database's — what's the core mechanism behind that?
options: 把连接池调得更大，减少每次建立连接的握手开销
把整张表都常驻内存缓存，写入先落内存再异步落盘
追加式 commit log：顺序写盘，避免原地更新的昂贵磁盘寻道
给每一列都自动建二级索引，加快后续按列查询
options_en: Make the connection pool bigger to cut per-connection handshake overhead
Keep the whole table resident in memory and write to memory first, flushing to disk asynchronously
An append-only commit log: writes go to disk sequentially, avoiding the expensive disk seeks of in-place updates
Automatically build a secondary index on every column to speed up later column-based queries
why: Cassandra 写入先追加到 commit log 并进 memtable，稍后 flush 成 SSTable；顺序写避开随机寻道，所以吞吐高。代价是读路径常要合并多个 SSTable。
why_en: Cassandra appends to a commit log and memtable first, then flushes SSTables later, trading easier writes for more read-side merging.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    W[写请求] --> M[Memtable]
    W --> L[(Append-only commit log)]
    L -->|顺序写盘| D[(磁盘)]
    M -->|稍后 flush| S[(SSTable)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database built to trade read performance for high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 落盘前先顺序写入的持久化日志，保证写入不丢失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A commit log is an append-only, sequentially written log a database writes to first so a committed write is never lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 内存里的有序写缓冲，写入先进入这里，之后批量刷成磁盘上的 SSTable。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is Cassandra's in-memory sorted write buffer, later flushed to disk as an SSTable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先建立并复用的数据库连接集合，减少连接建立开销，不改变磁盘写入模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool is a reused set of open database connections that cuts connection-setup overhead but doesn't change how data is written to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系库常用的索引结构，更新时通常要改写已有页面，容易带来随机 I/O。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is the balanced index structure relational databases commonly use, and updates often rewrite existing pages, causing random I/O.

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 把 memtable 定期刷到磁盘生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable, or Sorted String Table, is the immutable sorted file Cassandra periodically flushes a memtable to on disk.

scenario: 面试官追问「Cassandra 到底比关系型数据库快多少」，想看你是背答案还是懂前提。
scenario_en: The interviewer presses "exactly how much faster is Cassandra than a relational database", testing whether you recite a number or understand the caveats.
q: 同等普通硬件下，Cassandra 与传统关系型数据库的写吞吐量级对比约是？
q_en: On comparable commodity hardware, roughly how does Cassandra's write throughput compare to a traditional relational database's?
options: Cassandra 在追加写、横向扩展场景通常更容易做到高写吞吐；具体数字只作数量级锚点
两者都约 1,000 写/秒
Cassandra 100 写/秒 vs 关系型 10,000 写/秒
Cassandra 100 万写/秒 vs 关系型 1 写/秒
why: 可以把「Cassandra 常比传统关系库高一个数量级」当口头锚点，但它不是固定公式。真实吞吐取决于硬件、批量写、索引、事务/fsync 和数据模型。
why_en: Use Cassandra being roughly an order of magnitude easier to scale for writes as an anchor, not a fixed benchmark.
optionDirectness: 正确：强调追加写和横向扩展带来的量级优势。
太死：忽略 fsync、索引和批量写差异。
方向反了：Cassandra 通常是写吞吐更强的一侧。
过度夸张：不是可信的 benchmark。

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database built to trade read performance for high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于面试估算的粗量级参照，只帮助判断方向，不代表固定 benchmark。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An order-of-magnitude anchor is a rough sizing reference for interview math, not a fixed benchmark.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用表、行、列和关系约束组织数据的数据库，例如 MySQL 或 PostgreSQL。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A relational database stores data in tables, rows, columns, and relationships, such as MySQL or PostgreSQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 强制把内存中的写入刷到磁盘的系统调用，直接影响持久化写入的实际速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: fsync is the system call that forces buffered writes to disk, and it directly caps real-world durable write speed.

options_en: Cassandra often scales write-heavy append workloads more easily on comparable hardware; the exact number is only an order-of-magnitude anchor
Both are roughly 1,000 writes/sec
Cassandra 100 writes/sec vs relational 10,000 writes/sec
Cassandra 1,000,000 writes/sec vs relational 1 write/sec

scenario: 团队把写重的主存储换成了 Cassandra，写吞吐明显上去了；现在要评估这笔交换的代价。
scenario_en: The team switched the write-heavy primary store to Cassandra and write throughput clearly improved; now you need to weigh what that trade cost.
q: 选了 Cassandra 换来高写吞吐，代价是什么？
q_en: Choosing Cassandra for high write throughput comes at what cost?
options: 换成 Cassandra 后写入依然只能在单机上纵向扩容
读性能变差：读常要查多个文件并合并结果，可能比索引良好的关系库慢
写入完全不落盘，进程一重启数据就会消失
Cassandra 不支持任何副本机制，单点故障就会丢数据
options_en: Even after switching to Cassandra, writes can still only scale vertically on one machine
Read performance gets worse: reads often have to check multiple files and merge results, which can be slower than a well-indexed relational database
Writes are never persisted to disk, so data disappears the moment the process restarts
Cassandra has no replication mechanism at all, so a single node failure loses data
why: Cassandra 读一条数据常要检查多个文件再合并，读性能不如索引良好的关系库。用读性能换写性能，正是写重系统想要的交换。
why_en: Cassandra trades read performance for write performance, since reads often check multiple files and merge results.
tradeoff: 写入顺序追加换吞吐 vs 读取合并多个文件的成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database built to trade read performance for high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 增加更多机器分摊负载；Cassandra 恰恰是为水平扩展设计的，不是它的弱点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling means adding more machines to share load, and it's actually a strength Cassandra is designed around, not a weakness.

optionMeanings: 误以为换库本身限制了扩展方向。
点出 Cassandra 用读性能换写性能这条核心代价。
把「读复杂」误夸大成「不持久」，混淆了两个不同维度。
把「读要合并多文件」误夸大成「完全没有副本」，同样是维度混淆。
optionScenarioImpacts: Cassandra 恰恰是为水平扩展设计的，这个说法夸大了限制。
读一条数据要查多个文件再合并，比索引良好的关系库慢。
追加写只影响读取路径，不代表数据不落盘、不持久。
Cassandra 支持多副本，这个说法混淆了读代价和副本机制。

q: 「写读张力」（write vs. read tension）指的是？
q_en: What does "write vs. read tension" mean?
options: 系统设计里写请求和读请求物理上互斥，不能重叠执行
无论什么场景，读操作的资源开销都必然高于写操作
只要写入量大，就可以完全不设计任何读接口
为写优化往往损害读性能，反之亦然，必须先认清自己的瓶颈是哪边
options_en: Reads and writes are physically mutually exclusive in system design and can never overlap
Read operations always cost more resources than write operations, in every scenario
As long as write volume is high, you can skip designing any read interface at all
Optimizing for writes usually hurts read performance and vice versa, so you must first identify which side is your actual bottleneck
why: 这是扩展写入的根本矛盾：写优化伤读、读优化伤写。先确定瓶颈在哪边再优化，系统的不同部分可能需要不同的取舍。
why_en: Optimizing for writes usually degrades reads and vice versa, so identify which side is your bottleneck and optimize accordingly.
