tradeoff: 写优化（追加写/少约束） vs 读优化（索引/约束）

termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查询而维护的额外数据结构；每多一个索引，每次写入就要多更新一份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is extra structure maintained to speed up queries, and every added index means one more thing to update on every write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径和读路径的优化目标互相牵制：让一边更快，常会让另一边付出代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-versus-read tension means optimizing one path often makes the other path pay a cost.

q: 下面哪些数据库类型是为写重/顺序写场景做的取舍？（多选）
q_en: Which of these database types are built as trade-offs for write-heavy, sequential-write workloads? (select all)
options: 时序数据库（InfluxDB、TimescaleDB）：为大量带时间戳的顺序写而生，还内置 delta 编码省存储
日志结构数据库（LevelDB）：追加新数据而非原地更新
列存（ClickHouse）：为分析负载高效地批量写入
传统单机 OLTP 关系库：默认为极端写负载优化
options_en: Time-series databases (InfluxDB, TimescaleDB): built for high-volume timestamped sequential writes, with built-in delta encoding to save storage
Log-structured databases (LevelDB): append new data instead of updating in place
Column stores (ClickHouse): batch writes efficiently for analytics workloads
Traditional single-node OLTP relational databases: optimized by default for extreme write load
why: 时序库、日志结构库、列存都在各自方向上为写做了取舍；通用关系库是为混合负载设计的，并不为极端写负载优化。
why_en: Time-series databases, log-structured stores like LevelDB, and column stores like ClickHouse all trade toward write efficiency, unlike general-purpose relational databases.
optionScenarioImpacts: 时间戳顺序写能减少乱序更新，delta 编码还能压缩相邻点。
追加写把随机改页变成顺序写，后台再合并文件。
批量写列文件适合分析，但点更新通常不是强项。
通用关系库保留事务、索引和约束，极端写入会被这些开销拖住。

rows: 读写混合，非极端写优化

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为带时间戳的高频顺序写入优化的时序数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InfluxDB and TimescaleDB are time-series databases optimized for high-frequency, timestamped sequential writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只存相邻数值之间的差，而不是完整数值，用来压缩时序数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta encoding stores only the difference between consecutive values instead of full values, to compress time-series data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志结构存储引擎，靠追加写和后台合并代替原地更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LevelDB is a log-structured storage engine that appends writes and merges them in the background instead of updating in place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向分析场景的列式数据库，擅长批量写入和大范围扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ClickHouse is a column-oriented database built for analytics, good at batched writes and large scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列而不是按行组织数据的存储方式，适合批量写入和大范围分析扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A column store organizes data by column rather than row, which suits batched writes and large analytical scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向高频小事务读写的工作负载类型，例如下单、转账。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OLTP, or Online Transaction Processing, describes workloads of many small frequent read/write transactions, like placing an order.

q: 在不换数据库的前提下，哪些手段能让任意数据库写得更快？（多选）
q_en: Without switching databases, which of these actually make any database write faster? (select all)
options: 高写期间关掉昂贵特性：外键约束、复杂触发器、全文索引
调优 write-ahead log，例如 PostgreSQL 攒多个事务再刷盘
减少索引数量——写更快，但读要付出代价
给每张表都加更多二级索引
options_en: Disable expensive features during high-write periods: foreign key constraints, complex triggers, full-text indexing
Tune the write-ahead log, e.g. have PostgreSQL batch multiple transactions before flushing to disk
Reduce the number of indexes — writes get faster, reads pay for it
Add more secondary indexes to every table
why: 禁用昂贵特性、调 WAL 刷盘、砍索引都是「给写让路」的本地优化；加更多索引恰恰会拖慢写入。
why_en: You can speed up writes on any database by disabling expensive features, tuning write-ahead logging, and reducing index overhead.
optionScenarioImpacts: 少做外键、触发器和全文索引维护，每次写入要付的检查更少。
多笔事务合并刷盘，减少 WAL flush 次数，但崩溃窗口要谨慎设。
每少一个索引，写入少维护一份结构；代价是对应查询变慢。
二级索引越多，每次写入要更新的索引页越多。

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库强制校验关联表数据一致性的规则，每次写入都要额外检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key constraint is a rule the database enforces to keep related tables consistent, and it adds a check on every write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库先把变更顺序写入日志、再落到主存储的机制，用于崩溃恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log is the sequential log a database writes changes to before applying them to the main store, so it can recover after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主键之外为加速特定查询而建的额外索引，每建一个都会拖慢写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A secondary index is extra structure built beyond the primary key to speed up specific queries, and each one slows down writes further.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库在写入、更新或删除时自动执行的逻辑，会给每次写操作增加额外工作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A database trigger is logic that runs automatically on writes, updates, or deletes, adding extra work to each write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为文本搜索维护的索引结构，能加速搜索，但写入时也要同步更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full-text index supports text search, but it also has to be updated on each relevant write.

scenario: 面试里你想表达「换个写优化的数据库」，需要展示对取舍的理解而不是丢名词。
scenario_en: In the interview you want to argue for "switch to a write-optimized database", and need to show you understand the trade-off, not just drop a product name.
q: 哪种说法最能拿分？
q_en: Which phrasing earns the most credit?
options: 「我们把数据库换成社区里口碑更好、性能评测更亮眼的那一个就行了」
「解释为什么 Cassandra 的追加写比 MySQL 的 B-tree 原地更新快，或为什么指标采集选时序库」
「NoSQL 反正不用维护表结构，所以写入场景里永远比关系型数据库快」
「数据库选型其实不重要，只要不断加机器、堆更多实例就能解决」
options_en: "We'll just switch to whichever database has the best reputation and flashiest benchmarks."
"Explain why Cassandra's append-only writes beat MySQL's in-place B-tree updates, or why a time-series store fits metrics collection."
"NoSQL never has to maintain a schema, so it's always faster than relational databases for writes."
"Database choice doesn't really matter, just keep adding more machines and more instances."
why: 别只说「用更快的库」——要讲机制：追加写 vs B-tree 更新、时序库为何适合 metrics。展示你懂取舍，而不是背名词。
why_en: Do not just say use a faster database; explain why append-only writes beat B-tree updates or why a time-series store fits metrics.
whenOtherWins: 如果写入量估算下来单库完全扛得住，那连换库都不必提——一个调优过的通用数据库就够了。
tradeoff: 讲清写机制取舍 vs 只报数据库品牌名
optionMeanings: 只给结论，不解释机制，面试官听不出你是否真懂。
点名 Cassandra 的追加写和 MySQL 的 B-tree 原地更新两种机制的差异。
把一个笼统标签当成技术判断，忽略场景差异。
回避数据库选型这个决策点。
optionScenarioImpacts: 靠口碑和 benchmark 选型，没回答写路径为什么会更快。
把候选库和写入机制绑起来，能说明你知道代价。
NoSQL 也有数据模型和查询限制，不能当万能写入加速器。
只堆机器不解释分片键和写机制，等于跳过核心取舍。

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database built to trade read performance for high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: MySQL 等关系库常用的索引结构，更新时通常要原地改写页面，带来随机磁盘寻道。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is the balanced index structure MySQL and similar databases use, and updating it usually means rewriting pages in place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为带时间戳的高频顺序写入优化的数据库，如 InfluxDB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-series database is optimized for high-frequency, timestamped sequential writes, such as InfluxDB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见关系型数据库，默认面向通用 OLTP 负载，而不是极端写入吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MySQL is a common relational database aimed at general OLTP workloads rather than extreme write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组非传统关系模型数据库的统称，不等于所有场景都比关系库写得快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL, or Not Only SQL, is a broad family of non-relational databases, not a guarantee of faster writes in every case.

q: 水平分片的基本承诺是什么？
q_en: What's the basic promise of horizontal sharding?
options: 单机 1,000 写/秒，10 台「应该」能到 10,000 写/秒——把写量分摊到多台，各自处理可控的一份
只要给数据分了片，原本集中在少数热门用户身上的写入热点就会自动被完全拉平
分片之后，读请求就不再需要考虑数据分布问题，性能自动比单机时更快
把数据切成多片分开存放在不同机器上，能让原本的数据总量因此变得更小
options_en: If one server handles 1,000 writes/sec, 10 servers "should" reach 10,000 writes/sec by spreading writes so each handles a manageable share
Simply sharding the data automatically and completely flattens out write hot spots that were concentrated on a few popular users
After sharding, reads no longer need to think about data distribution at all and automatically get faster than on one machine
Splitting data into multiple shards across different machines makes the total amount of data stored smaller
why: 分片的理想态是线性扩展：写量均匀分摊，每台只扛可控的一份。多台服务器组成一个逻辑数据库，对应用（基本）透明。
why_en: Sharding promises near-linear scaling by spreading writes across servers so each handles a manageable portion, hidden behind one logical database.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    W[写入流量] --> H[按 partition key 哈希]
    H --> A[(Shard A)]
    H --> B[(Shard B)]
    H --> C[(Shard C)]
    A --> DBA[(DB A)]
    B --> DBB[(DB B)]
    C --> DBC[(DB C)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一份数据横向拆到多台服务器，每台只处理一部分写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across multiple servers so each one only handles a portion of the writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个分片承受远超其他分片的流量，即使整体分片均匀也可能出现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot spot is a single shard taking far more traffic than the others, which can still happen even with an evenly designed scheme.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器数增加 N 倍时，总吞吐也接近增加 N 倍；真实系统通常只能逼近它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linear scaling means N times as many machines gives close to N times the throughput, though real systems only approximate it.

q: Redis Cluster 是怎么决定一个 key 写到哪个节点的？
q_en: How does Redis Cluster decide which node a key gets written to?
options: 客户端按固定顺序依次把写请求发给每一个节点，不管 key 是什么
把 key 按字母表位置切成几段区间，落在哪段就写到对应节点
对 key 做 CRC 哈希得到 slot 号，slot 被分配到各节点，客户端查路由表后直写对应节点
所有写入请求先统一发给一个中心代理，再由它转发给具体节点
options_en: The client sends writes to every node in a fixed round-robin order regardless of the key
Split keys into ranges by alphabetical position, and write to whichever node owns that range
Hash the key with CRC to get a slot number; slots are assigned to nodes, and the client looks up the routing table and writes directly to the owning node
Every write first goes to one central proxy, which then forwards it to the right node
why: Redis Cluster 用简单 CRC 函数把 key 哈希成 slot 号，slot 分配给节点；客户端自己维护 slot→节点映射，直接把写发给负责的节点。
why_en: Redis Cluster hashes each key with a CRC function to a slot number, slots map to nodes, and clients route writes directly to the responsible node.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant N1 as 节点A (slots 0-5460)
    participant N2 as 节点B (slots 5461-10922)
    C->>C: CRC(key) → slot 7000
    C->>N2: 直接写到负责 slot 7000 的节点B
    N2-->>C: OK
codeSample:
# 客户端先算 key 属于哪个 slot
> CLUSTER KEYSLOT user:1000
(integer) 3999
# 查路由表得知 slot 3999 归节点B，直接写它
> SET user:1000:profile '{"name":"Ann"}'
OK

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的分片集群模式，用 slot 把 key 空间分配到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster is Redis's sharded cluster mode, assigning key-space slots across multiple nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种快速哈希校验算法，Redis Cluster 用它把 key 映射到 slot 号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRC, or Cyclic Redundancy Check, is a fast hashing algorithm Redis Cluster uses to map a key to a slot number.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 把 key 空间切成 16384 个槽位，每个槽位固定分配给某个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slot is one of Redis Cluster's fixed key-space buckets, and each slot is assigned to exactly one node.

scenario: 面试里你说了「sharding」，面试官追问「具体怎么分」。你要给出最关键的那个细节。
scenario_en: You said "we'll shard it" in the interview, and the interviewer follows up with "shard it how, exactly". You need the one detail that matters most.
q: 分片方案里最重要、必须主动讲清的细节是？
q_en: What's the most important sharding detail you must proactively spell out?
options: 先确定用哪家云厂商，再决定机房区域和可用区
先确定每台机器该配多大容量、什么型号的磁盘
先确定分片之间多久互相发一次心跳检测存活
如何选 partitioning key，让数据均匀铺开
options_en: First decide which cloud vendor to use, then the data center region and availability zone
First decide how much capacity and which disk model each machine should have
First decide how often shards send heartbeats to check each other are alive
How you pick the partitioning key so data spreads evenly
why: 面试官期待的不是「sharding」这个词，而是分区键怎么选：选好了（比如 hash userID），数据均匀分布，10 台机器才能真正拿到 10 倍收益。
why_en: The most important sharding detail is selecting a partitioning key that spreads data evenly, which is what actually realizes the ten-times gain.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官继续深挖「客户端怎么找到正确的分片」，就要展开 consistent hashing、虚拟节点、slot 分配这些路由机制。
tradeoff: 分区键选择 vs 其它次要实现细节
optionScenarioImpacts: 云区域影响延迟和容灾，但不能回答写入会不会均匀。
机器规格是容量计算，选错分区键时再大的机器也会热点。
心跳只判断节点存活，不决定一条写入落到哪里。
分区键决定每条写入的去向，直接决定负载是否打散。

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落在哪个分片的字段，选得好坏直接决定负载是否均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partitioning key is the field that decides which shard a row lands on, and picking it well or poorly directly determines whether load is even.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种分片路由算法，节点增减时只需重新分配少量 key，而不是全量重哈希。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing is a sharding scheme where adding or removing a node only reshuffles a small slice of keys instead of rehashing everything.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希环上的虚拟分片点，用来让真实节点承接多个小范围，减轻倾斜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node is a logical point on a consistent-hash ring that lets real nodes own many smaller ranges and reduces skew.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片系统把 key 空间切出的固定槽位，槽位再分配给具体节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slot is a fixed bucket of key space in a sharded system, later assigned to a concrete node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户的唯一标识符，常被选作分片或分区的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: userID is a user's unique identifier, commonly used as a sharding or partition key.

q: 用「用户所在国家」当分区键，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if you use "user's country" as the partition key?
options: 中国这类人口大国的分片过载，新西兰这类分片闲置——负载严重倾斜
选错分区键只会让数据变得难以查询，不会导致数据丢失
只要用了分片，负载天然就会在各节点间完全均匀
分区键只影响读路径的速度，跟写入的分布完全无关
options_en: A populous-country shard like China gets overloaded while a sparse-country shard like New Zealand sits idle — badly skewed load
Picking the wrong partition key only makes data harder to query, it doesn't cause data loss
As long as you shard at all, load naturally ends up perfectly even across nodes
The partition key only affects read-path speed and has nothing to do with write distribution
why: 国家这种低基数、分布不均的键会造成倾斜：写量涌向人口大国的分片，小国分片闲着。这就是坏分区键的经典画像。
why_en: Partitioning by country skews load badly, overloading the China shard while the New Zealand shard sits idle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条数据落在哪个分片的字段，基数太低或分布不均会造成倾斜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which shard a row lands on, and a low-cardinality or unevenly distributed key causes skew.

q: 补全选分区键的原则：
q_en: Fill in the principle for choosing a partition key:
text: 好的分区键要{{最小化}}各分片写入量的方差——图上「{{平}}即是好」；常见做法是对主要标识符（如 {{userId}} 或 postId）取{{哈希}}。
text_en: A good partition key should {{minimize}} the variance in writes per shard — "{{flat}} is good" on the chart; a common approach is to {{hash}} a primary identifier such as {{userId}} or postId.
why: 选键原则：让每个分片的写入量尽量一样多。对高基数主标识符取哈希通常就能做到，候选标识符一般就那几个。
why_en: Pick a key that minimizes variance in writes per shard, usually by hashing a primary identifier like the user ID or post ID.
whenOtherWins: 如果主要查询总是按另一个实体聚合，就要优先评估那个实体是否该做分区键，避免高频读跨片。
tradeoff: 写入均匀分布 vs 高频读是否跨片

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任意输入映射成固定范围数值的函数，用来把 key 均匀打散到各分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash function maps arbitrary input to a fixed-range value, used here to spread keys evenly across shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户的唯一标识符，是最常见的分区键候选之一，基数高、分布均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: userId is a user's unique identifier, one of the most common partition-key candidates because it has high cardinality and even distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 帖子的唯一标识符，也常作为按帖子维度分布数据的分区键候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: postId is a post's unique identifier and a common partition-key candidate for post-centered data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量各分片写入量离平均值有多远的统计量；越小表示越均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Variance measures how far each shard's write count is from the average; lower variance means more even load.

q: 写入完全均匀铺开了，但每个读请求都要跨所有分片收集数据，后果是？
q_en: Writes are perfectly spread out, but every read has to collect data from all shards — what's the consequence?
options: 读请求命中缓存的概率会因为分片布局自动提高
读写各自独立进行，分片布局对读延迟没有任何影响
每个读者都要向集群所有分片发网络调用，读开销巨大
分片把数据摊开后，写入吞吐反而会因此下降
options_en: The cache hit rate for reads automatically improves because of the sharding layout
Reads and writes are fully independent, so the sharding layout has no effect on read latency
Every reader has to make a network call to every shard in the cluster, so read overhead is huge
Spreading data across shards actually makes write throughput go down
why: 分区键不能只看写：如果读要打到每个分片（scatter-gather），网络调用的开销会吃掉分片收益。要同时问「这个请求要打几个分片？发生得多频繁？」
why_en: If every read must fan out to all shards, the network overhead can erase your sharding gains, so consider the read path when picking a key.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R[读请求] --> G[聚合层]
    G -->|scatter| S1[(Shard A)]
    G -->|scatter| S2[(Shard B)]
    G -->|scatter| S3[(Shard C)]
    S1 -->|partial| M[合并结果]
    S2 -->|partial| M
    S3 -->|partial| M
    M --> Resp[响应]

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求同时向多个分片发起子请求，再合并所有结果的读取模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scatter-gather is a read pattern where one request fans out to many shards and then merges all the partial results.

scenario: 在为读写最频繁的「最快」数据设计物理布局，需要一套判断分区方案是否会形成瓶颈的自检问题。
scenario_en: You're designing the physical layout for the "hottest" data — the rows with the most reads and writes — and need a self-check for whether the partitioning scheme creates a bottleneck.
q: 该问自己哪两个问题？
q_en: What two questions should you ask yourself?
options: 「这个请求要打几个分片？」和「这个请求发生得多频繁？」
「用 SQL 还是 NoSQL？」和「要不要加缓存？」
「机器多少核？」和「磁盘多大？」
「团队会不会运维？」和「预算多少？」
options_en: "How many shards does this request have to hit?" and "how often does this request happen?"
"SQL or NoSQL?" and "should we add a cache?"
"How many CPU cores?" and "how big is the disk?"
"Can the team operate it?" and "what's the budget?"
why: 目标是读写都尽量均匀铺开、同时把常一起访问的数据放一起。用「打几个分片 × 多频繁」来判断有没有造出瓶颈。
why_en: Ask how many shards each request must hit and how often that request happens to decide whether your layout creates a bottleneck.
whenOtherWins: 对低频请求，跨全部分片的 scatter-gather 可以接受；只有高频请求跨多分片时才必须重新设计布局。
tradeoff: 写均匀铺开 vs 读的 scatter-gather 成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求同时向多个分片发起子请求，再合并所有结果的读取模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scatter-gather is a read pattern where one request fans out to many shards and then merges all the partial results.

q: 水平分片和垂直分区的区别是？
q_en: What's the difference between horizontal sharding and vertical partitioning?
options: 水平分片和垂直分区其实是同一种技术换了个说法
水平分片切的是行，垂直分区切的是列——按访问模式把不同类型数据拆开
水平分片把表按列切开，垂直分区把表按行切开
垂直分区这种拆表方式只能用在缓存层，不能用在主存储
options_en: Horizontal sharding and vertical partitioning are really just two names for the same technique
Horizontal sharding splits rows; vertical partitioning splits columns — separating different data types by access pattern
Horizontal sharding splits tables by column; vertical partitioning splits tables by row
Vertical partitioning as a table-splitting technique only applies to the caching layer, never primary storage
why: 水平分片按行把同一张表铺到多台；垂直分区按列/类型拆表，把访问模式和扩展需求不同的数据分开存放。
why_en: Horizontal sharding splits rows across servers while vertical partitioning splits columns by access pattern.
tradeoff: 水平分片（按行扩展吞吐） vs 垂直分区（按列隔离访问模式）

rows: 不同访问模式互相干扰

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一张表的不同行分布到多台机器上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal sharding distributes different rows of one table across multiple machines.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一张表的不同列拆成多张表，按访问模式分开存放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical partitioning splits one table's columns into multiple tables, separated by access pattern.

scenario: 社交帖子的单张大表被三类操作互相干扰：用户写内容、系统高频更新互动计数、分析查询扫大量数据。要做垂直分区。
scenario_en: One monolithic post table is being hammered by three interfering workloads: users writing content, the system updating engagement counts constantly, and analytics scanning huge volumes. Time to vertically partition it.
q: 最合理的拆法是？
q_en: What's the most sensible way to split it?
options: 按帖子 ID 的奇偶把同一份带全部字段的大表复制成两张结构一模一样的表
把 content、like_count、view_count 等所有列统统塞进一个 JSONB 字段里存起来
拆成 post_content、post_metrics、post_analytics 三张表，按访问模式分开存放
什么都不拆分，就在被三种操作互相干扰的大表上继续叠加更多二级索引
options_en: Split the same full-column table into two structurally identical copies by odd/even post ID
Cram every column — content, like_count, view_count, and the rest — into one single JSONB column
Split into post_content, post_metrics, and post_analytics — three tables separated by access pattern
Don't split anything, and just keep adding more secondary indexes to the table three workloads are already fighting over
why: 按访问模式拆：内容表写一次读多次、指标表高频更新、分析表只追加。拆开后互不干扰，还能各自搬到最适合的数据库。
why_en: Split the monolithic table into content, metrics, and analytics tables so each access pattern stops interfering with the others.
whenOtherWins: 如果三类访问的量都不大，单表加索引就够了——垂直分区带来的多库运维成本只有在互相干扰成为真实瓶颈时才值得。
tradeoff: 拆表隔离访问模式 vs 单表加索引的运维简单

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 里以二进制格式存储 JSON 的列类型，查询灵活但不是关系建模的替代品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSONB is PostgreSQL's binary JSON column type — flexible to query, but not a substitute for proper relational schema design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一张表的不同列拆成多张表，按访问模式分开存放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical partitioning splits one table's columns into multiple tables, separated by access pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主键之外为加速特定查询而建的额外索引；在这张大表上继续加会放大写入干扰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A secondary index is extra structure beyond the primary key; adding more here would increase write interference.

q: 垂直分区后把三张表搬到不同数据库实例，哪些「表 → 优化方向」的搭配是对的？（多选）
q_en: After vertically partitioning into three tables and moving each to its own database instance, which "table → optimization" pairings are correct? (select all)
options: post_content → 传统 B-tree 索引，为读性能优化
post_metrics → 内存存储或专用计数器，扛高频更新
post_analytics → 时序优化存储或列式压缩数据库
三张表必须留在同一个实例里才正确
options_en: post_content → traditional B-tree indexes, optimized for read performance
post_metrics → in-memory storage or specialized counters, to absorb high-frequency updates
post_analytics → time-series-optimized storage or a column-compressed database
All three tables must stay on the same instance to be correct
why: 垂直分区的收益之一：每张表可以搬到为它的访问模式优化的数据库。内容配 B-tree 读优化、指标配内存计数、分析配时序/列存。
why_en: Each partition can move to a database optimized for it: B-tree indexes for content, in-memory counters for metrics, and columnar or time-series storage for analytics.
whenOtherWins: 如果三张表的访问量都低、事务还常跨列更新，留在同一个实例里更简单，避免分布式事务和运维成本。
tradeoff: 专用存储换性能 vs 多实例的运维成本
optionScenarioImpacts: 内容读多写少，B-tree 能让按 post_id 或 user_id 的读取更快。
互动计数高频变动，内存或专用计数器能减少关系库行锁压力。
分析事件只追加、常批量扫，列存或时序库能压缩并加速扫描。
强行同实例会让三种访问模式继续互相抢资源。

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库常用的索引结构，适合点查和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is the balanced index structure relational databases commonly use, well suited to point lookups and range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列存储相似值再压缩，适合分析表的大范围扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Columnar compression stores similar values by column and compresses them, which suits large analytical scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高频加减计数优化的存储或组件，用来减少通用关系库的行锁和写放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialized counter is storage or logic optimized for frequent increments and decrements, reducing row locks and write amplification.

scenario: 订单系统平时容量刚好够用，团队要求黑五当天必须能扛住平日 4 倍的下单写入量而不掉线。
scenario_en: The order system's normal capacity is just enough day to day, but the team requires it to absorb 4x the usual write volume on Black Friday without falling over.
q: 如果系统必须能扛峰值 4 倍的写入量，平时的容量利用率意味着什么？
q_en: If the system must always be able to absorb a 4x peak in write volume, what does that imply about normal-time capacity utilization?
options: 平时只能用到约 25% 的总容量，多出的 75% 是为峰值预留的
平时能用到 90% 也没问题，因为峰值来的时候还有缓冲时间去扩容
利用率高低跟系统要扛的峰值倍数完全没有关系
不管会不会遇到峰值，平时都必须把容量用满 100% 才划算
why: 公式是平时利用率 ≤ 1 / 峰值倍数；4 倍峰值就是 ≤25%。多数系统不会长期付 75% 闲置成本，所以会用队列或 load shedding 处理突发。
why_en: Normal utilization must be at most one divided by the peak multiplier, so a four-times peak means twenty-five percent utilization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统实际使用的容量占总配置容量的比例；公式是当前负载 / 总容量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Capacity utilization is the current load divided by total provisioned capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统过载时主动丢弃部分不重要写入，保住整体可用性的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding is deliberately dropping some low-value writes when the system is overloaded, to keep the rest of it available.

options_en: Normal-time usage is capped at roughly 25% of total capacity, with the other 75% reserved for the peak
Running at 90% normally is fine too, since there is buffer time to scale up when the peak hits
Utilization has nothing to do with how large the peak multiplier is
Regardless of whether a peak happens, normal-time capacity must be run at 100% to be worth it

q: 为什么「autoscaling」不是写突发的万能药？
q_en: Why isn't "autoscaling" a silver bullet for write bursts?
options: autoscaling 只对读流量生效，对写完全没用
扩缩容需要时间，而且数据库扩容常伴随停机或吞吐下降——恰好发生在业务最火的时刻
autoscaling 是需要额外付费的功能
autoscaling 触发时会主动删除旧数据
options_en: Autoscaling only works for read traffic and does nothing for writes
Scaling takes time, and database scaling often means downtime or reduced throughput — exactly when the business is busiest
Autoscaling is a feature that requires extra payment
Autoscaling deletes old data when it triggers
why: 扩容不是瞬时的，数据库系统扩容时常有停机或吞吐降级，正好撞上流量高峰。所以突发要靠缓冲（队列）或舍弃（load shedding），不能只赌 autoscaling。
why_en: Autoscaling takes time and database scaling often means downtime or reduced throughput exactly when traffic is spiking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据负载自动增减计算资源的机制；数据库层的自动扩容通常伴随停机或降速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autoscaling automatically adds or removes compute based on load, but database autoscaling often causes downtime or a throughput dip.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统过载时主动丢弃部分不重要写入，保住整体可用性的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding is deliberately dropping some low-value writes when the system is overloaded, to keep the rest of it available.

scenario: 写请求偶尔突发到数据库瞬时扛不住，团队考虑在应用和数据库之间插一层消息队列。
scenario_en: Write requests occasionally burst past what the database can instantly absorb, so the team considers putting a message queue between the app and the database.
q: 在写路径中加入 Kafka/SQS 队列，本质上解耦的是什么？
q_en: Adding a Kafka/SQS queue to the write path fundamentally decouples what?
options: 队列把原本一条链路的读请求和写请求彻底分成两条独立的路径
队列的作用是让客户端不用先经过 DNS 解析就能直接建立连接
写入的「接收」与写入的「处理」——接收快速入队，数据库按自己的稳定速率消费
队列把应用进程和它运行所在的操作系统内核彻底隔离开
options_en: The queue splits what used to be one path into a fully separate read path and write path
The queue lets the client establish a connection directly, skipping DNS resolution entirely
Write "acceptance" from write "processing" — accepting a write just enqueues it fast, while the database drains it at its own steady rate
The queue completely isolates the application process from the operating system kernel it runs on
why: 队列把「收下写请求」和「真正写库」分开：突发先进队列缓冲，数据库以稳定速率处理，这就是 burst absorption。
why_en: A write queue decouples write acceptance from write processing so the database drains at a steady rate while the queue absorbs bursts.
diagram:
flowchart LR C[客户端突发写] --> A[App Server] A --> Q[(Kafka / SQS 队列
缓冲突发)] Q -->|稳定速率| W[Worker] W --> D[(数据库)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管消息队列服务，作用和 Kafka 类似，用于缓冲异步写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, or Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed message queue, used similarly to Kafka to buffer asynchronous writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列充当缓冲区，吸收短时间的流量尖峰，让下游以稳定速率处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Burst absorption is the queue acting as a buffer that soaks up short traffic spikes so downstream systems can process at a steady rate.

q: 队列天然是异步的，这给客户端带来什么直接影响？
q_en: A queue is inherently asynchronous — what's the direct consequence for the client?
options: 客户端的写入请求经过队列缓冲之后反而会更快地落进数据库
应用只知道写进了队列、不知道是否已落库，客户端常需要回查机制确认写入最终完成
客户端必须放弃短连接、改用长期保持的连接才能往队列写数据
队列这一层的引入对客户端的调用方式完全没有任何影响
options_en: Buffering through the queue actually makes the client's write land in the database faster
The app only knows the write reached the queue, not whether it reached the database, so clients often need a way to poll back and confirm it eventually landed
The client must give up short-lived connections and switch to a long-held connection just to write to the queue
Introducing this queue layer has absolutely no effect on how the client calls the API
why: 入队成功 ≠ 落库成功。异步意味着确认语义变弱，很多场景要给客户端提供回查/回调机制来确认写入最终生效。
why_en: With an async queue the app only knows the write was enqueued, so clients often need a way to check back that it eventually reached the database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调用者提交请求后不等待结果立即返回，结果稍后才确定，需要额外机制去确认。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Asynchronous means the caller submits a request and returns immediately without waiting for the result, so confirming the outcome needs a separate mechanism.

q: 如果生产者持续以超过数据库消费能力的速率写入队列，会怎样？
q_en: If producers keep writing to the queue faster than the database can consume it, what happens?
options: 队列会自动限速生产者的写入
数据库会自动变快来追上速度
多余的写会被静默丢弃，用户不会察觉
队列无界增长，写入处理延迟越来越长，用户越来越不耐烦
options_en: The queue automatically throttles the producers
The database automatically speeds itself up to catch up
The excess writes are silently dropped and no one notices
The queue grows without bound and processing delay keeps increasing, so users get more and more impatient
why: 队列只是缓冲不是产能：入队速率长期大于出队速率就是无界积压，延迟不断攀升。此时即便扩库去追积压，用户体验往往已经恶化。
why_en: If writes enter the queue faster than the database can drain it, the queue grows without bound and processing delay keeps increasing.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P[生产者 10k/s] --> Q[(队列积压增长)]
    Q -->|消费者 4k/s| W[Worker]
    W --> D[(数据库)]
    Q -.延迟上升.-> U[用户等待]

termDefinitions.meaning: 下游跟不上时让上游减速或拒绝新请求的机制；没有它，队列就会持续积压。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure is a mechanism that slows or rejects producers when downstream can't keep up; without it, the queue keeps backing up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已经入队但还没被消费的消息数量；入队长期快于出队时会不断增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue backlog is the number of enqueued messages not yet consumed; it grows when enqueue rate stays above drain rate.

scenario: 数据库连平峰的稳态负载都扛不住，有人提议「加个 Kafka 队列解决写入问题」。
scenario_en: The database can't even handle normal steady-state load at average traffic, and someone proposes "just add a Kafka queue to fix the write problem".
q: 对这个提议的正确判断是？
q_en: What's the right judgment on this proposal?
options: 队列只该用于短暂突发的缓冲；用它掩盖稳态容量不足是在掩盖病根，队列终将被打爆
只要上了队列，就可以从此不再考虑数据库要不要扩容这件事
队列本身能让数据库处理写入的速度变得更快
只要把队列的容量配置得足够大，积压的问题就自然不存在
options_en: A queue should only buffer short-lived bursts; using it to mask insufficient steady-state capacity just hides the real problem, and the queue will eventually blow up
Once a queue is in place, you never have to think about scaling the database again
A queue by itself makes the database process writes faster
As long as the queue's capacity is configured big enough, backlog simply stops being a problem
why: 队列的正确用法是吸收短暂突发；如果稳态负载就超过数据库产能，队列只会积压成灾。候选人常犯的错就是拿队列糊底层问题。
why_en: Use queues for short-lived bursts, not to patch a database that cannot handle the steady-state load.
whenOtherWins: 如果负载真的是间歇性尖峰、稳态在产能之内，队列就是正确工具——先在需求阶段确认对延迟写入的容忍度。
tradeoff: 队列吸收短暂突发 vs 用它掩盖稳态容量不足
optionScenarioImpacts: 稳态超产能时入队永远快于出队，积压只会越来越大。
数据库仍要按自己的吞吐落库，队列不能取消容量规划。
队列改变到达时间，不改变数据库每秒能处理多少写。
容量变大只推迟爆掉时间，不会修复长期入队更快的问题。

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在非峰值时段的正常持续负载水平，是判断容量是否够用的基准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Steady-state load is the system's normal ongoing load outside of peaks, the baseline for judging whether capacity is sufficient.

scenario: 你在考虑给写路径加队列，但还没和面试官对齐需求。
scenario_en: You're considering adding a queue to the write path, but haven't yet aligned with the interviewer on requirements.
q: 加队列之前必须先在需求阶段确认什么？
q_en: Before adding a queue, what must you confirm at the requirements stage?
options: 先纠结队列中间件具体该选 Kafka 还是 SQS 这类产品细节
系统对「延迟写入」和「不一致读」的容忍度，确保队列不破坏关键的功能/非功能需求
先把队列要开几个分区这种容量参数早早定下来
先确定消费者服务打算用哪种编程语言去实现
options_en: Getting hung up on whether the queue product should be Kafka or SQS
How much tolerance the system has for delayed writes and inconsistent reads, so the queue doesn't break key functional or non-functional requirements
Locking in how many partitions the queue should have this early
Deciding upfront which programming language the consumer service will be written in
why: 队列引入异步和最终一致。先确认业务能否容忍写延迟和读到旧数据——多数系统在最高峰能容忍一点延迟，但不能想当然。
why_en: Before adding a queue, confirm at the requirements stage how much write delay and read inconsistency the system can tolerate.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求要求写后立读、强一致确认（如支付扣款），队列这种异步缓冲就不合适，得靠分片/扩容硬扛。
tradeoff: 异步缓冲换吞吐 vs 写后立读的强一致需求
optionMeanings: Kafka 和 SQS 都是消息队列产品，选型是实现细节，不是最先要确认的需求。
这道题问的正是这个：业务对写延迟、脏读的容忍边界决定队列能不能用。
分区数是队列容量的实现参数，晚点再定不影响一致性判断。
消费者语言是实现细节，不影响一致性/延迟这类业务需求。
optionScenarioImpacts: 先争产品名会跳过异步队列能不能满足业务语义的问题。
确认边界后，才能决定排队、回查和用户提示怎么设计。
分区数只能影响吞吐，不能回答写后是否必须立刻可见。
语言选择不改变队列带来的延迟写入和最终一致。

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管消息队列服务，作用和 Kafka 类似。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, or Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed message queue, used similarly to Kafka.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内读可能读到旧值，但最终会收敛到最新值的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a read right after a write may see a stale value, but the system eventually converges to the latest one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端写入成功后，后续读取必须立刻看到自己的最新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-writes means that after a client writes successfully, its later reads must immediately see that write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统确认写入后，后续读取都必须看到最新值，不能短暂读到旧数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means once a write is acknowledged, later reads must see the latest value, not a stale one.

q: 广告点击聚合器的两条核心功能需求是？（多选）
q_en: What are the two core functional requirements of an ad click aggregator? (Select multiple.)
options: 用户点击广告后被重定向到广告主网站
广告主能以最小 1 分钟粒度查询点击指标
系统负责广告定向与投放
支持跨设备的用户跟踪
options_en: Clicking an ad redirects the user to the advertiser's site.
Advertisers can query click metrics down to one-minute granularity.
The system handles ad targeting and serving.
The system supports cross-device user tracking.
optionMeanings: 点击后由系统把用户带到广告主的落地页
查询窗口最细可以按分钟切分，不是只有天级汇总
决定给谁看哪条广告、以什么创意展示
跨手机、电脑等设备识别同一个用户
optionScenarioImpacts: 这是唯一的用户侧动作，必须保证不漏记跳转
决定了聚合窗口最细要做到分钟级
这部分交给 Ad Placement Service 黑盒处理
需要跨端身份打通，题目开场就排除了这块
optionDirectness: 属于两条核心功能需求之一
属于两条核心功能需求之一
明确划出范围外，不是本题要设计的功能
跨端识别同样在范围外，本题不覆盖
optionMeanings_en: The system routes the user to the advertiser's landing page after a click.
Query windows can be sliced as fine as one minute, not just daily rollups.
This decides which ad to show whom and with what creative.
This links the same user's identity across phone, desktop, etc.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It's the only user-facing action, so it must never go untracked.
It sets the finest aggregation window you must support, down to a minute.
That logic lives inside the Ad Placement Service black box.
It needs cross-device identity resolution, which is ruled out upfront.
optionDirectness_en: One of the two core functional requirements.
One of the two core functional requirements.
Explicitly out of scope, not something this system designs.
Cross-device identity is also out of scope and not covered here.
why: 系统只对两件事负责：把点击导向广告主网站，以及让广告主按最细 1 分钟粒度查询指标；定向、投放、跨设备跟踪都留给别的系统。
why_en: The system only owns two things: redirecting the click and letting advertisers query metrics at one-minute granularity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据能被切分和查询的最小时间/维度单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Granularity is the finest time or dimension unit at which data can be queried.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据用户特征决定给谁展示哪条广告的逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ad targeting decides which ad to show which user based on their attributes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 选择并下发广告素材到具体展示位的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ad serving is the process of selecting and delivering ad creative to a placement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一用户在手机、电脑等不同设备上的行为关联起来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-device tracking links one user's activity across multiple devices.

q: 在广告点击聚合器的需求范围里，以下哪些被明确划为 out of scope？（多选）
q_en: In the ad click aggregator scope, which items are explicitly out of scope? (Select all that apply.)
options: 广告定向（targeting）与广告投放（serving）
跨设备跟踪、与线下营销渠道的整合

q: 补全本题的规模设定：
text: 规模：{{1000万}} 个活跃广告；峰值 {{1万}} 次点击/秒；按峰值约等于 10 倍平均，平均约 {{1000}} 次/秒；一天约 {{1亿}} 次点击。

why_en: These numbers tell you writes dwarf reads, so one database can't keep up — you need streaming buffers and pre-aggregation.

q: 面试估算里常用的「峰值流量 vs 平均流量」经验比值是？

峰值 = 平均

Peak equals the average.

Peak is roughly 10x the average.
why: 峰值≈10倍平均是常用的面试估算经验值：用它把峰值 1 万/秒换算成平均约 1000/秒，再乘 86400 秒得到日均约 1 亿次点击。
why_en: The interview rule of thumb is that peak traffic runs about ten times the average, which turns a 10k/s peak into roughly 1k/s average.
scenario: 开场估算广告点击聚合器的规模：题目给了峰值 1 万次点击/秒，要反推平均吞吐。

Use a meta-refresh page as a relay.
Have the advertiser's site install a callback script to notify us.

An intermediate HTML page that auto-redirects after a delay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事件发生后由第三方主动通知我方系统的机制。

q: 补全 Cassandra 的 LSM 写入路径：
q_en: Fill in Cassandra's LSM write path:
text: 写入先追加到磁盘上的 {{commit log}} 保证持久性，再写入内存中的有序结构 {{memtable}}，后者定期刷盘成不可变的 {{SSTable}} 文件。

why_en: Writes append to a commit log, land in an in-memory memtable, and get flushed to disk as immutable SSTables.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入内存结构前先落盘的追加日志，用于故障后恢复。

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存中的有序结构，缓冲最近写入，定期刷盘。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is an in-memory sorted structure that buffers recent writes before flushing to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: memtable 刷盘后生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is an immutable sorted file on disk produced by flushing a memtable.

Most direct: matches the pre-aggregated, per-minute-granularity design goal.
Less direct: unrelated to the click-aggregation pipeline.
Less direct: without aggregation this just duplicates the event store.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径完成之后，提前把数据按查询模式汇总好，换取读路径的低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-aggregation summarizes data ahead of time so read-path queries can return with low latency.

scenario: 「好方案」把点击写入事件库，每 N 分钟由批任务算出一次聚合结果。
scenario_en: The good design writes clicks to an event store and runs a batch job every N minutes to compute aggregates.
q: 这种设计有一个内在的新鲜度问题，是什么？
q_en: What freshness problem is built into this batch design?
options: 批处理会导致存储成本无限增长，拖垮预算
批处理架构本身无法做水平扩展
分析查询用到的 GROUP BY 语法太复杂，难以维护
数据永远滞后至少几分钟——广告主查到的总是旧数据
why: 批任务隔 N 分钟才跑一次，管道天然带几分钟延迟，与「尽可能实时」的需求冲突——这正是后面引入流处理的动机。
why_en: Batch jobs only run every N minutes, so the pipeline bakes in a few minutes of delay that conflicts with the near-real-time requirement.
options_en: Batch processing makes storage cost grow without bound and blows the budget.
The batch architecture itself cannot scale horizontally.
The GROUP BY syntax used for analytics queries is too complex to maintain.
Data always lags by at least a few minutes — advertisers always see stale data.
optionMeanings: 把批处理的问题错误定位到存储容量
把批处理的问题错误定位到扩展能力
把批处理的问题错误定位到查询接口的易用性
把问题准确定位到「结果新鲜度」这条决定性约束
optionScenarioImpacts: 存储成本是运维问题，跟批处理本身的延迟无关
Spark 和事件库都能水平扩展，扩展性不是批处理的短板
GROUP BY 语法并不复杂，复杂度不是这里的痛点
批任务每 N 分钟跑一次，查到的永远是上一批之前的数据
optionDirectness: 不够直接：批处理引入的核心风险不是存储膨胀
不够直接：批处理组件本身可以水平扩展
不够直接：查询语法跟批处理架构无关
最直接：批处理周期本身就是延迟的来源
optionMeanings_en: Misattributes the batch problem to storage capacity.
Misattributes the batch problem to scaling ability.
Misattributes the batch problem to query-syntax complexity.
Correctly locates the problem in result freshness.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Storage cost is an ops concern, unrelated to batch latency itself.
Spark and the event store both scale horizontally — scaling isn't the batch weakness.
GROUP BY isn't actually complex; syntax isn't the pain point here.
The batch job runs every N minutes, so results are always from the prior batch or older.
optionDirectness_en: Less direct: the core risk of batching isn't storage growth.
Less direct: the batch components themselves scale horizontally.
Less direct: query syntax is unrelated to the batch architecture.
Most direct: the batch interval itself is the source of the delay.

scenario: 批处理按固定 N 分钟窗口运行；某广告主大力投放，点击量突然飙升到数倍于平时。
scenario_en: Batch processing runs on a fixed N-minute window; a major advertiser campaign suddenly drives click volume several times above normal.
q: 流量突刺对这套批处理管道会造成什么连锁影响？
q_en: What chain reaction does a traffic spike cause in this batch pipeline?
options: 批处理架构天然能抗流量突刺，不会受影响
事件库检测到突刺会自动对写入限流
下一批数据窗口变大，任务可能跑得比批间隔还久，形成级联延迟
写入量超过阈值时，OLAP 会直接拒绝写入
why: 突刺让批任务变慢、待处理窗口越积越大，形成级联延迟；讽刺的是广告主最需要实时数据的大投放时刻，数据反而最陈旧。
why_en: A traffic spike inflates the batch window so the job can run longer than the interval, cascading staleness exactly when advertisers need fresh data most.
options_en: The batch architecture is naturally spike-proof and unaffected.
The event store detects the spike and auto-throttles writes.
The next batch gets a bigger window, the job may outrun the interval, and delay cascades.
OLAP will reject writes once volume crosses a threshold.
optionMeanings: 假设批处理架构对流量变化天然免疫
把「限流」这个能力错误地安在事件库头上
点出批处理在突刺下会级联延迟的真实机制
把「写入变慢」误当成「直接拒绝写入」
optionScenarioImpacts: 实际上批任务处理时长会随数据量线性增长，并不免疫
Cassandra 这类事件库能扛写入压力，但不会自己判断限流
下一批窗口变大，任务跑更久，再下一批窗口更大，延迟越滚越大
OLAP 只是写入变慢，架构上没有理由直接拒绝合法写入
optionDirectness: 不够直接：忽视了批任务耗时随数据量增长这一事实
不够直接：限流不是事件库在这个场景里的默认行为
最直接：准确描述了级联延迟这个连锁反应
不够直接：混淆了写入变慢和写入被拒绝
optionMeanings_en: Assumes the batch architecture is naturally immune to traffic changes.
Wrongly attributes rate-limiting behavior to the event store.
Names the real mechanism: batching cascades into staleness under a spike.
Confuses 'writes get slower' with 'writes get rejected outright'.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: In reality batch runtime grows roughly with data volume — it isn't immune.
Event stores like Cassandra can absorb write pressure, but they don't self-throttle like this.
A bigger window means a longer job, which means the next window is bigger still — delay compounds.
OLAP writes just get slower; there's no architectural reason for it to reject valid writes.
optionDirectness_en: Less direct: ignores that batch runtime scales with data volume.
Less direct: throttling isn't the event store's default behavior here.
Most direct: accurately names the cascading-delay mechanism.
Less direct: conflates slower writes with rejected writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次批任务要处理的数据时间范围，窗口越大处理越久。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The batch window is the time range of data one batch job processes; bigger windows take longer to run.

scenario: 有人提议在点击处理服务和事件库之间加一层队列，用来吸收写入尖峰。
scenario_en: Someone proposes adding a queue between the click processor and the event store to absorb write spikes.
q: 这层队列能解决什么、不能解决什么？
q_en: What does this queue solve, and what does it not solve?
options: 能压平写入尖峰，但解决不了「数据滞后几分钟」的延迟问题
加了队列之后，尖峰和延迟两个问题都能一次性解决
队列只能用来降低广告主查询接口的延迟
加队列反而会让延迟更严重，也扛不住尖峰
why: 队列只缓冲写入压力；只要聚合仍由定时批任务完成，新鲜度问题就还在——要同时解决两者，得换成流式处理。
why_en: A queue absorbs write spikes but does nothing for staleness as long as aggregation still runs on a batch schedule; fixing both needs stream processing.
diagram:
graph LR
    ClickSvc[Click service] --> Kafka[Kafka or Kinesis]
    Kafka --> EventStore[(Raw event store)]
    Kafka --> Flink[Flink aggregation]
    Flink --> OLAP[(OLAP)]
options_en: It smooths write spikes, but doesn't fix the 'data lags a few minutes' latency problem.
Adding a queue fixes both the spike and the latency problem at once.
The queue only helps reduce latency on the advertiser query API.
Adding a queue actually makes latency worse and still can't absorb spikes.
optionMeanings: 准确区分「写入保护」和「结果新鲜度」是两个独立问题
把队列的作用夸大成能解决聚合延迟
把队列的作用错放到查询路径而非写入路径
把队列的正面作用直接说反了
optionScenarioImpacts: 写入尖峰被削平，事件库不再被打爆，但批任务的调度周期没变
队列不参与聚合计算，无法让批任务跑得更勤
队列加在写入端，跟广告主的查询路径完全无关
队列削峰是它的标准作用，说它抗不了尖峰与事实相反
optionDirectness: 最直接：准确划清队列能解决和不能解决的边界
不够直接：混淆了「缓冲写入」和「加速聚合」
不够直接：队列不在查询路径上，起不了这个作用
不够直接：与队列削峰的基本作用相矛盾
optionMeanings_en: Correctly separates 'write protection' from 'result freshness' as two different problems.
Overstates the queue's role as if it also fixes aggregation latency.
Misplaces the queue's effect on the query path instead of the write path.
States the queue's actual benefit backwards.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Write spikes get smoothed and the event store stops getting overwhelmed, but the batch schedule is unchanged.
The queue isn't part of aggregation, so it can't make the batch job run more often.
The queue sits on the write side and has nothing to do with the advertiser query path.
Spike absorption is exactly what queues do — this claims the opposite.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: correctly draws the line between what the queue fixes and what it doesn't.
Less direct: conflates 'buffering writes' with 'speeding up aggregation'.
Less direct: the queue isn't on the query path at all.
Less direct: contradicts the queue's basic spike-absorption role.

scenario: 「最优方案」要求点击一进来就写入一个既能抗 1 万次/秒突刺、又持久可重放的缓冲，供下游实时聚合消费。
scenario_en: The optimal design needs a durable, replayable buffer that absorbs 10k-clicks-per-second spikes and feeds real-time aggregation.
q: 这个缓冲选什么组件？
q_en: Which component should this buffer use?
options: 用 SQS 这类标准消息队列做缓冲
Kafka 或 Kinesis 这类可重放的分布式日志流
跳过缓冲，点击直接写进 OLAP 分析库
缓冲放在应用进程的内存队列里
why: Kafka/Kinesis 天生分布式高吞吐、多副本持久化，消费后数据仍可重放，既扛得住突刺又防丢数据。
why_en: Kafka or Kinesis is distributed, durable, and replayable, so it absorbs click spikes while giving the aggregator a safety net if it falls behind.
whenOtherWins: 规模小、实时性要求不高时，「事件库 + 定时批处理」更简单，不值得为此引入流的运维复杂度。
tradeoff: 抗突刺+可重放的流缓冲 vs 更简单但无回放能力的普通队列
options_en: Buffer with a standard message queue like SQS
A replayable distributed log stream like Kafka or Kinesis
Skip the buffer and write clicks straight into OLAP
Keep the buffer in the application process's memory queue
optionMeanings: 标准队列，消息被消费后即删除，一般不支持按位点重放
分布式提交日志：多副本持久化，消费后仍可按 offset 重新读取
跳过缓冲层，点击直接写进聚合库
缓冲存在应用进程内存里，随进程重启而丢失
optionScenarioImpacts: 重放能力弱，Flink 重启后难以从丢失点找回历史事件
多副本抗节点故障，多日保留期让下游故障后能重新消费
OLAP 为读优化，扛不住 1 万/秒的写入尖峰，直接被打垮
进程重启或崩溃就把还没消费的点击全部丢了
optionDirectness: 不够直接：标准队列的重放能力不如日志流稳固
最直接：同时满足「抗突刺」和「可重放」两条约束
不够直接：OLAP 是读优化存储，不是写入缓冲层
不够直接：内存队列没有持久化，达不到「不丢数据」的要求
optionMeanings_en: A standard queue that deletes messages after consumption, generally without offset-based replay.
A distributed commit log: multi-replica durability with offset-based replay after consumption.
Skips the buffer entirely and writes clicks straight into the analytics store.
A buffer kept in application memory that disappears on process restart.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Weak replay support makes it hard for the aggregator to recover lost events after a restart.
Multi-replica durability plus a multi-day retention window lets consumers recover after failures.
OLAP is read-optimized and would buckle under a 10k/s write spike.
A process restart or crash loses every click that hadn't been consumed yet.
optionDirectness_en: Less direct: a standard queue's replay guarantees are weaker than a log stream's.
Most direct: satisfies both the spike-absorption and replayability constraints.
Less direct: OLAP is a read-optimized store, not a write buffer.
Less direct: an in-memory queue has no durability, failing the no-data-loss requirement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式、分区化的持久消息日志，消费后数据仍保留一段时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed, partitioned, durable message log that retains data for a period after consumption.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管流式数据服务，功能与 Kafka 类似。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis is AWS's managed streaming data service, functionally similar to Kafka.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管队列服务，消息一般消费即删，重放能力有限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS is AWS's managed queue service; messages are typically deleted once consumed, with limited replay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者可以从某个历史位点重新读取数据，用于故障恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replay lets a consumer re-read data from an earlier position, used for failure recovery.

scenario: 需要按分钟窗口实时聚合点击：事件可能乱序到达，要判断何时能安全关窗，还要求不重复计数、宕机不丢状态。
scenario_en: You need minute-window real-time click aggregation; events can arrive out of order, windows need safe closing, and state must survive failures without double counting.
q: 为什么用 Flink 而不是自己写 Kafka consumer 做内存计数？
q_en: Why use Flink instead of writing your own Kafka consumer with in-memory counters?
options: 裸 consumer 里维护一个内存 HashMap 计数，跟 Flink 效果完全一样，没必要多引入一个框架
Flink 只是给 Kafka consumer 包了一层，性能天然比裸 consumer 差
consumer 自己写 checkpoint 逻辑，就能拿到和 Flink 一样的 exactly-once 保证
Flink 自带事件时间窗口、watermark、exactly-once 和状态容错——这些在裸 consumer 上都要自己重造，且极易出错
why: 「consumer 内存计数、每分钟刷库」对中级候选人是合格答案，但乱序、关窗时机、精确一次、状态恢复这些难点都是在重新发明 Flink。
why_en: A raw consumer that counts in memory is a fine mid-level answer, but out-of-order events, safe window closing, exactly-once, and state recovery are exactly what Flink already solves.
whenOtherWins: 中级面试或需求确实简单时，普通 Kafka consumer 内存计数、每分钟落库是可以接受的答案。
tradeoff: 框架内建的正确性保证 vs 自研 consumer 的简单直接
options_en: A raw consumer keeping an in-memory HashMap count works exactly the same as Flink, so no new framework is needed.
Flink is just a wrapper around a Kafka consumer, so it's inherently slower than a raw consumer.
If the consumer writes its own checkpoint logic, it gets the same exactly-once guarantee as Flink.
Flink bundles event-time windowing, watermarks, exactly-once, and state fault tolerance — all painful and error-prone to rebuild on a raw consumer.
optionMeanings: 低估乱序事件和关窗时机对「内存计数」正确性的挑战
把「多一层抽象」等同于「性能更差」
把 checkpoint 当成 exactly-once 的全部
点出 Flink 把窗口、watermark、精确一次、容错打包提供
optionScenarioImpacts: 乱序、迟到、宕机恢复，HashMap 方案都没处理
开销换来的是正确性，不是单纯变慢
checkpoint 不解决「何时能安全关窗」
四项能力对应场景里的四个约束
optionDirectness: 不够直接：漏掉乱序和关窗时机两个核心难点
不够直接：混淆抽象开销与正确性保证
不够直接：exactly-once 需窗口和 checkpoint 协同
最直接：逐条对应乱序、关窗、去重、容错
optionMeanings_en: Underestimates how hard ordering and window timing make an in-memory counter.
Equates 'another abstraction layer' with 'worse performance'.
Treats checkpointing as the whole exactly-once story.
Names windowing, watermarks, exactly-once, and recovery bundled together.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A HashMap counter has no story for ordering, late data, or crash recovery.
The overhead buys correctness, not just slowness.
Checkpointing alone doesn't decide when a window can safely close.
The four capabilities map onto the scenario's four constraints.
optionDirectness_en: Less direct: misses ordering and window-timing, the two hardest problems.
Less direct: conflates overhead with correctness guarantees.
Less direct: exactly-once needs windowing plus checkpointing together.
Most direct: matches each constraint in the scenario one to one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流式处理框架，提供事件时间窗口、watermark、状态管理和精确一次保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing framework providing event-time windows, watermarks, state management, and exactly-once guarantees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证每条事件恰好被处理一次，既不丢也不重复计数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once means every event is processed exactly one time — no loss, no duplicate counting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理引擎定期把内部状态快照写到持久存储，故障后可以从快照恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint is a periodic snapshot of internal state saved to durable storage so processing can resume after a failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按事件真实发生时间而非到达时间划分的时间桶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An event-time window buckets events by when they actually happened, not when they arrived.

q: 相比裸 Kafka consumer，Flink 提供了哪些关键能力？（多选）
q_en: What key capabilities does Flink provide over a bare Kafka consumer? (Select multiple.)
options: 跨聚合窗口的点击去重
事件时间语义的窗口聚合：乱序事件也能落进正确的分钟桶
watermark：判断何时可以安全关闭一个窗口
exactly-once 处理保证与状态故障恢复
why: 事件时间窗口、watermark、精确一次、状态恢复是 Flink 的核心能力；但跨窗口去重做不到——去重必须在事件进流之前完成。
why_en: Flink gives you event-time windowing, watermarks, exactly-once processing, and state recovery, but cross-window deduplication has to happen before events enter the stream.
options_en: Deduplicating clicks across aggregation windows
Event-time semantics for windowed aggregation: out-of-order events still land in the correct minute bucket
Watermarks: deciding when it is safe to close a window
Exactly-once processing guarantees and state fault recovery
optionMeanings: 去重逻辑，要求判断同一个 key 是否跨越了聚合窗口边界
按事件实际发生时刻分桶，而不是按到达时刻分桶
追踪事件时间推进进度的信号，用来判断关窗的安全时机
处理引擎对「不丢、不重」和「故障后能恢复到中断点」的保证
optionScenarioImpacts: Flink 只在流内部工作，看不到进流之前已经发生过的重复点击
迟到几秒到达的点击，仍能落进它实际发生的那一分钟
没有 watermark，引擎不知道是要继续等还是可以关窗了
Flink 挂掉重启后，能从最近一次 checkpoint 恢复而不用重新算全量
optionDirectness: 不够直接：跨窗口去重必须在写入流之前完成，Flink 管不到
最直接之一：这正是 Flink 窗口语义的核心能力
最直接之一：watermark 是 Flink 自带的关窗判断机制
最直接之一：exactly-once 和状态恢复是 Flink 的标志性保证
optionMeanings_en: Deduplication logic that has to check whether the same key crosses a window boundary.
Buckets events by when they actually happened, not by when they arrived.
A signal that tracks event-time progress, used to decide when closing a window is safe.
The engine's guarantee of no loss or duplication plus resuming from the point of failure.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Flink only sees events once they're in the stream, so it can't catch duplicates that happened before that point.
A click that arrives a few seconds late still lands in the minute it actually occurred.
Without a watermark, the engine has no signal for waiting longer versus closing now.
After a crash, Flink resumes from the last checkpoint instead of recomputing everything.
optionDirectness_en: Less direct: cross-window dedup must happen before the stream, outside Flink's control.
Most direct: this is the core of Flink's windowing semantics.
Most direct: watermarks are Flink's built-in signal for closing windows.
Most direct: exactly-once and state recovery are Flink's signature guarantees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记事件时间已经推进到哪里的信号，用于判断何时能安全关窗。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watermark signals how far event time has progressed, used to decide when it's safe to close a window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事件在现实世界实际发生的时刻，而不是被系统处理的时刻。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Event time is when something actually happened in the real world, as opposed to when the system processed it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证每条事件恰好被处理一次，既不丢也不重复计数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once means every event is processed exactly one time — no loss, no duplicate counting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理引擎故障后，从最近一次保存的状态快照继续处理，而不是从零开始。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State recovery resumes processing from the last saved snapshot after a failure instead of starting over.

scenario: 点击可能因为网络延迟、重试等原因乱序或延迟到达聚合系统。
scenario_en: Clicks may arrive out of order or late because of network delay and retries.
q: 事件时间 vs 处理时间：本系统为什么用前者做聚合？
q_en: Event time vs. processing time: why aggregate by event time here?
options: 处理时间比事件时间更准确，因为用的是稳定的服务器时钟
事件时间和处理时间只差了一个时区换算
事件时间是点击实际发生的时刻，能让乱序到达的事件落进正确的分钟桶
事件时间的定义就是 Flink 收到这条事件的那个时刻
why: 点击发生的时刻才是业务上正确的归属依据；处理时间受网络和消费延迟影响，会把迟到事件记进错误的分钟桶。
why_en: Aggregating on event time — when the click actually happened — keeps out-of-order events in the correct minute bucket, unlike processing time.
tradeoff: 业务归属正确性（事件时间）vs 实现简单性（处理时间）

q: 哪种写法能保证正确合并？

options: INSERT INTO minute_agg (ad_id, minute_ts, clicks) VALUES (123, 1640000000, 40)
INSERT INTO minute_agg ... ON CONFLICT (ad_id, minute_ts) DO UPDATE SET clicks = minute_agg.clicks + EXCLUDED.clicks
INSERT INTO minute_agg ... ON CONFLICT (ad_id, minute_ts) DO UPDATE SET clicks = EXCLUDED.clicks
UPDATE minute_agg SET clicks = 40 WHERE ad_id = 123 AND minute_ts = 1640000000
why: 必须是「累加式」upsert：冲突时把新的部分计数加到已有值上。直接覆盖（SET = EXCLUDED）或裸 UPDATE 都会丢掉其他分区已写入的计数。
why_en: Only an additive upsert that sums the incoming partial count into the existing value merges concurrent writes from different partitions correctly.
tradeoff: 累加式 upsert 的正确性 vs 简单覆盖写入的低复杂度

既挡住重复点击，又不误伤再营销的合法重复曝光
下游统计里仍混着重复项，没有真正去重
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It would double-count a user's legitimate repeat views across different impressions.
Any second click by any user on that ad would get swallowed.
It blocks duplicate clicks while still counting legitimate repeat impressions from retargeting.
Downstream counts still include duplicates — nothing is actually deduped.
optionDirectness: 粒度太粗：挡住了再营销场景下的合法重复点击
粒度错位：广告是被无数用户共享点击的资源
最直接：正是题目要求的「按展示实例」去重粒度
没有实现幂等：幂等要求重复点击不改变计数结果
optionDirectness_en: Too coarse: it blocks legitimate repeat clicks from retargeting.
Wrong unit: an ad is a shared resource clicked by many users.
Most direct: this is exactly the per-impression dedup granularity required.
Not idempotent: idempotency requires duplicates not to change the count.

q: 「强制登录 + 按 userId+adId 去重」这个朴素方案的两大问题是？
q_en: What are the two main problems with forcing login and deduping by userId plus adId?
options: JWT 解析开销太大，拖慢点击路径
登录假设不成立，且去重粒度错在按广告而非按展示实例
Redis 容量存不下海量 userId 索引
点击事件里压根拿不到 adId 字段
options_en: JWT parsing overhead is too high and slows down the click path.
The login assumption doesn't hold, and the dedup granularity is wrong — it should be per impression, not per ad.
Redis can't hold the volume of userId indexes at this scale.
The click event doesn't actually carry an adId field.
why: 登录是产品层面的假设，未必满足；更致命的是它把去重粒度定错了——应该是「每用户每广告实例一次」而不是「每用户每广告一次」。
why_en: Requiring login may not hold, and deduping by user and ad ID wrongly merges legitimate repeat clicks from retargeting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告主故意在一段时间内向同一用户重复展示同一广告，是正常且常见的投放策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retargeting is when an advertiser deliberately re-shows the same ad to the same user multiple times, a normal advertising strategy.

optionScenarioImpacts: JWT 校验是微秒级操作，不是这个方案的真实瓶颈
会计漏再营销场景下同一用户对同一广告的多次合法点击
userId 只有几十字节，容量从不是这里的瓶颈
adId 本就是点击事件自带字段，取数不是障碍
optionScenarioImpacts_en: JWT validation is microsecond-scale — not the real bottleneck of this approach.
It would miscount legitimate repeat clicks from retargeting on the same ad.
userId is only a few dozen bytes — capacity was never the issue.
adId already comes attached to the click event — it's not missing.
optionDirectness: 跑题：性能不是这个朴素方案被否决的原因
最直接：同时点出登录假设和去重粒度两个真实缺陷
跑题：容量问题与方案本身的设计缺陷无关
跑题：字段可得性不是这个方案被淘汰的原因
optionDirectness_en: Off-topic: performance isn't why this naive approach fails.
Most direct: it names both the login assumption and the wrong dedup granularity.
Off-topic: capacity has nothing to do with this approach's real flaw.
Off-topic: field availability isn't why this approach is rejected.

q: 什么是一次 impression（曝光）？
q_en: What is an impression?
options: 用户点击广告发生的那一次动作
广告主期待的转化行为发生一次
广告素材第一次被创建出来
广告被展示在用户屏幕上一次，换位置就是新曝光
options_en: The single moment a user clicks the ad.
The moment the advertiser's desired conversion happens.
The one-time creation of the ad creative.
The ad is displayed once on screen; a new placement counts as a new impression.
why: 曝光按「展示」计数而不是按「广告」计数：同一用户在不同位置多次看到同一广告，就是多次曝光。这正是去重键的正确粒度。
why_en: An impression counts each time an ad is fetched and displayed, so the same ad shown in multiple placements yields multiple impressions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告被展示给用户的一次具体呈现，同一广告可以产生多个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one concrete instance of an ad being shown; the same ad can generate many impressions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点击广告后完成了广告主期望的后续行为，例如下单或注册。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conversion is when a user completes the advertiser's desired action after clicking, such as a purchase or signup.

optionMeanings: 把曝光等同于点击这个下游行为
把曝光等同于广告主期望的转化行为
把曝光等同于广告素材被创建的事件
曝光按「被展示的那一次」计数，粒度是展示位置
optionMeanings_en: Equates an impression with the downstream click action.
Equates an impression with the advertiser's desired conversion.
Equates an impression with the ad creative being created.
An impression counts by the moment it's actually displayed.
optionScenarioImpacts: 很多曝光根本不会被点击，两者不能画等号
转化发生在点击之后，属于题目声明的排除范围
一条广告创建后能展示成千上万次，创建只发生一次
同一广告在不同位置各自产生独立曝光
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Plenty of impressions are never clicked — the two aren't equivalent.
Conversion happens after a click and is explicitly out of scope.
One ad can be shown thousands of times after being created once.
The same ad shown in different placements yields separate impressions.
optionDirectness: 混淆概念：点击率＝点击数/曝光数，两者是分子分母关系
跑题：转化跟踪是题目明确排除的范围
错误粒度：曝光按展示次数计，不按广告条目计
最直接：这正是去重键要用的粒度基础
optionDirectness_en: Conflated concepts: CTR = clicks / impressions, they're not the same thing.
Off-topic: conversion tracking is explicitly out of scope.
Wrong unit: impressions count by display, not by ad record.
Most direct: this is the granularity the dedup key relies on.

scenario: 要求「每个用户每次看到的广告实例只计一次点击」，且不能强制用户登录。
scenario_en: Each ad instance shown to a user should count at most one click, and users cannot be forced to log in.
q: 去重键应该用什么？
q_en: What should the dedupe key be?
options: 登录用户的 userId 拼接 adId 作为去重键
客户端 IP 地址加 User-Agent 指纹
系统为每次广告展示单独生成的唯一 impression ID
点击发生的时间戳精确到秒级
options_en: The logged-in userId concatenated with the adId.
The client's IP address plus its User-Agent fingerprint.
The unique impression ID the system mints separately for every ad instance shown.
The click's timestamp, precise to the second.
why: impression ID 的粒度正好是「广告实例」：随广告下发到浏览器，点击时带回来作为幂等键，既不依赖登录，也兼容再营销。
why_en: A unique impression ID minted per ad instance serves as the idempotency key, sent to the browser with the ad and returned with the click.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品保证全员登录、且不存在再营销这类重复展示语义，userId+adId 去重实现更简单。
tradeoff: 依赖登录识别用户 vs 用免登录的展示级唯一标识去重

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告展示服务为每次广告曝光生成的唯一标识符，用作去重的幂等键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression ID is a unique identifier minted for each ad impression, used as the idempotency key for deduplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用网络地址和浏览器标识拼出的模糊用户特征，不是稳定唯一的标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP plus User-Agent fingerprinting combines network address and browser string into a fuzzy signal, not a stable unique ID.

optionMeanings: 沿用登录后的用户ID拼广告ID作为去重键
用网络地址和浏览器字符串拼出的模糊指纹
系统为每次展示单独生成的唯一标识
用点击发生的秒级时间作为去重键
optionMeanings_en: Reuse the logged-in userId concatenated with adId as the dedup key.
A fuzzy fingerprint built from network address and browser string.
A unique ID the system mints separately for each impression.
The click's arrival time rounded to the nearest second.
optionScenarioImpacts: 要求登录，且会把同用户对同广告的多次合法曝光误判为重复
同一 WiFi 下多用户共享 IP，换网络后指纹也会变
天然满足免登录，且粒度精确对齐每一次展示
同一秒内的不同点击会被误判成重复
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Requires login, and misjudges a user's multiple legitimate views of the same ad as duplicates.
Users sharing WiFi share an IP, and switching networks changes the fingerprint.
Naturally login-free, and its granularity aligns exactly with one impression.
Two distinct clicks in the same second would be wrongly flagged as duplicates.
optionDirectness: 违反「不能强制登录」的约束，粒度也错在广告而非展示
不够精确：指纹既不唯一也不稳定，误判率高
最直接：由系统生成，同时满足免登录和展示级粒度
键本身不具唯一性，热门广告下冲突概率很高
optionDirectness_en: Violates the no-forced-login constraint, and the granularity is wrong too.
Not precise enough: the fingerprint is neither unique nor stable.
Most direct: system-generated, satisfies login-free and per-impression granularity.
Not a unique key: collision risk is high for popular ads.

q: 为什么去重不能放在 Flink 的聚合逻辑里做？
q_en: Why shouldn't deduplication live inside Flink aggregation?
options: 重复点击可能落在分钟边界两侧，窗口内去重看不到彼此
Flink 没有状态存储
Kafka 不允许消费前修改数据
Flink 的窗口内存放不下去重集合
options_en: A duplicate click can land on opposite sides of a minute boundary, invisible to window-level dedup.
Flink has no state storage.
Kafka doesn't allow modifying data before it's consumed.
Flink's window memory can't hold the dedup set.
why: 窗口内去重挡不住跨窗口的重复：同一 impression 的两次点击分别落在 12:00:59 和 12:01:01 就会各计一次。去重必须前置到入流之前。
why_en: Deduplication must happen before the stream because duplicates landing on opposite sides of a window boundary would otherwise be counted twice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种流处理框架，按事件时间做窗口聚合，并提供状态管理和容错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing framework that performs windowed aggregation on event time with built-in state management and fault tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式消息队列/日志系统，用来缓冲和持久化事件流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging log used to buffer and durably store event streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理里按固定时间切分数据并分别计算指标的时间段，例如每分钟一个窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An aggregation window is a fixed time slice, like one minute, over which a stream processor computes metrics.

optionMeanings: 去重要发生在事件入流之前，而非窗口聚合阶段
断言 Flink 缺少维护中间状态的能力
断言 Kafka 禁止在消费前变更数据
把问题归因为窗口内存装不下已见集合
optionMeanings_en: Dedup must happen before events enter the stream, not during window aggregation.
Claims Flink has no way to maintain intermediate state.
Claims Kafka forbids modifying data before consumption.
Blames it on the window's memory being too small for the seen-set.
optionScenarioImpacts: 两次点击落在不同窗口时，窗口内去重完全看不到彼此
Flink 其实自带状态管理和 checkpoint，前提不成立
问题不在 Kafka 能不能改数据，而在去重的时机
就算内存无限大，跨窗口重复依旧存在
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Two clicks landing in different windows would never see each other.
Flink actually has built-in state management and checkpointing — the premise is false.
The issue isn't whether Kafka can be modified, it's dedup timing.
Even with unlimited memory, the cross-window duplicate problem remains.
optionDirectness: 最直接：这正是重复点击跨分钟边界导致重复计数的根因
事实错误：状态管理正是 Flink 的核心能力之一
跑题：瓶颈是窗口边界，不是 Kafka 的读写权限
不是根因：内存大小改变不了窗口边界问题
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: this is exactly why duplicates crossing a minute boundary get double-counted.
Factually wrong: state management is one of Flink's core features.
Off-topic: the bottleneck is the window boundary, not Kafka's read/write rules.
Not the root cause: memory size doesn't fix the window-boundary problem.
scenario: 点击已经进入 Flink，按分钟窗口做实时聚合后写入 OLAP。
scenario_en: The click has already entered Flink, which aggregates by minute windows and writes to OLAP.

scenario: 点击到达 Click Processor 时要用 impression ID 判重：重复的丢弃，新的进流。
scenario_en: When a click reaches the Click Processor, it uses impression ID to dedupe: duplicates are dropped and new clicks enter the stream.
q: 正确的处理流程是？
q_en: What is the correct processing flow?
options: 先写缓存占位，再写流
查缓存命中即丢弃；未命中先写流再登记缓存
全部直接入流，靠 Flink 窗口内去重
写 OLAP 时按主键去重
options_en: Write a cache placeholder first, then write to the stream.
Check the cache: a hit means drop it; a miss means write to the stream first, then register the ID.
Send everything straight into the stream and rely on Flink's window-level dedup.
Dedup by primary key when writing to the OLAP table.
why: 缓存是「见过的 impression ID」集合：命中即重复。新点击必须先落流再登记缓存，保证任何失败模式下点击本身不丢。
why_en: On each click we check the cache for the impression ID, drop it if present, and otherwise write to the stream first and then record the ID in the cache.
whenOtherWins: 若业务能容忍跨窗口的少量重复且没有对账需求，Flink 窗口内去重能挡住部分重复，实现更简单但不完整。
tradeoff: 先写流保事件 vs 先写缓存保不重复
diagram:
graph LR
    Click[Click with impressionId] --> Seen{Seen in dedup cache?}
    Seen -->|yes| Drop[Drop duplicate]
    Seen -->|no| Stream[Write event to stream]
    Stream --> Mark[Mark impression seen]
    Mark --> Redirect[Return redirect]

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向分析查询优化的列式数据库，擅长聚合但不擅长高频单条写入去重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An OLAP database is a columnar store optimized for analytical aggregation, not for high-frequency per-row dedup writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录「已经见过的 impression ID」的缓存集合，命中即判定为重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The dedup cache stores impression IDs already seen; a hit means the click is a duplicate.

optionScenarioImpacts: 写流失败时缓存已标记「见过」，这条点击永久丢失
任一步失败最多造成可被对账修正的重复，不会丢点击
跨窗口边界的重复点击会被窗口内去重漏掉（见062）
点击早被聚合成汇总行，原始 impression ID 已丢失
optionScenarioImpacts_en: If the stream write then fails, the cache already says 'seen' and the click is lost forever.
Any single failure at worst causes a duplicate reconciliation can fix — never a lost click.
Duplicates straddling a window boundary slip through window-level dedup (see card 062).
By the time it hits OLAP, clicks are already aggregated — the raw impression ID is gone.
optionDirectness: 顺序颠倒：拿丢失事件的风险换不来任何好处
最直接：把「不丢事件」放在「不重复」之前
不满足幂等要求：挡不住跨窗口的重复
时机太晚：聚合之后已无单条点击可去重
optionDirectness_en: Backwards ordering: it trades away event safety for nothing gained.
Most direct: it puts 'never lose the event' ahead of 'never double count.'
Fails the idempotency requirement: can't catch cross-window duplicates.
Too late: there's no individual click left to dedup after aggregation.

q: 去重流程里为什么必须「先写流、再写缓存」而不是反过来？
q_en: Why must the dedupe flow write to the stream before writing to the cache?
options: 因为缓存的写入延迟更高
因为 Kafka 要求先收到事件
两个顺序效果完全一样
缓存失败只造成可修复的重复；入流失败点击永久丢失
options_en: Because the cache has higher write latency.
Because Kafka requires receiving the event first.
Both orderings produce exactly the same outcome.
A cache failure only risks a fixable duplicate; a stream-write failure loses the click forever.
why: 这是不对称的失败权衡：多计一次能被每日对账修正，漏计一次却无处找回。所以宁可先保住事件、缓存登记放后面。
why_en: Writing the stream first means a cache failure only risks a fixable duplicate, while the reverse order could lose a click for good.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定期用离线批处理重新计算结果，与线上结果比对纠错的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reconciliation is a periodic batch job that recomputes results offline and corrects discrepancies against the live pipeline.

optionScenarioImpacts: 两者写入延迟其实都是毫秒级，不是顺序依据
Kafka 协议本身没有这类强制顺序要求
忽略了两种失败的后果不对称：重复可修，丢失不可逆
把风险敞口留在「可被对账修正」的一侧
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Both writes are actually millisecond-scale — latency isn't what drives the ordering.
Kafka's protocol has no such ordering requirement built in.
It ignores the asymmetry: duplicates are fixable, loss is not.
It keeps the risk exposure on the side that's recoverable.
optionDirectness: 跑题：决定顺序的是失败后果，不是延迟大小
事实错误：这是我们自己的容错设计，不是 Kafka 的约束
错误：先写缓存失败会让事件永久丢失，后果完全不同
最直接：这正是顺序选择背后的权衡依据
optionDirectness_en: Off-topic: the ordering is driven by failure consequences, not latency.
Factually wrong: this is our own fault-tolerance design, not a Kafka rule.
Wrong: a failed cache-first write can lose the click permanently — very different outcomes.
Most direct: this asymmetry is exactly what drives the ordering choice.

q: 只靠「唯一 impression ID 去重」会被怎么攻击？怎么防？
q_en: How can unique impression IDs still be attacked, and how do you defend against it?
options: 攻击者伪造全新唯一 ID 冒充点击；防法是签名验证 ID 与 adId
攻击者反复重放同一个已用过的 ID；防法把 ID 加长
攻击者直接清空我们的去重缓存；防法加装防火墙
唯一性天然防伪造，这套设计无法被攻击
options_en: An attacker forges brand-new unique IDs to pass as valid clicks; the fix is signing and verifying the ID with the adId.
An attacker replays the same already-used ID repeatedly; the fix is making IDs longer.
An attacker wipes out our dedup cache directly; the fix is adding a firewall.
Uniqueness alone naturally prevents forgery — this design can't be attacked.
why: 去重只挡「重复」，挡不住「伪造的新 ID」。签名让只有我们下发的 ID 才验得过，伪造的 ID 直接被拒。
why_en: An attacker could flood the system with fabricated unique impression IDs, so we sign each ID with an HMAC and verify the signature on every click.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用密钥生成消息摘要的对称签名算法，用来验证数据完整性和来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HMAC is a symmetric keyed hash algorithm used to verify a message's integrity and origin.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用同一把密钥重新计算签名并比对，判断数据是否被篡改或伪造。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Signature verification recomputes the signature with the shared key and compares it to detect tampering or forgery.

optionMeanings: 攻击面在「去重挡不住新伪造 ID」，防御靠密钥签名
假设攻击是重放同一个 ID，防御靠加长 ID
假设攻击是直接攻破缓存基础设施
断言唯一性本身就等于安全
optionMeanings_en: The attack surface is 'dedup can't stop brand-new forged IDs'; the defense is a keyed signature.
Assumes the attack is replaying one ID; the fix is making IDs longer.
Assumes the attack is directly breaching the cache infrastructure.
Asserts uniqueness alone equals security.
optionScenarioImpacts: 未持有密钥的伪造 ID，验签阶段就会被直接拒绝
重放同一 ID 本就会被去重缓存拦住，不是真缺口
防火墙防不住来自合法客户端的应用层伪造请求
唯一只保证不重复，挡不住凭空伪造新值
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A forged ID without the secret key fails verification immediately.
Replaying the same ID is already caught by the dedup cache — not the real gap.
A firewall can't stop application-layer forgery from a legitimate client.
Uniqueness only guarantees no duplicates, not that new values can't be fabricated.
optionDirectness: 最直接：精确对应攻击手法和密码学防御
攻击场景不成立：加长 ID 防不住伪造全新 ID
跑题：问的是去重逻辑漏洞，不是基础设施入侵
假设不成立：唯一和防伪造是两回事
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: it precisely matches the attack to its cryptographic defense.
Attack scenario doesn't hold: longer IDs don't stop forging brand-new ones.
Off-topic: the question is about a dedup-logic flaw, not infrastructure breach.
False premise: uniqueness and forgery-resistance are different properties.

q: HMAC 签名时为什么要把 adId 一起签进去？
q_en: Why include adId in the HMAC signature?
options: 为了让签名字符串更难被猜出规律
为了方便按 adId 做流分片
防止把一条广告的合法签名重放到另一条广告上
为了压缩点击事件的传输体积
options_en: To make the signature string harder to guess the pattern of.
To make sharding the stream by adId easier.
To stop a valid signature from one ad being replayed onto another ad.
To compress the size of the click event payload.
why: 只签 ID 本身挡不住「换广告重放」：拿到一批合法签名后打到别的广告上。把 adId 绑进签名，验签即校验两者匹配。
why_en: Signing the ad ID together with the impression ID prevents attackers from harvesting valid signed IDs and replaying them against different ads.

q: 在点击路径上做 HMAC 验签，开销是什么量级？

Second-scale, so it needs dedicated hardware.
It depends on the RSA key length.
Microsecond-scale — one hash computation, negligible latency.

why_en: HMAC verification is a microsecond-scale hash, cheap enough to run synchronously right in the click path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用密钥生成消息摘要的对称签名算法，用来验证数据完整性和来源。

q: 把幂等点击跟踪的完整流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the full idempotent click-tracking flow in order:
steps: Click Processor 验证 impression ID 的签名
Ad Placement Service 为每次广告展示生成唯一的 impression ID
未命中：先把点击写入流，再把 impression ID 加进缓存
用户点击广告，浏览器把签名的 impression ID 随点击数据一起发回
用密钥对 impression ID（连同 adId）做 HMAC 签名，随广告一起下发到浏览器
查询缓存：命中说明是重复点击，直接丢弃
why: 生成 ID → 签名下发 → 点击带回 → 验签 → 查重 → 先写流再登记缓存，这条链同时解决了去重、防伪造、防丢三件事。
why_en: This flow mints, signs, and verifies the impression ID, writing to the stream before caching it — solving dedup, forgery, and loss together.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    G["生成 impression ID"] --> S["HMAC 签名后随广告下发"]
    S --> C["点击时浏览器带回 ID"]
    C --> V["验签"]
    V --> D{"缓存里已存在？"}
    D -->|是| X["重复，丢弃"]
    D -->|否| W["先写流，再写缓存"]

q: 「广告主查询要低延迟」这条需求主要靠什么已经解决了？

Memorizing a limit doesn't show you understand why sharding is needed.
optionDirectness: 超出中级要求：中级重广度，不必给完整容错架构
最直接：这是文章给中级候选人划的及格线
要求过低：连需要预聚合的认识都没体现
考点错误：考的是设计推理，不是参数记忆
optionDirectness_en: Beyond the mid-level bar: E4 is breadth-first, not full fault tolerance.
Most direct: this is exactly the bar the article sets for mid-level.
Bar set too low: doesn't even show awareness that pre-aggregation is needed.
Wrong thing tested: interviews test design reasoning, not trivia recall.

资深阶段只考察设计广度，Staff+ 阶段则完全只考察技术深度
无论候选人处于哪个级别，面试官的期望标准都完全一致
Staff+ 候选人可以跳过高层设计，直接进入深挖环节

Senior candidates are tested purely on breadth, Staff+ purely on depth.

Staff+ candidates can skip the high-level design and jump straight to deep dives.

资深依然需要一定深度，Staff+ 也要能过一遍高层设计
若成立，晋升 Staff+ 就没有额外技术判断力要求
Staff+ 依然要过一遍高层设计，只是更快带过
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Both levels dig deep, but differ in breadth and how proactively they drive it.
Senior still needs some depth, and Staff+ still has to get through a high-level design.
If true, reaching Staff+ would add no extra technical judgment requirement.
Staff+ still walks through a high-level design, just faster.
optionDirectness: 最直接：准确对应文章对两级候选人的描述
过度简化：两级都是广度+深度组合，只是比例不同
与文章矛盾：两级在深挖程度和主动性上明确不同
与文章矛盾：Staff+ 是快速带过而非跳过
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: matches the article's description of both levels precisely.
Oversimplified: both levels blend breadth and depth, just in different ratios.
Contradicts the article: the two levels clearly differ in depth and proactivity.
Contradicts the article: Staff+ speeds through it, doesn't skip it.

q: Bitly（短链服务）设计中，哪些属于核心功能需求？（多选）
q_en: Which features are core functional requirements for designing a Bitly-style URL shortener?
options: 提交长 URL，拿到一个短链（可选自定义别名和过期时间）
通过短链访问原始长 URL（重定向）
用户注册与账号管理
点击量、地域分布等分析功能
why: 核心功能只有两条：缩短（含可选别名/过期）和重定向。账号体系和点击分析都划到 below the line——它们加复杂度但不是短链的本质。
why_en: The core functions are just shortening a URL with optional alias and expiration and redirecting via the short link, while auth and analytics are out of scope.
optionMeanings: 缩短：提交长 URL 换回短链，可选别名/过期。
重定向：访问短链跳回原始长 URL。
账号体系：注册、登录、用户管理。
点击分析：统计点击量和地域分布。
optionDirectness: 核心功能之一：创建短链本身。
核心功能之一：访问后完成跳转。
属于账号体系，不是短链本质功能。
属于统计分析，不是短链本质功能。
options_en: Submit a long URL and get back a short link, optionally with a custom alias and expiration date.
Visit the short link and get redirected to the original long URL.
User registration and account management.
Analytics such as click counts and geographic breakdown.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户自己指定的短码，替代系统自动生成的短码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A custom alias is a short code the user picks instead of one the system generates.

q: 补全 Bitly 的核心非功能需求：
q_en: Fill in Bitly's core non-functional requirements.
text: 短码必须{{唯一}}（一个短码只对应一个长 URL）；重定向延迟 < {{100}}ms；可用性 {{99.99}}%（可用性优先于一致性）；规模支持 {{10 亿}}条短链和 {{1 亿}} DAU。
why: 这四条 NFR 是后面所有深挖的锚点：唯一性驱动短码生成方案，低延迟驱动缓存/CDN，高可用驱动副本，规模数字驱动容量估算。
why_en: The non-functional requirements are unique short codes, sub-hundred-millisecond redirects, four-nines availability favoring availability over consistency, one billion URLs, and one hundred million daily active users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数，一天内至少使用一次产品的用户数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU is daily active users, the count of users who use the product at least once that day.

q: Bitly 的 NFR 里写「availability > consistency」，这句话的含义是？
q_en: What does availability greater than consistency mean in Bitly's non-functional requirements?
options: 必须强一致，宁可拒绝请求也不能返回旧数据
可用性和一致性要同时做到完全极致
优先保证可用，接受数据短暂不一致（CAP 选 AP）
这个系统的设计与 CAP 定理无关
why: 短链是读服务，用户拿不到重定向比读到一条稍旧的映射更糟，所以在分区/故障时优先可用。这也解释了为什么可以大胆用缓存和副本。
why_en: Choosing availability over consistency means the service keeps serving redirects even if some data is briefly stale, which justifies heavy caching and replication.
options_en: The system must stay strongly consistent even if that means rejecting requests.
Both availability and consistency must be pushed to their absolute limits at once.
It favors availability and accepts briefly stale data, an AP choice under CAP.
This system's design has nothing to do with the CAP theorem.
optionMeanings: 把强一致当成不可让步的硬需求。
误以为 CAP 两边能同时拉满。
CAP 里选 AP：可用优先，一致性放宽。
否认系统受 CAP 权衡约束。
optionDirectness: 金融账本这类不能读旧值的系统才会优先强一致。
单机或无分区假设下才可能同时追求两者。
短链读路径宁愿服务旧映射，也不要直接不可用。
只有非分布式单机服务才基本不用讨论 CAP。

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分区容错下，一致性和可用性只能二选一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says that under a network partition, a distributed system must trade off consistency against availability.

q: 这个读写比对数据库选型和优化重点最直接的含义是什么？
q_en: What does this read-write ratio imply for database choice and optimization focus?
options: 必须选择专门为高写吞吐设计的数据库（如宽列存储）
写路径几乎不构成瓶颈，优化预算应集中在读路径的缓存与索引
应该给写路径也加多级缓存来分担压力
读写比不影响架构决策，索引和缓存同等重要即可
why: 写入量极小，几乎任何数据库都扛得住；1000:1 的读写比意味着优化预算该压在读路径的缓存和索引上。
why_en: Writes are tiny in volume, so almost any database can handle them; a 1000:1 read-write ratio means the optimization budget belongs on read-path caching and indexing.
scenario: Bitly 的点击（读）与新建短链（写）之比约为 1000:1；写入端每天新建量级只有个位到两位数 QPS。
scenario_en: Bitly has roughly a 1000:1 read-to-write ratio, and new short-link creation is only single- to low-double-digit QPS.
options_en: We must choose a database built for very high write throughput, such as a wide-column store.
The write path is barely a bottleneck, so optimization budget should go to caching and indexing the read path.
We should add multi-level caching to the write path too.
The read-write ratio doesn't affect the architecture; indexing and caching matter equally.

q: 「读远多于写」这个观察，对 Bitly 设计最直接的影响是？
q_en: What is the main design implication of Bitly being far more read-heavy than write-heavy?
options: 必须换成强一致数据库，否则无法上线
必须优先对写路径做分片
应该去掉索引以减少写放大
读路径要激进缓存、读写分开扩展
why: 极端偏读意味着把优化火力集中在读路径：缓存、CDN、读服务独立扩容；写路径每秒约 1 行，几乎任何数据库都扛得住。
why_en: The extreme read skew means aggressive caching and independently scaled read paths matter most, making this a textbook scaling-reads problem.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Clicks["大量点击"] --> Read["Read Service 横向扩展"]
    Read --> Cache["缓存热门短码"]
    Cache -->|miss| DB[("Mapping DB")]
    Writes["少量创建"] --> Write["Write Service"]
    Write --> DB
options_en: We must switch to a strongly consistent database or the system cannot ship.
We must shard the write path first.
We should drop indexes to cut write amplification.
