The read path needs aggressive caching, and reads and writes should scale separately.
optionMeanings: 把读写比误判成一致性问题。
把优化重点错放在写路径分片。
把索引当成写入负担来削减。
把优化火力集中在读路径缓存。
optionDirectness: 一致性约束变强时才优先换强一致存储。
写入 QPS 很高且单库顶不住时才先分片写路径。
只有极端写重且索引拖垮写入时才考虑少建索引。
读远多于写时，缓存和读服务独立扩容更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门针对读多写少场景的扩展模式，靠缓存和只读副本分担压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scaling reads is a pattern for read-heavy systems that leans on caching and read replicas to absorb load.

q: Bitly 的核心实体（core entities）是哪一组？
q_en: Which set contains Bitly's core entities?
options: 短链、点击事件、广告
原始长 URL、短 URL、用户
用户、会话、支付
长 URL、DNS 记录、证书
why: 实体阶段只需要一个简短清单：原始长 URL、短 URL、创建它的用户。列出来对齐思路即可，字段细节留到高层设计再补。
why_en: The core entities are simply the original long URL, the short URL, and the user who created it.
options_en: Short link, click event, advertisement.
Original long URL, short URL, and the user.
User, session, payment.
Long URL, DNS record, certificate.
optionMeanings: 混入点击事件和广告等不相关实体。
实体阶段的标准三件套。
套用了电商/支付类系统的实体。
套用了网络基础设施类实体。
optionDirectness: 做点击分析或广告系统时，这组实体才会进入核心。
设计短链主路径时，这三者足够表达创建和重定向。
账号和支付型产品才需要会话、支付这类实体。
做域名托管或证书平台时，DNS 和证书才是业务实体。

scenario: 要设计「缩短 URL」的 REST 接口：客户端提交长 URL（可带自定义别名、过期时间），服务端在数据库里新建一条短码到长 URL 的映射。
scenario_en: You are designing the REST endpoint for shortening a URL: the client submits a long URL, optional alias, and expiration, and the server creates a new code-to-URL mapping.
q: 应该用哪个 HTTP 方法？
q_en: Which HTTP method should this endpoint use?
options: GET /urls?long_url=...
PUT /urls
POST /urls
DELETE /urls
why: 缩短 URL 是在数据库里「创建一条新资源」（长短映射），REST 里创建用 POST；请求体带 long_url、可选 custom_alias 和 expiration_date，返回 short_url。
why_en: Shortening creates a new mapping resource, so a POST to /urls with the long URL and optional alias and expiration is the right verb.
whenOtherWins: 如果是更新已有短链（比如改过期时间）才用 PUT；读取用 GET；REST 面试里 9/10 的情况就是按「动词对操作」选。
options_en: GET /urls?long_url=...
PUT /urls
POST /urls
DELETE /urls
optionMeanings: GET 用来读取已有资源。
PUT 用来更新已有资源。
POST 用来创建新资源。
DELETE 用来删除已有资源。
optionDirectness: 读取已有短链或查询详情时才用 GET。
客户端指定完整资源 ID 并覆盖已有资源时才用 PUT。
创建一条新的长短 URL 映射时用 POST。
删除已有短链或撤销资源时才用 DELETE。
tradeoff: 创建新资源用 POST vs 更新已有资源用 PUT

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用 HTTP 方法表达资源操作的 API 设计风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that maps HTTP verbs onto operations on resources.

q: 补全缩短 URL 的请求与响应：
q_en: Fill in the request and response for shortening a URL.
text: POST /urls 请求体包含 {{long_url}}、可选的 {{custom_alias}} 和可选的 {{expiration_date}}；响应返回 {{short_url}}。重定向接口是 GET /{short_code}，返回 HTTP {{302}} 跳转。
why: API 通常与功能需求 1:1 对应：一个 POST 创建映射，一个 GET 做重定向。把可选参数（别名、过期）放进请求体，契约就完整了。
why_en: The API is a POST to /urls taking the long URL with optional alias and expiration and returning the short URL, plus a GET on the short code that answers with a 302 redirect.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 302 状态码，表示临时重定向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 302 is a status code meaning the resource is temporarily located elsewhere.

q: 用户访问 GET /{short_code} 后，浏览器是如何到达原始长 URL 的？
q_en: After a user visits GET /{short_code}, how does the browser reach the original long URL?
options: 服务器返回 Location 头的 HTTP 重定向，浏览器自动跟随
服务器代理抓取长 URL 内容再返回给用户
服务器返回一个带链接的 HTML 页面等用户点击
客户端用 JS 轮询接口拿到长 URL 再跳转
why: 服务器查库拿到长 URL 后返回重定向响应（Location: 原始 URL），浏览器自动跳转——用户甚至不知道发生过一次重定向。
why_en: The server replies with an HTTP redirect carrying the long URL in the Location header, and the browser follows it automatically without the user noticing.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser
    participant S as Shortener
    participant DB as Mapping DB
    B->>S: GET /abc123
    S->>DB: lookup abc123
    DB-->>S: long_url
    S-->>B: 302 Location: long_url
    B->>B: follow redirect
options_en: The server replies with an HTTP redirect carrying a Location header, and the browser follows it automatically.
The server proxies and fetches the long URL's content, then returns it.
The server returns an HTML page with a link for the user to click.
The client polls an endpoint with JS to get the long URL, then navigates there.
optionMeanings: 标准 HTTP 重定向流程。
把短链服务当成代理服务器。
把重定向变成需要人工点击。
用轮询代替服务端重定向。
optionDirectness: 标准重定向让浏览器接手跳转，服务端只返回目标地址。
反向代理或网页抓取场景才会由服务端拉取内容。
需要人工确认离站时才会先返回带链接的页面。
异步等待结果的任务才适合客户端轮询。

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 重定向响应里指明跳转目标地址的响应头。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Location header in an HTTP redirect response tells the browser where to go next.

q: 在「浏览器是否缓存重定向」这个维度上，301 和 302 的区别是？
q_en: How do 301 and 302 differ in whether the browser caches the redirect?
options: 两者都会被浏览器缓存并跳过我们
302 会被缓存，301 反而不会
两者都不会被浏览器缓存
301 缓存后绕开我们，302 每次回源
why: 301 表示资源永久迁移，浏览器会记住并直接跳长 URL，流量绕开我们；302 表示临时位置，浏览器每次都先来问我们。这一个维度决定了控制权归属。
why_en: Browsers cache a permanent 301 and may skip our server on later visits, while a temporary 302 is not cached so every click still hits us.

rows: 后续可能绕过服务，难更新或统计
保留过期、修改和点击统计控制权

options_en: Both get cached by the browser and bypass us.
302 gets cached, but 301 does not.
Neither one gets cached by the browser.
A cached 301 bypasses us; a 302 always comes back to our server.
optionMeanings: 把两种重定向的缓存行为搞反或搞混。
把 301/302 的缓存关系说反了。
否认浏览器对重定向做任何缓存。
准确区分两者的缓存行为。
optionDirectness: 只有把永久和临时重定向都当成可缓存时才会这么判断。
这会把永久重定向和临时重定向的语义反过来。
调试环境可能禁用缓存，但不是浏览器默认语义。
短链控制权取决于 301 绕开服务端、302 回到服务端。
tradeoff: 301 让浏览器接管缓存换性能 vs 302 保留服务端控制权

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 301，表示资源永久搬走，浏览器通常会缓存这个跳转。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 301 signals a permanent move, and browsers typically cache that redirect.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 302，表示资源临时搬走，浏览器不缓存，每次都会回来问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 302 signals a temporary move, so browsers do not cache it and ask again each time.

scenario: 短链服务希望以后还能修改/过期链接，并保留统计每次点击的能力（即使分析暂时超纲）。
scenario_en: The URL shortener still wants the ability to update or expire links later and count every click, even if analytics is out of scope for now.
q: 重定向应该返回哪种状态码？
q_en: Which status code should the redirect return?
options: 301 Moved Permanently
302 Found（临时重定向）
200 OK
404 Not Found
why: 302 不被浏览器缓存，每次点击都经过我们的服务器：既保留了更新/过期链接的控制权，也保留了统计点击的能力，是短链的常规选择。
why_en: A 302 keeps every click flowing through our server, preserving control to update or expire links and the ability to count clicks.
whenOtherWins: 如果链接确定永不变更、且想靠浏览器缓存把延迟和服务器负载降到最低，301 更合适——代价是失去控制和统计。
options_en: 301 Moved Permanently.
302 Found, a temporary redirect.
404 Not Found.
optionMeanings: 永久重定向，浏览器会缓存跳转。
临时重定向，浏览器每次都回来问。
表示请求成功，不是跳转语义。
表示资源不存在。
optionDirectness: 目标永不变化且愿意让浏览器接管缓存时才选 301。
要保留修改、过期和点击统计能力时选 302。
返回页面内容而不是跳转时才用 200。
短码不存在或被删除时才返回 404。
tradeoff: 302 保留控制权和统计能力 vs 301 换浏览器缓存的性能

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 301，永久重定向，浏览器通常缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 301 is a permanent redirect that browsers typically cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 302，临时重定向，浏览器不缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 302 is a temporary redirect that browsers do not cache.

q: 如果短链服务用了 301，会带来什么后果？
q_en: What happens if the URL shortener uses a 301 redirect?
options: 浏览器缓存后跳长 URL，我们无法再更新/统计该短链
重定向响应本身会变得更慢
浏览器会拒绝执行这次跳转
数据库的写入压力会明显增大
why: 301 一旦被浏览器缓存，之后的请求绕开我们的服务器：想改目标、让链接过期、或统计点击都做不到了。这就是短链偏爱 302 的原因。
why_en: Once a 301 is cached, later clicks bypass our server entirely, so we lose the ability to change, expire, or track that short link.
options_en: The browser caches it and jumps straight to the long URL, so we lose the ability to update or track that link.
The redirect response itself becomes slower.
The browser refuses to follow the redirect.
Database write load rises noticeably.
optionMeanings: 301 缓存导致后续请求绕开服务器。
误以为状态码本身影响响应速度。
误以为 301 会被浏览器拒绝执行。
把重定向后果错误归到写路径。
optionDirectness: 301 缓存后，后续点击会绕开短链服务。
网络或服务端变慢时才会关注重定向响应耗时。
安全策略拦截或 URL 非法时，浏览器才可能拒绝跳转。
创建短链的写路径才会影响数据库写入压力。

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 301，永久重定向，浏览器通常会缓存这个跳转。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 301 is a permanent redirect that browsers typically cache.

q: 用户访问了一个已过期的短链，服务器应返回？
q_en: What should the server return when a user visits an expired short link?
options: 302 照常跳转
500 Internal Server Error
410 Gone
301 到首页
why: 服务器查库后会拿当前时间和过期时间比较；已过期的短链返回 410 Gone，语义是「资源曾存在但已永久失效」。
why_en: For an expired short link the server compares the current date to the stored expiration and returns a 410 Gone status.
options_en: Return a normal 302 redirect.
Return a 500 Internal Server Error.
Return 410 Gone.
Return a 301 redirect to the homepage.
optionMeanings: 把过期短链当正常短链处理。
把业务状态误判成服务器故障。
语义准确：资源曾存在但已失效。
用重定向到首页掩盖过期状态。
optionDirectness: 未过期且映射存在时才继续 302。
服务端异常或依赖故障时才用 500。
资源曾存在但现在失效时，410 的语义最贴合。
产品想兜底到首页时可这么做，但会丢失过期语义。

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 410，表示资源曾经存在，但已经永久不可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 410 Gone means the resource used to exist but is now permanently unavailable.

q: 把「创建短链」的处理流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the short-link creation flow in the correct order.
steps: 把短码（或别名）、长 URL、过期时间插入数据库
校验长 URL 格式（如 is-url 库）
生成短码；若用户给了自定义别名，先验证别名未被占用
把短 URL 返回给客户端
why: 顺序是：校验 → 生成短码（或用别名）→ 落库 → 返回。先校验能挡掉无效输入，短码生成是后面深挖的核心。
why_en: The creation flow validates the long URL, generates or accepts a short code, inserts the mapping into the database, and returns the short URL.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["客户端 POST /urls"] --> B["Primary Server
校验 URL 格式"] B --> C["生成短码 /
校验自定义别名"] C --> D[("数据库：短码→长URL
+过期时间")] D --> E["返回 short_url"]
tradeoff: 先校验挡掉脏输入 vs 先生成短码再校验的返工成本

q: 同一个长 URL 被多个用户提交时，为什么多数短链服务「不做去重」、允许多个短码指向同一长 URL？
q_en: Why do most URL shorteners avoid deduping the same long URL and allow multiple short codes for it?
options: 技术上做不到 URL 去重判断
不同用户想要各自的过期时间和别名，去重会丢掉这些功能
去重会让新短码和旧短码发生冲突
数据库无法按长 URL 做查询
why: 去重（同一长 URL 返回已有短码）省存储，但牺牲了按用户区分过期、分析和别名的能力。多数短链选择功能优先，不去重。
why_en: Most shorteners allow multiple codes per long URL because users may want separate expirations, analytics, or aliases, and deduplication trades those features for storage savings.
options_en: Deduplicating URLs is technically impossible.
Different users may want their own expiration and alias, and dedup would drop those features.
Deduplication causes new and old short codes to collide.
The database cannot query by long URL.
optionMeanings: 误判去重技术不可行。
点出去重牺牲的功能。
把去重和短码冲突混为一谈。
误判数据库查询能力。
optionDirectness: 数据量很小或离线批处理时，URL 去重技术上可行。
需要按用户保留别名、过期和分析时，不去重更合适。
短码冲突来自生成空间，不是长 URL 去重本身。
按 long_url 查重可以建索引，不是数据库能力问题。

scenario: 系统同时支持计数器生成的短码和用户自定义别名，担心未来某个计数器生成的短码恰好撞上已存在的自定义别名。
scenario_en: The system supports both counter-generated short codes and user-defined aliases, and you worry that a generated code could later collide with an existing alias.
q: 预防这种冲突的推荐做法是？
q_en: What is the recommended way to prevent this collision?
options: 每次生成短码后做一次全表扫描比对
干脆禁用自定义别名这个功能
让计数器从一个很大的数开始递增
给生成码加前缀、或用独立命名空间隔离两者
why: 用前缀字符或独立命名空间把「生成码」和「自定义别名」的取值空间隔开，两类短码天然不会相撞，无需运行时反复检查。
why_en: Prefix generated codes with a character custom aliases cannot use, or keep them in separate namespaces, so the two can never collide.
whenOtherWins: 如果别名功能流量极小，也可以只靠数据库 UNIQUE 约束兜底、冲突时报错重试——实现更简单，但把冲突留到了运行时。
options_en: Do a full table scan after generating every code to compare.
Just disable the custom alias feature entirely.
Start the counter from a very large number.
Prefix generated codes, or isolate them in a separate namespace from aliases.
optionMeanings: 用全表扫描代替命名空间隔离。
牺牲功能来规避冲突。
误以为起点够大就不会撞别名。
从取值空间上天然隔离两类短码。
optionDirectness: 表很小或离线校验时扫描还能接受，在线生成不适合。
产品决定取消别名时才算可行，但这改变了需求。
别名不受计数器大小约束，调大起点不能隔离空间。
前缀或命名空间让两类短码在生成前就分开。
tradeoff: 预先隔离取值空间 vs 运行时靠 UNIQUE 约束兜底重试

termDefinitions.meaning: 给不同来源的短码划分独立的取值范围，避免互相冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A namespace separates the value ranges of different code sources so they cannot collide.

q: 补全重定向的处理流程：
q_en: Fill in the redirect handling flow.
text: 浏览器发 GET /{short_code}；服务器在数据库里{{查找}}这个短码；找到且未{{过期}}（用当前时间对比过期时间）则取出长 URL，返回 {{302}} 重定向；已过期则返回 {{410}} Gone。
why: 重定向就是一次 key 查找加过期检查：命中未过期 → 302 跳转；过期 → 410。这条路径是全系统流量最大的路径，后面所有读优化都围绕它。
why_en: A redirect looks up the short code, checks the expiration date, and returns a 302 to the long URL or a 410 if the link has expired.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    Req["GET /{short_code}"] --> Lookup["按 short_code 查映射"]
    Lookup --> Found{"找到?"}
    Found -->|否| NotFound["404 Not Found"]
    Found -->|是| Expired{"已过期?"}
    Expired -->|是| Gone["410 Gone"]
    Expired -->|否| Redirect["302 Location: long_url"]

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 302，临时重定向状态码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 302 is the temporary-redirect status code.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 410 Gone，表示资源已永久失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 410 Gone means the resource is permanently unavailable.

q: 为什么所有短链请求天然会到达我们的服务器？
q_en: Why do all short-link requests naturally reach our server first?
options: 因为短链域名归我们所有，DNS 会把请求路由到我们的服务器
因为浏览器内置了处理短链的专属协议
因为我们在用户设备上预装了 SDK
因为用户的 ISP 做了特殊路由配置
why: 短链的关键前提：short.ly 是我们的域名，所以 short.ly/abc123 的每个请求都先落到我们的 Primary Server，我们才有机会查库并重定向。
why_en: Short URLs live on a domain we own, so every request to short dot l y naturally routes to our server where we can look up and redirect.
options_en: Because we own the short-link domain, DNS routes every request to our server.
Because browsers have a built-in protocol just for short links.
Because we preinstall an SDK on every user's device.
Because the user's ISP applies special routing rules.
optionMeanings: 域名所有权决定请求归属。
臆造一个不存在的浏览器协议。
臆造客户端需要预装 SDK。
把路由责任错误推给 ISP。
optionDirectness: 拥有短链域名时，DNS 会把请求导向我们的入口。
浏览器只需要普通 HTTP，不需要短链专属协议。
移动端深链或埋点 SDK 场景才依赖客户端组件。
运营商只负责网络传输，不决定应用层短码解析。

termDefinitions.meaning: 域名系统，把域名解析成服务器地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS resolves a domain name into the server address that should handle the request.

q: 关于过期短链的清理，文章推荐的做法是？
q_en: What is the recommended cleanup approach for expired short links?
options: 每次读请求都同步扫描并删除所有过期行
永远不清理，让过期行一直留在表里
后台定期清理，TTL 设为 ≤ URL 过期时间
把清理工作交给用户手动删除
why: 清理走后台批处理即可，不占用请求路径；更关键的是缓存 TTL 要不长于 URL 过期时间，否则缓存里会残留已过期的映射继续跳转。
why_en: Clean up expired rows with a periodic background job and set cache TTLs at or below URL expiration so stale entries evict themselves.
options_en: Synchronously scan and delete all expired rows on every read request.
Never clean up, leaving expired rows in the table forever.
Run a periodic cleanup job, and cap TTL at or below the URL's expiration.
Make users delete their own expired links manually.
optionMeanings: 把清理放进请求路径，拖慢读延迟。
完全不清理，数据只增不减。
后台批处理 + TTL 对齐，两头兼顾。
把运维责任转嫁给用户。
optionDirectness: 强实时删除要求才会把清理放近请求路径，但读延迟会受影响。
只读审计归档才可能长期保留，在线表不适合无限增长。
后台批处理避开读路径，TTL 对齐防止缓存继续跳转。
用户自助删除适合管理入口，不适合作为系统清理机制。

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cache entry lives before it must be refreshed.

q: Bitly 高层设计的三个核心组件及其职责，哪些描述正确？（多选）
q_en: Which descriptions correctly match the three core components in Bitly's high-level design?
options: Client：用户通过 Web/移动端与系统交互
Primary Server：接收请求，处理短码创建、校验等业务逻辑
Database：存短码到长 URL 的映射、别名和过期时间
Message Queue：所有读请求先排队
why: 最初的高层设计只需要三件套：客户端、承载业务逻辑的主服务器、存映射的数据库。消息队列在这个问题里并不需要——读是同步重定向。
why_en: The high-level design is just a client, a primary server holding the business logic, and a database storing the code-to-URL mappings.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client Web/Mobile"] -->|POST create url| Server["Primary Server"]
    Client -->|GET short code| Server
    Server -->|create / lookup| DB[("Mapping DB")]
    Server -->|short_url or 302| Client
options_en: Client: users interact with the system through web or mobile.
Primary Server: receives requests and handles business logic like code creation and validation.
Database: stores the mapping of short codes to long URLs, aliases, and expiration dates.
Message Queue: every read request is queued first.
optionMeanings: 客户端入口。
承载业务逻辑的服务层。
持久化映射数据的存储层。
臆造一个排队组件。
optionDirectness: 正确，是三件套里的客户端。
正确，是三件套里的服务器。
正确，是三件套里的数据库。
错误，读请求走的是同步重定向。

q: 设计短码生成方案时要同时满足哪些约束？（多选）
q_en: Which constraints must a short-code generation scheme satisfy at the same time?
options: 短码必须唯一
短码要尽可能短（毕竟是短链服务）
生成要高效（不能拖慢写入）
短码必须包含原 URL 的语义信息
why: 三条约束：唯一、短、高效——而且三者互相牵制（更长更不易撞但不「短」，查重保唯一但不「高效」）。语义可读性不是要求。
why_en: Short-code generation must balance three competing constraints: uniqueness, shortness, and efficient generation.
options_en: The short code must be unique.
The short code should be as short as possible.
Generation must be efficient and not slow down writes.
The short code must carry semantic meaning from the original URL.
optionMeanings: 唯一性约束。
长度约束。
生成效率约束。
臆造一个可读性约束。
optionDirectness: 正确，唯一性是硬约束。
正确，长度是短链服务的卖点。
正确，效率关系到写入体验。
错误，文章从未要求语义可读。

q: 「直接取长 URL 的前 N 个字符当短码」这个方案为什么不可行？
q_en: Why is taking the first N characters of the long URL as the short code not viable?
options: 这种前缀方案生成短码的速度太慢
共享前缀的 URL 会映射到同一短码，破坏唯一性
前缀字符串没法做 base62 编码
浏览器不认识这种格式的短码
why: 比如所有 www.linkedin.com/in/... 的链接前 8 个字符都一样，会全部撞到同一个短码上——违反第一条约束「唯一」，方案直接出局。
why_en: Taking a URL prefix fails because any two URLs sharing the first characters map to the same code, destroying uniqueness.
options_en: This prefix approach is too slow at generating codes.
URLs sharing a prefix collapse onto the same short code, breaking uniqueness.
A prefix string cannot be Base62 encoded.
Browsers do not recognize this short-code format.
optionMeanings: 把问题错误归为生成速度。
点出根本问题：唯一性被破坏。
臆造一个编码限制。
臆造浏览器兼容性问题。
optionDirectness: 生成速度不是前缀方案的瓶颈。
大量 URL 共享域名前缀时，前缀方案会直接撞码。
编码层通常能处理字符串，问题不在 Base62。
浏览器只看 URL 是否合法，不理解短码生成算法。

q: 为什么不直接用随机数生成器（如 Math.random()）生成短码？
q_en: Why not generate short codes directly with a random number generator such as Math.random()?
options: 生成一个随机数太耗费 CPU 资源
随机数结果没法用 base62 编码表示
随机数生成器只能产出偶数结果
熵不够，规模变大后短码碰撞概率会明显上升
why: 普通随机数生成器熵不够，存量 URL 增多后重复概率显著上升，每次都要查库验重。哈希函数的高熵输出是更好的「随机性来源」。
why_en: A plain random number generator lacks enough entropy to keep codes unique at scale, so collisions become likely as the URL count grows.
options_en: Generating a random number costs too much CPU.
A random number cannot be represented in Base62.
Random number generators only produce even numbers.
It lacks enough entropy, so collision probability rises noticeably as scale grows.
optionMeanings: 臆造 CPU 成本问题。
臆造编码限制。
臆造随机数只能是偶数。
熵不足，点出真实原因。
optionDirectness: CPU 成本通常不是生成短码的主要限制。
数字可以正常转成 Base62，编码不是瓶颈。
随机数分布不会被限制成只出偶数。
规模变大时，低熵随机值会带来更高碰撞率。

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量一个输出有多随机、多不可预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Entropy measures how random and unpredictable an output is.

q: 用 SHA-256 这类哈希函数生成短码，它提供的关键性质是？
q_en: What key properties does a hash function such as SHA-256 provide for short-code generation?
options: 确定性、固定长度输出、高熵（很少但不是零碰撞）
哈希输出保证绝对不会发生碰撞
哈希输出天然只有 6 个字符长
可以从哈希值直接反解出原始 URL
why: 哈希三性质：确定性、定长、高熵。注意它只是「很少」碰撞而非「不会」碰撞——这正是后面要处理的挑战。
why_en: A hash function gives determinism, a fixed-size output, and high entropy, though collisions are still possible rather than impossible.
options_en: Determinism, fixed-length output, and high entropy, though collisions are rare rather than impossible.
Hash output is guaranteed to never collide.
Hash output is naturally only six characters long.
You can reverse a hash value straight back to the original URL.
optionMeanings: 哈希函数的三条真实性质。
夸大成零碰撞保证。
臆造固定 6 字符长度。
误以为哈希可逆。
optionDirectness: 哈希适合把任意 URL 映射成稳定、高熵输出。
密码学哈希能降低碰撞概率，但不能给零碰撞承诺。
短码长度来自截断和编码策略，不是 SHA-256 天生 6 位。
需要可逆映射时不能只存哈希，必须保留数据库映射。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任意输入转换成固定长度、确定性输出的函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash function deterministically maps any input to a fixed-length output.

scenario: 你把哈希输出变成短码，但短码要能安全放在 URL path 里，并尽量紧凑。
scenario_en: You are turning hash output into a short code that must be compact and safe to place inside a URL path.
q: 应该使用哪种编码更合适？
q_en: Which encoding is the better fit?
options: Base64，直接保留 + 和 / 两个符号
十六进制，因为它的字符集最大
Base62：a-z/A-Z/0-9，避开 URL 里的特殊字符
原始二进制字节，直接拼进 URL
why: Base62 比十六进制更紧凑，同时避开 Base64 里的 / 和 +；前者会和路径分隔冲突，后者在查询串里可能被解释为空格。
why_en: Base62 is compact and URL-safe because it avoids Base64 characters like slash and plus.
whenOtherWins: 如果短码不放在 URL path 中，而是内部二进制 token，原始 bytes 或 Base64URL 也可能更合适。
options_en: Base64, keeping the plus and slash characters as-is.
Hexadecimal, because it has the largest character set.
Base62 using a-z, A-Z, 0-9, avoiding special characters in URLs.
Raw binary bytes appended directly to the URL.
optionMeanings: 误判 Base64 对 URL path 安全。
把字符集大小和合适性搞混。
紧凑且 URL 安全的编码方式。
把不可打印字节直接放进 URL。
optionDirectness: Base64URL 变体才适合 URL，原始 Base64 的 / 和 + 会添麻烦。
十六进制适合调试可读性，但相同信息会更长。
短码放在 path 里时，Base62 兼顾紧凑和 URL 安全。
内部 token 可以用二进制，直接拼进 URL 不合适。
tradeoff: 更紧凑的编码 vs 更大字符集但更长的编码

termDefinitions.meaning: 只用 a-z、A-Z、0-9 共 62 个字符表示数字的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Base62 represents numbers using only the 62 letters and digits a-z, A-Z, and 0-9.

q: 补全 Base62 的字符集选择：
q_en: Fill in the character set used by Base62.
why: 短链码通常出现在 URL path 里，字符越紧凑越好，但不能引入 path separator 或容易被转义的字符。
why_en: Base62 uses letters and digits while excluding URL-problematic slash and plus characters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 62 个字母数字字符表示数字，不含 / 和 + 。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Base62 encodes numbers using 62 letters and digits, excluding slash and plus.

q: 这对短码位数和碰撞处理策略意味着什么？
q_en: What does this imply for short-code length and collision handling?
options: 必须每次生成都改用 16 位短码才安全
编码空间足够大，可以完全跳过数据库唯一约束检查
218 万亿远超存量，8 位短码够用很久，约束+重试兜底
存量增长后应立刻切换到 UUID 作为短码
why: 218 万亿远超十亿级存量，8 位 Base62 短码空间还够用很久；仍要靠 UNIQUE 约束兜底碰撞，但不必现在就加长短码。
why_en: 218 trillion possible codes dwarf a billion-URL scale, so 8-character Base62 codes have plenty of headroom and still need a UNIQUE constraint as the collision safety net.
scenario: 8 位 Base62 编码给出约 62^8 ≈ 218 万亿种组合，你的服务当前存量约几十亿条短链。
scenario_en: Eight Base62 characters give about 62^8, or roughly 218 trillion combinations, while your service stores only a few billion short links today.
options_en: We must switch to 16-character codes right away for safety.
The code space is big enough that we can skip the database uniqueness check.
218 trillion dwarfs the current scale, so 8 characters last a long time with a constraint plus retries as the backstop.
We should switch to UUID short codes as soon as the count grows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 62 个字母数字字符表示数字的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Base62 encodes numbers using 62 letters and digits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库约束，保证某列的值不会重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UNIQUE constraint stops a database column from holding duplicate values.

q: 截取哈希前 N 位作为短码的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of truncating the first N characters of a hash as the short code?
options: 同一个 URL 每次哈希会得到不同结果
N 越短编码空间越小，存量变多后碰撞概率上升
哈希后的结果没法做 Base62 编码
生成的短码没办法存进数据库
why: 哈希输出高熵但不是无限空间；截断后只有固定大小的 code space，随着已有 code 数量增加，新 code 撞上的概率约为 n / |S|。
why_en: Truncating a hash limits the code space, so collision probability rises as more codes are stored.
options_en: Hashing the same URL twice gives a different result each time.
The shorter N is, the smaller the code space, so collision odds rise as more codes are stored.
A hash output cannot be Base62 encoded.
The generated short code cannot be saved to the database.
optionMeanings: 误判哈希函数是非确定性的。
点出截断带来的空间缩小问题。
臆造编码限制。
臆造存储限制。
optionDirectness: 加随机盐前，同一 URL 的哈希输出应该稳定。
截断让可用空间变小，存量越大越容易撞码。
哈希字节可以继续做 Base62 或其他编码。
短码是普通字符串，数据库存储不是主要风险。

scenario: 你采用哈希截断生成短码，数据库插入时发现 short_code 已存在。
scenario_en: You generate short codes by truncating a hash, and a database insert finds that the short_code already exists.
q: 最合理的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable way to handle this?
options: 直接覆盖掉已存在的旧映射
忽略这次冲突错误，照样返回该短码
先把旧的那条 URL 记录删掉
靠 UNIQUE 约束捕获冲突，加盐重试
why: 唯一约束是最终防线；冲突时用 salt/nonce 改变输入后重试，既保证唯一性，也避免把两个长 URL 指到同一个短码。
why_en: A unique constraint catches collisions, and bounded retries with a salt or nonce produce a different code safely.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务明确要求同一长 URL 永远复用同一短码，可以先做 canonical URL 查重并返回旧记录，而不是生成新码。
options_en: Overwrite the existing mapping directly.
Ignore the conflict error and return that code anyway.
Delete the old URL record first.
Let the UNIQUE constraint catch the conflict and retry with a salt.
optionMeanings: 覆盖会破坏别人已有的短链。
忽略冲突会让两条 URL 共用一个短码。
误删无关用户的数据。
唯一约束兜底 + 加盐重试。
optionDirectness: 覆盖只适合显式更新同一用户自己的短链。
忽略冲突会让一个短码指向两个不同目标。
删除旧记录会破坏已经发出去的短链。
唯一约束捕获冲突后，加盐重试能保住唯一性。
tradeoff: 运行时唯一约束兜底 vs 提前隔离取值空间

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库列级约束，插入重复值时会报错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UNIQUE constraint makes the database reject an insert that would duplicate an existing value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加进哈希输入的额外随机值，让同一输入能产生不同哈希结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A salt or nonce is extra randomness mixed into a hash input so the same input can produce a different output.

q: 哈希方案和递增计数器方案的关键取舍有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which tradeoffs matter between hash-based and incrementing-counter short-code generation?
options: 哈希方案可能碰撞，需要唯一约束和重试
计数器天然唯一，但需要全局协调计数值
计数器短码可能可预测，存在枚举风险
哈希方案不需要任何数据库写入
why: 哈希的难点是碰撞和查重；计数器的难点是协调和可预测性。两者都需要把 short_code 到 long_url 的映射写入持久存储。
why_en: Hashing trades collision handling for less coordination, while counters trade uniqueness for coordination and predictability concerns.

rows: 无需全局序列，输出高熵
可能碰撞，依赖 UNIQUE + 重试

tradeoff: 哈希省协调但可能碰撞 vs 计数器唯一但需全局协调
options_en: Hashing can collide, so it needs a uniqueness constraint and retries.
A counter is naturally unique, but requires global coordination of the counter value.
Counter-based codes can be predictable, creating an enumeration risk.
Hashing needs no database writes at all.
optionMeanings: 哈希方案的代价：碰撞处理。
计数器方案的代价：全局协调。
计数器方案的代价：可预测性。
臆造哈希方案不用写库。
optionDirectness: 正确，这是哈希方案的碰撞代价。
正确，这是计数器方案的协调代价。
正确，这是计数器方案的隐私代价。
错误，两种方案都要把映射写入数据库。

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局递增的整数序列，每次取值都不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter is a globally incrementing integer sequence that yields a new value each time.

scenario: 你想完全避免短码碰撞，并且写入量并不高，可以接受一个全局序列来源。
scenario_en: You want to avoid short-code collisions entirely, write volume is low, and a global sequence source is acceptable.
q: 哪种短码生成方式最直接？
q_en: Which short-code generation method is the most straightforward fit?
options: 直接截取原始 URL 的前 N 个字符
取全局递增 counter，再做 Base62 编码
让每台应用服务器各自从 0 开始计数
每次随机生成一个 2 位短码
why: 全局递增 counter 每次返回不同整数，再 Base62 后得到紧凑短码，天然避免碰撞。关键是 counter 必须全局唯一，而不能每台机器各算各的。
why_en: A global incrementing counter encoded with Base62 produces compact codes with no collisions.
whenOtherWins: 如果不能接受可预测短码，或希望同一 URL 的短码由内容确定，哈希加盐方案会更自然。
options_en: Take the first N characters of the original URL directly.
Take a global incrementing counter value and Base62-encode it.
Let each application server count up from zero on its own.
Randomly generate a 2-character code each time.
optionMeanings: 前缀方案会撞车，唯一性没保证。
全局唯一序列 + 紧凑编码。
各实例各算各的，会互相冲突。
2 位空间太小，碰撞几乎必然。
optionDirectness: 前缀方案只在输入天然互不相似时才勉强可用。
全局计数器给每次写入一个不同整数，适合零碰撞目标。
单机本地计数只适合单实例系统，多实例会重复。
极小码空间只适合玩具系统或测试数据。
tradeoff: 计数器零碰撞 vs 需要一个全局协调的序列来源

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局递增的整数序列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counter is a globally incrementing integer sequence.

q: Redis 为什么适合做全局 counter？
q_en: Why is Redis a good fit for a global counter?
options: Redis 的 INCR 是原子操作，能为并发请求返回不同值
Redis 会自动把短码写入 Postgres
Redis 只能单用户访问，所以没有并发
Redis 不需要持久化任何状态
why: Redis 单线程处理命令且 INCR 原子递增；两个并发请求不会拿到同一个 counter 值。这正好解决多个 Write Service 实例共享序列的问题。
why_en: Redis INCR is atomic, so concurrent writers receive distinct counter values from one shared sequence.
options_en: Redis's INCR is atomic, so concurrent requests always get distinct values.
Redis automatically writes short codes into Postgres.
Redis only allows single-user access, so there is no concurrency.
Redis needs no persisted state at all.
optionMeanings: 原子自增，天然避免竞态。
臆造 Redis 自动写别的数据库。
误判 Redis 不支持并发访问。
误判计数器不需要持久化。
optionDirectness: 多个写实例共享序列时，原子 INCR 可以避免重复值。
写数据库映射仍由应用服务负责，Redis 不会自动同步。
Redis 单线程执行命令，但可以服务很多并发客户端。
计数器状态必须可靠保存，否则重启后可能重复发号。

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令，并发调用也不会返回重复值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is Redis's atomic increment command, so concurrent calls never return the same value.

q: 补全 counter + Base62 的容量直觉：
q_en: Fill in the capacity intuition for counter plus Base62 short codes.
text: {{1B}} 个 URL 用 Base62 表示仍约为 {{6}} 个字符；到 {{62^6}}（约 560 亿）才需要进入 7 位。
why: counter 方案的短码长度会随规模增长，但 10 亿级仍很短。这个数字能反驳“递增 ID 一定很长”的误解。
why_en: One billion counter values still fit in about six Base62 characters, so counter-generated codes remain short.
scenario: 产品团队担心用户量长期增长后，counter 生成的短码会变得越来越长、不好分享。
scenario_en: The product team worries that as usage grows, counter-generated short codes will become too long to share.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 62 个字母数字字符表示数字的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Base62 encodes numbers using 62 letters and digits.

q: 递增 counter 生成短码的安全/隐私风险是什么？
q_en: What security or privacy risk comes from using an incrementing counter for short codes?
options: 递增计数器一定会产生短码碰撞
攻击者能枚举相邻短码，挖到未公开分享的 URL
生成的短码没办法被浏览器打开
数据库没法按 counter 值做查询
why: 连续 ID 经过 Base62 后仍可能被猜到相邻值，攻击者可以遍历短码。可用 secret XOR/可逆混淆、随机化范围或接受公共分享语义来权衡。
why_en: Sequential counters can make codes enumerable, so an attacker may discover nearby URLs unless the sequence is obfuscated.
options_en: An incrementing counter is guaranteed to cause short-code collisions.
An attacker can enumerate nearby codes and discover URLs that were never shared publicly.
The generated short code cannot be opened in a browser.
The database cannot query by the counter value.
optionMeanings: 误判计数器方案会碰撞。
点出可预测性带来的枚举风险。
臆造短码浏览器不兼容。
臆造 counter 列无法查询。
optionDirectness: 只有多个计数器没有协调时，counter 才可能重复。
短码可预测时，攻击者可以尝试相邻值枚举。
浏览器只需要合法 URL 字符，递增来源不影响打开。
counter 可以作为普通列查询，不是数据库限制。

scenario: 重定向请求拿到 short_code 后，要在 10 亿行映射表里快速找到 long_url。
scenario_en: A redirect request receives a short_code and must quickly find its long_url in a billion-row mapping table.
q: 数据库表上最关键的设计是什么？
q_en: What is the most important database table design for this lookup?
options: 把 short_code 设为主键或至少建唯一索引
每次全表扫描查找 short_code
只按 long_url 建索引
把所有字段存成一个 JSON 字符串且不建索引
why: short_code 是读取路径的查找键，把它设为 primary key/unique index 既保证唯一，又把查询从全表扫描变成索引查找。
why_en: Indexing short_code, usually as the primary key, gives fast lookup and enforces uniqueness.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询模式主要是按 user_id 列出某用户创建的所有短链，还需要额外的 user_id 索引，但重定向路径仍看 short_code。
options_en: Make short_code the primary key or at least add a unique index on it.
Do a full table scan for short_code on every lookup.
Only index long_url.
Store every field as one JSON string with no index at all.
optionMeanings: 把查找键做成索引，O(log n) 查找。
放弃索引，退化成线性扫描。
索引建在了不参与查找的列上。
既失去结构化查询也失去索引。
optionDirectness: 重定向路径以 short_code 为 key，主键或唯一索引匹配这个访问模式。
全表扫描只适合很小的表或离线任务。
按 long_url 查询适合去重，不服务重定向主路径。
JSON blob 适合少量灵活字段，不适合高频 key lookup。
tradeoff: 索引查找的存储/写入代价 vs 全表扫描的读延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 表里能唯一标识一行、且自动带索引的列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary key is the column that uniquely identifies a row and is automatically indexed.

q: 没有 short_code 索引时，重定向查找会退化成什么？
q_en: What does redirect lookup degrade into without an index on short_code?
options: 退化成 O(1) 的内存直接读取
退化成 full table scan，逐行检查
退化成自动命中 CDN 边缘节点
退化成只读一行元数据就返回
why: 没有索引，数据库只能扫描映射表找匹配 short_code；数据到百万/十亿级后，这会直接破坏 <100ms 重定向目标。
why_en: Without an index, redirect lookup becomes a full table scan, which is too slow at large scale.
options_en: It degrades to an O(1) in-memory read.
It degrades to a full table scan, checking rows one by one.
It degrades to automatically hitting a CDN edge node.
It degrades to reading just one metadata row and returning.
optionMeanings: 把没有索引的后果说反了。
没索引就只能逐行比对。
把数据库查找和 CDN 命中混为一谈。
臆造只读一行就能返回结果。
optionDirectness: O(1) 更像内存哈希表或缓存命中，不是无索引数据库查找。
没有索引时，数据库只能逐行找匹配 short_code。
CDN 命中发生在数据库之前，不能替代表内索引。
缺索引时无法直接定位单行，需要扫描候选行。

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐行检查整张表来找匹配数据，没有索引时的默认方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full table scan checks every row in a table to find matches, the default when there is no index.

q: 仅靠给 short_code 建索引，能撑住这个峰值吗？不能的话下一步是什么？
q_en: Can an index on short_code alone handle this peak, and if not, what comes next?
options: 能撑住，索引已经让查找变成 O(log n)，足够应对任何峰值
撑不住，应该放弃索引换成全表扫描
撑不住，应该把 short_code 改得更短来提速
撑不住，需要在数据库前加内存缓存，把大部分读挡在数据库外
why: 索引把查找降到 O(log n)，但单实例 IOPS 撑不住 60 万级峰值读；下一步是在数据库前加内存缓存。
why_en: Indexing brings lookups down to O(log n), but a single instance's IOPS cannot absorb a 600k-QPS peak, so the next step is an in-memory cache in front of the database.
scenario: 峰值场景下重定向读 QPS 能到 60 万级别，而单个数据库实例配合索引大约能扛约 10 万 IOPS。
scenario_en: At peak, redirect reads can reach about 600k QPS, while one indexed database instance handles roughly 100k IOPS.
options_en: Yes, the index already makes lookups O(log n), which is enough for any peak.
No, so we should drop the index and use a full table scan instead.
No, so we should shorten short_code further to speed things up.
No, we need an in-memory cache in front of the database to absorb most reads before they hit it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒输入输出操作数，衡量存储设备的读写吞吐能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IOPS is input/output operations per second, a measure of storage throughput.

q: 补全读流量估算：
q_en: Fill in the read-traffic estimate.
text: {{100M}} DAU * 每人每天 {{5}} 次重定向 = {{500M}} 次/天，平均约 {{5.8k}} QPS；若按 100x 峰值，要设计到约 {{600k}} read/s。
why: 这个估算解释了为什么只靠数据库索引还不够：平均值可控，但峰值读流量非常高，需要缓存和边缘层分担。
why_en: The traffic estimate shows why indexed database reads still need caching for peak redirect load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量系统需要承受的请求速率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is queries per second, the rate of requests a system must handle.

scenario: 短链读写比约 1000:1，热门短码会被反复点击，数据库索引仍可能扛不住峰值读。
scenario_en: The URL shortener has about a 1000:1 read-write ratio, popular short codes are clicked repeatedly, and database indexes may still fail under peak reads.
q: 应在应用和数据库之间加入什么？
q_en: What should be added between the application and the database?
options: 加一层内存缓存，存短码到长链的映射
加一个只处理写入的 Kafka topic
上线一套更复杂的登录系统
每次请求都重新生成一遍短码
why: 读重系统的第一层优化是缓存映射：命中时直接从内存返回 long_url，miss 再查数据库并回填缓存。
why_en: An in-memory cache stores short-code mappings so popular redirects avoid database reads.
whenOtherWins: 如果读量很低、数据量很小，单库索引可能已经足够，先加缓存反而增加运维复杂度。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client"] --> Read["Read Service"]
    Read --> Cache[("Redis / Memcached")]
    Cache -->|hit| Redirect["302 redirect"]
    Cache -->|miss| DB[("Mapping DB")]
    DB --> Fill["fill cache"]
    Fill --> Redirect
options_en: Add an in-memory cache layer that stores the short-code-to-long-URL mapping.
Add a Kafka topic that only handles writes.
Ship a more elaborate login system.
Regenerate the short code on every single request.
optionMeanings: 命中时直接从内存返回，miss 再查库回填。
队列解决的是写入异步化，不是读延迟。
登录系统与重定向读性能无关。
重新生成短码会破坏已有映射。
optionDirectness: 热门映射反复读取时，内存缓存能挡住大部分数据库读。
写入异步化适合写路径瓶颈，不解决同步重定向读压力。
登录系统解决身份问题，不会降低 short_code 查找延迟。
短码必须稳定映射，按请求重生成会破坏链接语义。
tradeoff: 缓存换读延迟 vs 引入失效和预热复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里没有目标数据，必须回源查数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache miss means the data is absent from cache and must be fetched from the database.

q: 按正确顺序排列一次缓存 miss 的重定向流程：
q_en: Put the redirect flow for a cache miss in the correct order.
steps: 把查到的 short_code -> long_url 映射写回缓存
请求到达 Read Service，先查 Redis/Memcached
缓存未命中，Read Service 查询数据库索引
返回 302 Redirect 到 long_url
why: cache-aside 路径是先查缓存，miss 再查库，随后回填缓存并完成重定向。这样热门短码后续请求会直接命中缓存。
why_en: The cache-aside flow checks cache first, reads the database on a miss, fills the cache, and then redirects.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant R as Read Service
  participant Cache as Cache
  participant DB as DB
  C->>R: GET /{code}
  R->>Cache: get(code)
  Cache-->>R: miss
  R->>DB: lookup(code)
  DB-->>R: long_url
  R->>Cache: set(code, long_url)
  R-->>C: 302 Location
tradeoff: 先查缓存省数据库负载 vs 缓存未命中时多一跳查库延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，未命中时再查数据库并回填缓存的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside means the app checks the cache first and, on a miss, reads the database and fills the cache.

q: 这个量级差距最支持哪条缓存设计判断？
q_en: Which cache design decision is best supported by this order-of-magnitude latency gap?
options: SSD 已经够快，不需要再引入内存缓存
HDD 和内存的访问延迟差距可以忽略不计
把热点 short_code 映射放进内存缓存，能带来数量级的读延迟收益
只要全部换成 SSD 就能达到内存缓存的效果
why: 内存比 SSD 快约 1000 倍、比 HDD 快约 10 万倍，这个量级差距正是给热点重定向加内存缓存的理由。
why_en: Memory is roughly 1,000 times faster than SSD and 100,000 times faster than HDD, and that gap is exactly why hot redirects deserve an in-memory cache.
scenario: 内存访问约 100 纳秒，SSD 约 0.1 毫秒，HDD 约 10 毫秒，量级依次拉开。
scenario_en: Memory access is about 100 nanoseconds, SSD is about 0.1 milliseconds, and HDD is about 10 milliseconds.
options_en: SSD is already fast enough, so there's no need to add an in-memory cache.
The latency gap between HDD and memory is negligible.
Putting hot short_code mappings in an in-memory cache buys an order-of-magnitude latency win.
Switching everything to SSD alone matches what an in-memory cache gives you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒输入输出操作数，衡量存储设备吞吐能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IOPS is input/output operations per second, a measure of storage throughput.

q: 引入内存缓存后要主动处理哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: Which issues must you actively handle after adding an in-memory cache?
options: 缓存预热，冷启动时 miss 仍会打到数据库
缓存失效，尤其是 URL 过期或删除后不能返回旧 long_url
容量和淘汰策略，如 LRU
所有写入都必须停止
why: 缓存提升读性能，但带来预热、失效、容量和淘汰策略。短链较少更新，失效难度比通用可变数据低，但过期时间必须和 TTL 对齐。
why_en: Caching adds warmup, invalidation, capacity, and eviction concerns even in a mostly read-heavy URL shortener.
options_en: Cache warmup: on a cold start, misses still hit the database.
Invalidation: an expired or deleted URL must not keep returning the old long_url.
Capacity and eviction policy, such as LRU.
All writes must stop.
optionMeanings: 冷启动阶段还没缓存住的数据。
过期/删除后缓存要跟着失效。
内存有限，得选谁被淘汰。
臆造缓存要求暂停写入。
optionDirectness: 冷启动或节点重启时，预热决定数据库会不会被 miss 打爆。
链接过期或删除时，失效策略决定是否会返回旧 long_url。
内存有限时，淘汰策略决定哪些热门短码能留在缓存里。
写入可以继续落库，缓存不要求暂停所有写入。

scenario: 短链支持 expiration_date，某个 short_code 已经过期，但缓存里还有旧映射。
scenario_en: Short links support expiration_date, and one short_code has already expired while the cache still holds the old mapping.
q: 缓存 TTL 应该如何设置？
q_en: How should the cache TTL be set?
options: 永不过期，减少数据库访问
TTL 应等于或短于 URL 剩余过期时间
统一设置成 10 年
只在客户端浏览器缓存
why: 缓存项不能活得比 URL 本身更久，否则过期短链仍可能被重定向。TTL 对齐 expiration_date 是最直接的防 stale 策略。
why_en: Cache TTL must not outlive the URL expiration time or expired links can keep redirecting.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务不支持过期或删除，长 TTL 更可接受；如果要求立即撤销，还需要主动失效或版本化。
options_en: Never expire the cache entry, to cut database access.
TTL should be equal to or shorter than the URL's remaining time to expiration.
Set every TTL to a flat 10 years.
Only cache it in the client's browser.
optionMeanings: 永不过期会让缓存活得比 URL 还久。
TTL 对齐过期时间，防止残留。
10 年等同于变相的永不过期。
把问题转移到客户端而非解决它。
optionDirectness: 没有过期语义的静态数据才适合永不过期缓存。
TTL 不超过 URL 剩余寿命，缓存就不会比短链活得更久。
十年 TTL 只适合近似永久资源，不适合会过期的短链。
浏览器缓存只能减少客户端请求，不能修服务端旧映射。
tradeoff: TTL 越短越新鲜 vs TTL 越长数据库压力越小

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cache entry lives before it must be refreshed.

scenario: 用户分布全球，热门短码希望尽量靠近用户完成重定向，减少跨区域往返。
scenario_en: Users are global, and popular short codes should redirect as close to the user as possible to reduce cross-region round trips.
q: 可以引入哪一层优化？
q_en: Which optimization layer can be introduced?
options: CDN 边缘节点直接执行重定向逻辑
只是把数据库磁盘容量调大
让用户手动复制粘贴 long_url
把所有请求都固定发到单一区域主库
why: CDN PoP 可以缓存热门 short_code 映射，edge function 甚至能直接返回 redirect，避免请求回源到 Primary Server。
why_en: A CDN and edge function can serve popular redirects near users without reaching the origin service.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户集中在单区域、延迟目标宽松或成本敏感，应用层缓存可能已经足够，不必先上边缘计算。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    User["Global user"] --> Edge["CDN PoP / Edge function"]
    Edge -->|hit| Redirect["302 near user"]
    Edge -->|miss| Origin["Origin Read Service"]
    Origin --> Store[("origin cache / DB")]
    Origin --> Edge
options_en: A CDN with edge nodes running the redirect logic directly.
Just increase the database's disk capacity.
Have users manually copy and paste the long_url.
Route every request to a single-region primary database.
optionMeanings: 把重定向逻辑搬到离用户最近的边缘。
磁盘容量和跨区域延迟无关。
牺牲产品体验来规避问题。
单区域架构反而加剧跨洲延迟。
optionDirectness: 全球用户访问热门短码时，边缘节点能减少回源距离。
磁盘容量不足时才扩容磁盘，不会解决跨区 RTT。
人工复制只适合临时绕过，不是短链产品体验。
单一区域主库适合简单部署，但会放大全球访问延迟。
tradeoff: 边缘就近响应换低延迟 vs 边缘失效/运维复杂度和成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 运行在 CDN 边缘节点上的代码，能在离用户最近的地方处理请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge function is code that runs on CDN edge nodes, handling requests close to the user.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN 在某个地理位置部署的边缘接入点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PoP (point of presence) is a CDN's edge location in a given geographic area.

q: CDN/edge redirect 的代价包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What costs come with CDN or edge redirects?
options: 全局缓存失效和一致性更复杂
边缘函数有执行时间、内存和依赖限制
调试和监控比中心化服务更难
它会让所有短码立刻变长
why: 边缘层用成本和复杂度换延迟：失效、资源限制、观测性和费用都要讨论。它不会改变短码本身长度。
why_en: Edge redirects trade latency for more complex invalidation, runtime limits, monitoring, and cost.
options_en: Global cache invalidation and consistency become more complex.
Edge functions have execution time, memory, and dependency limits.
Debugging and monitoring are harder than with a centralized service.
It makes every short code instantly longer.
optionMeanings: 多节点失效同步的真实成本。
边缘运行时的真实资源限制。
分布式边缘的可观测性成本。
臆造边缘计算改变短码长度。
optionDirectness: 正确，这是失效同步的真实代价。
正确，这是边缘运行时的真实代价。
正确，这是可观测性的真实代价。
错误，短码长度和部署位置无关。

q: 这个存储量级对数据库架构选择意味着什么？
q_en: What does this storage size imply for the database architecture choice?
options: 500GB 已经远超单机容量，必须从第一天就做分片
500GB 现代 SSD/单实例数据库能轻松容纳，不必一开始就做分片
这个量级下必须放弃关系型数据库，改用列式存储
存储量级这么大，建索引已经没有意义
why: 500GB 对现代 SSD 和单个数据库实例都不是问题；除非真的碰到硬件瓶颈，否则不必一开始就分片。
why_en: 500 GB is not a problem for a modern SSD or a single database instance, so sharding isn't necessary until a real hardware limit shows up.
scenario: 按每行约 500 bytes 估算，10 亿条短链映射总共约需 500GB 主数据存储。
scenario_en: At about 500 bytes per row, one billion short-link mappings require roughly 500 GB of primary data storage.
options_en: 500 GB already exceeds single-machine capacity, so sharding is required from day one.
500 GB comfortably fits on a modern SSD or single database instance, so sharding isn't needed on day one.
At this scale we must abandon relational databases for columnar storage.
At this scale, indexing no longer makes sense.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据切分到多台机器存储，用来突破单机容量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple machines to get past a single machine's capacity limit.

scenario: 短链系统读流量已由缓存承担，创建新短链每天约 100k，写入吞吐很低。
scenario_en: Reads are handled by cache, and the system creates about 100k new short links per day, so write throughput is low.
q: 数据库选择上最务实的答案是什么？
q_en: What is the most pragmatic database choice here?
options: 只能选 Cassandra，别的数据库都写不了
只能选图数据库来存这份映射
大多数成熟数据库都可以，Postgres 是合理默认
这个场景根本不需要持久化数据库
why: 写入量约 1 row/s，读峰值被缓存分担，Postgres/MySQL/DynamoDB 等都能做。面试里选自己熟悉且能解释 HA/索引/备份的数据库更重要。
why_en: Once reads are cached and writes are low, many databases work, with Postgres being a reasonable default.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求变成极高写入、多区域本地写或弱一致可接受，DynamoDB/Cassandra 这类方案可能更有优势。
options_en: Only Cassandra can handle the writes here.
Only a graph database can store this mapping.
Most mature databases can do this; Postgres is a reasonable default.
This scenario doesn't need a persistent database at all.
optionMeanings: 把低写入量场景过度设计。
映射关系不需要图结构。
写入量低、读已被缓存分担时的务实选择。
映射必须持久化，不能只靠缓存。
optionDirectness: 超高写入、多区域弱一致场景才会优先 Cassandra。
关系遍历密集时才需要图数据库，这里只是 code 到 URL 的映射。
低写入且读已缓存时，选择成熟熟悉的数据库更务实。
缓存只能加速读取，不能替代持久化映射。
tradeoff: 选熟悉的数据库换开发效率 vs 为未来极端写入预留专用数据库

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的开源关系型数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向海量写入和多区域场景的宽列存储数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column database built for very high write throughput and multi-region deployments.

scenario: 读请求远多于写请求，读路径是 GET /{short_code}，写路径是 POST /urls。
scenario_en: Read requests far outnumber writes: the read path is GET /{short_code}, and the write path is POST /urls.
q: 服务层如何拆分更利于独立扩展？
q_en: How should the service layer be split to scale independently?
options: 把 Read/Write Service 拆开，各自独立扩容
所有请求固定打到同一个实例
只留 Write Service，重定向交给客户端处理
把数据库拆成多张没有索引的表
why: 读写负载差异巨大时，拆分服务可让 redirect path 大规模横向扩展，而写路径保持较小规模并专注短码生成。
why_en: Separating read and write services lets the high-volume redirect path scale independently from the low-volume creation path.
whenOtherWins: 在早期低流量系统里，一个服务更简单；等读写负载和团队运维能力需要时再拆。
options_en: Split Read Service and Write Service apart so each scales independently.
Pin every request to the same single instance.
Keep only the Write Service and let the client handle redirects.
Split the database into multiple tables with no indexes.
optionMeanings: 读写负载差异大，各自独立扩容。
单实例没法应对高并发读。
客户端做不了服务端重定向。
拆表不解决查找效率问题。
optionDirectness: 读写负载差异大时，拆服务能让读路径单独横向扩容。
流量低的早期系统可以单实例，但高峰读会卡住。
客户端可以跟随重定向，但不能替代服务端查映射。
拆表只有配合正确索引和分片键时才有意义。
tradeoff: 读写分离换独立扩容能力 vs 多一层服务拆分和路由复杂度

q: 按正确顺序排列 counter 方案下创建短链的写入流程：
q_en: Put the write flow for creating a short link with the counter approach in the correct order.
steps: Write Service 把 counter 值编码成 Base62 短码
用户提交 long_url 到 POST /urls
Write Service 向 Redis INCR 获取全局唯一 counter
把 short_code、long_url、expiration_date 写入数据库并返回 short_url
why: 写路径先接收请求，再拿全局唯一 ID，编码为短码，最后持久化映射并返回给用户。
why_en: The write path receives the URL, gets a unique counter, encodes it, stores the mapping, and returns the short URL.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant W as Write Service
  participant R as Redis
  participant DB as DB
  C->>W: POST /urls
  W->>R: INCR counter
  R-->>W: next id
  W->>W: base62(id)
  W->>DB: insert mapping
  W-->>C: short_url
tradeoff: 预先批量取号段省网络调用 vs 单次 INCR 实现简单

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is Redis's atomic increment command.

q: 更高级别答案里，counter 方案还应补充哪些生产化细节？（多选）
q_en: Which production-readiness details should a stronger counter-based design include?
options: counter batching：每个 Write Service 申请一批号段，减少 Redis 网络调用
Redis Sentinel/Cluster：避免 counter 服务成为无保护单点
多区域 disjoint counter ranges：各区域本地写，避免跨区域协调
要求所有区域都从 counter=0 开始，方便调试
why: 号段批量、Redis 故障转移、多区域互斥范围是 counter 方案走向生产时的关键补强。所有区域从 0 开始会直接制造重复短码。
why_en: Production counter designs add batching, Redis failover, and disjoint regional ranges to reduce calls and preserve uniqueness.
options_en: Counter batching: each Write Service instance requests a batch of values, cutting Redis network calls.
Redis Sentinel/Cluster: avoids the counter service becoming an unprotected single point of failure.
Disjoint counter ranges per region: each region writes locally, avoiding cross-region coordination.
Require every region to start its counter at 0, for easier debugging.
optionMeanings: 批量取号段，减少网络往返。
计数器服务的高可用方案。
多区域各自独立取值范围。
臆造统一从 0 开始的调试便利。
optionDirectness: 正确，这是批量取号段的真实补强。
正确，这是高可用方面的真实补强。
正确，这是多区域协调的真实补强。
错误，这样会让区域间生成重复短码。

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的高可用方案，主节点故障时自动切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Sentinel and Cluster provide automatic failover when the primary Redis node fails.

q: CamelCamelCamel 这个系统的核心业务是什么？
q_en: What is CamelCamelCamel's core business?
options: 跨零售商比价搜索引擎
Amazon 官方价格 API
跟踪 Amazon 价格历史并做降价提醒
电商商品推荐系统
why: 它持续监控 Amazon 商品价格，用户设阈值后价格跌破即收到通知；100 万用户的 Chrome 插件还能直接在商品页显示历史价并一键订阅。
why_en: CamelCamelCamel tracks Amazon product prices over time and alerts users when a price drops below their chosen threshold, backed by a Chrome extension with a million users.
options_en: A price-comparison search engine across multiple retailers.
Amazon's own official price API.
A service that tracks Amazon price history and sends drop alerts.
A general e-commerce product recommendation engine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 运行在浏览器里的小程序，可以读取当前网页内容并上报数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Chrome extension is a small program that runs inside the browser and can read the current page and report data back.

q: 本题的两条核心功能需求是哪两条？（多选）
q_en: Which two are the core functional requirements for this problem? (multi-select)
options: 查看 Amazon 商品的价格历史
站内搜索和发现商品
订阅带价格阈值的降价通知
跨多家零售商做价格对比
why: 核心功能只有两条：看价格历史、订阅带阈值的降价提醒。站内搜索发现和跨零售商比价都被明确划到范围之外。
why_en: The two core functional requirements are viewing price history and subscribing to threshold-based price-drop alerts, while search and cross-retailer comparison are out of scope.
options_en: View price history for an Amazon product.
Search for and discover products on the site.
Subscribe to a price-drop alert with a threshold.
Compare prices across multiple retailers.

q: CamelCamelCamel 的核心非功能需求包括以下哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are CamelCamelCamel's core non-functional requirements? (multi-select)
options: 优先可用性，接受最终一致
价格历史查询延迟低于 500ms
价格数据必须强一致
亚分钟级的实时价格更新
why: 核心 NFR：可用性优先（最终一致）、支撑 5 亿商品、历史查询 <500ms、变价后 1 小时内通知。强一致和亚分钟实时更新被明确排除。
why_en: The core non-functional requirements are availability over strong consistency and sub-500-millisecond history queries, while strong consistency and sub-minute updates are explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Prioritize availability and accept eventual consistency.
Price history queries return in under 500 milliseconds.
Price data must be strongly consistent.
Prices update in near real time, under a minute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂看到旧数据是允许的，系统最终会收敛到最新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a read may briefly return stale data after a write, but the system converges to the latest value over time.

scenario: 面试官告诉你 CamelCamelCamel 要覆盖 Amazon 全站约 5 亿个商品，而且这是持续运行的目标规模，不是一次性上限。
scenario_en: The interviewer tells you CamelCamelCamel must cover roughly 500 million products across all of Amazon, and this is an ongoing steady-state target, not a one-time cap.
q: 这个商品规模量级，对整体架构提出的最直接要求是什么？
q_en: What does this product-scale order of magnitude most directly require of the overall architecture?
options: 只要把数据库服务器换成更贵机型就够了
采集和存储都必须支持水平扩展与按优先级分层
数量级不影响架构设计，先做完功能再说
商品越多，越应该优先做前端渲染优化
why: 5 亿商品让单机爬虫和单库存储都撑不住，逼出后面的分层爬取和存储拆分设计；数字本身不必死记，它改变的架构选择才是重点。
why_en: Half a billion products rules out a single crawler or a single database, which is exactly why the design needs tiered crawling and split storage.
options_en: Just upgrading to a bigger database server is enough.
Both collection and storage must scale horizontally with tiered priority.
The scale does not change the architecture; ship features first.
More products just means the frontend rendering needs work.

scenario: 非功能需求写明：价格跌破阈值后，通知必须在 1 小时内送达用户。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirements state that once a price drops below a user's threshold, the notification must reach them within one hour.
q: 这条 1 小时 SLA，直接排除了下面哪种通知实现方式？
q_en: Which notification implementation does this one-hour SLA directly rule out?
options: 每 2 小时跑一次的批量轮询 cron
价格变化时发布事件的实时管道
秒级消费事件的 Kafka 订阅者
变价后几分钟内触发的 webhook
why: 1 小时是给定 SLA，不是估算结果；2 小时 cron 的最坏等待约 2 小时，已经超过通知窗口。所以纯批量轮询被排除，通知链路要在变价时触发事件。
why_en: The one-hour SLA is a fixed target, and a two-hour cron can wait about two hours before notifying, so the alert path needs event-triggered processing.
options_en: A batch cron job that scans for changes every two hours.
A real-time pipeline that publishes an event on every price change.
A Kafka consumer that processes events within seconds.
A webhook fired within a few minutes of a price change.
optionDirectness: 只有通知窗口大于轮询周期、允许慢提醒时才合适。
写入价格时能发事件、要压低等待时间时合适。
已有事件流并要异步扇出通知时合适。
外部系统要被 HTTP 回调，而不是用户邮件时合适。
optionDirectness_en: Fits only when the alert window is longer than the polling interval.
Fits when price writes can emit events and waiting time matters.
Fits when an event stream already fans out alert work asynchronously.
Fits when an external system needs an HTTP callback, not user email.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务承诺的量化指标，比如「1 小时内送达通知」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA is a quantified service commitment, such as delivering a notification within one hour.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表周期性触发任务的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cron is a scheduler that triggers a job on a fixed recurring schedule.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定间隔扫描一批数据，找出期间发生的变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batch polling scans a batch of records on a fixed interval to find changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 状态变化发生时立即发布事件，让下游消费者异步处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Event-driven design publishes an event when state changes and lets downstream consumers react asynchronously.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事件发生时由服务端主动向指定地址发一次 HTTP 回调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook is an HTTP callback the server fires to a configured URL the moment an event happens.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式消息队列，用来在服务之间可靠地传递事件流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue used to reliably stream events between services.

scenario: 非功能需求写明：价格历史图表查询延迟必须低于 500ms，即使商品已经积累了几年的价格点。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirements state that price-history chart queries must stay under 500 milliseconds, even for products with years of accumulated price points.
q: 这条 500ms 延迟要求，最直接排除了下面哪种查询方式？
q_en: Which query approach does this 500ms latency requirement most directly rule out?
options: 每次请求现场扫描全部原始价格点做聚合
查预先算好的日/周/月聚合表
用 TimescaleDB 的 time_bucket 实时聚合
命中 Redis 里缓存好的图表数据
why: 500ms 是给定查询 SLO，不是推导值；热门商品几年价格点可达数千级。请求时现场聚合会把 CPU/IO 压到读路径上，所以要预聚合或时序库。
why_en: The 500 ms target is a read SLO, so chart requests should hit precomputed or time-series aggregates instead of scanning years of raw points.
options_en: Scanning and aggregating every raw price point on each request.
Reading a precomputed daily, weekly, or monthly summary table.
Using TimescaleDB's time_bucket for real-time aggregation.
Serving a chart already cached in Redis.

scenario: 这四个数字来自 CamelCamelCamel 的非功能需求，贯穿了后续所有深挖话题。
scenario_en: These four numbers come from CamelCamelCamel's non-functional requirements and run through every deep dive that follows.
q: 补全本题的规模与性能锚点：
q_en: Fill in this problem's scale and performance anchors:
text: 规模锚点：跟踪 {{5 亿}} 个商品；价格历史查询 < {{500}}ms；降价通知在 {{1 小时}} 内送达；一致性上接受{{最终一致}}。
why: 这些是给定锚点，不是背数字比赛：5 亿决定水平采集/存储，500ms 约束读路径，1 小时约束通知链路，最终一致允许异步化。
why_en: These anchors drive the design: scale splits collection and storage, 500 ms shapes reads, one hour shapes alerts, and eventual consistency allows async pipelines.

q: 以下哪项被明确划为范围之外（below the line）？
q_en: Which of these is explicitly out of scope (below the line)?
options: 查看商品价格历史
通过 Chrome 插件一键订阅
跨多家零售商的价格对比
订阅降价通知
why: 跨零售商比价、站内商品搜索发现、评论评分集成都在范围外；聚焦两条核心功能才能把时间留给深挖。
why_en: Cross-retailer price comparison is explicitly out of scope, along with product search and review integration.
options_en: Viewing a product's price history.
One-click subscribing through the Chrome extension.
Comparing prices across multiple retailers.
Subscribing to a price-drop notification.

q: 「优先可用性而非一致性」对这个系统的实际含义是？
q_en: What does "prioritize availability over consistency" actually mean for this system?
options: 每次读取都必须是最新价格
允许短暂陈旧，可用性优先于强一致
写入必须靠分布式事务保证
通知可以无限期延迟
why: 价格跟踪是历史趋势类产品，短暂陈旧无伤大雅；换来的是架构可以放心用异步管道、缓存和时序库，而不必为强一致付复杂度。
why_en: Prioritizing availability means price data may be briefly stale under eventual consistency, which frees the architecture to use asynchronous pipelines instead of distributed transactions.
options_en: Every read must return the absolute latest price.
Brief staleness is fine; availability wins over strong consistency.
Writes must be guaranteed by distributed transactions.
Notifications can be delayed indefinitely.

q: CamelCamelCamel 的数据模型里，以下哪些是核心实体？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are core entities in CamelCamelCamel's data model? (multi-select)
options: Subscription：关联用户与商品并保存触发阈值
Price：按时间序列记录商品价格变化
Product：被跟踪的 Amazon 商品及其元数据
Retailer：跨平台的零售商主档
why: 核心实体是 Product、User、Subscription、Price 四个；Retailer 属于被排除的跨零售商比价场景。Price 单独建模成时间序列是后面存储拆分的伏笔。
why_en: The core entities are Product, User, Subscription, and time-series Price, while a retailer entity belongs to the out-of-scope comparison feature.
options_en: Subscription: links a user to a product and stores the trigger threshold.
Price: a time series of a product's price changes.
Product: the tracked Amazon item and its metadata.
Retailer: a master record of a retailer for cross-platform comparison.

q: Subscription 实体在数据模型里承担什么角色？
q_en: What role does the Subscription entity play in the data model?
options: 存储商品的价格历史
记录用户的浏览行为
缓存爬虫的抓取结果
记录用户对商品的降价阈值
why: Subscription 是用户和商品之间的连接表，核心字段是 user_id、product_id 和 price_threshold；通知逻辑全靠它找到「谁关心这次降价」。
why_en: A subscription links a user to a product and stores the price threshold that triggers a notification.
options_en: Stores a product's price history.
Logs a user's browsing behavior.
Caches the crawler's fetch results.
Records the drop threshold a user set for a product.

q: Price 实体的正确建模方式是？
q_en: What is the correct way to model the Price entity?
options: 按时间序列记录每次价格变化
只在 Product 上存一个当前价格字段
存用户的历史订单价格
存通知发送日志
why: Price 是 append-only 的时间序列数据，每个商品随时间累积价格点；只有这样才能画出价格历史曲线，也因此它和 CRUD 表的存储需求完全不同。
why_en: Price is modeled as append-only time-series data capturing each change over time, which is what makes historical charts possible.
options_en: Record every price change as a time series.
Store only a single current-price field on Product.
Store a user's historical order prices.
Store a log of sent notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只追加新记录、不修改旧记录的写入模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Append-only means new records are added but existing rows are never updated or overwritten.

scenario: 设计查询价格历史的 GET 接口时，要决定 product_id 放 URL 路径还是放请求体。
scenario_en: While designing the GET endpoint for price history, you must decide whether product_id belongs in the URL path or the request body.
q: 为什么选择把 product_id 放在 URL 路径中？
q_en: Why put product_id in the URL path?
options: 路径参数天然加密更安全
GET 请求不允许带查询参数
利于网关/CDN 缓存，且符合 REST 资源语义
请求体无法传字符串
why: 资源 ID 进 URL 让同一商品的历史请求有稳定的可缓存键，同时符合 REST 的资源定位习惯；period 和 granularity 这类修饰参数放查询串。
why_en: Putting the product ID in the URL path gives a stable cacheable key and follows REST resource semantics, with modifiers like period and granularity in the query string.
whenOtherWins: 如果是多条件组合的复杂筛选或批量查询，参数塞不进一条 URL 时，才考虑 POST + 请求体的搜索型接口。
tradeoff: 路径参数的可缓存性 vs 请求体参数的灵活性
options_en: Path parameters are inherently encrypted and more secure.
GET requests are not allowed to carry query parameters.
It helps gateway or CDN caching and matches REST resource semantics.
A request body cannot carry string values.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用资源和标准 HTTP 方法组织 API 的风格，例如用 GET 读一个资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that models operations as resources accessed through standard HTTP methods like GET.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到离用户更近的边缘节点，加速静态或可缓存请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers closer to users to speed up static or cacheable requests.

q: 价格历史接口里 granularity 参数的作用是？
q_en: What does the granularity parameter do in the price-history endpoint?
options: 控制返回的压缩格式
控制数据粒度：长周期返回日级，近期返回小时级
控制分页大小
决定服务端缓存的 TTL
why: granularity 让同一个接口既能给 2 年图表返回日/月级均值，又能给近期图表返回小时级数据，避免把海量原始点全部推给客户端。
why_en: The granularity parameter lets the API return daily averages for long ranges and hourly points for recent windows instead of dumping raw data.
options_en: Controls the compression format of the response.
Controls data granularity: daily for long ranges, hourly for recent ones.
Controls the page size of the response.
Determines the server-side cache TTL.

scenario: 用户想看某商品最近 30 天的日级价格走势图，客户端需要发一个请求拿到画图数据。
scenario_en: A user wants to see a product's daily price trend for the last 30 days, and the client needs one request to fetch the chart data.
q: 哪个请求设计是正确的？
q_en: Which request design is correct?
options: GET /products/{id}/price?period=30d&granularity=daily
POST /products/price，把 id 放进请求体
GET /price-history?product_id=...
GET /products/{id}/price?period=30d&granularity=monthly
why: 读操作用 GET、资源 ID 进路径、period=30d 配 daily 粒度正好返回约 30 个点；monthly 粒度在 30 天区间里只剩 1 个点，画不成趋势图。
why_en: A GET with the product ID in the path plus a thirty-day period at daily granularity returns about thirty points, exactly what the chart needs.
whenOtherWins: 会改变状态的操作才用 POST，比如创建订阅；纯读取保持 GET 才能被网关和 CDN 缓存。
tradeoff: 资源路径 + 恰当粒度 vs 请求体传参或错配粒度
codeSample:
# 查询 30 天日级价格历史
GET /products/{product_id}/price?period=30d&granularity=daily
-> 200 PriceHistory[]

# 订阅降价通知
POST /subscriptions
{ "product_id": "...", "price_threshold": 249.99, "notification_type": "email" }
-> 200
options_en: GET the product's price with a 30-day period at daily granularity.
POST to a shared price endpoint with the product id in the body.
GET a price-history endpoint with product id only in the query string.
GET the same 30-day period but at monthly granularity.

q: 补全订阅接口的请求体字段：
q_en: Fill in the subscription endpoint's request body fields:
text: POST /subscriptions 的请求体包含 {{product_id}}、{{price_threshold}} 和 {{notification_type}} 三个字段，用户身份来自认证上下文而非请求体。
why: 订阅创建只需要「哪个商品、什么阈值、用什么渠道通知」；user_id 从网关认证里拿，防止客户端伪造别人的身份。
why_en: Creating a subscription takes the product ID, the price threshold, and the notification type, with the user identity coming from the authenticated session.

q: 把系统的核心数据流排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the system's core data flow into the correct order:
steps: 价格变化触发事件，进入通知处理流程
爬虫与 Chrome 插件从 Amazon 商品页采集当前价格
用户收到跌破阈值的降价邮件
价格数据经校验后写入价格库
why: 数据流是采集 → 校验入库 → 变价触发事件 → 通知用户。先对齐这条流，再决定各环节的组件，能提前暴露「数据从哪来」这个隐藏难点。
why_en: Data flows from collection by crawlers and the extension, through validation and storage, to change events that finally trigger user notifications.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["爬虫 + 插件采集价格"] --> B["校验后写入价格库"]
    B --> C["变价触发事件"]
    C --> D["邮件通知订阅用户"]

scenario: 题面只写了「看价格历史」和「订阅降价提醒」两条功能需求，没有提到数据从哪里来。
scenario_en: The prompt only lists two functional requirements, viewing price history and subscribing to drop alerts, without saying where the data comes from.
q: 这道题的「隐藏需求」是什么？
q_en: What is this problem's "hidden requirement"?
options: 数据采集本身，Amazon 不给官方 API
用户鉴权和权限管理
价格图表的前端渲染性能
邮件模板的多语言支持
why: 题面只说「看历史、订降价」，但没有 Amazon 的配合，价格数据的获取才是整题最硬的技术挑战，也是深挖的主战场。
why_en: The hidden requirement is acquiring the price data at all, since Amazon offers no API and actively discourages scraping.
options_en: Data acquisition itself, since Amazon offers no official API.
User authentication and permission management.
Frontend rendering performance for price charts.
Multi-language support for email templates.

scenario: Amazon 没有官方价格 API，还会对高频请求限流；候选人要先确认这条限流意味着什么。
scenario_en: Amazon has no official price API and rate-limits frequent requests; the candidate must first pin down what that rate limit implies.
q: 约 1 request/s/IP 的 Amazon 限流，对采集架构最直接的含义是什么？
q_en: What does Amazon's roughly one-request-per-second-per-IP rate limit most directly imply for the collection architecture?
options: 单机、单 IP 爬虫永远无法覆盖 5 亿商品，必须换一种采集思路
只要多开几个线程并发请求就能绕过限制
限流只影响爬虫，不影响插件上报的价格数据
限流意味着可以完全放弃数据采集这一步
why: 1 req/s/IP 表示每个 IP 每秒约 1 次请求；5 亿商品在单 IP 下约 15.8 年才扫完一轮。这个量级直接否掉只加线程的采集方案。
why_en: At one request per second per IP, a single IP needs about 15.8 years per full sweep, so threading alone cannot fix collection.
options_en: A single crawler on one IP can never cover five hundred million products; the approach must change.
Opening more concurrent threads is enough to get around the limit.
The rate limit only affects crawlers, not extension-reported prices.
The rate limit means data collection should simply be abandoned.

q: 高层设计中 API Gateway 承担哪些职责？
q_en: What responsibilities does the API Gateway carry in the high-level design?
options: 存储订阅数据
渲染价格图表
认证、限流，并把请求路由到对应服务
抓取 Amazon 商品页
why: 网关是入口：做认证和限流，然后把历史查询路由给 Price History Service、订阅操作路由给 Subscription Service。
why_en: The API gateway authenticates requests, applies rate limiting, and routes traffic to the right backend service.
diagram:
graph LR
    C[Client] --> G[API Gateway]
    G --> H[Price History Service]
    G --> S[Subscription Service]
    W[Web Crawler] --> P[Price Ingest]
    P --> TS[(Time Series DB)]
    P --> DB[(Primary DB)]
    DB --> N[Notification Worker]
options_en: Stores subscription data.
Renders price charts.
Authenticates, rate-limits, and routes requests to services.
Scrapes Amazon product pages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有请求的统一入口，负责认证、限流和路由到后端服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway is the single entry point for requests, handling authentication, rate limiting, and routing to backend services.

scenario: 价格历史服务要扛用户看图表的大量并发读，而爬虫按计划批量稳定写入，两者要不要拆成独立服务？
scenario_en: The price history service must absorb heavy concurrent reads from users viewing charts, while the crawler writes steadily on a schedule — should the two be split into separate services?
q: 拆分 Price History Service 和 Web Crawler Service 的核心理由是？
q_en: What is the core reason to split the Price History Service from the Web Crawler Service?
options: 扩缩容特征不同，拆开可独立优化
微服务永远优于单体
爬虫必须用另一种编程语言实现
同一个数据库不允许两个服务访问
why: 读侧随用户流量弹性伸缩，写侧按爬取计划平稳运行，负载曲线完全不同；拆开后互不拖累，各自独立调优。
why_en: The history service scales with bursty concurrent reads while the crawler runs on a steady schedule, so separating them lets each scale independently.
whenOtherWins: 产品极早期、流量很小时，单体加单库更省心；为拆而拆只会徒增运维成本。
tradeoff: 读密集服务的弹性伸缩 vs 写密集服务的稳定调度
options_en: Their scaling characteristics differ, so splitting lets each optimize independently.
Microservices are always better than a monolith.
The crawler must be implemented in a different language.
Two services are never allowed to access the same database.

scenario: Users/Products/Subscriptions 是小规模传统 CRUD 表；价格历史将涨到数十亿行、只追加不改、可接受最终一致。
scenario_en: Users, Products, and Subscriptions are small, traditional CRUD tables, while price history will grow to billions of append-only rows that can tolerate eventual consistency.
q: 存储层应该怎么安排？
q_en: How should the storage layer be organized?
options: 全部塞进同一个 Postgres，靠索引解决
每张表都独立一个数据库
全部迁到 Cassandra
CRUD 进 Primary，价格进 Price DB
why: 两类数据的规模、访问模式和一致性要求截然不同：拆开后 CRUD 库保持简单，价格库专注时序优化（分区、压缩、聚合），各自按需扩展。
why_en: Operational CRUD tables stay in a primary database while billions of append-only price rows go to a separate time-series-optimized store, so each scales on its own terms.
whenOtherWins: 数据量小、增长可预期时，单库加好索引就够了，不必提前拆分付运维成本。
tradeoff: CRUD 表的一致性需求 vs 时序数据的规模与聚合需求
options_en: Put everything in one Postgres instance and rely on indexing.
Give every single table its own database.
Migrate everything to Cassandra.
CRUD goes to the primary DB; price history goes to its own store.
optionMeanings: 索引改不了成本结构，仍是单点瓶颈。
拆分粒度过细，运维成本失控。
换库解决不了数据模型不匹配的问题。
按访问模式分层存储，各自独立扩展。
optionMeanings_en: Indexing alone doesn't fix the cost structure; still a single bottleneck.
Splitting every table is too fine-grained; ops cost spirals.
Swapping databases doesn't fix a data-model mismatch.
Splitting by access pattern lets each store scale independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种为高写入吞吐和水平扩展设计的宽列 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database designed for high write throughput and horizontal scaling.

q: 价格历史数据有哪些关键特征？（多选）
q_en: What are the key characteristics of the price history data? (multi-select)
options: 会增长到数十亿行
基本 append-only，几乎不修改旧行
需要时序优化（分区、聚合、压缩）
必须强一致才能使用
why: 十亿行、只追加、按时间查询聚合，是典型时序负载；且 NFR 明确接受最终一致，这正是它能与 CRUD 主库分家的原因。
why_en: Price history grows to billions of append-only rows needing time-series optimizations, and it explicitly tolerates eventual consistency.
options_en: It grows to billions of rows.
It is essentially append-only; old rows are rarely modified.
It needs time-series optimizations like partitioning and compression.
It must be strongly consistent to be usable.

q: 以下哪类数据不放在 Primary Database 里？
q_en: Which type of data does NOT belong in the Primary Database?
options: Users 用户表
Subscriptions 订阅表
价格历史时序数据
Products 商品表
why: Primary DB 收留规模小、CRUD 型的 Users/Products/Subscriptions；价格历史因体量和时序特征单独一个库。
why_en: Users, products, and subscriptions live in the primary database, while price history is kept in its own time-series store.
options_en: The Users table.
The Subscriptions table.
Time-series price history.
The Products table.

q: 补全价格历史的读路径：
q_en: Fill in the read path for price history:
text: 客户端发 GET 请求 → {{API Gateway}} 认证并路由 → Price History Service 按 {{product_id}} 和时间范围查 {{Price}} 表 → 返回 JSON 供图表渲染。
why: 读路径是最简单也最高频的一条链：网关做门卫，历史服务做查询，客户端拿 JSON 画图。所有后续优化（预聚合、时序库）都发生在查询那一步。
why_en: A read goes from the client through the gateway to the price history service, which queries the price table by product and time range and returns JSON for the chart.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant H as Price History
    participant T as Time Series DB
    C->>A: GET /products/:id/prices
    A->>H: productId + range + granularity
    H->>T: query buckets
    T-->>H: points
    H-->>C: chart data

scenario: 高层设计阶段只有 10-15 分钟，而爬虫的实现细节非常复杂，一旦展开就讲不完整体架构。
scenario_en: The high-level design phase only gets 10-15 minutes, and the crawler's implementation details are complex enough that unpacking them would eat the whole architecture discussion.
q: 对爬虫组件的正确处理方式是？
q_en: What is the right way to handle the crawler component here?
options: 当场展开讲爬虫的全部实现细节
认为爬虫不可行，直接砍掉这条需求
先黑盒处理，声明深挖阶段再展开
让面试官自己补充爬虫设计
why: 黑盒化复杂组件是框架化推进的关键技巧：先保证端到端架构成立，并明确告知面试官稍后深挖，掌控节奏又不显得回避。
why_en: Black-box the crawler in the high-level design by assuming it periodically writes prices, and explicitly defer the details to the deep dives.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官开场就把数据采集定为第一话题，就直接进入深挖，不必再走黑盒流程。
tradeoff: 端到端架构的完整性 vs 单个组件细节的深度
options_en: Explain every implementation detail of the crawler on the spot.
Decide the crawler is infeasible and drop the requirement.
Black-box it now and explicitly promise to go deep later.
Let the interviewer fill in the crawler design.

scenario: 订阅管理是用户账号类的增删改操作，价格历史是读密集的图表查询，考虑要不要共用一个服务。
scenario_en: Subscription management is account-style CRUD, while price history is read-heavy chart querying — should they share one service?
q: 正确的拆分判断是？
q_en: What is the correct split decision here?
options: 合并成一个服务，减少网络开销
拆开：CRUD 写操作 vs 读密集查询
订阅服务必须有状态，所以不能拆
只有引入 Kafka 之后才能拆
why: Subscription Service 处理创建/修改/删除订阅这类账号操作，Price History Service 专注高并发读；职责和负载模式不同，拆开各自演进。
why_en: Subscriptions are CRUD-style account operations while price history is read-heavy querying, so they are split into services with different access patterns.
whenOtherWins: 团队很小、流量很低时可以合并部署省运维，只要代码里保持模块边界清晰即可。
tradeoff: 账号类 CRUD 写操作 vs 图表查询的读并发
options_en: Merge into one service to save network overhead.
Split them: CRUD writes versus read-heavy queries.
The subscription service must be stateful, so it cannot be split.
Splitting is only possible after introducing Kafka.
optionMeanings: 省了网络跳数，但混淆了两种访问模式。
按写操作与读密集查询的差异拆分。
有状态与能否拆分之间没有必然关系。
拆分服务并不需要先引入消息队列。
optionMeanings_en: Saves a network hop but blurs two different access patterns.
Splits along the write-versus-read-heavy distinction.
Being stateful has no bearing on whether a service can split.
Splitting a service does not require a message queue first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式消息队列，用来在服务之间可靠地传递事件流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue used to reliably stream events between services.

q: 把初版轮询通知方案的执行流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the first-version polling notification flow into the correct order:
steps: 对每个变价，查 Subscriptions 表找出阈值 ≥ 新价的用户
把通知标记为已发送，避免重复提醒
定时任务每 2 小时启动一次
给命中的订阅发送邮件通知
扫 Price 表找出过去 2 小时的价格变化
why: cron 启动 → 扫变价 → 匹配订阅 → 发邮件 → 标记已发。这条流程简单能用，但它的两个硬伤（延迟、扫表开销）正是深挖 3 的切入点。
why_en: The cron job wakes every two hours, scans for price changes, matches subscriptions above the new price, sends emails, and marks them sent to avoid duplicates.
diagram:
graph TD
    S[Scheduler] --> Q[Product queue]
    Q --> C[Crawler pool]
    C --> P[Price parser]
    P --> DB[(Price table)]
    DB --> N[Notification scan]
    N --> U[User alert]

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表周期性触发任务的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cron is a scheduler that triggers a job on a fixed recurring schedule.

q: 初版「每 2 小时轮询」通知方案的主要问题是？
q_en: What is the main problem with the first-version "poll every 2 hours" notification design?
options: 延迟可达 2 小时，且每轮全表扫描很贵
邮件无法送达用户
订阅记录无法创建
爬虫会被轮询阻塞
why: 两小时的窗口直接违反 1 小时通知 NFR，而随规模增长、每轮扫描百万级价格与订阅记录会把数据库拖垮——这就是要转事件驱动的动机。
why_en: Polling every two hours means users can wait up to two hours and each run performs expensive database scans that will not scale.
options_en: Delay can reach two hours, and every run does an expensive full scan.
Emails cannot be delivered to users.
Subscription records cannot be created.
The crawler gets blocked by the polling job.

q: 轮询方案里如何避免同一个降价被重复通知？
q_en: In the polling design, how do you avoid notifying users twice for the same price drop?
options: 每轮都重发一遍无所谓
依赖用户手动屏蔽
给邮件加唯一标题
标记已发送，避免下一轮重复
why: cron 每轮都会扫到同一批变价，必须持久化「已通知」状态做幂等，否则用户每 2 小时被同一个降价轰炸一次。
why_en: After sending, the system marks the notification as sent so subsequent cron runs skip it and users are not repeatedly alerted for the same drop.
options_en: Just resend every round; it doesn't matter.
Rely on users to mute notifications manually.
Give the email a unique subject line.
Mark it sent so the next round skips it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，效果和执行一次一样，不会产生重复副作用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means repeating the same operation multiple times has the same effect as doing it once, with no duplicate side effects.

q: 「高效发现并跟踪 5 亿商品」这个深挖实际上拆成哪两个子问题？
q_en: The "efficiently discover and track 500 million products" deep dive actually splits into which two sub-problems?
options: 商品搜索与个性化推荐
用户增长与留存分析
商品发现 + 价格监控两个子问题
邮件送达率与退订管理
why: 发现是「找到所有商品」，监控是「决定谁多久查一次」；两者共享 Amazon 限流这个约束，但分开思考才能各自设计出有效方案。
why_en: The deep dive splits into product discovery, finding all products plus daily new ones, and price monitoring, deciding how often to refresh known products.
options_en: Product search and personalized recommendations.
User growth and retention analysis.
Product discovery plus price monitoring.
Email deliverability and unsubscribe handling.

scenario: Camelcamelcamel 已经要覆盖约 5 亿个存量商品，但 Amazon 每天还会继续上新；爬虫配额有限，不能把发现新品当成一次性导入任务。
scenario_en: CamelCamelCamel already needs to cover roughly 500 million existing products, but Amazon keeps adding new ones daily, and limited crawl budget means discovery can't be treated as a one-time import.
q: “每天约 3,000 个新品”这个数量级，对数据采集设计最重要的含义是什么？
q_en: What does "roughly 3,000 new products a day" most importantly imply for the data-collection design?
options: 商品发现必须是持续的增量 pipeline，而不是上线扫完存量就结束
新品数量太小，可以完全忽略 discovery
每天做一次全站全量爬取即可自然发现新品
把所有爬虫配额平均分给新旧商品保证公平
why: 这个数字不值得死记，价值在于它改变设计：商品发现要变成持续增量 pipeline，和已知商品的价格监控分开排优先级。
why_en: The point is not to memorize three thousand; the design implication is that product discovery must be a continuous incremental pipeline, separate from price monitoring for known products.
options_en: Discovery must be a continuous incremental pipeline, not a one-time import.
The new-product stream is small enough to ignore.
One full daily crawl naturally discovers new products.
Split crawl budget evenly across new and old products.
optionMeanings: 把数字转成架构结论：要持续发现新品。
把新增规模当成可忽略的边角问题。
继续用全量扫描解决 discovery。
把公平放在首位，忽略价值差异。
optionDirectness: 新增量会长期累积时，发现链路要持续运行。
只有新品能手工补录、且业务价值很低时，才可能忽略。
只有目录很小、爬虫配额充足时，全量日扫才可行。
平均分配适合价值接近的对象；这里冷热差异太大。
optionScenarioImpacts: 上线后每天都有新候选商品进入 discovery 队列。
目录会越来越旧，热门新品也可能长期缺失。
配额会被重复全量扫描吃掉，已知商品监控也变慢。
热门商品和新增商品都拿不到足够检查频率。
optionMeanings_en: Turns the number into an architecture conclusion.
Treats the new-product stream as negligible.
Keeps the brute-force full-crawl mindset.
Prioritizes fairness over value-aware scheduling.
optionDirectness_en: Use this when the daily stream keeps compounding.
This only works if new products can be manually backfilled.
This only works for a small catalog with plenty of crawl budget.
Equal split fits similar-value items, not a hot-and-cold catalog.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: New candidates keep entering the discovery queue after launch.
The catalog gets stale and hot new products may be missing.
Repeated full scans consume budget and slow known-product monitoring.
Hot products and new products both receive too little crawl frequency.

scenario: 单个爬虫按 Amazon 限流的每秒 1 个请求，去访问 5 亿商品页各一次。
scenario_en: A single crawler, limited to Amazon's one request per second, tries to visit each of 500 million product pages once.
q: 这个耗时量级说明了什么？
q_en: What does this order-of-magnitude duration tell you?
options: 约需 15.8 年，朴素单爬虫方案在工程上完全不可行
约需 6 天，短暂等一下就能覆盖全量
约需 1 年，调整一下爬取节奏就能接受
耗时不重要，只要爬虫不报错就行
why: 公式是 5 亿请求 ÷ 1 req/s ≈ 5 亿秒 ≈ 15.8 年；req/s 是每秒请求数。这个数直接否掉单 IP 全量爬取，后续才要分层和众包。
why_en: Five hundred million requests divided by one request per second is about 15.8 years, which rules out a single-IP full crawl.
options_en: About 15.8 years; a naive single crawler is simply not workable.
About 6 days; a short wait covers the whole catalog.
About 1 year; tweaking the crawl cadence would be acceptable.
The duration doesn't matter as long as the crawler doesn't error.

scenario: 部署 1,000 台不同 IP 的爬虫服务器，仍按每秒 1 请求/IP 的限流去刷新一遍 5 亿商品。
scenario_en: Even deploying 1,000 crawler servers on distinct IPs, still capped at one request per second per IP, to refresh all 500 million products once.
q: 这个耗时量级说明了什么？
q_en: What does this order-of-magnitude duration tell you?
options: 仍需 5 天以上，成本也不划算
约 1 小时就能刷完全部商品
约 30 分钟，性价比很高
耗时可以忽略，只看服务器成本
why: 公式是 5 亿 ÷ 1000 IP ÷ 1 req/s ≈ 50 万秒 ≈ 5.8 天；req/s 是每秒请求数。即使用千台机器，全量刷新仍慢过价格变化窗口，成本也不划算。
why_en: Even one thousand IPs need about 5.8 days per full refresh, so the system still misses price changes and pays too much infrastructure cost.
options_en: Still 5+ days, which is a poor cost tradeoff.
About one hour to refresh everything.
About 30 minutes, which is very cost-effective.
Duration doesn't matter, only server cost does.

q: 朴素网页爬虫方案的基本结构是？
q_en: What is the basic structure of a naive web crawler design?
options: 直接调用 Amazon 官方商品 API
只反复抓取 Amazon 首页
靠用户手动提交每个商品链接
种子页 + frontier 队列，递归跟进链接
why: 这就是经典 Web Crawler 设计：种子 URL + frontier 队列 + visited 追踪，遇到推荐位和「买过的人还看过」链接继续入队，逐步铺开整个目录。
why_en: A naive crawler starts from seed pages, keeps a frontier queue and a visited tracker, and recursively follows product links across the catalog.
diagram:
graph LR
    Seed[Seed URLs] --> Frontier[URL frontier]
    Frontier --> Fetch[Fetch product page]
    Fetch --> Parse[Parse price]
    Parse --> Store[(Price store)]
    Fetch --> Frontier
options_en: Call Amazon's official product API directly.
Repeatedly fetch only Amazon's homepage.
Rely on users to manually submit every product link.
Seed pages plus a frontier queue, following links recursively.

termDefinitions.meaning: 爬虫里存放待访问 URL 的队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The frontier queue holds URLs the crawler still needs to visit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录已访问过的 URL，防止爬虫重复抓取形成死循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The visited set records already-fetched URLs so the crawler does not loop forever re-fetching the same page.

scenario: 自建爬虫受 Amazon 限流约束，单个 IP 只能低频请求；系统又有约 5 亿商品、热门商品频繁变价、还有每天新品。你考虑最朴素的策略：所有商品同频轮询。
scenario_en: A self-built crawler is capped by Amazon's rate limit to low-frequency requests per IP; the system has roughly 500 million products, hot items that change price often, and new items daily. You consider the simplest strategy: poll every product at the same frequency.
q: 这种“所有商品同频轮询”的朴素爬取，在系统设计上会带来哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: What problems does this "poll every product at the same frequency" naive crawling strategy create? (multi-select)
options: 全量刷新周期太长，期间数百万次变价被漏掉
新品可能数周甚至数月后才被发现
热门商品一天变价多次，却长期拿着陈旧数据
无法解析 Amazon 页面的 HTML
why: 同频轮询把有限配额平均撒给所有商品，结果是全量刷新慢、发现滞后、热门数据陈旧；真正要做的是按价值排优先级，而不是解析能力的问题。
why_en: Uniform polling spreads scarce crawl budget evenly, causing slow refreshes, delayed discovery, and stale hot-product data; the fix is priority scheduling, not parsing.
options_en: The full refresh cycle is too long; millions of changes get missed.
New products may not be discovered for weeks or months.
Hot products change price often yet stay stale for a long time.
The system cannot parse Amazon's page HTML.
optionMeanings: 刷新周期问题：商品越多，扫一遍越慢。
discovery 延迟：新品只能等全量轮询碰到。
优先级错配：热门和冷门拿到同样低频率。
页面解析实现问题，非规模失败的根因。
optionDirectness: 全量刷新周期接近业务时限时，这是主风险。
新品持续进入目录时，需要独立 discovery 通道。
热门商品频繁变价时，调度要给它更高权重。
HTML 解析会影响实现质量，但不解释配额耗尽。
optionScenarioImpacts: 用户会看到过期价格，降价通知也可能错过窗口。
系统覆盖率随时间倒退，新品长期缺席。
最有用户价值的商品反而最容易陈旧。
即使解析写对了，轮询调度仍然不可扩展。
optionMeanings_en: The refresh-cycle problem of full polling.
The discovery-latency problem for new products.
A priority-mismatch problem between hot and cold items.
An HTML-parsing implementation concern.
optionDirectness_en: This is the main risk when refresh time exceeds the business window.
A steady new-product stream needs a separate discovery path.
Frequently changing hot products need higher crawl weight.
Parsing affects implementation quality, not crawl-budget exhaustion.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Users see stale prices and alerts can miss the useful window.
Coverage regresses over time as new products stay missing.
The highest-value products become stale first.
Even perfect parsing does not make uniform polling scalable.

q: 优先级爬取方案背后的关键分布规律是？
q_en: What key distribution pattern underlies the priority-crawling design?
