q: 真实系统通常会叠加哪些限流规则？（多选）
q_en: Which rate-limit rules do real systems typically layer together? (multi-select)
options: per-user limit
per-IP limit
global API capacity limit
endpoint-specific limit
why: 真实系统很少只有一个全局数字：per-user、per-IP、全局容量、endpoint 级规则会同时生效，命中最严格的一条就拒绝。
why_en: Production systems layer per-user, per-IP, global, and endpoint-specific limits, and enforce whichever rule is hit first.
options_en: A per-user limit
A per-IP limit
A global API capacity limit
An endpoint-specific limit

scenario: 多个真实用户可能共享同一个出口 IP（公司网络、公共 WiFi），但都已登录拿到各自账号。
scenario_en: Multiple real users can share the same egress IP (corporate network, public WiFi), but they are all logged in with their own accounts.
q: User ID 限流相比 IP 限流的主要优势是什么？
q_en: What is the main advantage of user-ID limiting over IP limiting?
options: IP 限流更精确，因为公网 IP 从不重复分配
已登录场景更公平：不会把共享 IP 下的多个用户误判成一个
User ID 限流不需要用户先登录鉴权
两者对完全匿名流量的效果完全一样
why: IP 天然适合匿名流量，但 NAT、公共 WiFi 会把很多真实用户并成一个 IP；已登录场景优先按 userId 分配限额更公平。
why_en: User-ID limits are fairer for logged-in traffic because IP limits can lump many real users behind the same NAT or public network into one bucket.
tradeoff: 已登录场景的公平性 vs 匿名流量下的可用性
options_en: IP limiting is more precise because public IPs are never reused
It is fairer for logged-in users because a shared IP will not be mistaken for one user
User-ID limiting does not require the user to log in first
Both behave identically for fully anonymous traffic

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个设备共用同一个公网 IP 出口的网络地址转换机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NAT lets many devices share one public IP address when talking to the internet.

q: Fixed Window Counter 的主要缺陷是什么？
q_en: What is the main flaw of the Fixed Window Counter algorithm?
options: 必须为每个请求单独存 timestamp
完全无法实现请求计数
窗口边界处可能双倍突发（两个相邻窗口各打满一次）
永远不能返回 reset time
why: 固定窗口简单省内存，但窗口切换瞬间没有平滑：用户可以在旧窗口尾部和新窗口头部各打满一次，短时间内拿到两倍配额。
why_en: Fixed windows are simple, but a client can burst up to twice its limit right across a window boundary.
tradeoff: 实现极简、只存一个计数器 vs 窗口边界处的突发失控
options_en: It must store a separate timestamp for every request
It cannot implement request counting at all
Two adjacent windows can each be maxed out, doubling the effective burst
It can never return a reset time

q: Sliding Window Log 的优点和代价是什么？
q_en: What are the benefit and cost of the Sliding Window Log algorithm?
options: 只需两个整数，但很不准确
支持突发流量，但不限制长期速率
完全不需要存储任何状态
精确统计滑动窗口请求，但要存大量 timestamp
why: 日志法记录每次请求时间，能精确回答过去 N 分钟发生了多少次，没有固定窗口的边界问题；代价是每个热点 client 要存、清理大量 timestamp。
why_en: Sliding window logs are exact because they track every request timestamp, but that precision costs memory and cleanup work per client.
tradeoff: 精确无边界效应 vs 每个 client 的存储与扫描开销
options_en: Only needs two integers, but is very inaccurate
Allows bursts, but does not cap sustained rate
Needs no stored state at all
Exact per-request count, but stores many timestamps

q: Sliding Window Counter 如何在成本和准确性之间折中？
q_en: How does the Sliding Window Counter trade off cost against accuracy?
options: 维护当前窗口和上一窗口两个计数器，按时间进度加权估算
保存所有请求的精确 timestamp
完全忽略上一窗口的数据
让 Redis 每秒重启清空状态
why: 它用当前窗口和上一窗口两个计数器，按当前窗口已过去的比例加权估算真实滑动窗口值，比固定窗口准，比日志省内存。
why_en: Sliding window counters approximate a true sliding window by weighting the previous and current window counters.
tradeoff: 内存只要两个计数器 vs 假设流量在窗口内均匀分布的近似误差
options_en: Keep current and previous window counters, weighted by elapsed time
Store the exact timestamp of every request
Ignore the previous window entirely
Restart Redis every second to clear state

scenario: API 流量天然 bursty，需要允许短暂突发，但也要限制长期平均速率，并且每个 client 状态要很小。
scenario_en: API traffic is naturally bursty: short bursts must be allowed, long-term average rate must still be capped, and per-client state must stay small.
q: 该设计最终选择哪种限流算法？
q_en: Which rate-limiting algorithm does this design finally choose?
options: 完整 Sliding Window Log
Token Bucket
全局互斥锁
只用 fixed window
why: Token Bucket 用 bucket capacity 控制突发、refill rate 控制长期速率，每个 client 只需两个字段，省内存又贴合 bursty 流量。
why_en: Token Bucket balances burst tolerance and sustained-rate control while needing only two small fields per client.
whenOtherWins: 如果必须精确限制任意滚动窗口内的请求数，Sliding Window Log 更准；规模很小时 Fixed Window 也够用。
tradeoff: 突发容忍加小状态 vs 任意滚动窗口的精确计数
options_en: A full Sliding Window Log
Token Bucket
A global mutex lock
Fixed window only

q: 补全 Token Bucket 的两个核心参数：
q_en: Fill in Token Bucket's two core parameters:
text: Token Bucket 用 {{bucket capacity}} 控制最大突发，用 {{refill rate}} 控制长期平均请求速率；每次请求消耗一个 token。
why: capacity 回答“最多能一口气打多少”，refill rate 回答“长期平均允许多少”；这比单纯请求数窗口更贴近 bursty 的 API 流量。
why_en: Token Bucket uses bucket capacity for burst size and refill rate for sustained request rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: token bucket 能装下的最大 token 数，决定允许的突发上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bucket capacity is the maximum number of tokens a bucket can hold, which caps how large a burst can be.

termDefinitions.meaning: token 补充进 bucket 的速率，决定长期平均允许速率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Refill rate is how fast tokens are added back to the bucket, setting the long-term sustained rate.

q: 把 Token Bucket 的单次检查流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put a single Token Bucket check into the correct order:
steps: 按 elapsed time 和 refill rate 补充 token，最多到 capacity
读取 client bucket 的 tokens 和 last_refill
如果 token >= 1，扣一个并允许请求
写回 tokens、last_refill，并设置 inactivity TTL
如果 token 不足，拒绝请求
why: 核心是 read-modify-write：先补充，再根据当前 token 决策，并持久化新状态。拒绝路径是否写回时间戳取决于实现，但原子边界不能拆开。
why_en: A token-bucket check reads state, refills tokens, decides allow or deny, and writes the updated state atomically.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Req[Request] --> Load[Load bucket]
Load --> Refill[Refill by elapsed time]
Refill --> Enough{Token available}
Enough -->|yes| Allow[Allow and decrement]
Enough -->|no| Deny[Return 429]

scenario: 多个 API Gateway 实例都要看到同一个用户的 token bucket 状态，且每次检查必须很快。
scenario_en: Multiple API Gateway instances must all see the same user's token-bucket state, and every check must stay fast.
q: 共享状态最合适放在哪里？
q_en: Where should the shared bucket state live?
options: 每个 gateway 的本地 map
离线数据仓库
Redis 这类内存 KV store
客户端 cookie
why: Redis 提供低延迟的跨实例共享状态、TTL 自动清理和原子脚本；只放本地会回到各 gateway 分裂计数的老问题。
why_en: Redis works as shared state because it is fast, supports TTL cleanup, and can run atomic update scripts across every gateway instance.
whenOtherWins: 单实例服务可以只用本地内存；需要长期审计分析时，应异步写日志系统，而不是挤占在线限流路径。
tradeoff: 跨实例共享一致 vs 本地内存更低的单跳延迟
options_en: A local map inside each gateway
An offline data warehouse
An in-memory KV store such as Redis
A client-side cookie

scenario: gateway 要读取某用户 bucket 的 token 数和最后 refill 时间，这两个字段存放在 Redis hash 中。
scenario_en: The gateway needs to read a user's token count and last-refill time, and both fields live in a Redis hash.
q: 哪条 Redis 命令最贴合这个读取？
q_en: Which Redis command best fits this read?
options: KEYS alice:bucket:*
BLPOP alice:bucket 0
PUBLISH alice:bucket check
HMGET alice:bucket tokens last_refill
codeSample:
HMGET alice:bucket tokens last_refill
HSET alice:bucket tokens <new_token_count>
HSET alice:bucket last_refill <current_timestamp>
EXPIRE alice:bucket 3600
why: bucket 状态是一个小 hash，HMGET 能一次读出 tokens 和 last_refill 两个字段；生产实现还要把整段判断放进原子脚本。
why_en: HMGET reads multiple fields of a Redis hash in one call, which fits reading a client's tokens and last-refill time together.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态只是一个数字，INCR/DECR 可能就够；Token Bucket 需要 tokens 和 last_refill 两个字段。
tradeoff: 定向读两个字段 vs 扫描/阻塞/广播类命令的开销
options_en: KEYS alice:bucket:*
BLPOP alice:bucket 0
PUBLISH alice:bucket check
HMGET alice:bucket tokens last_refill
optionMeanings: 列出所有 key（生产环境危险）
阻塞式弹出队列元素
发布消息给订阅者
一次读多个 hash 字段
optionDirectness: 不直接：这是运维排查命令
不直接：这是队列命令
不直接：这是发布订阅命令
最直接：正好对应 tokens+last_refill

q: 为什么 HMGET 后再 MULTI/HSET/EXEC 仍可能有竞态？
q_en: Why can a race condition still occur even after wrapping the write in MULTI/EXEC?
options: 读操作在事务外，两个 gateway 可能都读到旧值并放行
MULTI/EXEC 从不真正执行写入
Redis hash 里存不了时间戳
EXPIRE 会把所有用户一起删掉
why: MULTI/EXEC 只保证写入这一步原子，但读取 HMGET 发生在事务外；两个 gateway 同时读到同一个旧值时，可能都判断可放行，导致超发。
why_en: Wrapping only the write in MULTI/EXEC is not enough, because two gateways can read the same stale token count before either one writes back.
options_en: The read happens outside the transaction, so two gateways can both read a stale value and allow
MULTI/EXEC never actually performs the write
A Redis hash cannot store a timestamp
EXPIRE deletes every user's data at once

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 把多条命令打包成一个原子事务执行的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MULTI/EXEC groups several Redis commands into one atomic transaction.

scenario: 需要让读取 bucket、计算 refill、扣 token、写回状态在 Redis 里成为一个不可 interleave 的操作。
scenario_en: Reading the bucket, computing the refill, decrementing a token, and writing the state back all need to become one non-interleavable operation in Redis.
q: 应该使用什么机制？
q_en: What mechanism should be used?
options: 客户端 sleep 10ms
Redis Lua script
两个独立 HTTP 请求
只依赖 EXPIRE
codeSample:
-- EVAL rate_limit.lua alice:bucket now refill capacity
local tokens = redis.call('HGET', KEYS[1], 'tokens')
-- calculate refill, decide allow, HSET new fields atomically
return {allowed, remaining, resetTime}
why: Lua 脚本在 Redis 内部一次性原子执行，能把读取、计算、写回整段逻辑锁进一个不可 interleave 的操作，正是解决计数竞态的关键。
why_en: A Redis Lua script runs the whole read-calculate-write sequence as one atomic step inside Redis, closing the race window.
whenOtherWins: 简单固定窗口可以用 INCR+EXPIRE 这类单命令模式；Token Bucket 的计算更适合放进脚本。
tradeoff: 整段 read-modify-write 原子 vs 多命令往返的竞态风险
diagram:
flowchart LR
Gateway[Gateway] --> Lua[Redis Lua script]
Lua --> Read[Read tokens]
Lua --> Update[Refill and decrement]
Lua --> Result[Allow or deny]
options_en: The client sleeps 10ms
A Redis Lua script
Two independent HTTP requests
Rely only on EXPIRE

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 支持在服务端原子执行的小脚本，可以把多步逻辑合并成一次调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lua script lets Redis execute multiple steps atomically on the server in a single call.

q: Redis 适合限流状态的原因有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Why does Redis fit rate-limit state well? (multi-select)
options: 简单操作亚毫秒级
EXPIRE 可清理不活跃 bucket
支持复制/高可用
Lua 等机制支持原子操作
why: 限流状态小、热、生命周期短：Redis 的亚毫秒操作、EXPIRE 自动清理、复制/HA 和 Lua 原子脚本都贴合这个场景。
why_en: Redis fits rate-limit state because it is fast, supports TTL cleanup, can be replicated for availability, and can run atomic scripts.
options_en: Simple operations run in sub-millisecond time
EXPIRE cleans up inactive buckets
It supports replication for high availability
Mechanisms like Lua support atomic operations

scenario: 用户已经超出限制；这是交互式 API，请求排队会消耗资源并让响应时间不可预测。
scenario_en: A user has already exceeded the limit; this is an interactive API, and queuing requests would burn resources and make latency unpredictable.
q: 超限请求应该如何处理？
q_en: How should an over-limit request be handled?
options: 排队到窗口重置后再处理
静默丢弃无响应
fail fast，立即返回 HTTP 429
把请求写入长期数据库等待人工处理
why: 交互式 API 超限时立刻返回更可控：客户端能照 headers 退避重试。排队会占内存、诱发重复重试，还让响应时间变得不可预测。
why_en: Interactive APIs should fail fast with a 429 instead of queuing, because queued requests waste memory and make latency unpredictable.
whenOtherWins: 批处理或后台作业能接受排队等待；用户正在等待响应的交互式 API 通常不适合。
tradeoff: 立即失败、延迟可预测 vs 排队等待、更友好但更不可控
options_en: Queue the request until the window resets
Silently drop it with no response
Fail fast and return HTTP 429 immediately
Write it to a long-term database for manual review

q: HTTP 429 响应中常见的有用 headers 有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which headers are commonly useful on an HTTP 429 response? (multi-select)
options: X-RateLimit-Limit
X-RateLimit-Remaining
X-RateLimit-Reset
Retry-After
why: 这些 header 把限额、剩余额度、重置时间和建议等待时间都告诉客户端，好的客户端据此退避，而不是继续硬打 API。
why_en: Rate-limit headers tell the client the ceiling, remaining quota, reset time, and how long to wait before retrying.
options_en: X-RateLimit-Limit
X-RateLimit-Remaining
X-RateLimit-Reset
Retry-After

scenario: 请求被拒绝，客户端需要明确知道为什么失败以及何时重试。
scenario_en: A request is rejected, and the client needs to clearly know why it failed and when to retry.
q: 哪种响应最符合规范和用户体验？
q_en: Which response best matches the HTTP spec and gives a good client experience?
options: 返回 HTTP 200 成功状态，只在 body 里说明 error
返回 HTTP 500 服务器错误，且不附带任何 header
不返回任何响应，让客户端连接持续挂起
HTTP 429 + X-RateLimit-* + Retry-After
codeSample:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1640995200
Retry-After: 60
why: 429 是 Too Many Requests 的标准状态码，配合限额/剩余/重置 headers 能让客户端正确退避；不要用 200 或 500 掩盖限流语义。
why_en: A proper 429 response with rate-limit headers lets well-behaved clients understand the rejection and back off correctly.
whenOtherWins: 内部批处理协议可以用自定义错误码；面向公众的 HTTP API 应该遵守标准 429 语义。
tradeoff: 遵守 HTTP 语义方便客户端退避 vs 伪装成 200/500 让客户端困惑
options_en: Return HTTP 200 success and put the error only in the body
Return HTTP 500 with no headers at all
Send no response and leave the connection hanging
HTTP 429 with X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After

scenario: 单个 Redis 实例的典型操作吞吐约 100k-200k ops/sec，而一次限流检查至少要读一次、写一次。
scenario_en: A single Redis instance typically handles about 100k-200k ops/sec, and each rate-limit check needs at least one read and one write.
q: 这对能否用一个 Redis 实例支撑 1M requests/sec 的限流检查意味着什么？
q_en: What does this imply about supporting 1M requests/sec of rate-limit checks on a single Redis instance?
options: 不够：实际检查吞吐远低于 1M/sec，必须分片到多个实例
足够：单实例可以直接扛住 1M/sec
应该放弃 Redis，改成查询主数据库计数
应该把 refill rate 设为 0 来减轻压力
why: 一次检查至少 1 读 1 写，单实例约 100k-200k ops/sec 换算下来大概只能撑 50k-100k 次检查/sec，离 1M 差一个数量级，必须分片。
why_en: Because each check needs a read and a write, a single Redis instance realistically handles tens of thousands of checks per second, not a million, so sharding is required.
options_en: Not enough: real check throughput is far below 1M/sec, so it must be sharded
Enough: a single instance can directly handle 1M/sec
Abandon Redis and count against the primary database instead
Set the refill rate to zero to reduce load

scenario: 目标是 1M RPS，单 Redis 实例成为瓶颈；同一 client 的请求必须始终命中同一份 bucket 状态。
scenario_en: The target is 1M RPS and a single Redis instance is the bottleneck; the same client's requests must always hit the same bucket state.
q: Redis 状态应该如何扩展？
q_en: How should Redis state be scaled out?
options: 随机挑一个 Redis 实例写入状态
按 client identifier 一致性哈希到固定 shard
把同一份 bucket 复制到所有 shard 后随便读写
每个请求都广播给全部 Redis 实例
why: 按 client identifier 一致性哈希，保证同一 client 永远落在同一 shard，同时把负载摊开；Redis Cluster 可用 hash slot 自动路由。
why_en: Sharding by client identifier keeps each client's rate-limit state on one Redis shard while spreading different clients' load across shards.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则是全局总 QPS 而不是按 client，需要单独的全局或分层计数机制。
tradeoff: 同一 client 状态集中在一个 shard vs 全局总量类规则难以直接分片
options_en: Write to a randomly chosen Redis instance
Consistent-hash the client identifier onto a fixed shard
Copy the same bucket to every shard and read/write any of them
Broadcast every request to all Redis instances

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种让 key 稳定映射到某个节点、且扩缩容时只影响少量 key 的哈希方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps each key to a stable node so that adding or removing nodes only reshuffles a small fraction of keys.

q: 补全 Redis Cluster 的分片机制：
q_en: Fill in how Redis Cluster shards data:
text: Redis Cluster 把 keyspace 切成 {{16384}} 个 hash slots，并把这些 slots 分配到多个 Redis nodes。
why: 使用 Redis Cluster 时，gateway 不必自己维护一致性哈希细节，客户端/集群会根据 key 的 slot 自动路由到正确的节点。
why_en: Redis Cluster shards keys across 16,384 hash slots distributed over multiple nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 用来分配 key 归属节点的一个编号区间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash slot is a numbered bucket Redis Cluster uses to decide which node owns a key.

scenario: 每个 Redis shard 约能处理 100k checks/sec；目标总吞吐是 1M checks/sec。
scenario_en: Each Redis shard handles about 100k checks/sec, and the target total throughput is 1M checks/sec.
q: 要达到这个目标吞吐，Redis 状态应该怎么部署？
q_en: How should Redis state be deployed to hit this target throughput?
options: 继续用单实例，靠升级硬件解决
关闭一部分限流规则来降低压力
按 client key 分片到约 10 个实例
把所有数据复制到每个节点本地判断
why: 1M / 100k ≈ 10，量级上需要十几个 shard 而不是一个大实例；真实生产还要再加副本和余量。
why_en: One million divided by about 100k checks per shard is roughly ten shards, plus replicas and headroom in production.
options_en: Keep a single instance and just upgrade hardware
Turn off some rate-limit rules to reduce load
Shard state by client key across about ten instances
Copy all data to every node and decide locally

q: 把分片限流检查流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the sharded rate-limit check flow into the correct order:
steps: gateway 提取 userId/IP/API key 作为 identifier
Redis shard 内原子执行 Token Bucket 判断
对 identifier 做 consistent hash 或计算 Redis slot
根据结果返回 passes/remaining/resetTime
把请求路由到负责该 identifier 的 Redis shard
why: identifier 是分片键，必须稳定映射到同一 shard。到达 shard 后，算法本身和单实例 Token Bucket 基本一样。
why_en: The gateway extracts a stable identifier, routes it to the owning Redis shard, and runs the token-bucket decision there atomically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Req[Request key] --> Hash[Hash key]
Hash --> Shard[Redis shard]
Shard --> Lua[Atomic check]
Lua --> Decision[Allow or 429]

q: fail-closed 的含义是什么？
q_en: What does fail-closed mean?
options: 限流器故障时改为放行所有请求
只对已付费的用户执行限流
把超限请求排队等 Redis 恢复
无法判断时拒绝请求，保护后端但牺牲可用性
why: fail-closed 保守：判断不了就拒绝，保护后端但会牺牲可用性——健康的请求也可能被挡在门外。
why_en: Fail-closed rejects requests it cannot verify, protecting backends at the cost of rejecting some healthy traffic too.
tradeoff: 保护后端优先 vs 可用性优先
options_en: Switch to allowing all requests when the limiter fails
Only rate-limit paying customers
Queue over-limit requests until Redis recovers
Reject requests it cannot verify, protecting the backend at the cost of availability

q: fail-open 的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of fail-open?
options: Redis 不可用时流量直通后端，高峰可能引发级联故障
它会把所有健康请求也一起拒绝掉
它反而让限流判断更加精确
它要求每个客户端自己实现 Lua 脚本
why: fail-open 保住了可用性，但暂时失去限流保护；如果 Redis 正是因为流量或攻击才出问题，放开闸门可能直接压垮后端。
why_en: Fail-open keeps the API available but removes protection at the exact moment traffic or an attack may already be overwhelming the backend.
tradeoff: 可用性优先 vs 失去保护窗口
options_en: When Redis is unavailable, all traffic passes straight through and can cascade during a spike
It rejects every healthy request as well
It makes rate-limit decisions more precise
It requires every client to implement Lua itself

scenario: 社交平台在 viral 事件中流量突增；Redis-based 限流层故障或超时，系统无法可靠读取/更新计数，而后端数据库和应用也可能已经接近容量上限。
scenario_en: A social platform sees a traffic surge during a viral event; the Redis-based limiter fails or times out so counts can't be reliably read or updated, and the backend database and app are already near capacity.
q: 此时最直接选择哪种失败模式？
q_en: Which failure mode is the right call here?
options: fail-open
fail-closed
无限排队
客户端自觉限流即可
why: fail-closed = 限流器不可用时默认拒绝或降级拦截；在后端已接近容量时，它牺牲一部分可用性来避免流量绕过限流打爆数据库。fail-open = 限流器不可用时默认放行，用户可用性更高，但可能把 Redis 故障放大成级联故障。
why_en: Fail-closed rejects or degrades requests when the limiter is unavailable, protecting a near-capacity backend from a Redis outage becoming a cascading failure.
whenOtherWins: 如果后端余量很大、限流只是软配额或非关键保护，fail-open 更适合，因为它优先保证用户请求继续成功。
tradeoff: 下游保护/防级联故障 vs 用户可用性
options_en: Fail-open
Fail-closed
Queue requests indefinitely
Rely on client-side limiting alone
optionMeanings: 限流器故障时默认放行请求。
限流器故障时默认拒绝、返回错误或进入保守降级。
把请求一直挂起等待限流器恢复。
把限流责任交给客户端自行遵守。
optionScenarioImpacts: 用户成功率更高，但流量会绕过限流直接冲向已经紧张的后端。
会挡住部分健康请求，但保护后端不被打垮。
会堆积连接、线程和内存，可能把入口层也拖垮。
攻击者或异常客户端不会自觉配合，服务端失去强制保护。
optionDirectness: 不适合本场景：后端接近容量，放行会增加级联故障风险。
最直接：保护下游优先，短暂牺牲可用性。
不直接：无限排队通常比快速失败更危险。
不直接：限流必须由服务端强制执行。
optionMeanings_en: Allow requests by default when the limiter fails.
Reject or degrade requests by default when the limiter fails.
Keep requests waiting until the limiter recovers.
Rely on clients to voluntarily throttle themselves.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Availability is higher, but traffic bypasses the failed limiter and hits an already stressed backend.
Some valid requests are blocked, but the backend is protected while the limiter is unavailable.
Connections, threads, and memory can pile up and harm the entry layer.
Attackers or buggy clients will not reliably self-throttle.
optionDirectness_en: Not best here because the backend is already near capacity.
Most direct because downstream protection matters more than short-term availability.
Not direct because unbounded waiting is usually more dangerous than fast failure.
Not direct because rate limiting needs server-side enforcement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保护组件故障时默认放行请求；在限流场景里，就是 Redis/限流器超时或不可用时仍让请求进入后端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fail-open means allowing requests by default when the protective component fails, such as letting traffic through when Redis rate limiting times out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保护组件故障时默认拒绝或降级拦截请求；在限流场景里，就是无法判断配额时返回 429/503 或走保守拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fail-closed means rejecting or degrading requests by default when the protective component fails, such as returning 429 or 503 when quota cannot be checked.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个组件故障后，流量、重试或负载转移继续压垮下游组件，导致故障范围扩大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cascading failure is when one component failure shifts load or retries onto downstream components until more of the system fails.

scenario: Redis 已按 client 分片，但任一 shard 挂掉会影响其负责的一批用户；希望自动恢复写能力。
scenario_en: Redis is already sharded by client, but any shard going down affects the batch of users it owns; the goal is automatic recovery of write capability.
q: 标准高可用方案是什么？
q_en: What is the standard high-availability approach?
options: 只用单 master，完全不配副本
把 bucket 状态写进浏览器本地存储
每个 shard 配副本，故障时自动提升
每次故障都靠人工手动切换 Redis
why: master-replica 复制加自动 failover 是标准做法，Redis Cluster 能自动探测故障并提升副本；代价是成本和短暂复制延迟。
why_en: Standard Redis high availability uses master-replica replication with automatic promotion on failure, at the cost of extra infrastructure and brief replication lag.
whenOtherWins: 极小系统能接受单实例故障；跨地域强隔离需求可能要每区域独立集群加更复杂策略。
tradeoff: 自动故障恢复 vs 额外副本成本和复制延迟
options_en: Use a single master with no replicas at all
Write bucket state into the browser's local storage
Give every shard a replica and auto-promote it on failure
Fail over by hand every single time

q: 限流系统应监控哪些指标？（多选）
q_en: Which metrics should a rate-limiting system monitor? (multi-select)
options: Redis CPU、内存、网络连通性
限流检查成功率和延迟
进入 fail-open/fail-closed 降级模式的事件
每个用户的头像颜色
why: 限流器挡在请求入口，必须能快速发现 Redis 异常、决策延迟升高或降级模式被触发；跟限流健康无关的指标不该混进来。
why_en: Rate-limiter observability should cover Redis health, check latency and success rate, and transitions into fail-open or fail-closed.
options_en: Redis CPU, memory, and network connectivity
Rate-limit check success rate and latency
Events entering fail-open or fail-closed degraded mode
Every user's avatar color

scenario: 每次限流检查都要访问 Redis；如果 gateway 每次都新建 TCP 连接，额外握手会让请求延迟不可接受。
scenario_en: Every rate-limit check hits Redis; if the gateway opens a new TCP connection each time, the extra handshake makes request latency unacceptable.
q: 最重要的低延迟优化是什么？
q_en: What is the single most important low-latency optimization?
options: 每请求打开新连接以避免复用
把限流检查改成离线批处理
删除所有 headers
连接池 / 持久 Redis 连接
why: 连接池复用已建立的 TCP 连接，省掉每次 20-50ms 级别的握手开销；Redis 操作本身很快，连接管理常常才是主要延迟来源。
why_en: Connection pooling reuses established TCP connections and avoids repeated handshake overhead on the hot path.
whenOtherWins: 很低频的管理接口可以用简单短连接；核心请求路径必须复用连接。
tradeoff: 复用连接省握手延迟 vs 每次新建连接的简单但慢
options_en: Open a fresh connection per request to avoid reuse
Turn rate-limit checks into an offline batch job
Strip out all response headers
Connection pooling with persistent Redis connections

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用一组已建立的连接，而不是每次请求都重新握手。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Connection pooling reuses a set of already-open connections instead of opening a new one per request.

scenario: 用户分布全球；东京用户如果每次限流都访问弗吉尼亚 Redis，会多出明显网络延迟。
scenario_en: Users are distributed globally; if a Tokyo user's every rate-limit check hits Redis in Virginia, that adds noticeable network latency.
q: 最大的地理延迟优化是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest optimization for geographic latency?
options: 多区域部署 Gateway 和 Redis，就近完成限流
把所有流量强制回源到单一区域
只增加 HTTP 429 的 body 字段
直接关闭 TLS 加密传输
why: 限流状态放到离用户近的区域能省掉跨洋 RTT；代价是跨区域一致性更复杂，但限流通常可以接受区域间最终一致。
why_en: Deploying gateways and Redis regionally keeps rate-limit checks close to users and avoids cross-continent round trips.
whenOtherWins: 如果必须全局强一致限额，需要单一权威区域或分层协调，但会牺牲延迟。
options_en: Deploy gateways and Redis regionally, so checks stay local
Force all traffic back to a single origin region
Just add another field to the 429 response body
Simply turn off TLS encryption
optionMeanings: 把限流部署分散到用户附近的区域
所有请求都跨区域回中心处理
只改响应体格式，不改延迟路径
去掉传输层加密，不影响网络距离
optionMeanings_en: Spreads the limiter deployment near users
Every request still crosses regions to a central point
Only changes response format, not the latency path
Removes transport encryption, unrelated to network distance

q: 除连接池和地理部署外，文章提到哪些可选优化？（多选）
q_en: Besides connection pooling and geographic deployment, which optional optimizations does the article mention? (multi-select)
options: 每次请求都查询中央配置数据库
Redis pipelining 或 Lua scripts 减少往返
同用户突发请求的 request batching
本地缓存限流状态但要小心 stale
why: pipelining/Lua 减少往返，batching 摊薄热点请求，本地缓存要小心 stale；但每次查中央配置库会直接拖垮延迟目标，不该走这条路。
why_en: Pipelining, Lua scripts, careful batching, and cautious local caching can cut latency, while querying a central config database on every request would not.
options_en: Querying a central config database on every request
Redis pipelining or Lua scripts to cut round trips
Batching a burst of requests from the same user
Local caching of rate-limit state, done carefully to avoid staleness

q: Rate Limiter 中的 hot key 通常意味着什么？
q_en: What does a hot key usually mean in a rate limiter?
options: 某篇帖子被非常多不同用户同时读取
单个 client 请求量极高，压垮所在 shard
某张数据库表的 schema 设计得不好
所有用户的请求量都完全均匀
why: 限流状态按 client key 分片，所以 hot key 就是某一个 client 自己的请求量极大；可能是滥用攻击，也可能是合法高流量客户或 NAT 聚合。
why_en: A rate-limiter hot key is one client identifier sending enough traffic to overload the single shard that owns it.
options_en: One post is being read by many different users
One client sends extreme traffic and overloads its shard
A database table has a poorly designed schema
Every user's request volume is perfectly even

q: 对合法高流量 client，文章建议哪些处理方式？（多选）
q_en: For legitimate high-volume clients, which approaches does the article recommend? (multi-select)
options: 鼓励 client-side rate limiting 平滑流量
立刻永久封禁所有高流量 client
提供 batch API 减少检查次数
premium tiers 或 dedicated infrastructure
why: 合法高流量要引导承载，不是一刀切封禁：客户端限流平滑流量，批处理减少检查次数，付费/专用资源隔离压力。
why_en: Legitimate high-volume clients are handled with client-side limiting, batch APIs, or premium and dedicated infrastructure rather than blanket bans.
options_en: Encourage client-side rate limiting to smooth traffic
Permanently ban every high-volume client immediately
Offer a batch API to cut the number of checks
Offer premium tiers or dedicated infrastructure

q: 对滥用或攻击流量，哪些策略合理？（多选）
q_en: For abusive or attack traffic, which strategies are reasonable? (multi-select)
options: 持续触发限流后临时加入 blocklist
使用 Cloudflare/AWS Shield 等 DDoS 防护在更前面挡流量
完全依赖客户端自觉
降低 IP-based 规则对 NAT 的误伤并更多依赖 authenticated user limit
why: 恶意流量不能指望客户端自觉，应尽早用 blocklist 和上游 DDoS 防护挡住；共享 IP 也可能是合法 NAT，IP 规则要谨慎、多依赖已登录用户限额。
why_en: Abusive traffic needs blocklists and upstream DDoS protection, while IP-based rules must stay cautious about shared NATs.
options_en: Temporarily blocklist a client after it repeatedly hits limits
Use upstream DDoS protection such as Cloudflare or AWS Shield
Rely entirely on client good behavior
Ease IP-based rules for NAT and lean more on authenticated user limits

q: client-side rate limiting 在本设计中的定位是什么？
q_en: What role does client-side rate limiting play in this design?
options: 完全替代服务端限流
只用于数据库内部
有价值的补充，可平滑好公民流量，但不能作为安全边界
会让 HTTP 429 不再需要
why: 客户端限流能减少误伤和基础设施压力，但恶意客户端不会自觉遵守；服务端限流仍是保护系统必须有的边界。
why_en: Client-side limiting is a useful complement for well-behaved clients, but it cannot replace server-side enforcement.
tradeoff: 降低基础设施压力 vs 无法充当安全边界
options_en: A full replacement for server-side rate limiting
Something only used inside the database
A valuable complement that smooths well-behaved traffic, but not a security boundary
Something that makes HTTP 429 unnecessary

scenario: 限流规则偶尔调整，例如产品发布时临时提高 limit；允许几十秒内逐步生效，想保持实现简单。
scenario_en: Rate-limit rules change occasionally, such as temporarily raising a limit for a product launch; taking tens of seconds to propagate is fine, and the team wants a simple implementation.
q: 最常见的动态配置方案是什么？
q_en: What is the most common approach for dynamic configuration?
options: 每个请求都触发重新部署 gateway
把规则直接写进客户端代码里
只靠人工 SSH 登录改内存
配置库存规则，gateway 定期 polling 并缓存
why: 配置服务/数据库存规则，gateway 周期性 polling 并本地缓存，实现简单、够用；代价是变更到全网生效有延迟，比如最多 30 秒。
why_en: Polling a configuration store and caching results locally is simple and good enough when rule changes can take up to about 30 seconds to propagate.
whenOtherWins: 安全事件或高频交易等需要秒级强推配置时，push-based 方案更合适。
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 变更生效有延迟
diagram:
flowchart LR
Admin[Admin config] --> Store[Config store]
Store --> Watch[Watch or poll]
Watch --> Gateway[Gateway cache]
Gateway --> Checks[Limiter checks]
options_en: Redeploy the gateway on every single request
Hard-code the rules directly into client code
Only change memory by hand over SSH
Store rules in a config store; gateways poll and cache them

scenario: 安全事件中需要几秒内把新 limit 推到所有 gateway，不能等下一轮 30 秒 polling。
scenario_en: During a security incident, a new limit must reach all gateways within seconds — it can't wait for the next 30-second polling cycle.
q: 应考虑哪种配置分发？
q_en: Which configuration-distribution approach should be considered?
options: 用 ZooKeeper/Pub-Sub 做 push 配置通知
每天定时人工重启所有 gateway 才生效
把规则直接写死在部署镜像里
只手动更新其中一台 gateway
why: push-based 配置能立刻通知所有连接的 gateway，适合紧急规则变更；代价是要处理连接故障、部分更新和 fallback，复杂度更高。
why_en: Push-based configuration notifies every connected gateway immediately, which suits urgent changes but adds connection and partial-failure handling complexity.
whenOtherWins: 普通业务规则调整用 polling 更简单；push 只在对传播延迟敏感时才值得付出复杂度。
tradeoff: 秒级生效 vs 连接管理和部分失败的复杂度
options_en: Push-based notification via ZooKeeper or Pub/Sub
Restart every gateway by hand on a daily schedule
Bake the rules directly into the deployment image
Manually update just one single gateway

q: 把“选择 API Gateway + Redis Token Bucket”的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for choosing API Gateway plus Redis Token Bucket into the correct order:
steps: 用 Token Bucket 兼顾 burst 和 sustained rate
需求：每个请求前低延迟判断并保护后端
把限流放在 API Gateway，先于业务服务拒绝
用 Redis 共享各 gateway 的 bucket 状态
用 Lua 保证 read-calculate-update 原子

q: 把“扩展到 1M RPS”的决策链排成正确顺序：

q: 中级候选人在这题里至少应讲清楚什么？

只讨论前端错误提示文案

options_en: Implement a full ZooKeeper from scratch

scenario: 面试官让你设计 1M rps 的 distributed rate limiter。你已经说了 API Gateway + Redis + Token Bucket，接下来要体现 senior 深度。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to design a distributed rate limiter for 1M rps. You've already said API Gateway + Redis + Token Bucket, and now need to show senior-level depth.
q: 下一步最应该主动展开什么？

options: 只死记硬背固定窗口的定义
假装系统完全没有故障模式

把限流丢给客户端就当结束

why_en: Senior depth means explaining whether shared rate-limit state remains correct under concurrency, scale, and Redis failure, not merely naming more algorithms.
options_en: Only recite the definition of a fixed window
Pretend the system has no failure modes
Explain atomic updates, sharding, and failure degradation
Hand rate limiting to the client and stop there
optionMeanings: 只讲一个基础算法的定义。
只画正常路径，不讨论 Redis 或网络出问题。
把限流从单机算法推进到分布式生产问题：并发正确性、容量扩展、故障策略。
让客户端自己少发请求。
optionScenarioImpacts: 说明不了多个 gateway 同时更新同一用户 bucket 时会不会出错。
说明不了 Redis 超时、shard 挂掉、重试风暴时系统怎么保护后端。
覆盖了面试官最关心的坑：状态更新不能丢、Redis 不能单点、故障时不能把后端打爆。
可以作为补充，但攻击者或异常客户端不会可靠配合。
optionDirectness: 太浅：只到 junior/mid 的算法记忆。
太危险：分布式限流一定要讲故障。
最直接：这就是 senior 要主动补的深度。
不够：服务端限流不能靠客户端自觉。
optionMeanings_en: Only describe one basic algorithm.
Only draw the happy path and ignore Redis or network failures.
Move from a single-machine algorithm to production distributed concerns: correctness, scale, and failure behavior.
Ask clients to voluntarily send fewer requests.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This does not explain whether concurrent gateways can corrupt a user's bucket.
This does not explain what happens when Redis times out, a shard dies, or retries spike.
This covers the core risks: no lost state updates, no single Redis bottleneck, and no backend overload during failure.
It can help as a complement, but bad or buggy clients will not reliably cooperate.
optionDirectness_en: Too shallow because it is just algorithm recall.
Too risky because distributed rate limiters need failure handling.
Most direct because these are the senior-level distributed-systems issues.
Insufficient because server-side protection cannot rely on client honesty.

termDefinitions.meaning: 这里指一次限流判断里的“读 token、补 token、扣 token、写回状态”必须像一个不可拆开的步骤执行；否则多个 gateway 并发请求会互相覆盖，导致多放行或误拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Here atomicity means the read-refill-decrement-write rate-limit update runs as one indivisible step, so concurrent gateways cannot overwrite each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同 client 的 bucket 状态分散到多个 Redis shard；同一个 user/IP/API key 必须稳定落到同一个 shard，否则它的计数会被拆散，限流失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding spreads different clients' bucket state across Redis shards while keeping the same client key on the same shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 慢、超时或 shard 挂掉时系统如何反应：fail-open 是放行保可用性但可能打爆后端，fail-closed 是拒绝保护后端但会挡住正常用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A failure mode is how the system behaves when Redis is slow or down, such as fail-open for availability or fail-closed for backend protection.

rows: Lua 保证读改写不中断
按 key 分散到多个 shard

q: Staff+ 答案通常应体现什么？
q_en: What should a Staff+ answer typically demonstrate?
options: 只是多罗列几种算法的名字而已
完全回避任何权衡取舍的讨论
假设所有客户端天生值得信任
强调生产深度：多区域、可观测性、真实容量

options_en: Just list a few more algorithm names
Avoid any discussion of trade-offs entirely
Assume every client is inherently trustworthy
Emphasize production depth: multi-region, observability, real capacity

q: 最终 rate limiter 设计的关键组成包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are the key components of the final rate limiter design? (multi-select)
options: API Gateway 执行限流并返回 429 headers
Redis Cluster 分片存 token bucket 状态
Lua 原子执行 bucket 更新
每个请求长期写入分析数据库后再决定是否放行
why: 最终主路径要短：gateway 提取标识、命中对应 Redis shard、脚本原子判断，超限就快速返回 429；长期分析不该阻塞在线决策。
why_en: The final design keeps the hot path short: extract identity, hit the right Redis shard, decide atomically, and return 429 fast when over the limit.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> GW[API Gateway]
GW -->|extract id| Router[Shard Router]
Router --> R1[(Redis Shard A)]
Router --> R2[(Redis Shard B)]
Router --> R3[(Redis Shard C)]
R1 --> Rep1[Replica]
GW -->|allow| App[Backend API]
GW -->|429 headers| Client
options_en: The API Gateway enforces limits and returns 429 headers
Redis Cluster shards store token-bucket state
Lua executes bucket updates atomically
Every request is written to an analytics database before deciding

q: Dropbox 设计题的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
options: 从任意设备上传文件
从任意设备下载文件
分享文件并查看别人分享给自己的文件
自动跨设备同步文件
options_en: Upload a file from any device
Download a file from any device
Share a file and view files others have shared with you
Automatically sync files across devices
why: 这题覆盖上传、下载、分享和同步四条用户主路径；编辑文件和免下载预览属于范围外。
why_en: The core Dropbox requirements are upload, download, sharing, and automatic cross-device sync.
q_en: Which core functional requirements are in the Dropbox design? (Select all that apply)

q: Dropbox 设计题里，以下哪些被明确列为 below the line（范围外）？（多选）
options: 文件编辑
无需下载即可预览文件
每用户存储上限
病毒/恶意软件扫描
options_en: File editing
Previewing files without downloading them
A per-user storage limit
Virus / malware scanning
why: 这些是真实产品能力，但不是本设计主线；范围收紧后重点转向大文件传输、同步和可靠性。
why_en: Editing, previewing without download, storage limits, and malware scanning are out of scope for this design.
q_en: Which capabilities are below the line for this Dropbox design? (Select all that apply)

q: Dropbox 的核心非功能需求包括哪些？（多选）

安全可靠，文件丢失或损坏后可恢复

options_en: High availability, favoring availability over strict consistency
Support very large files, from hundreds of GB up to TB scale
Be secure and reliable, recovering files if they are lost or corrupted
Keep upload, download, and sync latency as low as possible

q_en: Which non-functional requirements matter most for Dropbox? (Select all that apply)

scenario: 面试给出设计假设：Dropbox 系统要支持单个文件最大 50GB。
q: 这个 50GB 假设主要决定了哪个设计判断？
options: 这意味着要给 users 表和 files 表重新建索引
文件已经很大，索性放弃所有缓存层
下载可以完全交给数据库处理，不必接入 CDN
单次 POST 不现实，必须做客户端分块和断点续传
options_en: This means the users and files tables need new indexes.
The file is already large, so drop every cache layer entirely.
Downloads can be handled entirely by the database, no CDN needed.
A single POST isn't realistic; the client must chunk and support resumable upload.
why: 50GB 远超单请求的超时和请求体限制，这个量级直接把设计推向客户端分块、进度展示和断点续传。
why_en: A 50GB file makes single-request upload impractical, forcing client-side chunking, progress tracking, and resumable uploads.
q_en: What design decision does the 50GB file-size assumption force?
scenario_en: The interview assumption is that Dropbox must support a maximum single-file size of 50GB.

q: 为什么 Dropbox 通常优先可用性而不是强一致？
options: 用户能接受另一地区几秒后才看到新文件
文件系统不需要任何安全机制
Blob Storage 无法跨区域复制
强一致性反而会让下载更快
options_en: Users can accept seeing a file uploaded elsewhere only a few seconds later.
A file system does not need any security controls.
Blob storage cannot replicate across regions.
Strong consistency actually makes downloads faster.
why: 文件同步允许几秒级延迟，不必像交易系统那样保证全局强一致读到最新写。
why_en: File sync can tolerate a few seconds of delay, unlike transactional systems that must guarantee every read sees the latest write.
tradeoff: 可用性优先（容忍短暂延迟） vs 强一致（每次读最新写）
optionDirectness: 对：另一地区几秒后才看到新文件是可接受的代价。
错：安全性和可用性策略无关，文件系统仍需加密和权限。
错：S3/Blob Storage 本身就支持跨区域复制。
错：强一致通常要等复制确认，反而拖慢下载。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: seeing a file a few seconds late in another region is an acceptable cost.
Wrong: security policy is unrelated to the availability-vs-consistency choice.
Wrong: blob storage like S3 already supports cross-region replication.
Wrong: strong consistency usually waits for replication acks, which slows downloads.
q_en: Why does Dropbox usually favor availability over strong consistency?

q: 补全 Dropbox 的核心实体：

q: 为什么请求体里不应让客户端直接传 user 信息作为授权依据？
options: HTTP 请求体这种格式没办法装下 JSON 数据
客户端传的内容能被伪造，应该从 session 或 JWT 里推导身份
上传时文件名字符会变得越来越长
这个云存储 S3 不支持保存 metadata 字段

This cloud storage, S3, does not support saving metadata fields.

why_en: User identity should come from a trusted auth context like a session or JWT, not from a forgeable request body.
optionDirectness: 错：HTTP body 完全可以是 JSON，这不是原因。
对：身份必须来自服务端验证的会话或令牌，不能信任请求体。
错：文件名长度和授权校验无关。
错：这个问题与 S3 是否支持 metadata 无关。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: HTTP bodies can absolutely contain JSON; that's not the reason.
Correct: identity must come from a server-verified session or token, not the request body.
Wrong: file name length has nothing to do with authorization.
Wrong: this is unrelated to whether S3 supports metadata.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端签发、代表已登录用户身份的凭证。

scenario: 文件 metadata 结构简单、关系少，主要查询模式是按用户列出文件和根据 fileId 做权限检查。

Elasticsearch 作为唯一真相

q_en: Which storage type is the best default for Dropbox metadata?
scenario_en: File metadata is simple, has few relationships, and is mainly queried by user or by fileId for permission checks.

scenario: 用户文件可能很多很大，应用服务器本地磁盘无法可靠、弹性地保存所有原始字节。

Redis Pub/Sub
S3 / GCS 这类 Blob Storage
options_en: The File Service's local file system.
A column in the metadata database.
Redis Pub/Sub.
Blob storage such as S3 or GCS.

whenOtherWins: 极小原型可以先用本地磁盘；生产级大文件和多设备访问才需要托管对象存储。
tradeoff: 托管对象存储的弹性与可靠性 vs 本地磁盘的简单实现
optionDirectness: 错：本地磁盘容量有限，服务器宕机就丢文件。
错：把大字节塞进数据库列会拖慢所有查询。
错：Pub/Sub 是消息通道，不持久化大对象。

Wrong: storing large bytes in a database column slows down every query.
Wrong: Pub/Sub is a messaging channel, not durable object storage.

q: 客户端先上传到 File Service，再由 File Service 上传到 S3 的主要问题是什么？

这个云存储 S3 拒绝接收后端发起的上传
metadata 记录这时候没法正常保存
用户看不到自己上传文件的名字
options_en: The file crosses the backend twice, which is slow, costly, and overloads app servers.
This cloud storage, S3, refuses uploads issued from a backend.
The metadata record cannot be saved properly at this point.
Users cannot see the name of the file they uploaded.
why: 客户端到后端、后端再到 S3，等于传两遍大文件；应用服务器还要扛大对象流量成为瓶颈。
why_en: Routing through the backend sends the file twice and turns application servers into a large-object bottleneck.
optionDirectness: 本题选它：双跳传输浪费带宽和延迟，还占满应用服务器连接。
错：S3 完全接受来自服务端的上传请求。
错：metadata 保存与上传路径无关，可独立完成。
错：文件名是 metadata 字段，与传输路径无关。
optionDirectness_en: Fits here: the double hop wastes bandwidth and latency, and saturates app server connections.
Wrong: S3 fully accepts uploads issued from a backend.
Wrong: saving metadata is independent of how bytes are transferred.
Wrong: the file name is a metadata field, unrelated to the transfer path.
q_en: What is the main problem with proxying uploads through the File Service?

scenario: 要让客户端绕过应用服务器直接上传到 S3，同时仍限制只能上传到授权位置和对象。

预签名上传 URL
让用户手动登录 S3 控制台
把文件先 base64 放进 JSON body

A presigned upload URL.
Have the user log into the S3 console manually.
Base64-encode the file into a JSON body.

why_en: The File Service signs a time-limited, path-scoped URL with its own credentials, so the client can PUT directly to S3 without the backend touching the bytes.
whenOtherWins: 内部管理工具或很小文件可以直接走后端上传；面向用户的大文件路径应绕开后端。
tradeoff: 客户端直传的速度与解耦 vs 后端代理上传的集中控制
optionDirectness: 错：暴露 root key 等于让攻击者拿到整个云账户。
本题选它：限时、限对象路径，客户端拿到就能直传 S3。
错：破坏产品体验，也不是可编程的流程。
错：50GB 塞进 JSON body 会撞穿所有请求大小限制。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: exposing the root key hands an attacker the entire cloud account.
Fits here: time-limited and path-scoped, letting the client upload directly to S3.
Wrong: it breaks the product experience and isn't a programmable flow.
Wrong: base64-encoding a large file into JSON blows past every request size limit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由服务端用云凭证签名、限时限路径的 URL，持有者可直接对该对象操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a time-limited, path-scoped URL signed by the server that lets the holder access that specific object directly.

q_en: What mechanism lets clients upload directly to S3 safely?
scenario_en: Clients should bypass app servers and upload directly to S3, while still being limited to an authorized object path.

q: 把普通 direct-to-S3 上传流程排成正确顺序：
steps: 客户端用 URL 直接 PUT 文件到 Blob Storage
File Service 生成 presigned URL 并把 metadata 标记为 uploading
客户端请求 POST /files/presigned-url 并提交 metadata
S3 通知后端文件已上传
后端把 metadata 状态更新为 uploaded
why: 控制面先建 metadata 和签名 URL，数据面直传 S3；对象到位后再把状态从 uploading 推进到 uploaded。
why_en: The control plane creates metadata and a signed URL first, the client uploads bytes straight to S3, then the backend marks metadata uploaded.

FileSvc -->|signed URL| Client

termDefinitions.meaning: 由服务端用云凭证签名、限时限路径的 URL，持有者可直接对该对象操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a time-limited, path-scoped URL signed by the server that lets the holder access that specific object directly.

q_en: Put the direct-to-S3 upload flow in the right order.

scenario: 上传 API 已从单个 POST /files 演进为先申请上传权限，再把字节直传对象存储。
q: 第一步 control-plane API 应该是什么？
options: GET /files/{fileId}/bytes -> all bytes through backend
DELETE /users/me
POST /files/presigned-url -> PresignedUrl
POST /files/search
options_en: GET /files/{fileId}/bytes streams all bytes through the backend.
DELETE /users/me.
POST /files/presigned-url returns a PresignedUrl.
POST /files/search.
why: 这个接口只处理 metadata、鉴权和签名，不接收文件字节，把应用服务器留在控制面。
why_en: This endpoint only handles metadata, authorization, and signing, keeping large bytes off the application server.
whenOtherWins: 文件很小且赶工期时，单个 POST 上传可以先用；生产级大文件路径必须拆开。
tradeoff: 控制面/数据面分离 vs 单接口实现简单
optionDirectness: 错：字节应走 S3 signed URL，不该经过后端。
错：删除用户与上传流程无关。
本题选它：只做授权和签名，字节走 S3 数据面。
错：搜索接口不属于初版上传 API。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: bytes should flow through an S3 signed URL, not the backend.
Wrong: deleting a user is unrelated to the upload flow.
Fits here: handles only authorization and signing; bytes go through S3 directly.
Wrong: search is not part of the initial upload API.
q_en: What should the first control-plane upload API be?
scenario_en: The upload API has evolved from one POST /files call into requesting upload permission first, then sending bytes to object storage.

q: 使用 Blob Storage 后，metadata 和 file bytes 之间会出现什么一致性问题？
options: 这个云存储 S3 会自动帮你创建用户账号
上传后文件名字段直接就无法保存
CDN 边缘节点会把数据库整个删掉
文件传上去了但 metadata 没存，或者反过来
options_en: This cloud storage, S3, automatically creates a user account for you.
The file name field simply cannot be saved after upload.
A CDN edge node deletes the entire database.
The file uploaded but metadata wasn't saved, or the reverse happened.
why: 大对象和元数据分处两个系统，没有单一事务；需要 status 字段和补偿清理来处理中间态。
why_en: Blob bytes and metadata live in two separate systems with no single transaction, creating partial-success states that need a status field and cleanup.
optionDirectness: 错：S3 不会创建用户账号，两者无关。
错：文件名完全可以正常保存。
错：CDN 不会删除数据库，场景不成立。
本题选它：两个系统各自成功/失败，产生中间不一致态。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: S3 does not create user accounts; unrelated.
Wrong: the file name can absolutely be saved.
Wrong: a CDN does not delete a database; this scenario doesn't apply.
Fits here: each system can succeed or fail independently, leaving an inconsistent middle state.
q_en: What consistency problem appears when metadata and file bytes live separately?

scenario: 用户下载大文件；如果后端先从 S3 下载再转发给用户，会形成双重下载和后端瓶颈。
q: 更好的下载路径是什么？
options: 鉴权后签发 presigned URL，交给客户端直传
所有下载请求都必须先经过后端服务器代理转发
把文件字节直接复制进 Metadata DB 的一列
要求终端用户自己安装一个数据库客户端软件
options_en: Authorize, then issue a presigned URL for the client to use directly.
Every download request must first be proxied through the backend server.
Copy the file bytes directly into a column of the metadata database.
Require end users to install a database client program themselves.
why: 后端只做鉴权和签 URL，数据面由对象存储直接服务，减少带宽、延迟和应用服务器负载。
why_en: The backend only authorizes and signs the URL; object storage serves the bytes directly, cutting bandwidth, latency, and app server load.
whenOtherWins: 需要在线转码、逐字节审计或文件很小时，后端代理仍可以接受。
tradeoff: 直传省后端带宽 vs 后端代理的集中控制/审计
optionDirectness: 本题选它：鉴权后签 URL，数据面完全绕开后端。
错：全量代理会让后端成为下载瓶颈。
错：复制进数据库会拖慢查询也浪费存储。
错：要求装数据库客户端不现实也不安全。
optionDirectness_en: Fits here: authorize then sign, leaving the data plane entirely off the backend.
Wrong: proxying everything turns the backend into a download bottleneck.
Wrong: copying bytes into the database slows queries and wastes storage.
Wrong: requiring a database client is impractical and insecure.
q_en: What is the better download path for large Dropbox files?
scenario_en: A user downloads a large file; if the backend fetches from S3 and forwards it, the file is downloaded twice and bottlenecks the backend.

scenario: S3 bucket 位于单一区域，全球用户下载大文件时跨地域延迟和带宽成本高。
q: 最合适的下载加速方案是什么？
options: 所有用户请求都固定从源站跨洲下载文件
用 CDN 缓存文件并发放短期 signed URL
把这些大文件统一塞进 Redis 内存缓存里
发动所有用户之间互相转发彼此的文件
options_en: Every user request always fetches across continents from the origin.
Cache files at CDN edge nodes and issue short-lived signed URLs.
Stuff all these large files into a Redis in-memory cache.
Have every user relay files back and forth to each other.
why: CDN 把热门文件放到离用户近的边缘节点，signed URL 仍保留访问控制。
why_en: A CDN caches files at edge locations near users while signed URLs keep access controlled.
whenOtherWins: 极冷、私密、只下载一次的文件不值得缓存，直接走 S3 signed URL 更省钱。
tradeoff: 边缘就近分发 vs 直连源站的简单与低成本
optionDirectness: 错：固定回源站，没有利用地理就近优势。
本题选它：边缘节点离用户近，直接解决跨洲延迟。
错：Redis 不是全球分发网络，无法就近服务。
错：用户互传不安全也不可控。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: always hitting one origin ignores geographic proximity.
Fits here: edge nodes sit close to users, directly solving cross-continent latency.
Wrong: Redis is not a global distribution network.
Wrong: peer file relay is insecure and uncontrollable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers near users.

q_en: What is the best way to accelerate global downloads?
scenario_en: The S3 bucket is in one region, so global users downloading large files face high cross-region latency and bandwidth cost.

q: CDN 下载方案的主要成本问题是什么？
options: 这个 CDN 网络完全没办法缓存任何文件
用了 CDN 之后所有下载反而全部变慢
CDN 计费较贵，靠 cache-control 和失效策略控制成本
CDN 边缘节点会绕过所有签名校验机制
options_en: This CDN network cannot cache any files at all.
Using a CDN actually makes every download slower.
CDNs are billed by traffic, so cache-control and invalidation policy controls cost.
CDN edge nodes bypass every signature check.
why: 不是所有文件都值得长期缓存在边缘，尤其是很少访问的私有文件；缓存策略决定成本与新鲜度。
why_en: Not every file deserves long-lived edge caching, especially rarely accessed private files, so cache policy controls cost.
optionDirectness: 错：缓存内容正是 CDN 的核心功能。
错：CDN 恰恰是为了加速，不是减慢。
本题选它：边缘缓存按流量计费，策略决定花多少钱。
错：signed URL 本就为配合 CDN 设计，不会被绕过。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: caching content is the core function of a CDN.
Wrong: a CDN exists to speed up delivery, not slow it down.
Fits here: edge caching is billed by traffic, and policy decides the cost.
Wrong: signed URLs are designed to work with CDNs, not bypass them.
q_en: What cost issue comes with using a CDN for Dropbox downloads?

q: 把 sharelist 直接放在 FileMetadata 中的主要查询问题是什么？
options: 下载单个文件时反而没法检查访问权限
这个字段没法存储 uploadedBy 上传者信息
这时候没法保存文件的大小字段
查看“分享给我”的文件可能要扫描全部文件的 sharelist
options_en: Downloading a single file can no longer check access permission.
This field cannot store the uploadedBy uploader information.
The file size field cannot be saved at this point.
Listing files shared with me may require scanning every file's sharelist.
why: sharelist 放在 metadata 里对单文件鉴权很方便，但反向查 user -> files 需要扫描很多文件。
why_en: A share list on each file's metadata is convenient for single-file checks but makes shared-with-me queries scan many files.
optionDirectness: 错：单文件权限检查恰恰是 sharelist 擅长的场景。
错：uploadedBy 完全能正常保存。
错：文件大小的存储与分享设计无关。
本题选它：inline sharelist 没有反向索引，只能全表扫描。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: single-file permission checks are exactly what a share list handles well.
Wrong: uploadedBy can be stored without issue.
Wrong: file size storage is unrelated to the sharing design.
Fits here: an inline share list has no reverse index, so it must scan every file.
q_en: What query problem comes from storing sharelist inside FileMetadata?

scenario: 用户打开页面时需要快速看到所有别人分享给自己的文件，不能扫描全量 FileMetadata。
q: 更合适的数据模型是什么？
options: 只在每个 FileMetadata 里放一份 sharelist 字段
每次请求都在线扫描一遍所有文件
SharedFiles 表：userId 分区键，fileId 排序键
让客户端自己维护一张全局权限表
options_en: Keep only a sharelist field inside each FileMetadata.
Scan through every file online on each request.
A SharedFiles table: userId as partition key, fileId as sort key.
Let the client maintain its own global permissions table.
why: SharedFiles 直接建模 user -> shared file 的反向关系，查询某用户被分享的文件很快，也免去双写同步。
why_en: A SharedFiles table models the user-to-shared-file relationship directly, making shared-with-me lookups fast without a dual-write sync problem.
whenOtherWins: 分享功能很少用、只需单文件鉴权时，metadata 内 sharelist 更简单。
tradeoff: 规范化反向表的查询效率 vs 内联 sharelist 的实现简单
optionDirectness: 错：只能扫描全部文件才能反查，规模变大就慢。
错：在线全表扫描不可接受，无法承载真实流量。
本题选它：userId 分区、fileId 排序，反查用户分享秒级完成。
错：客户端维护权限表既不安全也不一致。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: it can only be answered by scanning every file, which doesn't scale.
Wrong: an online full scan on every request cannot handle real traffic.
Fits here: partitioning by userId with fileId as sort key makes reverse lookups instant.
Wrong: client-maintained permissions are neither secure nor consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 用来决定数据分布和主查询路径的主键字段。

User[User] --> Share[(SharedFiles)]
Share --> File[File metadata]

File --> Blob[(Blob object)]
q_en: What data model best supports the shared-with-me view?
scenario_en: The shared-with-me page must list all files shared with a user quickly, without scanning every FileMetadata record.

scenario: 需要在 DynamoDB 中查询某个用户收到的所有分享，并允许一个用户拥有多条 shared file 记录。
q: 哪种主键设计最贴合？
options: PK=fileId, 无 sort key
PK=userId, SK=fileId
PK=fileName
PK=mimeType
options_en: PK=fileId, with no sort key.
PK=userId, SK=fileId.
PK=fileName.
PK=mimeType.

| userId (PK) | fileId (SK) |
| user1       | fileId1     |
| user1       | fileId2     |
| user2       | fileId3     |
why: userId 分区能高效列出该用户收到的分享，fileId 排序键支持一个用户多条记录并保持唯一。
why_en: Partitioning by userId lists a user's shared files efficiently, while fileId as the sort key allows many records per user with uniqueness.
whenOtherWins: 如果主查询是 file -> users，需要改用 fileId 分区或额外反向索引。
tradeoff: 按 user 高效反查 vs 按 file 高效反查
optionDirectness: 错：fileId 分区无法支持按用户高效反查。
本题选它：完全匹配「按用户列出分享」这个查询模式。
错：fileName 不是查询模式，也可能重复。
错：mimeType 把文件类型和授权混在一起。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: partitioning by fileId gives no benefit for per-user lookups.
Fits here: matches exactly the 'list shares by user' query pattern.
Wrong: fileName isn't the query pattern and can collide.
Wrong: mimeType conflates file type with authorization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定数据分布和主要查询路径的主键字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key is the primary key field that determines data distribution and the main query path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区键相同时用于排序和唯一区分记录的辅助键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The sort key orders and uniquely distinguishes records that share the same partition key.

q_en: Which DynamoDB key design best fits shared-with-me queries?
scenario_en: In DynamoDB, the system must list all files shared with a user and allow many shared-file records per user.

q: inverse sharedFiles cache 相比规范化 SharedFiles 表的主要风险是什么？
options: 反向缓存根本没法加速 shared-with-me 查询
这种反向缓存结构不能存 fileId 字段
必须和 sharelist 保持同步，双写失败就会不一致
这种缓存结构只能用在下载场景里
options_en: This inverse cache cannot speed up shared-with-me queries at all.
This inverse cache structure cannot store the fileId field.
It must stay in sync with the sharelist; a partial write leaves them inconsistent.
This cache structure can only be used for the download scenario.
why: 反向 cache 查询快，但如果和 sharelist 不同步，权限和列表就会出错；正规化到同一张表能减少双写。
why_en: An inverse cache is fast to read but risks drifting from the file metadata share list unless both are updated together.
tradeoff: 反向缓存的读取速度 vs 单一数据源的一致性
optionDirectness: 错：反向索引正是为了加速这类查询而存在。
错：fileId 完全可以作为反向缓存的值存储。
本题选它：两处数据、两次写，任一失败就产生不一致。
错：反向索引可用于列表、鉴权等多种场景。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: an inverse index exists precisely to speed up this query.
Wrong: fileId can absolutely be stored as the cache's value.
Fits here: two copies of the data need two writes, and either can fail alone.
Wrong: an inverse index serves listing and authorization, not just downloads.
q_en: What is the main risk of an inverse sharedFiles cache?

q: Local -> Remote 同步中，客户端 sync agent 需要做哪些事？（多选）
options: 监听本地 Dropbox 文件夹的文件系统事件
检测变更后本地排队待上传文件
调用上传 API 把变更推到远端
把远端当作 source of truth 尽快更新
options_en: Watch the local Dropbox folder for filesystem events.
Queue changed files locally after detecting a change.
Call the upload API to push changes to the remote server.
Treat the remote server as the source of truth and update it quickly.
why: 本地变更先被 agent 捕捉并排队，再通过上传 API 推到远端；远端是 source of truth。
why_en: The sync agent watches local changes, queues them, pushes updates through the upload API, and treats the remote server as the source of truth.
q_en: What should the client sync agent do for local-to-remote sync? (Select all that apply)

q: Dropbox 这个设计对同步冲突采用的简化策略是什么？
options: 人工合并每个字节
所有冲突都拒绝
强一致锁住全球文件
last write wins
options_en: Manually merge every byte.
Reject every conflicting write.
Lock the file globally for strong consistency.
Last write wins.
why: 版本控制被放到范围外，所以用 last write wins 简化冲突；真实产品通常保留旧块或用版本号，而不是直接覆盖。
why_en: The design simplifies conflicts with last-write-wins, since versioning is explicitly out of scope.
optionDirectness: 错：逐字节人工合并不可能自动化。
错：拒绝所有冲突会让用户无法正常保存文件。
错：全局锁文件不现实，也违背高可用目标。
本题选它：范围外的版本控制被简化成最后写入生效。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: manually merging every byte cannot be automated.
Wrong: rejecting every conflict would block normal saves.
Wrong: a global file lock is impractical and fights the availability goal.
Fits here: with versioning out of scope, the last write simply wins.
q_en: What simplified conflict strategy does this Dropbox design use?

q: Remote -> Local 只用 polling（轮询）同步，缺点是什么？
options: 变更发现慢，且没有变更时也浪费带宽/请求
无法保证最终一致
必须持久连接
不能使用 since timestamp
options_en: Change detection is slow, and idle polls waste bandwidth and requests.
It cannot guarantee eventual consistency.
It requires a persistent connection.
It cannot use a since timestamp.
why: 轮询简单可靠，但实时性差；没有变化时的请求也是纯浪费。
why_en: Polling is simple and reliable but detects changes slowly, and idle polls waste requests when nothing changed.
tradeoff: 轮询的简单可靠 vs 推送的实时性
optionDirectness: 本题选它：固定周期问一次，变化发现天然滞后。
错：轮询本身能保证最终一致，只是慢。
错：轮询是周期性请求，不需要持久连接。
错：轮询正好用 since timestamp 过滤增量。
optionDirectness_en: Fits here: asking on a fixed interval inherently delays change detection.
Wrong: polling still guarantees eventual consistency, just slowly.
Wrong: polling is periodic requests, not a persistent connection.
Wrong: polling is exactly how a since-timestamp filter is used.
q_en: What is the drawback of polling-only remote-to-local sync?

scenario: 客户端需要尽快知道远端文件变化，但 WebSocket/SSE 连接可能断开，消息也可能丢。
q: Dropbox 同步最稳妥的通知策略是什么？
options: 同步这件事完全只靠每小时轮询一次
单连接推送 change event，再靠周期性 polling 兜底
给每一个文件单独开一条 WebSocket 连接
同步通知完全依赖发邮件来提醒用户
options_en: Sync relies entirely on polling once every hour.
One connection pushes change events, backed by periodic polling.
Open a separate WebSocket connection for every single file.
Sync notifications rely entirely on sending emails to users.
why: push 给近实时体验，周期性 GET /files/changes 捕捉断线期间漏掉的事件，两者互补。
why_en: Push delivers near-real-time updates while periodic polling catches anything missed during a dropped connection.
whenOtherWins: 极简单低频系统可以只轮询；真正实时协作编辑需要更强的实时协议。
tradeoff: 推送的实时性 vs 轮询的可靠兜底
optionDirectness: 错：每小时轮询的延迟对同步体验来说太慢。
本题选它：单连接推送快，轮询兜底不丢事件。
错：每文件一条连接会耗尽连接和内存资源。
错：邮件延迟太高，无法支撑近实时同步。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: hourly polling is far too slow for acceptable sync latency.
Fits here: one push connection is fast, and polling backs it up so nothing is missed.
Wrong: a connection per file exhausts connections and memory.
Wrong: email is too slow to support near-real-time sync.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开的双向通信连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent, bidirectional connection between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器向客户端单向推送事件的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE (Server-Sent Events) lets a server push a one-way stream of events to the client.

q_en: What notification strategy is safest for Dropbox sync?
scenario_en: Clients need to learn about remote file changes quickly, but WebSocket or SSE connections can disconnect and miss messages.

q: 把 Remote -> Local 混合同步流程排成正确顺序：
steps: 客户端周期性调用 GET /files/changes?since={timestamp} 补漏
远端文件 metadata 发生 created/updated/deleted
服务器通过单条设备连接推送 change notification
客户端按通知拉取 metadata 或文件内容
如果推送连接断开，轮询仍能发现 missed changes
why: push 是快路径，polling 是可靠性兜底；两者都围绕 since timestamp 或 change cursor 收敛到一致。
why_en: Push is the fast path and periodic polling is the reliability fallback, both converging around a since-timestamp or change cursor.

flowchart LR

A dropped connection forces a restart from the beginning.
Users cannot see fine-grained progress.

options_en: Bandwidth should be capped at 10Mbps for billing purposes.
The upload endpoint needs no timeout settings at all.

scenario_en: The interview estimate says a 50GB file over a 100Mbps connection takes about 4,000 seconds, or roughly 1.11 hours.

数据库的连接数需要相应调大十倍

options_en: Just remove the API Gateway layer entirely.
A 50GB file can never fit through a single API-Gateway request.
Database connection limits need to be increased tenfold.

scenario: 要上传 50GB 文件，用户需要看到进度，断网或关浏览器后也能从已完成部分继续。
q: 应该采用什么策略？
options: 让服务端先收完整 50GB 文件再切块处理
直接禁止用户上传任何大文件
把整个文件塞进一个巨大的 JSON 字段里
客户端切成 5-10MB chunks 上传，支持断点续传
options_en: Have the server receive the full 50GB file before chunking it.
Simply disallow users from uploading any large file.
Stuff the entire file into one giant JSON field.
The client uploads in 5-10MB chunks with resumable support.
why: chunking 必须发生在客户端，否则仍然要先上传完整文件到服务器。chunk 粒度让进度、并行和断点续传都可实现。
why_en: Chunking must happen on the client, otherwise the whole file still has to be sent first; chunk granularity enables progress, parallelism, and resumability.
whenOtherWins: 很小文件可以单次上传；大文件和不稳定网络应使用分块/Multipart。
tradeoff: 客户端分块的可恢复性 vs 单请求实现的简单
diagram:
flowchart LR
LargeFile[Large file] --> Split[Split chunks]
Split --> Upload[Parallel uploads]
Upload --> Blob[(Multipart storage)]
Blob --> Complete[Complete upload]
Complete --> Meta[(Metadata DB)]
optionDirectness: 错：服务端先收完整文件等于没解决超时和限制问题。
错：禁止大文件违背核心产品需求。
错：JSON 字段无法承载 GB 级二进制内容。
本题选它：客户端切块才能真正实现进度和断点续传。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: the server still needs the whole file first, defeating the purpose.
Wrong: disallowing large files contradicts the core requirement.
Wrong: a JSON field cannot hold gigabytes of binary content.
Fits here: only client-side chunking actually enables progress and resumability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大对象拆成多个部分分别上传，再由存储服务合并的机制。

scenario_en: A 50GB upload needs progress feedback and must resume after a network drop or browser close.

q: 分块上传的 chunk 大小应该怎么理解？
text: chunk 大小不是死记数字：太大时{{失败重传成本高}}；太小时{{请求和元数据开销高}}；5-10MB 只是常见面试锚点。
why: 真正要记的是取舍：chunk 要够小，断线后不用重传整份大文件；也要够大，避免请求数、ETag 列表和进度状态爆炸。实际上下限看云厂商 multipart API。
why_en: The point is the tradeoff, not a magic number: chunks should be small enough for cheap retries and large enough to avoid excessive requests and metadata.
tradeoff: 失败重传成本 vs 请求/元数据开销

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端为了断点续传，把大文件切出来的一段字节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chunk is a byte range split from a large file so upload can resume after failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象存储提供的分块上传能力；每个云厂商会规定 part 的最小、最大大小和数量。

q: 只让客户端 PATCH chunk 状态的安全风险是什么？
options: 恶意客户端可伪造 chunk 状态，造成数据不一致
这样一来客户端就没法正常显示上传进度
这个云存储 S3 就不会返回上传成功
metadata 这张表没法存储数组字段
options_en: A malicious client can forge chunk status, causing data inconsistency.
This means the client can no longer show upload progress properly.
This cloud storage, S3, would not return upload success.
The metadata table cannot store array fields.
why: 客户端状态可伪造，不能当最终真相；需要服务端用 S3 校验后再确认整体状态。
why_en: Client-reported status can be forged and cannot be trusted as ground truth without server-side verification against S3.
optionDirectness: 本题选它：客户端可以谎报，造成 metadata 和 S3 实际状态脱节。
错：进度展示照常可以做。
错：这个风险和 S3 是否返回成功无关。
错：数组字段完全能存进 metadata 表。
optionDirectness_en: Fits here: a client can lie, decoupling metadata from what S3 actually has.
Wrong: progress display still works fine.
Wrong: this risk is unrelated to whether S3 returns success.
Wrong: array fields can absolutely be stored in the metadata table.

termDefinitions.meaning: S3 为对象或分片返回的校验值，用于确认内容是否匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ETag is a checksum S3 returns for an object or part, used to confirm the content matches.

q_en: What is the security risk of letting the client PATCH chunk status by itself?

scenario: 客户端上传每个 part 后拿到 ETag；后端需要确认这些 parts 确实存在于 S3 multipart upload 中。
q: 后端应如何验证 chunk 状态？
options: 后端完全信任客户端上报的 PATCH body
调用 S3 ListParts 校验 part 和 ETag
只看客户端本地显示的进度条数值
仅凭上传的文件名判断上传状态
options_en: The backend fully trusts the client-reported PATCH body.
Call S3 ListParts to verify the part number and ETag.
Just look at the progress bar value shown on the client.
Judge upload status purely from the uploaded file name.
why: S3 multipart 的单个 part 不触发事件通知，ListParts 能列出已上传 part 及 ETag 供后端核对。
why_en: Individual multipart parts don't trigger event notifications, so ListParts lets the backend confirm what S3 actually received.
whenOtherWins: 如果存储提供可靠的逐 part webhook，可改用事件驱动校验。
tradeoff: 服务端校验的可信度 vs 信任客户端上报的简单
optionDirectness: 错：完全信任客户端等于放弃校验。
本题选它：直接问 S3 已上传了哪些 part 和对应 ETag。
错：进度条只是 UI 状态，不代表存储真实情况。
错：文件名不包含任何分片上传信息。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: fully trusting the client abandons verification entirely.
Fits here: it asks S3 directly which parts and ETags actually exist.
Wrong: a progress bar is UI state, not storage truth.
Wrong: the file name carries no part-upload information.
q_en: How should the backend verify uploaded chunk state?
scenario_en: After each uploaded part, the client receives an ETag; the backend must verify those parts really exist in the S3 multipart upload.

q: 文件 fingerprint 在断点续传/去重中解决哪些问题？（多选）
options: 判断同一内容的文件是否以前尝试上传过
找到已经上传过的 chunks
避免把普通文件名当唯一标识
替代 fileId 作为 metadata 主键
options_en: Determining whether content identical to this file was uploaded before.
Finding which chunks have already been uploaded.
Avoiding relying on the plain file name as a unique identifier.
Replacing fileId as the metadata primary key.
why: fingerprint 基于内容识别重复和续传状态；fileId（如 UUID）仍应是 metadata 的主键，fingerprint 只是辅助字段。
why_en: Content fingerprints identify duplicates and resume state by content, while the file record still needs its own unique ID such as a UUID.
optionDirectness: 对：内容相同则 fingerprint 相同，能识别重复上传尝试。
对：chunk 级 fingerprint 能精确定位已传部分。
对：内容而非文件名才是可靠的去重依据。
错：fingerprint 是辅助字段，不该替代独立的 fileId。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: identical content produces the same fingerprint, revealing repeat upload attempts.
Correct: chunk-level fingerprints pinpoint exactly which parts already made it.
Correct: content, not the file name, is what makes dedup reliable.
Wrong: fingerprints should complement, not replace, an independent fileId.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于文件内容计算出的哈希值，如 SHA-256，用于识别相同内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fingerprint is a content hash, such as SHA-256, used to identify identical content.

q: 把大文件 multipart upload 流程排成正确顺序：
steps: 客户端用每个 part 的 presigned URL 上传 chunk，并回报 ETag
客户端计算整文件和每个 chunk 的 fingerprint
