后端 CreateMultipartUpload，保存 uploading metadata，并返回 uploadId 和各 part URL
后端用 ListParts 验证 chunks 后更新状态
why: 先识别内容和续传状态，再建 multipart session；所有 part 验证通过后才调用 CompleteMultipartUpload。
why_en: The flow fingerprints content first, opens a multipart session, uploads and verifies parts, then completes assembly.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Init[Create upload session] --> Urls[Get chunk URLs]
Urls --> Put[PUT chunks]
Put --> Verify[Backend verifies parts]
Verify --> Commit[Commit metadata]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大对象拆成多个部分分别上传，再由存储服务合并的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multipart upload splits a large object into parts uploaded separately, then assembled by the storage service.

termDefinitions.meaning: S3 为对象或分片返回的校验值，用于确认内容是否匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ETag is a checksum S3 returns for an object or part, used to confirm the content matches.

q_en: Put the large-file multipart upload flow in the right order.

q: 为什么 multipart upload 不意味着下载也必须按原始 chunks 下载？
options: 这个云存储 S3 永远只保存成多个不可组合的 parts
CDN 网络完全没办法下载大文件
组装完成后就是普通对象，下载可用 signed URL 或 Range
现在的浏览器完全没法处理 Range 请求
options_en: This cloud storage, S3, always keeps it as separate, unmergeable parts.
A CDN network cannot download large files at all.
Once assembled it is a normal object; downloads can use a signed URL or Range.
Modern browsers simply cannot handle Range requests.
why: multipart 是上传协议细节，完成后对象表现为一个普通对象；下载靠 HTTP Range 而不是知道原始 chunk 边界。
why_en: Multipart is only an upload-time detail; once complete, the object behaves like any normal object, and downloads can use HTTP Range requests.
tradeoff: 上传时的分片协议 vs 下载时的完整对象语义
optionDirectness: 错：CompleteMultipartUpload 正是为了合并成单一对象。
错：CDN 完全可以缓存和分发大对象。
本题选它：完成后是普通对象，下载不需要知道原始分片。
错：现代浏览器和 HTTP 原生支持 Range 请求。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: CompleteMultipartUpload exists specifically to merge parts into one object.
Wrong: a CDN can cache and serve large objects fine.
Fits here: once complete, it's a normal object, so downloads don't need the original chunk boundaries.
Wrong: modern browsers and HTTP natively support Range requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端只请求资源的某个字节区间，而不是整个文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An HTTP Range request asks for only a byte range of a resource instead of the whole file.

q_en: Why does multipart upload not force downloads to use the original chunks?

scenario: 文件只修改了一小段，跨设备同步时不希望重新上传/下载整个大文件。
q: 应该如何加速同步？
options: 总是重传整个文件
删除本地文件后重新下载
把变化写进 HTTP header
只同步发生变化的 chunks
options_en: Always retransmit the entire file.
Delete the local file and re-download it.
Write the change into an HTTP header.
Sync only the chunks that changed.
why: 分块除了帮上传恢复，也能让同步只传变化的块，小修改传输量大幅下降。
why_en: Chunking also enables syncing only the changed pieces, so a small edit transfers far fewer bytes than the whole file.
whenOtherWins: 小文件或变化遍布全文件时，整文件传输更简单且开销可接受。
tradeoff: 只传变化块的效率 vs 整文件传输的实现简单
optionDirectness: 错：整文件重传对小修改是巨大浪费。
错：删除重下比只传差异慢得多。
错：HTTP header 装不下文件内容变化。
本题选它：只传变化的部分，小改动几乎不占带宽。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: retransmitting the whole file is wasteful for a tiny change.
Wrong: delete-and-redownload is far slower than sending just the diff.
Wrong: HTTP headers cannot carry file content changes.
Fits here: transferring only the changed pieces costs almost nothing for a small edit.
q_en: How should Dropbox speed up sync after a small file edit?
scenario_en: Only a small part of a file changed, and cross-device sync should not upload or download the whole large file again.

q: 固定大小 chunk 在文件开头插入 1 字节会造成什么问题？
options: 后续 chunk 边界全偏移，fingerprint 大多跟着变化
插入字节之后只有第一个 chunk 会发生变化
这时候文件就没法再进行加密了
这时候 CDN 就没办法缓存这个文件了
options_en: All downstream chunk boundaries shift, and most fingerprints change too.
Only the first chunk changes after the byte is inserted.
The file can no longer be encrypted at this point.
A CDN can no longer cache this file at this point.
why: 固定边界对插入/删除很敏感，一次偏移会连锁改变后续所有块的哈希。
why_en: Fixed boundaries are sensitive to insertions; one shift cascades and changes the hash of every downstream chunk.
optionDirectness: 本题选它：边界全部后移，后续块内容和哈希跟着全变。
错：不止第一块，后面所有块都会跟着变化。
错：加密与 chunk 边界策略无关。
错：CDN 缓存能力和分块策略无关。
optionDirectness_en: Fits here: every downstream boundary shifts, so nearly every hash changes too.
Wrong: far more than just the first chunk changes.
Wrong: encryption is unrelated to chunk boundary strategy.
Wrong: CDN caching ability is unrelated to chunking strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于文件内容计算出的哈希值，用于识别相同内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fingerprint is a content hash used to identify identical content.

q_en: What happens when one byte is inserted at the start of fixed-size chunks?

scenario: 希望小范围编辑只影响附近块，而不是让后面所有固定大小块都重新计算和同步。
q: 应采用哪种 chunk 边界策略？
options: 永远固定每 5MB 切一刀，边界从不改变
CDC：用 rolling hash 按内容决定边界
按照文件名字符串的长度来切块
按照上传用户的 ID 来决定切块方式
options_en: Always cut every fixed 5MB; the boundary never changes.
CDC: use a rolling hash to set boundaries by content.
Chunk based on the length of the file name string.
Chunk based on the uploading user's ID.
why: CDC 用内容模式决定边界，小插入通常只影响周围少数 chunk。
why_en: Content-defined chunking sets boundaries from content patterns, so a small edit usually affects only a few nearby chunks.
whenOtherWins: 只需要上传续传、不做 delta sync 时，固定大小分块更简单。
tradeoff: 内容边界的局部影响 vs 固定边界的实现简单
diagram:
flowchart LR
File[File bytes] --> Rolling[Rolling hash]
Rolling --> Boundary[Content boundaries]
Boundary --> Fingerprint[Chunk fingerprints]
Fingerprint --> Delta[Upload changed chunks]
optionDirectness: 错：固定边界会让编辑点之后的所有块都偏移。
本题选它：边界跟着内容走，编辑影响被限制在局部。
错：文件名长度和文件内容毫无关系。
错：用户 ID 是授权信息，不该决定数据切分。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: fixed boundaries shift every chunk after the edit point.
Fits here: boundaries follow content, so an edit's impact stays local.
Wrong: file name length has nothing to do with file content.
Wrong: user ID is authorization data, not a basis for splitting bytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随窗口滑动增量计算的哈希，用于在内容中快速定位分块边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rolling hash is computed incrementally as a window slides over the data, used to quickly locate chunk boundaries by content.

q_en: Which chunk-boundary strategy keeps small edits local?
scenario_en: A small edit should only affect nearby chunks, not force every later fixed-size chunk to be recalculated and synced.

q: 提升上传、下载和同步速度的手段有哪些？（多选）
options: CDN 加速下载
chunks 并行上传和自适应 chunk 大小
只同步变化 chunks
对适合的文件客户端压缩后再上传
options_en: CDN accelerates downloads.
Parallel chunk upload with adaptive chunk size.
Sync only the changed chunks.
Compress suitable files on the client before uploading.
why: 下载靠就近边缘节点，上传靠并行分块，同步靠只传差异，压缩靠减少字节。
why_en: Downloads benefit from a nearby CDN edge, uploads from parallel chunking, sync from delta transfer, and suitable files from compression.
q_en: Which techniques improve upload, download, and sync speed? (Select all that apply)

scenario: 客户端准备上传一个 5GB 文本文件，网络较慢；压缩时间可能小于节省的传输时间。
q: 是否应压缩？
options: 不应压缩任何文件
必须让后端下载后再压缩
应在客户端压缩后上传，下载后客户端解压
先加密再压缩以提高压缩率
options_en: Never compress any file.
Have the backend download the file then compress it.
Compress on the client before uploading, decompress on the client after downloading.
Encrypt first, then compress to raise the compression ratio.
why: 文本类文件压缩比高，客户端压缩省传输字节且不让后端进数据路径。
why_en: Text files compress well, so client-side compression saves transfer bytes without pulling the backend into the data path.
whenOtherWins: PNG、视频等已压缩媒体收益很小，压缩/解压时间可能不值得。
tradeoff: 压缩节省传输时间 vs 压缩/解压本身消耗的时间
optionDirectness: 错：文本文件压缩收益明显，一律不压缩会浪费带宽。
错：后端下载后压缩仍先传了未压缩的完整文件。
本题选它：客户端压缩上传、客户端解压下载，后端不参与。
错：加密后数据近似随机，压缩效果会变差。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: text compresses well, so never compressing wastes bandwidth.
Wrong: downloading first still transfers the uncompressed file once already.
Fits here: compress on the client, decompress on the client, backend stays out of it.
Wrong: encrypting first makes data look random, hurting compression.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的通用压缩算法，速度与压缩比各有取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gzip, Brotli, and Zstandard are common general-purpose compression algorithms with different speed/ratio tradeoffs.

q_en: Should Dropbox compress this upload?
scenario_en: The client is uploading a 5GB text file over a slow network, and compression time may be less than the transfer time saved.

q: 为什么需要先压缩再加密？
options: 压缩会破坏所有加密
S3 不支持加密文件
CDN 只能服务未压缩文件
加密会让数据近似随机，先加密后压缩通常几乎压不动
options_en: Compression breaks all encryption.
S3 does not support encrypted files.
A CDN can only serve uncompressed files.
Encryption makes data look random, so compressing after encrypting barely shrinks it.
why: 压缩依赖数据里的冗余模式，加密恰恰要消除这种模式，所以要先压缩再加密。
why_en: Compression relies on redundancy in the data, and encryption is designed to remove exactly that pattern, so compress before you encrypt.
tradeoff: 先压缩后加密的高压缩比 vs 顺序颠倒时几乎无压缩收益
optionDirectness: 错：压缩本身不会破坏加密，问题在顺序。
错：S3 完全支持存储加密后的对象。
错：CDN 能正常缓存和分发已压缩内容。
本题选它：加密后的数据像随机噪声，压缩找不到规律。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: compression itself doesn't break encryption; ordering does.
Wrong: S3 fully supports storing encrypted objects.
Wrong: a CDN can cache and serve compressed content fine.
Fits here: encrypted data looks like noise, giving compression nothing to exploit.
q_en: Why should compression happen before encryption?

q: Dropbox 文件安全应覆盖哪些基础措施？（多选）
options: HTTPS 加密传输
S3/server-side encryption at rest
基于 share table / ACL 的访问控制
短期 signed URL
options_en: HTTPS encrypts data in transit.
Server-side encryption at rest in S3.
Access control based on a share table / ACL.
Short-lived signed URLs.
why: 传输、静态存储、访问控制、临时令牌是文件安全的四个基础层。
why_en: File security layers encryption in transit, encryption at rest, ACL-based access control, and short-lived signed URLs.
q_en: Which baseline security measures should Dropbox file storage cover? (Select all that apply)

q: signed URL 的安全局限是什么？
options: 它是 bearer token，拿到 URL 的人都能下载
这种签名 URL 完全没有办法设置过期时间
这种 URL 完全不能配合 CDN 一起使用
这种 URL 里必须包含用户的登录密码
options_en: It's a bearer token; whoever holds the URL can download it.
This signed URL has absolutely no way to set an expiration.
This kind of URL cannot be used together with a CDN at all.
This URL must contain the user's login password.
why: 短过期时间只能缩小泄露窗口，不能阻止持有者转发；更高安全场景可加 IP 绑定。
why_en: A short expiry only narrows the exposure window; it cannot stop a holder from forwarding the URL to someone else.
optionDirectness: 本题选它：谁拿到 URL 谁就能下载，直到它过期。
错：signed URL 恰恰以设置过期时间为核心机制。
错：CDN 的 signed URL 正是常见用法。
错：签名本身就是凭证，无需塞进密码。
optionDirectness_en: Fits here: whoever holds the URL can download until it expires.
Wrong: expiration is the core mechanism of a signed URL.
Wrong: signed URLs with a CDN are a common, well-supported pattern.
Wrong: the signature itself is the credential; no password is needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只要持有该凭证就能使用对应权限的令牌，不额外验证持有者身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bearer token grants access to whoever holds it, without further verifying the holder's identity.

q_en: What is the security limitation of a signed URL?

q: 把 CDN signed URL 的验证流程排成正确顺序：
steps: CDN 收到请求后用公钥验证签名并检查过期/限制
服务端用私钥对 path、expiration 等生成签名 URL
授权用户拿到 signed URL
验证通过则 CDN 返回内容，否则拒绝
用户向 CDN 请求该 URL
why: 服务端用私钥签发短期访问权，CDN 在边缘验证签名和过期时间，无需每次回源问应用服务。
why_en: The server signs short-lived access with its private key, and the CDN verifies the signature and expiry at the edge without asking the origin every time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> App[File Service]
App --> Token[Signed URL]
Client --> CDN[CDN validates token]
CDN --> Blob[(Blob origin)]
q_en: Put the CDN signed-URL validation flow in the right order.

q: 把“大文件上传”这一 marquee 决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 用 S3 multipart upload、per-part presigned URL 和 ETag/ListParts 验证
成本：metadata 和 object state 需要处理 uploading/complete/cleanup
需求：50GB 文件、进度条、断点续传、低后端带宽
选择客户端 chunking，避免服务端先收完整文件
用 fingerprint 支持续传和去重判断
why: 需求先排除单 POST，再把分块、指纹和 multipart 组合起来；代价是控制面状态机更复杂，但后端不再扛大对象流量。
why_en: The requirements rule out single-POST upload, then combine client chunking, fingerprints, and multipart upload, at the cost of a more complex control-plane state machine.
q_en: Put the large-file-upload decision chain in the right order.

q: Dropbox 这道题里，Senior 及以上候选人应主动深入哪些方向？（多选）
options: presigned URL / Blob Storage 直传
multipart upload、resumable upload 和 ETag 校验
CDN 下载、delta sync、content-defined chunking
把所有文件放进应用服务器本地磁盘
options_en: Presigned URLs and direct blob storage transfer.
Multipart upload, resumable upload, and ETag verification.
CDN downloads, delta sync, and content-defined chunking.
Storing all files on the application server's local disk.
why: 面试期望 Senior 快速过基础 API 和元数据模型，把时间花在大文件传输优化上。
why_en: Senior candidates are expected to move quickly through the basic API and data model, spending their time on large-file transfer optimizations.
optionDirectness: 对：直传避免后端代理大对象，是 Senior 必须掌握的优化。
对：处理 50GB 文件的核心复杂度都在这里。
对：这些是传输和同步的深度优化内容。
错：把文件放本地磁盘违背了整个设计的可靠性目标。
optionDirectness_en: Correct: direct transfer avoids proxying large objects through the backend, core senior-level knowledge.
Correct: this is where most of the complexity of handling a 50GB file lives.
Correct: these are deep optimizations for transfer and sync.
Wrong: storing files on local disk contradicts the whole design's reliability goal.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client Sync Agent] -->|metadata/auth| FileSvc[File Service]
FileSvc --> Meta[(Metadata DB)]
FileSvc -->|signed URL| Client
Client -->|upload/download bytes| S3[(S3 Blob Storage)]
S3 --> CDN[CDN]
CDN --> Client
FileSvc -->|push changes| Client
q_en: What should a senior candidate proactively dive into for Dropbox? (Select all that apply)

q: 端到端延迟目标定为 < 200ms，这个数字的依据是什么？
options: 建立连接的三次握手大约耗时 200ms 左右
本设计选定的体验目标，不是协议强制值
服务器推流协议规范里规定的最大间隔
内容分发网络边缘缓存的默认刷新周期
why: 200ms 不是硬分界，而是本设计采用的实时体验目标：低于这个量级通常会被感知为很快、接近即时。更严格的交互目标常会用 100ms 量级。
why_en: Two hundred milliseconds is a practical realtime target rather than a hard perception boundary; interactions under that range usually feel very fast, while stricter instant-feedback targets are often closer to 100ms.
options_en: The connection three-way handshake takes about 200ms.
This design's chosen target, not a protocol requirement.
The maximum interval defined by the server-push spec.
The default refresh period for the content delivery network cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

scenario: 面试官问你为什么把端到端延迟目标定在 200ms，而不是直接照抄某个协议或基础设施参数。
q_en: Why is the end-to-end latency target set below 200ms?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why the end-to-end latency target is 200ms instead of copying a protocol or infrastructure number.

scenario: 直播评论系统：不同观众看到同一条评论的时间略有先后完全无伤大雅，但评论区整体不可用会毁掉直播体验。
q: 非功能需求上该怎么做 CAP 取舍？
options: 一致性优先：所有观众必须在同一瞬间看到同一条评论
放弃分区容忍，假设网络永不分区
可用性优先、接受最终一致：评论晚几百毫秒到达没关系
用分布式事务同时保证强一致和高可用
why: 评论属于典型的可容忍短暂不同步的数据，所以可用性优先、最终一致即可。这条取舍直接决定了后面能用 DynamoDB、Redis pub/sub 这类偏可用的组件。
why_en: Live comments tolerate brief staleness, so the system prioritizes availability over consistency and accepts eventual consistency.
whenOtherWins: 涉及钱、库存扣减、订单这类不能读到旧值的业务必须倒向强一致，宁可短暂拒绝服务。
optionMeanings: 强一致优先的取舍
不现实：网络必然会分区
可用性优先、最终一致
同时硬要两者的强一致
optionDirectness: 本场景不需要瞬时一致
分区是分布式系统常态
评论可容忍短暂不同步
CAP 下强一致和高可用不可兼得
tradeoff: 可用性优先(最终一致) vs 强一致性
options_en: Consistency first: every viewer must see a comment at the exact same instant.
Drop partition tolerance and assume the network never partitions.
Availability first with eventual consistency: comments landing a few hundred ms late is fine.
Use distributed transactions to guarantee strong consistency and high availability together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统里一致性、可用性、分区容忍性三者的取舍框架
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP describes the tradeoff among consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许短暂不同步，但保证副本最终收敛到相同值
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows brief staleness but guarantees replicas converge over time.

q_en: How should we make the CAP tradeoff for live comments?
scenario_en: In live comments, viewers can see the same comment slightly apart in time, but an unavailable comment experience ruins the live stream.

q: FB Live Comments 的规模（scale）目标是？
options: 数百万路并发直播，单场直播每秒可达数千条评论
几千路直播，每场每秒几条评论
单路直播，百万评论总量
只需支撑工作日高峰的几万观众
why: 规模需求是双重的：横向是数百万路并发视频，纵向是热门单场每秒数千条评论。后面的分层方案（pub/sub、采样、CDN）就是围绕这两个维度展开的。
why_en: The system must scale to millions of concurrent live videos with thousands of comments per second on a single hot video.
options_en: Millions of concurrent live videos, with thousands of comments per second on a hot one.
A few thousand live videos, a handful of comments per second each.
One live video with a million comments in total.
Only needs to support a few tens of thousands of viewers at weekday peak.
scenario: 面试官让你先说清楚这套评论系统要扛住的规模量级，再继续往下设计。
q_en: What scale should FB Live Comments be designed for?
scenario_en: Before designing further, the interviewer asks you to state the order of magnitude the comment system must handle.

q: 对这类 product 风格的系统设计题，推荐的推进策略是？
options: 先把所有深挖点讲完再画高层图
先做完整容量估算再动手设计
从完整的数据库 schema 开始设计
按功能需求逐条顺序搭建设计，满足后再用非功能需求叠加深度
why: 策略是顺序推进：一条条满足功能需求，保证不迷失在细节里；功能齐了以后，再让非功能需求引导深挖和复杂度。
why_en: Build the design sequentially through each functional requirement, then use the non-functional requirements to layer on depth.
optionMeanings: 深挖优先、后画全景
先算容量再动手
先定 schema 再展开
功能优先、逐条推进
optionDirectness: 容易在细节里迷路，拖慢整体节奏
容量估算通常在设计过程中按需插入
过早定 schema 会在后续被迫返工
这是文章给出的推荐推进顺序
options_en: Cover every deep dive first, then draw the high-level diagram.
Do a full capacity estimate before designing anything.
Start from a complete database schema.
Work sequentially through each functional requirement, then layer depth from the non-functional ones.
q_en: How should you approach this product-style system design interview?

q: 补全三个核心实体：
text: 本题只有三个核心实体：{{User}}（既可以是观众也可以是主播）、{{Live Video}}（由其他团队管理、需要集成的直播视频）、{{Comment}}（用户发在直播上的消息）。
why: 实体是系统的「名词」：User、Live Video、Comment。其中 Live Video 归别的团队所有，我们只做集成。
why_en: The three core entities are the user, the live video owned by another team, and the comment posted on it.
q_en: Fill in the three core entities.

q: 为什么开局只列核心实体、而不直接给完整数据模型？
options: 设计太早还列不准字段，先立「名词」打地基，数据模型随设计推进再补全
数据模型在面试里不重要，可以全程跳过
面试官通常不会看你的 schema 设计
实体列表和完整 schema 本质上是同一件事
why: 开局阶段还无法准确枚举所有列/字段，硬写只会返工。先立住核心实体来引导思路，数据模型随设计逐步长出来。
why_en: Early in the design you cannot enumerate every column yet, so you start with core entities and grow the data model as the design progresses.
optionMeanings: 先实体后 schema 的顺序理由
忽视数据模型价值
忽视面试官关注点
混淆实体与完整字段设计
optionDirectness: 呼应先立「名词」的做法
数据模型仍需在设计中补全
面试官常会追问字段细节
完整 schema 需要更多信息才能定
options_en: Too early to pin down every field, so name the entities first and grow the schema as the design progresses.
The data model doesn't matter in interviews, so you can skip it entirely.
Interviewers usually never look at your schema.
An entity list and a full schema are essentially the same thing.
q_en: Why start with core entities instead of a full data model?

scenario: 设计发评论的 POST 接口，必须防止用户篡改请求、冒充他人发评论。
q: userId 应该从哪里来？
options: 放进请求体，由客户端自行填写 userId 字段
作为 URL 查询参数随请求传入
服务端从头部令牌中解析出身份
从 cookie 里直接读取明文 userId
why: 客户端只负责携带令牌，服务端校验令牌并从中提取 userId。身份不走请求体，用户就无法伪造 userId 冒充别人，这是现代 Web 应用的通用做法。
why_en: The server extracts the user id from a validated JWT or session token in the header, which prevents users from tampering with the request to impersonate others.
whenOtherWins: 内部受信服务间调用或管理后台代用户操作时，可以在请求体里显式传目标 userId，但仍要有服务级鉴权。
optionMeanings: 客户端自报身份，可伪造
URL 参数同样可被篡改
服务端从已签名令牌解出
cookie 明文同样不可信
optionDirectness: 客户端自填的 userId 可被伪造
查询参数一样能被客户端改写
令牌经签名校验，无法冒充
明文 cookie 没有防篡改保护
options_en: Put userId in the request body for the client to fill in.
Pass userId as a URL query parameter.
Server parses identity from the header token.
Read plaintext userId straight from a cookie.

termDefinitions.meaning: JSON Web Token，一种把用户身份编码进已签名令牌的方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes a user's identity claims.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端签发、代表已登录会话的令牌
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session token represents an authenticated session issued by the server.

tradeoff: 令牌解出身份 vs 请求体自报身份
q_en: Where should the userId come from?
scenario_en: You are designing the POST API for comments and must prevent users from tampering with the request to impersonate someone else.

q: 读这个创建评论的请求，正确的说法是？
options: userId 应补进请求体，方便服务器直接识别用户
liveVideoId 应该放进请求体而不是路径
这个请求会同时返回历史评论列表
视频 ID 走路径参数，评论内容走请求体，身份从令牌头解析

why_en: The create-comment endpoint takes the video id in the path, the message in the body, and the user identity from the auth token header.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client

optionMeanings: 把身份字段搬进 body
把资源定位符搬进 body

职责清晰的 REST 写法
optionDirectness: 身份应来自已签名令牌，不应由客户端自报

liveVideoId should live in the request body instead of the path.
This request also returns the list of historical comments.

scenario: 用户刚加入直播，页面要先显示加入之前最近的一页评论；之后如果继续往上滚，才加载更早的历史评论。
q: 加载「加入直播之前的历史评论」时，为什么不用已有的 since 参数？
options: since 参数本身查询效率太慢
since 不支持设置每页返回的数量
since 只能配合写路径一起使用
since 给的是比锚点更新的评论，方向反了
why: 对，历史评论应该用 cursor/before + limit。since 是「给我锚点之后的新评论」，适合断线后追赶；历史回看要「锚点之前的 N 条」，方向相反。
why_en: Yes: historical comments should use cursor/before plus limit. since means comments newer than the anchor, which is useful for catching up after disconnects; history loading needs the N comments before an anchor.
optionMeanings: 误归因到性能问题
误归因到分页大小限制
误解 since 的适用范围
方向相反：新旧顺序反了
optionDirectness: since 的问题不是慢，是方向反了
分页大小和 since 无关
since 本是读路径参数
历史加载要「锚点之前」，since 给的是「之后」
codeSample:
GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?limit=20
# 返回最近 20 条历史评论 + nextCursor

GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?before={nextCursor}&limit=20
# 往上滚时，继续取更早的 20 条

GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?since={lastSeenCommentId}
# 断线重连时，追赶更新的评论
options_en: The since parameter itself is too slow to query.
since doesn't support setting a page size.
since only works alongside the write path.
since returns comments newer than the anchor, which is the wrong direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 增量读取参数：返回某个锚点之后的新评论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: since is an incremental-read parameter that returns comments newer than an anchor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 历史分页参数：用上一页最早那条评论做锚点，继续取它之前的评论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: cursor/before is a history pagination marker that fetches comments older than the oldest item on the current page.

tradeoff: cursor 向历史方向翻页 vs since 向最新方向追赶
q_en: Why not use the existing since parameter to load comments from before joining?
scenario_en: A user has just joined a live video and needs the most recent page of comments from before joining; scrolling up should load older history.

scenario: 评论是结构简单的记录，没有复杂关系和事务需求，但要求快、可水平扩展、高可用。
q: 评论库选什么？
options: DynamoDB：快、可扩展、高可用，正好匹配简单记录的存取
图数据库 Neo4j：评论天然是图关系

why: 难点不在建立映射而在维护映射：观众来去、机器增减，负载均衡与 pub/sub 订阅两边的状态要持续对齐。
why_en: The ongoing challenge is coordination: subscriptions must track each server's changing viewer mix, and routing maps must stay in sync as servers scale.
optionMeanings: 计算开销并非真正瓶颈
与协同定位无关的能力误解
无依据的功能限制说法
真实的持续同步维护挑战
optionDirectness: 哈希计算本身很轻量
NGINX 完全支持流式响应
切换直播不受路由方案影响
持续维护订阅和路由的一致性才是难点
options_en: The computational cost of consistent hashing itself is too high.
NGINX-style proxies do not support streaming responses.
Viewers become completely unable to switch to a different video.
Both viewers and servers keep changing, so subscriptions need constant sync.
q_en: What is the main ongoing challenge with viewer co-location?

scenario: 不想管理 pub/sub 订阅关系，希望把路由逻辑集中在一处，还想以后加「按服务器负载路由」这类高级规则。
q: 哪种模型正中需求？
options: Dispatcher：维护路由映射，直接转发给对应服务器
把每条评论广播给系统里的所有服务器
让客户端定期自己主动拉取新评论
用数据库触发器来驱动评论推送逻辑
why: Dispatcher 把 pub/sub 模型整个反转：服务器不再订阅，由中心组件查映射后点对点投递。路由逻辑集中、好推理，加负载感知等规则也不用改推送服务器。
why_en: A dispatcher service inverts pub/sub by keeping a live map of which servers own which videos and forwarding each comment directly, centralizing the routing logic.
whenOtherWins: pub/sub 通常更简单、边角情况更少，是面试里作者优先推荐的方案。
optionMeanings: 集中路由、易加规则的方案
全量广播，浪费明显
退化回轮询模型
触发器不适合做推送
optionDirectness: 集中映射+直接转发正中需求
广播正是想避免的浪费
轮询不满足实时推送需求
数据库触发器难以承载路由逻辑
tradeoff: 集中式 Dispatcher 路由 vs 去中心化 pub/sub 订阅
options_en: Dispatcher: keeps a routing map and forwards directly to the right server.
Broadcast every comment to all servers in the system.
Have clients periodically pull new comments themselves.
Use a database trigger to drive the push logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护路由映射、把消息直接转发到目标服务器的中心组件
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dispatcher is a central component that keeps a routing map and forwards messages directly to servers.

q_en: Which model best matches these requirements?
scenario_en: You want to avoid managing pub/sub subscriptions, centralize routing logic, and later add rules such as routing by server load.

q: Dispatcher 自己如何避免成为单点？
options: 只能部署单实例，靠快速重启来兜底
多实例共享同一份协调存储中的映射
每个实例各自维护独立映射、互不通信
把映射直接硬编码写进配置文件里
why: Dispatcher 无状态化：映射的权威副本放在 Zookeeper/etcd 里，多实例共享同一份真相，挂一个不影响整体。
why_en: Multiple dispatcher instances run behind a load balancer and all consult the same coordination store like Zookeeper or etcd for consistency.
optionMeanings: 单实例＝单点，未解决问题
无状态多实例+共享真相
各说各话，映射会不一致
静态配置无法反映实时变化
optionDirectness: 单实例本身就是单点故障
无状态化+共享协调存储消除单点
互不通信会导致路由不一致
映射随观众和服务器变化，硬编码不可行
options_en: Deploy only a single instance and rely on fast restarts.
Multiple instances share one map from a coordination store.
Each instance keeps its own independent map with no sync.
Hard-code the mapping directly into a config file.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式协调服务，用来保存和同步共享状态或映射
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zookeeper or etcd is a distributed coordination service for storing and syncing shared state.

q_en: How does the Dispatcher avoid becoming a single point of failure?

q: Dispatcher 模型最大的运行期难点是？
options: 转发路径的延迟必然比 pub/sub 更高
Dispatcher 模型无法水平扩展
观众洪流下映射快速变化，需要高频刷新并协同做缓存失效，防止路由过期
Dispatcher 与 SSE 长连接不兼容
why: 映射的新鲜度就是 Dispatcher 的命门：viral 场景下服务器负责关系秒级变动，任何一份陈旧缓存都会把评论投错地方。
why_en: The dispatcher's hard part is keeping its routing map accurate during rapid change, requiring frequent refreshes and coordinated cache invalidation across instances.
optionMeanings: 缺乏依据的延迟断言
与实际设计相反的说法
真实的映射新鲜度挑战
无关的协议兼容性联想
optionDirectness: 延迟高低取决于实现，非必然
多实例本身就是为了水平扩展
映射的实时准确性才是真正难点
Dispatcher 只负责路由，不涉及连接协议
options_en: The forwarding path necessarily has higher latency than pub/sub.
The dispatcher model cannot scale horizontally.
Under a flood of viewers the map changes fast, requiring frequent refresh and coordinated cache invalidation to avoid stale routing.
The dispatcher is incompatible with SSE long connections.
q_en: What is the hardest runtime problem in the Dispatcher model?

q: 在这个场景下，为什么 Redis pub/sub（发布订阅广播）比 Kafka 更顺手？
options: Kafka 的延迟天生比 Redis pub/sub 更低
Redis 能持久化消息而 Kafka 反而不能
Kafka 能支持的订阅方数量比 Redis 更少
Kafka 应付动态订阅吃力，Redis 更灵活
why: 这里的订阅关系随观众换台不断变动，正是 Kafka 的短板、Redis pub/sub 的长处。维度是「动态订阅的灵活性」，不是吞吐。
why_en: Kafka is scalable and fault-tolerant but struggles with dynamic subscription churn, while Redis pub/sub offers low latency and handles viewers switching videos gracefully.
optionMeanings: 与事实相反的延迟断言
与事实相反的持久化断言
无依据的订阅数限制说法
真实的动态订阅灵活性差异
optionDirectness: 延迟比较与事实相反
持久化能力描述与事实相反
订阅方数量不是决定因素
动态订阅的灵活性才是本场景的关键维度
options_en: Kafka inherently has lower latency than Redis pub/sub.
Redis persists messages while Kafka cannot.
Kafka supports fewer subscribers than Redis.
Kafka struggles with dynamic subscriptions; Redis handles them better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐、可持久化的分布式消息日志系统
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed log system for durable messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

tradeoff: 动态订阅的灵活性 vs 吞吐与持久化保证
scenario: 推送服务器需要感知观众正在观看哪些直播，而观众会频繁在不同直播间切换，订阅关系持续变动。
q_en: Why is Redis pub/sub a better fit than Kafka in this scenario?
scenario_en: Push servers need to track which live videos their viewers are watching, and viewers switch between live rooms frequently.

q: Redis pub/sub 是 fire-and-forget（不保证送达），为什么在这里不致命？
options: 评论已经持久化在数据库里，掉线漏掉的评论靠断线追赶机制从库或缓存补回
Redis pub/sub 其实内置了消息重试，不会丢
因为还有 Kafka 在后面做兜底队列
观众永远不会感知到任何消息丢失
why: pub/sub 在这里只是「热路径通知」，不是唯一事实来源。数据库兜底 + 追赶机制，让偶发丢消息只是短暂延迟而非数据丢失。
why_en: Fire-and-forget is acceptable because comments are already persisted in the database and the catch-up mechanism recovers anything missed during a brief disconnect.
optionMeanings: 真实理由：数据库兜底+追赶机制
与事实相反的重试能力说法
设计中并不存在的兜底队列
过度乐观的无损断言
optionDirectness: 数据库+追赶机制让丢消息只是短暂延迟
Redis pub/sub 本身就是 fire-and-forget
本设计没有引入 Kafka 做兜底
短暂断线仍可能让观众错过一两条
options_en: Comments are already persisted in the database, and the reconnect catch-up mechanism recovers anything missed from storage or cache.
Redis pub/sub actually has built-in retries and never loses messages.
Because Kafka sits behind it as a backup queue.
Viewers will never notice any message loss at all.
q_en: Why is Redis pub/sub being fire-and-forget not fatal here?

scenario: 评论服务要把新评论广播出去，推送服务器只想收到与本机观众相关的那部分分片频道的消息。
q: 这组 Redis 命令实现的是什么？
codeSample:
# 推送服务器：按本机观众需要订阅分片频道
SUBSCRIBE comments:shard:7

# 评论服务：hash("lv_42") % 100 = 7，发布到对应分片
PUBLISH comments:shard:7 '{"liveVideoId":"lv_42","commentId":"c_9","message":"nice!"}'
options: 把评论持久化写入数据库存储
分片频道上的发布/订阅广播机制
带延迟投递功能的持久化消息队列
基于 SETNX 命令实现的分布式锁
why: SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH 是 Redis 的 pub/sub 原语；按 hash 分片的频道名让每台服务器只消费自己需要的流量，而不是全网广播。
why_en: These Redis commands implement sharded pub/sub, where only servers subscribed to that hash shard receive the published comment.
whenOtherWins: 需要可回放的持久日志、消费组和严格的吞吐保证时，应该用 Kafka topic 而不是 Redis 频道。
optionMeanings: 与命令语义无关的持久化
按分片精准投递的广播
延迟队列，命令不具备此能力
加锁语义，用的是另一个命令
optionDirectness: 这两个命令不涉及磁盘持久化写入
命令语义正是分片频道上的广播
Redis pub/sub 没有延迟投递能力
加锁要用 SETNX，这里没出现
options_en: Persisting the comment write to the database.
A publish/subscribe broadcast on a sharded channel.
A durable message queue with delayed delivery.
A distributed lock built on the SETNX command.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子命令：key 不存在时才写入，常用于实现锁
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SETNX is a Redis command that sets a key only if it is absent, often used to build locks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐、可持久化的分布式消息日志系统
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed log system for durable messaging.

q_en: What do these Redis commands implement?
scenario_en: The comment service needs to broadcast new comments, while push servers only want messages from the shard channels relevant to their local viewers.

scenario: 面试里要在「pub/sub + 观众协同定位」与「Dispatcher 服务」之间选一个作为主推的协调方案。
q: 作者建议优先押哪个？
options: 选 Dispatcher，因为听起来更高级一些

都不选，直接跳到讲 CDN 方案
pub/sub 更简单、边角情况更少，优先押它

why_en: Both approaches solve coordination, but pub/sub is typically simpler with fewer corner cases, making it the one to reach for in an interview.
whenOtherWins: 需要集中式路由逻辑、负载感知路由等高级规则时，Dispatcher 的可控性更强。

面试里缺乏聚焦的展开方式
跳过了协调问题本身

optionDirectness: 选型理由应该是工程权衡，不是印象

CDN 方案是另一个独立话题，不能跳过协调问题
作者明确以简单和边角情况作为优先依据
options_en: Pick dispatcher because it sounds more advanced.
Fully present both without choosing between them.
Skip both and jump straight to the CDN approach.
Pub/sub is simpler with fewer edge cases, so lead with it.
q_en: Which coordination approach should you lead with?
scenario_en: In the interview, you need to choose between pub/sub plus viewer co-location and a Dispatcher service as the primary coordination plan.

q: 超级直播每秒 5,000 条评论（平均 4 词一条）意味着什么？
options: 相当于不到 30 秒读完一整本《战争与和平》
数据库会因此先于推送层崩溃宕机
延迟会因此自动涨到 1 秒以上
每条评论大约能停留 1 秒，足够读完
why: 这组数字证明了一个质变：评论流快到超出人类阅读能力时，「每条必达、低延迟」的传统目标失去了意义。
why_en: At five thousand comments per second each message survives about four milliseconds on screen, far beyond human reading speed.
options_en: Equivalent to reading all of War and Peace in under 30 seconds.
The database would crash before the push layer does.
Latency automatically rises above 1 second as a result.
Each comment stays on screen about 1 second, long enough to read.
scenario: 世界杯决赛级别的超级直播，评论以每秒 5,000 条的速度涌入，面试官问这组数字说明了什么。
q_en: What does 5,000 comments per second, averaging four words each, imply?
scenario_en: For a World Cup final level live stream, comments arrive at 5,000 per second, and the interviewer asks what that number tells you.

q: 评论快到没人能逐条阅读时，系统的设计目标发生了什么变化？
options: 延迟要求反而变得比之前更严格了
必须给每条评论增加送达确认机制
低延迟逐条送达退位，用户要的是氛围
需要把公开评论功能改成私信功能
why: 这是本题最重要的洞察：极端规模下需求本身变了。用户要的是感受到人群的能量，这为采样和 CDN 快照两个方案打开了大门。
why_en: At mega-scale the requirements themselves change: users experience a collective vibe rather than reading individual comments, so strict per-message delivery stops mattering.
optionMeanings: 与洞察方向相反的推断
增加了不必要的强保证
真实洞察：需求本身质变
偏离主题的功能联想
optionDirectness: 延迟要求实际上放宽了，不是收紧
逐条确认违背了「氛围优先」的洞察
这正是本题最重要的认识转变
私信与群体氛围体验无关
options_en: Latency requirements actually get stricter than before.
Every comment now needs a delivery confirmation mechanism.
Reliable per-message delivery gives way to a collective vibe.
Public comments need to be turned into private messages.
q_en: How does the design goal change when comments arrive too fast to read one by one?

scenario: 单场超级直播评论如洪水，观众只需要看到「足够多」的评论来感受人群能量，不需要每条都看到。
q: 第一个减负手段是？
options: 无脑加推送服务器硬扛全量
直接关闭该直播的评论功能
改成每分钟批量投递一次
对评论流做采样：只把一小部分评论投递给每个观众
why: 既然没人读得完，就没必要全量投递。采样让每个观众收到可读数量的评论，同时保留现场感。
why_en: Since nobody can read them all, sampling delivers only a subset of comments to each viewer while preserving the feeling of crowd energy.
whenOtherWins: 普通流量的直播必须逐条投递——采样只在评论量超出人类阅读能力的超级流里才合理。
optionMeanings: 硬加机器扛全量，成本失控
直接关闭评论，体验最差
批量投递仍会造成显著延迟
采样降负载同时保留现场感
optionDirectness: 连接扛得住不代表消息量能降下来
这是逃避问题，不是解决问题
批量会让延迟远超实时目标
采样正面解决了消息量过大的问题
options_en: Blindly add more push servers to brute-force the full volume.
Just turn off comments for that live video.
Switch to delivering a batch once per minute.
Sample the comment stream: deliver only a subset to each viewer.
tradeoff: 采样保留现场感 vs 全量投递保证不丢条
q_en: What is the first way to reduce load?
scenario_en: In a super-hot live stream, comments arrive like a flood; viewers need enough comments to feel the crowd, not every single comment.

q: 自适应采样率大概怎么调？
options: 永远固定采样 10%，完全不随流速变化
评论流速越快，采样率反而调得越高
流速越快采样率越低，维持恒定可读速率
只在流量低谷、评论很少时才开启采样
why: 采样率跟着评论速度反向调节，目标是给观众一个恒定、可读的速率，无论后台实际多快。
why_en: The sampling rate adapts inversely to comment velocity, from about fifty percent at one hundred per second down to one or two percent at five thousand, keeping each viewer's rate roughly constant.
options_en: Always sample a fixed 10%, never adjusted by velocity.
The faster comments flow, the higher the sampling rate gets.
Faster flow means lower sampling rate, keeping a steady rate.
Only enable sampling during a lull when comments are sparse.
scenario: 超级直播的采样组件要根据当前评论速度动态调整采样比例，面试官问大致怎么调。
q_en: How should adaptive sampling roughly tune its rate?
scenario_en: The sampling component for a super-hot live stream adjusts its sampling ratio based on the current comment rate.

q: 比纯随机更聪明的采样会优先保留哪些评论？（多选）
options: 观众所关注用户发的评论
已经获得表情互动（reactions）的评论
认证账号发的评论
字数最多的评论
why: 采样可以带策略：社交关系、互动热度、账号可信度都能加权，让「最好的」评论有更高概率被看见。字数长短不是质量信号。
why_en: Smarter sampling prioritizes comments from followed users, comments already getting reactions, and verified accounts so the best comments are more likely to be seen.
optionMeanings: 关注关系带来的社交权重
已获得互动的热度信号
认证账号的可信度加权
字数长短，与质量无关
optionDirectness: 正确：关注关系是常见的排序信号
正确：已有互动是常见的排序信号
正确：认证状态是常见的排序信号
错误：字数不是评论质量的可靠指标
options_en: Comments from users the viewer follows.
Comments that have already gotten reactions.
Comments from verified accounts.
The longest comments by word count.
q_en: What should smarter-than-random sampling prefer to keep?

q: 采样大幅减负之后，还剩下什么痛点？
options: 采样会打乱评论原本的时间先后顺序
连接成本没降：仍要维持百万级持久连接
采样率一旦设定就再也无法调整
数据库这一侧的写入压力不减反增
why: 采样只减少了每条连接上的消息量，连接本身一个都没少。百万级长连接的成本仍然存在，这为 CDN 方案留下了空间。
why_en: Sampling cuts message volume but still leaves millions of persistent SSE connections to maintain, so infrastructure costs remain substantial.

连接数量丝毫未减，成本仍在
采样率本就是按速度自适应调节的
写路径和采样是完全独立的部分
options_en: Sampling scrambles the original chronological order.
Connection cost stays: millions of persistent connections remain.
Once set, the sampling rate can never be adjusted again.
Write pressure on the database side actually increases.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

q_en: After sampling cuts message volume, what pain point remains?

scenario: 世界杯决赛级别：单流数亿观众同时在线、评论洪流不断，连采样后的 SSE 连接成本都不可承受。
q: 最具扩展性的交付模型是？
options: 把现有的采样率压得比现在更低
换成 WebSocket 集群硬扛所有连接
按地域多部署几组边缘 SSE 服务器
反转成拉模型，把快照交给 CDN 分发

why_en: Seeing the Last-Event-ID header, the server replays the comments the client missed after that id and then resumes normal live streaming.

误把重连头当成鉴权字段
忽略头部导致漏发
按缺口精准补发后接回实时流
optionDirectness: 只需要补发缺失的那一段，不是全部
那个头部字段只标记断点位置，不做身份校验
忽略头部会让客户端错过这批评论
这正是该头部字段的设计目的
options_en: Push every comment from the very start of the live video.
Reset the connection and force the client to re-authenticate.
Just ignore the header and only send new comments going forward.
Replay from the gap, then seamlessly resume the live stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSE 请求头，标识客户端最后收到的事件 ID，用于断线重放
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-Event-ID is the SSE header the client resends on reconnect so the server can replay missed events.

q_en: In this reconnect flow, what does the server do after seeing Last-Event-ID: c_1088?

scenario: 想在重连时做更精细的 UX——比如显示「你错过了 47 条评论」、以 2-3 倍速平滑补播——而不是依赖浏览器默默续传。
q: 客户端该怎么做？
options: 只依赖浏览器原生的 Last-Event-ID 机制
客户端本地记录最后见到的评论 ID，重连时显式调用 GET 补齐历史
重连时直接刷新整个页面
让服务器为每个用户持久保存断点位置
why: 自己掌握断点和补课请求，就能自由设计重连体验：倍速动画补播、跳到实况的选项等。浏览器自动续传做不到这些。
why_en: Tracking the last comment id locally and requesting catch-up over explicit HTTP gives the client full control to animate missed comments or offer a jump-to-live option.
whenOtherWins: 简单 Web 客户端没有特殊 UX 要求时，浏览器原生 Last-Event-ID 自动续传就足够了。
optionMeanings: 自动机制，缺乏自定义体验的空间
客户端自控，可定制补播体验
粗暴刷新，体验差且状态丢失
服务端存储位置，增加不必要状态
optionDirectness: 原生机制无法定制倍速动画等体验
客户端自己掌握断点才能自由设计体验
整页刷新会打断观看体验
断点该由客户端掌握，不必让服务端存
options_en: Rely only on the browser's native Last-Event-ID mechanism.
The client tracks the last seen comment id locally and explicitly calls a GET to backfill on reconnect.
Just refresh the whole page on reconnect.
Have the server persist each user's resume position on its side.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSE 请求头，标识客户端最后收到的事件 ID，用于断线重放
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-Event-ID is the SSE header the client resends on reconnect so the server can replay missed events.

tradeoff: 客户端自控断点 vs 浏览器原生自动续传
q_en: What should the client do for a more controlled reconnect experience?
scenario_en: You want a refined reconnect UX, such as showing “you missed 47 comments” and replaying them at 2-3x speed, instead of relying on silent browser retry.

q: 移动端为兼顾电量，SSE（服务器推流）长连接该怎么管理？
options: 退到后台后也始终保持连接不断开
后台期间改用推送通知逐条发送评论
退后台前主动断开，回前台再补课
认为移动端只能靠轮询来实现
why: 与其让系统强制掐断，不如主动优雅断开并记好书签。省电、省资源，回前台后靠追赶机制无损恢复。
why_en: The app preemptively disconnects the SSE and records its position when backgrounded, then reconnects and catches up on foreground, which beats keeping a throttled background connection.
optionMeanings: 与省电目标相反的常开连接
与直播评论体量不符的通知轰炸
真实做法：主动断开+记录位置
误判移动端无法用 SSE
optionDirectness: 常开连接正是耗电的来源
逐条推送通知会造成骚扰式轰炸
主动断开省电，回前台靠追赶机制补齐
SSE 同样能在移动端正常工作
options_en: Keep the connection alive even when backgrounded.
Switch to sending each comment as a push notification while backgrounded.
Proactively disconnect before backgrounding, catch up on foreground.
Assume mobile can only be implemented with polling.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

q_en: How should mobile clients manage SSE long connections to save battery?

q: 断线补漏的重放范围该设多大边界？
options: 重放最近约 5 分钟比较合理，超出边界时优雅降级
无论断多久都做全量重放
只补最后 1 条评论就够
永不重放，重连即代表最新
why: 重放要有实际上限：短断线无缝补齐，长断线补太多反而淹没用户。5 分钟是一个合理的量级锚点。
why_en: Replay must be bounded, with about the last five minutes being reasonable and graceful degradation for longer gaps instead of dumping thousands of stale comments.
options_en: Replaying roughly the last five minutes is reasonable, with graceful degradation beyond that.
Always do a full replay no matter how long the disconnect was.
Just replay the last single comment.
Never replay; reconnecting means starting from the latest.
scenario: 用户断线重连后要补发错过的评论，面试官问重放范围该设多大边界。
q_en: What boundary should we set for replaying missed comments?
scenario_en: After a reconnect, the system must replay missed comments, and the interviewer asks where to bound that replay window.

q: 重连大概率被负载均衡到另一台推送服务器，重放漏掉的评论靠什么？
options: 由原来连接的那台服务器负责转发历史
客户端在本地保存全量的评论历史
断线时把用户锁定在原来那台服务器
共享缓存保存近期评论，任何服务器都能重放
why: 重放能力不能绑死在单台机器的内存里。把近期评论放进共享 Redis，重连落到哪台都能补课。
why_en: A shared Redis cache of recent comments lets whichever server the client reconnects to replay the missed history for any video.
optionMeanings: 原服务器可能已不可达
客户端存储不现实且不可靠
牺牲了负载均衡的灵活性
真实机制：跨机共享的近期缓存
optionDirectness: 原服务器未必还在或还认识该用户
全量本地存储代价过高、也不可靠
锁定服务器违背了负载均衡的初衷
共享缓存让重放能力与具体机器解耦
options_en: The originally connected server forwards the history.
The client stores the full comment history locally.
Pin the user to the original server during disconnect.
A shared cache holds recent comments so any server can replay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

q_en: If reconnect lands on another push server, what replays the missed comments?

q: HTTP 补课响应还在处理时，SSE（服务器推流）连接上又来了新评论，怎么避免重复或漏洞？
options: 直接丢弃 SSE 流送来的那部分评论
按评论 ID 去重，合并两条通道的数据
让 SSE 连接在补课期间暂停接收
认为两路数据天然不会重叠，无需处理
why: 两条通道并行时窗口重叠不可避免。评论 ID 是天然的去重键，客户端据此合并即可既不重复也不缺失。
why_en: When SSE and HTTP catch-up overlap, the client deduplicates by comment id and merges the two streams correctly.
optionMeanings: 会丢失实时到达的新评论
真实机制：按 ID 去重合并
暂停会造成新的空档
忽视了真实存在的重叠窗口
optionDirectness: 丢弃会漏掉真正的新评论
评论 ID 是天然的去重键
暂停连接会制造新的缺口
两条通道并行时重叠不可避免
options_en: Just drop whatever the SSE stream delivers during that window.
Deduplicate by comment id and merge the two channels.
Pause the SSE connection while catch-up is in progress.
Assume the two paths never overlap, so nothing needs handling.
q_en: How do we avoid duplicates or gaps when HTTP catch-up and SSE new events overlap?

q: 补全生产级断线处理的要点：
text: 面试谈断线处理：以 SSE 的 {{Last-Event-ID}} 机制为基础，但生产系统还需要{{有界}}重放（不能补一小时的评论）、客户端本地跟踪{{位置}}、以及无法重放时的优雅{{降级}}。
why: 这四件套表明你考虑过移动网络和用户行为的「脏现实」，而不是只背了协议特性。
why_en: Production reconnection needs the Last-Event-ID foundation plus bounded replay, client-side position tracking, and graceful degradation when replay is impossible.
q_en: Fill in the production-grade disconnect handling checklist.

q: 在 FB Live Comments 这道题上，mid-level 候选人的过关线是？
options: 独立提出 CDN 快照这类高阶方案
能背出 Kafka 的全部配置参数细节
全程交给面试官驱动设计即可过关
主动识别轮询局限，小提示下给出 pub/sub
why: mid-level 约 80% 广度 20% 深度：高层设计能满足功能需求，组件可以只有表层熟悉，后半程面试官接手驱动是正常的。
why_en: A mid-level candidate should proactively spot polling's limits and reach the pub/sub solution with minor hints, scaling it with interviewer help.
optionMeanings: 超出 mid-level 期望的深度
与本题无关的琐碎记忆
低估了 mid-level 应有的主动性
真实的 mid-level 过关标准
optionDirectness: 这是 senior/staff 才要求的深度
本题不考具体配置参数
面试官期望候选人先主动驱动前半程
这正是文章给出的 mid-level 标准
options_en: Independently propose an advanced approach like the CDN snapshot.
Recite every Kafka configuration parameter from memory.
Passing means letting the interviewer drive the whole design.
Proactively spot polling's limits, reach pub/sub with minor hints.
q_en: What is the passing bar for a mid-level candidate on FB Live Comments?

q: senior（E5）候选人在这道题上的期望是？
options: 期望与 mid-level 完全一致，没有区别
只需要深挖数据库选型这一个点
快速过完高层设计，几乎不需提示就给出 pub/sub，并主导扩展性讨论
必须提出 Dispatcher 服务才算过关
why: senior 约 60/40 广深比：省下时间聚焦扩展性深挖，能自己推理出初始设计的局限，并主导权衡讨论。
why_en: A senior candidate speeds through the high-level design, reaches pub/sub with minimal hints, and proactively leads the scaling discussion with clear trade-offs.
optionMeanings: 低估了 senior 应有的深度
把广度要求窄化成单点
真实的 senior 过关标准
把可选方案错当成必答项
optionDirectness: senior 的广深比明显高于 mid-level
深挖点不止数据库一处
这正是文章给出的 senior 标准
Dispatcher 只是备选方案，非必需
options_en: Expectations are identical to mid-level, no difference.
Only needs to deep-dive on the database choice.
Speed through the high-level design, reach pub/sub with almost no hints, and lead the scaling discussion.
Must propose the dispatcher service to pass.
q_en: What is expected from a senior, E5, candidate on this design?

q: staff+ 候选人在这道题上的标志性表现是？
options: 主动指出 pub/sub 的局限并给出对策
把 60% 的时间都花在广度铺陈上
等面试官主动指出问题后再修补设计
把重点放在展示 REST API 的基础细节上
why: staff+ 约 40/60 广深比：基础部分一笔带过，火力集中在深水区；面试官只应「聚焦」而不需要「引导」。
why_en: A staff-plus candidate proactively calls out the pub/sub solution's reliability and scalability limits, proposes fixes, and discusses concrete technology trade-offs in depth.
optionMeanings: 真实的 staff+ 标志性表现
广深比与 staff+ 期望相反
缺乏 staff+ 应有的主动性
把基础细节当成重点，本末倒置
optionDirectness: 这正是文章描述的 staff+ 表现
staff+ 应把大部分时间放在深度上
staff+ 应主动识别问题，不等提示
这些基础内容面试官默认你已掌握
options_en: Proactively call out pub/sub's limits and propose fixes.
Spend 60% of the time laying out breadth.
Wait for the interviewer to flag problems before fixing.
Focus on showing off basic REST API details.
q_en: What marks a staff-plus performance on this design?

q: FB Live Comments 练的「实时更新模式」还适用于哪些系统？
options: 夜间批量结算的 ETL 数据管道
要求即时送达的协作编辑、监控看板、游戏平台
对象存储里的冷数据归档服务
按月生成一次的统计报表服务
why: SSE 广播、pub/sub 分发、多服务器协调这一套原理是可迁移的：凡是「数据一产生就要送到所有相关客户端」的场景都在用同一模式。
why_en: The same real-time updates pattern of streaming delivery, pub/sub distribution, and server coordination applies to collaborative editing, live dashboards, and gaming.
optionMeanings: 批处理场景，与实时模式无关
真实的可迁移场景
与实时推送无关的存储场景
低频批处理，与实时无关
optionDirectness: 批处理场景不需要实时推送模式
这些场景同样要求数据即时送达
冷归档不涉及实时分发
月度报表不需要毫秒级送达
options_en: A nightly batch settlement ETL pipeline.
Collaborative editing, dashboards, and games that need instant delivery.
Cold data archival in object storage.
A statistics report generated once a month.
q_en: What other systems use the realtime update pattern from FB Live Comments?

q: FB News Feed 这道题里，用户之间的 follow 关系被简化成什么模型？
q_en: In the FB News Feed problem, what model is the user follow relationship simplified to?
options: 双向好友关系，两边必须互相确认
单向 follow：A 关注 B，不需要 B 同意
群组成员关系，需要管理员审批
只有互相关注才能看到对方的帖子
options_en: A bidirectional friend relationship that both sides must confirm.
A one-way follow: A follows B without B agreeing.
A group-membership relationship that needs admin approval.
Posts are visible only when both sides follow each other.
optionMeanings: 早期 Facebook 的好友模型，是双向的。
本题设定的模型：关注是一条有方向的边。
群组产品的成员关系，本题不涉及。
互相关注才能看见帖子的假想规则。
optionMeanings_en: Facebook's early friend model, which is bidirectional.
This problem's model: a follow is a one-directional edge.
A group-membership relation, not part of this problem.
A hypothetical rule requiring mutual follow to see posts.
why: 早期 Facebook 以双向好友为主，但本题明确简化为单向 follow：关注是一条有方向的边，不需要对方同意。
why_en: This problem deliberately simplifies to a one-way follow edge instead of Facebook's original bidirectional friend model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单向的关注关系，A 关注 B 不需要 B 同意。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A follow is a one-directional relationship where A follows B without B's consent.

q: News Feed 的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which features are in scope for the News Feed MVP? (Select all that apply.)
scenario: 面试官只给了一句话：设计 Facebook 的 News Feed。你要先圈定这道题的功能范围。
scenario_en: The interviewer only says: design Facebook News Feed. First, define the functional scope.
options: 用户能创建帖子
用户能关注（follow）他人
用户能按时间倒序查看关注对象的 feed，并能翻页
用户能点赞和评论帖子
帖子支持私密/受限可见性
options_en: Users can create posts.
Users can follow other people.
Users can view a reverse-chronological feed from who they follow, with pagination.
Users can like and comment on posts.
Posts support private or restricted visibility.
optionDirectness: 发帖是主写路径，后续决定 Post API 和 Post 表。
follow 建立社交边，后续决定 Follow 表和扇出方向。
时间倒序+翻页直接决定 Feed Service、GSI 和 cursor。
点赞评论会引入额外实体与计数，本题先排除。
可见性会引入权限过滤，本题先排除。
optionDirectness_en: Posting is the main write path and drives the Post API and table.
Follow creates the social edge and drives the Follow table and fan-out direction.
Reverse time order with paging drives Feed Service, the GSI, and the cursor.
Likes and comments add entities and counters, so they are left out here.
Visibility rules add permission filtering, so they are left out here.
why: 核心需求只有三类：发帖、关注、按时间倒序翻页看 feed。点赞评论和可见性控制被明确划到范围之外。
why_en: The core scope is only posting, following, and paging a reverse-chronological feed; likes, comments, and visibility rules are explicitly out of scope.

scenario: 面试官只给了一句话：设计 Facebook 的 News Feed。你量化出：最多 1 分钟陈旧、发帖和刷 feed 都要 500ms 内返回、约 20 亿用户。
scenario_en: The interviewer only says: design Facebook News Feed. You quantify the NFRs as up to one minute of staleness, post/feed responses under 500ms, and about two billion users.
q: 这些非功能数字最支持哪些设计判断？
q_en: Which design decisions do these non-functional numbers support?
text: 1 分钟陈旧窗口支持{{异步写扇出}}；500ms 延迟目标排除{{读时大扇出}}；20 亿用户要求认真做{{存储与分区}}。
why: 这四个数字直接驱动后面的架构决策：1 分钟陈旧窗口允许异步写扇出，500ms 排除了读时大扇出，20 亿用户决定了存储与分区策略。
why_en: These four numbers directly drive the architecture: the one-minute window enables async fan-out, 500ms rules out big read-time fan-out, and 2 billion users shapes storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在故障时仍能响应请求的能力，这里被优先于强一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Availability is the system's ability to keep responding during failures; here it is prioritized over strong consistency.

scenario: 社交 feed：用户晚 1 分钟看到新帖几乎无感知，但 app 打不开会直接流失用户。
scenario_en: In a social feed, a post appearing one minute late is barely noticed, but an unavailable app loses users.
q: 在一致性与可用性之间应该怎么选？
q_en: For this social feed, how should we choose between consistency and availability?
options: 优先可用性，接受最终一致——帖子可以短暂陈旧
优先强一致，宁可拒绝请求也不返回旧数据
读写都做线性一致
牺牲分区容忍来换两者兼得
options_en: Favor availability and accept eventual consistency; posts can be briefly stale.
Favor strong consistency, rejecting requests rather than returning stale data.
Make both reads and writes linearizable.
Give up partition tolerance to get both at once.
optionMeanings: 系统尽量保持能响应，容忍短暂陈旧。
系统尽量保证读到最新值，代价是可能拒绝请求。
最强的一致性模型，读写全局有序。
分布式系统里通常不可放弃分区容忍。
optionMeanings_en: The system stays responsive and tolerates brief staleness.
The system prioritizes fresh reads at the cost of possibly rejecting requests.
The strongest consistency model, with globally ordered reads and writes.
Partition tolerance is normally not something a distributed system can give up.
why: feed 陈旧一分钟没人在乎，打不开才是灾难，所以选可用性 + 最终一致。这个选择随后解锁异步扇出、缓存等一整套手段。
why_en: A one-minute-stale feed goes unnoticed but a down app does not, so this system favors availability with eventual consistency.
whenOtherWins: 支付、库存、抢票这类返回旧数据会造成真实损失的系统，必须反过来优先强一致。
tradeoff: 可用性 vs 一致性

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂时间内不同副本可能不一致，但最终会收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means replicas may briefly disagree after a write but converge to the same value over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强一致性模型，所有读写看起来像按一个全局顺序发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability is the strongest consistency model, where all reads and writes appear to happen in one global order.

q: 为什么非功能需求要写上具体数字，而不是只说『要快、要大』？
q_en: Why should non-functional requirements use concrete numbers instead of just saying 'fast' and 'large'?
options: 面试评分表硬性要求写数字
数字决定架构，量级不同设计不同
写数字显得更专业
方便直接换算需要多少台服务器
options_en: Interview rubrics rigidly require numbers.
Numbers decide the architecture: single-digit-millisecond and sub-second latency need very different designs.
Writing numbers just looks more professional.
It lets you directly convert to a server headcount.
optionMeanings: 假设有固定评分表逼你写数字。
把数字当作决定架构的约束。
把数字当成表演给面试官看的姿态。
把数字直接当容量规划的输入。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes there is a fixed rubric forcing you to write numbers.
Treats numbers as constraints that decide the architecture.
Treats numbers as a performance for the interviewer.
Treats numbers as a direct input to capacity planning.
why: 量化才能做取舍：要求个位毫秒的系统和允许一秒返回的系统，架构会截然不同，数字是后续每个决策的依据。
why_en: Quantifying requirements is what enables real tradeoffs, since a single-digit-millisecond system and a one-second system need very different architectures.

q: News Feed 设计里，架构上公认最难、最值得预留时间深挖的部分是？
q_en: In the News Feed design, which part deserves the most deep-dive time?
options: 用户认证与鉴权
帖子富文本的存储格式
海量关注/粉丝的扇出问题
数据库备份与恢复
options_en: User authentication and authorization.
The storage format for rich-text posts.
Fan-out: what happens when a user follows huge numbers of accounts, or an account has huge numbers of followers.
Database backup and recovery.
optionMeanings: 身份认证通常一句带过，不是本题重点。
帖子内容结构留空对象即可，不深挖。
关注关系在读写两侧都可能被放大成海量请求。
备份恢复是运维话题，本题不涉及。
optionMeanings_en: Authentication is usually mentioned briefly and isn't the focus here.
Post content is left as an empty object and not explored deeply.
The follow relationship can be amplified into massive requests on both read and write paths.
Backup and recovery is an operations topic, not covered here.
why: 难点是扇出：关注很多人让读扇出爆炸，被很多人关注让写扇出爆炸。基础需求要快速铺完，把时间省给这里。
why_en: The hard part is fan-out, since following many accounts explodes read fan-out and having many followers explodes write fan-out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求或写入在系统内部被放大成大量下游请求或写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one request or write gets amplified into many downstream requests or writes.

q: News Feed 系统的核心实体有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which entities are core to the News Feed system? (Select all that apply.)
options: User：系统中的用户
Follow：用户之间的单向链接，显式建成实体
Post：用户发布的帖子，出现在粉丝的 feed 里
Comment：帖子下的评论
Session：登录会话
options_en: User: a user of the system.
Follow: a one-directional link between users, modeled as its own entity.
Post: content a user publishes, shown in followers' feeds.
Comment: a comment under a post.
Session: a login session.
optionDirectness: User 是作者和读者，所有请求都围绕它授权。
Follow 是有向边，后续读写扇出都围绕它放大。
Post 是 feed 的内容来源，缓存和存储都围绕它设计。
Comment 会引入评论流和计数，本题先不建模。
Session 属于认证细节，不决定 feed 数据模型。
optionDirectness_en: User is both author and reader, and requests are authorized around it.
Follow is the directed edge that later read and write fan-out amplifies.
Post is the feed content source, so storage and caching revolve around it.
Comment would add comment streams and counters, so it is not modeled here.
Session is an auth detail and does not drive the feed data model.
why: 核心实体只有三个：User、Follow、Post。把 Follow 显式建成实体而不是 User 的属性，是后面所有扇出讨论的基础。
why_en: There are only three core entities: User, Follow, and Post, and modeling Follow as its own entity is the foundation for every fan-out discussion later.

scenario: 第一个功能：发帖。内容可能是富文本或其他结构化数据，且发帖人身份不能被客户端伪造。
scenario_en: The first feature is post creation. Content may be rich or structured, and the author identity must not be spoofable by the client.
q: 哪个 API 设计最合适？
q_en: Which post-creation API design is the best fit?
options: GET /posts?content=... 用查询参数传内容
POST /posts，body 只有 content 对象；身份取自请求头的 JWT，响应返回 postId
POST /posts，body 里带 userId 字段指明发帖人
PUT /posts，直接覆盖该用户最新一条帖子
options_en: GET /posts?content=... passing content as a query parameter.
POST /posts with only a content object in the body; identity comes from the JWT header, response returns postId.
POST /posts with a userId field in the body naming the author.
PUT /posts, directly overwriting the user's latest post.
optionMeanings: 把内容塞进 URL 查询参数。
内容进 body，身份走认证头。
把发帖人身份放进请求体字段。
把发帖语义改成幂等覆盖。
optionMeanings_en: Stuffs content into a URL query parameter.
Puts content in the body and identity in the auth header.
Puts the author's identity in a body field.
Changes posting semantics to an idempotent overwrite.
why: POST /posts 只带 content：内容留成对象以兼容富媒体，发帖人从认证头（JWT）取——放 body 里的 userId 客户端可以伪造。
why_en: POST /posts carries only a content object so it can hold rich media, while the author identity comes from the JWT header instead of a spoofable body field.
whenOtherWins: 如果客户端要离线生成、断网重试并保证幂等，PUT + 客户端生成的 postId 也是合理设计。
tradeoff: 身份来自可信请求头 vs 客户端自报身份

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把用户身份编码进请求头的签名令牌格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes a user's identity, carried in the request header.

q: 关注接口为什么选 PUT /users/[id]/follow 而不是 POST？
q_en: Why use PUT /users/[id]/follow instead of POST for the follow endpoint?
options: PUT 幂等，重复点击不报错
PUT 传输速度更快
POST 不支持路径参数
PUT 可以跳过网关鉴权
options_en: PUT is idempotent: double-clicking follow twice leaves the same result without an error.
PUT transmits faster.
POST doesn't support path parameters.
PUT can skip gateway authentication.
optionMeanings: 把关注建模成一个幂等的二元状态设置。
把选型理由归到网络速度。
误认为 POST 不能带路径参数。
误认为 PUT 有鉴权豁免。
optionMeanings_en: Models following as an idempotent binary state set.
Attributes the choice to network speed.
Wrongly assumes POST can't take path parameters.
Wrongly assumes PUT is exempt from auth.
why: 关注是二元状态，用 PUT 保证幂等，重复点击不会出错；取消关注（超纲）可用同一路径的 DELETE。
why_en: Following is a binary state, so PUT keeps it idempotent and repeated clicks never error out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，结果和执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation produces the same result no matter how many times it is repeated.

q: PUT /users/[id]/follow 中，『谁在关注谁』是如何确定的？
q_en: In PUT /users/[id]/follow, how do we know who follows whom?
options: body 里带 followerId 和 followeeId 两个字段
都放在 query string 里
被关注者来自 JWT，关注者是路径里的 [id]
关注者来自请求头的 JWT，被关注者是路径里的 [id]
options_en: Two body fields, followerId and followeeId.
Both values are passed in the query string.
The followee comes from the JWT, the follower is the path [id].
The follower comes from the JWT header, the followee is the path [id].
optionMeanings: 让客户端在 body 里同时申报双方身份。
把双方身份都塞进 URL 参数。
把路径参数和 JWT 的角色说反了。
把当前登录者当关注者，路径对象当被关注者。
optionMeanings_en: Lets the client declare both identities in the body.
Puts both identities into URL parameters.
Swaps the roles of the path parameter and the JWT.
Treats the logged-in user as follower and the path target as followee.
why: 发起关注的一定是当前认证用户（JWT 里的身份），路径参数 [id] 是被关注的人；身份永远不信任客户端传的 body。
why_en: The follower is always the authenticated caller from the JWT, while the path parameter [id] names who gets followed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把用户身份编码进请求头的签名令牌格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes a user's identity, carried in the request header.

scenario: feed 按时间从新到旧返回，客户端不断上滑加载更旧内容（无限滚动）。
scenario_en: The feed returns newest-to-oldest posts, and the client keeps scrolling upward to load older content.
q: 哪个接口设计最合适？
q_en: Which feed pagination API design is the best fit?
options: GET /feed?page=3&pageSize=20，偏移量分页
GET /feed 一次性返回全部 feed
GET /feed?pageSize={n}&cursor={timestamp}
POST /feed，body 传回全部已看过的 postId
options_en: GET /feed?page=3&pageSize=20, offset pagination.
GET /feed returning the entire feed at once.
GET /feed?pageSize={n}&cursor={timestamp}, with nextCursor in the response.
POST /feed with a body listing every postId already seen.
optionMeanings: 用页码+页大小做分页。
不分页，一次返回全部。
用时间戳游标做分页。
让客户端上报已看过的全部帖子。
optionMeanings_en: Paginate with a page number and page size.
Skip pagination and return everything at once.
Paginate with a timestamp cursor.
Have the client report every post already seen.
why: 已看到的最旧帖子的时间戳一个值就完整描述进度，每页返回比它更旧的 N 条，比 offset 更稳定（新帖插入不会错位）。
why_en: A single timestamp cursor fully describes how far the user has scrolled, and it stays stable even when new posts are inserted, unlike offset pagination.
whenOtherWins: 数据量小且几乎不变的列表（后台管理页）用 offset/limit 更省事。
tradeoff: 游标分页的稳定性 vs offset 分页的简单直观

termDefinitions.meaning: 翻页用的标记，记录用户已看到的位置，用来取下一页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cursor is a pagination marker recording how far a user has scrolled, used to fetch the next page.

q: feed 接口里的 cursor 具体代表什么？
q_en: What does the cursor in the feed API represent?
options: 当前用户的 ID
服务端分配的页码
一个随机的会话令牌
用户已看到的最旧帖子的时间戳
options_en: The current user's ID.
A page number assigned by the server.
A random session token.
The timestamp of the oldest post the user has already seen.
optionMeanings: 把游标误认成用户标识。
把游标误认成传统页码。
把游标误认成认证令牌。
游标就是最旧已见帖子的时间戳。
optionMeanings_en: Mistakes the cursor for a user identifier.
Mistakes the cursor for a classic page number.
Mistakes the cursor for an auth token.
The cursor is exactly the timestamp of the oldest post seen.
why: 用户从新往旧看，一个时间戳就能标记『看到哪了』，天然有序、无需服务端存状态。
why_en: Since users scroll from newest to oldest, a single timestamp marks exactly how far they've read, with no server-side state needed.

q: 定义 API 时把帖子的 content 保持为空对象、暂不展开结构，动机是什么？
q_en: Why keep the post content field as an empty object instead of modeling its structure now?
options: 留扩展位，也把时间留给核心难点
帖子内容其实存在另一个系统里
JSON 不允许深层嵌套
内容结构由前端决定，后端无权定义
options_en: It leaves room for structured rich content while saving interview time for higher-value topics.
Post content is actually stored in a separate system.
JSON doesn't allow deeply nested structures.
Content structure is decided by the frontend, and the backend has no say.
optionMeanings: 把留白当成扩展位+时间管理的双重决定。
把内容归到一个假想的外部系统。
对 JSON 能力的错误认知。
把结构设计权完全让给前端的错误说法。
optionMeanings_en: Treats the placeholder as both an extension point and a time-management move.
Attributes content to an imaginary separate system.
A wrong belief about JSON's capabilities.
A wrong claim that structure is entirely the frontend's call.
why: content 留成对象可以日后装任何富内容；不深挖 Post 结构也是刻意的时间管理，把精力留给扇出这类核心难点。
why_en: Leaving content as an object keeps room for any future rich content, and skipping its details is a deliberate way to save time for the harder fan-out problems.

scenario: 发帖服务只往数据库写数据、本机不保存任何状态；流量增长时希望直接加机器就能扩容。
scenario_en: The post service only writes to the database and keeps no local state, so traffic growth should be handled by adding more machines.
q: 发帖链路的高层设计应该是？
q_en: What should the high-level post creation path look like?
options: 一台高配服务器垂直扩容
把会话状态放各服务器内存并做粘性路由
无状态 Post Service，加机器即扩容
先拆成几十个微服务再谈扩容
options_en: One beefier server, scaled vertically.
Keep session state in each server's memory with sticky routing.
API gateway plus load balancer in front of a stateless, horizontally scaled Post Service.
Split into dozens of microservices before even discussing scaling.
optionMeanings: 靠升级单机硬件扩容。
让每台服务器持有会话状态。
无状态服务水平扩展的标准形状。
在没有必要时过早做微服务拆分。
optionMeanings_en: Scales by upgrading a single machine's hardware.
Has each server hold its own session state.
The standard shape of a stateless, horizontally scaled service.
Splits into microservices prematurely, before it's needed.
why: 每台主机无状态（只写库），所以水平扩展极其简单：网关/负载均衡后面随意加机器。
why_en: Because every host is stateless and only writes to the database, horizontal scaling is as simple as adding more machines behind the gateway and load balancer.
whenOtherWins: 若服务必须维护本机状态（长连接、会话），要先做状态外置或粘性会话才能水平扩。
tradeoff: 无状态水平扩展 vs 有状态但可能更快的本地路径

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务实例不在本机保存请求间的状态，因此可以随意加减实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stateless service keeps no per-request state on the instance, so instances can be added or removed freely.

scenario: 存帖子：按 ID 写入/读取的简单键值访问模式，20 亿用户规模，需要能预置极高吞吐。
scenario_en: Posts are simple key-value writes and reads by ID at a 2-billion-user scale, with very high provisioned throughput.
q: 文中选择的存储及理由是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits posts, and why?
options: DynamoDB：负载均匀时吞吐很高
单实例 Postgres，靠索引硬撑
Neo4j，社交产品默认用图数据库
全内存数据库，所有帖子放 RAM
options_en: DynamoDB: simple and horizontally scalable, delivering very high throughput as long as load is spread evenly across partitions.
A single Postgres instance, pushed hard with indexes.
Neo4j, on the assumption social products default to a graph database.
An all-in-memory database, keeping every post in RAM.
optionMeanings: 分区式 KV 存储，靠均匀负载换高吞吐。
单机关系型数据库。
专用图数据库。
把全部数据放内存的存储形态。
optionMeanings_en: A partitioned key-value store trading even load for high throughput.
A single-instance relational database.
A purpose-built graph database.
A storage shape that keeps all data in RAM.
why: 访问模式是简单 KV（按 ID 存取），DynamoDB 简单又能水平扩到极高吞吐——前提是负载在分区间均匀。
why_en: Since access is a simple by-ID key-value pattern, DynamoDB scales to very high throughput as long as load stays even across partitions.
whenOtherWins: 需要复杂关系查询或多表事务时，关系型数据库更合适。
tradeoff: 水平扩展的简单 KV vs 复杂关系查询能力

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管 key-value 数据库，靠分区实现水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value database that scales horizontally by partitioning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款专用的图数据库，擅长多跳关系遍历。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Neo4j is a purpose-built graph database good at multi-hop relationship traversal.

scenario: follow 是多对多关系，本题只需三种简单查询：A 是否关注 B、A 关注了谁、谁关注 A，不做多跳遍历。
scenario_en: Follow is a many-to-many relationship, but this problem only needs three simple queries: does A follow B, who does A follow, and who follows A.
q: 关系数据用什么存？
q_en: What should store follow relationships?
options: Neo4j 专用图数据库
triple store 三元组存储
文档数据库，用嵌套数组存粉丝列表
普通 KV 表自己把图建模出来
options_en: A dedicated graph database like Neo4j.
A triple store.
A document database, storing follower lists as nested arrays.
A plain key-value table that models the graph itself.
optionMeanings: 专用图数据库，强项在多跳遍历。
以三元组存关系的图数据库形态。
把关注列表塞进文档的嵌套数组。
用两个键就能表达关系的 KV 建模。
optionMeanings_en: A dedicated graph database, strong at multi-hop traversal.
A graph-database form that stores relationships as triples.
Storing follower lists as nested arrays inside a document.
Modeling the relationship with just two keys in a KV table.
why: 图数据库的价值在遍历和图推导，这题查询固定又简单，KV 表两个键就能表达，还避开了给自己挖『如何扩展图库』的坑。
why_en: Graph databases earn their keep on traversal, but this problem's queries are fixed and simple enough that a two-key KV table covers them without adding a new system to scale.
whenOtherWins: 要做朋友的朋友、图 embedding 这类多跳遍历时，专用图数据库才真正值得引入。
tradeoff: 简单 KV 建模 vs 专用图数据库的遍历能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款专用的图数据库，擅长多跳关系遍历。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Neo4j is a purpose-built graph database good at multi-hop relationship traversal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以（主体, 谓词, 客体）三元组存储关系数据的图数据库形态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A triple store models relationships as subject-predicate-object triples.

q: 在『多跳遍历/图推导』这个维度上，专用图数据库和自建 KV 关系表的对比是？
q_en: How do a graph database and a custom KV relationship table compare for multi-hop traversal?
options: 两者能力一样，只差价格
KV 表更擅长遍历
图数据库擅长跨节点步进；KV 表只适合固定的单跳查询
图数据库只是营销概念，没有真实能力差异
options_en: Both have the same capability, differing only in price.
The KV table is actually better at traversal.
Graph databases excel at stepping across nodes; a KV table only fits fixed single-hop queries.
Graph databases are just marketing, with no real capability difference.
optionMeanings: 认为两种存储的遍历能力等价。
把遍历优势说反了。
按『多跳 vs 单跳』划分两者的强项。
否认图数据库有任何真实技术优势。
optionMeanings_en: Claims the two stores have equal traversal capability.
Reverses which one is actually better at traversal.
Splits the strengths by 'multi-hop vs single-hop'.
Denies graph databases have any real technical edge.
why: 图数据库的强项是需要在节点间反复步进的查询——朋友的朋友、图 embedding；固定的单跳查询，KV 表就够，还省掉运维一个新系统。
why_en: Graph databases shine at queries that hop repeatedly between nodes, while a fixed single-hop query is fully covered by a KV table without adding a new system.
tradeoff: 多跳遍历能力 vs 运维简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询需要在图上连续跳过多个节点，比如朋友的朋友。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-hop traversal means a query must step across several graph nodes in sequence, like friends of friends.

scenario: 在 DynamoDB 建 Follow 表，要求：① 点查『A 是否关注 B』；② range 查『A 关注的所有人』。
scenario_en: Build a DynamoDB Follow table that can point-check whether A follows B and range-query everyone A follows.
q: 主键应该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the Follow table primary key be designed?
options: PK = userFollowing，SK = userFollowed
PK = userFollowed，SK = userFollowing
PK = 随机 followId，无 SK
把整份关注列表序列化成一个大 JSON 存成单行
options_en: Partition key = userFollowing, sort key = userFollowed.
Partition key = userFollowed, sort key = userFollowing.
Partition key = a random followId, with no sort key.
Serialize the whole follow list into one giant JSON row.
optionMeanings: 以关注者为分区键、被关注者为排序键。
把分区键和排序键的角色对调。
用无意义的随机键，丢掉排序能力。
把整张表压缩进一行大 JSON。
optionMeanings_en: Partitions by the follower, sorts by the followee.
Swaps which field is the partition key and which is the sort key.
Uses a meaningless random key and loses sort capability.
Compresses the whole table into one giant JSON row.
codeSample:
Table: Follow
  Partition key: userFollowing
  Sort key:      userFollowed

-- A follows B?   get(PK=A, SK=B)
-- who does A follow?  query(PK=A)
why: 分区键 userFollowing + 排序键 userFollowed：两键齐给就是点查关系，只给分区键就是 range 查 A 的全部关注对象。
why_en: Partitioning by userFollowing and sorting by userFollowed lets you point-query the relationship with both keys, or range-query everyone A follows with just the partition key.
whenOtherWins: 若最高频查询是『谁关注了我』，就该把 userFollowed 当分区键——这正是反向 GSI 补上的方向。
tradeoff: 服务『我关注了谁』 vs 服务『谁关注我』

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定数据落在哪个物理分区的键，同分区键的数据支持排序键的 range 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which physical partition data lands on; items sharing a partition key can be range-queried by sort key.

q: Follow 表上那个 GSI（全局二级索引）是用来做什么的？
q_en: What is the GSI on the Follow table used for?
options: 提升写入吞吐
给帖子按时间排序
防止重复关注
反转键序，支持查粉丝列表
options_en: Boosting write throughput.
Sorting posts by time.
Preventing duplicate follows.
Reversing the key order to support a range query for 'all followers of a user'.
optionMeanings: 把索引的作用误归到写吞吐。
把索引的作用误归到帖子排序。
把索引的作用误归到去重约束。
反向 GSI：PK=userFollowed，SK=userFollowing。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly attributes the index's role to write throughput.
Wrongly attributes the index's role to sorting posts.
Wrongly attributes the index's role to a dedupe constraint.
The reverse GSI: partition key userFollowed, sort key userFollowing.
why: 主表只能按『我关注了谁』查；把键反过来建 GSI，才能按 userFollowed 一次 range 查询拉出全部粉丝——写扇出时 worker 就靠它。
why_en: The base table only answers 'who I follow', so the GSI reverses the keys to range-query all of a user's followers, which is exactly what fan-out workers rely on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引，支持另一种查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key that supports another query pattern.

q: Follow 表 + 反向 GSI 一共支持哪些查询？（多选）
q_en: Which queries are supported by the Follow table plus the reverse GSI? (Select all that apply.)
options: PK+SK 点查：判断 A 是否关注了 B
主表 PK range 查询：A 关注的所有人
GSI PK range 查询：关注 A 的所有人
一条查询直接拿到『朋友的朋友』
options_en: PK+SK point lookup: is A following B?
Base-table PK range query: everyone A follows.
GSI PK range query: everyone who follows A.
A single query that returns 'friends of friends' directly.
optionDirectness: 两键齐给用于判重或判断 A 是否已经关注 B。
主表分区键查询用于拉出 A 的关注列表。
反向 GSI 分区键查询用于写扇出时拉粉丝列表。
朋友的朋友需要多跳遍历，这张 KV 表不负责。
optionDirectness_en: Both keys are used for dedupe or checking whether A already follows B.
A base-table partition-key query returns everyone A follows.
A reverse-GSI partition-key query returns followers for write fan-out.
Friends-of-friends needs multi-hop traversal, which this KV table does not own.
why: 三种查询正好覆盖全部功能需求：关系点查、正向列表、反向列表。多跳遍历不支持——那是图数据库的领域。
why_en: These three queries cover the full functional scope: relationship lookup, forward list, and reverse list, but multi-hop traversal is left to graph databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引，支持另一种查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key that supports another query pattern.

q: 补全 Follow 表的键设计：
q_en: Complete the key design for the Follow table.
text: Follow 主表：分区键 {{userFollowing}}、排序键 {{userFollowed}}；GSI 把两键反转，分区键为 {{userFollowed}}，用于查某用户的粉丝列表。
why: 键设计决定查询能力：主表服务『我关注了谁/是否关注』，反向 GSI 服务『谁关注我』。写扇出与读路径都建立在它上面。
why_en: The key design decides which queries are possible: the base table serves who I follow, and the reverse GSI serves who follows me.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

scenario: 你已经用 DynamoDB 分别建了 Post 表和 Follow 表，面试官追问生产环境的表设计惯例。
scenario_en: You have modeled separate Post and Follow tables in DynamoDB, and the interviewer asks about production table-design practice.
q: 关于 DynamoDB 的表设计，AWS 官方推荐的生产实践是什么？
q_en: What DynamoDB table-design practice does AWS recommend for production?
options: DynamoDB 不支持多张表
AWS 推荐单表，面试分表也可以
必须严格一个实体一张表
GSI 免费且数量无限，随便加
options_en: DynamoDB doesn't support multiple tables.
AWS recommends single-table design in production, but splitting tables for clarity in an interview is fine.
Every entity must strictly get its own table.
GSIs are free and unlimited, so add as many as you like.
optionMeanings: 对 DynamoDB 能力的错误认知。
生产实践单表 vs 面试表达分表的区别。
把『可以分表』误解成『必须分表』。
对 GSI 成本和配额的错误认知。
optionMeanings_en: A wrong belief about DynamoDB's capabilities.
Distinguishes production's single-table practice from an interview's split-table clarity.
Misreads 'tables may be split' as 'tables must be split'.
A wrong belief about GSI cost and quotas.
why: 生产上 AWS 推荐把多个实体塞进一张表（single-table design）；面试里分表讲清楚完全没问题。
why_en: In production AWS recommends packing multiple entities into one table, but splitting tables for a clearer interview explanation is perfectly fine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一张 DynamoDB 表里存多种实体，用键设计区分类型，是 AWS 推荐的生产实践。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single-table design stores multiple entity types in one DynamoDB table, distinguished by key design; it is AWS's recommended production pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

scenario: 刷 feed 是重读负载，查询模式与发帖、关注完全不同，希望能独立扩缩容和演进。
scenario_en: Feed reads are heavy and have a very different query pattern from posting and following, so this logic should scale and evolve independently.
q: 架构上应该怎么组织这块逻辑？
q_en: How should the feed-generation logic be organized architecturally?
options: 并入 Post Service 一起处理
并入 Follow Service
拆出一个独立的 Feed Service
下放到客户端自行聚合
options_en: Fold it into the Post Service.
Fold it into the Follow Service.
Split it out into its own Feed Service.
Push it down to the client to aggregate itself.
optionMeanings: 让写密集的 Post Service 兼管读密集的 feed。
让 Follow Service 兼管 feed 生成。
为 feed 单独建立一个读密集服务。
让客户端自己拉数据拼 feed。
optionMeanings_en: Has the write-heavy Post Service also handle the read-heavy feed.
Has the Follow Service also handle feed generation.
Stands up a dedicated read-heavy service just for the feed.
Has the client fetch data and assemble the feed itself.
why: feed 生成读多写少、查询模式独特，和发帖/关注放一起会互相拖累扩容；单独拆出 Feed Service 能独立优化读路径。
why_en: Feed generation is read-heavy with a distinct query pattern, so bundling it with posting or following would slow both down.
whenOtherWins: 系统和团队都很小时，先合在一个服务里更简单；过早拆分只会增加运维负担。
tradeoff: 独立扩容能力 vs 拆分带来的运维复杂度

q: 把 naive（朴素）feed 生成的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the naive feed-generation steps in the right order.
steps: 把汇总的全部帖子按时间倒序排好，返回给用户
从 Follow 表查出该用户关注的所有账号
用 Post 表的 GSI 拉取这些账号的帖子
why: 朴素三步：拿关注列表 → 拉各账号帖子 → 排序返回。它功能正确，但每一步都会在规模变大时爆炸。
why_en: The naive flow is three steps: fetch the follow list, pull each account's posts, then sort and return, and it works correctly but every step explodes at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

scenario: 拿到关注列表后，要按时间序快速取出『这批 creator 的全部帖子』，而 Post 表目前只能按 postId 存取。
scenario_en: After getting the follow list, we need to fetch all posts by those creators in time order, but the Post table currently only supports postId access.
q: 怎么补上这个能力？
q_en: How do we add this access pattern?
options: 加 GSI：creatorId 分区、createdAt 排序
扫全表再按 creator 过滤
把每条帖子冗余复制进所有粉丝的行
在应用层内存里维护 creator 到 posts 的映射
options_en: Add a GSI to the Post table: partition key creatorId, sort key createdAt.
Scan the entire table and filter by creator in memory.
Duplicate every post into every follower's own row.
Maintain a creator-to-posts mapping in application memory.
optionMeanings: 按作者分区、按时间排序的二级索引。
全表扫描后再过滤的暴力做法。
把写扇出提前搬到发帖那一刻做冗余复制。
把持久化状态错放进无状态应用进程。
optionMeanings_en: A secondary index partitioned by author and sorted by time.
A brute-force full-table scan followed by filtering.
Moves write fan-out to post time via redundant copies.
Puts persistent state in the wrong place: a stateless app process.
why: GSI 用 creatorId 分区、createdAt 排序，就能按账号一次 range 查询拉出时间序的帖子，是 naive 读路径的基础索引。
why_en: A GSI partitioned by creatorId and sorted by createdAt lets a single range query return an account's posts in time order.
whenOtherWins: 彻底走预计算 feed 后主读路径不再依赖它，但未预计算大 V 的实时拉取仍需要这个 GSI。
tradeoff: 读侧一次 range 查询 vs 额外维护一个索引的写开销

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

q: 看到 naive feed 方案，应该立刻在心里拉响哪些警报？（多选）
q_en: What warning signs should you see in the naive feed design? (Select all that apply.)
options: 用户可能关注了大量账号
被关注的每个账号可能各有海量帖子
两者叠加，待排序的帖子总集可能非常大
DynamoDB 不支持按排序键做 range 查询
options_en: The user may follow a huge number of accounts.
Each followed account may have a huge number of posts.
Combined, the total set of posts to sort can become enormous.
DynamoDB can't range-query by sort key.
optionDirectness: 关注数越大，一次 feed 请求要打的下游查询越多。
单账号帖子越多，每个 creator 查询返回的候选越大。
两个因子相乘后，内存排序集合会快速失控。
GSI 排序键本来就支持 range 查询，这不是警报。
optionDirectness_en: The larger the follow count, the more downstream queries one feed request triggers.
The more posts each creator has, the larger each creator query can return.
Multiplying both factors makes the in-memory sort set grow out of control.
A GSI sort key is designed for range queries, so this is not the alarm.
why: 三个警报同根同源：扇出。关注多则查询多，帖子多则每个查询返回多，乘起来排序集巨大。
why_en: All three alarms share one root cause, fan-out: more follows means more queries, more posts per account means bigger results, and multiplied together the sort set explodes.

q: 为什么说 news feed 是『scaling reads』模式的教科书案例？
q_en: Why is a news feed a textbook scaling-reads problem?
options: 写远多于读
读写基本均衡，无从优化
内容无法缓存，只能加机器
读远多于写，且集中在近期内容
options_en: Writes far outnumber reads.
Reads and writes are roughly balanced, leaving nothing to optimize.
Content can't be cached, so the only lever is adding machines.
Reads vastly outnumber writes, and users mostly look at the first few items, so aggressively caching recent content pays off hugely.
optionMeanings: 把读写比例说反了。
假设这个负载没有优化空间。
误认为 feed 内容不可缓存。
读密集且集中在近期内容的负载模式。
optionMeanings_en: Reverses the actual read/write ratio.
Assumes this workload has no room to optimize.
Wrongly assumes feed content can't be cached.
A read-heavy workload concentrated on recent content.
why: feed 是典型读密集负载，且读集中在最新的少数几条上，所以预计算 feed、缓存近期帖子、聪明分页收益极高。
why_en: The feed is a classic read-heavy workload concentrated on the newest few items, which is exactly why precomputing feeds and caching recent posts pay off so well.

scenario: 要做无限滚动：必须用尽量少的状态表达『用户看到哪了』，而 feed 严格按时间从新到旧展示。
scenario_en: For infinite scroll, we need minimal state to express where the user has read to, and the feed is strictly newest to oldest.
q: 用什么作为翻页游标最合适？
q_en: What is the best pagination cursor?
options: offset 页码
用户已看到的最旧帖子的时间戳
服务端会话里记录完整浏览位置
客户端回传全部已见 postId 列表
options_en: An offset page number.
The timestamp of the oldest post the user has already seen.
A full scroll position recorded in a server session.
The client sends back a list of every postId already seen.
optionMeanings: 按页码计数的传统分页。
把已见位置压缩成一个时间戳。
在服务端为每个会话存完整状态。
让客户端携带不断增长的已见列表。
optionMeanings_en: Traditional pagination counted by page number.
Compresses the seen-position into a single timestamp.
Stores full state per session on the server.
Has the client carry an ever-growing list of seen posts.
why: 倒序浏览下，最旧已见帖子的时间戳一个数就完整描述进度：下一页是比它更旧的 N 条。
why_en: In a newest-first feed, the timestamp of the oldest post seen fully describes progress, since the next page is just the N posts older than it.
