whenOtherWins: 排序不是纯时间（个性化打分）时，需要改用编码了排序键的不透明 cursor。
tradeoff: 无状态时间戳游标 vs 服务端存储的浏览位置

termDefinitions.meaning: 翻页用的标记，记录用户已看到的位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cursor is a pagination marker recording how far a user has scrolled.

q: 为什么支持翻页几乎不需要新增任何基础设施？
q_en: Why does pagination need almost no new infrastructure here?
options: GSI 已按 createdAt 排序，直接加时间过滤
翻页逻辑全部在客户端完成
DynamoDB 自带页码功能
因为 feed 不需要翻页
options_en: The Post table's GSI is already sorted by createdAt, so a range query directly supports 'older than cursor'.
All pagination logic runs entirely on the client.
DynamoDB comes with a built-in page-number feature.
Because the feed doesn't actually need pagination.
optionMeanings: 复用已有排序索引的 range 查询能力。
把服务端职责错放到客户端。
对 DynamoDB 能力的错误认知。
与需求『用户能翻页』直接矛盾。
optionMeanings_en: Reuses the existing sorted index's range-query capability.
Wrongly shifts server responsibility to the client.
A wrong belief about DynamoDB's built-in capabilities.
Directly contradicts the stated requirement to support paging.
why: GSI 的排序键就是 createdAt，range 查询天然支持『小于某时间戳』，翻页版流程只是多加了一个过滤条件。
why_en: Since the GSI is already sorted by createdAt, a range query naturally supports 'less than this timestamp', so pagination is just one extra filter on the existing flow.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

q: 补全带翻页的 feed 读取流程：
q_en: Complete the paginated feed read flow.
text: 翻页版流程：查出关注列表 → 拉取这些账号{{早于 cursor 时间戳}}的帖子 → 按时间{{倒序}}排序返回，并附上 {{nextCursor}} 供下一页使用。
why: 与 naive 流程唯一的区别是第二步多了时间过滤。cursor 向过去推进，每页都是更旧的内容。
why_en: The only difference from the naive flow is an added time filter in step two, and the cursor keeps moving further into the past with each page.

scenario: Feed Service 处理一次刷 feed 请求时，内部要挨个查询数百个被关注账号的帖子。
scenario_en: For one feed request, Feed Service internally queries posts from hundreds of followed accounts.
q: 什么是 fan-out on read？
q_en: What is fan-out on read?
options: 一次写请求触发多次下游写
一次读扇出成大量下游请求
读请求被复制到多个只读副本
缓存雪崩的另一种叫法
options_en: One write request triggers many downstream writes.
One read request fans out into many downstream requests inside the system, like querying hundreds of followed accounts to build one feed.
A read request gets replicated to multiple read replicas.
Another name for a cache stampede.
optionMeanings: 这描述的其实是写扇出。
读时现算：一个读请求内部炸开成多个请求。
把只读副本的路由误认为扇出。
把缓存雪崩和读扇出混为一谈。
optionMeanings_en: This actually describes write fan-out, not read fan-out.
Computing at read time: one read request explodes into many internal requests.
Confuses read-replica routing with fan-out.
Conflates a cache stampede with read fan-out.
why: 读扇出 = 进来一个请求、内部炸开成许多请求。用户关注得越多，Follow 查询越慢、Post 查询越多，延迟越不可控。
why_en: Fan-out on read means one incoming request explodes into many internal requests, so the more accounts a user follows, the more unpredictable the latency gets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次读请求在系统内部被放大成大量下游请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read means one read request gets amplified into many downstream requests inside the system.

scenario: 刷一次 feed 时，请求在内部会扇出成数十到上百次下游查询；面试官问你对扇出数量级的经验判断。
scenario_en: One feed refresh can fan out into tens or hundreds of downstream queries; the interviewer is asking for your order-of-magnitude judgment.
q: 这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this fan-out scale support?
options: 扇出超过 10 个请求就不可接受
上千级扇出很常见，不必担心
几十到上百常见，上千级基本不可行
扇出数量与延迟无关
options_en: Any fan-out above 10 requests is unacceptable.
Fan-out in the thousands is common and nothing to worry about.
Tens to hundreds of fan-out requests are common, but thousands are basically unworkable for a low-latency service.
The amount of fan-out has no effect on latency.
why: 10s-100s 的扇出是正常工程现实；1000s 级别在延迟敏感的在线服务里几乎撑不住，这个量级感帮你判断何时必须换思路。
why_en: Tens to hundreds of fan-out requests are normal engineering reality, but thousands are nearly unworkable for a latency-sensitive service and signal it's time to precompute instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求或写入在系统内部被放大成大量下游请求或写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one request or write gets amplified into many downstream requests or writes.

scenario: 关注数极大的用户读 feed 时扇出失控；而这个系统读远比写频繁、且容忍 1 分钟陈旧。
scenario_en: Users who follow huge numbers of accounts make read fan-out explode, while this system is read-heavy and tolerates one-minute staleness.
q: 优化的核心思路应该是？
q_en: What is the core optimization idea?
options: 把扇出搬到写时：发帖即预写各粉丝 feed
无限增加只读副本
让客户端并行发起所有查询
把排序逻辑下放给 CDN
options_en: Move the work from read time to write time: precompute each follower's feed the moment a post is created.
Keep adding an unlimited number of read replicas.
Let the client fire off all the queries in parallel.
Push the sorting logic down to the CDN.
optionMeanings: fan-out on write：把扇出成本转移到写路径。
只加副本，不改变扇出本身的形状。
把服务端的扇出问题转嫁给客户端设备。
CDN 是静态内容分发层，不是动态排序引擎。
optionMeanings_en: Fan-out on write: shifts the fan-out cost onto the write path.
Just adding replicas without changing the shape of fan-out itself.
Offloads the server's fan-out problem onto the client device.
A CDN distributes static content; it isn't a dynamic ranking engine.
why: 读多写少 + 容忍短暂陈旧 = 把昂贵的扇出搬到写路径：发帖时预写各粉丝的 feed，读的时候一次点查就够。
why_en: Being read-heavy and tolerant of brief staleness is exactly what justifies moving the expensive fan-out to write time, so a post prewrites into each follower's feed.
whenOtherWins: 对粉丝数百万的大 V，写扇出的代价反过来爆炸，这些账号应保留读时拉取。
tradeoff: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read

termDefinitions.meaning: 在写入（发帖）时就把结果预先分发到每个下游位置，而不是等读时再算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on write means pushing results out to every downstream location at write time instead of computing them on read.

scenario: 只有极少数用户关注了 10 万个账号；为这条长尾把整体架构复杂度拉满并不划算。
scenario_en: Only a tiny fraction of users follow 100,000 accounts, so optimizing the whole architecture for that tail is not worth it.
q: 如何处理这条长尾，避免为它抬高整体架构复杂度？
q_en: How should we handle this long tail without making the whole architecture more complex?
options: 坚持在技术上无条件支持无限关注
问面试官能否给关注数设上限
直接禁止这类用户使用产品
忽略这个边缘情况不谈
options_en: Insist on unconditionally supporting unlimited follows at any technical cost.
Check with the interviewer whether a follow cap is acceptable (like Facebook's 5000-friend limit), or give these users a slightly degraded experience.
Simply ban these users from the product.
Ignore this edge case and never mention it.
optionMeanings: 为极端长尾无条件加码架构复杂度。
用产品层面的上限来限定技术问题的边界。
把边缘用户直接排除在产品之外。
对已发现的问题选择不提及。
optionMeanings_en: Unconditionally scales up architectural complexity for an extreme tail.
Uses a product-level cap to bound the technical problem.
Excludes edge-case users from the product entirely.
Chooses not to mention a problem already identified.
why: 生产系统对极端用户设上限或差异化体验很常见；和面试官确认『产品能不能改』既现实又展示产品意识。
why_en: Production systems commonly cap extreme users, and asking the interviewer whether the product can flex is realistic and shows product judgment.
whenOtherWins: 若无限关注被确认为硬性需求，就必须靠混合扇出等架构手段真正解决。
tradeoff: 产品层面设上限 vs 架构层面无限支持

q: PrecomputedFeed 表的结构是什么样的？
q_en: What does the PrecomputedFeed table look like?
options: PK = postId，值是粉丝列表
PK = userId、SK = createdAt，每条帖子一行
PK=userId，值是倒序 postID 列表，截断约 200
一张宽表冗余存储帖子全文
options_en: Partition key postId, with a value holding the follower list.
Partition key userId, sort key createdAt, one row per post.
Partition key userId, with a value holding a reverse-chronological list of postIDs capped around 200, looked up only by userId.
A wide table redundantly storing full post text.
optionMeanings: 把键设计反过来，围绕帖子而不是用户。
每条帖子存一行，条目数会随粉丝数线性增长。
每用户一条紧凑条目，只按 userId 点查。
把帖子全文也复制进这张表。
optionMeanings_en: Inverts the key design around the post instead of the user.
Stores one row per post, growing linearly with follower count.
One compact entry per user, looked up only by userId.
Also duplicates full post text into this table.
why: 每个用户一条紧凑条目：倒序 postID 列表、限长约 200，只按 userId 点查，因此零二级索引。
why_en: Each user gets one compact entry, a reverse-chronological postID list capped around 200, looked up only by userId with no secondary index needed.

q: feed 条目为什么只存 postID 列表、还截断在 200 条左右？
q_en: Why store only a list of postIDs in each feed entry and cap it around 200 items?
options: DynamoDB 单行只允许 2KB
200 是 SQS 的批量投递上限
客户端一次最多渲染 200 条
紧凑条目控制总存储，长尾靠回退方案
options_en: DynamoDB limits every row to 2KB.
200 is SQS's batch-delivery limit.
The client can render at most 200 items at once.
Keeping entries compact controls total storage at 2B users, and real users rarely scroll that deep, with a fallback covering those who do.
optionMeanings: 对 DynamoDB 行大小限制的错误引用。
把 SQS 的批处理限制错套用在这里。
把存储上限归因到客户端渲染能力。
紧凑存储 + 长尾覆盖率低 + 有回退方案的组合理由。
optionMeanings_en: Cites a wrong DynamoDB row-size limit.
Wrongly borrows SQS's batching limit for this decision.
Attributes the cap to client-rendering capacity.
A combination of compact storage, low tail coverage, and a fallback path.
why: 紧凑条目 = 可控成本：10 字节的 postID × 200 条才 2KB。这个 200 可以按尾部用户受影响程度和成本权衡上下调。
why_en: A compact entry keeps cost controlled since 200 ten-byte postIDs is only 2KB, and this cap can be tuned up or down based on the tail impact and cost tradeoff.

q: 用户真的把 200 条预计算 feed 翻完了，系统怎么办？
q_en: What should the system do if a user really scrolls past the 200 precomputed feed items?
options: 返回空页并提示没有更多内容
从头循环再显示一遍
回退到 naive 路径现查更旧内容
系统必须为每人预存 10 万条以避免这种情况
options_en: Return an empty page saying there's no more content.
Loop back and show the same content again from the top.
Fall back to the naive path: query the Follow table and the Post table's GSI on demand for older content.
The system must pre-store 100,000 entries per user to avoid this.
optionMeanings: 直接放弃对长尾用户的支持。
用错误的循环体验掩盖数据不足。
把预计算路径当快路径，naive 路径当慢路径兜底。
为避免罕见场景付出不成比例的存储代价。
optionMeanings_en: Simply gives up on supporting tail users.
Masks insufficient data with a broken looping experience.
Treats the precomputed path as fast path and the naive path as a slow fallback.
Pays a disproportionate storage cost to avoid a rare scenario.
why: 预计算只是快路径，不是唯一路径：翻穿了就退回按需查询的 naive 方案，快慢路径分层覆盖不同场景。
why_en: Precomputation is only the fast path, not the only one, so once it's exhausted the system falls back to the on-demand naive query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

q: 在『读 feed 时要做多少工作』这个维度上，预计算 feed 和 naive 现查的对比是？
q_en: How do precomputed feeds and naive on-demand reads compare on read-path work?
options: 两者读时工作量一样，只差数据新旧
naive 更快，因为不用维护额外的表
预计算方案读时也要现场排序全部帖子
预计算一次点查；naive 现查+全量排序
options_en: Both do the same amount of read-time work, differing only in data freshness.
Naive is faster because it avoids maintaining an extra table.
The precomputed approach still sorts every post at read time.
Precomputed: one point query returns a ready list. Naive: fetch the follow list, query per account, then sort everything.
optionMeanings: 认为两种方案的读时开销相等。
把维护额外表的成本和读时工作量混为一谈。
误解预计算方案还需要现场排序。
点查 vs 现查+排序的真实工作量对比。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes the two approaches cost the same at read time.
Conflates the cost of maintaining an extra table with read-time work.
Wrongly believes the precomputed approach still sorts on read.
The real contrast: a point query versus on-demand query plus sort.
why: 预计算把『查 N 个账号 + 排序』的成本提前付掉，读路径退化成一次点查；代价转移到写路径。
why_en: Precomputation pays the cost of querying N accounts and sorting upfront, reducing the read path to a single point query while shifting the cost to writes.
tradeoff: 读时一次点查 vs 写时预付扇出成本

q: 『如果用户往回翻 100 页怎么办？』的现实工程答案是？
q_en: What is the practical engineering answer to 'what if a user scrolls back 100 pages'?
options: 必须完整支持，不计成本
大多数系统不支持极深翻页
把全部历史缓存到客户端
为深翻页单独建一套集群
options_en: It must be fully supported, whatever the cost.
Most systems simply don't support very deep pagination, because real users never scroll that far.
Cache a user's entire history on the client.
Stand up a separate cluster just for deep pagination.
optionMeanings: 为极端场景无条件投入成本。
承认深翻页是罕见场景，选择不优化。
把服务端问题转嫁到客户端存储。
为一个几乎不会发生的场景单独建基础设施。
optionMeanings_en: Unconditionally invests in an extreme scenario.
Accepts deep pagination is rare and deliberately doesn't optimize for it.
Shifts a server-side problem onto client storage.
Stands up dedicated infrastructure for a scenario that almost never happens.
why: 深翻页是典型的『理论问题』：真实产品直接不支持或弱支持。敢说『这个场景我们选择不优化』本身就是成熟判断。
why_en: Very deep pagination is a classic theoretical concern that real products simply don't support well, and saying so out loud is itself a sign of engineering maturity.

scenario: 预计算 feed 的存储估算：每个 postID 约 10 字节，每人保留约 200 条，系统约 20 亿用户。
scenario_en: Precomputed-feed storage estimate: each postID is about 10 bytes, each user keeps about 200 entries, and the system has about 2 billion users.
q: 这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this storage estimate support?
options: 每用户 2KB，总计约 4TB——对现代系统完全可行
每用户 2MB，总计 4PB，不可行
每用户 20KB，总计 40TB，需要重新设计
每用户 200B，总计 400GB，可以忽略存储问题
options_en: About 2KB per user, roughly 4TB total, comfortably feasible for a modern system.
About 2MB per user, roughly 4PB total, infeasible.
About 20KB per user, roughly 40TB total, needing a redesign.
About 200B per user, roughly 400GB total, small enough to ignore storage entirely.
why: 10B × 200 = 2KB/人；2KB × 20 亿 = 4TB。动手把存储算出来再下结论『合理』，是面试里该展示的习惯。
why_en: 10 bytes times 200 entries is 2KB per user, and 2KB times 2 billion users is about 4TB, which is a comfortable number for a modern system.

scenario: 已知每用户 feed 存储约 2KB/月的成本，而 Facebook 每个美国用户年收入约 100 美元。
scenario_en: Per-user feed storage costs about 2KB per month, while Facebook earns roughly $100 per US user per year.
q: 判断这笔存储值不值，有条好用的经验法则是？
q_en: What rule of thumb helps decide whether this storage cost is worth it?
options: 和竞品的存储量对比
按每用户美元成本对比收入
只看总量是否超过 1PB
找存储团队审批预算
options_en: Compare total storage against competitors.
Convert cost to dollars per user or tenant and compare it against the revenue that user brings in; here it's a fraction of a cent a month, no problem.
Just check whether the total exceeds 1PB.
Ask the storage team to approve the budget.
why: 把成本折算到『每用户多少钱』再对比『每用户赚多少钱』，一句话就能证明设计经济上成立。
why_en: Converting cost to dollars per user and comparing it against revenue per user is a quick way to prove a design is economically sound.

q: 预计算 feed 大幅改善了读性能，但同时制造了什么新问题？
q_en: What new problem does precomputing the feed create?
options: 读延迟反而上升
feed 的时间顺序会错乱
存储成本失控到不可行
读扇出变成了写扇出
options_en: Read latency actually goes up.
The feed's time ordering gets scrambled.
Storage cost spirals out of control.
A single post from a high-follower account must efficiently update a million follower feeds; read fan-out has become write fan-out.
optionMeanings: 与预计算的实际效果相反的错误说法。
预计算不改变排序逻辑本身。
存储成本已估算过，是可控的。
扇出成本从读路径转移到了写路径。
optionMeanings_en: The opposite of what precomputation actually achieves.
Precomputation doesn't change the sorting logic itself.
Storage cost was already estimated and is under control.
The fan-out cost has moved from the read path to the write path.
why: 扇出没有消失，只是从读路径搬到了写路径：粉丝越多，发帖时要更新的 feed 条目越多。
why_en: Fan-out hasn't disappeared, it has just moved from the read path to the write path, since more followers means more feed entries to update per post.

q: 补全选择 fan-out on write 的推理：
q_en: Complete the reasoning for choosing fan-out on write.
text: 敢把扇出搬到写时，是因为这个系统{{读}}远多于写，且非功能需求允许 {{1 分钟}}内的帖子陈旧——发帖后有一个短窗口，可以异步把 postId 写进各粉丝的 {{PrecomputedFeed}} 表。
why: 这是条件反射级的推理链：读密集 + 容忍陈旧 → 写时预计算。没有那 1 分钟窗口，异步扇出就不成立。
why_en: This is a reflexive chain: read-heavy plus staleness-tolerant leads directly to precomputing at write time.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统必须让新帖立刻对所有粉丝可见，就不能靠异步写扇出，只能读时拉取或同步写。
tradeoff: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read

termDefinitions.meaning: 在写入时把结果预先分发到每个下游位置，而不是等读时再算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on write pre-distributes results to downstream locations at write time instead of computing them on read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按用户保存的预计算 feed 列表，读时可一次点查返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PrecomputedFeed is a per-user prebuilt feed list that can be returned with one point lookup.

q: 发帖时由 Post Service 同步『一口气』写完百万粉丝的 feed，为什么行不通？
q_en: Why can't Post Service synchronously blast feed writes to millions of followers?
options: DynamoDB 不支持批量写入
会破坏帖子的时间排序
单机连接/延迟撑不住，负载也不均
SQS 有消息大小限制
options_en: DynamoDB doesn't support batch writes.
It would break the post's time ordering.
A single host can't sustain the connection count or latency, and load becomes wildly uneven, with the host handling a celebrity's post pegged while others sit idle.
SQS has a message size limit.
optionMeanings: 对 DynamoDB 批写能力的错误认知。
同步写扇出与排序逻辑无关。
单机物理极限 + 主机间负载不均的双重死因。
这里还没涉及 SQS，属于无关选项。
optionMeanings_en: A wrong belief about DynamoDB's batch-write support.
Synchronous write fan-out has nothing to do with sort order.
The dual killers: single-host physical limits plus uneven cross-host load.
SQS isn't even in play yet here, an unrelated option.
why: 同步 blast 的死因有二：单机物理极限（连接数、延迟窗口），以及主机间负载的极端不均。
why_en: A synchronous blast dies for two reasons: a single host's physical limits on connections and latency, and the extreme load imbalance it creates across hosts.

q: 同步 blast 写扇出的具体问题包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What concrete problems does synchronous write fan-out create? (Select all that apply.)
options: 单个 Post Service 主机能建立的连接数有限
在延迟预算内根本写不完百万条 feed
主机间负载严重不均：一台在写百万条、另一台几乎闲置
会把帖子内容本身写坏
options_en: A single Post Service host can only open so many connections.
There's no way to finish writing a million feeds within the latency budget.
Load is badly imbalanced across hosts, one writing a million entries while another sits nearly idle.
It would corrupt the post content itself.
optionDirectness: 连接数上限会先卡住单台 Post Service 主机。
百万级同步写会直接打穿发帖返回的延迟预算。
负载不均会让一台机器爆满、其他机器闲着。
扇出方式影响容量和延迟，不会把帖子内容写坏。
optionDirectness_en: Connection count becomes a hard limit on one Post Service host.
A million synchronous writes blows through the post-response latency budget.
Load imbalance leaves one machine pegged while others sit idle.
Fan-out affects capacity and latency; it does not corrupt the post content.
why: 连接上限、延迟预算、负载不均三座大山，任何一座都足以否掉同步方案；数据本身不会写坏，问题在容量与均衡。
why_en: Connection limits, latency budget, and load imbalance are three separate blockers, and any one alone rules out the synchronous approach.

scenario: 系统允许发帖到 feed 可见之间有小于 1 分钟的延迟；要把百万级 feed 写摊平，且写入能力可水平扩容。
scenario_en: The system allows less than one minute from posting to feed visibility; it must spread million-scale feed writes and scale workers horizontally.
q: 写扇出应该怎么架构？
q_en: How should write fan-out be architected?
options: 发帖入队，异步 worker 车队消费更新
Post Service 同步向所有粉丝分片广播 RPC
用数据库触发器逐行触发更新
每小时跑一次批处理统一合并
options_en: On post creation, enqueue one message and let a fleet of async workers consume it and update follower feeds.
Have the Post Service synchronously broadcast RPCs to every follower shard.
Use database triggers to fire an update row by row.
Run one batch job every hour to merge everything at once.
optionMeanings: 队列 + 可水平扩容的异步 worker 车队。
本质仍是同步 blast，只是换了 RPC 形式。
把扇出逻辑塞进数据库触发器。
用固定周期的批处理牺牲实时性。
optionMeanings_en: A queue plus a horizontally scalable fleet of async workers.
Still a synchronous blast underneath, just wrapped in RPC form.
Buries the fan-out logic inside database triggers.
Trades away freshness for a fixed-interval batch job.
why: 既然容忍延迟，就把写请求排进队列，让可横向扩容的 worker 车队慢慢消化，负载被抹平。
why_en: Since the system tolerates a short delay, queuing the writes and letting a horizontally scalable fleet of workers drain them smooths out the load.
whenOtherWins: 若产品要求发帖立刻全局可见（强一致），队列带来的延迟不可接受，只能回到读时拉取。
tradeoff: 队列+异步 worker 的可扩展性 vs 立即一致的同步写

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管消息队列服务，提供 at-least-once 投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS is AWS's managed message queue that guarantees at-least-once delivery.

q: 对这条写扇出队列的硬性要求是什么？
q_en: What hard guarantee does the write fan-out queue need?
options: 必须提供 exactly-once 语义
必须严格 FIFO 保序
支持 at-least-once 投递、高度可扩展即可
必须是自建 Kafka 集群
options_en: It must offer exactly-once semantics.
It must be strictly FIFO-ordered.
At-least-once delivery plus high scalability is enough.
It must be a self-hosted Kafka cluster.
optionMeanings: 更强但通常更难实现和更贵的投递语义。
要求消息严格按顺序处理。
常见托管队列（如 SQS）默认提供的语义。
把具体产品选型误当成硬性要求。
optionMeanings_en: A stronger but usually harder and pricier delivery guarantee.
Requires messages to be processed in strict order.
The default guarantee offered by common managed queues like SQS.
Wrongly treats one specific product choice as a hard requirement.
why: 任何满足 at-least-once + 可扩展的队列都行，at-least-once 意味着可能重复投递，worker 的更新要能容忍重复。
why_en: Any queue that offers at-least-once delivery and scales horizontally works, and since at-least-once can redeliver, the worker's update logic just needs to tolerate duplicates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息投递语义：消息不会丢，但可能被重复投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery guarantees a message is never lost but may be delivered more than once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，结果和执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation produces the same result no matter how many times it is repeated.

scenario: 发帖事件已入队，worker 要完成扇出：得知道是哪条帖子、谁发的，然后更新每个粉丝的 feed 条目。
scenario_en: A post event is already queued. The worker must know which post was created and who created it, then update each follower's feed entry.
q: 消息内容与 worker 逻辑，哪种设计正确？
q_en: Which message payload and worker behavior is correct?
options: 消息内嵌帖子全文，worker 推送给所有在线粉丝
消息只带 postId+creatorId，worker 查粉丝并更新 feed
发帖方先查好全部粉丝、塞进消息里再入队
worker 定期扫描 Post 表发现新帖
options_en: Embed the full post text in the message; the worker pushes it to every online follower.
The message carries only postId and creatorId; the worker queries the reverse Follow GSI for followers and prepends the postId to each follower's feed list.
Have the poster look up every follower and stuff them into the message before enqueueing.
Have workers periodically scan the Post table to discover new posts.
optionMeanings: 把大内容塞进消息，消息体随帖子长度膨胀。
消息保持最小，粉丝查询和更新都留给 worker。
把本该由 worker 做的查询提前搬到发帖路径。
用轮询代替事件驱动，天然有延迟和浪费。
optionMeanings_en: Stuffs large content into the message, so message size grows with post length.
Keeps the message minimal, leaving follower lookup and updates to the worker.
Moves the worker's own lookup work upstream into the posting path.
Replaces event-driven processing with polling, adding delay and waste.
why: 消息保持最小（postId + creatorId），粉丝查询和 feed 更新都留给 worker 做，入队快、扩容压力在 worker 侧。
why_en: Keeping the message minimal, just postId and creatorId, lets the worker do the lookup and update, so enqueueing stays fast.
whenOtherWins: 粉丝量巨大时，一条消息可拆成多条、各带一段粉丝区间，避免单条消息的工作量畸大。
tradeoff: 消息小+worker 承担查询 vs 消息大+发帖方预先查询

termDefinitions.meaning: 在原表之外用不同分区键/排序键重新组织数据的二级索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is a secondary index with a different partition and sort key from the base table.

q: 异步 worker 方案落地后，仍然要面对的挑战是？
q_en: What challenge remains after moving fan-out to async workers?
options: 队列会随机丢消息
SQS 的费用高到不可行
无法保证 feed 的时间排序
worker 总吞吐大，单条消息工作量方差极大
options_en: The queue randomly loses messages.
SQS's cost is prohibitively high.
There's no way to guarantee the feed's time ordering.
The worker fleet needs enormous total throughput, and per-message work varies wildly, three orders of magnitude between pushing to a million followers versus a thousand.
optionMeanings: 对 at-least-once 队列可靠性的错误认知。
对托管队列成本的夸大说法。
排序逻辑与异步化无关，仍按时间戳排。
worker 车队吞吐与单条消息工作量方差的双重压力。
optionMeanings_en: A wrong belief about an at-least-once queue's reliability.
An exaggerated claim about a managed queue's cost.
Ordering logic is unrelated to going async; it still sorts by timestamp.
The dual pressure of fleet throughput and huge per-message work variance.
why: 小账号几百次写不算什么，大账号一条消息就是百万级工作，方差极大意味着大任务可能需要拆分。
why_en: A small account's writes are trivial, but one message for a mega account can mean millions of updates, so huge tasks may need splitting.

scenario: 某账号有 9000 万+粉丝，发一条帖等于 9000 万次 feed 写入，队列也救不动。
scenario_en: One account has 90 million or more followers, so one post would mean 90 million feed writes; even the queue cannot make that cheap.
q: 『great』级别的混合方案是？
q_en: What is the 'great' hybrid fan-out design?
options: 为大 V 建一条更大的专用队列
限制大 V 的发帖频率
高粉账号打 flag 跳过预计算，读时合并
把大 V 的帖子直接推送到所有客户端
options_en: Build an even bigger dedicated queue just for celebrities.
Rate-limit how often celebrities can post.
Flag high-follower accounts as 'skip precomputation': async workers ignore them, and the feed read merges in their recent posts separately.
Push a celebrity's post directly to every client.
optionMeanings: 只是把队列做大，量级问题本质没变。
用限制发帖频率规避问题，改变了产品行为。
只对高粉丝量的账号切换扇出策略。
不现实的全局广播推送。
optionMeanings_en: Just makes the queue bigger; the order-of-magnitude problem is unchanged.
Sidesteps the problem by rate-limiting posting, changing product behavior.
Gives up write fan-out for top accounts and falls back to read-time merging.
An unrealistic global push to every client.
why: 对头部账号放弃写扇出、改回读时拉取：Follow 表打 flag，worker 忽略，读侧合并，9000 万次写就此绕开。
why_en: For top accounts, this gives up write fan-out and falls back to read-time pulling, flagging them in the Follow table so workers skip them.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统里根本没有头部账号，全员统一 fan-out on write 更简单，犯不着做混合。
tradeoff: 头部账号读时合并 vs 全员统一写扇出

q: 混合方案下，用户请求 feed 时 Feed Service 具体做什么？
q_en: In the hybrid design, what does Feed Service do when a user requests their feed?
options: 只读预计算表，忽略大 V
全部现场拉取重新计算
随机在两种方式里选一种
预计算部分+大 V 近期帖子，读时合并
options_en: Only read the precomputed table and ignore celebrities.
Recompute everything from scratch on every request.
Randomly pick one of the two approaches each time.
Fetch the (partial) precomputed feed, pull recent posts from un-precomputed celebrity accounts, and merge them at read time.
optionMeanings: 会漏掉被 flag 账号的内容，体验不完整。
放弃了预计算带来的全部读性能收益。
没有依据的随机选择，行为不可预测。
两段拼接：预计算部分 + 实时拉取部分。
optionMeanings_en: Would drop content from flagged accounts entirely, an incomplete experience.
Throws away all the read-performance gains precomputation bought.
An unmotivated random choice with unpredictable behavior.
Two-part stitching: the precomputed part plus a real-time pulled part.
why: 读路径变成两段拼接：Feed 表里的预计算部分 + 被 flag 账号的实时近期帖子，绝大多数内容仍走快路径。
why_en: The read path becomes a two-part merge: the precomputed part from the Feed table plus real-time recent posts from flagged accounts, with most content still on the fast path.

scenario: 面试官追问：所以到底应该选 fan-out on write 还是 fan-out on read？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether the system should use fan-out on write or fan-out on read.
q: 体现设计成熟度的回答是？
q_en: Which answer shows design maturity?
options: 不必一刀切：按账号粒度分别选择，大多数用户其实两者兼用
永远 fan-out on write，读性能至上
永远 fan-out on read，写成本至上
看数据库品牌决定
options_en: It doesn't need to be one-size-fits-all: choose per account, and most users actually get a bit of both.
Always fan-out on write, read performance above all.
Always fan-out on read, write cost above all.
It depends on the database vendor.
optionMeanings: 按对象特征分别施策的混合策略。
把一种策略当成万能解，忽视头部账号的写爆炸。
把另一种策略当成万能解，忽视普通用户的读延迟。
把架构决策错误地归因到数据库品牌。
optionMeanings_en: A hybrid policy that adapts to each account's characteristics.
Treats one strategy as universal, ignoring write explosions for top accounts.
Treats the other strategy as universal, ignoring read latency for normal users.
Wrongly attributes the architecture decision to database vendor.
why: 混合方案的精髓：同一系统内按对象特征分别施策，不需要 one-size-fits-all 的答案。
why_en: The essence of the hybrid design is applying different strategies within the same system based on each account's characteristics, instead of forcing one-size-fits-all.
whenOtherWins: 小规模或账号分布均匀的系统里，统一策略更简单，混合方案的复杂度只有存在头部账号时才值得。
tradeoff: 按账号分层的混合策略 vs 全局统一策略

q: 混合扇出方案的代价是什么，怎么调节？
q_en: What is the cost of hybrid fan-out, and how can it be tuned?
options: 写路径整体变慢，无法调节
读时合并变贵，靠阈值调节平衡
存储直接翻倍
必须升级为强一致数据库
options_en: The whole write path gets slower, with no way to tune it.
Reads now require merging, increasing the Feed Service's compute cost; the follower-count threshold for skipping precomputation can be tuned to balance it.
Storage simply doubles.
The database must be upgraded to strong consistency.
optionMeanings: 错误归因，且否认了调节空间。
把合并成本明确指向读路径，并给出可调旋钮。
对存储代价的夸大说法。
与本题的一致性设计无关。
optionMeanings_en: A wrong attribution that also denies any tuning room.
Correctly points the merge cost at the read path, with a tunable knob.
An exaggerated claim about storage cost.
Unrelated to this problem's consistency design.
why: 把合并从写时挪到读时，读侧 CPU 变贵；阈值调高则读更省、写更贵，反之亦然，可按负载调优。
why_en: Moving the merge to read time adds compute cost there, and the follower-count threshold is a knob trading cheaper reads for pricier writes.

q: 补全混合扇出的机制：
q_en: Complete the hybrid fan-out mechanism.
text: 混合扇出：在 {{Follow}} 表上给高粉账号的关注关系打上不预计算的 flag；{{异步 worker}} 消费队列时跳过这些账号；读 feed 时把预计算列表与这些大 V 的{{近期帖子}}合并。
why: 三个环节缺一不可：flag 标在关注关系上、worker 侧忽略、读侧补拉合并，让扇出策略精确到账号粒度。
why_en: All three parts are required together, the flag on the follow relationship, the worker skipping it, and the read-side merge, giving fan-out strategy per-account precision.

q: 把『大 V 发帖如何扇出』的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the celebrity-post fan-out decision chain in the right order.
steps: 升级：给高粉账号打 flag 跳过预计算，读时再合并其近期帖子
需求：大 V 发帖要写入百万级粉丝的 feed，但系统容忍 <1 分钟延迟
缓解：读侧合并增加的计算量，用粉丝数阈值调节预计算的范围
选型：发帖消息进 SQS，由异步 worker 车队执行写扇出
代价：消息工作量方差巨大，9000 万粉丝的账号写扇出仍不可行
why: 完整链条：容忍延迟的需求 → 队列+异步 worker → 头部账号仍爆炸 → 打 flag 混合扇出 → 用阈值调节读写平衡。
why_en: The chain runs from a delay-tolerant requirement, to a queue of async workers, to top accounts still exploding, to hybrid flagging with a tunable threshold.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有高粉账号，统一 fan-out on write 更简单，不需要引入 flag 和读时合并。
tradeoff: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管消息队列服务，提供 at-least-once 投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS is AWS's managed message queue that guarantees at-least-once delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发帖时把 postId 写进粉丝 feed，读路径因此更便宜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on write writes the postId into follower feeds at post time, making reads cheaper.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刷 feed 时现场拉取并合并关注对象的帖子，写路径因此更便宜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read pulls and merges followed accounts' posts when the feed is read, making writes cheaper.

scenario: 系统里同时评估了发帖时预计算 feed、和刷 feed 时现查现拼这两种扇出策略。
scenario_en: The system evaluates both precomputing feeds at write time and assembling feeds on demand at read time.
q: fan-out on write 与 fan-out on read 在『代价发生在什么时候』上的区别是？
q_en: How do fan-out on write and fan-out on read differ in when the cost is paid?
options: on write：读时干活；on read：写时干活
两者的代价完全相同
on write 写贵读省；on read 写省读贵
两者都把代价推给后台批处理
options_en: On write: the work happens at read time; on read: the work happens at write time.
The two have exactly the same cost profile.
On write: a post fills every follower's feed upfront, so reads are cheap and writes are expensive; on read: the feed is assembled on the fly, so writes are cheap and reads are expensive.
Both push their cost onto a background batch job.
optionMeanings: 把两种模式的代价时机说反了。
忽视两者本质上是对称但相反的取舍。
按『谁贵谁便宜』精确刻画两种模式。
两者都不依赖后台批处理，是实时路径的取舍。
optionMeanings_en: Swaps which mode incurs cost at which time.
Ignores that the two are symmetric but opposite tradeoffs.
Precisely characterizes which side is cheap and which is expensive for each mode.
Neither mode relies on a background batch job; it's a real-time path tradeoff.
why: 预计算把成本搬到写路径（粉丝多则写爆炸），现查把成本留在读路径（关注多则读爆炸）；谁便宜取决于读写比例。
why_en: Precomputing moves cost onto the write path since more followers means bigger writes, while on-demand reads keep cost on the read path instead.
tradeoff: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read

scenario: 非功能需求写明：系统容忍最多 1 分钟的帖子陈旧。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirement says the system tolerates at most one minute of post staleness.
q: 写扇出必须在多长时间内完成？这个预算从哪来？
q_en: How quickly must write fan-out finish, and where does that budget come from?
options: 1 秒内，来自用户体验直觉
约 1 分钟，来自陈旧上限要求
1 小时内，批处理惯例
没有明确时限
options_en: Within 1 second, based on a UX intuition.
About 1 minute, taken directly from the non-functional requirement's staleness ceiling.
Within 1 hour, following batch-processing convention.
There is no defined deadline.
why: 非功能需求写明容忍 <1 分钟陈旧，这就是异步扇出的全部时间预算，需求里的数字最终都会变成设计约束。
why_en: The non-functional requirement caps staleness at under a minute, and that number becomes the entire time budget for async fan-out.

q: 帖子的读取生命周期通常是什么样的？
q_en: What does a post's read lifecycle usually look like?
options: 多数帖子几天转冷；爆款头几小时爆读
所有帖子的读量均匀分布
越老的帖子读得越多
读取完全随机，无规律可循
options_en: Most posts go nearly unread after a few days, while a high-follower account's post gets an explosive burst of reads in its first few hours.
Read volume is spread evenly across all posts.
Older posts get read more than newer ones.
Reads are completely random with no discernible pattern.
optionMeanings: 读取高度偏斜、集中在近期和爆款上的真实模式。
假设没有热点、没有时间衰减的理想化模式。
与真实使用行为相反的说法。
否认任何可利用的读取规律。
optionMeanings_en: The real pattern: reads skew heavily toward recent and viral content.
An idealized pattern assuming no hotspots and no time decay.
The opposite of real usage behavior.
Denies any exploitable pattern in reads at all.
why: 读取高度偏斜且集中在近期：绝大多数帖子热几天，爆款帖子头几小时读量巨大，这决定了缓存收益极高。
why_en: Reads skew heavily toward recent content, since most posts stay hot for only days while a viral post bursts in its first hours.

scenario: 某条爆款帖子 Post1 独占了分区的大量读请求，其余帖子所在分区几乎没有流量。
scenario_en: A viral post, Post1, takes a large share of reads on one partition while partitions for other posts are nearly idle.
q: DynamoDB 能扩到极高吞吐的关键前提是什么？违反了会怎样？
q_en: What condition lets DynamoDB scale to very high throughput, and what happens when it is violated?
options: 用最新代的存储实例
开启自动备份
把预置吞吐买得足够高
负载必须均匀，否则热分区成瓶颈
options_en: Using the newest generation of storage hardware.
Turning on automatic backups.
Provisioning enough throughput up front.
Load must be spread evenly across the keyspace; if one post hogs the requests while others get none, a hot partition becomes the bottleneck.
optionMeanings: 与吞吐扩展的物理前提无关的选项。
备份是可靠性手段，不是吞吐扩展的前提。
预置再高，负载不均时单分区仍会被打爆。
揭示 DynamoDB『可无限扩展』的隐藏前提。
optionMeanings_en: Unrelated to the physical precondition for throughput scaling.
Backups are a durability feature, not a throughput-scaling precondition.
No matter how high provisioned throughput is, an uneven load still overwhelms one partition.
Reveals the hidden precondition behind DynamoDB's 'infinite scaling' claim.
why: 『可无限扩展』的 KV store 都有同一行小字：负载要均匀。爆款帖子恰恰制造极端不均，这是热分区问题的根源。
why_en: Every 'infinitely scalable' key-value store hides the same fine print, load must stay even, and a viral post creates exactly the kind of imbalance that breaks it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载集中在少数几个分区、其余分区却很空闲的不均衡状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot partition is a shard that receives far more load than the others, breaking even distribution.

q: 帖子数据有一个对缓存非常友好的性质，是什么？
q_en: What property of post data makes it very cache-friendly?
options: 帖子都很小，内存随便放
帖子没有多媒体内容
创建远多于编辑，长 TTL 安全
用户不在乎帖子内容是否最新
options_en: Posts are all tiny, so memory is never a concern.
Posts never contain multimedia content.
Posts are almost only ever created, rarely edited, so the cache can safely use a long TTL.
Users don't care whether post content is up to date.
optionMeanings: 对帖子大小的过度简化假设。
对帖子内容形态的错误假设。
『创建远多于编辑』这一决定性性质。
把缓存友好性错误归因到用户态度。
optionMeanings_en: An oversimplified assumption about post size.
A wrong assumption about post content types.
The decisive property: creation vastly outnumbers edits.
Wrongly attributes cache-friendliness to user attitude.
why: 『创建远多于编辑』意味着缓存内容几乎不会过时：长 TTL 安全，只需在罕见编辑发生时精确失效。
why_en: Since posts are almost only created and rarely edited, cached content almost never goes stale, making a long TTL safe with precise invalidation only on the rare edit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的过期时间，过期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the expiration time after which a cached entry must be refreshed.

scenario: 爆款帖子的读流量正在打爆 Post 表的单个分区；帖子创建后极少被修改。
scenario_en: A viral post is overwhelming one Post-table partition, and posts are rarely modified after creation.
q: 『good』级别的解法是？
q_en: What is the 'good' solution for hot post reads?
options: 加分布式缓存：Redis 长 TTL + LRU
把 DynamoDB 预置吞吐调高十倍
把帖子搬到 S3
限制单条帖子的阅读次数
options_en: Insert a distributed cache between readers and the Post table: shard by postId on a Redis cluster, with a long TTL and LRU eviction.
Provision DynamoDB throughput ten times higher.
Move posts into S3.
Cap how many times a single post can be read.
optionMeanings: 在数据库前加一层缓存吸收读流量。
花更多钱硬扛，不解决负载不均本身。
对象存储不适合这种低延迟点查场景。
限制阅读次数直接违背产品目标。
optionMeanings_en: Adds a cache layer in front of the database to absorb read traffic.
Throws more money at it without fixing the underlying imbalance.
Object storage isn't built for this kind of low-latency point lookup.
Capping reads directly contradicts the product's goal.
why: 只要缓存装得下大多数近期帖子，绝大部分读就不再落库；长 TTL 可行是因为帖子极少编辑，LRU 自动腾出冷帖空间。
why_en: As long as the cache holds most recent posts, most reads never hit the database, and a long TTL is safe because posts are rarely edited while LRU frees space for cold posts.
whenOtherWins: 若读负载本来均匀、量级不大，DynamoDB 直查就够，缓存只是多余的复杂度。
tradeoff: 缓存吸收热点读 vs 直查数据库的简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用淘汰策略，优先清掉最久没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU evicts the entry that has gone the longest without being accessed.

q: Post 缓存在什么时机做失效（invalidate）？
q_en: When should the Post cache be invalidated?
options: 每次有新帖创建时全量失效
编辑时按 postId 精确失效
每小时定时清空
永不失效，全靠 TTL
options_en: Flush the entire cache every time a new post is created.
Precisely invalidate by postId only when a post is edited; a new post needs no invalidation.
Clear the whole cache on a fixed hourly schedule.
Never invalidate at all, relying purely on TTL.
optionMeanings: 把创建事件误当成需要失效的情况。
只在编辑时精确删除对应 key。
与实际的编辑事件无关的定时策略。
完全放弃主动失效手段。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly treats post creation as something needing invalidation.
Deletes only the matching key, and only on an edit event.
A time-based policy unrelated to actual edit events.
Gives up active invalidation entirely.
why: 新帖不存在缓存里，谈不上失效；只有编辑会让缓存变陈旧，只需在编辑时删掉对应 postId 的条目。
why_en: A new post was never cached, so there's nothing to invalidate, and only an edit makes the cache stale, so deleting that one postId is enough.

scenario: 分布式帖子缓存由 N 台主机组成，每台主机有 M 内存。
scenario_en: The distributed post cache has N hosts, and each host has M memory.
q: 这个集群总容量怎么估算，说明了什么？
q_en: How do we estimate total cache-cluster capacity, and what does it imply?
options: 等于单台主机的内存 M
等于数据库的总大小
无法估算，只能靠压测
约 N×M，大多数读会命中缓存
options_en: Equal to a single host's memory M.
Equal to the database's total size.
Impossible to estimate, only load testing can tell.
Roughly N times M; as long as it holds most recent posts, most reads hit the cache.
why: 分片式缓存容量随节点数线性增长（N×M）；结合读集中在近期帖子的模式，不大的集群就能挡住大部分读流量。
why_en: A sharded cache's capacity scales linearly with node count, roughly N times M, and since reads concentrate on recent posts, even a modest cluster absorbs most read traffic.

q: 按 postId 分片的帖子缓存，还残留什么问题？
q_en: What problem remains with a postId-sharded post cache?
options: 热 key 原样搬进缓存单点
缓存的成本高于数据库
TTL 无法与 LRU 共存
Redis 不支持按 key 分片
options_en: The hot-key problem gets copied straight into the cache: the shard holding a viral post gets crushed while other nodes sit underused.
The cache costs more than the database.
TTL and LRU can't coexist.
Redis doesn't support sharding by key.
optionMeanings: 每个 key 固定只落在一台缓存节点上。
对缓存与数据库相对成本的无关说法。
对 Redis 淘汰机制的错误认知。
对 Redis 分片能力的错误认知。
optionMeanings_en: In a sharded cache, each post lives on exactly one node.
An unrelated claim about the relative cost of cache versus database.
A wrong belief about Redis's eviction mechanics.
A wrong belief about Redis's sharding capability.
why: 分片缓存里每个帖子只住一个节点，爆款的全部流量仍砸向单点，很多主机反而利用率低下。
why_en: In a sharded cache each post lives on exactly one node, so a viral post's entire traffic still slams a single node while the rest sit underused.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问的单个缓存 key，容易压垮承载它的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single key that receives disproportionately heavy traffic and can overload the node holding it.

scenario: 单个爆款帖子的读流量超过任何一台缓存节点的能力上限，按 postId 分片没有出路。
scenario_en: A single viral post has more read traffic than any one cache node can serve, so postId-based sharding has no path forward.
q: 『great』级别的缓存架构是？
q_en: What is the 'great' cache architecture?
options: 在分片缓存前面再加一层缓存
复制式：任何实例都能服务任意帖子
给热分片换更大的机器
把爆款帖子内联进每个用户的 feed 条目
options_en: Add yet another cache layer in front of the sharded cache.
Switch to a replicated cache: every instance can serve any post, and the load balancer spreads requests across all N instances.
Upgrade the hot shard's node to a bigger machine.
Inline the viral post directly into every user's feed entry.
optionMeanings: 叠加一层缓存并不改变单点热 key 的本质问题。
每个实例持有相同数据，任何实例都能应答。
垂直扩容单个节点，仍有物理上限。
让存储随粉丝数线性膨胀的错误方向。
optionMeanings_en: Stacking another cache layer doesn't fix the underlying single-node hot-key issue.
Every instance holds the same data, so any instance can answer.
Vertically scaling one node still hits a physical ceiling.
The wrong direction, letting storage balloon with follower count.
why: 从『每个帖子只住一个节点』改成『每个实例都可服务任何帖子』，热 key 吞吐直接乘 N，且无需任何协调。
why_en: Switching from 'each post lives on one node' to 'every instance can serve any post' multiplies hot-key throughput by N with zero coordination needed.
whenOtherWins: 没有极端热 key、但数据量大时，分片缓存能容纳多得多的不同帖子，总命中率更高。
tradeoff: 复制式的热 key 吞吐 vs 分片式的总容量

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个缓存实例都保存相同的完整数据副本，任何实例都能应答任意 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replicated cache keeps a full copy on every instance so any instance can answer any key.

q: 复制式缓存的代价是什么？
q_en: What is the cost of a replicated cache?
options: 写扇出量变大
读延迟显著上升
初期 miss 变多，最多 N 次回源
无法再设置 TTL
options_en: Write fan-out volume goes up.
Read latency rises significantly.
More initial misses: the same viral post may be fetched from the origin once per instance, N times instead of once.
TTL can no longer be set.
optionMeanings: 复制式缓存与写路径的扇出机制无关。
对读延迟的错误归因。
每个实例独立冷启动，各自回源一次。
对 TTL 支持的错误认知。
optionMeanings_en: A replicated cache is unrelated to the write-path fan-out mechanism.
A wrong attribution of read latency.
Each instance starts cold independently and fetches from origin once.
A wrong belief about TTL support.
why: 每个实例独立回源，冷启动时同一帖子最多 N 次 miss；拿 N 次回源换 N 倍热 key 吞吐是划算的交换。
why_en: Each instance fetches from the origin independently, so a cold start can cost up to N misses for the same post, a fair trade for N times the hot-key throughput.

q: 分片缓存与复制缓存，在『单个热 key 的吞吐上限』维度上的区别是？
q_en: How do sharded and replicated caches differ on single-hot-key throughput?
options: 分片卡单点；复制乘 N 倍
两者的热 key 吞吐相同
复制式的热 key 吞吐更低
取决于 TTL 设多长
options_en: Sharded: hot-key throughput is roughly one node's limit; replicated: roughly N times one node's limit, with no coordination needed.
The two have identical hot-key throughput.
A replicated cache actually has lower hot-key throughput.
It depends entirely on how long the TTL is set.
optionMeanings: 按候选各自的热 key 吞吐上限精确对比。
忽视了两种架构在这一维度上的本质差异。
把两者的能力关系说反了。
TTL 与热 key 吞吐上限是两个不同的维度。
optionMeanings_en: Precisely contrasts each candidate's hot-key throughput ceiling.
Ignores the fundamental difference between the two on this dimension.
Reverses which one actually has higher capacity.
TTL and hot-key throughput ceiling are two unrelated dimensions.
why: 这是空间换吞吐：分片容量大但热 key 卡单点；复制容量小但热 key 吞吐乘 N。
why_en: This is capacity traded for throughput: sharding caps a hot key at one node, while replication multiplies hot-key throughput by N.
tradeoff: 热 key 吞吐 vs 总缓存容量

scenario: 用 Redis 缓存帖子：key 按 postId；帖子极少编辑所以 TTL 可以设 1 天；一旦编辑要立刻失效。
scenario_en: Use Redis to cache posts by postId. Posts are rarely edited, so TTL can be one day, but edits must invalidate immediately.
q: 哪组命令符合这套策略？
q_en: Which Redis command sequence matches this caching strategy?
options: SET post:p123 ... EX 60，一分钟就过期
SET post:p123 ...（不带 TTL），并在创建新帖时 DEL
SET post:p123 ... EX 86400，编辑帖子时 DEL post:p123
只用 GET post:p123，miss 时不做任何回填
options_en: SET post:p123 ... EX 60, expiring after one minute.
SET post:p123 ... with no TTL, and DEL it whenever a new post is created.
SET post:p123 ... EX 86400, and DEL post:p123 whenever the post is edited.
Only GET post:p123, doing no backfill at all on a miss.
optionMeanings: TTL 远短于『极少编辑』的实际变化频率。
在错误的时机（创建）做失效，且没有过期兜底。
长 TTL 匹配低变化率，编辑时精确失效。
只读不写，缓存永远不会被填充。
optionMeanings_en: A TTL far shorter than how rarely posts actually change.
Invalidates at the wrong moment (creation) and has no expiry as a backstop.
A long TTL matching low change frequency, with precise invalidation on edit.
Read-only with no write path, so the cache never gets populated.
codeSample:
# fill on miss, long TTL (1 day)
SET post:p123 '{"content":"..."}' EX 86400

# read path
GET post:p123

# post edited: precise invalidation
DEL post:p123
why: 长 TTL（EX 86400）匹配『帖子几乎不变』的事实，编辑时 DEL 精确失效；TTL 60 秒会造成大量无谓 miss。
why_en: A long TTL of EX 86400 matches how rarely posts change, while DEL on edit gives precise invalidation, unlike a 60-second TTL that would cause needless misses.
whenOtherWins: 若帖子频繁编辑且必须立刻可见，就该缩短 TTL 或改成写时同步更新缓存。
tradeoff: 长 TTL+精确失效 vs 短 TTL 的保守新鲜度

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的过期时间，过期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the expiration time after which a cached entry must be refreshed.

q: 把『爆款帖子读扇出』的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the viral-post read fan-out decision chain in the right order.
steps: 代价：分片缓存自身也有热 key——爆款所在的分片照样被打爆
缓解：接受最多 N 次回源和更小的有效容量，DynamoDB 能吸收这点波动
需求：爆款帖子头几小时读量巨大，而 DynamoDB 只有负载均匀才能高吞吐
升级：换成复制式缓存+负载均衡，任何实例都能服务任何帖子
选型：在 Post 表前加分布式缓存，长 TTL + LRU
why: 链条完整走一遍：热读需求 → 加缓存 → 缓存自己也热 → 复制式缓存摊平 → 接受少量回源。
why_en: The chain runs from a hot-read requirement, to adding a cache, to the cache itself getting hot, to replication spreading the load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问的单个缓存 key，容易压垮承载它的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single key that receives disproportionately heavy traffic and can overload the node holding it.

q: 复制式缓存能装下的『不同帖子总数』比分片式少，为什么可以接受？
q_en: Why is it acceptable that a replicated cache holds fewer distinct posts than a sharded cache?
options: 因为帖子会自动压缩
因为可以无限加内存
因为旧帖子根本没人读，不缓存也没影响
DynamoDB 兜得住这点额外 miss
options_en: Because posts get automatically compressed.
Because memory can be added without limit.
Because nobody reads old posts anyway, so not caching them has no impact.
Because the DynamoDB backend can absorb some read-throughput variability, and the small extra misses fall well within that.
optionMeanings: 对缓存机制的错误假设。
忽视了成本随内存线性增长的现实。
过度绝对化『旧帖子没人读』这个说法。
把后端的吞吐余量当作接受更小有效容量的理由。
optionMeanings_en: A wrong assumption about how caching works.
Ignores that cost still scales linearly with memory added.
Overstates 'nobody reads old posts' as an absolute.
Treats the backend's throughput headroom as the reason to accept smaller effective capacity.
why: 复制牺牲了有效容量，换来热 key 吞吐；落库的 miss 变多一点没关系，DynamoDB 不是不能读，只是不能被单点打爆。
why_en: Replication trades away effective capacity for hot-key throughput, and the extra misses falling through to DynamoDB are easily absorbed.

q: 面试官禁止使用 Elasticsearch / Postgres 全文索引后，设计上你被迫要亲手做的核心工作是？
q_en: When Elasticsearch and Postgres full-text search are off limits, what core work must you build yourself?
options: 亲手设计数据布局与倒排索引
改用 NoSQL 自带的搜索功能
放弃关键词搜索改做前缀匹配
把过滤逻辑全放到客户端本地
why: 没有现成全文索引可依赖，你必须自己决定数据如何布局、如何构建倒排索引、如何扩展——这正是这类题要考的底层功。
why_en: With no off-the-shelf full-text index available, you must design the data layout, build the inverted index, and scale it yourself.
options_en: Hand-build the data layout and an inverted index yourself.
Rely on a NoSQL database's built-in search.
Drop keyword search and only do prefix matching.
Push all filtering to the client side.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开箱即用的分布式搜索引擎，内部本身就用倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an off-the-shelf search engine built on inverted indexes.

q: 为 FB 帖子搜索定义需求时，哪些属于核心功能需求？（多选）
q_en: When defining requirements for FB Post Search, which are core functional requirements?
options: 用户能创建和点赞帖子
用户能按关键词搜索帖子
搜索结果能按时间或点赞数排序
搜索结果按用户兴趣做个性化排序
why: 核心需求只有三条：创建/点赞、关键词搜索、按时间或赞数排序；个性化被明确划出范围，这个决定让后面的缓存设计大为简化。
why_en: The core requirements are creating and liking posts, keyword search, and sorting by recency or like count, while personalization is explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Users can create and like posts.
Users can search posts by keyword.
Results can be sorted by recency or like count.
Results are personalized to each user's interests.

q: FB 帖子搜索里，下列哪些被划为范围外（out of scope）？（多选）
q_en: In FB Post Search, which items are out of scope?
options: 模糊匹配（搜 bird 命中 ostrich）
隐私规则与过滤
新帖 1 分钟内可被搜索
搜索页对新帖做实时推送更新
why: 模糊匹配、个性化、隐私、复杂相关性排序、多媒体、实时更新都在范围外；「新帖 1 分钟内可搜」恰恰是核心非功能需求，不是范围外。
why_en: Fuzzy matching, privacy filters, and realtime result updates are out of scope, whereas making new posts searchable within a minute is a core requirement.
options_en: Fuzzy matching (searching bird also matches ostrich).
Privacy rules and filtering.
New posts searchable within one minute.
Realtime push updates to the search page.

scenario: 明确需求阶段，你在考虑是否把「搜索结果个性化」留在范围内，这个决定将影响后续架构的复杂度。
scenario_en: During requirements clarification, you are deciding whether personalized search results are in scope, which will drive downstream architecture complexity.
q: 把个性化划出范围，对系统设计最大的红利是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest system-design benefit of making personalization out of scope?
options: 数据库可以少建一个索引
不再需要 API 网关
相同查询人人同结果，查询级缓存极其有效
写入路径可以完全省掉
why: 没有个性化意味着搜索结果只取决于查询本身、人人相同，结果可以进缓存和 CDN 被海量复用；所以值得当面问「个性化是不是硬需求」。
why_en: Dropping personalization means identical queries return identical results for everyone, which makes query-level caching and CDN reuse dramatically more effective.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品硬性要求千人千面的搜索结果，查询级缓存基本失效，只能退到缓存更底层的索引数据、在线上做个性化重排。
options_en: The database needs one fewer index.
You no longer need an API gateway.
Identical queries return identical results, so query-level caching becomes extremely effective.
The write path can be dropped entirely.
tradeoff: 无个性化换来缓存高复用 vs 千人千面的相关性

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径最前端的入口，负责鉴权、限流后转发给后端服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway authenticates and rate-limits requests before forwarding them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

scenario: FB Post Search 面试先给定两个目标：中位搜索延迟 <500ms，新帖 <1分钟可搜。这些是 SLO/SLA 目标，不是由帖子量公式算出的结果。
scenario_en: In the FB Post Search interview, median search latency under 500 ms and new posts searchable within one minute are given SLO/SLA targets, not capacity-derived numbers.
q: 这些 NFR 数字分别约束哪条设计路径？
q_en: Which design paths do these NFR numbers constrain?
text: 500ms 约束{{查询路径}}，推动内存索引、缓存和避免请求时全量排序；1分钟约束{{新帖可见性}}，反推索引流水线延迟和缓存 TTL 上限。
why: 这两个数不是算出来的容量结果，而是面试中先约定的用户体验目标。真正的计算发生在后面：用它们倒推索引、缓存、冷热分层和写入流水线。
why_en: The five-hundred-millisecond and one-minute numbers are service targets, not derived constants, and they constrain the query path and freshness path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟、吞吐、可用性这类衡量系统「好不好」的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements cover latency, throughput, and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队希望系统达到的内部目标，如中位搜索 <500ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service level objective is an internal target for system behavior, such as median search latency under five hundred milliseconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议：对外承诺的服务指标，如新帖 1 分钟内可搜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service level agreement is a promised service level, such as new posts being searchable within a minute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存存活时间。超过 TTL 后缓存条目过期，系统必须重新取或重算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time to live is how long a cache entry may live before it expires and must be refreshed.

q: 「老帖、冷门帖也要可搜索，但允许更慢」这条需求在为哪个设计决策埋伏笔？
q_en: Which later design decision is hinted by the requirement that old and unpopular posts are searchable but slower?
options: 放弃高可用目标
冷热分层：热数据进内存、冷数据下沉廉价存储
换一台更大的单机数据库
把所有索引都搬进 CDN
why: 大数据量系统天然有热/冷数据之分：热数据高频访问要内存级速度，冷数据低频访问可放磁盘、远端库甚至磁带；这条 NFR 正是后面「冷索引下沉 S3」的伏笔。
why_en: Allowing old or unpopular posts to be slower foreshadows a hot-cold split where hot data lives in memory and cold data moves to cheaper, slower storage.
options_en: Abandon the high-availability goal.
A hot-cold split: hot data in memory, cold data on cheaper storage.
Switch to a single bigger database machine.
Move all indexes into the CDN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

q: 补全写入侧的规模估算（10 亿用户，每天按约 10 万秒取整）：
q_en: Fill in the write-side scale estimate for 1B users and roughly 100K seconds per day.
text: 每人每天 1 帖 → 约 {{10k}} posts/秒；每人每天 10 个赞 → 约 {{100k}} likes/秒；点赞写入量是发帖的 {{10}} 倍。
why: 用 1B ÷ 100k 秒的快捷除法得出发帖 10k/s、点赞 100k/s；点赞比发帖多一个数量级，这个观察直接决定了后面必须重点优化点赞写入。
why_en: A billion users produce roughly ten thousand posts and one hundred thousand likes per second, so likes outnumber post creations ten to one.
scenario: 规模估算：10 亿用户，每天约 10 万秒，估算写入侧的量级。
scenario_en: Estimate write-side order of magnitude from 1B users and about 100K seconds per day.

q: 由这个读规模，读路径最该具备的能力是？
q_en: Given this read scale, what capability does the read path need most?
options: 读会突发到 10 倍，重复查询要能被缓存/CDN 吸收
读量极小，单台机器就足以承载全部流量
读远大于写，就该牺牲写路径来保读
读流量根本无法估算，直接跳过这步
why: 搜索读约 10k/s 但可能突发 10 倍；因为无个性化、查询重复度高，读路径靠结果缓存和 CDN 吸收峰值，而不是一味加索引机器。
why_en: Search reads run about ten thousand per second but can spike tenfold, so the read path leans on result caching and a CDN to absorb bursts.
scenario: 10 亿用户、每人每天约 1 次搜索，读流量还可能突发到平时的 10 倍以上。
scenario_en: With 1B users and about one search per user per day, read traffic can still spike over 10x.
options_en: Reads can spike 10x, so repeated queries must be absorbable by a cache/CDN.
Read volume is tiny; a single machine can carry all traffic.
Reads dominate writes, so sacrifice the write path to protect reads.
Read traffic can't be estimated, so skip this step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

q: 对比估算结果（写约 110k/s vs 搜索 10k/s），关于系统性质最重要的结论是？
q_en: Comparing about 110K writes/s with 10K searches/s, what is the key system takeaway?
options: 系统读多写少，应重点优化读路径
系统写多读少——别被「搜索」二字骗成读为主
读写均衡，无需特别优化
数据量不大，单机即可承载
why: 这题最容易犯的错是被「搜索系统」带偏、假设读是大头；估算揭示写入（尤其点赞）远超读，写路径才是主要瓶颈。
why_en: The estimates reveal a write-heavy system, overturning the common assumption that a search problem must be read-heavy.
options_en: The system is read-heavy; optimize the read path.
The system is write-heavy—don't let the word 'search' fool you into assuming reads dominate.
Reads and writes are balanced; no special optimization.
The data is small; one machine suffices.

q: 这个存储量级对搜索系统提出的设计要求是？
q_en: What does this storage scale force the search system to do?
options: 内存放不下 3.6PB，索引要设上限、冷数据下沉便宜存储
数据量不大，一台大内存机器即可
把全部帖子原文都塞进 Redis 加速
存储不是问题，无需特别处理
why: 3.6 万亿帖 × 1kb ≈ 3.6PB，全量放内存/单机不可行；这直接催生后面给索引设上限、把冷门关键词下沉 blob 存储的设计。
why_en: Ten years of a billion posts a day is about 3.6 petabytes, far too much to keep in memory, which forces index caps and cold blob storage.
scenario: FB 运营 10 年、每天约 10 亿帖、每帖元数据约 1kb，原始存储估算约 3.6 PB。
scenario_en: After 10 years at roughly 1B posts per day and 1 KB metadata per post, raw storage is about 3.6 PB.
options_en: 3.6 PB won't fit in memory, so indexes must be capped and cold data pushed to cheap storage.
The data is small; one big-memory machine is enough.
Stuff every post's full text into Redis for speed.
Storage isn't a concern; no special handling needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

q: FB 帖子搜索的核心实体（User/Post/Like）里，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about the core User/Post/Like entities in FB Post Search are correct?
options: User——发帖的主体
Post——被搜索的对象，有内容、作者，隐含点赞数
Like——我们主要关心它的计数而非每条记录
Comment——搜索的主要目标
why: 实体刻意简单：User、Post、Like 三个，且对 Like 只关心 count；实体简单就不必恋战，快速推进到 API 和设计。
why_en: The entities are just User, Post, and Like, and for likes we mostly care about the count rather than individual records.
options_en: User — the author who creates posts.
Post — the searchable object with content, author, and an implicit like count.
Like — we mostly care about its count, not each record.
Comment — the primary search target.

q: FB 帖子搜索的 API 应该是什么形状？
q_en: What shape should the FB Post Search API have?
options: 单一搜索端点，写入直连数据库
全部收敛为一个 GraphQL 端点
搜索复用写入端点
写路径（发帖/点赞）+ 查询路径（搜索）两条腿
why: API 分两条腿：写入端点接帖子与点赞、搜索端点服务查询；并向面试官说明真实系统中写入多半来自事件总线，独立端点只是为了讲解清晰。
why_en: The system exposes a write path for posts and likes plus a search query path, and in production the writes would likely arrive via an event stream like Kafka.
options_en: A single search endpoint, with writes going straight to the database.
Everything collapsed into one GraphQL endpoint.
Search reuses the write endpoint.
A write path (create post / like) plus a query path (search) — two legs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志/流平台，可分区并行、缓冲突发、持久化事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log that partitions load and buffers event bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让客户端按需声明字段的单端点查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a single-endpoint query language where clients request exact fields.

q: 设计只聚焦「搜索」时，对上游 Post Service / Like Service 的正确处理方式是？
q_en: If the design focuses only on search, how should you treat upstream Post and Like services?
options: 假设它们已存在且正常工作，只从它们接收事件
必须从零开始重新设计这两个服务
把它们合并进搜索服务统一实现
忽略它们，让客户端直连索引

q_en: Complete this common blind spot in real-time system design candidates.
text: 引入 WebSocket 通常是为了它的{{双向}}通信能力；很多候选人只画「左到右」的箭头（客户端如何请求服务），却漏掉图上的{{右到左}}箭头——内部服务如何把消息推回{{客户端}}。这就是 real-time updates 模式。

q: 把客户端连接到正确 Document Service 服务器的流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the flow for connecting a client to the correct Document Service server in order.
steps: HTTP 升级为 WebSocket；服务器在 docId → socket 映射中登记该连接
客户端带着 docId 向任意一台文档服务器发起 HTTP 连接（round robin 均可）
从 Document Operations DB 加载该文档的既有操作（若尚未加载），准备处理编辑
该服务器查哈希环：若该 docId 不归自己管，返回 redirect 指向正确服务器
why: 先随便连一台 → 用环配置重定向到正确服务器 → 升级成 WebSocket 并登记 → 加载操作。客户端最终直连正确服务器，无需中间代理。
why_en: The client hits any server, gets redirected by the hash ring lookup to the right one, upgrades to a websocket, and the server loads the stored operations to begin processing.

why_en: The beauty of consistent hashing is that adding or removing a server redistributes only a small portion of the connections instead of nearly all of them.
scenario: Document Service 集群要新增或下线一台服务器，文档到服务器的映射由一致性哈希环决定。

No connections need to migrate at all

q: Google News 首版功能范围包括哪些？（多选）

scenario: 新闻平台在分区或依赖抖动时需要做 CAP 取舍，用户更能接受看到稍旧新闻，而不是 feed 完全不可用。
scenario_en: During partitions or dependency hiccups, the news platform must make a CAP tradeoff: users would rather see slightly stale news than no feed at all.
q: 首要应该偏向 CAP 的哪一侧？
q_en: Which side of CAP should the first design favor?
options: 强一致优先，宁可返回错误也不能旧
可用性优先，允许短时间旧内容
事务隔离优先，所有 feed 请求串行化
完全实时优先，每次都绕过缓存查源
options_en: Favor strong consistency, even if that means returning an error instead of stale data.
Favor availability, accepting slightly stale content for a short time.
Favor transaction isolation, serializing every feed request.
Favor full real-time reads, bypassing the cache on every request.
why: 新闻 feed 不是金融扣款，短暂旧内容比空白页更可接受，因此偏向可用性。
why_en: A news feed should favor availability over strict consistency because slightly stale content beats showing nothing at all.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统处理账户余额、库存扣减或合规审计，强一致会比可用性更重要。
tradeoff: 可用性优先 vs 强一致优先
optionMeanings: 宁可拒绝请求也不给旧数据的策略。
接受短暂陈旧但始终有响应的策略。

每次都跳过缓存直接查源头数据。

optionDirectness: 本场景不适合，因为新闻场景更怕空白页而非旧内容。
在本场景适合，因为匹配可用性优先的要求。

本场景不适合，因为实时性不是本题强调的目标。

scenario: 为新闻聚合器设计数据模型，用户可以匿名浏览，feed 按地区展示。

q: 把文章采集流水线按正确顺序排列：

why_en: The collection job discovers publishers, fetches article metadata, processes media, then stores structured data with the object-storage URL.

Dedup --> DB[(Article DB)]
DB --> Cache[Feed cache]

q: 在新闻不断插入 feed 顶部时，OFFSET/LIMIT 分页最典型的问题是什么？

The client is unable to pass a limit parameter.
The database cannot sort results by publish time.
Pagination makes caching impossible.

本题不选，因为limit 参数本就能正常传递。

why_en: A timestamp cursor anchors to a fixed boundary, so newly inserted articles never shift the older results.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据集很小且几乎不变，offset 分页更简单也够用。
tradeoff: 稳定边界的 cursor 分页 vs 实现更简单的 offset 分页

q: 补全 Google News 的关键非功能目标：
q_en: Fill in the key nonfunctional targets for Google News:
