q: Web Crawler 常用的默认礼貌限速大致是多少？
options: 全系统每秒 1 个请求
每个域名每秒 1 个请求
每个域名每秒 1000 个请求
每个 Worker 每天 1 个请求
why: 礼貌限速按域名维度控制，常见默认是每个域名约 1 rps。全系统仍可通过同时抓取大量不同域名取得高吞吐。
why_en: The crawler limits each domain to about one request per second while achieving aggregate throughput across many domains.
options_en: About one request per second, system-wide.
About one request per second, per domain.
About one thousand requests per second, per domain.
About one request per day, per worker.
scenario: 多个爬虫实例同时抓取同一批域名，需要一个默认的、不必特别设计就能遵守的礼貌限速基线。
q_en: What is a common default polite crawl rate for a web crawler?
scenario_en: Multiple crawler instances fetch from the same set of domains and need a default polite rate limit that is easy to enforce.

scenario: 多个爬虫实例要共同遵守每个域名每秒最多 1 个请求的规则，不能只靠单机内存计数。
q: 更合适的限流实现是？
options: 把所有 URL 按字母排序
只依赖 S3 的吞吐限制
Redis 等中心化存储里的按域名滑动窗口计数
每个 Worker 自己 sleep 1 秒
why: 分布式 Worker 需要共享限流状态，Redis 滑动窗口能按域名统计当前窗口请求数。单机 sleep 看不到其他 Worker 的请求。
why_en: A shared Redis sliding window lets distributed crawlers enforce per-domain request limits consistently.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单实例爬虫，本地令牌桶就足够；如果域名量非常大，还要考虑限流 key 的分片和过期策略。
diagram:
flowchart TD
URL[URL] --> Domain[Extract domain]
Domain --> Token[Domain token bucket]
Token -->|allowed| Fetch[Fetch now]
Token -->|limited| Delay[Delay queue]
tradeoff: 共享的分布式限流状态 vs 单机本地计时
options_en: Sort all URLs alphabetically.
Rely only on S3's throughput limits.
A centralized per-domain sliding-window counter, such as in Redis.
Have each worker just sleep for one second.
q_en: What rate-limiting implementation fits this distributed crawler?
scenario_en: Multiple crawler instances must jointly enforce at most one request per second per domain, so a single worker's memory counter is not enough.

q: 限流窗口重置时多个 Worker 同时重试，最容易产生什么问题？
options: 所有 URL 都会被自动去重
DNS 缓存会立刻全部命中
S3 里的对象会被自动删除
同步重试会让大家抢同一个域名配额，形成反复失败
why: 如果 Worker 都在同一时刻醒来，它们会再次拥挤到同一个域名窗口。加随机 jitter 能把重试打散，减少同步冲突。
why_en: Jitter spreads retry attempts over time so workers do not stampede the same per-domain rate-limit window.
options_en: All URLs get automatically deduplicated.
DNS caches suddenly hit one hundred percent.
Objects in S3 get automatically deleted.
Synchronized retries collide on the same domain quota and keep failing together.
q_en: What problem happens when many workers retry at the same rate-limit window reset?

q: 这组 BOE 带宽推算得到的结论是什么？
options: 单机网络理论上限约 12,500 页/秒，但这只是理论峰值
单机实际就能稳定跑到约 12,500 页/秒
带宽和页面大小对估算机器数量没有意义
这个数字说明应该改成抓更小的页面
why: 200 Gbps 换算成约 12,500 页/秒只是纯网络理论上限；DNS、限流、重试等现实损耗会让实际吞吐明显更低。
why_en: The bandwidth math gives a theoretical per-machine ceiling of about twelve thousand five hundred pages per second, but real throughput will be far lower once you account for DNS, rate limits, and retries.
scenario: 网络优化型实例带宽约 200 Gbps，平均页面体量约 2MB，这决定了单机纯网络维度的理论抓取速度上限。
options_en: The theoretical per-machine ceiling is about 12,500 pages per second, but it is only a theoretical peak.
A single machine can actually sustain 12,500 pages per second in practice.
Bandwidth and page size are irrelevant to estimating fleet size.
This number implies you should switch to crawling smaller pages.
q_en: What conclusion does this back-of-the-envelope bandwidth estimate give?
scenario_en: A network-optimized instance has about 200 Gbps of bandwidth, and the average page transfer is about 2 MB, which sets the per-machine theoretical network ceiling.

q: 把这个 30% 折扣系数放进估算的目的是什么？
options: 把所需机器数直接提高到原来的 3 倍
把理论峰值折算成更贴近现实的吞吐，用来估算需要多少机器
证明可以完全忽略 DNS 和限流这些因素
说明只需要原计划 30% 的机器成本
why: 30% 利用率把纯网络峰值打折成贴近现实的吞吐（约 3,750 页/秒），这个折扣后的数字才用于估算机器数。
why_en: The thirty-percent utilization factor discounts the theoretical peak down to a realistic sustainable throughput that is actually used to size the fleet.
scenario: 同一套 BOE 假设进一步估计，因为 DNS、延迟、限流、重试等现实损耗，实际能有效利用的带宽大约只有 30%。
options_en: It directly triples the number of machines required.
It discounts the theoretical peak into a realistic sustained throughput used to size the fleet.
It proves DNS and rate limiting can be fully ignored.
It means the project only needs 30% of the original machine budget.
q_en: Why include a 30% utilization discount in the estimate?
scenario_en: Using the same back-of-the-envelope assumptions, real losses from DNS, latency, rate limits, and retries mean only about 30% of bandwidth is effectively usable.

q: 单机抓完 10B 页面耗时计算在设计讨论里起什么作用？
options: 说明页面大小对完成时间没有任何影响
证明应该直接放弃 5 天这个时间要求
算出单机约 31 天，需多机并行才压进 5 天预算
证明单机完全可以满足 5 天的时间要求
why: 单机耗时约 31 天远超 5 天预算，这个差距就是论证需要并行扩容到多台机器的依据。
why_en: The single-machine estimate of about thirty-one days is far beyond the five-day budget, which is exactly the gap that justifies scaling out to many machines.
scenario: 把 10B 页面除以约 3,750 页/秒的单机吞吐，得到单机独立完成全部抓取所需的时间。
options_en: It shows page size has no effect on completion time.
It proves the five-day requirement should be abandoned.
It shows a single machine needs about 31 days, proving parallel machines are required to fit the five-day budget.
It proves a single machine can already meet the five-day requirement.
q_en: What role does the single-machine time estimate play in the design discussion?
scenario_en: Divide 10 billion pages by the single-machine throughput of about 3,750 pages per second to estimate how long one machine would need.

q: 用 8 台机器线性并行估算的重点是什么？
options: 机器数量对完成时间没有任何实际影响
无论用多少台机器都无法在 5 天内完成任务
线性假设在真实系统里永远精确成立
线性并行可把 31 天压到约 3.9 天，重点是估算路径
why: 除以并行机器数只是粗略线性近似；面试更看重你能给出估算路径并承认假设局限，而不是记住这个数字。
why_en: Dividing by the number of parallel machines is only a rough linear approximation, and interviewers care more that you can walk through the estimate and admit its limits than that you memorize the number.
scenario: 把单机约 31 天的估算线性除以并行机器数，示例用 8 台机器。
options_en: The number of machines has no effect on completion time.
No number of machines can finish within five days.
The linear assumption always holds exactly in real systems.
Linear parallelism cuts about 31 days to about 3.9 days, but the point is the estimation path, not the exact figure.
q_en: What is the point of the eight-machine linear parallelism estimate?
scenario_en: Take the roughly 31-day single-machine estimate and divide it linearly by the number of parallel machines; this example uses eight machines.

q: 为什么每个域名 1 rps 的礼貌限制不等于全系统只能 1 rps？
options: 因为爬虫可以同时访问数百万不同域名，每个域名各自限速
因为 robots.txt 可以被忽略
因为 S3 会替爬虫下载网页
因为 DNS 查询不算请求
why: 限速维度是域名，不是全局；并行抓取大量不同域名时，聚合吞吐仍然很高。这个解释能化解礼貌和高吞吐看似矛盾的问题。
why_en: The one-request-per-second limit is per domain, so crawling many domains concurrently still allows high aggregate throughput.
tradeoff: 限速维度是域名 vs 全系统聚合吞吐
options_en: Because the crawler can hit millions of distinct domains at once, each rate-limited on its own.
Because robots.txt can simply be ignored.
Because S3 downloads the pages on the crawler's behalf.
Because DNS lookups do not count as requests.
q_en: Why does a one-rps-per-domain politeness limit not mean the whole crawler is limited to one rps?

scenario: Parser Worker 只需要从对象存储读取 HTML、抽文本、写回文本，但必须跟上 URL Fetcher 的产出速度。
q: Parser Worker 更适合怎样扩缩容？
options: 只在每天午夜运行一次
按下游队列积压动态扩缩容
固定一台机器，完全不做并发
按 DNS TTL 来扩缩容
why: 解析阶段计算和 I/O 相对简单，可以用队列积压作为伸缩信号，通过 Lambda、Fargate 或 Worker 池扩展。这样不必提前精确估算解析机器数。
why_en: Parser workers can autoscale based on the downstream queue backlog so they keep pace with fetchers without fixed capacity guesses.
whenOtherWins: 如果解析包含复杂模型推理或严格批处理窗口，可能需要专门容量规划；本题解析任务较常规。
tradeoff: 按积压信号弹性伸缩 vs 固定容量预先规划
options_en: Run it only once a day at midnight.
Autoscale based on the downstream queue backlog.
Fix it at one machine with no concurrency.
Scale it based on DNS TTL.
q_en: How should Parser Workers scale up and down?
scenario_en: Parser workers read HTML from object storage, extract text, and write the text back, but they must keep up with the URL Fetchers' output rate.

q: DNS 耗时占比较高对 Web Crawler 设计意味着什么？
options: 这个比例只在小规模才成立，规模变大反而更快
应放弃自建缓存，把解析全交给单一第三方
大规模抓取下 DNS 是真实瓶颈，需缓存加多 provider
DNS 查询耗时可以完全忽略，无需任何优化措施
why: 70% 的耗时占比说明大规模抓取下 DNS 是真实瓶颈，缓存解析结果和使用多个 provider 是直接的应对手段。
why_en: A seventy-percent time share means DNS is a genuine bottleneck at crawler scale, and caching lookups plus using multiple providers are the direct fixes.
scenario: 早期爬虫研究（如 Mercator 论文）发现，没有自建解析优化前，DNS 查询可能占到每个线程耗时的约 70%。
options_en: This ratio only holds at small scale and gets better automatically at large scale.
You should drop self-managed caching and rely on a single third-party provider.
At crawler scale, DNS is a real bottleneck that needs caching and multiple providers.
DNS lookup time can be ignored entirely with no optimization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS resolves a domain name into an IP address.

q_en: What does a high DNS time share imply for web crawler design?
scenario_en: Early crawler research, such as the Mercator paper, found that before custom resolver optimizations, DNS lookups could take about 70% of each thread's time.

scenario: 爬虫会反复抓取同一域名下的多个 URL，DNS 解析在高并发下成为瓶颈。
q: 第一层 DNS 优化是什么？
options: 每次请求都强制绕过缓存
把 DNS 查询写入 S3
用 Bloom Filter 代替 DNS
在 Crawler 中缓存域名到 IP 的解析结果
why: 同一域名的多个 URL 可以复用 DNS 结果，减少网络往返和外部 DNS 压力。缓存需要尊重 TTL，但它是最直接的优化。
why_en: Caching DNS results lets many URLs on the same domain reuse one lookup and reduces external resolver load.
whenOtherWins: 如果域名解析高度动态或 TTL 极短，缓存时间要更保守；如果单一 provider 达到限额，还要叠加多 provider。
tradeoff: 缓存复用解析结果 vs 每次都发起新查询
options_en: Force every request to bypass the cache.
Write DNS query logs into S3.
Replace DNS lookups with a Bloom filter.
Cache the domain-to-IP resolution inside the crawler.

termDefinitions.meaning: DNS 记录的缓存有效期，过期后需要重新解析。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a DNS record stays valid in cache before it must be re-resolved.

optionMeanings: 错：绕开缓存等于放弃优化
错：S3 不能替代域名解析
错：Bloom Filter 不做域名解析
对：复用解析结果减少往返
q_en: What is the first DNS optimization layer?
scenario_en: The crawler repeatedly fetches multiple URLs from the same domain, and DNS resolution becomes a bottleneck at high concurrency.

scenario: 第三方 DNS provider 有 QPS 限制，单 provider 很容易在全网抓取时触顶；团队希望快速降低被限流风险。
q: 第三方 DNS 限流下的务实优化是什么？
options: 多个 DNS provider 轮询分摊请求
停止 DNS 解析，直接猜 IP
把所有域名固定到同一个 IP
只抓取没有域名的 URL
why: 多 DNS provider 轮询能分散负载，降低单点限流风险。它不学术但很实用，适合在面试里展示真实约束意识。
why_en: Round-robining across multiple DNS providers spreads resolver load and reduces the chance of hitting one provider's rate limits.
whenOtherWins: 如果团队能运营自建高性能 resolver，自建也可能更优；若流量很小，单 provider 加缓存就足够。
tradeoff: 多 provider 分摊限流风险 vs 单一 provider 简单但脆弱
options_en: Round-robin across multiple DNS providers.
Stop resolving DNS and guess the IP directly.
Pin every domain to the same IP address.
Only crawl URLs that have no domain name.
q_en: What practical optimization helps when a third-party DNS provider rate-limits you?
scenario_en: Third-party DNS providers have QPS limits, and one provider can hit its cap during web-scale crawling, so the team wants a quick way to reduce throttling risk.

q: 补全 URL 级去重和内容级去重的区别：
text: {{URL 级去重}} 在入队前查 Metadata DB，避免同一 URL 重复抓；{{内容级去重}} 在抓取后对页面内容哈希，识别不同 URL 返回相同内容。
why: URL 去重便宜但不够，因为不同 URL 可能返回同一页面。内容哈希去重能跳过重复内容的解析和存储。
why_en: URL deduplication avoids repeated URLs before enqueueing, while content deduplication hashes fetched pages to catch identical content served by different URLs.
q_en: Fill in the difference between URL-level and content-level deduplication:

scenario: 抓取后需要判断 HTML 内容是否已经见过，希望准确、不引入误判，并且 Metadata DB 能承受索引写入。
q: 这个爬虫更偏向的实用内容去重方案是？
options: 完全跳过内容去重这一步
hash 存入 Metadata DB 并建索引
只比较 URL 字符串是否相同
只用进程内存 Set，不落盘
why: 内容 hash 加索引简单、准确，现代数据库维护大索引通常可接受。这个方案比 Bloom Filter 更适合追求准确和简单的主线设计。
why_en: Storing content hashes in the metadata database with an index is simple, exact, and practical for deduplicating fetched pages.
whenOtherWins: 如果内存和查询延迟极端敏感且能接受少量漏抓，Bloom Filter 可以更省空间；只做 URL 去重会漏掉重复内容。
tradeoff: 简单准确的 hash 索引 vs 省内存但有误判的 Bloom Filter
options_en: Skip content deduplication entirely.
Store the content hash in the metadata DB and index that column.
Only compare URL strings.
Use an in-memory set with no persistence.
q_en: Which practical content-deduplication approach fits this crawler best?
scenario_en: After fetching a page, the crawler must tell whether the HTML content has been seen before; it wants exact results and the Metadata DB can handle indexed writes.

q: Bloom Filter 在内容去重里的核心语义是什么？
options: 它能返回原始 HTML
它能替代所有数据库索引且没有误差
说不存在时一定不存在，说存在时只是可能存在
说存在时一定存在，说不存在时只是可能不存在
why: Bloom Filter 没有 false negative，但有 false positive。用于去重时，可能把没抓过的内容误判为已抓过。
why_en: A Bloom filter can prove an item is absent but only says it is probably present, so false positives are the main trade-off.
scenario: 系统要在抓取后判断内容是否已抓过；对比 Bloom Filter 和精确 hash 索引在「是否存在」判断上的语义差异。
tradeoff: 精确但重的 hash 索引 vs 省内存但有 false positive 的 Bloom Filter
options_en: It can return the original HTML content.
It can replace every database index with zero error.
Saying 'absent' is always certain; saying 'present' is only probable.
Saying 'present' is always certain; saying 'absent' is only probable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 概率型集合结构：不存在时一定准确，存在时可能是假阳性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic set: a negative answer is certain, but a positive answer can be a false positive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 误判为存在，实际上并不存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive means the filter says an item is present when it actually is not.

q_en: What is the core Bloom filter semantic in content deduplication?
scenario_en: The crawler must decide after fetching whether content has been seen before, so compare Bloom filters and exact hash indexes on existence-check semantics.

q: 在爬虫内容去重中使用 Bloom Filter 的主要风险是什么？
options: 一定会重复抓取所有页面
会让对象存储失去持久性
会禁止 URL 深度字段
误判某个新页面已经抓过，从而跳过它
why: false positive 会让系统误以为某个内容 hash 已存在，导致少量新页面被跳过。可以增大 filter 和 hash 函数数量来降低概率，但不能完全消除。
why_en: The risk is a false positive that causes the crawler to skip a page it has not actually processed.
scenario: 系统已经决定用 Bloom Filter 做内容去重，用来快速跳过可能重复的页面。
options_en: It will definitely re-crawl every single page.
It strips durability from object storage.
It forbids using a URL depth field.
It may mistakenly treat an unseen page as already crawled and skip it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 概率型集合结构，可能有假阳性但没有假阴性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic set that can produce false positives but never false negatives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 误判为已存在，实际是新内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive here means new content is wrongly treated as already seen.

q_en: What is the main risk of using a Bloom filter for crawler content deduplication?
scenario_en: The crawler has chosen a Bloom filter for content deduplication so it can quickly skip pages that appear to be duplicates.

scenario: 面试官问 Bloom Filter 是否应该用于本题内容去重；系统追求简单准确，现代数据库索引成本可接受。
q: 内容去重里是否应该优先使用 Bloom Filter？
options: 先用 hash 索引；Bloom Filter 留作可选优化
完全不需要任何去重
只靠 URL 字符串比较就够了
坚持用 Bloom Filter，因为它永远不会误判
why: Bloom Filter 有趣但对这条主线偏过度设计；hash 索引更简单且准确。能说明何时 Bloom Filter 胜出，比机械套数据结构更高级。
why_en: The practical answer is to use an indexed content hash first and treat a Bloom filter as an optional optimization with false-positive cost.
whenOtherWins: 当 hash 集合极大、内存/查询压力极高、业务能接受少量漏抓时，Bloom Filter 才更有吸引力。
diagram:
flowchart LR
HTML[Raw HTML] --> Extract[Extract text]
Extract --> Hash[Content fingerprint]
Hash --> Seen[(Seen index)]
Seen --> Store[Store if new]
tradeoff: 简单准确优先 vs 省内存但要接受 false positive
options_en: Start with a hash index; keep the Bloom filter as an optional later optimization.
Skip deduplication entirely.
Rely only on comparing URL strings.
Insist on a Bloom filter because it never makes mistakes.
optionMeanings: 对：先用精确集合挡重复，之后再加概率过滤层
错：会导致大量重复内容入库
错：不同 URL 可能返回同一内容
错：概率结构仍可能把新内容当旧内容
q_en: Should a Bloom filter be the first choice for content deduplication here?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether a Bloom filter should be used for content deduplication; the system prefers simple exact behavior and can afford a database index.

q: Crawler trap 指的是什么？
options: 队列里的死信消息
让爬虫在同一站点无限跟链接、难以结束的页面结构
DNS provider 的免费额度
S3 的对象版本控制
why: Crawler trap 可能通过自链接、日历页、无限参数等方式制造无限链接空间。爬虫如果没有边界，会把时间耗在局部站点上。
why_en: A crawler trap is a link structure that keeps the crawler following effectively endless pages within the same site.
options_en: A dead-letter message sitting in a queue.
A link structure that keeps the crawler following endless links on one site.
A DNS provider's free-tier quota.
S3 object versioning.
q_en: What is a crawler trap?

q: 防止 crawler trap 的简单措施是什么？
options: 直接禁用所有 DNS 缓存机制
永远优先抓取最深的链接
记录 link-hop depth，超阈值停止扩展
把所有 URL 强行改成同一个域名
why: depth 是从种子 URL 起算的链接跳数，不是路径段数。超过 15-20 这类阈值时停止扩展，可以避免在无限站点结构里耗尽时间。
why_en: Tracking link-hop depth from the seed URL and cutting off branches beyond a threshold prevents crawler traps from consuming the crawl.
options_en: Disable all DNS caching.
Always prioritize the deepest links first.
Record link-hop depth and stop expanding a branch past a threshold.
Rewrite every URL to the same domain.
q_en: What is a simple way to avoid crawler traps?

scenario: 需求后来要求抓取 React/Angular 页面中由 JavaScript 加载出来的正文，而静态 HTML 里没有这些内容。
q: 抓取 JavaScript 动态内容需要引入什么能力？
options: 只增加 SQS 可见性超时
只提高 DNS 查询的 QPS
用 Bloom Filter 代替浏览器渲染
用 headless browser 渲染后再抽取正文
why: 动态内容需要执行 JavaScript 并等待页面渲染，普通 HTTP 抓 HTML 不够。Headless browser 能解决，但成本和复杂度明显更高。
why_en: JavaScript-rendered pages require a headless browser to execute scripts and extract the rendered content.
whenOtherWins: 如果页面正文已经在服务端 HTML 中，普通 fetch 更便宜、更快；动态渲染处理在本题主范围外。
tradeoff: 渲染后抽取覆盖 JS 内容 vs 普通 HTTP 抓取更便宜更快
options_en: Just increase the SQS visibility timeout.
Just raise the DNS query rate limit.
Replace browser rendering with a Bloom filter.
Render with a headless browser like Puppeteer or Playwright, then extract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有图形界面、可编程控制的浏览器，能执行 JavaScript 渲染页面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A headless browser is a scriptable browser without a GUI that can execute JavaScript to render a page.

optionMeanings: 错：可见性超时和渲染能力无关
错：DNS 速度不影响页面渲染
错：Bloom Filter 不能渲染页面
对：只有渲染后才能拿到 JS 内容
q_en: What capability is needed to crawl JavaScript-rendered content?
scenario_en: The requirement expands to text loaded by JavaScript in React or Angular pages, and that text is missing from the static HTML.

scenario: 有些 URL 指向非常大的文件，系统只想抓取适合文本抽取的页面，避免下载超过 10MB 的对象。
q: 抓取前更合适的优化是什么？
options: 先用 HEAD 探测 Content-Length
直接 GET 下载完整文件再决定
把整个文件塞进队列消息体
直接关闭所有失败重试机制
why: HEAD 可以用很小的代价读取 Content-Length 等元数据，提前跳过大文件。这样节省带宽和 Worker 时间。
why_en: An HTTP HEAD request can check Content-Length cheaply so oversized files are skipped before downloading the body.
whenOtherWins: 如果服务端不支持 HEAD 或 Content-Length 不可信，可能需要带 Range 的探测或下载后中止策略。
tradeoff: 先探测大小再决定 vs 先下载再判断
options_en: Send a HEAD request to probe Content-Length before deciding.
GET the entire file first and decide afterward.
Stuff the file into the queue message body.
Turn off all retries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只请求响应头、不下载响应体的 HTTP 方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HEAD is an HTTP method that fetches only the response headers, not the body.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 响应头，声明响应体的字节大小。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content-Length is a response header that declares the size of the response body in bytes.

q_en: What is the better pre-fetch optimization?
scenario_en: Some URLs point to very large files, and the crawler only wants pages suitable for text extraction, avoiding objects larger than 10 MB.

scenario: 需求从一次性抓取变成每月重新抓取，且不同 URL 应按最近抓取时间、重要性或变化频率安排下次抓取。
q: 持续重新抓取时应该新增哪个组件？
options: 单机本地队列
URL Scheduler
更大的 robots.txt 文件
只读 DNS 缓存
why: URL Scheduler 根据 last crawl time、优先级或 popularity 决定何时把 URL 放回队列。持续更新和一次性 crawl 的调度问题不同。
why_en: A URL scheduler decides when to re-enqueue pages based on recency, priority, or popularity for continual crawling.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求只是一次性离线抓取，解析 Worker 直接把新 URL 入队即可，不必单独引入调度器。
diagram:
flowchart TD
URL[Candidate URL] --> Rules[Trap heuristics]
Rules --> Depth[Depth and pattern caps]
Rules --> Score[Quality score]
Score --> Frontier[Priority frontier]
tradeoff: 按时间/优先级调度重新抓取 vs 一次性抓取无需调度
options_en: A single-machine local queue.
A URL Scheduler.
A bigger robots.txt file.
A read-only DNS cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据上次抓取时间、优先级或热度决定何时重新入队的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A URL scheduler decides when to re-enqueue a page based on recency, priority, or popularity.

q_en: What component should be added for ongoing recrawls?
scenario_en: The requirement changes from a one-time crawl to a monthly recrawl, and different URLs should be scheduled by last crawl time, importance, or change frequency.

scenario: 业务希望优先抓取重要域名或热门页面，但队列系统本身不提供单队列内的严格优先级消费。
q: 队列不支持严格优先级时，一个简单可解释的方案是什么？
options: 只在 Metadata DB 改字段，不改消费逻辑
禁用死信队列
多个优先级队列，Worker 先轮询高优先级
把所有 URL 随机打散
why: 多个队列或 Kafka 多 topic 可以模拟优先级，Worker 先消费高优先级再降级消费普通队列。这样不必在单队列里实现复杂排序。
why_en: Separate queues or topics per priority let crawlers poll high-priority work first without requiring sorted consumption inside one queue.
whenOtherWins: 如果队列产品原生支持优先级，可直接使用；如果所有 URL 价值接近，单队列更简单。
tradeoff: 多队列模拟优先级 vs 单队列里排序
options_en: Only change a field in the Metadata DB without changing consumption logic.
Disable the dead-letter queue.
Multiple priority queues, with workers polling the high-priority one first.
Shuffle all URLs randomly.
q_en: What simple priority scheme works when the queue lacks strict priority support?
scenario_en: The business wants to crawl important domains or popular pages first, but the queue does not support strict priority inside one queue.

q: 把「可恢复且礼貌的爬虫」核心决策链排成正确顺序。
steps: 用 SQS visibility timeout、ChangeMessageVisibility 和 DLQ 管理重试与失败隔离
在 Metadata DB 中保存 URL/Domain 状态和对象存储引用
先承认单体 Crawler 任一步失败都会让进度难以恢复
用 robots 规则、每域名锁和共享限流保证礼貌抓取
把抓取与解析拆成流水线阶段，队列消息只传记录 id
why: 先识别单体失败面，再拆流水线并持久化状态；有了队列语义后才能可靠重试，最后叠加 robots 和限流保证对外部站点友好。
why_en: The robust design starts by isolating pipeline stages, persists metadata, uses SQS retry semantics, and then layers in robots-aware politeness controls.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[Single crawler failure risk] --> B[Pipeline stages]
  B --> C[Metadata DB references]
  C --> D[SQS retry and DLQ]
  D --> E[Robots and rate limits]
q_en: Put the core decision chain for a recoverable and polite crawler in the correct order.

q: WhatsApp 设计题的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are core functional requirements for the WhatsApp design problem? (select all)
options: 音视频通话
创建最多 100 人的群聊
发送 / 接收消息
离线期间的消息在重新上线后仍能收到（30 天内）
options_en: Audio and video calling
Creating group chats with up to one hundred participants
Sending and receiving messages
Receiving messages sent while offline (within thirty days)
why: 核心功能是群聊（上限 100 人）、收发消息、离线补收（30 天）以及消息里带媒体；音视频通话、商家交互、注册资料管理都明确划到范围之外。
why_en: The core requirements are group chats capped at one hundred people, sending and receiving messages, offline delivery within thirty days, and media, while calling is explicitly out of scope.

scenario: 群聊功能要求最多支持 100 人同时在一个会话里；这个上限后续会反复出现在建群事务、CDN 收益评估和 Pub/Sub 发布次数的计算中。
scenario_en: Group chat must support up to 100 participants in one conversation at once; that cap keeps resurfacing later in the create-chat transaction, the CDN payoff analysis, and the pub/sub publish-count math.
q: 群上限定为 100 人，这个量级最直接支持下面哪个实现判断？
q_en: With the group cap set at 100 people, which implementation judgment does that number most directly support?
options: 100 人已经足够多，必须像 Kafka 一样为每个群单独建一条消息队列
上限只是产品文案，对存储和路由设计没有实际约束
创建群聊时可以把所有参与者记录放进单个 DynamoDB 事务，只有逼近上限的大群才需要分批写
既然上限是 100，Pub/Sub 就必须一律按 chat 而不是 user 分区
options_en: One hundred is large enough that each group needs its own Kafka topic, like a message queue
The cap is only marketing copy with no real constraint on storage or routing
Creating a chat can fit all participant records into a single DynamoDB transaction; only chats near the cap need batched writes
Because the cap is 100, Pub/Sub channels must always be partitioned by chat instead of by user
optionDirectness: 只有群规模很大且每群需要独立顺序消费时，单群队列才更像合理选择。
只有这个数字不参与事务、路由或扇出计算时，才可以把它当纯产品限制。
当参与者数能落进单事务上限时，一次事务写完整成员关系最简单。
按 chat 分区适合每个群都有大量订阅者在线收同一份实时流。
why: 群上限 100 人和 DynamoDB 单事务 100 items 的上限贴边，所以建群写入默认能塞进一次事务，只有大群逼近上限时才要分批；这个数字后面还会影响 CDN 收益评估和分区发布次数。
why_en: The hundred-person group cap lines up with DynamoDB's hundred-item transaction limit, so creating a chat normally fits one transaction and only needs batching near the cap.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录某个会话里都有哪些成员的关联表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ChatParticipant is the join table recording which members belong to which chat.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志型消息队列，常用于高吞吐事件流的持久化与顺序消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-based message queue used for durable, ordered consumption of high-throughput event streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布订阅模型：发布者把消息发到主题或频道，订阅者从对应主题接收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is a publish-subscribe model where publishers send to topics or channels and subscribers receive from them.

scenario: 非功能需求要求「消息在中心服务器保存不超过必要时长」，服务端对离线用户未投递消息的保留期限设为 30 天。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirement says messages should not sit on central servers longer than necessary, and the retention window for undelivered messages to offline users is set at thirty days.
q: 30 天这个留存期限，最直接支持下面哪种实现方式？
q_en: Which implementation does that thirty-day retention window most directly support?
options: 在应用代码里永久保存每条消息，仅在读取时按 30 天过滤展示
30 天只是产品说法，数据库层不需要任何过期机制
把所有消息定期打包转移到冷备份，永不删除
给 Inbox、Message 和附件条目统一设 30 天 TTL，交由存储层自动删除
options_en: Keep every message forever in application code and only filter by thirty days on read
Thirty days is only marketing language; the database layer needs no expiration mechanism
Periodically bundle all messages off to cold backup and never delete them
Set a thirty-day TTL on the Inbox, Message, and attachment rows and let the store expire them automatically
why: TTL 是零运维成本满足「不超必要时长」的实现方式：到期由存储层自动删除，不需要应用代码扫表过滤或人工归档。
why_en: A thirty-day retention window is best implemented as a TTL on the storage rows so the database expires old data automatically, instead of filtering old rows in application code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储条目设置的存活期限，到期后由存储层自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TTL is an expiration time after which the storage layer automatically deletes the item.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

q: 这几项被划出范围，分别让系统省掉了哪块设计？（多选）
q_en: For each item ruled out of scope, which piece of the design does it let you skip? (select all)
options: 不做音视频通话，就不用设计实时媒体流的中继/SFU 组件，Chat Server 只处理文本与附件元数据
不做商家交互，Chat/Message 实体就不用为「商业账号」单独设计消息模板或计费字段
不做注册与资料管理，User 实体就不用设计头像、简介变更的广播机制
既然通话不在范围内，实时收发消息也可以退回普通 HTTP 轮询，不必保留 WebSocket 长连接
options_en: Skipping calling means you never design a real-time media relay or SFU component; the Chat Server only handles text and attachment metadata
Skipping business interactions means Chat and Message never need a separate message template or billing field for business accounts
Skipping registration and profile management means the User entity never needs a broadcast mechanism for avatar or bio changes
Since calling is out of scope, real-time messaging can also fall back to plain HTTP polling instead of keeping a persistent WebSocket
why: 划出范围省掉的是那个功能自己的组件（SFU、商业消息模板、资料变更广播），不影响其他仍在范围内的需求；实时消息本身仍要求低延迟双向推送，跟通话是否在范围无关。
why_en: Ruling a feature out of scope only removes that feature's own component, not the messaging path, which still needs a persistent low-latency connection regardless of calling.
scenario: 面试官明确把音视频通话、商家/企业交互、注册与资料管理划到范围外，只保留群聊、收发消息、离线补投和媒体附件。
scenario_en: The interviewer explicitly puts audio/video calling, business interactions, and registration/profile management out of scope, keeping only group chat, messaging, offline delivery, and media attachments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实时音视频通话里转发媒体流的服务器组件，只做转发不做混流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SFU is a server component in real-time calling that forwards media streams to participants without mixing them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

scenario: 非功能需求把「消息投递给在线用户」的延迟目标定在 500ms 以内。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirement sets a latency target of under five hundred milliseconds for delivering messages to online users.
q: 500ms 这个延迟目标，最直接把系统接口设计推向哪个方向？
q_en: Which direction does that five-hundred-millisecond latency target most directly push the interface design?
options: 客户端每 500ms 发一次 HTTP 轮询，查询是否有新消息
维持一条长连接（WebSocket），服务器直接把消息推给在线客户端
把消息统一批量打包，每隔几秒发送一次以节省带宽
延迟目标只影响 UI 动画速度，与传输方式无关
options_en: Have the client send an HTTP poll every 500ms to check for new messages
Keep a persistent connection (WebSocket) so the server can push messages straight to online clients
Batch messages together and send them out every few seconds to save bandwidth
The latency target only affects UI animation speed and has nothing to do with the transport
why: 500ms 排除了轮询间隔带来的延迟下限，只有服务器主动推送的长连接才能稳定达标。
why_en: A five-hundred-millisecond delivery target rules out polling-style delays and pushes the design toward a persistent connection that the server can push through immediately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

q: 除了低延迟，本题的核心非功能需求还有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Besides low latency, which of these are also core non-functional requirements for this problem? (select all)
options: 详尽的安全与反爬虫防护
保证消息必达（deliverability）
支撑数十亿用户的高吞吐
消息在中心服务器保存不超过必要时长，且系统能抵御单组件故障
options_en: Exhaustive security and anti-scraping protections
Guaranteed deliverability of messages
High throughput to support billions of users
Messages stored no longer than necessary, with resilience to component failures
why: 核心 NFR：必达、数十亿用户高吞吐、消息不超期存储、组件级容错；安全细节与反爬虫被明确放到 below the line。
why_en: The core non-functional requirements are guaranteed deliverability, billions of users at high throughput, minimal server-side retention, and resilience to component failures, while deep security work is out of scope.

q: 规划阶段关于 1:1 聊天与群聊的关键洞察是什么？
q_en: What is the key planning insight about one-on-one chat versus group chat?
options: 1:1 只是 2 人的群聊特例，按通用群聊模型处理
1:1 和群聊差异太大，必须两套独立系统
先只实现 1:1，群聊等以后重构
群聊可以用多次 1:1 发送来模拟
options_en: One-on-one chat is just the two-person special case, modeled with the general group-chat approach
One-on-one and group chat differ too much and need two separate systems
Build only one-on-one chat first and refactor in group chat later
Simulate a group chat by sending the same message one-on-one to each member
why: 把 1:1 看成 2 人的群聊，就能用一套通用模型覆盖两种场景；另一个规划洞察是把问题拆成「持久必达」和「实时投递」两部分。
why_en: One-on-one chats are just group chats with two participants, so the design solves the general group case while focusing on the dominant one-on-one traffic.

q: 补全 WhatsApp 设计的四个核心实体：
q_en: Fill in the four core entities of the WhatsApp design:
text: 核心实体：{{User}}（用户）、{{Chat}}（2-100 人的会话）、{{Message}}（消息）、{{Client}}（同一用户可能有多台设备）。
why: 实体是推理问题的语言基础；把 Client 与 User 分开，正是后面多设备深挖的伏笔。实体列错等于在坏地基上盖楼。
why_en: The four core entities are users, chats of two to one hundred people, messages, and clients, since one user may own several devices.

q: 为什么实体里除了 User 还要单独定义 Client？
q_en: Why does the entity list define a separate Client alongside User?
options: 为了给每台设备单独计费
Client 只是 User 的别名，没有实际区别
为了做灰度实验分流
一个用户可能有多台设备，投递与同步要精确到设备
options_en: To bill each device separately
Client is just an alias for User with no real difference
To route users into A/B experiments
A user may own multiple devices, so delivery and sync must be tracked per device
why: 用户 ≠ 设备：一个账号可能有多个客户端，各自的送达状态不同。这个区分让后面「Inbox 按 client 而非 user」的改造顺理成章。
why_en: A user can own several devices at once, so delivery and sync must be tracked per client rather than per user.

scenario: 聊天应用里客户端要高频地发送消息，同时服务器要把别人发来的消息实时推给它——收发双向且频繁。
scenario_en: In a chat app the client sends messages frequently, and the server must also push other people's messages to it in real time — traffic is bidirectional and frequent.
q: 系统接口最合适的形态是？
q_en: What is the best shape for the system interface here?
options: REST + 客户端定时轮询
GraphQL 查询
双向 WebSocket 长连接，命令即 API
每条消息发起一个新的 HTTP 请求
options_en: REST with client-side polling on a timer
GraphQL queries
A bidirectional WebSocket connection, with commands acting as the API
A fresh HTTP request for every single message
why: 高频双向更新是双向 socket 的标准适用场景：客户端开 app 即建立连接，之后收发都以命令形式走这条连接。这是实时更新模式的典型应用。
why_en: High-frequency bidirectional updates are the perfect case for a persistent WebSocket connection that carries commands in both directions.
whenOtherWins: 普通「请求-响应」型产品用 REST 更合适；本设计里附件上传也刻意绕开 socket，走独立的 HTTP 服务。
tradeoff: 长连接双向实时推送 vs 简单请求-响应模型

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 方法和资源路径的请求-响应式 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is a request-response API style built on HTTP verbs and resource paths.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端在一次请求里按需声明所需字段的查询语言型 API。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL lets a client specify in one request exactly which fields it wants back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层安全协议，为连接提供加密和身份校验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS encrypts a connection and verifies the identity of the parties on it.

q: 除了 WebSocket over TLS，文中提到还有哪种同样可行的传输方案？
q_en: Besides WebSocket over TLS, which other transport does the article say would work just as well?
options: HTTP/1.1 短轮询
在原始 TLS 加密的 TCP 连接上跑自定义协议
UDP 组播
Server-Sent Events 单向推送
options_en: HTTP/1.1 short polling
A custom protocol running over a raw TLS-encrypted TCP connection
UDP multicast
One-way Server-Sent Events
optionMeanings: 反复发起短连接 HTTP 请求轮询。
在加密的裸 TCP 连接上自定义报文格式。
面向组播、不保证送达的 UDP。
服务器单向持续推送的 HTTP 机制。
why: 面试里选 WebSocket（TLS 保证安全）即可，但自定义协议跑在 TLS 加密的裸 TCP 上同样成立——WhatsApp 真实实现更接近后者。
why_en: A custom protocol over a raw TLS-encrypted TCP connection would work just as well as WebSockets for this design.

q: 补全客户端发往服务器的四个核心命令：
q_en: Fill in the four core commands the client sends to the server:
text: 客户端→服务器命令：{{createChat}} 建会话、{{sendMessage}} 发消息、{{createAttachment}} 建附件、{{modifyChatParticipants}} 增删成员；服务器→客户端则有 chatUpdate 和 newMessage 等对应命令。
why: API 以 socket 上的命令形式定义，每个客户端命令都有推送给其他客户端的镜像命令。面试时可以只写命令名，细节「稍后回来补」完全可接受。
why_en: The client sends createChat, sendMessage, createAttachment, and modifyChatParticipants commands, and the server pushes mirrored commands like newMessage to other clients.

q: 客户端收到 newMessage 后必须回 ack，这一步换来了什么？
q_en: What does requiring the client to ack after receiving newMessage actually buy you?
options: 服务器确认送达客户端才清理 Inbox
客户端渲染速度更快
减少 WebSocket 握手次数
允许消息乱序到达
options_en: The server only clears the Inbox once it confirms the message reached the client
The client renders messages faster
It reduces the number of WebSocket handshakes
It allows messages to arrive out of order
why: 回执机制不起眼但至关重要：强制客户端 ack，服务器才有「消息已全程送达」的确定性，必达保证就建立在它之上。
why_en: Forcing clients to acknowledge receipt lets the server know a message truly reached the device, which is the foundation of guaranteed delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the confirmation signal a client sends back after receiving a message.

q: 负载均衡器应该怎么选？

L4 就够：没有 L7 需求时性能更高
DNS 轮询即可，不需要 LB
客户端自己挑服务器
options_en: It must be L7 because L7 is "more advanced"
L4 is enough: without any L7 need, it performs better
Plain DNS round robin, no load balancer needed
Let the client pick a server itself
why: 很多现代 L7 LB 也支持 WebSocket，但这里用不上 L7 的路径/Header 路由或按请求分摊能力，所以 L4 足够且一般更快。
why_en: An L4 load balancer is sufficient and generally faster here because none of the L7 capabilities like path-based routing are actually needed.
whenOtherWins: 需要按路径 / Header 把流量分发到不同服务、或想把同一客户端连接后的多个 HTTP 请求摊到多台服务器时，L7 才有价值。

q: 处理 createChat 时服务端要写哪些记录？
q_en: Which records does the server write when handling createChat?

只写 ChatParticipant 记录，会话本身没有元数据
先在 Message 表写一条占位消息，之后再回填成员
一条 Chat 记录加每人一条 ChatParticipant，小群一次事务，大群分批写
options_en: Write only one chat record, leaving no record of who the participants are
Write only ChatParticipant records, leaving the chat itself with no metadata
Write a placeholder row in the Message table first and backfill members later
One chat record plus one ChatParticipant record per member, one transaction for small chats and batched writes for large ones
optionMeanings: 只写会话本身，忽略成员关系。
只写成员关系，忽略会话元数据。
先占位一条消息记录。
同时写会话记录和每个成员的参与者记录。

q: Chat 表的主键怎么设计？

options: chatId + createdAt 复合主键
participantId 作主键
chatId 简单主键即可——通常只按会话 ID 查详情
会话名称作主键

participantId as the primary key
A simple primary key on chatId is enough, since lookups are almost always by chat id
The chat name as the primary key

q: ChatParticipant 表如何支持「查某个会话的全部成员」？
q_en: How does the ChatParticipant table support looking up every member of a chat?
options: chatId 作分区键、participantId 作排序键，一次 Query 拿到全部成员
全表 Scan 后再用应用代码过滤，成本随数据量线性增长
按 participantId 分区再二次过滤
把成员列表冗余成 Chat 表里的一个大字段
options_en: chatId as the partition key and participantId as the sort key, so one query returns every member
A full table scan filtered in application code, with cost growing linearly with data size
Partition by participantId and filter a second time
Redundantly store the member list as one big field on the Chat table
why: chatId 分区 + participantId 排序，Query 单个分区就拿到该会话全部成员，这是 DynamoDB 一查多行的标准建模。
why_en: With chat id as the partition key and participant id as the sort key, one query on the partition returns every member of the chat.
codeSample:
Table: ChatParticipant
PK (partition key): chatId
SK (sort key):      participantId

# Query(chatId = "chat_123") -> all rows for that chat

q: 反向查询「某用户加入的全部会话」怎么高效实现？
q_en: How do you efficiently answer the reverse query of every chat a given user belongs to?
options: 再建一张反向表，应用双写维护，容易不一致
对 ChatParticipant 做全表扫描
客户端本地缓存全部会话列表，规模大了不现实
建 GSI：participantId 分区键、chatId 排序键，自动同步
options_en: Build a separate reverse table maintained by application double-writes, which is prone to drift
Full table scan over ChatParticipant
Cache the entire chat list locally on the client, unrealistic at scale
Add a GSI keyed by participantId with chatId as sort key, kept in sync automatically
optionMeanings: 在应用层再维护一张反向表。
对主表做全表扫描过滤。
在客户端本地缓存全部结果。
用数据库自带的全局二级索引重新分区数据。
why: 全局二级索引把同一份数据按另一维度重新分区，反向查询变成一次 Query；GSI 由 DynamoDB 自动同步，不需要应用双写。
why_en: A global secondary index keyed by participant id with chat id as the sort key answers the reverse lookup, and DynamoDB keeps it in sync automatically.
codeSample:
GSI: ParticipantChats
PK (partition key): participantId
SK (sort key):      chatId

# Query(participantId = "user_42") -> all chats for that user
# DynamoDB keeps this index in sync with the base table automatically

q: 对基础设施类面试，文中强烈推荐的起步方法论是？

q: 单机 Chat Server 用什么追踪「谁连着我」？
q_en: What does a single-host Chat Server use to track who is currently connected?
options: 每次去数据库查连接表
Redis 里存一个全局在线集合
内存哈希表：userId 映射连接对象
写文件日志再解析
options_en: Query a connections table in the database on every send
Keep a global set of online users in Redis
An in-process hash map mapping userId to its WebSocket connection
Write to a log file and parse it back
why: 内存哈希表把 userId 映射到 socket 连接，发消息时直接查表下发；这也是后面「连接只存在于某台服务器内存里」这一路由难题的根源。
why_en: The server keeps an in-memory hash map from user id to WebSocket connection so it knows who is connected and can push messages directly.

q: 单机方案里发一条消息的三步是？
q_en: What are the three steps of sending a message in the single-host design?
options: 查参与者 → 查连接 → 逐个下发
先写磁盘再统一群发
向所有在线用户广播、由客户端过滤
先发给最活跃的用户再补发其他人
options_en: Look up participants, look up each connection, then send to each
Write to disk first, then broadcast to everyone at once
Broadcast to all online users and let the client filter
Send to the most active user first, then backfill the rest
why: sendMessage 进来后：查参与者、查连接、逐个下发。简单可用，但它隐含了所有人在线且连在同一台服务器的强假设。
why_en: The server looks up the chat participants, finds each one's WebSocket in its hash map, and sends the message over each connection.

options: 所有用户都在线

所有用户连在同一台 Chat Server 上

options_en: Every user is online
Every message is smaller than 1KB
Every user is connected to the same Chat Server
Every user holds one usable WebSocket connection
why: 三个强假设分别对应三块深挖：离线 → Inbox 持久化；同一台服务器 → Pub/Sub 路由；连接可用 → 心跳与故障检测。
why_en: The naive design assumes everyone is online, on the same server, and holding a live connection, and each assumption maps to a later deep dive.

scenario: 用户离线时发给他的消息，30 天内重新上线必须能收到；在线用户则要即时收到。
scenario_en: A message sent to an offline user must still be delivered if they reconnect within thirty days, while online users need it delivered immediately.
q: 文中的存储设计是？
q_en: What is the article's storage design for this?
options: 完全依赖客户端本地存储互相同步
每个接收者有 Inbox：在线即时投递，离线等回来补发
把离线消息转成推送通知即可
为每个用户建一个 Kafka topic 当收件箱
options_en: Rely entirely on client-side local storage syncing with each other
Each recipient gets an inbox: deliver immediately if online, or wait for reconnect if offline
Just convert offline messages into push notifications
Create one Kafka topic per user as their inbox
optionMeanings: 把同步责任全部丢给客户端本地存储。
为每个接收者建一份持久化的未投递队列。
把离线消息简化成一次性推送通知。
借用消息队列的每用户 topic 当收件箱。
why: Inbox 是必达与离线支持的核心：先写库再投递，ack 后删除。它把「持久必达」与「实时投递」解耦成两条路径。
why_en: Each recipient gets an inbox of undelivered messages that is written before any delivery attempt and cleared only after the client acknowledges.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品只服务在线场景（比如直播弹幕），不需要 Inbox，直接经连接推送、丢了就丢了。
tradeoff: 持久 Inbox 保证离线必达 vs 只走实时推送的简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息持久化到磁盘、按 topic 组织、并维护消费者位点的分布式消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue that persists messages to disk, organizes them into topics, and tracks consumer offsets.

scenario: 群聊里接收者可能离线，也可能 Chat Server 在实时推送前崩溃；这题考的是先把“必须投递给谁”落到可靠存储。
scenario_en: In a group chat a recipient may be offline, or the Chat Server could crash before the real-time push; this card tests durably recording who still needs delivery before anything else.
q: 把「发送一条消息」的完整流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the full flow of sending a message into the correct order:
steps: Chat Server 写 Message 表 + 为每个接收者创建 Inbox 条目（持久化）
发送者经 WebSocket 发出 sendMessage
Chat Server 尝试经各在线参与者的连接实时投递 newMessage
Chat Server 查 ChatParticipant 表得到全部参与者
已连接客户端回 ack，服务器从 Inbox 删除该消息
向发送者返回 SUCCESS 和最终 messageId
why: 先写 Inbox，是为了先落下“谁还没收到”的债务。Message 存正文，Inbox 存每个接收者的待投递指针；实时 WebSocket 只是加速路径，ack 后才清理。
why_en: Write the inbox before realtime push so delivery obligation is durable. The message table stores the body once. Inbox rows store per-recipient pending delivery state. Realtime WebSocket push is a fast path. If the server crashes before push, recipients can replay from the inbox after reconnect. Delete or mark an inbox row only after that recipient ACKs.
tradeoff: 可靠投递优先 vs 在线用户即时推送；多写一份 Inbox 换来离线补拉和崩溃恢复
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as 发送者
    participant CS as Chat Server
    participant DB as DynamoDB
    participant R as 接收者
    S->>CS: sendMessage
    CS->>DB: 查 ChatParticipant
    CS->>DB: 写 Message + Inbox（持久化）
    CS-->>S: SUCCESS + messageId
    CS->>R: newMessage（尽力而为）
    R-->>CS: ack
    CS->>DB: 删除 Inbox 条目

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient delivery queue stored in a database, not just an in-memory list.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据写到数据库或日志里。进程重启后，数据仍然能被读回来。

termDefinitions.meaning: 会话成员表。Chat Server 用它找出这条消息应该投递给哪些用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ChatParticipant is the membership table that tells the server which users should receive a message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the confirmation signal a client sends back after receiving a message.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

q: 离线客户端重新连接后的补发流程是？
q_en: What is the redelivery flow when an offline client reconnects?
options: 无差别重发最近 24 小时的全部消息，浪费带宽也不精确
客户端自己去扫 Message 表，既没权限也没索引
查 Inbox 拿未投递 ID，取消息体下发，ack 后删除
等下一条新消息到来时顺带同步，安静期会一直漏
options_en: Blindly resend every message from the last 24 hours, wasting bandwidth and imprecise
Have the client scan the Message table itself, with neither the permission nor the index to do so
Read the Inbox for undelivered ids, fetch each body, deliver, then delete after ack
Wait until the next new message arrives and piggyback a sync then, missing everything during a quiet period
why: 重连同步 = Inbox 找 ID、Message 表取体、下发、ack 后删。同一套 ack 语义同时服务在线投递和离线补发。
why_en: On reconnect the server reads the inbox for undelivered message ids, fetches each message, delivers them over the socket, and deletes entries once acknowledged.
diagram:
graph LR
    Client[Reconnect client] --> Server[Chat server]
    Server --> Inbox[(Inbox rows)]
    Inbox --> Missed[Undelivered messages]
    Missed --> Client
    Client --> Ack[Ack delivered]
    Ack --> Inbox

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the confirmation signal a client sends back after receiving a message.

scenario: Inbox 与 Message 表里超过 30 天的旧数据需要定期清理，既控制存储也满足「保存不超必要时长」。
scenario_en: Rows older than thirty days in the Inbox and Message tables need periodic cleanup, both to control storage and to satisfy the "no longer than necessary" requirement.
q: 最省事的清理机制是？
q_en: What is the least effort way to handle this cleanup?
options: 每天跑全表扫描批量删除
给条目设 TTL，到期自动删除
依赖客户端发起删除请求
写个 cron 脚本逐行比对时间戳
options_en: Run a full table scan every day and batch-delete
Set a TTL on the entries and let them expire automatically
Rely on the client to send a delete request
Write a cron script that compares timestamps row by row
optionMeanings: 定时批量全表扫描后删除。
存储层原生的过期自动删除。
把删除动作交给客户端触发。
自己写脚本逐行比对时间戳。
why: 给条目设 TTL 让存储层自动过期，零运维成本地满足 30 天上限；这与附件存储的 30 天 TTL 是同一思路。
why_en: Setting a time-to-live on the inbox and message items lets the store expire old rows automatically and honors the thirty-day retention limit.
whenOtherWins: 若业务要求永久聊天历史（云端全量同步类产品），TTL 删除就不适用，需要专门的归档与分层存储。
tradeoff: TTL 自动过期的零运维 vs 定时任务人工可控的清理节奏

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储条目设置的存活期限，到期后由存储层自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TTL is an expiration time after which the storage layer automatically deletes the item.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

scenario: 2 亿活跃用户，人均每天约发送 20 条消息。
scenario_en: There are two hundred million active users, each sending about twenty messages a day on average.
q: 由此估算出的发送速率量级，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Which conclusion does the resulting send-rate estimate most directly support?
options: 算下来每天约 4 亿条、峰值也就百来条/秒，随便一台单机数据库都扛得住
算下来每天约 40 亿条、约 4 万条/秒——这个量级已经超出单机数据库的合理范围，写入必须走可水平扩展的存储
算出来的数字大到荒谬，说明这类估算在面试里没有意义
算下来约 400 万条/秒，逼近现有任何存储方案的物理极限，必须自建存储引擎
options_en: Work it out to about four hundred million a day and only about a hundred per second at peak, which any single database host can handle
Work it out to about four billion a day, roughly forty thousand per second — big enough to rule out a single database host, so writes need a horizontally scalable store
The resulting number is absurdly large, meaning this kind of estimate is pointless in an interview
Work it out to about four million per second, pushing against the physical limit of any existing storage option
why: 200M × 20 条/天 = 40 亿条/天 ≈ 4 万条/秒；这个量级排除了单机方案，但还没到需要自研存储的地步，推动设计转向可水平扩展、可分片的存储。
why_en: Two hundred million users sending about twenty messages a day works out to roughly forty thousand messages per second, big enough to rule out a single database host but not so extreme that a horizontally sharded store can't handle it.

scenario: 在上一步估算的发送速率基础上，每条 1:1 消息要写一次 Message、一次接收者 Inbox，再叠加群聊的多接收者放大。
scenario_en: Building on the previous send-rate estimate, every one-on-one message writes once to Message and once to the recipient's Inbox, plus the extra fan-out from group chats.
q: 算上双写与群聊放大后的总写入量级，最支持哪个结论？
q_en: Counting the double write and the group fan-out, which conclusion does the total write-rate estimate support?
options: 总写入量级冲到约 1000 万/秒，DynamoDB 撑不住，必须自研存储引擎
双写和群聊放大可以忽略不计，量级和单条发送速率一样
这类估算不可靠，唯一办法是直接上生产环境压测
总写入量级约 10 万/秒——以 userId 为分区键的 DynamoDB 完全能承接，不需要更换存储
options_en: It spikes to about ten million writes per second, more than DynamoDB can take, so a custom storage engine is required
The double write and group fan-out are negligible; the load is the same as the raw send rate
This kind of estimate is unreliable; the only way to know is to load-test in production
The total lands around one hundred thousand writes per second, well within reach for DynamoDB partitioned by userId
optionDirectness: 只有估算已接近托管数据库的分区吞吐上限时，才该考虑自研存储。
只有每条消息只落一行、没有收件箱和群成员扇出时，发送速率才等于写入速率。
压测适合校准容量余量，但面试里先要用估算判断方案是否同量级可行。
按接收者分散写入时，10 万写/秒是可以继续用托管存储的量级。
why: 1:1 消息每条写一次 Message、一次接收者 Inbox；算上群聊约 10 万写/秒，对按 userId 分区的 DynamoDB 不构成压力——这一步证明了 Inbox 方案的可行性。
why_en: Counting the message write plus inbox entries and group fan-out, the load is roughly one hundred thousand writes per second, well within DynamoDB's reach with user id as the partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条写入或消息被放大成多条下游操作的过程，例如一条群消息要分发给每个成员。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is when a single write or message multiplies into many downstream operations, like delivering one group message to every member.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保存消息正文、发送者、会话和时间等元数据的主记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Message record stores the body, sender, chat, timestamp, and related metadata for one message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户标识，作为分区键时会把不同用户的收件箱写入分散到不同分区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A userId is the user identifier; as a partition key, it spreads inbox writes across users.

q: 把附件二进制直接存进数据库（经 WebSocket 上传）有哪两个核心问题？
q_en: What are the two core problems with storing attachment bytes directly in the database over the WebSocket upload?
options: 成本太低不划算，其实存储成本不是这里的瓶颈
事务冲突太多，其实这不是并发写入的问题
数据库不擅长大二进制 blob，且拖累 Chat Server 带宽
无法给附件设 TTL，其实 TTL 一直可以设置
options_en: Not cost-effective because storage is too cheap, but cost is not the real bottleneck here
Too many transaction conflicts, but this is not actually a concurrent-write problem
Databases are not built for large binary blobs, and it drags down the Chat Server's bandwidth
You cannot set a TTL on an attachment, but a TTL can always be set
optionMeanings: 把问题归到成本不划算上。
把问题归到事务冲突上。
把问题归到数据库不适合大 blob、且拖累服务器带宽上。
把问题归到无法设置过期上。
why: 这是明确的反面教材：数据库不为大 blob 优化，聊天服务器也不该被「傻存傻取」拖垮带宽——媒体要交给专用设施。
why_en: Databases are not built for large binary blobs, and ferrying media through the chat servers cripples the bandwidth they need for messaging.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储条目设置的存活期限，到期后由存储层自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TTL is an expiration time after which the storage layer automatically deletes the item.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为大二进制对象（图片、视频、附件）设计的存储服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage is an object store purpose-built for large binary files such as images, video, and attachments.

q: 「Chat Server 收下媒体再转存 blob 存储（30 天 TTL）」这个 Good 方案的遗留问题是？
q_en: What problem is left unsolved by the "Good" design where the Chat Server accepts media and forwards it to blob storage with a thirty-day TTL?
options: blob 存储比数据库更贵
Chat Server 仍要转发媒体，浪费一跳
无法生成预签名 URL
下载必须回源数据库
options_en: Blob storage is more expensive than a database
The Chat Server still has to forward every upload, a wasted hop
Pre-signed URLs cannot be generated this way
Downloads must still go back to the database
why: 转存方案解决了「别存数据库」，但媒体流量仍穿过 Chat Server；这一跳是纯浪费，于是引出预签名 URL 直传的 Great 方案。
why_en: The chat server still has to receive and forward every upload, a wasted hop that motivates letting clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为大二进制对象（图片、视频、附件）设计的存储服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage is an object store purpose-built for large binary files such as images, video, and attachments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带临时签名和有效期的 URL，持有者不用额外身份验证就能直接读写对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL carries a temporary signature and expiry that lets whoever holds it read or write an object store directly without further authentication.

scenario: 希望媒体上传完全不占用 Chat Server 带宽，同时只有获得授权的用户能上传和下载。
scenario_en: You want media uploads to consume zero Chat Server bandwidth, while only authorized users can upload or download.
q: 理想的附件方案是？
q_en: What is the ideal design for attachments here?
options: 客户端直传到公开可写的存储桶，谁都能上传下载
把媒体 base64 编码后走 WebSocket 消息，拖慢聊天连接
上传走 FTP、下载走 HTTP，缺现代认证和加密
客户端换预签名 URL 直传 blob 存储，消息里只带附件 URL，下载同样凭预签名 URL
options_en: Have the client upload directly to a publicly writable bucket that anyone can read or write
Base64-encode the media and send it as a WebSocket message, which slows down the chat connection
Upload over FTP and download over HTTP, lacking modern authentication and encryption
The client exchanges a call for a pre-signed URL and uploads straight to blob storage; the message carries only the attachment URL, and downloads use a pre-signed URL too
why: 预签名 URL 同时解决授权与带宽：Chat Server 只签发临时 URL 和保存附件元数据。blob 是最终文件；chunk/multipart 只是大文件直传时的分段上传方式。
why_en: Clients use pre-signed URLs to upload media bytes directly to object storage; chunking is only a multipart upload detail, not a different storage destination.
whenOtherWins: 若上传路径需要服务端处理（转码、病毒扫描、内容审核），让媒体先经过服务器反而有价值。
tradeoff: 客户端直传省 Chat Server 带宽 vs 经服务器中转换取服务端处理能力
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C[发送客户端] -->|1. getAttachmentTarget| CS[Chat Server]
    CS -->|2. 预签名 PUT URL| C
    C -->|3. 单次 PUT 或 multipart| B[(Blob/Object 存储\nTTL 30 天)]
    C -->|4. 消息只带 mediaId/objectKey| CS
    R[接收客户端] -->|5. 请求下载权限| CS
    CS -->|6. 预签名 GET URL| R
    R -->|7. 直连下载| B
codeSample:
# small file: one signed PUT URL
PUT /bucket/att/9f2

# large file: signed URLs per part, then complete multipart upload
PUT /bucket/att/9f2?partNumber=1&uploadId=...
PUT /bucket/att/9f2?partNumber=2&uploadId=...
POST /bucket/att/9f2?uploadId=... # complete

termDefinitions.meaning: 带临时签名和有效期的 URL，持有者不用额外身份验证就能直接读写对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL carries a temporary signature and expiry that lets whoever holds it read or write an object store directly without further authentication.

termDefinitions.meaning: Binary Large Object 存储：按 objectKey 存图片、视频、附件这类不透明字节对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage stores opaque byte objects such as images, videos, and attachments, addressed by an object key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大文件直传方式：客户端把同一个 blob 拆成多个 part 直传到对象存储，最后由存储服务合成一个对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multipart upload lets the client upload one large object as multiple parts directly to object storage, then complete them into one object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: 较老的文件传输协议，缺少现代认证和流式能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FTP is an older file-transfer protocol that lacks modern authentication and streaming support.

q: 为什么这里给 blob 存储前面加 CDN 的收益有限？
q_en: Why is the payoff of putting a CDN in front of blob storage limited here?
options: CDN 无法传输图片视频
每个附件最多被 100 人下载，缓存复用率太低
CDN 与 TTL 冲突
预签名 URL 不能配 CDN
options_en: A CDN cannot transfer images or video
Each attachment is downloaded by at most a hundred people, so cache reuse is too low
A CDN conflicts with TTL expiration
Pre-signed URLs cannot be paired with a CDN
why: CDN 的价值在「同一内容被海量用户重复拉取」；附件受众被 100 人上限封顶，命中复用少，加 CDN 属于低性价比。
why_en: Since at most one hundred participants will ever fetch an attachment, cache reuse is tiny and a CDN adds little value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点、就近返回的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers near users so it can be served locally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带临时签名和有效期的 URL，持有者不用额外身份验证就能直接读写对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL carries a temporary signature and expiry that lets whoever holds it read or write an object store directly without further authentication.

scenario: 在 WhatsApp 附件设计里，Chat Server 先鉴权，然后返回一个短期有效的预签名 URL。客户端拿这个 URL 直接把图片/视频上传到 blob 存储，下载时也从 blob 存储取，媒体字节不再经过 Chat Server。
scenario_en: In the WhatsApp attachment design, the Chat Server authorizes the request and returns a short-lived pre-signed URL. The client uploads images and video straight to blob storage with that URL, and downloads come from blob storage too, so media bytes never pass through the Chat Server.
q: 采用预签名 URL 直传附件后，哪些问题仍然没有自动解决？（多选）
q_en: After switching to direct pre-signed-URL uploads, which problems are still not automatically solved? (select all)
options: 如果想「所有接收者都下载完成后立刻删除附件」，还需要额外记录每个接收者的下载状态并触发删除
端到端加密、密钥分发、链接泄露后的访问控制等安全问题仍要额外设计
附件大小被限制在 1 MB 以内
媒体文件的上传字节流仍必须经过 Chat Server
options_en: If you want to delete the attachment immediately after every recipient downloads it, you still need per-recipient download tracking and a delete trigger
End-to-end encryption, key distribution, and access control after link leakage still need separate design
Attachment size is capped at 1 MB
The uploaded media bytes still have to pass through the Chat Server
why: 预签名 URL 只解决带宽和临时授权直连，不会自动追踪下载状态，也不会替你做端到端加密、密钥管理和权限收回。
why_en: A pre-signed URL only solves bandwidth and temporary authorization; it does not track downloads or handle encryption, key management, or revocation for you.
whenOtherWins: 如果附件必须先做服务端扫描、转码或合规审核，可以让上传先进入隔离区，再异步放行给接收者。
tradeoff: 预签名 URL 直传省带宽 vs 仍需独立设计生命周期和安全控制
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C[客户端] -->|请求上传权限| CS[Chat Server]
    CS -->|返回短期预签名 URL| C
    C -->|媒体字节直传| B[(Blob 存储)]
    B -->|TTL 到期自动删| X[默认过期]
    D[下载状态跟踪] -.额外设计.-> B
    K[加密和密钥管理] -.额外设计.-> C
optionMeanings: 选项在说生命周期：文件何时删、谁触发删。
选项在说安全模型：加密、访问、泄露后如何处理。
选项把问题定义成文件大小上限。
选项把问题定义成数据路径：字节是否仍经过 Chat Server。
optionScenarioImpacts: 全部收完即删需要额外记录每人下载状态并触发删除。
URL 泄露、密钥、加密、扫描都要另有机制。
预签名 URL 配合 multipart upload 能传大文件，不天然限于 1 MB。
Chat Server 只发 URL、存元数据，不再搬运媒体本体。
optionDirectness: 若要收完即删，必须补接收者级状态。
若要端到端保密或链接可撤销，必须另做。
只有单请求大小受限时才是问题；直传可分段。
只有媒体仍经 Chat Server 时才成立；直传已移走带宽。
optionMeanings_en: This option is about attachment lifecycle: when it is deleted and what triggers that.
This option is about the security model: encryption, access, and what happens after a leak.
This option frames the issue as a file-size limit.
This option frames the issue as a data-path question: do bytes still pass through the Chat Server.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Delete-after-all-downloads needs separate per-recipient download tracking and a delete trigger.
Link leakage, key exchange, encryption, and malware scanning all need separate mechanisms.
Pre-signed URLs paired with multipart upload can carry large files, not naturally capped at 1 MB.
The Chat Server only issues the URL and stores metadata; it no longer carries the media bytes.
optionDirectness_en: This matters when attachments must be deleted immediately after every recipient downloads them.
This matters when end-to-end secrecy, revocation, or link-leak handling is required.
This would matter only if the upload path still had a single-request size limit.
This would matter only if media bytes still flowed through the Chat Server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器用自己的存储凭证签出来的短期链接，客户端凭它直接上传或下载某个对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL is a short-lived link signed by the server with its storage credentials, letting the client upload or download one object directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储条目设置的存活期限，到期后由存储层自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TTL is an expiration time after which the storage layer automatically deletes the item.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有发送方和接收方能解密内容，服务器即使转发或存储也看不到明文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: End-to-end encryption means only the sender and recipients can decrypt the content; servers that relay or store it cannot read the plaintext.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为图片、视频、附件等大二进制对象设计的对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage is object storage designed for large binary objects such as images, videos, and attachments.

scenario: WhatsApp 级聊天应用有 10 亿注册用户。做容量估算时，先用「注册用户 × 同时在线比例」得到并发连接基数。
scenario_en: A WhatsApp-scale chat app has one billion registered users. Capacity estimation starts with registered users times the concurrent-online ratio to get the base connection count.
q: 按 20% 同时在线比例估算，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Estimating with a twenty-percent concurrent-online ratio, which conclusion does this most directly support?
options: 约 2000 万；服务器数量会被估小
约 10 亿；几乎所有注册用户都在线
约 2 亿；后续容量估算都以它为基数
无需估算；单机容量大就不看集群
options_en: About twenty million; server count would be underestimated
About one billion; almost every registered user is online
About two hundred million; later capacity estimates use it as the base
No estimate is needed if one host has high connection capacity
why: 估算标准：注册用户 × 同时在线比例。聊天应用可用 20% 粗估：10 亿 × 0.2 = 2 亿并发连接，再用它算服务器数、心跳量和轮询量。
why_en: Use registered users times the concurrent-online ratio; for chat, a rough 20% gives 1B × 0.2 = 200M connected users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时在线比例：某一时刻在线连接数占注册用户总数的粗略比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The concurrent-online ratio is the rough fraction of registered users connected at one moment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并发连接：同一时刻服务器需要同时维持的客户端连接数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concurrent connections are the client connections the servers must keep open at the same time.

scenario: WhatsApp 以单机（Erlang）可以撑住 100-200 万条 WebSocket 连接闻名，而同时在线连接数约 2 亿。
scenario_en: WhatsApp is famous for a single Erlang host holding one to two million WebSocket connections, while total concurrent connections are around two hundred million.
q: 把单机连接容量和总并发数放在一起看，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Putting per-host connection capacity next to total concurrency, which conclusion does that most directly support?
options: 单机容量被低估到 1-2 万，必须部署上万台服务器才够
单机能扛百万连接，但 2 亿并发仍需上百台服务器
单机连接容量足够大，2 亿并发只需要个位数台服务器
连接容量与服务器台数无关，只由带宽决定
options_en: Per-host capacity is underestimated at ten to twenty thousand, requiring tens of thousands of servers
Even at millions of connections per host, two hundred million concurrent users still needs hundreds of servers
Per-host capacity is large enough that a single-digit number of servers covers two hundred million users
Connection capacity has nothing to do with server count and is purely a function of bandwidth
why: WhatsApp 以单机 100-200 万连接闻名，但 2 亿并发还是要数百台服务器——「单机放不下」正是所有路由深挖的起点。
why_en: WhatsApp famously served one to two million connections per host, yet two hundred million concurrent users still demand hundreds of chat servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高并发、高容错设计的函数式编程语言，WhatsApp 早期靠它实现单机百万级连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Erlang is a functional programming language built for high concurrency and fault tolerance, which is how WhatsApp originally handled millions of connections per host.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

q: 「只往 L4 LB 后面加更多 Chat Server」这个天真方案为什么直接失败？
q_en: Why does the naive plan of just adding more Chat Servers behind an L4 load balancer fail outright?
options: LB 撑不住 WebSocket 握手
服务器未必持有接收者的连接，无法投递
服务器数量太多成本失控
DynamoDB 不支持多个写入者
options_en: The load balancer can't handle WebSocket handshakes
The server has no guarantee of holding the recipients' connections, so it cannot deliver
Too many servers make the cost spiral out of control
DynamoDB does not support multiple writers
optionMeanings: 把失败归到负载均衡器握手能力上。
把失败归到连接与服务器绑定、跨机器不可见上。
把失败归到服务器成本上。
把失败归到数据库写入限制上。
why: 连接只活在某台服务器的内存里；水平扩容后发送方和接收方大概率不在同一台，裸加机器根本无法投递。面试里千万别停在这一步。
why_en: A server that accepts a message has no guarantee of holding the recipients' connections, so naive horizontal scaling simply cannot deliver events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

scenario: 裸加 Chat Server 无法投递之后，一个常见的直觉方案是借助消息队列：为系统里的每个用户单独建一条队列 topic 当它的收件箱。
scenario_en: Once naively adding Chat Servers fails to deliver messages, a common instinct is to reach for a message queue: give every user in the system their own topic to act as their inbox.
q: 「每个用户一个 Kafka topic 当 Inbox」为什么行不通？
q_en: Why doesn't giving every user their own Kafka topic as an inbox work?
options: Kafka 不支持多消费者订阅
Kafka 无法持久化消息
topic 无法动态创建，这也不是这里的真正瓶颈
Kafka 不是为数十亿 topic 设计的，元数据开销太大
options_en: Kafka does not support multiple consumers on one topic
Kafka cannot persist messages
Topics cannot be created dynamically, but that is not the real bottleneck either
Kafka is not built for billions of topics; the metadata overhead is too large
optionMeanings: 把问题归因到消费者订阅模型。
把问题归因到持久化能力。
把问题归因到 topic 创建方式。
把问题归因到每个 topic 的固定元数据开销。
why: 很多候选人条件反射地掏队列，但 Kafka 每个 topic 都有量级 50KB 的开销，数十亿 topic 完全不现实；「super topic」聚合方案又等于蹩脚地重造 Pub/Sub。
why_en: Kafka is not built for billions of topics since each carries about fifty kilobytes of overhead, which alone would mean over fifty terabytes for a billion users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息持久化到磁盘、按 topic 组织、并维护消费者位点的分布式消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue that persists messages to disk, organizes them into topics, and tracks consumer offsets.

scenario: 想让「谁负责哪个用户」变成确定映射：按 userId 一致性哈希把用户固定分配到 Chat Server，服务器之间直连投递。
scenario_en: You want "which server owns which user" to be a deterministic mapping: consistent-hash users by userId onto a fixed Chat Server, and deliver via direct server-to-server connections.
q: 这个方案还需要什么配套基础设施？
q_en: What supporting infrastructure does this approach still require?
options: 中心注册表（ZooKeeper/etcd）记录哈希段归属
一个全局关系型数据库存路由，写入会成为瓶颈
客户端向全网广播自己的位置
DNS 泛解析到任意服务器
options_en: A central registry such as ZooKeeper or etcd recording which hash segments each server owns
A single global relational database storing routes, which becomes a write bottleneck
Clients broadcast their own location to the whole network
Wildcard DNS resolving to any server
why: 一致性哈希方案的核心配套是服务注册与哈希段分配（ZooKeeper/etcd）；连接请求按 userId 定位归属服务器，事件也直接发往「拥有」该用户的那台。
why_en: Consistent hashing needs a central registry like ZooKeeper or etcd that tracks each chat server's address and the hash ranges it owns.
whenOtherWins: 不想自己管理伸缩编排、能接受多一跳毫秒级延迟时，Redis Pub/Sub 更省心，也是文中评级更高的选择。
tradeoff: 服务器直连低时延 vs 自管路由编排（注册表、扩容迁移）的运维复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式协调服务，常用来做服务注册和配置的强一致存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a distributed coordination service commonly used for service registration and strongly consistent configuration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式强一致键值存储，常用于服务发现和配置管理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a strongly consistent distributed key-value store commonly used for service discovery and configuration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 和节点都映射到同一个哈希环上，节点增减时只影响环上相邻的一小段映射关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing places both keys and nodes on the same hash ring so adding or removing a node only reshuffles a small neighboring slice of the mapping.

q: 一致性哈希直连方案要付出哪些代价？（多选）
q_en: What costs does the consistent-hashing direct-connect approach pay? (select all)
options: 每台 Chat Server 都要与所有其他 Chat Server 保持连接，迫使服务器「个头大、数量少」
扩容 / 缩容要精细编排连接迁移，避免用户集体重连引发惊群
伸缩过渡期要向新旧两台服务器同时发送事件，防止丢消息
userId 从此不能再作数据库分区键
options_en: Every Chat Server must stay connected to every other Chat Server, forcing servers to be few and large
Scaling in or out requires carefully orchestrated connection draining to avoid a thundering herd
During a scaling transition, events must be sent to both the old and new owning server so nothing is lost
userId can no longer be used as a database partition key
why: 全网状互连 + 伸缩编排 + 过渡期双发，问题都可解，但面试官会期待你逐个讲清怎么解——所以它只评 Good 而非 Great。
why_en: Every server must connect to every other server, scaling requires careful connection draining to avoid a thundering herd, and events must go to both owners during transitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量客户端因同一事件在同一时刻集体重连或重试，瞬间打垮后端的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thundering herd happens when a huge number of clients reconnect or retry at the same instant and overwhelm the backend.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行数据被分配到哪个物理分区的键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which physical partition a row of data lands on.

scenario: 上百台 Chat Server 之间要互相转发消息，接收者可能连在任何一台上；希望用现成的轻量组件专门做服务器间的消息中转。
scenario_en: Hundreds of Chat Servers need to forward messages to each other since a recipient could be connected to any of them; you want an off-the-shelf lightweight component dedicated to that inter-server relay.
q: 文中评为最优（Great）的方案是？
q_en: Which approach does the article rate as the best ("Great") solution?
options: RabbitMQ 配死信队列
每用户一个 Kafka topic
Redis Pub/Sub：按 userId 建频道做服务器间转发
Chat Server 之间 gRPC 全网状广播
options_en: RabbitMQ with a dead-letter queue
One Kafka topic per user
Redis Pub/Sub: build a channel per userId for inter-server forwarding
A full mesh of gRPC calls between all Chat Servers
optionMeanings: 带死信队列的消息队列中间件。
为每用户建一条持久化 topic。
按 userId 建频道的轻量转发服务。
服务器间点对点全网状 RPC 广播。
why: Redis Pub/Sub 用极轻的 socket 映射在服务器之间摆渡消息：订阅该用户频道的服务器收到发布后转发进 WebSocket，专器专用。
why_en: Redis Pub/Sub is purpose-built for bouncing messages between servers, using lightweight per-user channels that subscribing chat servers forward into their sockets.
whenOtherWins: 不愿新增 Redis 依赖、且团队能驾驭连接编排时，一致性哈希直连也可行，还省掉经 Redis 的一跳延迟。
tradeoff: 专用轻量转发（Pub/Sub）vs 自建一致性哈希直连路由的运维成本
diagram:
graph LR
    Sender --> ServerA[Chat server A]
    ServerA --> DB[(Durable message store)]
    ServerA --> PubSub[Redis Pub/Sub by user]
    PubSub --> ServerB[Chat server B]
    ServerB --> Recipient

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持多种路由模式的消息队列中间件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RabbitMQ is a message-queue broker that supports several routing patterns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息持久化到磁盘、按 topic 组织、并维护消费者位点的分布式消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue that persists messages to disk, organizes them into topics, and tracks consumer offsets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP/2 的高性能二进制 RPC 框架，常用于服务间通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a high-performance binary RPC framework built on HTTP/2, commonly used for service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 和节点都映射到同一个哈希环上，节点增减时只影响环上相邻的一小段映射关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing places both keys and nodes on the same hash ring so adding or removing a node only reshuffles a small neighboring slice of the mapping.

scenario: 上百台 Chat Server 要互相转发消息；候选方案是继续沿用消息队列 Kafka，或者换成专门做转发的 Redis Pub/Sub。
scenario_en: Hundreds of Chat Servers need to forward messages to each other; the candidates are sticking with the Kafka message queue or switching to Redis Pub/Sub, which is purpose-built for relaying.
q: 在「每个 topic / 频道的开销」维度上，Kafka 与 Redis Pub/Sub 的关键区别是？
q_en: On the dimension of per-topic or per-channel overhead, what is the key difference between Kafka and Redis Pub/Sub?
options: 两者都要为每个频道写磁盘，持久化成本一样高
Kafka 的 topic 更轻量
Redis Pub/Sub 也要维护消费位点
Kafka 落盘且维护 offset，开销大；Pub/Sub 只是内存指针
options_en: Both must write to disk for every channel, so persistence cost is the same
Kafka topics are actually the lighter-weight option
Redis Pub/Sub also has to track a consumer offset
Kafka persists to disk and tracks offsets, carrying real overhead; Pub/Sub is just an in-memory pointer
optionMeanings: 认为两者磁盘开销一样。
把两者轻重关系说反。
认为 Pub/Sub 也要维护消费位点。
区分持久化落盘和内存指针转发。
why: 同样是发布订阅，Kafka 为持久化与位点付出高昂的 per-topic 成本；Redis Pub/Sub 不管存储、只转发，所以能撑住海量频道。
why_en: Kafka persists messages and tracks consumer offsets per topic, while Redis Pub/Sub channels are just in-memory pointers to subscriber connections with no storage at all.
tradeoff: Pub/Sub 轻量不持久化 vs Kafka 持久化带来的强投递保证

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息持久化到磁盘、按 topic 组织、并维护消费者位点的分布式消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue that persists messages to disk, organizes them into topics, and tracks consumer offsets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

q: Redis Pub/Sub 的投递语义是？
q_en: What is Redis Pub/Sub's delivery guarantee?
options: at-most-once：无人订阅或故障时消息就丢了
exactly-once，绝不重复也绝不丢
at-least-once，可能重复
全局有序且必达
options_en: At-most-once: the message is lost if no subscriber is listening or Redis fails
Exactly-once, never duplicated and never lost
At-least-once, may be duplicated
Globally ordered and guaranteed delivery
why: Pub/Sub 不保证送达：无人订阅或瞬断即丢。单看这点像缺陷，但配合「先持久化后发布」的写路径，它恰好只承担尽力而为的实时通道。
why_en: Redis Pub/Sub is at-most-once, so a message is simply lost if no subscriber is listening or Redis hiccups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种投递语义：消息最多送达一次，可能因故障直接丢失，但绝不会重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-most-once delivery means a message is delivered zero or one time; it can be lost on failure but is never duplicated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种投递语义：消息至少送达一次，可能重复，但不会凭空丢失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery guarantees a message arrives one or more times; it may duplicate but never silently disappears.

q: Pub/Sub 可能丢消息，为什么系统整体仍能保证必达？
q_en: Pub/Sub can drop messages, so why does the system as a whole still guarantee delivery?
options: Redis 会对失败的发布自动重试
客户端每次都重发全部消息
先持久化写 Message/Inbox，再尽力而为发布
负载均衡器会缓存未送达的消息
options_en: Redis automatically retries failed publishes
The client resends every message every time
The message is durably written to Message and Inbox before the best-effort publish
The load balancer caches undelivered messages
why: 顺序是命门：持久化在前、发布在后，实时通道再不可靠也只是「晚到」，不会「丢失」。这一行字撑起了整个可靠性论证。
why_en: Because messages are durably written to the message and inbox tables before publishing, a dropped pub/sub message is recovered on reconnect or by polling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

q: 补全发消息的写路径顺序：
q_en: Fill in the order of the write path for sending a message:
text: 写路径：1) 持久化写 {{Message}} 表并创建 {{Inbox}} 条目 → 2) 向发送者返回{{成功}} → 3) 发布到 {{Pub/Sub}} 做尽力而为的实时投递。
why: 先落库、再应答、最后发布——这个顺序保证了 at-most-once 的实时通道不会危及必达承诺。
why_en: The write path durably stores the message and inbox entries, returns success to the sender, and only then publishes to pub/sub for best-effort delivery.
diagram:
graph LR
    Send[sendMessage] --> Persist[Persist message]
    Persist --> Inbox[Write recipient inbox]
    Inbox --> Publish[Publish to recipient channel]
    Publish --> Deliver[Online server delivers]
    Deliver --> Ack[Client ack]

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

q: 用户连上某台 Chat Server 后，这台服务器要做什么才能收到发给该用户的消息？
q_en: Once a user connects to a Chat Server, what must that server do to receive messages addressed to them?
options: 把用户写进全局路由数据库
订阅该 userId 频道，转发进 WebSocket
定时轮询该用户的 Inbox
广播通知所有其他 Chat Server
options_en: Write the user into a global routing database
Subscribe to that userId channel and forward into the WebSocket
Poll that user's Inbox on a timer
Broadcast a notification to every other Chat Server
why: 连接建立 → 服务器代订该用户频道；任何服务器要送消息给他，只需向这个频道发布，由订阅方转发到 socket。
why_en: On connection the chat server subscribes to that user's pub/sub channel and forwards anything received on it into the WebSocket.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。

q: 单个 Redis 实例撑不下全部 Pub/Sub 流量时怎么扩？
q_en: How do you scale out when a single Redis instance can't handle all the Pub/Sub traffic?
options: 换回 Kafka
垂直扩容加内存
按 userId 分片到多个 Redis 实例
不需要扩，单实例永远够用
options_en: Switch back to Kafka
Vertically scale by adding more memory
Shard by userId across multiple Redis instances
No scaling needed, one instance is always enough
optionMeanings: 换回持久化消息队列。
单实例垂直加内存。
按 key 把频道横向分片到多实例。
认为规模不会增长。
why: 实践中不会把所有 pub/sub 压到一台 Redis：按 userId 分区频道、横向铺一组实例，每台各管一片。
why_en: In practice you shard pub/sub across a cluster of Redis instances, partitioning channels by user id so each node handles a fraction of them.

q_en: Which conclusion does that benchmark number most directly support?
options: 单台 Redis 每秒撑死也就 1000 条，说明 Pub/Sub 完全不适合这个场景
要达到这个吞吐必须堆上百台 Redis，成本高到不现实
单台 Redis 实测约 10 万条/秒只用 27% 资源，说明 Pub/Sub 天然高吞吐

options_en: A single Redis host tops out at about one thousand updates a second, so Pub/Sub is unsuitable for this case
Hitting this throughput requires stacking up hundreds of Redis instances, too costly to be realistic
A single Redis host forwarded about a hundred thousand updates a second at only 27% utilization, showing pub/sub is naturally high-throughput

why: Pub/Sub「够不够快」有实证：Canva 单机 10 万条/秒只用了 27% 资源；它只做转发不管存储，所以能这么高效。
why_en: Canva benchmarked one hundred thousand pub/sub updates per second on a single Redis host at only twenty-seven percent utilization, because pub/sub just passes messages without persisting them.
