内存占用暴涨，单机撑不住集群规模
无法与 TLS 共存，安全性明显下降
经 Redis 多一跳，增加个位数毫秒延迟
options_en: Messages must be written to disk twice, slowing writes noticeably
Memory usage explodes, more than a single host can hold at cluster scale
It cannot coexist with TLS, clearly weakening security
Every message takes one extra hop through Redis, adding single-digit-millisecond latency
why: 没有免费的路由：多一跳就多几毫秒，外加 Chat Server 与 Redis 集群之间的连接网格——但这两个代价都在可控范围。
why_en: Ferrying messages through Redis adds single-digit milliseconds of latency plus a manageable mesh of connections between chat servers and the Redis cluster.

q_en: Put the decision chain for "how message routing scales to hundreds of millions of connections" into the correct order:
steps: 选型：Redis Pub/Sub，按 userId 建频道做服务器间转发
需求：数十亿用户、约 2 亿并发连接，收发双方常连在不同 Chat Server
缓解：发布前先持久化写 Inbox / Message，再用心跳 + 序号 + 轮询补漏
代价：at-most-once 可能丢推送，且经 Redis 多一跳毫秒级延迟
排除：裸加 LB 无法保证持有接收者连接；每用户 Kafka topic 元数据开销爆炸
why: 需求 → 排除坏方案 → 选型 → 代价 → 缓解。能把这条链讲顺，就是这道题深挖部分的主线得分点。
why_en: The chain runs from hundreds of millions of connections, through rejecting naive load balancing and per-user Kafka topics, to Redis Pub/Sub, its at-most-once cost, and the durable-write-first mitigation.
tradeoff: 服务器间路由的时延成本 vs 自建路由的运维复杂度

q: 假设人均 250 个 1:1 会话：Pub/Sub 按 chat 分区与按 user 分区，订阅开销怎么比？
q_en: With about 250 one-on-one chats per user, how does subscription overhead compare between chat-level and user-level Pub/Sub partitioning?
options: 两种方式开销相同
chat 分区每人订 250 个；user 分区订 1 个
按 chat 只需 1 个订阅，更优
按 user 需要 250 个订阅，更差
options_en: The two approaches have identical overhead
Chat-level needs 250 subscriptions per person; user-level needs just one
Partition by chat needs only 1 subscription, so it is better
Partition by user needs 250 subscriptions, so it is worse
why: 1:1 主导时，按 chat 分区意味着每个在线用户拖着 250 个订阅；按 user 分区 1 人 1 频道 1 订阅，发布时也只发 1 个频道。
why_en: With two hundred fifty one-on-one chats per user, chat-level channels force two hundred fifty subscriptions per user while user-level channels need exactly one.
tradeoff: 按 user 分区精简订阅数 vs 按 chat 分区精简发布次数

q: 100 人大群里发一条消息：两种分区的发布开销怎么比？
q_en: For one message in a hundred-person group, how does the publish cost compare between the two partitioning schemes?
options: user 分区发布 99 次；chat 分区 1 次
两者都只发布 1 次
按 chat 分区要发布 100 次
发布开销与分区方式无关
options_en: User-level publishes 99 times; chat-level needs 1
Both approaches publish exactly once
Partition by chat needs 100 publishes
Publish cost has nothing to do with the partitioning scheme
why: 大群翻转了结论：按 user 每条消息放大成 99 次发布，按 chat 只要 1 次。分区选择取决于会话数量与会话规模的分布。
why_en: In a hundred-person group a user-partitioned scheme publishes ninety-nine times per message while a chat-partitioned scheme publishes once.
tradeoff: 按 chat 分区精简发布次数 vs 按 user 分区精简订阅数

scenario: WhatsApp 的流量以 1:1 会话为绝对主体，群上限也被刻意压在 100 人。
scenario_en: WhatsApp's traffic is overwhelmingly one-on-one, and the group cap is deliberately kept at 100.
q: Pub/Sub 频道最终应该按什么分区？
q_en: How should Pub/Sub channels ultimately be partitioned?
options: 按地理区域
按会话（chat）
按设备（client）
按用户（user）：每人 1 频道 1 订阅
options_en: By geographic region
By chat
By client device
By user: one channel and one subscription per person
why: 分区跟着流量形态走：1:1 主导 + 群上限 100，按 user 分区订阅最省、发布可控，是本题的正确答案。
why_en: Because WhatsApp is dominated by one-on-one chats with a hard hundred-member cap, partitioning channels by user is the right call.
whenOtherWins: 以大群为主的产品（Slack 频道、Discord 服务器）里按 chat 分区更划算——一次群发从 99 次发布降到 1 次。
tradeoff: 订阅开销最小化（1:1 主导）vs 发布开销最小化（大群主导）

q: 面向高级候选人的解法是？
q_en: What solution should a senior candidate propose here?
options: 直接禁止创建大群
自适应分区：大群改用群级频道，切换期双发防丢
大群消息降级为客户端轮询
把大群拆成多个 25 人小群
options_en: Simply forbid creating large groups
Adaptively repartition: large chats switch to a chat-level channel, publishing to both during the crossover
Downgrade large-group messages to client polling
Split every large group into multiple 25-person groups
why: 按群大小自适应切换分区策略：小群走用户频道、大群走群频道；切换期给服务器留出订阅时间、双发防丢——边缘情况要单独讲清。
why_en: Adaptively partition by chat for groups above a size threshold, having users subscribe to those chat channels, and publish to both channels briefly when a group crosses the threshold.
whenOtherWins: 若群规模上限低且分布均匀，固定按 user 分区就够了——不值得为不存在的边缘情况引入自适应切换的复杂度。
tradeoff: 固定分区的实现简单 vs 自适应切换覆盖大群长尾的额外复杂度

options: Pub/Sub 频道必须从 userId 改成 clientId
新增 Clients 表，按 userId 记录设备
Inbox 从按 user 改为按 client——每台设备一份未投递队列
查会话参与者之后还要展开查每人的全部客户端，把消息投递到所有客户端
options_en: Pub/Sub channels must switch from userId to clientId
Add a Clients table keyed by userId to track devices
Inbox moves from per-user to per-client — every device gets its own undelivered-message queue
After looking up chat participants, also expand to each participant's full device list and deliver to every device
why: 多设备 = Clients 表 + 按 client 的 Inbox + 投递展开到每台设备；唯独 Pub/Sub 不用动，服务器仍订 userId 频道再本地分发。
why_en: Multi-device support adds a clients table, a per-client inbox, and fan-out of every message to all of a user's clients, while pub/sub stays keyed by user id.

q_en: After the multi-device change, what needs to change on the Pub/Sub side?
options: 不用改：仍订 userId 频道，本地分发到各设备
频道全部改为 clientId
改为按 chat 分区
换成持久化队列
options_en: Nothing changes: still subscribe by userId and fan out locally to each device
All channels switch to clientId
Switch to partitioning by chat
Replace it with a durable queue
why: 分发到设备发生在 Chat Server 内部（它知道该用户本机有哪些连接），所以 Pub/Sub 维持 userId 粒度即可——好设计的改动面就该这么小。
why_en: Nothing changes on the pub/sub side because servers still subscribe by user id and fan out to that user's device connections locally.

scenario_en: Once the Inbox moves from per-user to per-client, every message's storage and delivery cost scales with the device count.
q: 限制每账号客户端数量这个决定，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Which conclusion does the decision to cap clients per account most directly support?
options: 不限制客户端数量，体验优先，反正 DynamoDB 存储便宜
限制在约 3 个客户端/账号——写放大和存储都随设备数线性增长，必须封顶避免失控
限制在 100 个客户端，和群聊人数上限对齐才统一
客户端数量与存储成本无关，不需要设限
options_en: Do not cap client count at all, prioritize experience since DynamoDB storage is cheap
Cap it at about three clients per account — write and storage amplification grow linearly with device count, so it must be capped to stay under control
Cap it at one hundred clients, matching the group participant limit for consistency
Client count has nothing to do with storage cost, so no cap is needed
optionDirectness: 只有每个账号设备数很小且有硬配额监控时，不设产品上限才可控。
当每台设备都有独立收件箱和投递状态时，低个位数上限能控制写放大。
只有客户端设备数也按群成员那套扇出模型计算时，才有理由对齐 100。
只有收件箱仍按 user 存一份时，客户端数量才不会直接放大存储。
why: Inbox 按 client 之后，写放大与存储随设备数线性增长；限 3 台是在功能与成本之间画的一条线，同时还需要停用机制清理已不存在的客户端。
why_en: Capping accounts at about three clients keeps the per-device storage and delivery amplification from blowing up.

q: 多设备场景下继续用「按 user 的 Inbox」会发生什么？
q_en: What goes wrong if you keep a per-user Inbox in a multi-device world?
options: 写入吞吐立即翻倍
Redis 频道数爆炸
手机 ack 后条目被删，离线设备收不到
群聊功能整体不可用
options_en: Write throughput instantly doubles
The number of Redis channels explodes
Once the phone acks, the entry is deleted, so an offline device never receives it
Group chat stops working entirely
why: 按 user 的 Inbox 只有一份送达状态：任一设备 ack 就删，其他设备从此漏消息。这正是 Inbox 必须降到 client 粒度的原因。
why_en: With a per-user inbox, one device's acknowledgment deletes the entry, so a laptop that was off never receives those messages.

scenario: 要比较「发现一条已经死掉的连接」有多快：什么都不做只等 TCP 自己超时，和加一层应用层心跳。
scenario_en: Compare how fast you can notice a dead connection: doing nothing and waiting for plain TCP to time out, versus adding an application-level heartbeat.
q: 在「发现死连接的速度」上，裸 TCP keepalive 与应用层机制的差别是？
q_en: On the speed of detecting a dead connection, how does bare TCP keepalive compare to an application-level mechanism?
options: TCP keepalive 分钟级；心跳秒级
两者速度相当
TCP keepalive 是毫秒级，更快
应用层心跳反而更慢
options_en: TCP keepalive is minute-scale; a heartbeat is second-scale
The two approaches detect failures at about the same speed
TCP keepalive is millisecond-scale, so it is actually faster
Application-level heartbeats are actually slower
optionMeanings: TCP 层被动超时检测死连接。
认为两种机制速度一样。
误以为 TCP keepalive 是毫秒级。
误以为应用层心跳反而更慢。
why: 弱网下 socket 名义上开着、实际已死；TCP 层面要几分钟才能发现，「什么都不做」对实时聊天不可接受。
why_en: TCP keepalives often take minutes to notice a dead connection, far too slow for chat, while application-level heartbeats detect it within seconds.
tradeoff: 检测速度（心跳秒级）vs 额外的探测开销

rows: 投递 ACK 超时重试

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序送达的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测包，用来确认对方仍然存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small probe message sent at a fixed interval to confirm the other side of a connection is still alive.

scenario: 希望在给用户投递消息的当口就能发现 WebSocket 已经悄悄死掉，并且尽量复用现有机制。
scenario_en: You want to notice a silently dead WebSocket right when you try to deliver a message to the user, reusing as much of the existing machinery as possible.
q: 与现有 ack 机制自然搭配的做法是？
q_en: What approach pairs naturally with the existing ack mechanism?
options: 等 TCP 自己超时关闭，分钟级才能发现死连接
每条消息盲发两遍，靠冗余掩盖丢包
投递后等客户端 ACK，短超时内没等到就重试，几次失败后断开逼客户端重连同步
把所有弱网用户降级为轮询，牺牲了所有人的实时性
options_en: Wait for TCP to time out and close on its own, which only detects failure on a minute scale
Blindly send every message twice, masking loss with redundancy
Wait for the client ACK after delivery, retry on a short timeout, and close after repeated failures so the client reconnects and syncs
Downgrade every user on a weak network to polling, sacrificing real-time delivery for everyone
optionMeanings: 什么都不做，交给 TCP 自己超时。
对每条消息都盲目重复发送。
投递后等 ACK，超时重试、屡败断开。
把所有弱网用户整体降级为轮询。
why: 客户端 ack 本来就要发（用于清 Inbox），服务器只需加一个投递超时判定：超时重试、屡败断开。改动小、语义顺。
why_en: The server waits for the client acknowledgment after each delivery, retries on a short timeout, and closes the socket after repeated failures so the client reconnects and syncs.
whenOtherWins: 要在「安静期」也能发现死连接，必须再加周期性心跳——仅靠投递 ACK 只有在有消息可发时才起作用。
tradeoff: 复用现有 ACK 机制、实现成本低 vs 只有发消息时才能探测的安静期盲区

q: 「只靠投递 ACK 超时」检测死连接的盲区是？
q_en: What is the blind spot of detecting dead connections purely from delivery ACK timeouts?
options: ACK 报文太大浪费带宽
会频繁误杀健康连接
服务器内存不够存定时器
安静期挂掉时发现不了，要等下条消息才暴露
options_en: The ACK payload is too large and wastes bandwidth
It frequently kills healthy connections by mistake
The server does not have enough memory for timers
A connection that dies during a quiet period goes unnoticed until the next message
why: 投递超时是「被动」检测：没有消息就没有探测。真正的时间上界要靠主动心跳来给。
why_en: Delivery-based detection only works while sending, so a connection that dies during a quiet period goes unnoticed until the next message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the confirmation signal a client sends back after receiving a message.

scenario: 需要给死连接检测一个有保证的时间上界，即使会话完全安静也能触发。
scenario_en: You need a guaranteed upper bound on dead-connection detection time, one that still fires even if the conversation is completely silent.
q: 标准方案是？
q_en: What is the standard solution?
options: 服务器定时 ping，超时不回 pong 即断开
每分钟强制重建所有连接
客户端每秒上报一次状态全量
依赖运营商网络事件通知
options_en: The server pings on a timer, and a missed pong closes it
Force-rebuild every connection once a minute
The client reports its full state every second
Rely on carrier network failure notifications
why: 主动心跳把检测从「等消息」变成「定时探测」：死连接在秒级被发现并关闭，重连 + Inbox 同步兜住不漏消息。
why_en: The server pings every ten to thirty seconds and closes the connection if no pong arrives within about five seconds, catching dead sockets within seconds.
whenOtherWins: 如果能接受「只在发消息时才发现死连接」的弱实时场景，仅用投递 ACK 超时可以省掉这份心跳流量。
tradeoff: 有保证的检测时间上界 vs 心跳带来的额外探测流量

graph LR

scenario: 心跳间隔设为 10 秒、pong 超时设为 5 秒。
scenario_en: The heartbeat interval is set to ten seconds and the pong timeout to five seconds.
q: 补全心跳检测上界的算式：
q_en: Fill in the formula for the heartbeat detection upper bound:
text: 心跳间隔 {{10}} 秒、pong 超时 {{5}} 秒时，任何死连接最迟 {{15}} 秒内被发现——心跳给出的是检测时间的保证上界。
why: 上界 = 间隔 + 超时。这句「10 + 5 = 15 秒内必被发现」是面试里量化心跳价值的标准表述。
why_en: With a ten-second heartbeat interval and a five-second timeout, any dead connection is detected within fifteen seconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测包，用来确认对方仍然存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small probe message sent at a fixed interval to confirm the other side of a connection is still alive.

scenario: 2 亿在线用户，心跳间隔设为 10 秒。
scenario_en: There are two hundred million online users, with a ten-second heartbeat interval.
q: 由此算出的 ping/pong 交换量级，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Which conclusion does the resulting ping/pong exchange rate most directly support?
options: 算下来约 20 亿次/秒，远超任何基础设施能承受的范围，心跳机制不可行
算下来小到可以忽略，不需要为心跳做任何容量规划
这个量级只取决于消息大小，与在线用户数无关
算下来约 2000 万次/秒——量大但每条都是几字节的小消息，实践中可以接受
options_en: It comes out to about two billion a second, far beyond what any infrastructure could bear, making heartbeats infeasible
It comes out small enough to ignore entirely, no capacity planning needed for heartbeats
The figure depends only on message size, not on the number of online users
It comes out to about twenty million a second — a big number, but each message is only a few bytes, which is acceptable in practice
why: 200M / 10s = 2000 万次/秒的 ping/pong。说出这个数字并解释「消息极小所以没问题」，比回避它更加分。
why_en: Two hundred million connections on a ten-second interval means about twenty million tiny ping-pong exchanges per second, which is acceptable in practice.

scenario: Pub/Sub 尽力而为可能漏推，需要给已连接客户端一个最朴素的兜底手段拿回漏掉的消息。
scenario_en: Pub/Sub's best-effort delivery can drop a push; connected clients need the simplest possible backstop for recovering a missed message.
q: 这个兜底方案是？
q_en: What is that backstop mechanism?
options: 客户端重启即可
直接信任 Pub/Sub 不会丢
客户端定时发 sync 请求，服务器补发未投递消息
每天凌晨做一次全量同步
options_en: Just have the client restart
Trust Pub/Sub not to drop anything
Clients periodically send a sync request and the server pushes undelivered messages
Run one full sync for everyone at midnight
why: 周期轮询「查 Inbox 补漏」永远有效但代价线性：间隔就是延迟与负载之间的可调旋钮，多数场景「够用」。
why_en: Connected clients periodically send a sync request every thirty to sixty seconds and the server pushes down any undelivered inbox messages.
whenOtherWins: 想要秒级发现丢失得靠序号 + 心跳组合；轮询间隔越短负载越高，它更适合当最后一道防线。
tradeoff: 轮询兜底覆盖全场景 vs 轮询间隔在延迟与负载之间的取舍

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。

scenario: 2 亿在线用户，如果都采用每 30 秒一次的 sync 轮询兜底。
scenario_en: Two hundred million online users all use a thirty-second sync-polling backstop.
q: 由此算出的轮询负载量级，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Which conclusion does the resulting polling load most directly support?
options: 算下来只有约 7 千次查询/秒，负载小到可以把轮询直接当主力投递机制
算下来约 700 万次查询/秒——纯轮询只能当兜底，不能当实时投递的主力；拉长间隔能降载但要用延迟换
算下来约 7 亿次查询/秒，说明这个方案在任何规模下都不可行
算出来的负载与在线用户数无关，只取决于消息大小
options_en: It comes out to only about seven thousand queries a second, small enough to make polling the primary delivery mechanism
It comes out to about seven million queries a second — pure polling can only be a backstop, not the primary delivery path; a longer interval cuts load at the cost of latency
It comes out to about seven hundred million queries a second, meaning this approach is infeasible at any scale
The resulting load has nothing to do with the number of online users, only message size
why: 200M / 30s ≈ 700 万 QPS，全是「查一下有没有漏」的开销。这正是纯轮询只能做兜底、不能做主力的原因。
why_en: Two hundred million clients polling every thirty seconds adds about seven million sync queries per second, trading load against latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询/请求数，用来衡量系统吞吐的常用单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS measures how many queries or requests a system handles each second.

q: 每个 chat 一个单调递增序号，客户端如何用它发现漏消息？
q_en: With one monotonically increasing sequence number per chat, how does the client use it to detect a missed message?
options: 序号用于端到端加密，和漏消息无关
序号驱动 UI 排序动画，纯展示层用途
服务器按序号做负载均衡，与客户端无关
客户端记本地最后序号，跳号即知有漏，立刻请求重新同步
options_en: The sequence number is used for end-to-end encryption, unrelated to missed messages
The sequence number drives the UI's sort animation, a display-only use
The server load-balances using the sequence number, unrelated to the client
The client remembers its last local sequence number; a gap in numbering reveals a miss and triggers an immediate resync
why: 序号让「丢失」变得可观测：缺口即证据。生成端用 Redis INCR 这类原子自增即可，成本极低。
why_en: Clients track the last sequence number seen, so receiving number five right after three reveals the missing four and triggers a resync.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条消息带的单调递增编号，客户端靠比对编号发现是否漏收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number is a monotonically increasing id on each message that lets a client spot gaps by comparing numbers.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令，单步完成「读取当前值并加一」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is a Redis command that atomically reads a counter and increments it in a single step.

q: 「靠序号缺口发现丢失」这个机制的固有局限是？
q_en: What is the inherent limitation of detecting loss purely from sequence-number gaps?
options: 序号很快就会溢出
INCR 不是原子操作
缺口要等下条消息才能发现，安静期会一直漏
客户端无法持久化序号
options_en: Sequence numbers will overflow quickly
INCR is not actually atomic
A gap is only detectable when another message arrives, so silence hides it
Clients cannot persist a sequence number
why: 缺口检测是被动的：没有下一条消息就没有对照物。这个局限直接引出「把序号捎带进心跳」的组合方案。
why_en: Gap detection only fires when another message arrives, so a miss followed by silence goes undetected and polling is still needed as a backstop.

scenario: 想在几乎不新增负载的前提下，把漏推检测的时间压进一个心跳周期。
scenario_en: You want to compress missed-push detection time down to roughly one heartbeat interval while adding almost no extra load.
q: 文中的组合方案是？
q_en: What is the article's combined solution?
options: 把心跳间隔缩短到 1 秒
维护每用户全局序号，捎带在心跳 ping 里发现落后
让 Redis Pub/Sub 升级成 at-least-once
取消轮询、全信心跳
options_en: Shorten the heartbeat interval to 1 second
Keep one global sequence per user and piggyback it on heartbeat pings to detect lag
Upgrade Redis Pub/Sub to at-least-once delivery
Drop polling entirely and trust heartbeats alone
why: 心跳反正要发，捎带一个数字近乎零成本；一个全局用户序号能覆盖该用户所有会话的丢失。代价是需要原子计数器这个额外依赖。
why_en: Keep a single incrementing sequence per user and piggyback it on each heartbeat ping so clients detect any missed message within one heartbeat interval.
whenOtherWins: 没有心跳基础设施、或不想为原子计数器加依赖时，单纯拉长间隔的轮询更简单，只是发现丢失更慢。
tradeoff: 心跳捎带序号，近零额外成本 vs 引入原子计数器这个新依赖

scenario: 要为每个用户维护全局单调递增的消息序号（发往该用户的每条消息 +1），用于漏消息检测，且并发下不能出错。
scenario_en: You need a globally monotonically increasing message sequence number per user (incremented for every message sent to them) for miss detection, and it must be correct under concurrency.
q: 用哪条 Redis 命令原子地生成下一个序号？
q_en: Which Redis command atomically generates the next sequence number?
options: GET seq:user:123 之后再 SET 加一
INCR seq:user:123
EXPIRE seq:user:123 60
PUBLISH seq:user:123 next
options_en: GET seq:user:123 and then SET it plus one
INCR seq:user:123
EXPIRE seq:user:123 60
PUBLISH seq:user:123 next
why: GET 再 SET 是两步读改写，会在并发下产生相同序号；INCR 在 Redis 单线程内一步完成自增并返回新值，天然原子。
why_en: INCR atomically increments and returns the counter in a single step, whereas a separate get and set race under concurrency.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要会话内定序，可按 chat 计数（INCR seq:chat:456）；全局用户序号的优势是一个数字覆盖该用户所有会话的丢失检测。
tradeoff: INCR 单步原子自增 vs GET+SET 两步读改写的竞态风险

INCR seq:user:123    # 原子自增，返回新序号

# 客户端对比本地值，落后即请求同步

q: 生产系统实践中通常怎样组合可靠投递的三种机制？
q_en: How do production systems typically combine the three reliable-delivery mechanisms?
options: 只用轮询，简单可靠
只用心跳即可覆盖一切
三者互补：心跳测连接，序号测漏消息，轮询兜底
只用序号，其余多余
options_en: Use polling alone, it is simple and reliable
Heartbeats alone cover everything
The three complement each other: heartbeats catch dead sockets, sequence numbers catch drops, polling backstops
Use sequence numbers alone, the rest is redundant
why: 三种机制针对三类故障，缺一角就留一个盲区：连接死了靠心跳、消息漏了靠序号、以上都失灵还有轮询。
why_en: Production systems combine heartbeats to catch dead connections, sequence numbers to catch missed messages, and periodic polling as the final backstop.

scenario: 分布式系统里消息乱序不可避免；聊天用户更在乎「新消息尽快出现」而不是严格的全局顺序。
scenario_en: Out-of-order messages are unavoidable in a distributed system; chat users care more about seeing new messages fast than about strict global ordering.
q: 对乱序消息，文中的态度是？
q_en: What is the article's stance on out-of-order messages?
options: 不做严格重排，直接按服务器时间戳展示
用向量时钟实现全序广播
所有消息经单一队列串行化
统一延迟 5 秒再排序显示
options_en: Do not strictly reorder; just display by the server-received timestamp
Use vector clocks for total-order broadcast
Serialize every message through a single queue
Uniformly delay display by 5 seconds to let reordering happen
why: 严格保序要付出延迟与重排机制的复杂度，而聊天用户宁要快不要序——产品需求决定了不值得做。
why_en: The design deliberately does not enforce strict ordering because chat users prefer seeing new messages fast over guaranteed order.
whenOtherWins: 必须按事件时间严格处理的流计算才值得等迟到数据——如 Flink 的有界乱序水位线策略，先等待再处理。
tradeoff: 展示速度优先 vs 严格全局顺序需要的等待与重排复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台服务器把时钟对齐到同一参考时间的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes server clocks to a shared reference time.

scenario: 所有 Chat Server 需要给消息一个统一、可复现的展示顺序，即使到达顺序不同。
scenario_en: Every Chat Server needs to give messages one consistent, reproducible display order, even when they arrive in a different order.
q: 补全消息排序的实际做法：
q_en: Fill in the actual approach to message ordering:
text: 所有 Chat Server 经 {{NTP}} 同步时钟；消息到达时盖上{{服务器接收}}时间戳，客户端一律按此时间戳排序展示，从而让所有客户端看到{{一致}}的顺序。
why: NTP 不保证完美时钟但足够好；用「服务器收到时间」作为统一排序键，各端展示顺序一致，即使到达顺序不同。
why_en: Chat servers sync clocks over NTP and stamp each message on arrival, and clients display messages sorted by that server timestamp for a consistent order everywhere.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台服务器把时钟对齐到同一参考时间的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes server clocks to a shared reference time.

q: 按服务器接收时间排序的可见副作用是什么？
q_en: What is the visible side effect of ordering messages by server-received time?
options: 部分消息会永久丢失
偶尔消息会插到发送更晚的消息上方，用户能接受
时钟漂移会让消息重复
客户端必须缓存全部历史
options_en: Some messages are permanently lost
Occasionally a message pops in above one sent later, and users find it acceptable
Clock drift causes duplicate messages
Clients must cache the entire message history
why: 接收时间 ≠ 发送时间，偶发的 pop-in 在所难免；但这是拿微小的视觉瑕疵换实时性，用户买账。
why_en: Occasionally a message pops in above one that was actually sent later, and users find that acceptable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台服务器把时钟对齐到同一参考时间的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes server clocks to a shared reference time.

q: 「用户每次发消息 / 收消息 / 回心跳都更新一次 lastSeen 字段」这个 naive 方案的问题？
q_en: What is the problem with the naive design of updating a lastSeen field every time a user sends a message, receives a message, or answers a heartbeat?
options: 读取延迟太高，其实读一条记录很快
巨大写放大：心跳把写入推到百万级/秒，且数据立刻过时
时间戳精度不够，这不是这里的真正问题
会暴露用户隐私 IP，其实字段里没有 IP
options_en: Read latency becomes too high, but reading one record is actually fast
Massive write amplification: heartbeats push writes to millions per second, and the data is stale the instant it lands
Timestamp precision is insufficient, but that is not the real problem here
It leaks user IP addresses, but the field never stores an IP
optionMeanings: 把问题归到读取延迟上。
把问题归到心跳驱动的写放大上。
把问题归到时间戳精度上。
把问题归到隐私泄露上。
why: 每个活动都写库，写入量被心跳放大到数百万/秒，换来的却是「查到时已过时」的数据——成本与价值完全倒挂。
why_en: Updating last seen on every action creates millions of low-value writes per second that are stale the moment they land, paying for consistency nobody needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测包，用来确认对方仍然存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small probe message sent at a fixed interval to confirm the other side of a connection is still alive.

scenario: 要做「最后在线时间」，希望存储与写入都最小化。两个洞察：用户断连时服务器一定知道；用户在线时他自己能实时告诉你。
scenario_en: You want to build "last seen" while minimizing both storage and writes. Two insights: the server always knows when a user disconnects, and an online user can tell you about it in real time.
q: 文中的设计是？
q_en: What is the article's design?
options: 只在断连时写一条记录，查询时并行读表、经 Pub/Sub 问对方是否在线，合并显示
每分钟对全体在线用户做快照，负载随在线人数线性增长
客户端之间 P2P 互相询问，对方离线时完全查不到结果
在负载均衡器上采集日志离线分析，只能查历史查不了当下
options_en: Write a record only on disconnect, then on query read that table and ask over Pub/Sub in parallel and merge the results
Snapshot every online user once a minute, with load scaling linearly with who is online
Have clients ask each other directly, peer to peer, which finds nothing once the target is offline
Collect load-balancer logs for offline analysis, which only shows history, not the current state
why: 把「在线」交给实时询问、把「离线时间」交给断连时的一次写入：存储最小（每人一条）、写入最少（仅断连时）。
why_en: Durably record only the last disconnect, and on a query check that table while asking the live user over pub/sub in parallel, merging the two responses.
whenOtherWins: 用户量小或需要完整在线历史审计时，按活动直接写库更简单、信息也更全。
tradeoff: 存储与写入最小化 vs 在线状态的实时精确性

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

q: 两台服务器可能先后为同一用户写断连时间戳，如何防止旧值覆盖更新的值？
q_en: Two servers might write a disconnect timestamp for the same user out of order — how do you stop a stale value from overwriting a newer one?
options: 写之前抢一把全局锁
随机退避后再写
只允许固定一台服务器负责写
DynamoDB 条件写：新时间戳更大才更新
options_en: Grab a global lock before writing
Write after a random backoff delay
Let only one fixed server be responsible for writing
A DynamoDB conditional write that only updates when the new timestamp is greater
optionMeanings: 写前抢全局锁。
随机退避后重试写入。
固定单一写者角色。
只有新值更大才允许提交的条件写。
why: 条件写把「比较再更新」压进存储层原子完成：晚到的旧时间戳会条件失败，不会倒退覆盖更近的断连时间。
why_en: A DynamoDB conditional write that only updates when the new timestamp is greater prevents two servers from racing and clobbering a more recent disconnect time.
codeSample:
UpdateItem LastSeen
  Key: { userId: "u_42" }
  SET lastDisconnect = :new
  ConditionExpression: :new > lastDisconnect
# fails harmlessly if another server already wrote a newer timestamp

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有满足指定条件（如新值大于旧值）才提交的写操作，由存储层原子完成「比较并更新」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write only commits when a stated condition holds, letting the store atomically compare and update in one step.

q: 客户端查询他人 last seen 的完整流程是？
q_en: What is the full flow when a client queries someone else's last seen?
options: 直接读 LastSeen 表并原样返回，不会去问对方当前是否真的在线
服务器并行读 LastSeen 表，同时经 Pub/Sub 问对方是否在线，合并两路结果显示
向全部 Chat Server 广播查询再投票，开销随集群规模线性增长
轮询目标用户直到回应，请求会一直阻塞等待，没有并行的兜底路径
options_en: Read the LastSeen table directly and return it as-is, without asking whether they are actually online right now
The server reads LastSeen and asks the target over Pub/Sub in parallel, then merges the two results to display
Broadcast the query to every Chat Server and vote, with cost scaling linearly with cluster size
Poll the target user repeatedly until they respond, blocking the whole time with no parallel fallback
why: 一次查询、两路并行响应（数据库的历史值 + 实时的在线确认），由客户端合并——存储与实时各答各的强项。
why_en: The server checks the last-seen table and in parallel forwards the query to the target's channel, and the client merges the database answer with any live online reply.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 请求者客户端
    participant A as Chat Server A
    participant DB as LastSeen 表
    participant B as Chat Server B（目标所在）
    C->>A: getLastSeen(target)
    par 并行
        A->>DB: 读最后断连时间
        A-->>C: updateLastSeen($DATE)
    and
        A->>B: 经 Pub/Sub 转发 getLastSeen
        B-->>C: updateLastSeen(ONLINE)（若在线）
    end
    C->>C: 合并：ONLINE 则绿点，否则显示断连时间

scenario: WhatsApp 要显示联系人是否在线或最后在线时间。为少写库，方案只在用户断连时写 LastSeen 表；查询时并行读表并经 Pub/Sub 问对方是否在线。
scenario_en: WhatsApp needs to show whether a contact is online or their last-seen time. To minimize writes, the design writes the LastSeen table only on disconnect, and a query reads that table while asking over Pub/Sub in parallel whether the target is online.
q: 这个 last-disconnect 方案还剩哪些风险和补强？（多选）
q_en: What risks and mitigations remain for this last-disconnect design? (select all)
options: 两路响应可能先后到达，客户端要能等待或平滑更新 UI
Chat Server 崩溃时可能来不及写断连时间
补强：连接建立时也写一次 LastSeen 表
必须每秒刷新所有用户的 last seen
options_en: The two responses may arrive apart, so the client must wait or update the UI smoothly.
A Chat Server crash may happen before it writes the disconnect time.
Mitigation: also write the LastSeen row when a connection is established.
Every user's last seen must be refreshed every second.
why: 这个方案用少量写入换取近似在线状态，所以剩余风险在合并两路响应和断连上报可靠性。连接时也写一次 LastSeen 是低成本加固；每秒全量刷新会把写入量打爆。
why_en: The design saves writes, but the client must merge two responses and the server may miss a disconnect, so writing on connect adds a cheap safety net.
tradeoff: 最小写入量 vs 在线状态鲁棒性
optionMeanings: 这是客户端合并两路结果的问题。
这是断连事件依赖服务器上报的问题。
这是用连接事件补一条持久记录。
这是把 last seen 改成全量心跳写入。
optionScenarioImpacts: 数据库先回时间、在线确认后到时，UI 不能闪烁或误导用户。
服务器崩溃可能让最后断连时间停在旧值。
用户重连时会刷新状态，降低漏记断连造成的错误窗口。
在线人数越多，写入量越接近心跳风暴。
optionDirectness: 查询路径有两个异步答案时，这项是客户端展示层必须处理的边界。
断连写入依赖连接所在服务器存活时，这项是主要可靠性风险。
需要缩短漏写断连造成的错误窗口时，连接时写一次是低成本补强。
只有能接受心跳级写入风暴时才会这么做；本题正是要避免它。
optionMeanings_en: This is the client-side merge problem.
This is the risk of depending on the server to report disconnects.
This adds a durable write on the connection event.

optionScenarioImpacts_en: If the database answer arrives first, the UI must not flicker or mislead.
A crashed server can leave the last disconnect time stale.
Reconnects refresh state and shrink the error window from a missed disconnect.
Write load grows with every online user's heartbeat.
optionDirectness_en: When the query has two asynchronous answers, the client UI must handle this boundary.
When disconnect writes depend on the owning server surviving, this is the main reliability risk.
Writing once on connect is a cheap mitigation when you need to shrink the stale-state window.
This only fits if heartbeat-scale write load is acceptable, which this design avoids.

q_en: Fill in the expected breadth-to-depth ratio at each level:
text: 面试期望的广度 : 深度——中级约 {{80}}:20、高级约 60:{{40}}、Staff+ 约 40:{{60}}；级别越高，越要主动识别问题并引领 deep dive，而不是等面试官来驱动。

q: Yelp 题的产品核心最准确地说是什么？
q_en: What is the core product being designed in the Yelp problem?
options: 本地商家搜索、浏览和评论平台
在线视频上传和播放平台
实时拼车调度系统
面向商家的广告竞价系统
options_en: A local business search, browsing, and review platform.
An online video upload and playback platform.
A real-time ride-hailing dispatch system.
A business-facing ad auction system.
why: 本题围绕本地商家发现和评论：用户搜索商家、查看商家和评论、留下评分和文字评论。广告、推荐和地图展示都不是主线。
why_en: The Yelp design centers on local business search, business detail viewing, and user reviews, not ads or recommendations.

scenario: 面试官已经把 Yelp 定义为本地商家搜索与评论平台，要求你先划定 MVP 范围内的核心功能。
scenario_en: The interviewer defines Yelp as a local business search and review platform, and asks you to scope the MVP features first.
q: Yelp 本地商家点评网站的核心功能需求有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core functional requirements belong in the MVP for a local business review site?
options: 为用户生成个性化推荐流
查看商家详情和评论
给商家留下 1-5 星评分和可选文字评论
按名称、经纬度位置和类别搜索商家
options_en: Generate a personalized recommendation feed for each user.
View business details and their reviews.
Leave a 1-5 star rating with optional text review.
Search businesses by name, lat/long location, and category.
why: 核心功能是商家搜索、详情+评论查看、写评论三件事；个性化推荐和地图展示属于范围外。
why_en: The core functions are searching businesses, viewing details with reviews, and creating reviews — not personalized recommendations.

q: Yelp 题的核心非功能需求包括哪些？（多选）

所有评论写入必须跨区域强一致同步
扩展到 100M 日活用户和 10M 商家
高可用，接受最终一致
options_en: Search latency under about 500 milliseconds.
All review writes must be strongly consistent across regions.
Scale to 100M daily active users and 10M businesses.
High availability, with eventual consistency accepted.
why: 核心是低延迟搜索、高可用和百万级规模；评论和搜索结果可接受最终一致，不要求跨区域强一致同步。

q: Yelp 题里，用来防止刷分和竞对恶意差评的核心业务约束是什么？

每个用户对每个商家只能留一条评论
每个搜索请求必须返回全量商家
每个城市只能有一个类别

Each user may leave only one review per business.
Every search request must return the full business set.
Each city may only have one category.
why: 一人一商家一评是后续数据库约束深挖的基础，用来防止同一用户刷分或竞品恶意刷差评。
why_en: The key constraint is that each user may leave only one review per business, preventing rating manipulation.

替代全文索引
